Therefore, we plan to continue our policy mix, including the efforts to deepen our financial market particularly to regain economic momentum as achieved before, as well as to maintain financial sector stability and investor trust in facing the forthcoming political agenda of the presidential and parliament elections in 2014. Distinguished Committee Members, Before ending my remark, I would like to underline two points as our lesson learned from the emerging markets situation. First, We realized that the policies taken by advanced economies, especialy the Fed tapering, have significant impact to emerging markets, so the Fed should take into account those impacts in formulating and implementing its policy. Global communication between advanced economies and emerging markets will also help to minimize the negative impacts caused by unecessary overreactive policies. Second, for domestic policy response, the understanding of central bank and government about macroeconomic problems become the key in formulating prompt policy responses. Both authorities are also required to have good communication and coordination, so they will be able to introduced appropriate policy mix to address those macroeconomic problems. Finally, I personally hope that various work plans for SCAV activities in 2014 could help Emerging Market Economies, including Indonesia, in strengthening the assessment of the potential financial vulnerabilities so as we could leverage on other countries experience to enhance our economic and financial resilience against any potential vulnerabilities. Thank you. 4

Title: Welcome Remark "The IILM Sukuk Awareness Program" by Dr. Halim Alamsyah, Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia, Jakarta, 21 March 2014
text: BANK INDONESIA Welcome Remark 'The IILM Sukuk Awareness Program' by Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Jakarta, 21 March 2014 Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim,  H.E. Profesor Datuk Rifaat Ahmed Abdel Karim, CEO of the International Islamic Liquidity Management (IILM)  H.E. Mr. Isa Rachmatarwata from Ministry of Finance  Distinguished Resource Persons, Seminar Participants, Ladies and Gentlemen Assalamualaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh and very good morning 1. It is my great pleasure to be here to welcome all seminar participants. Welcome to Bank Indonesia to Prof. Rifaat Ahmed Abdel Karim and the IILM team. Today we will have a half day seminar to discuss about 'the International Islamic Liquidity Management (IILM) Sukuk Program. Some of you probably have heard about the IILM, but probably most of seminar participants didnt know or even never heard about the IILM, its objective and also its business model. Therefore, as a member of the IILM, today Bank Indonesia is facilitating this seminar to introduce the IILM and its sukuk program to Indonesian financial market players, not only to Islamic financial markets but also to conventional market players. 2. As you may aware, the International Islamic Liquidity Management (IILM) was established on October 25th, 2010 by 10 central banks and monetary authorities which are Bank Indonesia, Bank Negara Malaysia, Central Bank of Qatar, Kuwait, Mauritius, Nigeria, Turkey, United Arab Emirates, Luxembourg and the Islamic Development Bank. The objective of the IILM establishment is creating and issuing short-term sharia compliant instruments to facilitate effective cross-border Islamic liquidity management. Seminar Participants, 3. Global Islamic Finance Report (GIFR) 2013 reported that the size of global Islamic finance assets reached US1.6 trillion at the end 2012. This assets size is expected to cross US1.8 trillion in 2013 and US2.1 trillion by the end 2014. Islamic banking industry dominates the Islamic finance with share around 80.4%, while the share of sukuk accounted for 14.5%. Global sukuk outstanding is expected to reach US275 billion at the end of 2013. All those global sukuk issued are medium and long-term sukuk. We can say that none of short-term global sukuk was issued. Page 1 BANK INDONESIA 4. For Indonesia case, the Government has issued several series of global sukuk with outstanding reached US4.15 billion with at least 5 years tenure. For short-term sukuk, the Government has launched Sharia Treasury Bill (Surat Perbendaharaan Negara Syariah/SPNS) with maturity less than a year. Currently the outstanding of this short-term sukuk is Rp4,35 trilion or equivalent to US0.4 billion, but all those short-term sukuk are in rupiah denomination. 5. Therefore, the IILM tries to fulfill the absence of short-term global sukuk in the market in order to promote cross-border liquidity management. The IILM has started to issue short-term sukuk last year and currently the outstanding of the IILM sukuk reached US1.35 billion. It is still very small amount compare to global sukuk outstanding reached around US275 billion. Seminar Participants, Ladies and Gentlemen 6. We realized that currently Islamic financial markets have limited access and instruments to short-term funding options in raising liquidity as compared to conventional markets. Therefore, liquidity becomes one of the major problems in developing Islamic finance, besides product codification, legal infrastructure, regulatory framework, and human resources gap. We do hope that the presence of the IILM and its breakthrough in issuing short-term global sukuk will help the industry in managing short-term liquidity. 7. Finally, through this seminar, I wish all participants will have better understanding about the IILM business model. Thus, we can elaborate the opportunity to cooperate in promoting liquidity management and accelerating Islamic finance development. May Allah SWT give us the strength and patient to persist fulfilling our duty to develop Islamic finance in Indonesia. Thank you for your kind attention, Wassalamualaikum Wr. Wb. Dr. Halim Alamsyah Page 2

Title: Sambutan Gubernur Bank Indonesia, Agus D.W. Martowardojo pada Peluncuran Bersama Kartu Berlogo Nasional GPN, Jakarta, 3 Mei 2018
text: Joint Launch of GPN National Logo Card Bank Indonesia, 3rd May 2018 Which we respect, - Men ten Ba and Usaha Miiik Negara, Mrs. Rini Soemarno - Minister of Social Affairs, Mr. Idrus Marham - Member of the Board of Commissioners of the Financial Services Authority, Mr. Heru Kristiyana - Member de wan Governor of Bank Indonesia - Chairman of the National Bank Association - Chairman of The Indonesian Payment System Association - Bank Leaders and Partners in the Field of Payment Systems - Happy Attendees and Invitees, Assaiamu'aiaikum warahmatuiiahi wabarakatuh In the Morning and Sa lam Sejahtera For All of Us 1. Praise and gratitude we pray for the presence of God Almighty, for by His grace and grace we can gather in good health on this day. 2. Our presence today marks an important milestonein the development of payment system in Indonesia, namely the launch of Together with the National Payment Gateway (GPN) Logo Card. NPG can start full implementation and be widely used by the community thanks to harmonious and synergistic cooperation between Bank Indonesia and the Government, especially the Ministry of Social Affairs, the Ministry of SOEs and the Ministry of PUPR, OJK as well as the banking and payment system industry. For this reason, at the beginning of this speech, we would like to express our high appreciation for the support of all of you. Ladies and gentlemen, 3. The payment system in Indonesia is developing very fast. The increasingly widespread internet of things such as e-commerce, fintech and application-based transportation services has led to the need for a secure, efficient, smooth, and reliable payment system that continues to grow ningkat. Various innovations related to payment methods and means are widely offered to facilitate, cheapen and speed up the transaction process. 4. The dynamics of such changes need to be addressed carefully and carefully by regulators. Regulators need to address not only the potential, but also the risks that the innovation contains. Policymakers need to weigh the impact of regulation from various sides, which are often trade-offs, between short-term impacts and long-term sustainability. Important aspects of concern in policy formulation include business competition, price formation, innovation incentives, industrial attractiveness for investors and quality and timeliness of policy responses. 5. Considering the dynamics of rapid and comprehensive changes in the payment system sector, Bank Indonesia has prepared a Blueprint for the Development of the Indonesian Payment System. This blueprint allows us to carry out an organized and planned response, is not ad-hoc, so it can provide clarity on future directions not only for regulators, but also for industry, business actors and the public. Hadi cans that we respect, 6. The launch of NPG is an important momentum in the embodiment of the Indonesian Payment System Blueprint. NPG is a breakthrough in eliminating fragmentation through interconnection and interoperability bi litas between Pern baya ran System Service Providers. 7. Kami noted that in the midst of the rapid need for transactions, there are still fragmentation, inefficiency, and security risks faced by consumers. Fragmentation arose due to the tendency of the industry to build payment system platforms of an exclusionary nature f, that is, it can only serve its own issued instruments. The existing platforms are also not interconnected or interconnected with each other, so they have not been able to provide an ecosystem of services that can serve each other (interoperable). The simplest illustration that we often encounter is the large number of ATM machines in the mall and the lining of EDC machines at the supermarket cashier. 8. Such fragmentation in turn gives birth to inefficiency, which can be seen from several main points, namely: 95 The investment cost of expanding infrastructure and technology is high, as the industry is reluctant to share services, such as investment in ATM machines and EDC that are so large only for one location. 3/7 In fact, if these machines can be interoperable, there is such a great potential to relocate them to areas across the country that are still experiencing shortages. So that it will be able to encourage the expansion of access and financial inclusion in Indonesia. 95 People become necessary to have many cards, because the acceptance of cards is still limited. This is because certain cards can only be used in certain payment terminal machines, as a result of each ATM or EDC cannot accept all types of cards. 95 Even if accepted, cards used at different ATM / EDC terminals will be charged a relatively high fee, where the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) can reach 2-3% per transaction. This cost is certainly ultimately borne by konsumen. From the decline in MDR alone, economic savings reached Rpl.3T to Rpl.8T. Along with the wider use of NPG, the efficiency caused to the national economy will certainly be greater. 9. The presence of NPG is expected to be enjoyed by all levels of society and make it easier for people to make payment transactions. at a lower cost. These lower costs can be enjoyed by merchants and buyers. The benefit felt by merchants is a decrease in the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) which originally ranged from 2% to 3% to only 1%. Meanwhile, the community Cardholders can enjoy lower administration fees. In fact, for recipients of Government social assistance, NPG imposes an MDR of 0%. Thus, beneficiaries or assistance are not charged for disbursement. 10. For banks, the presence of NPG can expand customer acceptance through easy access to all payment channels. Banks do not need to compete in providing payment channel infrastructure, so they can be more flexible and focused on improving the quality of service to their customers. 11. This benefit encourages banks to provide strong support for NPG from the time it is introduced until it reaches the implementation stage. Of the total 100 Payment System Service Providers (PJSP), 98 of them have obtained approval to issue ATM and Debit cards with the GPN logo. 12. In order to further expand the acceptance of cards bearing the NPG logo, banks and Bank Indonesia will conduct a joint campaign. The NPG campaign will be carried out in all cities in Indonesia, involving the role of all Bank Indonesia Representative Offices in collaboration with the Regional Banking Deliberation Board (BMPD). Ladies and Gentlemen we are proud of, 13. Prior to these remarks, we witnessed a strong statement of commitment from the NPG Support Institute. NPG organizers are supported by 3 institutions, namely Standard Institutions , Switching Institutions, and Services Institutions. 14. Bank Indonesia has established the Indonesian Payment System Association (ASPI) as the ATM and Debit Card Standard Institution and standard institution for electronic money. The Standards Institute has the function of compiling, developing, and managing Standards for the interconnection and interoperability of payment instruments, payment channels, and switching, as well as security. 15. Bank Indonesia has also established Switching Institutions , namely Artajasa, Rintis, Alto, and Jalin in 2017. Switching Institutions have the task of organizing the processing of domestic payment transaction data securely and efficiently. 16. Furthermore, Bank Indonesia will establish PT Penyelesaian Transaksi Elektronik Nasional (PTEN) as a Services Institution, which has duties, including maintaining the security of payment transactions and the confidentiality of customer data; reconciling, clearing, and settlement; developing systems for fraud prevention and handling payment transaction disputes in the context of consumer protection. 17. On this occasion, we also invite all partners from the banking industry and payment systems both domestically and externally to participate and support NPG and other payment system policies. We believe that the policies we have launched can maintain the continuity of the development of a healthy payment system industry in Indonesia. As we all know, the potential for payment system development in Indonesia is very broad in line with the increasing economic growth, income an increasingly tall society as well as demographic bonuses with an increased composition of the productive age. Ladies and gentlemen we respect, 18. NpG implementation is the foundation for future Payment System policies, such as strengthening electronic money regulation and qr code standardization. Furthermore, NPG is also a starting point for developments related to the stem payment that we are currently coordinating with the Government, especially with the Ministry of Social Affairs, Ministry of SOEs and Ministry of Public Works and Public Housing. These developments include, among others, the Expansion of Social Aid Program nontunai, EBIPP {Electronic Bi IIs/ Invoices Presentment and Payment) to realize a national service system for bill payments and Multi Lane Free Flow {MiFF) for jaIan toll. 19. Regarding Electronic Money, we have strengthened regulations that include strengthening the institutional aspects of electronic money issuers, among others, through minimum capital arrangements. In addition, it strengthens aspects of consumer protection and aspects of security and acceptance of electronic money through the obligation to increase transaction security standards and domestic processing obligations through NPG. Through these strengthening measures , the integrity and national security as well as the resilience of the financial system of nasional are expected to be maintained, without hindering the pace of innovation and development dynamic industry. 20. Furthermore, regarding the QR Code, Bank Indonesia considers the need for national standardization for QR Code payments Indonesia. Currently, we compile the national QR Code standard together with stakeholders, namely associations, banking and the financial technology industry. The national standard QR Code according to the plan will be set by us in the near future. Ta mu and the Invitation we described, 21. As the end of our remarks, we would once again like to express our gratitude and high appreciation to the Ministry and related Institutions, industry, and associations for their support to the successful development and implementation of NPG. 22. With the cooperation and synergy that has been well established, we believe that the goal of NPG as a Unifying National Payment Transaction can be realized. May God always recognize and ease our steps together in realizing a more prosperous Indonesian society. Thank you and Thank You Wassaiamu'aiaikum warahmatuiiahi wabarakatuh Governor of Bank Indonesia Agus D.W. Martowardojo
text_original: @ BANK INDONESIA SAMBUTAN GUBERNUR BANK INDONESIA Peluncuran Bersama Kartu Berlogo Nasional GPN Bank Indonesia, 3 Mei 2018 Yang kami hormati, - Men ten Ba dan Usaha Miiik Negara, Ibu Rini Soemarno - Menteri Sosiai, Bapak Idrus Marham - Anggota Dewan Komisioner Otoritas Jasa Keuangan, Bapak Heru Kristiyana - Anggota De wan Gubernur Bank Indonesia - Ketua Perhimpunan Bank Nasional - Ketua Asosiasi Sistem Pembayaran Indonesia - Para Pimpinan Bank dan Mitra Kerja di Bidang Sistem Pembayaran - Hadirin dan Undangan yang berbahagia, Assaiamu'aiaikum warahmatuiiahi wabarakatuh Seta mat Pagi dan Sa lam Sejahtera Untuk Kita Semua 1. Puji dan syukur kita panjatkan kehadirat Tuhan Yang Maha Kuasa, karena atas rahmat dan karunia-Nya kita dapat berkumpul dalam keadaan sehat walafiat pada hari ini. 2. Kehadiran kita pada hari ini menandai suatu milestonepenting dalam pengembangan Sistem Pembayaran di Indonesia yaitu Peluncuran Bersama Kartu Berlogo Gerbang Pembayaran Nasional (GPN). GPN dapat memulai implementasi secara penuh dan digunakan secara luas oleh masyarakat berkat kerja sama yang harmonis dan sinergis antara Bank Indonesia dengan Pemerintah khususnya Kementerian Sosial, Kementerian BUMN dan Kementerian PUPR, OJK serta industri perbankan dan sistem pembayaran. Untuk itu dalam awal sambutan ini, kami mengucapkan apresiasi yang tinggi atas dukungan Bapak dan Ibu sekalian. Bapak dan Ibu sekalian, 3. Sistem Pembayaran di Indonesia berkembang sangat cepat. Semakin meluasnya the internet of things seperti e-commerce, fintech dan jasa transportasi berbasis aplikasi menyebabkan kebutuhan akan sistem pembayaran yang aman, efisien, lancar, dan andal terus meningkat. Berbagai inovasi terkait cara dan sarana pembayaran marak ditawarkan untuk mempermudah, mempermurah dan mempercepat proses bertransaksi. 4. Dinamika perubahan tersebut perlu disikapi dengan cermat dan hati- hati oleh regulator. Regulator perlu memerhatikan tidak hanya potensi, namun juga risikoyang dikandung inovasi tersebut. Perumus kebijakan perlu menimbang dampak regulasi dari berbagai sisi yang seringkali bersifat trade-off, antara dampak jangka pendek dan kesinambungan jangka panjang. Aspek-aspek penting yang menjadi perhatian dalam perumusan kebijakan mencakup persaingan usaha, pembentukan harga, insentif inovasi, daya tarik industri bagi investor dan kualitas maupun ketepatan waktu respons kebijakan. 5. Mempertimbangkan dinamika perubahan yang bersifat cepat dan menyeluruh di bidang sistem pembayaran, Bank Indonesia menyusun Blueprint Pengem ba ngan Sistem Pembayaran Indonesia. Blueprint ini memungkinkan kami melakukan respons yang tertata dan terencana, tidak bersifat ad-hoc, sehingga dapat memberikan kejelasan arah ke depan tidak hanya bagi regulator, namun juga bagi industri, pelaku usaha dan masyarakat. Hadi tin yang kami hormati, 6. Diluncurkannya GPN merupakan momentum penting dalam pengejawantahan Blueprint Sistem Pernbayaran Indonesia. GPN menjadi terobosan dalam menghilangkan fragmentasi melalui interkoneksi dan interopera bi litas antar Penyelenggara Jasa Sistem Pern baya ran. 7. Kami mencermati, ditengah pesatnya kebutuhan bertransaksi, masih terdapat fragmentasi, inefisiensi, dan risiko keamanan yang dihadapi konsumen. Fragmentasi muncul karena kecenderungan industri untuk membangun platform sistem pembayaran yang sifatnya eksklusif, yaitu hanya dapat melayani instrumen yang diterbitkannya sendiri. Platform-platform yang ada juga belum saling terhubung atau interconnected satu sama lain, sehingga belum mampu menyediakan ekosistem layanan yang dapat saling melayani (interoperabel). Ilustrasi paling sederhana yang sering kita jumpai adalah banyaknya deretan mesin ATM di mall dan berjejernya mesin EDC di kasir supermarket. 8. Fragmentasi tersebut pada gilirannya melahirkan inefisiensi, yang dapat dilihat dari beberapa hal utama, yaitu: <95> Biaya investasi perluasan infrastruktur dan teknologi menjadi tinggi, karena industri enggan berbagi layanan, seperti investasi mesin ATM dan EDC yang begitu besar hanya untuk di satu lokasi. 3/7 Padahal, apabila mesin-mesin tersebut dapat saling interoperabel, terdapat potensi yang begitu besar untuk merelokasinya ke daerah-daerah di penjuru tanah air yang masih mengalami kekurangan. Sehingga akan mampu mendorong perluasan akses dan keuangan inklusif di Indonesia. <95> Masyarakat menjadi perlu untuk memiliki banyak kartu, karena akseptasi kartu yang masih terbatas. Hal ini dikarenakan kartu tertentu hanya dapat digunakan di mesin terminal pembayaran tertentu, akibat setiap ATM atau EDC tidak dapat menerima semua jenis kartu. <95> Kalaupun diterima, kartu yang digunakan pada terminal ATM / EDC yang berbeda akan dikenakan biaya yang relatif tinggi, dimana Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) dapat mencapai 2-3% per transaksi. Biaya ini tentu pada akhirnya ikut ditanggung oleh konsumen. Dari penurunan MDR saja penghematan secara ekonomi mencapai Rpl,3T sampai dengan Rpl,8T. Seiring dengan penggunaan GPN yang semakin luas, efisiensi yang ditimbulkan bagi perekonomian nasional tentunya akan semakin besar. 9. Kehadiran GPN diharapkan dapat dinikmati seluruh lapisan masyarakat dan memudahkan masyarakat untuk melakukan transaksi pembayaran. dengan biaya lebih rendah. Biaya yang lebih rendah tersebut dapat dinikmati oleh pedagang (merchant) dan pembeli. Manfaat yang dirasakan oleh merchant adalah penurunan Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) yang semula berkisar antara 2% sampai dengan 3% menjadi hanya 1%. Sementara, masyarakat pemegang kartu dapat menikmati turunnya biaya administrasi. Bahkan, untuk penerima bantuan sosial Pemerintah, GPN mengenakan MDR sebesar 0%. Sehingga, penerima manfaat atau bantuan tidak dikenakan biaya untuk melakukan pencairan. 10. Bagi bank, kehadiran GPN dapat memperluas akseptasi nasabahnya melalui kemudahan akses terhadap seluruh kanal pembayaran. Bank tidak perlu berkompetisi dalam menyediakan infrastruktur kanal pembayaran, sehingga dapat lebih leluasa dan fokus dalam meningkatkan kualitas layanan kepada nasabahnya. 11. Kemanfaatan tersebut mendorong perbankan untuk memberikan dukungan yang kuat terhadap GPN sejak diperkenalkan hingga sampai pada tahap implementasi. Dari total 100 Penyelenggara Jasa Sistem Pembayaran (PJSP), 98 diantaranya telah memperoleh persetujuan untuk menerbitkan kartu ATM dan Debet berlogo GPN. 12. Dalam rangka semakin memperluas akseptasi kartu berlogo GPN, Perbankan dan Bank Indonesia akan melakukan joint campaign. Kampanye GPN akan dilakukan di seluruh kota di Indonesia, dengan melibatkan peran seluruh Kantor Perwakilan Bank Indonesia bekerja sama dengan Badan Musyawarah Perbankan Daerah (BMPD). Bapak dan Ibu yang kami banggakan, 13. Sebelum sambutan ini, kita menyaksikan pernyataan komitmen yang kuat dari Lembaga Pendukung GPN. Penyelenggara GPN didukung oleh 3 lembaga yaitu Lembaga Standar, Lembaga Switching, dan Lembaga Services. 14. Bank Indonesia telah menetapkan Asosiasi Sistem Pembayaran Indonesia (ASPI) sebagai Lembaga Standar Kartu ATM dan Debet serta Lembaga Standar untuk Uang Elektronik. Lembaga Standar memiliki fungsi untuk menyusun, mengembangkan, dan mengelola Standar untuk interkoneksi dan interoperabilitas instrumen pembayaran, kanal pembayaran, dan switching, serta security. 15. Bank Indonesia juga sudah menetapkan Lembaga Switching yaitu Artajasa, Rintis, Alto, dan Jalin pada tahun 2017. Lembaga Switching memiliki tugas menyelenggarakan pemrosesan data transaksi pembayaran domestik secara aman dan efisien. 16. Selanjutnya, Bank Indonesia akan menetapkan PT Penyelesaian Transaksi Elektronik Nasional (PTEN) sebagai Lembaga Services, yang memiliki tugas antara lain menjaga keamanan transaksi pembayaran dan kerahasiaan data nasabah; melakukan rekonsiliasi, kliring, dan setelmen; mengembangkan sistem untuk pencegahan fraud serta menangani perselisihan transaksi pembayaran dalam rangka perlindungan konsumen. 17. Pada kesempatan ini kami juga mengundang segenap mitra kerja dari industri perbankan dan sistem pembayaran baik domestik maupun eksternal untuk turut berpartisipasi dan mendukung GPN serta kebijakan-kebijakan sistem pembayaran lainnya. Kami yakin bahwa kebijakan yang telah kami luncurkan dapat menjaga kesinambungan perkembangan industri sistem pembayaran yang sehat di Indonesia. Sebagaimana kita ketahui bersama, potensi pengembangan sistem pembayaran di Indonesia sangat luas seiring dengan pertumbuhan ekonomi yang terus naik, pendapatan masyarakat yang bertambah tinggi serta bonus demografi dengan komposisi usia produktif yang meningkat. Hadirin yang kami hormati, 18. Implementasi GPN merupakan landasan bagi kebijakan-kebijakan Sistem Pembayaran ke depan seperti antara lain penguatan pengaturan uang elektronik dan standarisasi QR code. Selanjutnya, GPN juga merupakan titik tolak dari pengembangan-pengembangan terkait sistem pembayaran yang saat ini sedang kami koordinasikan dengan Pemerintah khususnya bersama Kementerian Sosial, Kementerian BUMN dan Kementerian Pekerjaan Umum dan Perumahan Rakyat. Pengembangan-pengembangan tersebut antara lain mencakup Perluasan Bansos nontunai, EBIPP {Electronic Bi IIs/Invoices Presentment and Payment) untuk mewujudkan sistem layanan yang bersifat nasional untuk pembayaran tagihan serta Multi Lane Free Flow {MiFF) untuk jaIan tol. 19. Terkait Uang Elektronik, kami telah melakukan penguatan regulasi yang mencakup Penguatan terhadap aspek kelembagaan Penerbit uang elektronik antara lain melalui pengaturan modal minimum. Selain itu dilakukan penguatan aspek perlindungan konsumen dan aspek keamanan serta akseptasi uang elektronik melalui kewajiban peningkatan standar keamanan transaksi dan kewajiban pemrosesan domestik melalui GPN. Melalui langkah-langkah penguatan ini, integritas dan keamanan nasional serta resiliensi sistem keuangan nasional diharapkan akan tetap terjaga, tanpa menghambat laju inovasi dan perkembangan industri yang dinamis. 20. Selanjutnya terkait QR Code, Bank Indonesia memandang perlu standardisasi nasional untuk QR Code payments Indonesia. Saat ini standar nasional QR Code tengah kami susun bersama-sama dengan stakeholders yaitu asosiasi, perbankan dan industri teknologi finansial. Standar nasional QR Code menurut rencana akan segera kami tetapkan dalam waktu dekat. Ta mu dan Undangan yang kami muiiakan, 21. Sebagai akhir sambutan kami, sekali lagi kami ingin menyampaikan terima kasih dan penghargaan yang tinggi kepada Kementrian dan Lembaga terkait, industri, serta asosiasi atas dukungannya terhadap kesuksesan pengembangan dan implementasi GPN. 22. Dengan kerja sama dan sinergi yang telah terjalin dengan baik, kami yakin bahwa tujuan GPN sebagai Pemersatu Transaksi Pembayaran Nasional dapat diwujudkan. Semoga Tuhan YME senantiasa merestui dan meringankan langkah kita bersama dalam mewujudkan masyarakat Indonesia yang lebih sejahtera. Sekian dan Terima Kasih Wassaiamu'aiaikum warahmatuiiahi wabarakatuh Gubernur Bank Indonesia Agus D.W. Martowardojo

Title: Penjelasan Gubernur BI Pada Rapat Kerja Dengan Komisi XI DPR RI, 25 September 2006
text: EXPLANATION BY THE GOVERNOR OF BANK INDONESIA AT A WORKING MEETING WITH COMMISSION XI of the House of Representatives Rl ON SEPTEMBER 25 , 2006 9595959595959595959595959595 Dear Member De wan, 1. First of all, let us express our gratitude to the Chairman and Members of Commission XI of the House for inviting us to today's Working Meeting. In accordance with the agenda we obtained, this Working Meeting will discuss the Single Presence Policy (SPP), Banking Risk Management and the development of Bl's subsidiaries . With regard to today's topic, before we listen to any further input, questions and views of the Board Members, allow us to briefly explain per banking development until July 2006, Bl's banking policy, especially regarding the Single Presence Policy and Risk Management Certification, which will be followed by a brief presentation on development of Bl's subsidiary. Development and Kof Banking work Dear De wan Members, 2. Entering the second half of 2006, banking performance continued to show encouraging developments. Almost all major banking indicators show positive developments, and in general, the banking industry has been able to cope well with the business risks it faces, including reducing pressures. to the high operating costs and non-performing loans. As of the end of July 2006, the number of bank loans remained increasing. Total loans provided reached Rp 758.4 trillion, an increase of Rp28.2 trillion compared to December 2005, or grew by 3.87%. The amount of deposits and total banking assets also increased to reach Rp 1,161.0 trillion and Rp 1,517.1 trillion, compared to the end of December 2005 of Rp 1,127.9 trillion and Rp 1,469.8 trillion. Consequently, the LDR of the banking industry increased from 64.7% in December 2005 to 65.3% in July 2006. 3. Bank profitability at the end of July 2006 was relatively stable compared to the end of December 2005. The net interest rate (Nile) of the banking industry increased while the ROA actually fell slightly. Meanwhile, the capital ratio increased from 19.5% at the end of December 2005 to 20.7% at the end of July 2006. 4. In terms of risk, in general, banks are still able to manage the business risks they face even though the risks faced are still relatively high due to the relatively high interest rates. and the trend of rising global interest rates. Credit risk in the future is still quite high, especially due to the lack of conducive investment climate and the impact of natural disasters in various regions. The high credit risk is reflected in the increasing number of non-performingloans (NPLs). Both gross and net NPLs increased from 8.3% and 4.8% respectively as of the end of December 2005 to 8.9% and 5.2% in July 2006. Meanwhile, the bank's resilience in facing liquidity risks is considered adequate. Bank Indonesia Policy in the Banking Sector Dear Councillors, 5. The performance of the banking industry is inseparable from the policies adopted by Bank Indonesia in the banking sector. During the 1st semester of 2006, Bl's policy remained focused on strengthening banking system stability in order to create financial system stability and promote the banking intermediation function. The policy is pursued through the implementation of programs that have been launched in the Indonesian Banking Architecture (API). Furthermore, in the medium to long term, the provisions and provisions of the Bl will remain focused on strengthening the operational joints of the banking industry and the application of the prudential principle. Thus, it is expected that by the end of 2010 an Indonesian banking industry will be formed that is more resilient, competitive in the global environment and useful in the process Indonesia's economic development . 6. To be able to realize the banking industry in accordance with this vision. Bl pursued several policy strategies whose implementation was carried out gradually by adjusting to the dynamics that occurred in the national banking industry. To get a healthy, sturdy, effective and beneficial banking industry for the whole society. Bank Indonesia views the API pillar 1 - Strengthening thePanglo-Integrity Structure of Indonesia, through a consolidation process , as a must. In the last 2 years, efforts to consolidate the banking industry have been taken by implementing 2 strengthening policy strategies which until now are still continuing to b continue the process. First. in 2005. Bank Indonesia has issued a capital provision for the national banking industry that stipulates that the minimum amount of capital that must be owned by banks in 2010 is Rp. 100 billion. The fulfillment of the minimum capital ju mmlah can be carried out in stages by each bank with the achievement of the target of the amount of interim capital of Rp. 80 billion by the end of the year 2007. Second. Bl has also outlined a policy to determine the existence of a Bank with Good Performance (BKB) or also known as Anchor Bank which is expected to be able to became the fulcrum in consolidation through the acquisition process of small banks. 7. The implementation of these two policy strategies is still being pursued, especially by placing more emphasis on the implementation of the supervision process. Furthermore, so that efforts to structure and strengthen the desired structure of the banking industry can occur at all levels, in 2006 Bl also outlined a policy of yang third. namely the single presence policy for Indonesian banks. As we announced some time ago, it is hoped that this policy will be able to encourage consolidation in the banking business strategy, while also managing aspects business competition in the banking industry itself. With this step, the improvement of the efficiency of the banking industry as a whole will also be optimized. In the event of a merger between banks owned by the same business group, the potential and financing ability of the bank will be even greater because the maximum credit limit (BMPK) will increase in line with the increase in the amount of capital. Syndicated financing cooperation will also be easily formed, if the business strategies of banks in one ownership group are controlled in a consolidated manner. 8. In terms of bank supervision, we consider the sole proprietorship policy to be very effective to support Bank Indonesia's efforts to improve the bank supervision system towards a consolidated supervision approach. Communication between the supervisory authority and the bank controller becomes smoother given the single point of contact, which in turn will improve the monitoring function of Bl. Technically, the consolidated bank financial statements are a very effective medium in mapping all risk exposures of the bank and all financial subsidiaries that are in one ownership auspices. 9. The Sole Proprietorship Policy in Indonesian Banking that we are going to issue basically stipulates that each party can only be a controlling shareholder (PSP) in one bank. As for PSPs that currently have more than one bank, alternatives are given that can be taken to adjust their ownership structure, namely through reducing share ownership so that the person concerned only becomes a PSP in one bank, combining the banks it owns either through merger or consolidation, or by forming a holding company (Bank Holding Company - BHC) in Indonesia to oversee the banks it owns. The sole proprietorship policy is expected to be fully implemented by 2010. 10. The designation of 2010 as the deadline for implementing the sole proprietorship policy is essentially inseparable from the time frame for api implementation in 2010. From the beginning. Bl sees that 2010 is the year when all the restructuring and strengthening programs of the banking industry pursued so far will be able to deliver the expected results. A banking industry that is healthy, sturdy, efficient and beneficial to the whole society. As for 2008, what we have previously said is an intermediate target or milestone needed in directing the journey of the banking industry towards 2010. In that year, the banking industry presumably need to evaluate the various preparatory processes that have been and remain to be carried out to realize the commitment to the alternatives that have been chosen. 11. We understand that the 3 alternatives we offer to choose from by the banking industry are not simple things. Therefore. Bl is always open to intensive discussion and exchange with various parties involved in t. The understanding and understanding of the parties through a process of cooperation and coordination is the key to the success of this policy. In this case, we assess that determining alternative steps that will be taken early will be very useful to give yang enough time in making preparations. Bl will always be accommodating and ready to help facilitate the entire process, from the preparation of a business plan to the implementation process. In the near future, we plan to issue this SPP in the form of guidelines that can provide guidance for banks in conducting consolidation. 12. The issuance of directives and guidelines for the implementation of the SPP will also be followed by the issuance of several other banking provisions aimed at providing wider wiggle room for the industry in performs its functions. Bl as a public institution is fully aware that to be able to get out of the entanglement of existing problems, this nation needs the contribution and participation of all its elements . Since recent times Bl has continued to try to find and examine all the possibilities that can be done to dynamize the nation's economy, without having to sacrifice stability which has been achieved at this time. We reviewed the various provisions of the existing provisions to find these possibilities. Currently , we have completed the process of adjusting the PBI regarding BMPK, and Good Corporate Governance which is expected to provide more free space for banks to move in carrying out its intermediation function. In addition, we are also entering the final stage of preparing a BiB on banking policies in disaster areas, providing incentives in the merger process and various other policies that we view relevan with the needs of the nation today. All these rules and provisions, are expected to be completed in the near future, and can then be issued as a policy package in the banking sector . Dear Member De wan, 13. In order to improve the quality of banking management and operations and as an implementation of Pillar 4 of the API, Bl has issued regulations regarding risk management certification for administrators and general officials bank. This provision in essence aims to provide competency standards for management and officials of commercial banks in managing the risks faced in banking operations. everyday. Competency standards are important considering that the intermediation function carried out by banks requires adequate leadership and expertise in the management of fund collection and distribution so that the risks associated with the implementation of the bank's business activities can be anticipated and managed properly. 14. To realize banking resources that have the required competencies, risk management certification is carried out in 5 (five) levels which are carried out in a tiered manner and their application is adjusted with the scale of the bank's business and the complexity of the bank's management and officer positions, this tiered certification program is referred to as a regular program. This certification is carried out in accordance with international standards used by the Global Association of Risk Professionals (GARP), an independent non-profit institution in the field of risk management established by risk professionals from various countries. The use of standards and cooperation with GARP is crucial because at this time there are no institutions / organizations that carry out risk management certification with boothdar quality equivalent to international standards. 15. Before conducting a regular program, there is a need to equalize the perception of understanding from bankers who will in time participate in the regular program followed by the top leadership and komisaris bank each. On the basis of this need, a fast-track program was held for the directors and commissioners of commercial banks, which was carried out with a brief but comprehensive workshop method, with the aim of provide a fundamental understanding to bankadvocates. 16. The obligation to have a risk management certificate for the management and officers of the bank under these provisions will be effective on August 3 , 2010 and it will be one of the administrative requirements in the fit & proper test for the management and executive officers of commercial banks. In this case, bank administrators and officials who do not have a risk management certificate as of August 3, 2010 are no longer allowed to occupy their positions. 17. To support the implementation of risk management certification as required by these provisions, the Indonesian of Risk Professional Association (IRPA) and the Federation Indonesian Association of Banks (FIAB) then established a professional certification body that Kemudian is known as the Risk Management Certification Agency (BSMR). This institution has been registered with the National Professional Certification Agency (BNSP) as an institution that has the authority to carry out banking risk management certification. 18. Furthermore, considering that the existence of this professional certification body is very important for improving the quality of human resources in the banking industry, Bank Indonesia provides temporary support to BSMR in the form of providing work facilities in bank indonesia office complexes. In due course later BSMR is encouraged to have its own place. As was the original intention at the time of its establishment, in the future BSMR will also cooperate and coordinate intensively with the existing banker professional association, namely the Bankir Association. Indonesia in the process of managing and implementing banker certification programs. 19. With the use of GARP certification materials and standards in the implementation of risk management certification in Indonesia, the risk management certificate issued by BSMR is endorsed by GARP and received recognition in a international as well as financial risk manager (FRM) certificates and other garp-issued certificates . 20. In order to update the knowledge, ability, competence, and expertise of bank administrators and officials in the field of risk management, the provisions of Bl stipulate that the owner of the risk management certificate (both regular program certificates and executive programs), are periodically required to follow refreshment programs . This means that the refreshment program is the main means for the implementation of risk management in line with the latest developments in the banking industry. The owner of the regular program certificate level I and II is required to follow the refresh program 1 time in 4 years, while the owner of the regular program certificate level III, IV and V and the certificate owner the executive program is required to follow the refreshment program 1 time in 2 years. Fulfillment of the obligations of the refreshment program can be done by participating in seminars or workshops organized by education providers (training provided) risk management which recognized by the BSMR. Development of Bank Indonesia Subsidiaries Dear Member De wan, 21. Law No. 23 of 1999 concerning Bl as amended by Law No. 3 of 2004 article 64 states that Bl can only make capital participation in legal entities or other entities that are indispensable in the performance of bl's duties and with the approval of the House. Article 77 of the Bl Law also regulates the implementation period , which is no later than 5 years after the Law is enacted. 22. To fulfill the mandate of the Act. Bl has attempted to divest Bl's participation in Bl's subsidiaries , which include PT Askrindo, PT Bahana Pembinaan Usaha Indonesia (PT BPUI) and Indover Bank. The divestment process against Indover Bank was even carried out before Law No. 23 of 1999 was enacted, namely in 1996. However, the sale of Indover bank shares was delayed due to the economic and monetary crisis that has hit Indonesia since mid-1997. 23. Until now, the progress of divestment of Bl's subsidiary is still ongoing. The divestment process of Bl's participation in PT Askrindo has been carried out through the offering of PT Askrindo's shares andthere is another shareholder, namely the Minister of State-Owned Enterprises on February 15, 2006. We can say that the authorized capital of PT Askrindo is IDR 500 billion and the paid-up capital is IDR 400 billion with a composition of Bl's ownership of 55% and the Government c.q. The Ministry of Finance by 45%. PT Askrindo's performance is quite encouraging, which is reflected in the growth of assets and profits in recent years 24. Meanwhile, the authorized capital of PT BPUI is IDR 50 billion and the paid-up capital is IDR 22.5 billion r, with Bl ownership of 82.2% and the Government c.q. The Ministry of Finance at 17.8%. The performance of PT BPUI in recent years shows encouraging conditions, which is reflected in the improvement in equity in recent years. We can say that the divestment of Bl's participation in PT BPUI was carried out after the completion of the debt restructuring process of PT BPUI. Another problem of PT BPUI that is still pending is the settlement of PT AIA's option rights to 40% ownership of PT BPUI's shares. In this case, Bl continued to explore the possibility of canceling the transfer of the shares in question and returning the option rights funds to PT AIA. 25. Another bl subsidiary is Indover Bank. Indover bank's authorized capital is EUR 90.80 million and the paid-up capital is EUR 48.03 million with 100% ownership of Bl. Indover bank's financial performance in recent years shows less than encouraging conditions, which is reflected in indover bank's losses in 2004 and 2005. As an effort to improve financial conditions, indover bank is currently conducting a restructuring program by lay-off employees to reduce operational costs. The divestment process of Bl's participation in Indover bank is being carried out with the Government through state-owned banks. Sampai is currently only PT. The Indonesian Export Bank has formally submitted a desire to acquire Indover bank. 26. Furthermore, in order to divest Bank Indonesia in the three subsidiaries, a high-level meeting was held between the Governor of Bl, Minister of State-Owned Enterprises and Minister of Finance on August 28, 2006. Some of the agreements decided between Bl and the Government are as follows: - The Government and Bl agreed to carry out the divestment of Bl's subsidiary, as mandated by Law No. 23/1999 on Bl as amended by Law No. 3/2004, to the Government, and for its implementation a Bl Subsidiary Divestment Settlement Team will be formed, with representatives from Bl. - In the event of divestment of Indover bank, the Government and Bl agreed to appoint IDX as an investor representing government banks, in accordance with applicable regulations. Dear Member De wan, 27. Such are our distinguished Mr. and Mrs. Board Members, our brief presentation on the latest banking developments, Bl banking policy especially regarding the Single Presence Policy and Risk Management Certification, as well as development of Bl's subsidiary. Ke front. Bl will continue efforts to achieve financial system stability and increase the role of banking intermediation. Meanwhile, the implementation of divestment of Bl's subsidiaries in order to fulfill the mandate stated in the Bl Law, is expected to be carried out optimally through close coordination with the Government. Jakarta, September 25th, 2006
text_original: PENJELASAN GUBERNUR BANK INDONESIA PADA RAPAT KERJA DENGAN KOMISI XI DPR Rl TANGGAL 25 SEPTEMBER 2006 <95><95><95><95><95><95><95><95><95><95><95><95><95><95> Anggota De wan yang terhormat, 1. Pertama-tama perkenankanlah kami menyampaikan terima kasih kepada Pimpinan dan Anggota Komisi XI DPR yang telah mengundang kami dalam Rapat Kerja hari ini. Sesuai dengan agenda yang kami peroleh, Rapat Kerja kali ini akan membahas mengenai Single Presence Policy (SPP), Risk Management Perbankan dan perkembangan anak perusahaan Bl. Berkaitan dengan topik hari ini, sebelum kami mendengarkan masukan, pertanyaan serta pandangan lebih lanjut dari Anggota Dewan, ijinkanlah kami untuk memaparkan secara singkat perkembangan perbankan sampai dengan bulan Juli 2006, kebijakan perbankan Bl terutama mengenai Single Presence Policy dan Sertifikasi Manajemen Risiko, yang akan dilanjutkan dengan pemaparan singkat mengenai perkembangan anak perusahaan Bl. Perkembangan dan Kinerja Perbankan Anggota De wan Yang Terhormat, 2. Memasuki paruh kedua tahun 2006, kinerja perbankan tetap menunjukkan perkembangan yang menggembirakan. Hampir seluruh indikator utama perbankan menunjukkan perkembangan positif, dan secara umum perbankan masih dapat mengatasi risiko usaha yang dihadapinya dengan baik, termasuk mengurangi tekanan terhadap tingginya biaya operasional dan kredit bermasalah. Sampai dengan akhir Juli 2006, jumlah kredit perbankan masih tetap meningkat. Total kredit yang diberikan mencapai Rp 758,4 triliun, meningkat Rp28,2 triliun dibandingkan Desember 2005, atau tumbuh sebesar 3,87%. Jumlah DPK dan total aset perbankan juga meningkat sehingga mencapai Rp 1.161,0 triliun dan Rp 1.517,1 triliun, dibandingkan akhir Desember 2005 sebesar Rp 1.127,9 triliun dan Rp 1.469,8 triliun. Dengan perkembangan tersebut, LDR perbankan meningkat dari 64,7% pada Desember 2005 menjadi 65,3% pada Juli 2006. 3. Profitabilitas perbankan pada akhir Juli 2006 relatif stabil dibandingkan akhir Desember 2005. Pendapatan bunga bersih (Nil) industri perbankan mengalami kenaikan sementara ROA justru turun tipis. Sementara itu, rasio permodalan mengalami peningkatan dari 19,5% pada akhir Desember 2005 menjadi 20,7% pada akhir Juli 2006. 4. Dari segi risiko, secara umum perbankan masih dapat mengelola risiko usaha yang dihadapinya meskipun risiko yang dihadapi masih relatif tinggi sehubungan dengan masih relatif tingginya suku bunga serta trend kenaikan suku bunga global. Risiko kredit dipandang masih cukup tinggi, terutama sehubungan belum kondusifnya iklim investasi dan dampak bencana alam di berbagai daerah. Tingginya risiko kredit tersebut tercermin dari semakin meningkatnya jumlah kredit bermasalah atau nonperforming loans (NPL). NPL baik gross maupun net meningkat masing-masing dari 8,3% dan 4,8% per akhir Desember 2005 menjadi 8,9% dan 5,2% pada Juli 2006. Sementara itu, daya tahan perbankan dalam menghadapi risiko likuiditas dinilai memadai. Kebijakan Bank Indonesia di Bidang Perbankan Anggota Dewan yang Terhormat, 5. Kinerja perbankan dimaksud tidak terlepas dari kebijakan yang telah ditempuh Bank Indonesia di bidang perbankan. Selama semester 1-2006, kebijakan Bl tetap difokuskan untuk memperkuat stabilitas sistem perbankan guna menciptakan stabilitas sistem keuangan dan mendorong fungsi intermediasi perbankan. Kebijakan tersebut ditempuh melalui implementasi program-program yang telah dicanangkan dalam Arsitektur Perbankan Indonesia (API). Selanjutnya untuk jangka menengah panjang, peraturan dan ketentuan Bl akan tetap difokuskan pada upaya penguatan sendi-sendi operasional perbankan dan penerapan prinsip kehati-hatian. Dengan demikian diharapkan pada akhir tahun 2010 akan terbentuk suatu industri perbankan Indonesia yang lebih berketahanan, berdaya saing di lingkungan global dan bermanfaat dalam proses pembangunan ekonomi Indonesia. 6. Untuk dapat mewujudkan industri perbankan sesuai dengan visi tersebut. Bl menempuh beberapa strategi kebijakan yang penerapannya dilakukan secara gradual dengan menyesuaikan pada dinamika yang terjadi dalam industri perbankan nasional. Untuk mendapatkan sebuah industri perbankan yang sehat, kokoh, efektif dan bermanfaat bagi seluruh masyarakat. Bank Indonesia memandang program API pilar 1 - Penguatan Struktur Perbankan Indonesia, melalui proses konsolidasi adalah suatu keharusan. Dalam 2 tahun terakhir ini, upaya untuk mengkonsolidasikan industri perbankan dimaksud telah ditempuh dengan menerapkan 2 strategi kebijakan penguatan yang hingga saat ini masih terus berlangsung prosesnya. Pertama. di tahun 2005 lalu. Bank Indonesia telah menerbitkan ketentuan permodalan bagi industri perbankan nasional yang menetapkan jumlah modal minimum yang harus dimiliki oleh bank pada tahun 2010 adalah Rp. 100 milyar. Pemenuhan jummlah modal minimum tersebut dapat dilakukan secara bertahap oleh setiap bank dengan pencapaian target jumlah modal interim sebesar Rp. 80 milyar pada akhir tahun 2007 mendatang. Kedua. Bl juga telah menggariskan kebijakan untuk menetapkan adanya Bank dengan Kinerja Baik (BKB) atau dikenal pula dengan sebutan Anchor Bank yang diharapkan akan mampu menjadi tumpuan dalam konsolidasi melalui proses akusisi pada bank-bank kecil. 7. Penerapan kedua strategi kebijakan tersebut hingga saat masih terus diupayakan, terutama dengan lebih memberikan penekanan dalam pelaksanaan proses pengawasan. Selanjutnya, agar upaya penataan dan penguatan struktur industri perbankan yang diinginkan dapat terjadi di semua level, maka pada tahun 2006 ini Bl juga menggariskan kebijakan yang ketiga. yaitu kebijakan kepemilikan tunggal (single presence policy) bagi perbankan Indonesia. Sebagaimana telah kami umumkan pada beberapa waktu yang lalu, diharapkan kebijakan ini akan dapat mendorong konsolidasi dalam strategi usaha perbankan, sekaligus pula menata aspek persaingan usaha di industri perbankan sendiri. Dengan langkah ini, peningkatan efisiensi industri perbankan secara keseluruhan juga akan dapat dioptimalkan. Dalam hal terjadi merger diantara bank-bank yang dimiliki suatu kelompok usaha yang sama, maka potensi dan kemampuan pembiayaan bank akan semakin besar karena batas maksimum pemberian kredit (BMPK)nya akan meningkat sejalan dengan kenaikan jumlah modalnya. Kerjasama sindikasi pembiayaan pun akan dapat dengan mudah terbentuk, jika strategi usaha bank-bank yang berada dalam satu kelompok kepemilikan dikendalikan secara terkonsolidasi. 8. Dari segi pengawasan bank, kebijakan kepemilikan tunggal kami pandang sangat efektif untuk mendukung upaya Bank Indonesia dalam menyempurnakan sistem pengawasan bank menuju ke pendekatan pengawasan berdasarkan risiko secara terkonsolidasi (consolidated supervision). Komunikasi antara otoritas pengawas dengan pengendali bank menjadi lebih lancar mengingat adanya single point of contact, yang pada gilirannya akan meningkatkan fungsi monitoring Bl. Secara teknis, laporan keuangan bank yang dikonsolidasikan adalah media yang sangat efektif dalam memetakan seluruh eksposure risiko bank dan seluruh anak perusahaan keuangan yang berada dalam satu naungan kepemilikan. 9. Kebijakan Kepemilikan Tunggal pada Perbankan Indonesia yang akan kami terbitkan pada dasarnya mengatur bahwa setiap pihak hanya dapat menjadi pemegang saham pengendali (PSP) pada satu bank. Adapun PSP yang saat ini telah memiliki lebih dari satu bank, diberikan alternatif yang dapat ditempuh untuk menyesuaikan struktur kepemilikannya, yaitu melalui pengurangan kepemilikan saham sehingga yang bersangkutan hanya menjadi PSP pada satu bank, menggabungkan bank-bank yang dimilikinya baik melalui merger atau konsolidasi, atau dengan membentuk perusahaan induk (Bank Holding Company - BHC) di Indonesia untuk membawahi bank-bank yang dimilikinya. Kebijakan kepemilikan tunggal tersebut diharapkan telah dapat diimplementasikan secara penuh pada tahun 2010. 10. Penetapan tahun 2010 sebagai batas waktu pelaksanaan kebijakan kepemilikan tunggal pada hakekatnya tidak terlepas dari kerangka waktu implementasi API tahun 2010. Sedari awal. Bl melihat bahwa tahun 2010 adalah tahun dimana seluruh program penyehatan dan penguatan industri perbankan yang diupayakan selama ini akan dapat memberikan hasil sebagaimana yang diharapkan. Sebuah industri perbankan yang sehat, kokoh, efisien dan bermanfaat bagi seluruh masyarakat. Adapun tahun 2008 yang pernah kami sampaikan terdahulu merupakan sebuah target antara atau milestone yang diperlukan dalam mengarahkan perjalanan industri perbankan menuju tahun 2010. Di tahun itu, industri perbankan kiranya perlu mengevaluasi berbagai proses persiapan yang telah dan masih harus dilakukan untuk mewujudkan komitmen terhadap alternatif yang dipilih. 11. Kami memahami bahwa 3 alternatif yang kami tawarkan untuk dipilih oleh industri perbankan bukanlah hal yang sederhana. Oleh karena itu. Bl senantiasa terbuka untuk berdiskusi dan bertukar pikiran secara intensif dengan berbagai pihak yang terkait. Pemahaman dan pengertian para pihak melalui proses kerjasama dan koordinasi adalah kunci keberhasilan kebijakan ini. Dalam hal ini, kami menilai penetapan alternatif langkah yang akan ditempuh secara dini akan sangat bermanfaat untuk memberikan waktu yang cukup di dalam melakukan persiapan. Bl akan senantiasa akomodatif dan siap membantu memfasilitasi keseluruhan proses, mulai dari penyusunan rencana bisnis sampai dengan proses implementasinya. Dalam waktu dekat, SPP ini kami rencanakan untuk dapat segera diterbitkan dalam bentuk guidelines yang dapat memberikan tuntunan bagi perbankan di dalam melakukan konsolidasi. 12. Penerbitan arahan dan petunjuk pelaksanaan SPP dimaksud akan diikuti pula dengan penerbitan beberapa ketentuan perbankan lain yang bertujuan untuk memberikan ruang gerak yang lebih luas bagi industri dalam menjalankan fungsinya. Bl sebagai lembaga publik menyadari sepenuhnya bahwa untuk dapat keluar dari belitan permasalahan yang ada, bangsa ini membutuhkan kontribusi dan peran serta dari seluruh elemennya. Sejak beberapa waktu belakangan ini Bl terus mencoba mencari dan mengkaji semua kemungkinan yang dapat dilakukan untuk mendinamisasikan perekonomian bangsa, tanpa harus mengorbankan kestabilan yang telah diraih saat ini. Berbagai ketentuan perbankan yang ada kami review untuk menemukan kemungkinan-kemungkinan tersebut. Saat ini kami telah menyelesaikan proses penyesuaian PBI mengenai BMPK, dan Good Corporate Governance yang diharapkan akan dapat memberikan ruang gerak yang lebih leluasa bagi perbankan di dalam menjalankan fungsi intermediasinya. Selain itu, kami juga tengah memasuki tahap akhir penyusunan PBI mengenai kebijakan perbankan di wilayah bencana, pemberian insentif dalam proses merger dan berbagai kebijakan lain yang kami pandang relevan dengan kebutuhan bangsa saat ini. Semua aturan dan ketentuan tersebut, diharapkan akan dapat diselesaikan dalam waktu dekat, dan selanjutnya dapat diterbitkan sebagai sebuah paket kebijakan bidang perbankan. Anggota De wan yang Terhormat, 13. Dalam rangka meningkatkan kualitas manajemen dan operasional perbankan serta sebagai implementasi dari Pilar 4 API, Bl telah menerbitkan peraturan mengenai sertifikasi manajemen risiko bagi pengurus dan pejabat umum bank. Ketentuan ini pada intinya bertujuan untuk memberikan standar kompetensi bagi pengurus dan pejabat bank umum dalam mengelola risiko yang dihadapi pada kegiatan operasional perbankan sehari-hari. Standar kompetensi menjadi penting mengingat fungsi intermediasi yang dilakukan bank memerlukan adanya keterampilan dan keahlian yang memadai dalam pengelolaan penghimpunan maupun penyaluran dana sehingga risiko-risiko yang terkait dengan pelaksanaan kegiatan usaha bank dapat diantisipasi dan dikelola dengan baik. 14. Untuk mewujudkan sumber daya perbankan yang memiliki kompetensi yang dipersyaratkan, sertifikasi manajemen risiko dilakukan dalam 5 (lima) tingkat yang dilaksanakan secara berjenjang dan penerapannya disesuaikan dengan skala usaha dan kompleksitas bank serta jenjang jabatan pengurus dan pejabat bank, program sertifikasi yang berjenjang ini disebut sebagai program reguler. Sertifikasi ini dilaksanakan sesuai dengan standar internasional yang digunakan oleh Global Association of Risk Professionals (GARP), suatu lembaga independen nirlaba di bidang manajemen risiko yang didirikan oleh risk professionals dari berbagai negara. Penggunaan standar dan kerjasama dengan GARP ini merupakan hal yang krusial karena pada saat ini belum ada lembaga/organisasi yang melaksanakan sertifikasi manajemen risiko dengan standar kualitas yang setara dengan standar-standar internasional. 15. Sebelum melakukan program reguler, terdapat kebutuhan untuk menyamakan persepsi pemahaman dari bankir yang pada saatnya akan mengikuti program reguler yang diikuti oleh pimpinan puncak dan komisaris bank masing-masing. Atas dasar kebutuhan ini, diadakan program fast-track bagi direksi dan komisaris bank umum, yang dilaksanakan dengan metoda workshop secara singkat namun komprehensif, dengan tujuan untuk memberikan pemahaman mendasar kepada pengurus bank. 16. Kewajiban untuk memiliki sertifikat manajemen risiko bagi pengurus dan pejabat bank berdasarkan ketentuan tersebut akan berlaku efektif pada tanggal 3 Agustus 2010 dan hal tersebut akan menjadi salah satu persyaratan administratif dalam uji kepatutan dan kelayakan (fit & proper test) bagi pengurus dan pejabat eksekutif bank umum. Dalam hal ini, pengurus dan pejabat bank yang tidak memiliki sertifikat manajemen risiko mulai tanggal 3 Agustus 2010 tidak diperkenankan lagi menduduki jabatannya. 17. Untuk mendukung pelaksanaan sertifikasi manajemen risiko sebagaimana dipersyaratkan ketentuan tersebut, Indonesian of Risk Professional Association (IRPA) dan Federation Indonesian Association of Banks (FIAB) kemudian mendirikan suatu lembaga sertifikasi profesi yang kemudian dikenal sebagai Badan Sertifikasi Manajemen Risiko (BSMR). Lembaga ini telah terdaftar pada Badan Nasional Sertifikasi Profesi (BNSP) sebagai lembaga yang memiliki kewenangan untuk melakukan sertifikasi manajemen risiko perbankan. 18. Selanjutnya mengingat keberadaan lembaga sertifikasi profesi ini sangat penting bagi peningkatan kualitas sumber daya manusia di industri perbankan, maka Bank Indonesia memberikan dukungan sementara kepada BSMR dalam bentuk penyediaan fasilitas kerja di kompleks perkantoran Bank Indonesia. Pada waktunya nanti BSMR didorong akan memiliki tempatnya sendiri. Sebagaimana niat awal pada saat pendiriannya, ke depan BSMR juga akan bekerja sama dan berkoordinasi secara intensif dengan asosiasi profesi bankir yang ada yaitu Ikatan Bankir Indonesia di dalam proses pengelolaan dan pelaksanaan program-program sertifikasi bankir. 19. Dengan digunakannya materi dan standar sertifikasi GARP dalam pelaksanaan sertifikasi manajemen risiko di Indonesia, maka sertifikat manajemen risiko yang diterbitkan oleh BSMR di-endorse oleh GARP dan mendapat pengakuan secara internasional sebagaimana halnya sertifikat Financial Risk Manager (FRM) dan sertifikat lainnya yang diterbitkan GARP. 20. Dalam rangka mengkinikan pengetahuan, kemampuan, kompetensi, dan keahlian pengurus dan pejabat bank dalam bidang manajemen risiko, ketentuan Bl menetapkan bahwa pemilik sertifikat manajemen risiko (baik sertifikat program reguler maupun program eksekutif), secara periodik diwajibkan mengikuti program penyegaran. Hal ini mengingat program penyegaran merupakan sarana utama bagi terlaksananya penerapan manajemen risiko yang sejalan dengan perkembangan terkini di industri perbankan. Pemilik sertifikat program reguler tingkat I dan II wajib mengikuti program penyegaran 1 kali dalam 4 tahun, sedangkan pemilik sertifikat program reguler tingkat III, IV dan V serta pemilik sertifikat program eksekutif wajib mengikuti program penyegaran 1 kali dalam 2 tahun. Pemenuhan kewajiban program penyegaran tersebut dapat dilakukan dengan mengikuti seminar atau workshop yang diselenggarakan oleh penyelenggara pendidikan (training provided) manajemen risiko yang diakui oleh BSMR. Perkembangan Anak Perusahaan Bank Indonesia Anggota De wan yang Terhormat, 21. UU No. 23 tahun 1999 tentang Bl sebagaimana diubah dengan UU No. 3 tahun 2004 pasal 64 menyatakan bahwa Bl hanya dapat melakukan penyertaan modal pada badan hukum atau badan lainnya yang sangat diperlukan dalam pelaksanaan tugas Bl dan dengan persetujuan DPR. Pasal 77 UU Bl tersebut juga mengatur jangka waktu pelaksanaan yaitu selambat-lambatnya 5 tahun sejak UU diberlakukan. 22. Untuk memenuhi amanat UU tersebut. Bl telah berupaya melakukan divestasi terhadap penyertaan Bl pada anak perusahaan Bl, yang meliputi PT Askrindo, PT Bahana Pembinaan Usaha Indonesia (PT BPUI) serta Indover Bank. Proses divestasi terhadap Indover Bank bahkan telah dilakukan sebelum UU No. 23 tahun 1999 diberlakukan, yaitu pada tahun 1996. Namun penjualan saham Indover bank tersebut tertunda akibat krisis ekonomi dan moneter yang melanda Indonesia sejak pertengahan tahun 1997. 23. Sampai saat ini, progress divestasi terhadap anak perusahaan Bl masih terus berlangsung. Proses divestasi penyertaan Bl pada PT Askrindo telah dilaksanakan melalui penawaran saham PT Askrindo kepada pemegang saham yang lain yaitu Menteri Negara BUMN pada tanggal 15 Februari 2006. Dapat kami sampaikan bahwa modal dasar PT Askrindo adalah sebesar Rp500 miliar dan modal disetor sebesar Rp400 miliar dengan komposisi kepemilikan Bl sebesar 55% dan Pemerintah c.q. Departemen Keuangan sebesar 45%. Kinerja PT Askrindo cukup menggembirakan yang tercermin dari pertumbuhan aset dan laba beberapa tahun terakhir 24. Sementara itu, modal dasar PT BPUI adalah sebesar Rp50 miliar dan modal disetor sebesar Rp22,5 miliar, dengan kepemilikan Bl sebesar 82,2% dan Pemerintah c.q. Departemen Keuangan sebesar 17,8%. Kinerja PT BPUI beberapa tahun terakhir menunjukkan kondisi yang menggembirakan yang tercermin dari membaiknya ekuitas dalam beberapa tahun terakhir. Dapat kami sampaikan bahwa pelaksanaan divestasi penyertaan Bl pada PT BPUI dilakukan setelah selesainya proses restrukturisasi hutang PT BPUI. Permasalahan PT BPUI lainnya yang masih pending adalah penyelesaian hak opsi PT AIA terhadap kepemilikan 40% saham PT BPUI. Dalam hal ini Bl tetap menjajagi kemungkinan untuk membatalkan pengalihan saham dimaksud dan mengembalikan dana hak opsi kepada PT AIA. 25. Anak perusahaan Bl lainnya adalah Indover Bank. Modal dasar Indover bank adalah sebesar EUR 90.80 juta dan modal disetor mencapai EUR 48.03 juta dengan kepemilikan Bl sebesar 100%. Kinerja keuangan Indover bank beberapa tahun terakhir menunjukkan kondisi yang kurang menggembirakan, yang tercermin dari ruginya Indover bank pada tahun 2004 dan 2005. Sebagai upaya memperbaiki kondisi keuangan, saat ini Indover bank melakukan program restrukturisasi dengan melakukan lay-off pegawai untuk menurunkan biaya operasional. Proses divestasi penyertaan Bl pada Indover bank sedang dilakukan dengan pihak Pemerintah melalui bank BUMN. Sampai saat ini hanya PT. Bank Ekspor Indonesia yang telah mengajukan secara resmi keinginan untuk mengakuisisi Indover bank. 26. Selanjutnya, dalam rangka divestasi Bank Indonesia pada ketiga anak perusahaan, telah dilakukan high level meeting antara Gubernur Bl, Meneg BUMN dan Menkeu pada tanggal 28 Agustus 2006. Beberapa kesepakatan yang diputuskan antara Bl dan Pemerintah sebagai berikut: - Pemerintah dan Bl sepakat untuk melaksanakan divestasi anak perusahaan Bl, sebagaimana diamanatkan oleh UU No. 23/1999 tentang Bl sebagaimana telah diubah dengan UU No. 3/2004, kepada Pemerintah, dan untuk pelaksanaannya akan dibentuk Tim Penyelesaian Divestasi Anak Perusahaan Bl, dengan wakil dari Bl. - Dalam hal divestasi Indover bank, Pemerintah dan Bl sepakat untuk menunjuk BEI sebagai investor yang mewakili bank pemerintah, sesuai dengan ketentuan yang berlaku. Anggota De wan yang terhormat, 27. Demikianlah Bapak dan Ibu Anggota Dewan yang terhormat, paparan singkat kami mengenai perkembangan perbankan terkini, kebijakan perbankan Bl terutama mengenai Single Presence Policy dan Sertifikasi Manajemen Risiko, serta perkembangan anak perusahaan Bl. Ke depan. Bl akan terus melanjutkan upaya pencapaian stabilitas sistem keuangan dan peningkatan peran intermediasi perbankan. Sementara itu, pelaksanaan divestasi terhadap anak perusahaan Bl dalam rangka pemenuhan amanat yang tercantum dalam UU Bl, diharapkan akan terlaksana secara optimal melalui koordinasi yang erat dengan Pemerintah. Jakarta, 25 September 2006

Title: Pidato Deputi Gubernur, S. Budi Rochadi pada Penandatanganan Perjanjian Kerjasama Antara Departemen Kelautan Dan Perikanan Dan Bank Indonesia
text: REMARKS BY THE DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF BANK INDONESIA SIGNING OF COOPERATION AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE MINISTRY OF MARITIME AFFAIRS AND FISHERIES AND BANK INDONESIAJAKARTA, AUGUST 26, 2009 Which I Respect: - Director General of the Directorate General of Processing and Marketing of Fishery Products, Sdr. Martani Huseini, - Officials within the Department of Marine Affairs and Fisheries - Banking leaders - Chairman of the KKMB Task Force for the Marine and Fisheries Sector - KKMB , Happy Audience Assalamu alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh, and peace be upon us all First of all let us say praise and gratitude to the presence of Allah Almighty because with His mercy and grace on this occasion we can be together present to carry out an activity that is pent ing, namely the signing of a Cooperation Agreement between the Directorate General of Processing and Marketing of Fishery Products - Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries with Bank Indonesia on Consultant Development Finance/Assistance to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises of Bank Partners (KKMB) and Preparation of a Book of Financing Patterns for Marine and Fisheries Sector Products/Services. This activity is a follow-up to the implementation of the Joint Agreement between the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries and Bank Indonesia which was signed on 14th April 2009. This cooperation agreement will be a framework that will keep the efforts we make to support MSMEs run in a directed, effective and efficient. Our exalted sirs, Improving people's lives through increasing income and employment opportunities is the end of every effort we make in the economic field. At present, the path we must take to achieve such noble ideals does not seem to be easy. The slowdown in the growth of the global and domestic economy in 2009, has implications for the lack of sufficient employment for the entire existing labor force. To overcome this, it requires hard work, perseverance, cooperation, direction, and priorities that are not sufficient in development. The selection of a short-term policy strategy appropriately, without having to lose direction and a long-term vision is an important aspect that must be formulated immediately. The development of the MSME sector is a choice of alternative short-term solutions that are believed to be effective in providing jobs and answering the problem of high unemployment rates which in turn are expected able to reduce poverty. The experience of this nation proves that MSMEs with their various distinctive content characteristics, are able to play a role in maintaining social and economic stability by becoming an economic safety net in times of crisis without having to be given subsidies by the Government. Data from the Central Bureau of Statistics (BPS) 2008 shows that the number of MSMEs in Indonesia is 51.3 million units or 99.9% of the total business units in Indonesia, with employment reaching 90.9 million workers employment or 97.04% of the total labor force. The contribution of this sector also in the formation of GDP is very significant, which is more than 55.6%. The amount of attention to the potential of MSMEs lately has also been observed by international banks, which have begun to look at MSMEs in Indonesia as a potential sector that has market share big and hasn't been worked on much. They aggressively began to develop and explore micro financing outlets as an effort to penetrate the market. Ladies and Gentlemen whom I respect, The development of bank lending to MSMEs, until now, still shows the development of meningkat with the annual financing ratio ranging from 49% - 51% of total bank loans or reaching Rp 700.8 trillion. However, around 52.8% of MSME loans are still given in the form of consumption loans. As for business capital, MSMEs still rely on their own capital or the help of relatives and have not been touched much by banks. The largest distribution of MSME loans was focused on the trade sector with a share of 25.6%, while to the Agricultural sector it only reached 3.3%, including the subsector fisheries whose share is only 9%. This development shows that there is still low or suboptimal financing to the Agricultural Sector, including the Fisheries sub-sector. 2008 BPS data also shows that of the existing 51.3 million MSMEs, around 15.42 million are included in the feasible category, but not yet bankable. From the MSME side, the reasons revolve around the inability to provide collateral (for micro-enterprises) and the fear that banks will charge high interest rates (for small businesses and intermediate). From the banking side, they see other things as a barrier to credit flow to MSMEs. Banks see that MSMEs are still facing business feasibility problems, both regarding financial aspects and marketing and labor aspects. Therefore, the development of the MSME sector requires efforts to overcome this asymmetric information. This is where Financial Consultants/MSME Companions of Bank Partners (KKMB) can reduce asymmetric information by becoming a "link" between MSMEs and banks. The empowerment of KKMB in the marine and fisheries sector, which we will strive for together through this cooperation agreement, I hope to bridge the mutually beneficial relationship between MSMEs and banks. Kam i also hopes that the KKMB that has been trained, can immediately foster MSMEs in the marine and fisheries sector, making them bankable, able to obtain the banking credit they need as well as keeping the return smooth. Father, Mother and attendees whom I respect Bank Indonesia's commitment to the development and empowerment of MSMEs, as one of the important priorities, will continue to be carried out. Almost all forms of discourse and thought formulation carried out through discussions, seminars, workshops, and even surveys, research and information provision have been carried out by Bank Indonesia. Various programs that are direct or indirect have also been aimed at the MSME sector, such as: KKMB as it is today. Linkage of BPR and Commercial Bank Programs, facilitators of foreign assistance for the development of MSMEs, Bazaar of banking-MSME intermediation, as well as facilitation of the establishment of a pilot project for the MSME cluster and Indonesian Business Information Data (DIBI). In line with the KKMB empowerment strategy, Bank Indonesia, within the framework of the Technical Assistance, since 2003 has provided training to KKMB and the establishment of several pilot projects of training institutions in Bandung, Surabaya, Jakarta, Semarang, Banjarmasin and Makassar. Besides. Bank Indonesia initiated the establishment of the KKMB Task Force in several provinces consisting of local governments, banks and local Bank Indonesia. This task force, in addition to providing training, is also a means to introduce KKMB to local banks. From 2005 to the first semester of 2009, Bank Indonesia has provided training to 3217 KKMB with accumulated credit disbursements through KKMB amounting to Rp.1.2 trillion involving 1,446 bank offices with the number of MSMEs is 50,114. In addition to Bank Indonesia's efforts to develop KKMB, there are severaleras of internal obstacles to KKMB that need to be considered for optimality of its role. First, KKMB must understand and understand the business being accompanied. Second, KKMB is not a side job. Third, KKMB must try to proactively pick up the ball, looking for business projects that can be connected to the bank. Fourth, related to the existence of fees (fees) to KKMB which are considered burdensome for MSMEs, it is necessary to think of a solution to replace it, for example by using banking social activity (CSR) funds or government agencies. Besides. banks are expected to be willing to open themselves to cooperate with KKMB and do not consider KKMB as a competitor of the bank's Account Officer. Banks can take advantage of the KKMB Task Force as a means to select KKMB who have performed well in starting their cooperation. In addition to training, bank Indonesia's technical assistance is also provided through the preparation of a lending model for superior commodities. As of 2008, Bank Indonesia has issued a financing pattern of 103 commodities, including 30 commodities for the marine and fisheries sector. To support the rapid development of Islamic financial institutions in recent years . Bank Indonesia has also published a book on the pattern of financing yaan with the sharia system, including nursery cultivation and gourami farming and enlargement. Father Mother and Attendees, That's all I can say. Before closing, allow me to twist the words from Prahalad in his book "Fortune at the Bottom of Pyramid: Eradicating Poverty Through Profits": "If we stop thinking of the poor as victims or as a burden and start recognising them as resilient and creative entrepreneurs, a whole new world of opportunity will open up". This message is not for bankers, or microfinance institutions, but reminds all of us, governments, entrepreneurs, NGOs, and MSME activists, that the potential in the sector is "bottom of "it's huge and very significant for economic growth and employment. And this is what this Cooperation Agreement is for. Thus my welcome, may Allah Almighty endow the good steps that we are and will take. Wassalamu'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh. Jakarta, August 26th, 2009 Bank Indonesia DR. S. Budi Rochadi Deputy Governor
text_original: SAMBUTAN DEPUTI GUBERNUR BANK INDONESIA PENANDATANGANAN PERJANJIAN KERJASAMA ANTARA DEPARTEMEN KELAUTAN DAN PERIKANAN DAN BANK INDONESIA JAKARTA, 26 AGUSTUS 2009 Yang Saya Hormati: - Direktur Jenderal Direktorat Jenderal Pengolahan dan Pemasaran Hasil Perikanan, Sdr. Martani Huseini, - Pejabat di lingkungan Departemen Kelautan dan Perikanan - Para pimpinan perbankan - Ketua Satuan Tugas KKMB sektor Kelautan dan Perikanan - Para KKMB, Hadirin yang berbahagia Assalamu alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh, dam salam sejahtera untuk kita semua Pertama-tama marilah kita mengucapkan puji dan syukur ke hadirat Allah SWT karena dengan rahmat dan karunia-Nya pada kesempatan ini kita dapat bersama-sama hadir untuk melaksanakan sebuah kegiatan yang penting, yakni penandatanganan Perjanjian Kerjasama antara Direktorat Jenderal Pengolahan dan Pemasaran Hasil Perikanan - Departemen Kelautan dan Perikanan dengan Bank Indonesia tentang Pengembangan Konsultan Keuangan/Pendamping Usaha Mikro, Kecil dan Menengah Mitra Bank (KKMB) dan Penyusunan Buku Pola Pembiayaan Produk/Jasa Sektor Kelautan dan Perikanan. Kegiatan ini merupakan tindak lanjut pelaksanaan Kesepakatan Bersama antara Departemen Kelautan dan Perikanan dengan Bank Indonesia yang telah ditandatangani tanggal 14 April 2009 yang lalu. Perjanjian kerjasama ini akan menjadi sebuah kerangka kerja yang akan menjaga agar upaya yang kita lakukan untuk mendukung UMKM berjalan secara terarah, efektif dan efisien. Bapak-lbu yang kami muliakan, Meningkatkan taraf hidup rakyat melalui peningkatan pendapatan dan kesempatan kerja merupakan ujung dari setiap upaya yang kita lakukan di bidang perekonomian. Saat ini, jalan yang harus kita tempuh untuk mencapai cita-cita mulia tersebut tampaknya tidak mudah. Perlambatan pertumbuhan ekonomi global dan domestik di tahun 2009 ini, berimplikasi pada tidak cukup tersedianya lapangan pekerjaan bagi seluruh angkatan kerja yang ada. Guna mengatasi hal ini, diperlukan kerja keras, ketekunan, kerja sama, arah, serta prioritas yang jelas dalam pembangunan.
