Title: Sambutan Gubernur Bank Indonesia, Darmin Nasution pada Rapat Koordinasi Nasional (Rakornas) Tim Pengendalian Inflasi Daerah (TPID) kedua, 16 Maret 2011, di Jakarta
text: REMARKS BY THE GOVERNOR OF BANK INDONESIA , DR. DARMIN NASUTION OPENING OF THE NATIONAL COORDINATION MEETING OF THE REGIONAL INFLATION CONTROL TEAM 2011JAKARTA, 16 MARCH 2011 Dear Vice President of the Republic of Indonesia, Prof. Dr. Boediono Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs, Minister of finance Minister of Home Affairs, Minister of Agriculture, Chairman of the Inflation and Interest Rate Committee, Commission XI of the House of Representatives of the Republic of Indonesia, Speakers and Moderators, Governors, Regents, Mayors and Leaders of Bank Indonesia in the regions, as well as happy invitees, Assa/amu'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh, Sela mat pagi and peace be upon us all, 1. On this sunny morning, let us together offer praise and gratitude to God Almighty, for for for his mercy and blessings we da pat gather together in the event of the Meeting National Coordination of Regional Inflation Control Team in 2011. We would like to express our deepest gratitude for the approval of Mr. Vice President to attend with all of us; We would like to thank all the attendees who were able to attend this event. Happy Ladies and Gentlemen, 2. The TPID National Coordination Meeting this time is the second time, after in 2010 in Bali the first TPID Rakornas was held. The implementation of the TPID National Coordination Meeting this time is the result of excellent cooperation between Bank Indonesia, the Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs and the Ministry of Home Affairs. At the time of the first TPID National Coordination Meeting, there were 38 national inflation-forming cities that already had a Team or Forum for Coordination of National Development and Inflation Control, or commonly called TPID. Regarding the development of TPID, let me convey on this occasion to the Vice President, that as of today, out of a total of 66 cities that are the basis for calculating inflation in Indonesia by the Central Statistics Agency, TPIDs have been formed in 55 cities with 32 of them being provincial capitals. 3. The rapid increase in the number of TPIDs formed in the last 1 year shows the magnitude of attention, awareness, concern and commitment of regional heads to the importance of efforts to realize price sta bi litas in the regions. For this reason, on this good occasion, we would like to express our highest appreciation to local governments and other stakeholders in the regions, for the various active efforts made in order to support the realization of price stability and control regional inflation in particular. Father and Mother whom I respect, 4. The central theme raised at the second National Coordination Meeting was "Optimization of Handling Problems of Production, Supply and Distribution of Strategic Food Commodities in order to Support Price Stability and National Food Security". I view that this national coordination meeting has an important meaning and is a momentum to further strengthen policy coordination and synergy between the Central Government, Regional Governments and Bank Indonesia in order to support the creation of price stability. 5. In this regard, the objectives of organizing the 2011 TPID National Coordination Meeting II include: a. mem ba ng un communication and trust {building trust) as well as developing a network of {networking) between fellow TPIDs. b. strengthening vertical coordination, namely coordination and cooperation between the central and regional governments, as well as horizontal coordination, namely between local governments and between related institutions both at the central level and regions, in support of the realization of price stabilization. c. discusses and discusses solutions/follow-ups related to the supply, distribution and market structure of food commodities in the regions. d. discusses efforts to increase agricultural production capacity in the regions, especially strategic food commodities, as well as anticipatory measures taken by local governments to face weather anomalous conditions that still potentially occurring in 2011, and the threat of global inflation is getting stronger. Happy Ladies and Gentlemen, 6. The theme of the National Coordination Meeting this time is also very strategic and relevant to the challenges faced by the national economy in the future, especially in facing the potential threat of inflationary pressures both from global and domestic. Therefore, on this occasion, let me briefly convey the latest developments in the economy and the challenges that we will face some time in the future. 7. We should be grateful that in 2010, the performance of the national economy in general was quite encouraging. Economic growth achieved 6.1%/ accompanied by an increase in investment and exports, thus supporting more balanced growth compared to the previous year. The balance of payments posted a surplus of USD 30.2 billion. For the record, as of March 10, 2011, foreign exchange reserves reached USD 102.02 billion. Meanwhile, the financial system has been maintained amidst the increasingly dynamic global financial markets after the crisis. 8. Bank Indonesia is optimistic that economic gains will continue. 2011 is going to be a very promising year. Various indicators show that sources of economic growth continue to improve in a balanced manner; depends not only on consumption but also exports and investments. The opportunity to achieve higher growth is wide open with Indonesia just one level away from the {investmentgrade} investment-worthy zone. 9. Even so, 2011 will also be more challenging for macro policy management, especially inflation control policies, after last year CPI inflation reached 6.96% or above target 5%b11%. Although the high inflation is mainly sourced from wishfulthinking is a problem faced by many countries, but our inflation is also still higher than other countries in the region. Happy Ladies and Gentlemen, 10. The challenges of controlling inflation have become increasingly severe with the continued increase in commodity prices in the international market, including the prices of wheat, sugar and soybeans. Bank Indonesia considers the risk of future inflationary pressures stemming from the risk of disruption of food supply is still quite high. If not handled anticipatoryly and adequately, sustainable food inflationary pressures may affect commodity prices in the core inflation group, either directly or indirectly. On the other hand, we also need to anticipate climate change that will disrupt the domestic food supply. 11. On the monetary side, Bank Indonesia has implemented various policies since last year in order to control inflationary pressures. Tight monetary policy signals were further strengthened by an increase in the BI rate by 25 bps to 6.75% in early February 2011. The decision to hold the BI rate in March 2011 did not change the direction of Bank Indonesia's monetary policy. In addition, Bank Indonesia has also provided room for rupiah exchange rate appreciation in line with capital inflows that have increased again. The strengthening of the Rupiah helped to ease inflationary pressures from the external side (imported inflation}, while taking into account the competitiveness of Indonesia's exports. Bank Indonesia also implements macroprudential policy in order to manage capital inflows while controlling economic liquidity. 12. The magnitude of the inflation risk stemming from supply disruptions implies that controlling inflation cannot rest entirely solely on monetary policy, but requires a policy that is strenuous. as an integration of monetary, fiscal, and sectoral policies across all fronts and levels. 13. In this regard, I am of the view that the cooperation between the Government and the Bank through the Inflation Control Team, both at the central level (TPI) which has been initiated since 2005 and the regions (TPID) since the year 2008 was an embodiment of a very important cohesion. Given their very strategic role, TPI and TPID need to continue to be strengthened in institutional aspects and coordination. 14. This is very important considering the role of regional inflation in the formation of considerable national inflation. By removing the weight of Jakarta's inflation, the role of regional inflation reaches around 77%. In addition, considering that the contributors to inflation in each region are quite unik, it needs special handling adjusted to the conditions of each region. 15. In order to make their functions more tangible, TPI and TPID are no longer enough just as a forum for exchanging information, but need to be directed to sharpen the implementation of various work programs focused on supply-side improvements , particularly food commodities, through improved production, distribution, industrial organization, and market structure, including trade arrangements. Happy Ladies and Gentlemen, 16. By looking at the latest developments, I see that there are three strategic things that should be discussed TPID National Coordination Meeting this time. First, it is necessary for each region to prepare an action plan to face the threat of rising food prices. Various anticipatory measures immediately {immediate policies} need to be prepared immediately , especially regarding the handling of supply problems and the flow of distribution of goods. Increasing food production through extensification and intensification is an important issue amid the factors of extreme weather conditions and are increasingly difficult to predict. 17. Second, oerlunva improves cross-institutional coordination as one of the necessary prerequisites to support the effectiveness of various price stability policies. In this connection, we need to formulate a strategy that can be used to further encourage the strengthening of synergistic and effective institutional relationships. 18. Third, the need to formulate a policy strategy with medium-long-term dimensions to improve the organization of industry and market structure, including trade arrangements, especially food commodities; and accelerating efforts to increase economic capacity. 19. These various strategic issues will be on the agenda of the first day of this National Coordination Meeting. I can report to Mr. Vice President that the National Coordination Meeting on the first day was attended by the surroundings 300 participants, including all regional heads based in 66 cities, were sampled for the calculation of national inflation. Furthermore, the National Coordination Meeting on the second day will enter into a technical implementation discussion, and will be attended by around 150 participants representing each TPID, both local government officials and regional Bank Indonesia offices. 20. As one of the tangible manifestations of steps to strengthen cross-institutional coordination to support price stability and increase Economic capacity, this morning will also be signed two texts of cooperation between the Government and Bank Indonesia. First, a Memorandum of Understanding between the Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs and the Ministry of Home Affairs with Bank Indonesia on Coordination of Regional Inflation Monitoring and Management. Through this collaboration, it is hoped that more effective monitoring and management of regional inflation will be carried out, with the functioning of the TPID Coordination Working Group at the central level. 21. Second, the Memorandum of Understanding between the Ministry of Agriculture and Bank Indonesia on Business Development Cooperation in the Agricultural Sector. The purpose of this collaboration is to synergize resources in the context of business development in the agricultural sector and encourage increased access of agricultural sector businesses to sources of financing. The fathers I respect, 22. Before concluding this speech, I would like to express my appreciation for the close committee cooperation between Bank Indonesia, the Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs, and the Ministry of Home Affairs for the implementation of the National Coordination Meeting. this. I would also like to express my gratitude to the speakers and speakers who have been willing to attend this event. 23. I expect the Second National Coordination Meeting of the Regional Inflation Control Team in 2011 to be a concrete step to produce a more comprehensive and concrete solution in overcoming national and regional inflation problems, and encouraging national economic capacity building. 24. We ask that the Vice President of the Republic of Indonesia would like to witness the signing of the two cooperation texts between the Government and Bank Indonesia, as well as officially open the TPID National Coordination Meeting. Thank you. Wassalamu'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh.
text_original: SAMBUTAN GUBERNUR BANK INDONESIA DR. DARMIN NASUTION PEMBUKAAN RAPAT KOORDINASI NASIONAL TIM PENGENDALIAN INFLASI DAERAH 2011 JAKARTA, 16 MARET 2011 Yang terhormat Wakil Presiden Republik Indonesia, Prof. Dr. Boediono Menteri Koordinator Bidang Perekonomian, Menteri Keuangan, Menteri Dalam Negeri, Menteri Pertanian, Ketua Panja Inflasi dan Suku Bunga, Komisi XI DPR RI, Para Narasumber dan Moderator, Para Gubernur, Bupati, Walikota dan Pemimpin Bank Indonesia di daerah, serta para undangan yang berbahagia, Assa/amu'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh, Sela mat pagi dan salam sejahtera bagi kita semua, 1. Di pagi hari yang cerah ini, marilah kita bersama-sama memanjatkan puji dan syukur kehadirat Tuhan Yang Maha Esa, karena atas rahmat dan hidayah-Nya kita da pat berkumpul bersama dalam acara Rapat Koordinasi Nasional Tim Pengendalian Inflasi Daerah Tahun 2011. Kami haturkan terima kasih yang sebesar-besarnya atas perkenan Bapak Wakil Presiden untuk hadir bersama kita semua; tak lupa kami ucapkan terima kasih kepada seluruh hadirin yang dapat hadir dalam acara ini. Bapak dan Ibu yang berbahagia, 2. Rakornas TPID kali ini adalah yang kedua kalinya, setelah pada 2010 di Bali diselenggarakan Rakornas TPID yang pertama. Penyelenggaraan Rakornas TPID kali ini merupakan hasil kerjasama yang sangat baik antara Bank Indonesia, Kementerian Koordinator Bidang Perekonomian dan Kementerian Dalam Negeri. Pada saat penyelenggaraan Rakornas TPID yang pertama, tercatat 38 kota pembentuk inflasi nasional yang telah memiliki Tim atau Forum Koordinasi Perna ntauan dan Pengendalian Inflasi, atau yang biasa disebut TPID. Terkait perkembangan TPID, perkenankan dalam kesempatan ini saya menyampaikan kepada Bapak Wakil Presiden, bahwa sampai dengan hari ini, dari total 66 kota yang menjadi dasar penghitungan inflasi di Indonesia oleh Badan Pusat Statistik, TPID telah terbentuk di 55 kota dengan 32 diantaranya merupakan ibukota provinsi. 3. Pesatnya peningkatan jumlah TPID yang terbentuk dalam kurun waktu 1 tahun terakhir menunjukkan besarnya perhatian, kesadaran, kepedulian dan komitmen para Kepala Daerah terhadap pentingnya upaya mewujudkan sta bi litas harga di daerah. Untuk itulah, pada kesempatan yang baik ini kami sampaikan apresiasi yang setinggi- tingginya kepada pemerintah daerah dan pemangku kepentingan lainnya di daerah, atas berbagai upaya aktif yang dilakukan dalam rangka mendukung terwujudnya stabilitas harga dan pengendalian inflasi daerah pada khususnya. Bapak dan Ibu yang saya hormati, 4. Tema sentral yang diangkat pada Rakornas kedua ini adalah "Optimalisasi Penanganan Masalah Produksi, Pasokan dan Distribusi Komoditas Pangan Strategis dalam rangka Mendukung Stabilitas Harga dan Ketahanan Pangan Nasional". Saya memandang, rakornas kali ini memiliki makna penting dan menjadi momentum untuk lebih memperkuat koordinasi dan sinergi kebijakan antara Pemerintah Pusat, Pemerintah Daerah dan Bank Indonesia dalam rangka mendukung terciptanya stabilitas harga. 5. Dalam kaitan tersebut, tujuan penyelenggaraan Rakornas II TPID 2011 antara lain untuk: a. mem ba ng un komunikasi dan kepercayaan {building trust) serta mengembangkan jejaring kerja {networking) antara sesama TPID. b. memperkuat koordinasi vertikal, yaitu koordinasi dan kerjasama antara pemerintah pusat-daerah, maupun koordinasi horizontal yaitu antar pemerintah daerah dan antar lembaga terkait baik di tingkat pusat dan daerah, dalam mendukung terwujudnya stabilisasi harga. c. membahas dan mencari solusi/tindaklanjut terkait dengan masalah pasokan, distribusi dan struktur pasar komoditas pangan di daerah. d. membahas upaya peningkatan kapasitas produksi pertanian di daerah terutama komoditas pangan strategis, serta langkah-langkah antisipasi yang perlu ditempuh pemerintah daerah menghadapi kondisi anomali cuaca yang masih berpotensi terjadi di 2011, dan ancaman inflasi global yang semakin kuat. Bapak dan Ibu yang berbahagia, 6. Tema Rakornas kali ini juga sangat strategis dan relevan dengan tantangan yang dihadapi perekonomian nasional kedepan, terutama dalam menghadapi potensi ancaman tekanan inflasi baik dari global maupun domestik. Oleh karena itu, dalam kesempatan ini, perkenankan saya menyampaikan secara ringkas perkembangan terkini perekonomian serta tantangan yang akan kita hadapi beberapa waktu ke depan. 7. Kita patut bersyukur bahwa pada 2010 lalu, kinerja ekonomi nasional secara umum cukup menggembirakan. Pertumbuhan ekonomi mencapai 6,1%/ disertai peningkatan investasi dan ekspor sehingga menopang pertumbuhan yang lebih berimbang dibandingkan tahun sebelumnya. Neraca pembayaran membukukan surplus USD 30,2 miliar. Sebagai catatan, per 10 Maret 2011 cadangan devisa mencapai USD 102,02 miliar. Sementara itu, sistem keuangan tetap terjaga ditengah semakin dinamisnya pasar keuangan global paska krisis. 8. Bank Indonesia optimis perbaikan ekonomi akan terus berlanjut. Tahun 2011 ini akan menjadi tahun yang sangat menjanjikan. Berbagai indikator menunjukkan sumber-sumber pertumbuhan ekonomi terus membaik secara berimbang; tidak hanya bergantung pada konsumsi tetapi juga ekspor dan investasi. Peluang untuk mencapai pertumbuhan lebih tinggi terbuka lebar dengan Indonesia hanya berjarak satu tingkat lagi dari zona layak investasi {investmentgrade}. 9. Meskipun demikian, tahun 2011 juga akan lebih menantang bagi pengelolaan kebijakan makro, terutama kebijakan pengendalian inflasi, setelah tahun lalu inflasi IHK mencapai 6,96% atau di atas target 5%<b1>1%. Meski tingginya inflasi yang terutama bersumber dari pangan merupakan persoalan yang dihadapi banyak negara, namun inflasi kita juga masih lebih tinggi dibandingkan negara lain di kawasan. Bapak dan Ibu yang berbahagia, 10. Tantangan pengendalian inflasi menjadi semakin berat dengan terus meningkatnya harga komoditas di pasar internasional, termasuk harga gandum, gula, dan kedelai. Bank Indonesia memandang risiko tekanan inflasi ke depan yang bersumber dari risiko gangguan pasokan pangan ini masih cukup tinggi. Apabila tidak ditangani secara antisipatif dan memadai, tekanan inflasi pangan yang berkelanjutan dapat memengaruhi harga komoditas dalam kelompok inflasi inti, baik secara langsung maupun tidak langsung. Di pihak lain, kita juga tetap perlu mengantisipasi perubahan iklim yang akan menganggu pasokan pangan di domestik. 11. Di sisi moneter, Bank Indonesia sejak tahun lalu telah menempuh berbagai kebijakan dalam rangka mengendalikan tekanan inflasi. Sinyal kebijakan moneter yang cenderung ketat semakin diperkuat melalui kenaikan BI rate sebesar 25 bps menjadi 6,75% pada awal Februari 2011. Keputusan untuk menahan BI rate pada Maret 2011 tidak mengubah arah kebijakan moneter Bank Indonesia. Selain itu, Bank Indonesia juga memberi ruang penguatan nilai tukar Rupiah sejalan dengan aliran modal masuk yang kembali meningkat. Penguatan Rupiah tersebut membantu meredam tekanan inflasi dari sisi eksternal {imported inflation}, dengan tetap memperhatikan daya saing ekspor Indonesia. Bank Indonesia juga menempuh kebijakan makroprudential dalam rangka mengelola capital inflows sekaligus mengendalikan likuiditas perekonomian. 12. Besarnya risiko inflasi yang bersumber dari gangguan pasokan menyiratkan bahwa pengendalian inflasi tidak dapat sepenuhnya hanya bertumpu pada kebijakan moneter, namun memerlukan kebijakan yang menyeluruh sebagai sebuah keterpaduan kebijakan moneter, fiskal, dan sektoral di seluruh lini dan jenjang. 13. Dalam kaitan ini, saya memandang bahwa kerjasama Pemerintah dan Bank melalui Tim Pengendalian Inflasi, baik di tingkat pusat (TPI) yang telah dirintis sejak tahun 2005 maupun daerah (TPID) sejak tahun 2008 merupakan perwujudan dari keterpaduan yang sangat penting. Mengingat peranannya yang sangat strategis, TPI dan TPID ini perlu terus diperkuat dalam aspek kelembagaan maupun koordinasinya. 14. Hal ini menjadi semakin penting mengingat peranan inflasi daerah terhadap pembentukan inflasi nasional yang cukup besar. Dengan mengeluarkan bobot inflasi Jakarta, peran inflasi daerah mencapai sekitar 77%. Disamping itu, mengingat penyumbang inflasi di tiap daerah cukup unik maka perlu penanganan yang khusus disesuaikan dengan kondisi kedaerahan masing-masing. 15. Agar fungsinya lebih nyata, TPI dan TPID tidak lagi cukup hanya sebagai wadah pertukaran informasi, namun perlu diarahkan untuk mempertajam implementasi berbagai program kerja yang difokuskan pada peningkatan sisi pasokan, terutama komoditas pangan, melalui perbaikan produksi, distribusi, organisasi industri, dan struktur pasar, termasuk pengaturan tata niaga. Bapak dan Ibu yang berbahagia, 16. Dengan mencermati perkembangan terakhir, saya memandang terdapat tiga hal strategis yang patut menjadi bahan pembahasan Rakornas TPID kali ini. Pertama, perlunya setiap daerah mempersiapkan rencana aksi menghadapi ancaman kenaikan harga pangan. Berbagai langkah antisipasi dan segera {immediate policies} perlu segera disusun khususnya terkait penanganan masalah pasokan dan arus distribusi barang. Peningkatan produksi pangan melalui ekstensifikasi dan intensifikasi menjadi isu penting di tengah faktor kondisi cuaca yang ekstrim dan semakin sulit diprediksi. 17. Kedua, oerlunva meningkatkan koordinasi lintas kelembagaan sebagai salah satu prasyarat yang diperlukan untuk mendukung efektivitas berbagai kebijakan stabilitas harga. Dalam kaitan ini, kita perlu merumuskan strategi yang tepat untuk lebih mendorong penguatan hubungan kelembagaan yang bersifat sinergis dan efektif. 18. Ketiga, perlunya perumusan strategi kebijakan yang berdimensi jangka menengah panjang untuk membenahi organisasi industri dan struktur pasar, termasuk tata niaga, khususnya komoditas pangan; serta mengakselerasi upaya peningkatan kapasitas perekonomian. 19. Berbagai permasalahan strategis tersebut akan menjadi agenda hari pertama Rakornas ini. Dapat saya laporkan kepada Bapak Wakil Presiden bahwa Rakornas pada hari pertama ini dihadiri oleh sekitar 300 peserta, termasuk seluruh kepala daerah yang berkedudukan di 66 kota yang menjadi sampel perhitungan inflasi nasional. Selanjutnya, Rakornas pada hari kedua akan masuk ke pembahasan implementasi yang bersifat teknis, dan akan diikuti oleh sekitar 150 orang peserta perwakilan masing-masing TPID, baik pejabat pemerintah daerah maupun kantor Bank Indonesia daerah. 20. Sebagai salah satu wujud nyata langkah penguatan koordinasi lintas kelembagaan untuk mendukung stabilitas harga dan peningkatan kapasitas perekonomian, pada pagi ini juga akan ditandatangani dua buah naskah kerjasama antara Pemerintah dan Bank Indonesia. Pertama, Nota Kesepahaman Kementerian Koordinator Bidang Perekonomian dan Kementerian Dalam Negeri dengan Bank Indonesia tentang Koordinasi Pemantuan dan Pengelolaan Inflasi Daerah. Melalui kerjasama ini diharapkan terselenggaranya pemantauan dan pengelolaan inflasi daerah yang lebih efektif, dengan difungsikannya Kelompok Kerja Koordinasi TPID di tingkat pusat. 21. Kedua, Nota Kesepahaman Kementerian Pertanian dengan Bank Indonesia tentang Kerjasama Pengembangan Usaha di Sektor Pertanian. Tujuan kerjasama ini adalah untuk mensinergikan sumber daya dalam rangka pengembangan usaha di sektor pertanian dan mendorong peningkatan akses usaha sektor pertanian kepada sumber- sumber pembiayaan. Bapak-Ibu yang saya hormati, 22. Sebelum mengakhiri sambutan ini, saya ingin menyampaikan apresiasi atas kerjasama kepanitiaan yang erat antara Bank Indonesia, Kementerian Koordinator Bidang Perekonomian, dan Kementerian Dalam Negeri atas pelaksanaan Rakornas ini. Ucapan terima kasih juga saya sampaikan kepada para pembicara dan narasumber yang telah bersedia untuk menghadiri acara ini. 23. Saya mengharapkan Rapat Koordinasi Nasional kedua Tim Pengendalian Inflasi Daerah tahun 2011 ini menjadi langkah nyata menghasilkan solusi yang lebih komprehensif dan kongkrit dalam mengatasi permasalahan inflasi nasional maupun daerah, dan mendorong peningkatan kapasitas perekonomian secara nasional. 24. Kami mohon kiranya Bapak Wakil Presiden Republik Indonesia berkenan untuk da pat menyaksikan acara penandatanganan dua naskah kerjasama antara Pemerintah dan Bank Indonesia tersebut, serta membuka secara resmi acara Rakornas TPID ini. Sekian dan terima kasih. Wassalamu'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh.

Title: Penjelasan Dewan Gubernur Bank Indonesia Pada Rapat Kerja Dengan Komisi IX DPR RI Tanggal 10 Juni 2002 Mengenai Anggaran Tahunan Bank Indonesia
text: EXPLANATION OF THE BOARD OF GOVERNORS OF BANK INDONESIA AT A WORKING MEETING WITH COMMISSION IX OF THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES ON JUNE 10, 2002 CONCERNING THE ANNUAL BUDGET OF BANK INDONESIA Conference Time: IV Year of Session: 2001 - 2002 Dear Members of the Council, First of all, let us thank the Chairman of Commission IX of the House of Representatives and all members of the House for inviting us to attend the Working Meeting today. This meeting has a very important meaning for us, especially in order to convey various information and explanations regarding the implementation of Bank Indonesia's duties mandated by the Law as well as to obtain various inputs from Board Members that are useful for efforts to improve the implementation of our duties in the monetary, banking and payment system sectors in the future. Moreover, we view this kind of meeting as a form of embodiment of Bank Indonesia accountability to the Dpr-RI. In this working meeting, as invited by the Board members, we will explain the bank indonesia budget for the current year 2002, the implementation of the 2002 Bank Indonesia budget, and preliminary discussions on the 2003 Bank Indonesia budget. However, as was the case at the last Working Meeting, beginning our explanation of the implementation of the Bank Indonesia budget, allow us on this occasion to first briefly submit a report on the latest developments on the policy measures taken by Bank Indonesia. Dear Members of the Council, As the Board members have understood, at the beginning of 2002, Bank Indonesia estimates that in 2002, if exports and investment can be increased and the banking restructuring program runs in line with expectations, economic growth in 2002 is projected to reach 3.5% - 4.0%. Bank Indonesia also set the CPI inflation target at 9%-10% for 2002, taking into account high inflation expectations and the magnitude of the impact of government policies in the field of prices and income. As of the end of May 2002, economic-monetary conditions showed positive developments, particularly reflected in the continued strengthening of the rupiah exchange rate and the decline in rupiah interest rates. Primary money is also under control under its indicative target, while the banking intermediation function is beginning to show improvement, as seen in the increase in third-party funds and the number of new bank lending. The annual inflation rate also tends to decrease although inflationary pressures in May 2002 were felt again after experiencing deflation for the previous two consecutive months. The improvement in economic conditions is inseparable from a number of advances in the economic restructuring process, one of which is reflected in the continuation of the asset divestment process by IBRA, such as in the bca divestment process and other divestment plans (PT Indosat, PT Telkom, PT Indofarma, and Bank Niaga). This progress is also accompanied by the support of a relatively controlled homeland security situation. The two advances made both from the economic and non-economic sides have ultimately contributed to the positive sentiment of the market, which is reflected in the declining perception of business risk as can be seen from the decrease in swap premiums and risk premiums. Positive expectations for the results of the government's debt assessment in Paris Club III also add to the existing confidence. These various indicators in turn caused the exchange rate to gradually strengthen and along with the controlled development of primary money has been followed by a reduction in the SBI interest rate. In general, Indonesia's economic growth in Q1-2002 increased by 2.15% (y-t-y) compared to the fourth quarter of 2001. In the 1st quarter of 2002, household consumption expenditure although in real terms increased by 1.02% compared to the previous quarter, but government consumption expenditure decreased by 1.03% and physical investment decreased by 2.45%. Similarly, exports and imports increased by 2.89% and 1.82%, respectively, but in aggregate demand remained weak. Meanwhile, in line with the increasing world oil price, oil and gas export revenues showed an increase in Q1/2002 compared to the previous quarter. On the monetary side, after experiencing deflation in the previous two months, the intensity of the general price pressure in May 2002 began to be felt. May experienced inflation of 0.80% (m-t-m) or higher than the previous month which experienced deflation of minus 0.24%. However, inflation on an annual basis (y-o- y) decreased to 12.93% compared to the previous month of 13.30%. The occurrence of inflation in May 2002 was mainly due to the enactment of government policies in the field of prices, especially the increase in fuel prices and transportation tariffs, as reflected in the increase in prices of the transportation and communication group by 3.40% (m-t-m) and the housing group by 0.78% (m-t-m). The two terse groups also contributed the highest to inflation this month, 0.40% and 0.18%, respectively. The impact of the Government's policy on inflation this month is relatively high, reaching 0.41%. Meanwhile, price pressures from the supply side with regard to supply availability and distribution are not visible. The increase in prices in the food group tends to be more related to the increase in transportation costs due to the increase in fuel prices, thus impacting inflation in the group by a large rate of 0.58%. Meanwhile, food group inflation reached about 0.39% (m-t-m) or 11.93% (y-o-y), lower than the non-food group of 1.12% (m-t-m) or 13.85% (y-o-y). The food group's contribution to inflation this month was 0.17%, while other groups, outside the transportation and communications group and housing group, contributed relatively little inflation. In terms of the exchange rate, in May 2002, the rupiah appreciated significantly again until it broke the level below Rp9,000 per USD. The rupiah closed at a level of Rp8,830 or strengthened 500 points (5.7%) compared to the previous month of Rp9,330 per USD. Similarly, on average, the rupiah strengthened 377 points (4.1%) to Rp9,118,- compared to last month's Rp9,495 per USD. Strong market sentiment and the availability of foreign exchange supply have boosted rupiah appreciation until May 2002, which was the strongest level since September 2001. Positive expectations for capital inflows into the country related to the sale of shares/privatization of SOEs, including PT. Indosat, PT. Telkom, PT. Indofarma, and the divestment process of Bank Niaga, contributed a lot in strengthening the rupiah exchange rate. Similarly, Indonesia's success in restructuring the restructuring of government and private external debt, as well as projections of improving the Indonesian economy, have fostered strong optimism of Indonesia's economic revival. Sentiment from the development of regional currencies that tend to strengthen against the USD juga also spurred further appreciation of the rupiah exchange rate. Fundamentally, from the gap in analysis between the demand and supply of forex, an idea is obtained that the market is still obtaining sufficient supply. The adequacy of supply can be seen from interbank transactions which show that offshore parties sell more USD. Meanwhile, domestic supply was obtained from the influx of soe privatization funds and the improvement in exports in recent months. The stronger positive sentiment in the market is reflected in the decrease in swap premiums for all tenors. 1-month and 3-month swap premiums decreased from 14.70% to 13.70% and 13.20%, respectively. Meanwhile, from the calculation of the Real Effective Exchange Rate (REER), the strengthening of the rupiah exchange rate is considered to be quite competitive. In real terms, the rupiah exchange rate is still undervalued with a REER index of 86.64 compared to the previous month of 82.94 (index with a base year of 1995). Similarly, the Bilateral Real Exchange Rate (BRER) figure of 62.17 is also still competitive compared to export competitors such as Malaysia 67.08, Thailand 63.10 and China 84.90 (index with a base year of June 1997). In line with inflation and exchange rates, our monetary policy is directed towards maintaining the momentum of success that has been achieved, especially to maintain macroeconomic stability (especially inflation and exchange rates) while continuing to provide positive signals for economic recovery. Monetary control remains aimed at absorbing excess liquidity to match the real needs of the economy so as not to exert new pressures on inflation and the rupiah exchange rate. We carry out monetary control through open market operations, rupiah intervention, and foreign exchange sterilization. With conducive monetary economic conditions, the 1-month SBI rate has tended to decline from 17.5% in early January 2002 to 15.17% in the first week of June 2002. The Rupiah Intervention rate has also been lowered by 100 bps for all tenors, to 14.125% - 14.875% for an overnight period of up to 7 days. The lower SBI interest rate and rupiah intervention have also been followed by a reduction in deposit rates and bank loans. Currently, the deposit rate is at 13.73%, while the interest rate on working capital loans is around 19.25%. Dear Members of the Council, In the banking sector, at the beginning of 2002, national banking performance showed several improvements, as reflected by an increase in fund raising and lending, improvements in capital aspects, improvements in non-performing loans (NPLs) and an increase in net interest margin (NIM). Nevertheless, the banking industry still faces challenges in the form of an intermediation function that has not recovered as quickly as expected to support the economic recovery process. Therefore, in 2002 Bank Indonesia will continue to implement banking policy measures directed at the banking restructuring strategy framework, which includes two major parts, namely (i) the banking restructuring program which includes government guarantees, commercial bank recapitalization programs, and bank loan restructuring; (ii) and resilience strengthening programs that include infrastructure development and improving good corporate governance and strengthening the bank supervision system. In 2002, the main policy priority was directed at strengthening the resilience of the banking system through maximizing the implementation of the 25 Basle Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision , the description of which was outlined in the Master Plan for Improving the Effectiveness of Bank Supervision. Efforts to maintain the CAR of banks that have reached 8% continue to be carried out, especially for banks whose capital structure is still vulnerable to the influence of rising interest rates and weakening exchange rates as well as declining loans. On the other hand, to restore the banking intermediation function, we will encourage banks to channel more credit to sectors that have been deemed ready and have relatively low risks such as export credit and SME credit. To that end, Bank Indonesia has also signed an agreement with the Coordinating Minister for People's Welfare on Poverty Reduction through the Empowerment and Development of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises. In the agreement, Bank Indonesia, among others, will encourage commercial banks and rural banks to increase lending to micro, small and medium enterprises in accordance with the business plan of each bank, for poverty reduction, while still paying attention to the principle of prudence. In addition, efforts to improve bank health are also supported by efforts to reduce the number of non-performing loans (NPLs) of national banks by requiring banks to achieve the NPL target of 5% by the end of 2002. Furthermore, steps to strengthen banking infrastructure will continue to be taken by encouraging the development of Islamic banks and rural banks and together with the government to prepare for the establishment of the Deposit Insurance Corporation and the Financial Services Authority. In addition, we also allow on this occasion to convey the implementation and follow-up of the provisions on know your customer principles which are the implementation of anti-money laundering in the banking sector. Based on reviews by independent consultants, there are banks that have fully complied with the principle of knowing customers. However, there are also several other banks that are continuously trying to update customer data bases and training for employees who number in the thousands. To facilitate the implementation of these provisions, better coordination between Bank Indonesia and the banking sector will continue to be carried out. Dear Members of the Council, In order to support the effective implementation of monetary policy and efforts to create a sound banking system, in the field of payment system, in 2002 Bank Indonesia continued to make various efforts enhancements to create an electronic payment system that is efficient, fast, secure, and reliable. In the field of cash payment systems, the policy is directed at providing money that is fit for circulation and meets the needs of the community both in terms of nominal and type of fractions. Meanwhile, in the field of cashless financing systems, policy measures are directed at reducing payment risks, improving the quality and service capacity of payment systems and regulating payment system supervision in order to encourage the realization of a fast, secure, and efficient payment system. Dear Members of the Council, As is known, the objective of Bank Indonesia is to achieve and maintain rupiah stability. To achieve this goal, Bank Indonesia has three tasks as we have explained one by one above, yes, it is to establish and implement monetary policy, regulate and maintain a smooth payment system and regulate and supervise banks. In order to carry out the task and achieve the goals that have been set, we prepare an annual work plan that is prepared by referring to the Annual Strategic Goals of Bank Indonesia (STBI) which has been established by the Board of Governors. The annual work plan is further stated in the form of the Annual Budget of Bank Indonesia (ATBI) and together with the ev of the allegation of the implementation of the current year's budget , submitted to the Board People's Representative (DPR-RI) as a form of transparency and accountability in the implementation of Bank Indonesia's duties. The BI Indonesia reflects Bank Indonesia's work program which is further elaborated in the form of a revenue and expenditure budget. The assumptions used in the preparation of the ATBI are made based on prudent principles in line with the projections of economic conditions and developments that are expected to occur in the current year n . These assumptions include economic growth, inflation rate, SBI discount rate, and rupiah exchange rate. Prudence in the preparation of the Financial Instrumental System stability is very important considering that financial sustainability or financial fortitude of Bank Indonesia is also a condition for the effectiveness of monetary policy implementation. Next, let us give an explanation of the esteemed councillor's question about; Bank Indonesia's 2002 budget, Bank Indonesia's 2002 budget, and an overview of Bank Indonesia's 2003 budget. BANK INDONESIA BUDGET 2002 Dear Members of the Council, As the board members understand, the submission of the Annual Budget of Bank Indonesia (ATBI) to the House of Representatives is an obligation in accordance with Bank Indonesia Law, which among others is stated that no later than 15 (fifteen) days Before the start of the fiscal year, the Board of Governors shall determine the annual budget of Bank Indonesia which must be submitted to the House of Representatives and the Government in conjunction with the evaluation of the implementation of the year's budget walked. In connection with the characteristics of Bank Indonesia as a Central Bank institution, especially its duties and functions to establish and implement monetary policy, regulate and maintain the smooth running of the payment system and regulate and supervising banks, the format and material of the Bank Indonesia Annual Budget (ATBI) are different from the State Budget (APBN). As was done in previous years, the assumptions used in the preparation of the 2002 ATBI were made based on prudent principles, in line with projections of conditions and developments. an economy that is still in the process of recovery. The assumptions used in the preparation of the Bank Indonesia Budget for the year 2002 are: Budget Exchange Rate of Rp9,000/USD, Inflation of 9%, SBI Discount of 14%, and Economic Growth of 4%. Considering the limitations, especially the financial capability of Bank Indonesia, the strategy of allocating the budget to the expenditure is prioritized in the implementation of the following programs: a. Maintaining monetary stability as reflected in the inflation rate and rupiah exchange rate. b. Improving the payment system in the form of expanding the application of Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS), developing a clearing system at Bank Indonesia offices and tackling the increasing circulation of counterfeit money. c. Seeking the restoration of the national banking intermediation function through the acceleration of the banking restructuring program which includes the financingof banking institutions; strengthening the resilience of the banking system as well as improving the regulation and strengthening of the bank supervision system. d. Accelerate Bank Indonesia's transformation program in order to improve the effectiveness of Bank Indonesia's function implementation in order to meet stakeholder demands. e. Improving the human resource management system, internal financial management system , information technology system, and internal supervision system. IMPLEMENTATION OF BANK INDONESIA BUDGET UNTIL THE END OF MAY 2002 Dear Members of the Council, As of May 31, 2002, economic and monetary conditions had improved relatively, as reflected in the development of the rupiah exchange rate which reached below the assumption of the exchange rate used in setting the budget. which is IDR 9,000 per USD. In this regard, the realization of the budget until May 31, 2002 is as follows: 95 The realization of receipts is close to 50% of the targeted in the year 2002 amounted to Rp25.2 trillion. 95 The realization of expenditure reached around 40% of what was estimated in 2002 of Rp20.5 trillion. The explanation of bank Indonesia's 2002 budget realization for certain posts until the end of May 2002 is as follows: 1. Acceptance a. Realization of receipts due to foreign exchange management. Revenues due to foreign exchange management mainly come from coupun and interest on securities, trading or trading securities and other foreign exchange transactions. As of May 2002, receipts have reached around 70% of the targeted Rp. 17.6 trillion. Of this amount, around 60% comes from the result of the exchange rate difference where the average prevailing exchange rate is above the assumption of the budget rate of RP9,000. b. Realization of bunqa acceptance This revenue consists of receiving interest on credit provision prior to the enactment of the 1999 Bank Indonesia Law and receiving interest on government bonds. Specifically regarding the receipt of interest on Government Bonds (SUP), in 2002 it is targeted at Rp7.2 trillion (SUP No.01 to No.06). But until now, the acceptance has not been realized. 2. Expense a. Expenditure on monetary deposition By the end of May 2002 , the realization of expenditure for monetary control operations in the form of SBI discounts had reached Rp7.8 trillion, while the target by the end of 2002 was Rp14.2 trillion. The realization of SBI interest costs was influenced by the realization of SBI volume, which reached Rp 101 trillion from the targeted Rp 90 trillion. In addition, it is also due to the high level of disconto average SBI which until the end of May 2002 was around 16%, while the target assumption for the beginning of 2002 averaged 14%. b. Expenditures on interest payments on foreign loans Until the end of May 2002, the realization of interest payments on foreign loans amounted to Rp 1.3 trillion, while the target until the end of 2002 was Rp.5.1 trillion. The low realization of interest payments on foreign loans until the end of May 2002 was mainly due to the decline in international interest rates. Dear Members of the Council, On this occasion, please also allow us to present projections for bank indonesia budget realization until the end of December 2002. Taking into account macroeconomic and policy developments that are underlying as well as developments in other aspects affecting Bank Indonesia's operational activities, the realization of Bank Indonesia's financial condition is estimated to indicate that revenue achievement will be lower than expenditure realization. This is reflected as follows: 1. Acceptance a. Realization of receipts due to foreign exchange management The recent appreciation of the rupiah is expected to continue until the end of 2002. This condition affects Bank Indonesia's revenue, so it is estimated that by the end of 2002 the revenue target cannot be achieved. b. Realization of interest receipt If by the end of 2002 the receipt of interest from SUP cannot be realized, this will affect Bank Indonesia's revenue. 2. Expense a. Expenditures for monetary control Taking into account economic conditions that have not been able to absorb excess liquidity in the banking industry, even though the SBI discount rate has shown a decline, it is estimated that the volume of SBI will continue to increase. Thus, the overall SBI discount cost budgeted at IDR 14.2 trillion is expected to be exceeded. b. Expenditures on interest payments on foreign loans Although there is a tendency to slightly increase in international interest rates, when associated with the development of rupiah appreciation, it is estimated that the realization of interest payments on foreign loans will be slightly lower than planned. GAM BARAN GENERAL FINANCIAL CONDITION OF BANK INDONESIA 2003 Dear Members of the Council, As we stated at the beginning, in preparing the annual budget of Bank Indonesia (ATBI), Bank Indonesia did so prudently, in line with the projected economic conditions and developments expected to occur in the current year. For the determination of the 2002-2003 ATBI, the assumptions used for 2003 are, economic growth, inflation rate, SBI discount rate, rupiah exchange rate, and average primary money. In terms of economic growth, we can say that Indonesia's economic prospects in 2003 will be able to grow higher than in the year 2002. Progress in the implementation of economic and financial programs adopted by the government and Bank Indonesia is expected to increase business confidence. This is further expected to be an attraction for foreign capital inflows to Indonesia. The better economic outlook in 2003 was also driven by the significantly improved global economy. The world economy is expected to grow by 4.1% in the year 2003, much higher compared to the previous year which was expected at 2.7%. Indonesia's exports are expected to grow higher with this external development. With various forecasts of improving internal and external conditions, Bank Indonesia projects economic growth in 2003 to reach around 4.2 - 5.2%. Economic growth in 2003 is predicted to still come from consumer growth, albeit with declining growth. Meanwhile, investment is predicted to experience higher growth than in 2002 in line with declining political and security uncertainty and declining rates. flowers in d nature of the land. The role of exports in economic growth is also expected to increase in line with the increasing demand for Indonesian export goods. On the supply side, economic growth is expected to be contributed by all economic sectors. Meanwhile, the rupiah exchange rate is expected to have the potential to continue strengthening. In 2003, the average rupiah exchange rate is expected to strengthen in the range of Rp 8,500 - Rp 9,500. This will happen as long as the following factors can be met so thata in turn can improve the perception of market participants, namely: meaningful progress in the restructuring program economy and finance, improving business conditions, lending to the real sector have been doing well, increasing investment and foreign affairs, and progress that significant in the sale of assets by IBRA and the privatization of SOEs. This forecast will become more optimistic if there is hope of continued improvement in political, financial and economic risks. Meanwhile, in relation to the projected inflation rate, we can say that the outlook for inflation in 2003 is expected to decrease to around 8%-10%. This is in line with the expected exchange rate which will strengthen so that it will reduce the prices of imported goods and production costs in the country. Inflationary pressures will also be relatively lessened in line with the availability of basic necessities, especially food, which have a large weight in inflation. Meanwhile, inflationary pressures are primarily expected to be felt from the impact of the implementation of government policies to reduce fuel subsidies and increase TDL and cigarette excise. Dear Members of the Council, Taking into account the economic outlook and the high pressures of the next year, as well as the various challenges faced in monetary control, Bank Indonesia will strive to consistently implement policies in the monetary, banking and payment system fields. In the monetary sector, monetary policy will be directed at controlling primary money to remain in line with the real needs of the economy. Efforts to control the monetary will be carried out with positive real interest rates in the adequate range of around 4.0%-5.0%. Operationally, monetary control is carried out by optimizing monetary instruments, especially through open market operations with SBI auctions. In addition, these efforts will also be supported by conducting foreign exchange sterilization. Apart from being an effort to absorb excess liquidity, foreign exchange sterilization is also intended to reduce pressure on the rupiah exchange rate. All measures in the monetary sector will be carried out in a prudent and measured manner so that price stability is maintained so that it can support the eco-nomi recovery process. ongoing and sustainable economic growth in the medium-long term. In the banking sector, the top policy priority is directed at strengthening the resilience of the banking system. To achieve this, Bank Indonesia will continue to maximize the implementation of the 25 Basle Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision, the elaboration of which is outlined in the Master Plan for Improving the Effectiveness of Bank Supervision. Efforts to maintain the CAR of banks that have reached 8% continue to be acknowledged, especially for banks whose capital structure is still vulnerable to the effects of rising interest rates and weakening values. exchanges as well as declining credit quality. In addition, to strengthen national banking institutions, an assessment is currently being carried out on the development of national banking institutions that are integrated with the development of institutions other financial. On the other hand, the efforts that have currently been initiated in the field of implementing PBI Know Your Customer as well as the development of an integrated debtor information system are also continuing in 2003 Meanwhile, to restore the banking intermediation function, Bank Indonesia will encourage banks to channel more credit to sectors deemed ready and have relatively low risks such as export credit and credit for SMEs as well as making improvements to several provisions to speed up intermediation. In addition, efforts to improve bank health are also supported by continuous efforts to reduce the number of Non-Performing Loans (NPLs) of national banks by requiring banks to bank to achieve npls target of 5% by the end of 2002. Meanwhile, efforts that need to be made to strengthen national bank infrastructure can be made by continuing to encourage the development of Islamic banks and the existence of rural banks and together with the government is preparing for the establishment of the Deposit Insurance Corporation, and the Financial Services Supervisory Agency. In the field of payment system, policies will be directed to accelerate the development and implementation of an efficient, accurate, safe, and reliable national payment system through improving service quality payment system. In the field of money circulation, Bank Indonesia will reorganize money distribution channels in order to further ensure the availability of money in all Bank Indonesia Offices (KBI) and improve money withdrawal services. cash in to the community. In addition, Bank Indonesia always strives to improve the quality of new money issued by prioritizing the use of visible and visible security elements. Meanwhile, in terms of non-cash payments, the policy will be directed at reducing payment risk, increasing the quality and service capacity of the payment system as well as regulating system supervision. fast, secure and efficient payments. In addition, Bank Indonesia also continues to make regulatory efforts regarding the implementation of payment system services using non-cash payment instruments and supporting services as well as conducting arrangements related to efforts to overcome the failure of the clearing participant in the settlement of his settlement obligations. Dear Members of the Council, Taking into account the monetary economic outlook and the policy measures to be taken by Bank Indonesia in 2003 as we stated above, let us present an overview of the financial condition of Bank Indonesia in 2003. We need to convey that the general picture is the subject of preliminary discussions on several important matters that need to be considered in the preparation of the draft Annual Budget of Bank Indonesia year 2003, which in due course will be presented to the Members of the Council as an implementation of Law No. 23 of 1999. In principle, the financial condition of Bank Indonesia will be affected by the implementation of Bank Indonesia's duties as mandated in the law. As members of the Board of Indonesia understand, the objective of Bank Indonesia is to achieve and maintain rupiah stability , in the sense of achieving a fairly low inflation rate and a stable Rupiah exchange rate . The stability of the Rupiah is very necessary in supporting sustainable economic growth and thus increasing the provision of employment opportunities. To achieve this goal, Bank Indonesia has adopted monetary policy in order to control the circulation of money in accordance with the real needs of the economy. To that end, Bank Indonesia incurs moneter control costs, mostly in the form of interest payable on SBI monetary instruments. We can also convey that all the costs of monetary control have so far become a burden on Bank Indonesia. In this connection, we can put forward an overview of the expenditure burden in the Bank Indonesia budget which is expected to arise from the implementation of monetary control in 2003. On the one hand, with the forecast of a decrease in the inflation rate and the strengthening of the Rupiah exchange rate, the a SBI rate in 2003 is expected to decline compared to the year 2002. But on the other hand, in line with increasing economic activity, it is estimated that primary money will also increase. This will result in an increase in the volume of SBI that must be issued by Bank Indonesia in order to control monetary control. Thus, the overall expenditure burden of monetary control is expected to increase in 2003. Meanwhile, in terms of revenue, we can state that most of it comes from the investment made by Bank Indonesia on foreign exchange reserves. In this connection, the tendency of international interest rates in 2003, which will affect the acceptance of foreign exchange management in foreign exchange, is expected to increase slightly. However, on the other hand, in line with the forecast that the Rupiah exchange rate will strengthen as previously stated, foreign exchange management receipts if converted to Rupiah are expected to decrease. Meanwhile, the expected interest receipts from the SUP have not yet been realized. With the picture of receipts and expenditures as above, we can generally convey that the financial condition of Bank Indonesia in 2003 is expected to still face a fairly heavy burden. This needs to be our common concern considering the importance of maintaining the financial condition of the central bank in order to carry out its duties to maintain the stability of the Rupiah value necessary for the sustainability of the national economic recovery process. For this reason, it is considered necessary to continue efforts to find alternative monetary instruments that can reduce the cost of monetary control. One way that can be pursued is to use government bonds as an alternative monetary instrument as is done in many other countries, in addition to its important role as a reference in the formation of a medium - long-term interest rate structure in the market. Jakarta, June 10th, 2002
text_original: PENJELASAN DEWAN GUBERNUR BANK INDONESIA PADA RAPAT KERJA DENGAN KOMISI IX DPR Rl TANGGAL 10 JUNI 2002 MENGENAI ANGGARAN TAHUNAN BANK INDONESIA Masa Persidangan : IV Tahun Sidang : 2001 - 2002 Anggota Dewan yang terhormat, Pertama-tama, perkenankan kami mengucapkan terima kasih kepada Pimpinan Komisi IX DPR Rl beserta seluruh Anggota Dewan yang telah mengundang kami untuk menghadiri Rapat Kerja pada hari ini. Pertemuan ini memiliki arti yang sangat penting bagi kami, terutama dalam rangka menyampaikan berbagai informasi dan penjelasan mengenai pelaksanaan tugas Bank Indonesia yang diamanatkan oleh Undang-Undang sekaligus untuk mendapatkan berbagai masukan dari Anggota Dewan yang berguna bagi upaya perbaikan dalam pelaksanaan tugas kami di bidang moneter, perbankan, dan sistem pembayaran ke depan. Lebih dari itu, pertemuan semacam ini pada hakikatnya kami pandang sebagai salah satu bentuk perwujudan dari akuntabilitas Bank Indonesia kepada DPR-RI. Dalam rapat kerja kali ini, sebagaimana undangan dari Anggota Dewan, kami akan memaparkan mengenai anggaran Bank Indonesia tahun berjalan 2002, pelaksanaan anggaran Bank Indonesia 2002, dan pembicaraan pendahuluan anggaran Bank Indonesia tahun 2003. Namun demikian, sebagaimana halnya pada Rapat Kerja- Rapat Kerja yang lalu, mengawali penjelasan kami atas pelaksanaan anggaran Bank Indonesia tersebut, perkenankanlah kami dalam kesempatan ini untuk terlebih dahulu secara singkat menyampaikan laporan perkembangan terakhir atas langkah-langkah kebijakan yang telah ditempuh Bank Indonesia. Anggota Dewan yang terhormat, Sebagaimana telah Anggota Dewan maklumi, pada awal tahun 2002, Bank Indonesia memperkirakan bahwa dalam tahun 2002, apabila ekspor dan investasi dapat ditingkatkan dan program restrukturisasi perbankan berjalan sesuai dengan harapan, pertumbuhan ekonomi tahun 2002 diprakirakan dapat mencapai 3,5% - 4,0%. Bank Indonesia juga menetapkan sasaran laju inflasi IHK sebesar 9%-10% untuk tahun 2002 dengan memperhatikan masih tingginya ekspektasi inflasi dan besarnya dampak kebijakan pemerintah di bidang harga dan pendapatan. Dalam perkembangannya, sampai dengan akhir Mei 2002, secara umum kondisi ekonomi-moneter menunjukkan perkembangan yang positif, khususnya tercermin pada berlanjutnya penguatan nilai tukar rupiah secara signifikan dan menurunnya suku bunga rupiah. Uang primer juga terkendali di bawah target indikatifnya, sementara fungsi intermediasi perbankan mulai menunjukkan perbaikan, seperti terlihat pada meningkatnya dana pihak ketiga dan jumlah pemberian kredit baru perbankan. Laju inflasi secara tahunan juga cenderung menurun meskipun tekanan inflasi pada bulan Mei 2002 terasa kembali setelah selama dua bulan sebelumnya berturut-turut mengalami deflasi. Membaiknya kondisi perekonomian tersebut tidak terlepas dari terdapatnya sejumlah kemajuan dalam proses restrukturisasi ekonomi yang salah satunya tercermin dari kelanjutan proses divestasi aset oleh BPPN seperti dalam proses divestasi BCA dan rencana divestasi lainnya (PT Indosat, PT Telkom, PT Indofarma, dan Bank Niaga). Kemajuan ini juga diiringi dengan dukungan situasi keamanan dalam negeri yang relatif terkendali. Kedua kemajuan yang dicapai baik dari sisi ekonomi dan non ekonomi tersebut pada akhirnya telah turut membentuk sentimen positif pasar yang tercermin dari menurunnya persepsi atas risiko usaha sebagaimana terlihat dari menurunnya premi swap dan premi risiko. Ekspektasi positif atas hasil penjadualan utang Pemerintah dalam Paris Club III juga turut menambah kepercayaan yang ada. Berbagai ndikator ini pada gilirannya menyebabkan nilai tukar secara gradual mengalami penguatan dan seiring dengan perkembangan uang primer yang terkendali telah diikuti dengan penurunan suku bunga SBI. Secara umum, pertumbuhan ekonomi Indonesia dalam Triwulan 1-2002 meningkat 2,15% (y-t-y) dibandingkan triwulan IV-2001. Dalam triwulan 1-2002 tersebut, pengeluaran konsumsi rumah tangga meskipun secara riil meningkat sebesar 1,02% dibandingkan triwulan sebelumnya, namun pengeluaran konsumsi pemerintah menurun sebesar 1,03% dan investasi fisik menurun sebesar 2,45%. Demikian pula ekspor dan impor meningkat masing-masing sebesar 2,89% dan 1,82%, namun secara agregat permintaan masih lemah. Sementara itu, sejalan dengan meningkatnya harga minyak dunia, penerimaan ekspor migas menunjukkan peningkatan pada triwulan 1/2002 dibanding dengan triwulan sebelumnya. Di sisi moneter, setelah dalam dua bulan sebelumnya mengalami deflasi, intensitas tekanan harga secara umum pada bulan Mei 2002 mulai terasa. Bulan Mei mengalami inflasi sebesar 0,80% (m-t-m) atau lebih tinggi dari bulan sebelumnya yang mengalami deflasi sebesar minus 0,24%. Namun demikian, inflasi secara tahunan (y-o- y) mengalami penurunan menjadi 12,93% dibandingkan bulan sebelumnya sebesar 13,30%. Terjadinya inflasi pada bulan Mei 2002 tersebut terutama disebabkan oleh diberlakukannya kebijakan pemerintah di bidang harga, khususnya kenaikan harga BBM dan tarif angkutan, seperti tercermin pada peningkatan harga kelompok transportasi dan komunikasi sebesar 3,40% (m-t-m) serta kelompok perumahan sebesar 0,78% (m-t-m). Kedua kelompok tersebut juga memberikan sumbangan tertinggi terhadap inflasi bulan ini, masing-masing 0,40% dan 0,18%. Dampak kebijakan Pemerintah terhadap inflasi dalam bulan ini relatif tinggi yaitu mencapai sebesar 0,41 %. Sementara itu, tekanan harga dari sisi penawaran khususnya berkaitan dengan ketersediaan pasokan dan distribusi tidak terlihat. Kenaikan harga pada kelompok makanan cenderung lebih terkait dengan meningkatnya biaya pengangkutan akibat naiknya harga BBM, sehingga berdampak pada inflasi kelompok tersebut sebesar 0,58%. Sementara itu, inflasi kelompok makanan mencapai sekitar 0,39% (m-t-m) atau 11,93% (y-o-y), lebih rendah dari kelompok bukan makanan 1,12% (m-t-m) atau 13,85% (y-o-y). Sumbangan kelompok bahan makanan terhadap inflasi bulan ini sebesar 0,17%, sementara kelompok lainnya, di luar kelompok transportasi dan komunikasi serta kelompok perumahan, memberikan sumbangan inflasi relatif kecil. Di sisi nilai tukar, pada bulan Mei 2002, nilai tukar rupiah kembali menguat secara signifikan hingga menembus level di bawah Rp9.000,- per USD. Rupiah ditutup pada level Rp8.830,- atau menguat 500 poin (5,7%) dibandingkan bulan sebelumnya Rp9.330,- per USD. Demikian pula secara rata-rata, rupiah menguat 377 poin (4,1%) menjadi Rp9.118,- dibandingkan bulan lalu Rp9.495,- per USD. Kuatnya sentimen pasar serta tersedianya pasokan valas telah mendorong apresiasi rupiah sampai dengan bulan Mei 2002, yang merupakan level terkuat sejak September 2001. Ekspektasi positif terhadap aliran modal masuk ke dalam negeri yang terkait dengan penjualan saham/privatisasi BUMN, antara lain PT. Indosat, PT. Telkom, PT. Indofarma, dan proses divestasi Bank Niaga memberikan andil yang tidak sedikit dalam penguatan nilai tukar rupiah. Demikian pula, keberhasilan Indonesia dalam merestrukturisasi utang luar negeri pemerintah dan swasta, serta proyeksi akan membaiknya ekonomi Indonesia, telah menumbuhkan optimisme yang kuat akan kebangkitan ekonomi Indonesia. Sentimen dari perkembangan mata uang regional yang cenderung menguat terhadap USD juga turut memacu apresiasi kurs rupiah lebih lanjut. Secara fundamental, dari gap analisis antara permintaan dan penawaran valas, diperoleh gambaran bahwa pasar masih memperoleh pasokan yang cukup. Kecukupan pasokan terlihat dari transaksi antar bank yang menunjukkan pihak offshore lebih banyak menjual USD. Sementara itu, pasokan dari dalam negeri diperoleh dari masuknya dana privatisasi BUMN serta membaiknya ekspor dalam beberapa bulan terakhir. Semakin kuatnya sentimen positif yang bekembang di pasar terefleksi pada penurunan premi swap untuk semua tenor. Premi swap 1 bulan dan 3 bulan mengalami penurunan masing-masing dari 14,70% menjadi 13,70 % dan 13,20%. Sementara itu, dari perhitungan Real Effective Exchange Rate (REER) penguatan nilai tukar rupiah tersebut dipandang masih cukup kompetitif. Secara riil, nilai tukar rupiah masih undervalued dengan indeks REER 86,64 dibandingkan bulan sebelumnya 82,94 (indeks dengan tahun dasar 1995). Demikian pula, angka Bilateral Real Exchange Rate (BRER) sebesar 62,17 juga masih kompetitif dibandingkan negara pesaing ekspor seperti Malaysia 67,08, Thailand 63,10 dan China 84,90 (indeks dengan tahun dasar Juni 1997). Sejalan dengan perkembangan inflasi dan nilai tukar tersebut, kebijakan moneter yang kami lakukan diarahkan untuk menjaga momentum keberhasilan yang telah dicapai, terutama untuk menjaga kestabilan ekonomi makro (khususnya inflasi dan nilai tukar) sambil terus memberikan sinyal yang positif bagi pemulihan ekonomi. Pengendalian moneter tetap ditujukan untuk menyerap kelebihan likuiditas agar sesuai dengan kebutuhan riil perekonomian sehingga tidak memberikan tekanan baru terhadap inflasi dan nilai tukar rupiah. Pengendalian moneter tersebut kami lakukan melalui operasi pasar terbuka, intervensi rupiah, dan sterilisasi valas. Dengan kondisi ekonomi moneter yang cukup kondusif, suku bunga SBI 1 bulan telah cenderung menurun dari 17,5% pada awal Januari 2002 menjadi 15,17% pada minggu pertama Juni 2002. Suku bunga Intervensi Rupiah juga telah diturunkan 100 bps untuk semua tenor, sehingga menjadi 14,125% - 14,875% untuk jangka waktu overnight sampai 7 hari. Penurunan suku bunga SBI dan Intervensi Rupiah tersebut juga telah diikuti oleh penurunan suku bunga deposito dan kredit perbankan. Dewasa ini suku bunga deposito berada pada 13,73%, sementara suku bunga kredit modal kerja sekitar 19,25%. Anggota Dewan yang terhormat, Di bidang perbankan, pada awal tahun 2002, kinerja perbankan nasional menunjukkan beberapa perbaikan yang tercermin dari peningkatan penghimpunan dana dan pemberian kredit, perbaikan aspek permodalan, perbaikan non performing loan (NPL) serta meningkatnya net interest margin (NIM). Meskipun demikian, perbankan masih menghadapi tantangan berupa fungsi intermediasi yang belum pulih secepat yang diharapkan guna mendukung proses pemulihan ekonomi. GAM BARAN UMUM KONDISI KEUANGAN BANK INDONESIA 2003 Anggota Dewan yang terhormat, Sebagaimana kami sampaikan di awal, dalam menyusun anggaran tahunan Bank Indonesia (ATBI), Bank Indonesia melakukannya secara berhati-hati, sejalan dengan proyeksi kondisi dan perkembangan ekonomi yang diharapkan terjadi pada tahun berjalan. Dari sisi pertumbuhan ekonomi, dapat kami sampaikan bahwa prospek ekonomi Indonesia tahun 2003 akan dapat tumbuh lebih tinggi dibanding dengan tahun 2002. Kemajuan dalam pelaksanaan program-program ekonomi dan keuangan yang ditempuh pemerintah dan Bank Indonesia diharapkan dapat meningkatkan kepercayaan dunia usaha (business confidence). Hal ini selanjutnya diharapkan dapat menjadi daya tarik masuknya modal asing ke Indonesia. Prospek ekonomi yang lebih baik di tahun 2003 juga didorong oleh kondisi perekonomian dunia yang diperkirakan akan membaik secara signifikan. Ekonomi dunia diperkirakan akan tumbuh sebesar 4,1% pada tahun 2003, jauh lebih tinggi dibandingkan dengan tahun sebelumnya yang diperkirakan sebesar 2,7%. Ekspor Indonesia diharapkan akan tumbuh lebih tinggi dengan perkembangan di sisi eksternal ini. Dengan berbagai perkiraan membaiknya kondisi di sisi internal dan eksternal tersebut, Bank Indonesia memprakirakan pertumbuhan ekonomi 2003 dapat mencapai sekitar 4,2 - 5,2%. Pertumbuhan ekonomi 2003 diprakirakan masih akan berasal dari pertumbuhan konsumsi, walaupun dengan pertumbuhan yang semakin menurun. Sementara itu, investasi diprakirakan akan mengalami pertumbuhan yang lebih tinggi dari tahun 2002 sejalan dengan menurunnya ketidakpastian di bidang politik dan keamanan serta menurunnya suku bunga di dalam negeri. Peran ekspor dalam pertumbuhan ekonomi juga diperkirakan akan meningkat seiring dengan meningkatnya permintaan barang-barang ekspor Indonesia. Dari sisi penawaran, pertumbuhan ekonomi diprakirakan disumbang oleh seluruh sektor ekonomi. Sementara itu, nilai tukar rupiah diprakirakan memiliki potensi untuk terus menguat. Dalam tahun 2003, rata-rata nilai tukar rupiah diperkirakan menguat dalam kisaran Rp 8.500 - Rp 9.500. Hal ini akan terjadi sepanjang faktor-faktor berikut dapat dipenuhi sehingga pada gilirannya dapat memperbaiki persepsi pelaku pasar, yaitu: kemajuan yang berarti dalam program restrukturisasi ekonomi dan keuangan, perbaikan kondisi dunia usaha, penyaluran kredit ke sector riil telah berjalan dengan baik, peningkatan investasi dari luar negeri, dan kemajuan yang signifikan dalam penjualan aset oleh BPPN dan privatisasi BUMN. Prakiraan ini akan menjadi lebih optimis apabila terdapat harapan terus membaiknya risiko politik, keuangan, dan ekonomi. Sementara itu, terkait dengan proyeksi laju inflasi, dapat kami sampaikan bahwa prospek inflasi pada tahun 2003 diperkirakan akan menurun menjadi sekitar 8%- 10%. Hal ini sejalan dengan perkiraan nilai tukar yang akan menguat sehingga akan menurunkan harga-harga barang impor dan biaya produksi di dalam negeri.
