Di satu sisi, dengan perkiraan akan menurunnya laju inflasi dan menguatnya nilai tukar Rupiah, suku bunga SBI pada tahun 2003 diperkirakan akan menurun dibandingkan dengan tahun 2002. Namun di sisi lain, sejalan dengan meningkatnya aktivitas perekonomian, maka diperkirakan uang primer juga akan mengalami peningkatan. Hal ini akan berakibat pada meningkatnya volume SBI yang harus dikeluarkan Bank Indonesia dalam rangka pengendalian moneter. Dengan demikian, secara keseluruhan beban pengeluaran pengendalian moneter diperkirakan akan mengalami peningkatan pada tahun 2003. Sementara itu, dari sisi penerimaan, dapat kami kemukakan bahwa sebagian besar berasal dari hasil penanaman yang dilakukan Bank Indonesia atas cadangan devisa. Dalam hubungan ini, kecenderungan suku bunga internasional pada tahun 2003, yang akan mempengaruhi penerimaan pengelolaan devisa dalam valuta asing, diperkirakan akan sedikit mengalami peningkatan. Namun di sisi lain, sejalan dengan perkiraan nilai tukar Rupiah yang akan menguat sebagaimana dikemukakan sebelumnya, maka penerimaan pengelolaan devisa jika dikonversi ke Rupiah diperkirakan akan mengalami penurunan. Sementara itu, penerimaan bunga yang diharapkan dari SUP belum dapat direalisasikan. Dengan gambaran penerimaan dan pengeluaran seperti di atas, secara umum dapat kami sampaikan bahwa kondisi keuangan Bank Indonesia pada tahun 2003 diperkirakan masih akan menghadapi beban yang cukup berat. Hal ini perlu menjadi perhatian kita bersama mengingat pentingnya menjaga kondisi keuangan bank sentral dalam rangka melaksanakan tugasnya untuk menjaga kestabilan nilai Rupiah yang diperlukan bagi kesinambungan proses pemulihan ekonomi nasional. Untuk itu, dipandang perlu untuk meneruskan upaya-upaya mencari alternatif instrumen moneter yang dapat mengurangi biaya pengendalian moneter. Salah satu cara yang dapat ditempuh adalah dengan menggunakan surat utang negara sebagai alternatif instrumen moneter seperti yang dilakukan di banyak negara lain, di samping peran pentingnya sebagai acuan dalam pembentukan struktur suku bunga jangka menengah - panjang di pasar. Jakarta, 10 Juni 2002

Title: Penjelasan Dewan Gubernur Bank Indonesia Pada Rapat Kerja Dengan Komisi IX DPR RI Tanggal 20 November 2002
text: EXPLANATION OF THE BOARD OF GOVERNORS OF BANK INDONESIA AT THE WORKING MEETING WITH COMMISSION IX OF THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES ON 20 NOVEMBER 2002 9595959595959595959595959595959595959595959595959595959595 Dear Members of the Council, First of all, let us thank the Chairman of Commission IX of the House of Representatives and all members of the House for inviting us to attend the Working Meeting today. Not to forget, on this good occasion also, let us express our congratulations on performing fasting services for the Councillors who are carrying out this Ramadan fasting service. For us, today's Working Meeting has an important meaning , especially considering some of the agendas and issues that will be specifically discussed -- namely the problem of bank settlement in liquidation , the 2003 Bank Indonesia Budget plan, as well as the National Banking Lanscape-which is essentially part of the agenda we are currently finalizing, and is a part that is not separated from the duties in the field of monetary, banking, and payment systems as well as the internal management that we have been carrying out so far . Therefore, in this Working Meeting, in addition to these specific issues, let us briefly convey the developments and policies in the monetary field. , banking, and sistem payments for the period up to November 2002 especially regarding the impact of the Bali tragedy. Within that framework, as members of the Board already know, as a fulfillment of the mandate outlined in Law No. 23 of 1999 concerning Bank Indonesia, especially article 58 paragraph 3, on Every quarter we have submitted a Progress Report on the Implementation of Bank Indonesia's Duties and Authorities to the House of Representatives (DPR). The last Quarterly Report we submitted to the Board Members is the Quarterly Report 111-2002 (July - September 2002) which we submitted in October 2002. Dear Members of the Council, We should be grateful because until October 2002, monetary-economic developments continued to show a stable development, even though it had been colored by the bombing tragedy in Bali. The maintained economic and monetary stability in October 2002 is reflected in the relatively controlled inflation rate, primary money which is still below its educational target , as well as relatively stable interest rates. The bombing in Bali did cause the depreciation of the rupiah exchange rate, but the depreciation of the rupiah can be minimized. Meanwhile, the bank intermediation function continued to improve in the form of an increase in deposits and the disbursement of new loans, including loans to SMEs, in line with the gradual reduction in interest rates. The development of prices reflected in the CPI in October 2002 was recorded at 0.54%, relatively no different from 0.53% in the previous month (m-t-m). On an annual basis, inflation still shows a decrease from 10.48% in September 2002 to 10.33% (y-o-y), while in the first ten months of 2002 inflation has reached 6.74% (y-t-d). The effect of rising fuel (diesel) prices and the regulation of sugar import trade arrangements as well as a slight stagnation in the flow of goods distribution became the source of inflationary pressures in October 2002. Meanwhile, the Indonesian economy in the quarter of 111-2002 experienced a growth of 3.92% compared to the same quarter of 2001. The growth rate was higher than expected although the domestic consumption boost still showed slowing growth. Economic growth also increased by 2.39% compared to the previous quarter, while in three quarters, economic growth rose by 3.39%. Private consumption as a driving force for growth continued to increase by 4.9% although it slowed down compared to the previous quarter, 6.3%. On the other hand, government consumption increased by 15.95%. Meanwhile, the increase in exports in the quarter of 111-2002 reached 1.61%, while investment activities, in the quarter of 111-2002, reached an increase of 2.1% compared to the same period the previous year, although cumulatively in three quarters it decreased by -3.65%. Meanwhile, the rupiah exchange rate in October 2002 tended to weaken. The rupiah exchange rate closed at a level of Rp9,215 per US dollar at the end of October 2002 or point-to-point depreciated 215 points (2.3%) compared to the previous month of Rp9,000 per US dollar. The weakening of the exchange rate was mainly due not only to the negative sentiment of market participants in responding to the bomb blasts in Bali, but also due to regional factors. Nevertheless, the Government's efforts in rehabilitating the impact of Bali and its handling measures, as well as Bank Indonesia's efforts to maintain rupiah exchange rate stability have been able to minimize further rupiah exchange rate declines. In line with controlled inflation and exchange rates, as well as the development of primary money, the development of primary money is also under control and below the established indicative target, monetary policy is directed to maintain positive expectations of economic actors on the prospect of economic recovery by continuing to provide signals that are expected to further stimulate business activities in the real sector. Efforts to stimulate economic activity in the real sector have been carried out by Bank Indonesia since early 2002 by continuing to signal a gradual, consistent and prudent reduction in the SBI rate. Until October, the SBI interest rate had decreased despite slowing down. The Weighted Average (PRC) 1-month SBI interest rate decreased by 12 bps from 13.22% in September 2002 to 13.10% at the end of October 2002. In relation to the development of primary money, although there was a decrease in confindence due to the Bali tragedy, the condition of primary money still followed its seasonal pattern and there was no excessive withdrawal of currency. Primary money is still in a safe position. In October, primary money was recorded at Rp124.7 trillion, or an increase of Rp0.9 trillion compared to the position at the end of September 2002. Dear Members of the Council, In the banking sector, we can report that in line with monetary stability and signals of lower SBI interest rates, banking performance until September also improved, as indicated by progress in outstanding credit indicators, new lending, Non-Performing Loans (NPL), and capital. The banking intermediation function as of September 2002 showed that conditions continued to improve as reflected in deposits that increased from Rp811.2 trillion to Rp815.0 trillion (0.47%). Meanwhile, credit position increased by around Rp10.6 trillion (2.82%) from Rp377.0 trillion to Rp387.7 trillion. On the other hand, the approval of the new credit ceiling reached the level of Rp18.5 trillion or a decrease of Rp4.1 trillion when compared to the previous month which reached Rp22.6 trillion. From the approval of the new credit ceiling, a withdrawal of IDR 11.1 trillion has been made, of which IDR 3.6 trillion or 32% of which is the distribution of loans to debtors with a credit ceiling below IDR 5 billion (microcredit), Small Business Loans (KUK), and Medium Enterprises Loans (SMEs). Thus the number of new loans that have been disbursed to SMEs during 2002 reached Rp24.7 trillion. A significant increase in new credit realisations in the reporting month (the largest during 2002), saw the Loan to Deposit Ratio (LDR) ratio increase by 108 points from 35.82% in August to 36.90% in September. In line with the improving banking conditions, bank policy adopted by Bank Indonesia remains focused on continuing the banking restructuring program and continuing to accelerate the recovery of the banking intermediation function. In line with that, Bank Indonesia continues to maximize the implementation of the 25 Basle Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision, the elaboration of which is enshrined in the Master Plan for Improving the Effectiveness of Bank Supervision. Meanwhile, steps to accelerate the recovery of the banking intermediation function will continue to be carried out by encouraging the banking industry to channel more credit to sectors that are anglicized by gaps. is ready and has relatively low risks such as export credit and credit for SMEs while still paying attention to the principle of sound credit. Dear Members of the Council, Specifically regarding the development of the Settlement of 16 Banks in Liquidation, we would like to inform you that the implementation of the liquidation of 16 BDL was carried out by the Liquidation Team (TL) formed by the GMS as stipulated in the Regulations Government No. 25 of 1999 dated May 3, 1999 concerning The Revocation of Business Licenses, Dissolution and liquidation of Bank (PP) and Decree of the Board of Directors of Bank Indonesia No. 32/53/KEP/DIR dated May 14, 1999 concerning Procedures for Revocation of Business Licenses, Dissolution and Liquidation of Commercial Banks (SK Dir). Based on the aforementioned PP and SK, TL, among others, is tasked with (i) conducting an inventory of BDL's wealth and obligations, (ii) determining the mode of liquidation , preparing a work plan and budget, (iii) prepare the Verification Balance sheet and the Final Balance sheet of liquidation, and (iv) hold an AGM at the end of the liquidation implementation In order for TL to carry out the saplings of these tasks properly, the TL is given the authority to, among other things: a. conduct negotiations and other actions in the framework of the sale of property and collection of debtors, b. negotiate and pay obligations to creditors, c. request the court to cancel all legal actions of the Bank, which resulted in losses of bank assets committed within 1 (one) year prior to the revocation of the business license. d. filing a lawsuit or claim against the bank's managing agent and/or shareholders who participated is the cause of the financial difficulties faced by the bank or is the cause of the bank's failure. We can say that the liquidation process is carried out no later than 5 (five) years from theformation of the Liquidation Team. Furthermore, if within the intended period the liquidation of the bank cannot be completed while there are still unsold BDL assets , then TL can sell the remaining assets in question by auction through the State Auction Office or other institutions using the highest bidding method no later than 6 (six) months from the end of the liquidation period bank. Considering that 16 BDL were revoked their business licenses on November 1, 1997, the establishment of TL by the GMS was admitted in November - December 1997, then according to the provisions mentioned above the period of service of TL BDL will end around November - December 2002 or around May - June 2003 if an auction is held after the end of liquidation. Dear Y ang Councillor, In addition to providing liquidity assistance in the form of debit balances as an effort to save banks before liquidation, the Government also takes a policy by providing bailouts for payments to all depositors, depositors and depositors, who agreed to pay arrears of interbank debt and trade finance obligations including to 16 BDL. The amount of Rp and Foreign Currency bailouts and debit balances that have been given as well as the amount of repayment that has been made 16 BDL per position on September 30, 2002 as in the following table this: No Information Initial balance Redemption Final balance 1. Rp bailout fund IDR 5.34 trillion IDR 2.12 trillion (39.7%) IDR 3.21 trillion 2. Va bailout USD 43.9 million USD 22,7 million (51,7%) USD 21,2 million 3. Debit balance IDR 6.16 trillion - IDR 6.16 trillion All such bailouts and debit balances have been dissregarded to the Government based on a cessie deed between the Governor of Bank Indonesia and the Government of BPPN dated February 22, 1999. Based on Article 9 of the Government Regulation and Article 19 of the Decree of The Directorate, Bank Indonesia has the authority to supervise the implementation of the dissolution of legal entities and liquidation of banks. The supervisory function of bank liquidation by Bank Indonesia is intended to monitor the implementation of bank liquidation carried out by TL so as not to keepg from the applicable provisions. Meanwhile, the role of the Government and IBRA is related to the cessie transfer of BLBI to the Government, including the transfer of bailouts and negative current account balances. In this regard, if it is related to the liquidation provisions, the position of the Government cq IBRA against BDL is that it is the party that replaces the position of the depository customer funds and other creditors fyide Article 17 PP and Article 40 letter b and e SK Dir). Based on data from TL, as of September 2002 the number of BDL assets that have been disbursed is around Rp3.4 trillion. Meanwhile, the total BDL obligations that have been settled are around Rp 6.4 trillion. The low proceeds from asset sales and credit collection carried out by TL are dueto various obstacles faced by TL, namely : - The legality of assets in the form of fixed assets controlled by TL is very weak, including the absence of a power of attorney to sell from the owner, fixed property on behalf of other parties. - Credit is mostly given to parties related to the crediting process that is not based on sound credit provisions such as weak credit analysis, weak collateral insufficient provisions , collateral in the form of Personal Guarantees, collateral in the name of other parties and so on. As a result of this, almost all loans given to related parties are bad debts that are difficult to collect - It requires considerable costs both for credit collection and in the asset disbursement process, especially costs for managing credit collection / collateral execution and asset disbursement so that the final result obtained is reduced - There is a credit collection that is settled through legal process and to date belum obtained a judgment of permanent force With the picture of the development above, as well as considering the condition of the remaining problematic assets, it is estimated that more intensive efforts will still be needed so that at the end of the liquidation of all BDL it is expected that dapat settle all its obligations including obligations to the Government in the form of bailouts and debit balances. Dear Members of the Council, Furthermore, as part of the direction of national banking policy in the future, we have reviewed and formulated the policy direction in the Indonesian Banking Architecture (API) which is some in the past it was known as the National Banking Landscape . Let us give a little description of the national banking landscape as follows. As is understandable, Indonesian banking has been believed by various groups, domestically and internationally, to be the industry worst affected by the Asian financial crisis that has lasted since mid-1997. As a result of the crisis, there were closures (liquidations) of banks and mergers which had an impact on reducing the number of banks from 239 banks in 1996 to 141 banks in November 2002. Although the banking industry in recent years has shown improving conditions, it is still felt to be vulnerable to internal and external pressures. In addition, the development of increasingly complex banking products/services is accompanied by increasingly diverse risks in line with the development of information technology and economic globalization, demands a more solid banking order that is able to face all changes in the future and ensure financial system stability. In connection with the foregoing, it is necessary to compile an Indonesian Banking Architecture as a "policy direction" for the national banking system. Within that framework, the vision of The Indonesian Banking Architecture is to achieve a sound, strong and efficient banking system in order to realize financial system stability and promote national economic development. To realize the vision of the Indonesian Banking Architecture mentioned above, we have set several goals to be achieved, namely: 1. The creation of a healthy domestic banking tour receipt that is able to meet the needs of the community to encourage sustainable national economic development. 2. The creation of a banking industry that is strong and has high competitiveness and has resilience in responding torisks. 3. The creation of good corporate governance in order to strengthen the internal conditions of the national banking system. 4. The creation of an effective system of bank regulation and supervision and referring to international standards. 5. The realization of a complete infrastructure to support the creation of a healthy banking industry. 6. The realization of consumer empowerment and protection of banking service users. Dear Members of the Council, The preparation of the Indonesian Banking Architecture in addition to considering important issues in the banking industry, also considers the influence of dynamic factors that are beyond the control of the banking industry such as macroeconomic stability, legal framework, globalization, information technology developments, stakeholder commitment and social, political and security stability as well as the application of regional autonomy. In this regard, Bank Indonesia has established 6 (six) pillars that form the foundation for the Indonesian Banking Architecture, namely: 1. A sound banking structure that is able to encourage national economic development and international competitiveness; 2. Strengthening the internal conditions of the banking industry; 3. An effective regulatory system capable of anticipating the development of domestic and international financial markets; 4. Independent and effective bank supervision system; 5. Creation and strengthening of supporting infrastructure for the banking industry; 6. Customer protection and empowerment. Some of the steps that have been taken to answer the six pillars in the framework of the preparation of the Indonesian Banking Architecture above include: (i) conducting preliminary studies and research particularly on strategic issues of the banking industry, as well as (ii) holding a limited series of meetings and discussions with banking experts and practitioners, Banking Associations, Government Governments intah Daerah, Regional Chamber of Commerce and Industry, academics and students. Some things that can be concluded from the limited meetings and discussions include the concept of financial services under one roof (universal banking), the need for an ideal bank, bank status foreign exchange/non-foreign exchange, the role of Regional Development Banks in Regional Autonomy and efforts to protect and empower consumers. Considering that the Indonesian Banking Architecture is comprehensive, its preparation requires a fairly long time and is expected to be completed by the end of 2003. Furthermore, the implementation of the Indonesian Banking Architecture will be carried out in stages for a span of 10 years, starting in 2004. Dear Councillors, To achieve the objectives of the Indonesian Banking Architecture , there are several preconditions needed for the Indonesian Banking Architecture to be implemented. Some of these preconditions include macroeconomic stability, social stability, politics and security, adequate information technology, and commitment from stakeholders. The precondition in our opinion is very important because both macroeconomic stability and social, political and security stability are dynamic conditions that are directly or will indirectly affect the development of the banking industry. In addition, the availability of information technology and the commitment of stakeholders will greatly determine the implementation process and achievement of the vision of the Indonesian Banking Infrastructure, so that will determine the shape of the banking industry in the future. We realize that the preparation of the Indonesian Banking Architecture needs to accommodate various inputs and suggestions from various interested parties in the banking industry so that the Indonesian Banking Architecture can effectively implemented. In that regard, we sincerely expect input and suggestions from respected members of the Board as one of the parties with an interest in the banking industry to improve the drafting of Indonesian Banking Architecture . Dear Members of the Council, In order to support the effectiveness of monetary policy implementation and encourage efforts to create a sound banking system, Bank Indonesia has also continued various improvement efforts to creating an efficient, fast, secure, and reliable national payment system. Broadly speaking, the policy in the payment system consists of policies in the cash and non-cash payment systems. In the field of cash payment systems, Bank Indonesia strives to meet the public's needs for banknotes and coins for payment purposes and to maintain the money in circulation. In this regard, we need to state about the efforts we take in tackling the circulation of counterfeit money in the community, Bank Indonesia continues to increase various efforts both preventive and repressive, among others, through research on the elements of security features of money that use higher technology so that it will make it difficult for counterfeiting, implement socialization measures regarding the characteristics of the authenticity of rupiah currency to various groups of people through the mass media, the provision of information facilities in the form of hotline services and research on the elements of money security using higher technology so that it will make it difficult for counterfeiting. To make it easier for the public to distinguish between real rupiah and counterfeit rupiah currency, Bank Indonesia has conducted an assessment of the improvement of existing security elements, especially in denomination banknotes of Rp 50,000, Rp 20,000, and Rp 10,000. In addition to these efforts, Bank Indonesia continues to cooperate with relevant agencies, including the Coordinating Board for the Eradication of Counterfeit Money (BOTASUPAL) and the Indonesian National Police in the eradication of counterfeit money, among others by providing training at formal educational institutions for police officers. In the field of non-cash payment systems, the policy is directed at reducing payment risks and improving the quality and service capacity of payment systems. The measures taken to reduce payment system risk are through the implementation of the Bank Indonesia-Rea/ Time Gross Settlement (BI-RTGS) system, which we plan to implement by the end of 2002. Some other policies adopted to reduce payment system risk include the implementation of lowering the nominal limit (capping) of credit notes through the clearing system, the preparation of schemes to overcome the failure of clearing participants in settling settlement obligations. The policies to improve the quality and capacity of payment system services include the development of intercity clearing, the development of clearing automation in several KBI and the improvement of the blue print of the National Payment System. Dear Members of the Council, We recognize that the quality and effectiveness of policies in the monetary, banking, and payment systems that we formulate, establish, and implement ultimately are largely determined also by the quality of human resources we have and solid organizational support. Within that framework, in line with Bank Indonesia's Transformation program that has been launched since 2001, we have entered a process of change in the organization towards a new organization that is better able to anticipate and adapt to global changes and meet the expectations of Bank Indonesia stakeholders. This demand for fundamental change is partly due to the existence of a new law No. 23 of 1999. Because the mandate in the new law requires adjustments to the vision, mission, mindset, culture and commitment of all Bank Indonesia employees. The internal change program has continued to roll out until now we have successfully carried out and has gone through several stages. Some of the organizational change projects carried out include the implementation of a system New Planning, Budgeting, and Performance Management. Within the framework of the new Planning, Budgeting and Performance Management System and based on the main foundations of Law No. 23 of 1999, we compiled the 2003 Bank Indonesia Annual Budget (ATBI). As members of the Board understand, we can say that the objective of Bank Indonesia as mandated by Law No. 23 of 1999 concerning Bank Indonesia is to achieve and maintain rupiah stability both against goods and services (inflation rate) and against other countries' currencies (rupiah exchange rate). To achieve this task, Bank Indonesia has 3 (three) tasks that are interrelated with each other, namely: establishing and implementing monetary policy, regulating and maintaining a smooth payment system and supervising banks. In order to carry out the duties and objectives set forth, Bank Indonesia shall prepare an annual work plan prepared with reference to the strategic objectives of Bank Indonesia prepared by the Board of Governors. The strategic objectives are prepared based on the mission, vision and strategic values of Bank Indonesia. At the 2002 Strategic Forum which was attended by all work units, the Board of Governors has set strategic goals which are further elaborated into the activities of each work unit, both units at the Head Office, Bank Indonesia offices and at Representative Offices abroad. In 2002, in the financial and budgetary sector, Bank Indonesia continued to strive to reach a meeting point to resolve issues related to Bank Indonesia Liquidity Assistance (BLBI), so that in June 2002 the main points of agreement with the government were reached. The points of agreement need to be elaborated into a more detailed agreement between the Government and Bank Indonesia and in due course will be reported by the Government to the House of Representatives. To carry out the duties of Bank Indonesia as described above, the preparation of the Bank Indonesia Annual Budget for 2003 is based on the principle of prudence and efficiency improvement, in line with projected economic conditions and developments in 2003. The assumptions used in preparing the 2003 budget are: economic growth of 4%, inflation rate of 8%, interest rates set in the range of 12% to 12% sd. 13%, exchange rate of Rp/USD of Rp9,000, interest rate on foreign loans ranges from 1.5% to 1.5% sd. 2.5%, New Government Bonds (SUP) have been implemented, and efficiency improvements have been made. In addition to the assumptions of the 2003 budget that have been set out above, the preparation of the 2003 ATBI is also based on the realization of the 2002 budget both on the revenue side and on the expenditure side. Budget realization in terms of revenue until October 2002 was Rp25,446 billion, or 98% of atbi FY-2002 of Rp26,093 billion. The foreign exchange management sector contributed 72% to Bank Indonesia's revenues in 2002. In addition, revenue from credit provision is the second largest revenue contributing sector or 27%. In terms of expenditure, budget realization in the same position reached Rp 19,328 billion or 66% of the FY-2002 ATBI of Rp29,239 billion. Expenditures in the context of determining and implementing monetary policy are the largest component of expenditures, amounting to Rpl 6,875 billion or 87%, including for SBI interest costs and rupiah interventions of Rpl 3,724 billion and foreign exchange management costs. Meanwhile, expenditures for the regulation and smoothness of the payment system amounted to Rp843 billion or 4%. Then the bank regulation and supervision sector and the internal resource management sector posted expenditures of IDR 54 billion (0.2%) and IDR 556 billion (8%), respectively. Up to the same position, Bank Indonesia's surplus was recorded at Rp6,118 billion. Based on the realization of the 2002 budget and taking into account economic conditions and socio-political developments that occurred, atbi in 2003 it is estimated that the number of receipts will decrease when compared to 2002. The relatively stable movement of the USD exchange rate and the reduction in interest rates on foreign assets have resulted in revenues in terms of foreign exchange management activities tending to decrease. Meanwhile, other revenue components, namely receipts from the implementation of the payment system as well as banking regulation and supervision, tend to remain. On the expenditure side, the expenditure burden of monetary control is expected to decrease as the SBI interest rate and rupiah intervention are expected to be lowered. Spending from the payment system sector and bank supervision tends to increase because in 2003 improvements were still being made in the national payment system and procedures and increased costs in regulating and supervising banks. Referring to the estimated receipts that tend to decrease and the estimated expenditures which although the changes are relatively small, in 2003 the amount of receipts will be smaller than the amount of expenditure. Efforts to optimize revenue and cost efficiency will be carried out, including the following: a. Improving acceptance by optimizing existing sources of acceptance and exploring new sources of acceptance, b. Improving the cost efficiency of monetary control, c. Improve the cost efficiency of internal resource management. Through savings and budget implementation that adheres to the principle of prudence, it is hoped that the objectives and duties of Bank Indonesia can be carried out properly. Dear Members of the Council, Taking into account monetary and banking economic conditions in October as well as the potential for increased price pressures until the end of 2002, Bank Indonesia estimates that economic growth will be slightly lower due to lower investment and export realization than previously estimated. The impact of the Bali tragedy on macroeconomics in the short term is expected to affect foreign exchange receipts, especially the tourism sector. Meanwhile, the rupiah exchange rate for the rest of 2002 is expected to stabilize within the expected range. Inflationary pressures in the last two months of 2002 are expected to be higher than originally expected in line with the increase in demand in the face of religious holidays and the end of the year as well as the realization of an increase in retail selling prices (HJE) and cigarette excise in November 2002. In relation to the increasing demand for public goods and services, Bank Indonesia considers that supply-side policy needs attention, especially regarding the increase in supply and the smooth flow of goods distribution. In line with that, monetary policy adopted by Bank Indonesia continues to maintain economic liquidity conditions to match the real needs of the economy. Considering that future inflationary pressures are more influenced by seasonal factors and government policies in the field of prices, where core inflation is not affected much, monetary policy can be directed to accommodate economic growth. This policy direction is in line with efforts to stimulate the improving bank intermediation function, thereby ensuring the availability of financing for economic activities. In the banking sector, efforts to develop a sound banking system by adhering to the principle of banking prudence remain the main focus of the banking policy direction. In relation to efforts to rehabilitate the impact of the Bali tragedy, Bank Indonesia still has room to move and considers it necessary to support efforts to accelerate economic recovery after the Bali tragedy. In this regard, Bank Indonesia will ask the banks to restructure loans for debtors or businessmen directly affected by the Bali bombings, which the bank considers appropriate for a restructuring policy. To that end, Bank Indonesia will consider granting leeway to the provisions, especially the criteria for collectibility within a certain period of time to banks that restructure the loans in question. Dear Members of the Council, In closing, several improvements in economic-monetary conditions to date are expected to continue and can provide stimulus for further economic recovery efforts. Monetary policy measures adopted by Bank Indonesia are still directed at maintaining the positive expectations of these economic actors for the economic recovery prospects by continuing to provide signals to further stimulate business activities in the real sector. Improvements in the real sector are expected to be a stimulus for the banking system to more actively channel credit to the business world. However, it is also necessary to realize that the effectiveness of monetary policy will also be determined by support in the form of other economic policies. In addition, the alignment and coordination of macroeconomic policies, namely monetary, fiscal, and real sector policies, is also a proper factor. In addition, fertilizing similar views, partnerships, and deeper support between the Government, Bank Indonesia, and the House of Representatives and several other relevant agencies is also absolutely necessary. The continuity of the economic recovery process lies in the support of other policies that help the real sector in improving its production capacity, policies that are able to improve the competitiveness of domestic products in terms of production costs, policies to create jobs so as to maintain or even increase people's purchasing power, as well as policies that ensure social stability and security for business certainty. Jakarta, 20th November 2002

Tak lupa, dalam kesempatan yang baik ini pula, perkenankanlah kami menyampaikan ucapan selamat menunaikan ibadah puasa bagi Anggota Dewan yang menjalankan ibadah puasa Ramadhan ini. Bagi kami, Rapat Kerja pada hari ini memiliki makna yang penting terutama mengingat beberapa agenda dan permasalahan yang secara khusus akan dibahas -- yakni permasalahan penyelesaian bank dalam likuidasi, rencana Anggaran Bank Indonesia Tahun 2003, serta Lanscape Perbankan Nasional-yang pada dasarnya merupakan sebagian agenda yang saat ini tengah kami selesaikan, dan merupakan bagian yang tidak terpisahkan dari tugas-tugas di bidang moneter, perbankan, dan sistem pembayaran serta manajemen intern yang kami emban selama ini. Oleh karena itu, dalam Rapat Kerja kali ini, disamping permasalahan-permasalahan khusus tersebut, ijinkanlah kami menyampaikan secara singkat perkembangan dan kebijakan di bidang moneter, perbankan, dan sistem pembayaran periode sampai dengan bulan November 2002 khususnya menyangkut dampak dari tragedi Bali. Dalam kerangka itu, sebagaimana Anggota Dewan telah ketahui, sebagai pemenuhan amanat yang digariskan dalam Undang-Undang No. 23 Tahun 1999 tentang Bank Indonesia khususnya pasal 58 ayat 3, pada setiap triwulan kami telah menyampaikan Laporan Perkembangan Pelaksanaan Tugas dan Wewenang Bank Indonesia kepada Dewan Perwakilan Rakyat (DPR). Laporan Triwulanan yang terakhir kami sampaikan kepada Anggota Dewan yakni Laporan Triwulan 111-2002 (Juli - September 2002) dimana telah kami sampaikan pada bulan Oktober 2002. Anggota Dewan yang terhormat, Kita patut bersyukur karena sampai dengan bulan Oktober 2002, perkembangan ekonomi-moneter tetap menunjukkan perkembangan yang stabil, kendatipun telah diwarnai oleh peristiwa tragedi bom di Bali. Tetap terjaganya stabilitas ekonomi dan moneter pada bulan Oktober 2002 ini tercermin dari laju inflasi yang relatif terkendali, uang primer yang masih berada di bawah target indikatifnya, serta tingkat suku bunga relatif stabil. Peristiwa bom di Bali memang menyebabkan depresiasi nilai tukar rupiah, namun depresiasi rupiah tersebut dapat diminimalisir. Sementara itu, fungsi intermediasi perbankan terus membaik berupa peningkatan Dana Pihak Ketiga (DPK) dan penyaluran kredit baru termasuk kredit kepada UKM sejalan dengan penurunan suku bunga secara bertahap. Perkembangan harga-harga yang tercermin dalam IHK pada bulan Oktober 2002 tercatat sebesar 0,54%, relatif tidak berbeda dibandingkan 0,53% pada bulan sebelumnya (m-t-m). Secara tahunan inflasi masih menunjukkan penurunan dari 10,48% pada bulan September 2002 menjadi 10,33% (y-o-y), sementara dalam sepuluh bulan pertama tahun 2002 inflasi telah mencapai 6,74% (y-t-d). Pengaruh kenaikan harga BBM (solar) dan pengaturan tata-niaga impor gula serta sedikit tersendatnya arus distribusi barang menjadi sumber tekanan inflasi pada bulan Oktober 2002. Sementara itu, ekonomi Indonesia pada triwulan 111-2002 mengalami pertumbuhan 3,92% dibandingkan triwulan yang sama tahun 2001. Angka pertumbuhan tersebut lebih tinggi dari yang diperkirakan meskipun dorongan konsumsi domestik masih menunjukkan pertumbuhan yang melambat. Pertumbuhan ekonomi juga mengalami kenaikan sebesar 2,39% dibandingkan triwulan sebelumnya, sementara dalam tiga triwulan, pertumbuhan ekonomi naik 3,39%. Konsumsi swasta sebagai motor penopang pertumbuhan tetap mengalami kenaikan sebesar 4,9% meskipun melambat dibandinkgan triwulan sebelumnya, 6,3%. Di sisi lain, konsumsi pemerintah mengalami kenaikan sebesar 15,95%. Sementara itu, kenaikan ekspor pada triwulan 111-2002 mencapai sebesar 1,61%, sedangkan kegiatan investasi, pada triwulan 111-2002 ini mencapai kenaikan 2,1% dibandingkan periode yang sama tahun sebelumnya, meskipun secara kumulatif dalam tiga kuartal menurun -3,65%. Sementara nilai tukar rupiah pada bulan Oktober 2002 cenderung melemah. Nilai tukar rupiah ditutup pada level Rp9.215,- per dolar AS pada akhir bulan Oktober 2002 atau secara point-to-point melemah 215 poin (2,3%) dibandingkan dengan bulan sebelumnya Rp9.000,- per dolar AS. Melemahnya nilai tukar terutama disebabkan bukan hanya oleh faktor sentimen negatif pelaku pasar dalam menyikapi peledakan bom di Bali, tetapi juga karena faktor regional. Namun demikian, upaya Pemerintah dalam merehabilitasi dampak Bali dan langkah penanganannya, serta upaya Bank Indonesia dalam menjaga kestabilan nilai tukar rupiah telah dapat meminimalisasi penurunan nilai tukar rupiah lebih lanjut. Sejalan dengan terkendalinya inflasi dan nilai tukar, serta perkembangan uang primer juga terus terkendali dan berada di bawah target indikatif yang telah ditetapkan, maka kebijakan moneter diarahkan untuk tetap menjaga ekspektasi positif pelaku ekonomi tersebut terhadap prospek pemulihan ekonomi dengan terus memberikan sinyal yang diharapkan akan semakin mendorong kegiatan usaha di sektor riil. Upaya mendorong kegiatan ekonomi di sektor riil tersebut telah dilakukan Bank Indonesia sejak awal 2002 dengan terus memberikan sinyal penurunan suku bunga SBI sscara bertahap, konsisten dan berhati-hati. Sampai dengan bulan Oktober suku bunga SBI mengalami penurunan meskipun melambat. Rata-rata Tertimbang (RRT) suku bunga SBI 1 bulan menurun 12 bps dari 13,22% pada bulan September 2002 menjadi 13,10% pada akhir Oktober 2002. Berkaitan dengan perkembangan uang primer, kendatipun sempat terjadi penurunan confindence akibat tragedi Bali, namun kondisi uang primer masih mengikuti pola musimannya dan tidak terjadi penarikan uang kartal yang berlebihan. Uang primer masih dalam posisi yang aman. Pada bulan Oktober uang primer tercatat sebesar Rp124,7 triliun, atau mengalami peningkatan sebesar Rp0,9 triliun dibandingkan dengan posisi akhir bulan September 2002. Anggota Dewan yang terhormat, Di bidang perbankan, dapat kami laporkan bahwa sejalan dengan stabilitas moneter dan sinyal penurunan suku bunga SBI, kinerja perbankan sampai dengan bulan September juga membaik, seperti ditunjukkan oleh kemajuan dalam indikator outstanding kredit, penyaluran kredit baru, Non Performing Loan (NPL), dan permodalan. Fungsi intermediasi perbankan sampai dengan bulan September 2002 menunjukkan kondisi yang terus membaik sebagaimana tercermin dalam DPK yang meningkat dari Rp811,2 triliun menjadi Rp815,0 triliun (0,47%). Sementara itu, posisi kredit meningkat sekitar Rp10,6 triliun (2,82%) dari Rp377,0 triliun menjadi Rp387,7 triliun. Di sisi lain, persetujuan pagu kredit baru mencapai level Rp18,5 triliun atau menurun sebesar Rp4,1 triliun bila dibandingkan dengan bulan sebelumnya yang mencapai Rp22,6 triliun. Dari persetujuan pagu kredit baru tersebut, telah dilakukan penarikan sebesar Rp11,1 triliun yang Rp3,6 triliun atau 32% diantaranya merupakan penyaluran kredit kepada debitur dengan pagu kredit di bawah Rp5 miliar (kredit mikro), Kredit Usaha Kecil (KUK), dan Kredit Usaha Menengah (UKM). Dengan demikian jumlah kredit baru yang telah disalurkan kepada UKM selama tahun 2002 mencapai Rp24,7 triliun. Peningkatan realisasi kredit baru yang signifikan pada bulan laporan (terbesar selama tahun 2002), membuat rasio Loan to Deposit Ratio (LDR) meningkat sebesar 108 poin dari sebesar 35,82% pada bulan Agustus menjadi sebesar 36,90% pada bulan September. Sejalan dengan perbaikan kondisi perbankan tersebut, kebijakan perbankan yang ditempuh Bank Indoensia tetap difokuskan pada kelanjutan program restrukturisasi perbankan serta terus mendorong percepatan pemulihan fungsi intermediasi perbankan. Sejalan dengan itu, Bank Indonesia terus memaksimalkan penerapan 25 Basle Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision yang penjabarannya dituangkan dalam Master Plan Peningkatan Efektivitas Pengawasan Bank. Sementara itu, langkah percepatan pemulihan fungsi intermediasi perbankan terus dilakukan dengan mendorong perbankan untuk lebih banyak lagi menyalurkan kredit kepada sektor-sektor yang dianggap telah siap dan memiliki risiko yang relatif rendah seperti kredit ekspor dan kredit bagi UKM dengan tetap memperhatikan prinsip perkreditan yang sehat. Anggota Dewan yang terhormat, Khusus menyangkut perkembangan Penyelesaian 16 Bank Dalam Likuidasi, dapat kami sampaikan bahwa pelaksanaan likuidasi 16 BDL tersebut dilakukan oleh Tim Likuidasi (TL) yang dibentuk oleh RUPS yang diatur dalam Peraturan Pemerintah No 25 Tahun 1999 tanggal 3 Mei 1999 tentang Pencabutan Izin Usaha, Pembubaran dan likuidasi Bank (PP) dan Surat Keputusan Direksi Bank Indonesia No 32/53/KEP/DIR tangal 14 Mei 1999 tentang Tata Cara Pencabutan Izin Usaha, Pembubaran dan Likuidasi Bank Umum (SK Dir). Berdasarkan PP dan SK tersebut di atas, TL antara lain bertugas untuk (i) melakukan inventarisasi kekayaan dan kewajiban BDL, (ii) menentukan cara likuidasi, menyusun rencana kerja dan anggaran, (iii) menyusun Neraca Verifikasi dan Neraca Akhir Likuidasi, dan (iv) menyelenggarakan RUPS pada akhir pelaksanaan likuidasi Agar TL dapat melaksanakan tugas-tugas tersebut dengan baik, maka TL diberikan kewenangan untuk antara lain: a. melakukan perundingan dan tindakan lainnya dalam rangka penjualan harta kekayaan dan penagihan terhadap debitur, b. melakukan perundingan dan pembayaran kewajiban kepada kreditur, c. meminta pengadilan untuk membatalkan segala perbuatan hukum Bank, yang mengakibatkan kerugian harta bank yang dilakukan dalam jangka waktu 1 (satu) tahun sebelum pencabutan izin usaha. d. mengajukan gugatan atau tuntutan kepada pengurus dan atau pemegang saham bank yang turut serta menjadi penyebab kesulitan keuangan yang dihadapi bank atau menjadi penyebab kegagalan bank. Dapat kami sampaikan bahwa proses likuidasi dilaksanakan selambat- lambatnya 5 (lima) tahun terhitung sejak terbentuknya Tim Likuidasi. Selanjutnya apabila dalam jangka waktu dimaksud likuidasi bank tidak dapat diselesaikan sementara masih terdapat aset BDL yang belum terjual, maka TL dapat menjual sisa aset dimaksud secara lelang melalui Kantor Lelang Negara atau lembaga lainnya dengan menggunakan metode penawaran tertinggi selambat-lambatnya 6 (enam) bulan sejak berakhirnya jangka waktu pelaksanaan likuidasi bank.
