Hal ini disebabkan oleh faktor bisnis model industri keuangan syariah di Indonesia, khususnya perbankan syariah, yang lebih fokus pada pemenuhan kebutuhan di sektor riil dan sangat menjaga 'maqasid syariah'. Hal ini berbeda dengan negara lain yang peranan produk-produk di sektor keuangan (pasar uang dan pasar modal) lebih dominan. Secara esensi, struktur pengembangan keuangan syariah di Indonesia akan lebih kuat dibanding dengan negara lain. Kekurangan instrumen di pasar keuangan syariah tersebut berdampak pada pengelolaan likuiditas perbankan syariah. Pengelolaan likuiditas perbankan syariah masih mengandalkan mekanisme Pasar Uang Antar Bank Syariah (PUAS) dengan menggunakan instrumen Sertifikat Investasi Mudharabah (SIMA), dan melakukan penempatan di instrumen yang diterbitkan oleh Bank Indonesia, yakni FASBI Syariah dan SBI Syariah. Masih sedikit sekali portofolio penempatan pada instrumen sukuk. Tingginya porsi pengelolaan likuiditas perbankan syariah pada instrumen bank sentral menyebabkan pengembangan pasar keuangan syariah menjadi terkendala dan mekanisme self adjustment menjadi kurang optimal. Penerbitan Surat Perbendaharaan Negara Syariah (SPNS) dan mekanisme transaksi 'komoditi murabahah' dapat menjadi suatu terobosan instrumen yang dapat digunakan oleh perbankan syariah dalam melakukan pengelolaan likuiditasnya. Ketersediaan instrumen pengelolaan likuiditas menjadi sangat penting dalam mencegah terjadinya krisis yang berkelanjutan pada industri keuangan syariah. Para pakar yang tergabung dalam IAEI dapat membantu industri dalam melakukan inovasi produk keuangan syariah, khususnya untuk perbankan syariah. Agar jangan sampai kekurangan instrumen keuangan syariah tersebut diisi oleh instrumen dari negara lain yang belum tentu sesuai dengan kondisi pasar keuangan dan perbankan syariah domestik. Kendala lainnya yang perlu mendapat perhatian serius adalah upaya untuk memenuhi gap SDI dari tenaga kerja domestik agar tidak diisi oleh tenaga kerja asing. Perlu disaari bahwa salah satu butir kesepakatan dalam MEA 2015 adalah freedom of movement for skilled and talented labours. Hal ini merupakan tantangan yang serius, mengingat pusat-pusat pendidikan dan pelatihan keuangan dan perbankan syariah berada di luar negeri seperti Bahrain, Uni Emirat Arab, dan Malaysia. Pelaku industri perbankan syariah dapat bekerjasama mendirikan 'pusat pendidikan dan pelatihan perbankan syariah' untuk mencetak tenaga ahli guna memenuhi gap tersebut daripada saling bersaing dan melakukan 'pembajakan pegawai'. IAEI tentunya dapat berperan dalam menyediakan tenaga ahli untuk mengajar di pusat pendidikan dan pelatihan tersebut. Agar lebih terarah dan tepat guna, IAEI juga dapat membantu melakukan penelitian untuk mengidentifikasi jenis-jenis keahlian yang dibutuhkan oleh industri perbankan syariah sehingga strategi 'link and match' dapat dijalankan. Penutup Berbagai peluang dan tantangan di atas menunjukkan bahwa upaya keras dari seluruh stake holders industri keuangan syariah sangat dibutuhkan. Perlu keterpaduan langkah dari para praktisi, akademisi maupun asosiasi agar pengembangan menjadi lebih efektif dan efisien karena dapat menghindari terjadinya redundancy dan suaranya menjadi lebih di dengar. Untuk itu, peran IAEI dalam mempelopori dan mendorong keterpaduan langkah untuk menjawab berbagai tantangan tersebut sangat diperlukan sehingga industri keuangan syariah nasional semakin berkualitas, berkembang secara berkelanjutan dan mampu bersaing dalam kancah persaingan global, khususnya dalam menyambut MEA 2015. *** 1 Disampaikan dalam Ceramah llmiah Ikatan Ahli Ekonomi Islam (IAEI), Milad ke-8 IAEI, 13 April 2012 2 Jumlah penduduk Indonesia berdasarkan sensus penduduk tahun 2010 mencapai 237,6 juta jiwa. 3 Dengan menggunakan asumsi nilai kurs sebesar Rp9.100/US$, maka nilai aset perbankan syariah pada akhir tahun 2011 mencapai US$16,37 miliar, outstanding sukuk (negara dan korporasi) sebesar US$4,41 miliar, asuransi syariah sebesar US$0,97 miliar, reksadana syariah sebesar US$0,61 miliar. 4 Berdasarkan Pasal 1 A ayat (1) huruf h UU No.42 Tahun 2009: 'penyerahan Barang Kena Pajak oleh Pengusaha Kena Pajak dalam rangka perjanjian pembiayaan yang dilakukan berdasarkan prinsip syariah, penyerahannya dianggap langsung dari Pengusaha Kena Pajak kepada pihakyang membutuhkan Barang Kena Pajak'. --------------- ------------------------------------------------------------ --------------- ------------------------------------------------------------

Title: Rapat Kerja BI dan Komisi IX DPR RI 9 Oktober 2001: Penjelasan Dewan Gubernur BI Atas Pertanyaan Lisan Anggota Komisi IX DPR RI dalam Raker 20 September 2001
text: WORKING MEETING BL AND COMMISSION IX DPR Rl Dated 9 October 2001: Explanation of the Board of Governors of BANK INDONESIA On Oral Questions of Members of Commission IX of the House of Representatives Rl submitted atthe Working Meeting on September 20, 2001 I. QUESTIONS CONCERNING THE MONETARY SPHERE A. Inflation Control Problems The Councillor who asked about the issue of controlling inflation was Sdr. Suratal HW, Sdr. Sudirman, Sdr. Abdullah Zainie, Sdr. Danial Tandjung, and Sdr. Abdullah Al Wahdi. Question : 1. Is there a new method of overcoming inflasi discovered by Bank Indonesia researchers? 2. Is the money supply that occurred at this time in accordance with the LOI/IMF? How does Bank Indonesia control primary money? 3. With the continued increase in interest rates in line with Bank Indonesia's efforts to control inflation, the burden on the state budget is getting bigger and the intermediation function is not working. It's best not to be too much of a problem that the economy is running. What is the point of low inflation (0%) if the economy stagnates? 4. Are there other attempts to suppress inflation and reduce the currency in circulation. Because what has been done so far has only resulted in an increase in interest rates which actually has a bad impact on other sectors. 5. When does Bank Indonesia start lowering the SBI rate? Answer : Dear Members of the Council, From the questions of the Board members , we can convey the following explanation: 1. Monetary Control Framework Judging from its duties and authorities, as mandated by Law No. 23 of 1999, Bank Indonesia has the aim of achieving and maintaining the stability of the rupiah . The stability of the rupiah value referred to in the article is the stability of the value of the rupiah against goods and services as measured by or reflected in the development of the inflation rate and against currencies of other countries that are measured by or reflected in the development of the rupiah exchange rate against the currencies of other countries. With the reformulation of objectives based on the Bank Indonesia Law, Bank Indonesia enters a new chapter and carries out its main task from multiple objectives to single objectives, namely achieving and maintaining stability of the rupiah value. In the field of exchange rates, under the current floating exchange rate system, the rupiah exchange rate is more determined by thestrength of supply and demand in the market. Bank Indonesia policy is thus not intended to direct exchange rate movements to reach a certain level, but rather to prevent exchange rate fluctuations which is excessive among others through the policy of increasing the supply in the forex market as long as necessary. In line with that, bank Indonesia's task is directed at maintaining price stability (inflation rate), in order to support sustainable economic development and improvement of the welfare of the people as described above. The formation of inflation is basically influenced by the interaction between demand and aggregate supply. The condition of aggregate demand is influenced by various variable developments originating from the side of public and government consumption, public and government investment, as well as from the external side. From the aggregate supply side, the developments that occur are largely influenced by the magnitude of input factors (labor and capital), government structural policies, unemployed production capacity and various shocks such as distribution disruptions and seasonal influences. Moving on from the results of the interaction of aggregate demand and supply, then macro-wise there will be one production gap either excess or reduced. In the condition of overproduction inequality, the inflationary pressures that occur will be reduced. Conversely, if the production gap that occurs is reduced, then normatively the inflation that occurs will increase. Inflationary pressures stemming from increased demand are known as demand pull inflation, while inflationary pressures caused by changes on the supply side are known as cost push inflation. In addition, inflationary pressures are also attributable to public inflation expectations, which, among others, can be triggered by government policies in the field of prices and income as well as rupiah depreciation. In relation to inflationary pressures stemming from the weakening of the rupiah exchange rate, we can explain that the effect of the exchange rate on inflation can occur either directly or indirectly. The direct impact of exchange rate depreciation on inflation (exchange rate pass through) is explained through changes in the prices of imported goods which directly affect the prices of goods in the country. Meanwhile, the indirect pass through impact of the weakening of the exchange rate on inflation occurred through an increase in production costs on the business sector which still has a high import content. From this explanation, it can be said that Bank Indonesia's control over inflation has become very limited, because inflation is influenced by many factors. Therefore, Bank Indonesia always conducts an assessment of economic developments, including conducting surveys, especially on possible inflationary pressures. Furthermore, the monetary policy response is based on the results of the assessment. It should also be conveyed that inflation control cannot be done only through monetary policy, but also other macroeconomic policies such as fiscal policy and policies in the real sector. For this reason, coordination and cooperation between cross-sectoral institutions is very important in dealing with this inflation problem. Monetary policy adopted by Bank Indonesia can basically only affect the demand side of the economy and public inflation expectations indirectly. The demand side of the economy, apart from being influenced by monetary policy, is also influenced by fiscal policy. Monetary and fiscal policy coordination will determine changes on the demand side of the economy. Meanwhile, the supply side is influenced by policies that affect the provision and distribution of goods and services in the economy, such as sectoral policies, minimum wages and other policies related to the provision of various industrial needs of the country. Meanwhile, public inflation expectations are not only influenced by inflationary behavior in the past (adaptive expectations) but also influenced by rational expectations. On the other hand, monetary policy cannot directly affect supply-side developments such as the harvest season and the development of administered prices , which can also affect the rate of inflation. The responsibility of controlling inflation imposed on Bank Indonesia also indirectly means that in the medium-long term, the influence of non-monetary factors on inflation needs to be continuously reduced, among others, through measures to enable market mechanisms to work properly. Control of Base Money (Primary Money) as an Operational Target In order to achieve the goal of realizing price stability (low inflation), Bank Indonesia uses primary money (MO) as the operational target of the monetary control program. In order to control primary money, Bank Indonesia constantly identifies factors that cause the ups and downs in the position of primary money, both from the demand and supply sides. On the demand side, the high increase in primary money mainly comes from the high demand for currency by the public as one of the components of primary money. Meanwhile, another factor that can be fully controlled by Bank Indonesia, namely the Bank's Positive Current Account Balance at Bank Indonesia, has relatively no significant changes. The demand for currency by the public is largely dependent on the behavior of the people who use the currency, making it difficult to be controlled by Bank Indonesia. Meanwhile, from the supply side, the increase in primary money mainly came from the expansion of government accounts (NOG), especially for the payment of subsidies, projects and interest on bonds through the banking sector, as well as the General Allocation Fund (DAU) to implement the Regional Autonomy Law. The increasing liquidity in the banking industry amidst the suboptimal banking intermediation function, as reflected by the low level of bank lending to the corporate sector, is feared to encourage the banking industry to act speculatively, which will encourage the weakening of the rupiah exchange rate. To overcome these problems, Bank Indonesia always strives to absorb excess liquidity through opt instruments, namely auction SBI and rupiah intervention. In the current situation where inflationary pressures are still high but economic growth is slowing, the monetary policy that must be pursued by Bank Indonesia has become increasingly difficult and dilemmatic. On the one hand, high inflationary pressures and volatile exchange rates require Bank Indonesia to tighten monetary conditions by absorbing excess liquidity in the economy, which will have an impact on rising interest rates. On the other hand, the economic slowdown demands an easing of monetary policy to avoid disruption of the ongoing economic recovery process. Implementation of Monetary Control Operations Monetary control operations are carried out with the main instrument of SBI (Bank Indonesia Certificate) which is carried out with a maturity period of 1 month and 3 months. With the potential for inflationary and exchange rate pressures in the coming period as well as high growth of primary money, monetary policy remains aimed at reducing base money growth towards a direction that is more in line with the real needs of economic activity. As previously stated, the growth target for primary money until the end of December 2001 was 11%-12% while until the end of March 2001 it was in the range of 12%-13%. In this relationship, Bank Indonesia continues to develop a daiam model to set monetary targets in accordance with economic needs, including cash flow projection as a reference for monetary control operations. In order to absorb excess liquidity, the monetary control strategy needs to be carried out in a prudent and measured manner by minimizing the negative impact of excessive interest rate increases. For this reason, the monetary control strategy adopted is as follows: a. Open Market operations should be directed towards efforts to minimize excess liquidity in the banking industry, including excess bank reserves, SBI, and rupiah intervention, more accurately so as not to cause signals excessive increase in interest rates. b. Rupiah intervention in the pastis used as "fine tuning" to absorb excess liquidity that is not accommodated by OPT with the right timing and magnitude and while still pursuing signals the increase in the flower rate is not excessive. c. Sterilization in the forex market is an open option to help absorb rupiah liquidity while increasing supply in the thin foreign exchange market so as to reduce pressure and value fluctuations exchange rupiah. Controlling Inflation With An Inflation Targeting Approach Terkait with the new methods/methods of dealing with inflation asked by the Board Members, Bank Indonesia realizes that recently there have been symptoms of a shift in the duties of the Central Bank which were originally of the nature of "multiple objectives" become focused on controlling inflation (single objective). In particular, in terms of this inflation control strategy, Bank Indonesia seeks to implement inflation targeting (IT). The choice of THIS IT method is also in line with the current trend of central banks in the world because it has proven to be quite effective in fighting inflation. In addition, its operational targets in various countries have shifted from quantinty targeting (primary money) to price targeting (interest rates). Some of the reasons underlying the tendency of Central Bank to implement Inflation Targeting are, First, empirical evidence suggests that long-term monetary policy can only affect the rate of inflation and cannot affect real variables such as economic growth or unemployment rate. Monetary policy can only affect short-term real variables . - Second, achieving low inflation is a prerequisite for achieving sustainable economic growth, because the economy is not spurred to grow beyond its capacity. - Ketiqa, by setting inflation as a single target, the target will become a nominal anchor (nominal reference) to formulate monetary policy and reference for various economic activities. The strategies used by Bank Indonesia to achieve the low inflation target are: assesses the effectiveness of monetary instruments and monetary policy transmission channels. determine the ultimate goal of monetary policy. identify the variables that cause inflationary pressures. formulate a monetary policy response. The central bank's inflation target cannot be reactively set but rather looks at the next few periods (forward looking) taking into account the effects of monetary policy delays and paying close attention to the projections (outlook) of the medium and long-term inflation rate. In addition to its development, pure inflation targeting has not been fully feasible, including due to the high fiscal burden that allows the Government to reduce subsidies by implementing policies in the field of administered prices, unclear institutional mechanisms (between the Government, Bank Indonesia and the House of Representatives), and banking conditions that have not been possible to implement inflation targeting. Alternative Assessment of Inflation Control Methods Looking for alternatives/methods of controlling inflation, Bank Indonesia continues to strive to conduct in-depth studies and research on the possibility of improving the effectiveness of various monetary tools owned by Bank Indonesia. The results of these studies are expected to provide an alternative monter tool that is better used by Bank Indonesia to achieve its goal of achieving and maintaining the stability of the rupiah value. In addition, Bank Indonesia also continues to strive to improve the quality of research results related to factors affecting Indonesia's inflation more accurately. In relation to the need for information on inflationary pressures that are more appropriately used in monetary policy formulation, Bank Indonesia is currently developing a number of approaches/methods to calculate core inflation, namely inflation influenced by monetary policy. As members of the Board know that one of the uses of core inflation is that it can be used as guidance for the implementation of Monetary Policy of Bank Indonesia. The resulting core inflation calculation is expected to provide a more appropriate direction and timing for Bank Indonesia to carry out a monetary policy. In addition, Bank Indonesia will also continue to develop better monetary policy formulation by developing policy rules based on transmission mechanisms believed to be applicable in Indonesia. Based on these rules, the implementation of monetary policy can be carried out in a more disciplined and systematic manner and forward looking, which means that the monetary authority is not reactive to inflation that occurs but is more directed at the trend of inflation in the future. Through a series of developments in the field of economic research and monetary policy, it is hoped that in the future Bank Indonesia can perform its duties even better. 2. Problems Faced by Daiam Efforts to Achieve Primary Money Goals Operationally, Bank Indonesia continues to use primary money as its operational target in accordance with the indicative target set by the Government's Letter of Intent (LOI) to the IMF but with due regard to the development of buga tribes that occur. Since May 2001, the position of primary money has continued to experience a high increase until it exceeds the indicative target set. The average annual growth of primary money until August 2001 has reached 18.3% while the target growth of primary money is 11% - 12% in December 2001 and by 12% - 13% in March 2002. The position of primary money until September continued to be above its indicative target, this is related to the increasing demand for currency by the public, in addition to expenditures from the NCG for the General Allocation Fund (DAU) or payment of salaries of civil servants. Some of the motives that drive public demand for the currency are for transactions, just in case, and for speculation. The demand for currency by the community for transactions has increased due to the increase in fuel prices, transportation tariffs and the tendency to weaken the rupiah exchange rate against the US dollar. The public's need for the currency has become increasingly high in connection with the increasing situation in the country such as Memorandum II and the Special Session which encourages people to keep larger currency for the purpose of vigilance. From these developments, if Bank Indonesia "all out" strives to ensure that the growth of primary money from month to month is within the set target range, then what happens is a high interest rate increase. Such conditions are certainly undesirable, as they can have a less favorable impact on banking restructuring, fiscal burdens, and hinder economic growth. However, this high growth of primary money can trigger inflation and the possibility of speculative actions against foreign exchange as well as for unproductive transactions. Such conditions are a dilemma for Bank Indonesia to formulate and implement monetary policy. High Interest Rates (Nominal) As a Resultante of Monetary Control In addition to its development, the tendency to weaken the rupiah exchange rate against the US dollar and the increase in public expectations of the inflation rate have caused the banking industry to continue to increase the bidding rate at each SBI auction. This condition resulted in the SBI interest rate for both 1 and 3 months continuing to increase until it reached the position of 17.67% at the mid-August 2001 auction. By looking at the high position of the SBI interest rate, which is expected to have a negative effect on the government's banking and financial sectors, further liquidity absorption efforts continue to be carried out in a more prudent and measured manner by minimizing excessive interest rate increases. In line with that, efforts to achieve the primary money target will be pursued by more effectively other instruments besides the auction SBI, namely rupiah intervention and foreign exchange sterilization. In relation to the large demand for interest rate reductions at Bank Indonesia, it can be argued that the interest rates that occur in the market are basically the resultante of the auction process that is determined by the market itself. Meanwhile, the high position of the SBI interest rate is still necessary considering the potential for inflationary pressures. In addition, this condition is also based on the high expectations of market participants for the weakening rupiah exchange rate, which is reflected in the high forward rate position which results in the low covered interest rate differential SBI and even reaches a negative position for deposit rates. These two considerations encourage Bank Indonesia not to lower the SBI interest rate in the near future. In this relationship, if pressures on the rate of inflation and the exchange rate have decreased persistently and the obstacles to the national economic recovery can be overcome, then Gradually Bank Indonesia can gradually lower interest rates to stimulate economic growth. 3. Implementation and Trade-off of Daiam Monetary Control Price controls directed at low inflation rates are often perceived by various groups as a "less partial" move to boost the economy. Therefore, controlling inflation from the monetary side will have an impact on increasing interest rates so that it is considered unable to support the smooth running of the business world and hinder the economic recovery process . In fact, the stability of persisten prices, if credible, will actually give rise to "confidence" for economic actors, without them having to bother doing adjustments to production costs and on the consumer side are not burdened with prices that continue to soar. For this reason, the central bank's inflation reduction is an important prerequisite for the realization of a solid foundation for a more sustainable economic recovery. long. Controlling inflation by Bank Indonesia under such conditions has become difficult and dilemmatic. In the fiscal sector, for example, the burden of paying interest on variable rate bonds is increasingly felt and causes the fiscal burden to increase by around Rp2 trillion every 1% increase in the SBI interest rate. Meanwhile, in the banking sector, a 1% increase in the SBI interest rate will have an impact on weak banks or banks that are still consolidating, which is feared to re-emerge difficulties. its financials. B. Exchange Rate System Issues The Councillor who asked about the exchange rate system issue was Sdr. Daniel Budi Setiawan, Sdr. Sudirman, Sdr. Anthony Zedra Abidin, Sdr. Fx. Soemitro, and Sdr. Mukhtar. Question : 1. The volatile exchange rate cannot provide certainty to the business world. Can Bank Indonesia provide certainty as to what exactly the exchange rate will be? 2. The exchange rate had strengthened after the formation of the new government. But now it is actually weakening and even reaching Rp9800 per dollar. What are Bank Indonesia's measures to deal with this? We also know that Bank Indonesia is unable to intervene in large numbers . 3. Why is the exchange rate still volatile? 4. It turns out that free floating actually afflicts the people, not in accordance with the theory. Is it appropriate for free floating exchange rates to be applied in countries that are experiencing a crisis? I think that needs to be reviewed. 5. Is it time for Bank Indonesia to determine the fixed value that is adjustmented so that branda cannot play foreign exchange anymore as a commodity? Answer : Dear Councillors, Given the questions from council members in substance related to each other, let us unify the answers to the questions posed. Application of exchange rate system in Indonesia Over the past 30 years, Indonesia has implemented various exchange rate systems, namely the fixed exchange rate system (August 1971 - November 1978), a controlled floating exchange rate system with a widening intervention band (November 1978 to August 14, 1997) and a floating exchange rate system (August 14, 1997 until now). Changes in the application of exchange rate regimes from one system to another are carried out in line with the situation and conditions of the Indonesian economy and the increasing integration with the world economy. The presentation of the chronology of the application of the exchange rate system is expected to provide an understanding of the advantages and disadvantages of each system. Fixed Exchange Rate (August 1971 - November 1978) In addition to its implementation, each exchange rate system has its own advantages and disadvantages. In the fixed exchange rate system, the exchange rate can be maintained stable over time . To keep the exchange rate at the level set by the central bank must actively intervene so that it must have a large amount of foreign exchange reserves, especially if there is a tendency to demand for forex. In Indonesia, a fixed exchange rate system with a foreign exchange control system pexisted in the 70s is still possible because at that time financial institutions were not yet developed, the volume of foreign exchange transactions was still relatively small and the foreign exchange market has not yet developed, so the pressures on the exchange rate require the intervention of entral banks to be able to maintain the exchange rate at the level of certain are relatively small. Nowadays, the national economy has become increasingly open to the world economy, and the financial sector is developing rapidly with its various financial instruments and the mobility of capital flows is getting higher. Under such conditions, on the one hand, the application of a fixed exchange rate will provide certainty to the business world. However, on the other hand, the system will be increasingly difficult to maintain because in the busiest economic system there are external pressures that affect the rupiah exchange rate. Efforts to maintain the rupiah exchange rate at a certain level where the central bank must continue to intervene, thus requiring large foreign exchange reserves that are often unable to deal with huge global external market forces. Another alternative, namely adjustments in the form of devaluation policies such as those that had been done several times in the 1970s, would cause massive speculation turmoil if ma the company expects the Central Bank to no longer be able to maintain the exchange rate. Thus, it is increasingly difficult for Bank Indonesia to maintain this fixed exchange rate system. Controlled Floating Exchange Rate (November 1978 to August 14, 1997) Theimplementation of a controlled floating exchange rate system provides a certain range for the exchange rate to move with the market. In addition to its implementation, the floating system is under control from time to time adjusted for the difference in inflation between Indonesia and the currency baskets of Indonesia's trading partner countries and competitors, to maintain its real effective exchange rate (Real Effective Exchange Rate). With the adjustment of the inflation difference, the development of the rupiah exchange rate during the controlled exchange rate system is relatively stable and easy to predict. However, with the development of the financial sector and high capital mobility, exchange rate turmoil will be even greater , especially if there is a devaluation issue. Although the intervening band (range) has been continuously widened, in the end the Central Bank was unable to withstand the speculative attack on the exchange rate at the beginning of the crisis period, due to limited foreign exchange reserves . The exchange rate became volatile and market forces were so dominant that it did not cause a drain of foreign exchange reserves. Therefore , this system was abandoned and we switched to a floating exchange rate system. Floating Exchange Rate In the floating exchange rate system, fluctuations are difficult to avoid, for example, the exchange rate once reached Rp. 16,000 per US dollar in 1998, then strengthened by Rp. 6,900 per US dollar in October 1999, but weakened again to Rp.7,463 per US dollar in March 2000 and Rp. 11,300 in June 2001. After the new government, the exchange rate strengthened to Rp.8600 per US dollar in August 2001 but still fluctuated. Efforts undertaken by Daiam to maintain exchange rate stability by Bank Indonesia and the Government include: absorbing excess liquidity in the money market through open market operations, conducting exchange sterilization foreigners, limiting rupiah transactions between banks and non-residents and scheduling government debt through Paris ClubS I and II. It can be informed that in the form of a floating exchange rate system, Bank Indonesia may intervene at any time. Bank Indonesia generally intervenes as an effort to increase the supply of foreign exchange in the market to reduce price volatility that occurs in the market and not pointn at a certain level/rate. With the increasing demands of the public towards the possibility of implementing a fixed exchange rate system that better reflects the existence of certainty, it is worth saying that taking into account the structural characteristics of the economy as well as the volatility that affects it, the implementation of a fixed exchange rate system at this time will be more at high risk to the occurrence of speculative attacks given the limited reserves Bank Indonesia's foreign exchange and politically will be more expensive if the short jan gka daiam is forced to devalue. Even by implementing a controlled floating system, if the uncertainty factor can be resolved, it is expected that the exchange rate will strengthen again and become relatively stable. Based on the experience of countries in the world, an exchange rate system suitable for a country, is not necessarily successfully implemented in other countries. For example, Hong Kong managed to maintain its economic stability with a fixed exchange rate system (Currency Board System), but Argentina with its CBS system could not avoid the crisis and currently, the economy is in a downturn so it needs IMF assistance. Singapore, which implements a free-floating system , has managed to maintain the stability ofthe exchange rate and its economy. Therefore, the successful implementation of an exchange rate system depends largely on the conditions in each country. Factors affecting the development of the exchange rate Recent rupiah exchange rate developments have been influenced by three main factors. First, short-term expectations of market participants (market sentiment) are often reflected in short-term fluctuations in the exchange rate. Second, fundamental factors in the form of inflation rate, economic growth, and balance of payments performance. Third, the microstructure of the foreign exchange market, namely the financial condition of banks and corporate. The three main factors are interrelated with each other and have caused a vicious circle of problems (vicious circles) both on a macro and micro scales and the exchange rate turmoil that we experience is a symptom of the economic problems we face. During the period (first semester of 2001), the exchange rate experienced quite high volatility. It is undeniable, that the short-term expectations of market participants so far have been greatly influenced by the instability of the socio-political situation (political risks), which market participants in general are feared to interfere with the continuity of economic recovery (economic risks) in the future. With the relatively stable socio-political situation today compared to the past, the first factor affecting the exchange rate (market sentiment) is expected to be resolved soon. However, on the other hand, the excessive exchange rate turmoil in the past has caused various disruptions to the economic structure of both macro and micro scales. On a macro scale, the economic fundamental factors that occur can significantly affect exchange rate movements, for example, with the deterioration of Indonesia's Balance of Payments performance. Similarly, fundamental conditions reflected in the high demand for debt repayment and conditions of long-term fiscal stability and sustainability can affect exchange rate movements. Meanwhile, the long-term debt of private external debt remains quite high and remains the main source of pressure on foreign exchange demand in the market. Meanwhile, the source of foreign exchange supply derived from capital inflows in the form of foreign investment and the return of capital due to capital flight that occurred in daiam in recent years have not been realized. Meanwhile, although the trade balance is in surplus, it has not made a significant contribution to the availability of foreign exchange in the country. In the current context of the national economy, to be able to influence market sentiment, efforts are needed to increase fundamentals, which is reflected in the consistent implementation of economic recovery programs. The success of the rupiah exchange rate's strengthening and stability in fundamental terms can occur through the creation of significant FDI foreign capital inflows, reflecting strong investor confidence as well as rupiah exchange rate stability. Meanwhile, micro-scale exchange rate turmoil has severely affected the performance of the banking industry and the real sector. The financial condition of corporate and individual banks greatly affects the demand and supply of foreign exchange in the market while maintaining a short or long position of foreign exchange. Thus, although the political situation in daiam negeri has relatively improved, some economic fundamental problems, both on a macro and micro scale, have not undergone significant changes to provide support for the achievement of rupiah exchange rate stability. C. Exchange Rate Development Question : 1. We would like to ask the veracity of the statement contained in the Second Quarter report which states that: "The condition of the forex market is illiquid, the cost of hedging is expensive, the needs of the USD are met from spot market so that the exchange rate becomes weaker. This can be seen from spot transactions that are larger than hedging transactions". Answer : Dear Members of the Council, As stated above, the formation of the price (exchange rate) of the rupiah against the USD is largely determined by how strong the demand and availability of foreign exchange supply is. Exchange rate movements in the spot market are price formations that are influenced by factors that are more short-term in nature. In contrast to price formation in the swap market, it is more influenced by long-term perceptions that are still overwhelmed by uncertainty. Therefore, in the swap or forward market, market participants take into account the premium which is the price of the risk that will be received/paid as a means of hedging (hedging) on the exposure of the currency owned. As mentioned above, in the Jakarta foreign exchange market there are changes in the composition of foreign exchange market transactions. Spot transactions are higher than swap transactions in April, May, and August 2001. This phenomenon is caused by the higher cost of premiums along with the increasing need for market hedging. The high cost of the premium causes the increase in hedging transactions not as large as additional spot transactions. Meanwhile, the worsening condition of the bank's balance sheet has reduced the ability of domestic banks to provide hedging facilities. This situation has encouraged businesses to hedge more in the off-shore swap market or perform hedging functions through spot transactions by buying foreign exchange early for their foreign exchange needs in the future. During certain periods this resulted in a surge in spot transaction volumes exceeding swap transaction volumes. Furthermore, with the increasingly volatile exchange rate, the need for hedging, especially from corporations, is also increasing, causing hedging costs to become more expensive, as reflected in the high swap premium rate. Moreover, coupled with the high risk factors and uncertainty, market participants' expectations of the rupiah exchange rate will deteriorate in the long term. This can be seen in the daiam phenomenon of the last two months (August and September 2001), which shows the high number of swap transactions compared to spot transactions. Spot transaction volumes for August and September (provisional figures) in 2001 amounted to USD14.7 billion and USD6.4 billion, respectively. Meanwhile, swap transaction volume reached USD17.1 billion and USDS.2 billion in the same period. This high number of swap transactions reflects the high need for hedging in the last two-month period. This is likely to happen because the strengthening of the rupiah has not been persistent and has not been followed by its long-term prospects, as reflected in the high swap premium and risk premium in Indonesia. Accountability Issues for Achieving Rupiah Stability Question from Abdullah Al Wahdi Question: That in chapter III, the objectives and duties of Bank Indonesia Article 7 are to achieve and maintain the stability of the rupiah exchange rate but in fact until now Bank Indonesia has been unable to carry out its duties to achieve rupiah stability, in other words, Bank Indonesia has failed its duties and responsibilities. How is Bank Indonesia accountable in this regard. If in other countries the Central Bank is unable to carry out this task, it retreats. Whether the Board of Governors of Bank Indonesia is ready to step down as a moral responsibility to the Nation and state. Answer: Dear Members of the Council, As mandated by Law No. 23/1999 article 7, Bank Indonesia's task is to achieve and maintain rupiah stability . The stability of the rupiah value in question is the stability of the rupiah against goods and services, which is reflected in the development of the inflation rate and stability against the currencies of other countries which is reflected on the development of the rupiah exchange rate against the currencies of other countries. This certainly provides a new implication and challenge for Bank Indonesia in the implementation of its duties. The task of achieving and maintaining the stability of the rupiah against goods and services and currencies of other countries means that Bank Indonesia must maintain an internal balance so that inflation remains low and at the same time also maintains an external balance so that the rupiah exchange rate is strong and stable. Nevertheless, it must be acknowledged that this task is not an easy task for its implementation. Controlling the money supply and or interest rate will indeed be able to affect the rate of inflation and the rupiah exchange rate but there are many other factors that can affect it. Daiam hal inflation, for example, as is known, inflation can be influenced by factors derived from the demand side and factors derived from the supply side . Bank Indonesia, through monetary policy, can only influence demand sides such as investment and public consumption. On the other hand, monetary policy cannot directly affect supply-side developments such as the harvest season and the development of administered commodity prices . prices) which can also affect the rate of inflation. The responsibility of controlling inflation imposed on Bank Indonesia thus indirectly also means that in the medium to long term, the influence of non-monetary factors to inflation need to be continuously reduced, among other things, through measures to allow the proper working of market mechanisms. During the transition period, Bank Indonesia will pay more attention to inflation caused by monetary factors or what is usually also disebut with core inflation or underlying inflation. In terms of the rupiah exchange rate, it is fully realized that with the adoption of the free float exchange rate system, the rupiah exchange rate is more determined by the strength of supply and demand in the market. In additionto economic and technical fundamental factors, market sentiment factors that are a mirror of risk factors and uncertainties often color the movement of the rupiah exchange rate. Therefore, Bank Indonesia's policy is not intended to direct the movement ofthe exchange rate to reach a certain level, but rather to prevent fluctuations in the value of excessive exchange, among others, through a policy to provide a supply of foreign exchange if necessary. In relation to accountability for the implementation of the gas tu, Bank Indonesia routinely and on time always provides reports on the implementation of tasks in the monetary, banking, and system sectors. payments are made to members of the Board every three months. Daiam the report, Bank Indonesia in detail explains the efforts taken by Daiam to achieve the objectives and obstacles faced in accordance with the mandate of the Law on Banks Indonesian. In addition, policy measures in the monetary and banking sector which are the results of monthly Board of Governors Meetings are also routinely socialized to the public as one of the manifestations of transparency and accountability of Bank Indonesia. It shall be the next authority of the members of the Board to carry outthe supervisory function of the implementation of the duties of the Board of Governors of Bank Indonesia, based on these reports. Of course, the Board of Governors of Bank Indonesia has always carried out its duties in accordance with Law No. 23 of 1999 concerning Bank Indonesia. E. H. Foreign Debt Issues The Councillor who inquired about the issue of foreign debt was Sdr. Anthony Zedra Abidin. Question : I hope that Bank Indonesia will also think about and take responsibility for how to reduce the burden of this foreign debt problem, not only is it a debt scheduling but also there must be responsibility responsibility on the part of the lender, because in my opinion the responsibility should be by both parties. Answer : Dear Members of the Council, Bank Indonesia as a partner of the Government is certainly very concerned about the issue of Government External Debt Rl, because this problem will have an impact on various economic sectors both it is the fiscal sector, the real sector and the monetary sector which are the main focus of Bank Indonesia's duties. Nonetheless, Bank Indonesia is not directly responsible for the issue of Government External Debt. As a partner of the government, one of the roles of Bank Indonesia daiam to find solutions to the settlement of Government External Debt is to try to find sources of funds from the daiam of the country, another antara with develop the market for public daiam bonds (government bonds). This alternative will help the Government reduce dependence on Foreign Debt . Meanwhile, until now, we must admit that the Rl m government has relied on rescheduling, especially through the Paris Club, in order to reduce or resolve the debt burden. overseas. The rescheduling itself has a huge effect on reducing the burden on the government's budget in the short term, so as to provide more free wiggle room for the government to reorganize its 'cash flow' and prioritise existing funds for financing other sectors that are relatively more productive than paying down debt obligations . Therefore, the successful re-scheduling of the burden of repayment of foreign debt through the Paris Club is also important and is a determining factor for the success of achieving the acceleration of the development process national economy. In order to resolve this issue of foreign debt, as it is known that the efforts that can be taken in addition to 'rescheduling' are generally through a more 'straightforward' way i.e. 'debt reduction' or another alternative i.e. through 'debt conversion'. Meanwhile, 'debt reduction' efforts for the Rl Government , especially through the Highly Indebted Poor Country (HIPC) mechanism, seem to have very little chances. Based on the results of our research, Indonesia has not met some of the main tor requirements of a country to be grouped into HIPC. In addition, before being able to enter the HIPC group, debtors who apply for debt reduction must first be eligible according to the rules of the game under the Paris Club framework under the criteria of 'Na Ples Terms', among others, the debtor must have a good 'track record' at the Paris club and the IMF program, only accepting loans in the form of IDA from the World Bank and with a GDP per Capita of USD755. Even this criterion has not been met by Indonesia. Currently, the countries that are classified as HIPC are generally poor countries in Latin America such as: Bolivia, Honduras and Nicaragua. While the two countries in ASIA that follow this mechanism are Laos and Vietnam. The 'debt relief' mechanism is also carried out through the 'debt conversion' mechanism, including through the Debt for Nature Swap (DNS). DNS is in principle one of the efforts to remove some of the debt and convert some of its other obligations into daiam obligations in the form of currency domestik to finance conservation maintenance nature. DNS is one of the important alternatives considering the amount of Indonesia's external debt which has reached around USD136 billion, an amount that many consider to have exceeded the threshold the limit of Indonesia's ability to restore it. Meanwhile, on the other hand, the quality of nature conservation continues to decline and the ability of the government and the private sector to finance nature conservation and conservation programs in Indonesia is very limited. DNS is one of the attractive benefits because it offers solutions to foreign debt problems that are beneficial both for debtors and NGOs and for creditors. Judging from the benefits of restoring environmental conservation and the need for other alternatives to reduce the repayment of government external debt other than through rescheduling, DNS is an alternative that needs to be considered for immediate implementation in Indonesia. Countries that have participated in this skim include Bolivia, Ecuador, Costa Rica and the Philippines. In Indonesia itself, the challenge of implementing DNS is mainly whether the government can establish a cooperation with NGOs considering the formation of frictions between the government and NGOs which often make the government 'reluctant' to cooperate with NGOs. Answer : Dear Members of the Council, As part of the ongoing restructuring program, banks were asked to increase and maintain their capitalization (CAR) of at least 8% by the end of 2001. Anticipating such policy, Bank Indonesia has taken various steps, including: Make projections to find out which banks are estimated to be unable to meet the CAR target; Conducting meetings with bank owners to identify the problems faced and the strategic steps that will be taken to resolve these problems. If all efforts to be made by the owners of these banks do not produce results and the target of achieving car 8% is not met, Bank Indonesia will take several steps in accordance with the provisions which sells, namely as follows: i. These banks will be placed under special supervision of Bank Indonesia (special surveillance) and Bank Indonesia can implement cease and desist orders for a certain period of time, namely ordering banks tok stop certain business activities, ask banks and/or bank owners to increase capital, carry out mergers or consolidations with other banks, sell banks to buyers who are willing to take transfer of all bank obligations, hand over the management of ashed or part of the bank's activities to other parties; and/or sell part of the bank's assets and/or obligations to the bank or the other party. ii. If the period has been set (3 months for banks that do not go public and 6 months for banks to go public) the bank's condition decreases rapidly (i.e. the CAR ratio is less than 2% and is considered unable to be increased to 8% and the reserve requirement ratio of rupiah is less than 0% and cannot be completed) then the bank is designated as a Frozen Business Activity Bank (BBKU) and submitted to IBRA. iii. If after the end of the period, the bank is still unable to increase its CAR, but Bank Indonesia considers that the bank: - can increase CAR to 8%; - can resolve the problem of waiver and/or violation of BMPK; - may lower non-performing loans; - has a considerable influence on the national or regional economy. then Bank Indonesia determines the bank with the status of Bank Daiam Penyehatan (BDP) and submits it to IBRA, with conditions, among others. iv. For banks that are considered not to meet the criteria in point (iii) mentioned above, Bank Indonesia will determine the bank with BBKU status and submit it to IBRA. v. If the BDP restructuring program by BPPN cannot be completed within the agreed period or based on BPPN considerations, the BDP restructuring program cannot be implemented even though it has not exceeded the term At the agreed time, Bank Indonesia can change the status of the bank in question from BDP to BBKU. vi.
