Terima kasih dan semoga Allah SWT senantiasa melindungi dan membimbing kita semua. Wassalamu'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh. 10

Title: Keynote Speech GBI Darmin Nasution pada Seminar: "Financial Lecture: Pasca-Investment Grade: What Next?" - Harian Bisnis Indonesia, 18 Januari 2012
text: Keynote Speech Dr. Darmin Nasution Seminar: "Financial Lecture: Post-Investment Grade: What Next?" Bisnis Indonesia Daily 18th January 2012 Which I respect General Leader of The Indonesian Business Daily , Prof. H.Sukamdani Sahid Gitosarjono Minister of State-Owned Enterprises, Mr. Dahlan Iskan President Director of PT. BRI Mr. Sofyan Basir And ladies and gentlemen, Assalamu'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh, Morning mats and greetings to all of us, 1. On this occasion, let us together offer thanksgiving to the hadirat of Allah SWT because it is by His grace alone that we are given the opportunity to be able to attend and discuss in the seminar with Theme: Financial Lecture: Post-Investment Grade: What's Next? I thank Bisnis Indonesia Daily and PT. BRI as the organizer of this seminar, which has invited me to convey the delivery in the seminar event which I judged to have the right momentum. 2. Through this seminar , we are expectedto better understand the strengths and weaknesses that exist in our economy, so that we are able to formulate various measures to continue to drive the economy perform the better. To achieve this, of course, we need to continue to explore and leverage the great potential that we have, and simultaneously need to solve several structural problems so that our economy can grow higher and sustainably. Only with high and sustainable growth can we overcome the problem of impoverishment and unemployment, which are the real problems around us. Father and Mother whom I respect, 3. The increase in Indonesia's rating to investment grade is not a success that we achieve suddenly, but after we have walked a long journey. As we all know, during the crisis in 1998 Indonesia's rating plummeted sharply by 6 notches in just less than a year, from BBB- to B-. This has an impact on the decline in investor confidence in the domestic economy, resulting in a wave of capital withdrawals and a halt in capital inflows, especially in the form of private external debt. On the other hand, the economy experienced a fairly deep contraction of -13%, while inflation soared to double digits. Our banking industry must also be recapitalized at a huge cost. 4. As we try to rise from the slump of the crisis, the economy is still too weak to deal with external and internal shocks. The problem of excess liquidity, the misalignment of strategy and policy implementation, and the still fragile resilience of the economic infrastructure to external shocks, has sedentaryly become an open problem full of risks . Since 2005 we have also faced a more complex period, especially as a result of global financial imbalances and soaring international oil prices. 5. It was only after 14 years of reforms in the economic, financial, and political fields that indonesia's rating from BB to BBB- at the end of 2011 confirmed that Indonesia is currently considered worthy of being an investment place. Of course this is an encouraging achievement because it occurs at a time when many ratings of other countries, especially in Europe, are actually lowered. This paradoxical condition further strengthens the belief that amid the increasing uncertainty of global conditions in recent times, our economy continues to have a fairly good resilience. This achievement is also the fruit of hard work and cooperation among all policymakers, actors in the business world and the financial sector, as well as society at large. 6. At this time, we should be grateful because in the midst of the persistence of global turmoil, the resilience of the financial sector and the national economy is increasingly tested for resilience. I see that the Indonesian economy has so far been isolated from the impact of the propagation of the European crisis through trade channels. We can also maintain the integrity of the financial system amid the intense pressure of the European crisis through financial market channels. 7. During 2011 macro stability was maintained. This opens up space for us to be able to steer various macroeconomic indicators moving forward on track and growing balanced marked by increased investment and exports. In 2011, the Indonesian economy was able to grow by 6.5%, surpassing the achievement in 2010 of 6.1%. More than that, growth high economistsi also achieved with low inflation of 3.79%. For the second time in the last 3 years our inflation has been below 5%. 8. We have also taken the bitter lessons of the 1997/1998 crisis to be more careful in keeping the financial system stable. The various improvements that have been taken over the past decade have made our banking sector more resilient and tested in absorbing instability risks such as market turmoil global finance in 2008 and 2011. Theimprovement of capital conditions and the consistency of the application of the bank's precautionary principle seem to be quite effective in containing the drastic deterioration of industrial conditions. Happy Ladies and Gentlemen, 9. Achieving investment grade although it is believed that it will provide various benefits to the economy, is certainly not the ultimate goal. This is more of an assessment of our position so that we can be better at determining the way forward. The challenge is how we can leverage Indonesia's entry into this investment-worthy zone to spur economic growth to its potential level which I estimate to be around 7.0%. I see that we have an opportunity to achieve it if we can take advantage of the great potential we have and simultaneously solve various structural problems at the micro level that still continue to be an innate burden (perennial) from year to year. 10. One of the great potentials that we must take advantage of is Indonesia's demographic advantage, both in terms of the large size of the domestic market, demographic transitions dominated by the population of productive age, as well as the rational behavior of the community in managing their consumption levels. The demographic transition is meant to be the ratio of the dependence of the unproductive age population to the productive age which is in a downward trend, so that it is conducive to the formation of larger savings and investments and per capita income to a higher level. ll.Meanwhile, our society also shows increasingly rational behavior with its ability to manage consumption levels according to income levels and make adjustments to the shocks it faces. This behavior has an impact on the high resilience of people's consumption levels and an increase in the savings ratio. This is reflected in the growth of household consumption which was able to survive around 4.0% in the period of the 2009 global crisis. 12. Indonesia's entry into the investment grade zone also reflects the declining financing risk premium. This should open a broader door for the private sector to access sources of financing such as through the issuance of bonds at a lower cost. 13. Improving the risk premium, demographic transition, supported by maintained macroeconomic stability will only be utilized to achieve high and sustainable growth if the domestic market has the potential a sizable one was responded to appropriately. This needs to be achieved by encouraging long-term (structural) sources of growth in a balanced manner , namely the accumulation of capital (K), both physical capital and human capital (H), and total productivity factor (TFP). 14. Given the wide scope of structural problems, urgent improvements need to be prioritized at several points of structural constraints that hinder the most (the most binding constraints') in the eyes of business actors , namely various constraints in the field of infrastructure, both hard and soft infrastructure (quality of human resources). U.S. ker infrastructure includes technical infrastructure such as highways, ports, and electricity, while soft infrastructure includes science, health and environmental infrastructure, and education, including an environment conducive to the development of innovation. 15. The progress of policy implementation on the structural side will be a key factor in the process of decreasing inflation (disinflation) because it will increase economic capacity. It should be noted that the conducive demographic momentum in Indonesia is expected to last only until 2025-2030. Therefore, significant structural improvement measures before the arrival of the period will be crucial in determining the sustainability of Indonesia's economic growth to the level of which is higher in the medium to long term. Father and Mother whom I respect, 16. In financial markets, the land of the national banking industry after the 1998 crisis has been much more resilient. The banking industry has a fairly strong capitalization, as reflected in its capital adequacy ratio of 17% well above 8%. Meanwhile, credit risk is also much better as indicated by NPLs which are still below 5%. 17. However, I see that the role of banks can still be optimized in supporting national economic development. Data shows that the ratio of bank lending to GDP in Indonesia is still very low, only around 30%, while in other countries such as Malaysia, Thailand and China it has reached above 100%. This is in line with the results of BI's survey of financing sources, which shows that the role of banks is still limited. The company still relies on internal funds. This condition illustrates the large space for Indonesian banks to strengthen their role in the economy. In addition, this also indicates the potential for expansion from the business world which is still quite large. 18. On the other hand, banks still have assets that from a macro perspective are less productive, namely in the form of placement of monetary instruments and government securities. These assets should be channeled in the form of credit, so that banks can more optimally take a role in economic development. Due to the lack of bright global economic prospects in 2012, banks should also play a more 'countercyclical' role by increasing their role in financing the economy, rather than being 'procyclical'. Father and Mother whom I respect, 19. In recent years we have been able to maintain macro stability, which is very important as an "element of continuity" in providing space for the economy to continue to grow. Without macro stability it is impossible for the economy to grow sustainably. Therefore, we still need to maintain macro stability, including by continuing to strengthen self-protection tools { self protection} given the increasing uncertainty and risks in the global environment. On the other hand, we must race against time to make various structural improvements so that we can optimize the growth potential we have. 20. From Bank Indonesia's side, with the view that macroeconomic management in the future still has to deal with the risk of global and the complexity of domestic problems that are so large, Bank Indonesia's policy on the year 2012 will be directed in order to: a. Optimizing the role of monetary policy in boosting economic capacity while mitigating the risk of a slowdown in the global economy. b. Improving banking efficiency to optimize its contribution to the economy, while strengthening banking resilience. c. Improve the efficiency, reliability, and security of the payment system, both in the national payment system and the relationship between the payment system and abroad. d. Strengthening macro resilience by strengthening coordination in crisis prevention and management (FMD). e. Supporting the empowerment of the real sector, including continuing efforts to expand banking access (financial inclusion) to the public 21. The interest rate response will be directed to be consistent in achieving the CPI inflation target of 4.5 percent b1 1 percent in 2012 and 2013, as well as to maintain economic strengthening momentum and mitigate risks from the global economic slowdown. This interest rate policy will be complemented by macroprudential policy, to mitigate the risk of vulnerability in consumptive sectors whose growth is unsustainable or has the potential to experience asset price bubbles. 22. Bank Indonesia's policy is considered to be directed towards maintaining exchange rate stability, thereby providing certainty for all economic actors. Since January 2012, exchange rate stabilization policy will be supported by the implementation of the policy of obligation to receive foreign exchange proceeds from exports (DHE) and foreign exchange debt (DULN) in domestic banks. 23. In order to control inflation in the regions, the function of the Bank Indonesia Office (KBI) as a facilitator and catalyst for regional development acceleration will be optimized, especially in eastern Indonesia where the growth disparity is still quite wide. KBI will be encouraged to carry out its functions effectively, by strengthening the relationship with local governments. 24. The implementation of the task of the TPID (Regional Inflation Control Team) in the future needs to be supported by a strategic goods price information system, especially including information on production and stocks nationally. To be able to realize this, of course, requires a strong commitment and support from many parties including from relevant ministries such as the Ministry of Agriculture and the Ministry of Trade, including from local governments. 25. In order to improve banking competitiveness, prime lending rate (PLR) policy will be continued to ensure market mechanisms are running well so that policy targets can be achieved. As a follow-up to the bank supervision side, enhanced enforcement of the provisions by requiring the Bank's Business Plan (RBB) to include targets for increasing efficiency and reducing lending rates at a reasonable level. Bank Indonesia is also "reviewing" the practice of providing interest rates on third party funds (DPK) above the interest rate set by the Depository Institution (LPS). Ladies and gentlemen, 26. These are the main points of my view on Indonesia's post-investment grade economic potential. We hope that the investment grade status that we have achieved can be maintained, even improved by the quality of ratingwya. Efforts in this direction are very important because they will improve the quality of capital flows, especially those that are indispensable to support future economic growth. 27. I hope that at today's meeting we can discuss and formulate various new perspectives, especially in an effort to optimize the economic potential that we have. Finally, may Allah the Most Merciful and Merciful xx\e-ridhoi this activity and always bestow His guidance, guidance, and mercy upon all of us. Terhyme of love. Wassalamu 'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh. Dr. Darmin Nasution
text_original: Keynote Speech Dr. Darmin Nasution Seminar: "Financial Lecture: Pasca-Investment Grade: What Next?" Harian Bisnis Indonesia 18 Januari 2012 Yang saya hormati Pemimpin Umum Harian Bisnis Indonesia Bapak Prof. H.Sukamdani Sahid Gitosarjono Meneg BUMN, Bpk Dahlan Iskan Direktur Utama PT. BRI Bpk Sofyan Basir Dan Bapak-Ibu undangan lainnya, Assalamu'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh, Sela mat pagi dan salam sejahtera bagi kita semua, 1. Pada kesempatan ini mari bersama-sama kita panjatkan puji syukur ke hadirat Allah SWT karena atas rahmatNya sajalah kita diberi kesempatan untuk dapat hadir dan berdiskusi dalam seminar dengan tema: Financial Lecture: Pasca-Investment Grade: What Next? Saya berterimakasih kepada Harian Bisnis Indonesia dan PT. BRI sebagai penyelenggara seminar ini, yang telah mengundang saya untuk menyampaikan penghantar dalam acara seminar yang saya nilai mendapat momentum yang tepat. 2. Melalui seminar ini kita diharapkan akan lebih memahami kekuatan dan kelemahan yang ada dalam perekonomian kita, sehingga kita mampu merumuskan berbagai langkah untuk terus mendorong perekonomian berkinerja semakin baik. Untuk mencapai hal itu, tentunya kita perlu terus menggali dan memanfaatkan potensi besar yang kita miliki, dan secara bersamaan perlu menyelesaikan beberapa persoalan struktural agar perekonomian kita dapat tumbuh lebih tinggi dan berkesinambungan. Hanya dengan pertumbuhan yang tinggi dan berkesinambungan, maka masalah kemiskinan dan pengangguran yang merupakan masalah riil di sekeliling kita dapat kita atasi bersama. Bapak dan Ibu yang saya hormati, 3. Meningkatnya rating Indonesia menjadi investment grade bukanlah keberhasilan yang kita raih secara tiba-tiba, tetapi setelah kita menapaki perjalanan yang panjang. Seperti kita ketahui bersama, pada masa krisis tahun 1998 rating Indonesia anjlok tajam 6 notch hanya dalam kurang dari setahun yaitu dari BBB- menjadi B-. Ini berdampak pada merosotnya kepercayaan investor terhadap perekonomian domestik, sehingga terjadi gelombang penarikan modal dan terhentinya arus modal masuk khususnya dalam bentuk utang luar negeri swasta. Di pihak lain, perekonomian mengalami kontraksi yang cukup dalam -13%, sementara inflasi melonjak hingga double digit. Industri perbankan kita pun harus direkapitalisasi dengan biaya yang sangat besar. 4. Ketika kita berusaha bangkit dari keterpurukan krisis, perekonomian pun masih terlalu lemah untuk berhadapan dengan guncangan eksternal dan internal. Masalah ekses likuiditas, belum selarasnya strategi dan implementasi kebijakan, serta masih rapuhnya daya tahan infrastruktur ekonomi terhadap guncangan eksternal, secara menetap telah menjadi masalah terbuka yang penuh risiko. Sejak tahun 2005 kita pun menghadapi masalah yang lebih kompleks, terutama sebagai imbas dari ketidakseimbangan keuangan global dan melonjaknya harga minyak internasional. 5. Baru setelah selama 14 tahun kita melakukan reformasi di bidang ekonomi, keuangan, dan politik, meningkatnya rating Indonesia dari BB+ ke BBB- pada akhir tahun 2011 lalu mengkonfirmasi bahwa Indonesia saat ini dinilai layak menjadi tempat investasi. Tentu ini adalah sebuah pencapaian yang membesarkan hati karena terjadi pada saat banyak rating negara lain khususnya di Eropa yang justru diturunkan. Kondisi paradoks tersebut semakin memperkuat keyakinan bahwa di tengah meningkatnya ketidakpastian kondisi global belakangan ini, perekonomian kita tetap memiliki ketahanan yang cukup baik. Pencapaian tersebut juga merupakan buah dari hasil kerja keras dan jalinan kerjasama di antara semua pemangku kebijakan, para pelaku di dunia usaha dan sektor keuangan, serta masyarakat secara luas. 6. Saat ini, kita patut bersyukur karena di tengah persistensi gejolak global, daya tahan sektor keuangan dan perekonomian nasional semakin teruji ketangguhannya. Saya melihat, ekonomi Indonesia sejauh ini masih terisoIasi dari dampak rambatan krisis Eropa melalui jalur perdagangan (trade channel). Kita juga masih dapat menjaga integritas sistem keuangan di tengah besarnya tekanan rambatan krisis Eropa melalui jalur pasar keuangan (financial market channel). 7. Selama tahun 2011 kestabilan makro tetap terjaga. Ini membuka ruang bagi kita untuk dapat mengarahkan berbagai indikator ekonomi makro bergerak melaju pada jalurnya yang tepat (on-track) dan tumbuh berimbang ditandai dengan meningkatnya investasi dan ekspor. Pada tahun 2011 lalu ekonomi Indonesia mampu tumbuh 6,5%, melampaui pencapaian tahun 2010 lalu sebesar 6,1%. Lebih dari itu, pertumbuhan ekonomi yang tinggi juga kita raih dengan inflasi yang rendah sebesar 3,79%. Untuk kedua kalinya dalam 3 tahun terakhir inflasi kita berada dibawah 5%. 8. Kita juga telah mengambil pelajaran pahit dari krisis 1997/1998 untuk lebih berhati-hati dalam menjaga stabilitas sistem keuangan. Berbagai pembenahan yang telah ditempuh selama satu dasawarsa terakhir telah menjadikan sektor perbankan kita lebih tangguh dan teruji dalam menyerap risiko instabilitas seperti gejolak pasar keuangan global pada tahun 2008 dan 2011. Perbaikan kondisi permodalan dan konsistensi penerapan prinsip kehati-hatian bank tampaknya cukup efektif dalam menahan terjadinya pemburukan kondisi industri secara drastis. Bapak dan Ibu yang berbahagia, 9. Pencapaian investment grade meskipun diyakini akan memberikan berbagai keuntungan bagi perekonomian, tentu saja bukanlah menjadi tujuan akhir. Hal tersebut lebih merupakan penilaian terhadap posisi kita sehingga dapat lebih baik dalam menentukan langkah ke depan. Tantangannya adalah bagaimana kita dapat memanfaatkan masuknya Indonesia ke zona layak investasi ini untuk memacu pertumbuhan ekonomi ke tingkat potensialnya yang saya perkirakan sekitar 7,0%. Saya memandang, kita memiliki peluang untuk mencapainya apabila kita dapat memanfaatkan berbagai potensi besar yang kita miliki dan secara bersamaan menuntaskan berbagai persoalan struktural di tingkat mikro yang masih terus menjadi beban bawaan (perennial) dari tahun ke tahun. 10. Salah satu potensi besar yang harus kita manfaatkan adalah keuntungan demografi Indonesia, baik dalam hal ukuran pasar domestik yang besar, transisi demografi yang didominasi oleh penduduk usia produktif, maupun perilaku rasional masyarakat dalam mengelola tingkat konsumsinya. Transisi demografi dimaksud adalah rasio ketergantungan penduduk usia tidak produktif terhadap usia produktif yang sedang dalam kecenderungan menurun, sehingga kondusif bagi pembentukan tabungan dan investasi yang lebih besar serta pendapatan per kapita ke tingkat yang lebih tinggi. ll.Sementara itu, masyarakat kita juga menunjukkan perilaku yang semakin rasional dengan kemampuannya dalam mengelola tingkat konsumsi sesuai tingkat pendapatan dan melakukan penyesuaian terhadap shocks yang dihadapinya. Perilaku ini berdampak pada tingginya risiliensi tingkat konsumsi masyarakat dan meningkatnya rasio tabungan. Hal ini tercermin dari pertumbuhan konsumsi rumah tangga yang dapat bertahan di sekitar 4,0% pada periode krisis global 2009. 12. Masuknya Indonesia ke zona investment grade juga mencerminkan premi risiko pembiayaan yang semakin menurun. Ini seharusnya membuka pintu yang lebih luas bagi sektor swasta dalam melakukan akses ke sumber pembiayaan seperti melalui penerbitan obligasi dengan biaya yang lebih rendah. 13. Perbaikan premi risiko, transisi demografi, yang didukung oleh terjaganya stabilitas makroekonomi hanya akan dapat dimanfaatkan untuk mencapai pertumbuhan yang tinggi dan berkelanjutan apabila potensi pasar domestik yang cukup besar direspons secara tepat. Hal ini perlu ditempuh dengan mendorong sumber-sumber pertumbuhan jangka panjang (struktural) secara seimbang yaitu akumulasi kapital (K), baik modal fisik dan modal manusia (H), serta faktor produktivitas total (TFP). 14. Mengingat luasnya cakupan permasalahan struktural, perbaikan mendesak perlu diprioritaskan pada beberapa titik kendala struktural yang paling menghambat {the most binding constraints') di mata pelaku usaha yaitu berbagai kendala di bidang infrastruktur, baik infrastruktur keras maupun lunak (kualitas SDM). Infrastruktur keras mencakup infrastruktur teknis seperti jalan raya, pelabuhan, dan listrik, sedangkan infrastruktur lunak mencakup infrastruktur sains, kesehatan dan lingkungan hidup, serta pendidikan, termasuk di dalamnya lingkungan yang kondusif bagi berkembangnya inovasi. 15. Kemajuan implementasi kebijakan di sisi struktural ini akan menjadi faktor kunci terhadap proses menurunnya inflasi (disinflasi) karena akan memperbesar kapasitas perekonomian. Perlu dicatat bahwa momentum demografi yang kondusif di Indonesia tersebut diperkirakan hanya akan berlangsung hingga tahun 2025- 2030. Oleh karena itu, langkah-langkah perbaikan strukural yang signifikan sebelum datangnya periode tersebut akan sangat krusial dalam menentukan sustainabilitas pertumbuhan ekonomi Indonesia ke tingkat yang lebih tinggi dalam jangka menengah panjang. Bapak dan Ibu yang saya hormati, 16. Di pasar keuangan, ketanahan industri perbankan nasional pasca krisis 1998 telah jauh lebih tangguh. Perbankan memiliki permodalan yang cukup kuat, sebagaimana tercermin dari rasio kecukupan modalnya sebesar 17% jauh di atas 8%. Sementara itu, risiko kredit juga jauh lebih baik sebagaimana diindikasikan oleh NPL yang masih berada dibawah 5%. 17. Namun, saya melihat peran perbankan masih dapat dioptimalkan dalam mendukung pembangunan ekonomi nasional. Data menunjukkan rasio penyaluran kredit perbankan terhadap PDB di Indonesia masih sangat rendah, hanya sekitar 30%, sementara di negara-negara lain seperti Malaysia, Thailand dan China telah mencapai di atas 100%. Hal tersebut sejalan dengan hasil survey BI terhadap sumber pembiayaan yang menunjukkan peran perbankan masih terbatas. Perusahaan masih mengandalkan dana internal. Kondisi ini menggambarkan masih besarnya ruang bagi perbankan Indonesia untuk memperkuat perannya dalam perekonomian. Selain itu, hal tersebut juga mengindikasikan potensi ekspansi dari dunia usaha yang masih cukup besar. 18. Di pihak lain, perbankan masih memiliki aset yang dari perspektif makro kurang produktif, yaitu dalam bentuk penempatan instrumen moneter maupun surat berharga negara. Aset tersebut seharusnya disalurkan dalam bentuk kredit, sehingga perbankan dapat lebih optimal mengambil peran dalam pembangunan ekonomi. Sehubungan dengan kurang cerahnya prospek ekonomi global di tahun 2012 ini, seharusnya perbankan juga lebih berperan 'countercyclical' dengan meningkatkan perannya dalam pembiayaan perekonomian, bukannya bersikap 'procyclical'. Bapak dan Ibu yang saya hormati, 19. Dalam beberapa tahun terakhir kita telah mampu mempertahankan stabilitas makro, yang sangat penting sebagai "elemen kontinuitas" dalam menyediakan ruang bagi perekonomian untuk terus tumbuh. Tanpa stabilitas makro sangat mustahil perekonomian dapat tumbuh berkelanjutan. Oleh karena itu stabilitas makro tetap perlu kita pertahankan, termasuk dengan terus memperkuat alat proteksi diri {self protection} mengingat semakin tingginya ketidakpastian dan risiko dalam lingkungan global. Di pihak lain, kita harus berpacu dengan waktu untuk melakukan berbagai perbaikan struktural agar kita dapat mengoptimalkan potensi pertumbuhan yang kita miliki. 20. Dari sisi Bank Indonesia, dengan memandang bahwa pengelolaan ekonomi makro kedepan masih harus berhadapan dengan risiko global dan kompleksitas permasalahan domestik yang begitu besar, kebijakan Bank Indonesia pada tahun 2012 akan di arahkan dalam rangka: a. Mengoptimalkan peran kebijakan moneter dalam mendorong kapasitas perekonomian sekaligus memitigasi risiko perlambatan ekonomi global. b. Meningkatkan efisiensi perbankan untuk mengoptimalkan kontribusinya dalam perekonomian, dengan tetap memperkuat ketahanan perbankan. c. Meningkatkan efisiensi, kehandalan, dan keamanan sistem pembayaran, baik dalam sistem pembayaran nasional maupun hubungan sistem pembayaran dengan luar negeri. d. Memperkuat ketahanan makro dengan memantapkan koordinasi dalam manajemen pencegahan dan penanganan krisis (PMK). e. Mendukung pemberdayaan sektor riil termasuk melanjutkan upaya perluasan akses perbankan (financial inclusion) kepada masyarakat 21. Respon suku bunga akan diarahkan agar konsisten untuk pencapaian sasaran inflasi IHK sebesar 4,5 persen <b1> 1 persen pada tahun 2012 dan 2013, sekaligus untuk menjaga momentum penguatan ekonomi dan memitigasi risiko dari perlambatan ekonomi global. Kebijakan suku bunga ini akan dilengkapi dengan kebijakan makroprudensial, untuk memitigasi risiko kerentanan pada sektor-sektor konsumtif yang pertumbuhannya tidak sustainable atau berpotensi mengalami penggelembungan harga aset (asset bubble). 22. Kebijakan Bank Indonesia dinilai tukar akan tetap diarahkan untuk menjaga stabilitas nilai tukar sehingga memberikan kepastian bagi seluruh pelaku ekonomi. Sejak Januari 2012, kebijakan stabilisasi nilai tukar akan didukung oleh implementasi kebijakan kewajiban penerimaan devisa hasil ekspor (DHE) dan devisa utang luar negeri (DULN) di bank domestik. 23. Dalam rangka pengendalian inflasi di daerah, fungsi Kantor Bank Indonesia (KBI) sebagai fasilitator dan katalisator percepatan pembangunan di daerah akan dioptimalkan, terutama di wilayah timur Indonesia dimana disparitas pertumbuhannya masih cukup lebar. KBI akan didorong untuk menjalankan fungsinya secara efektif, dengan memperkuat jalinan hubungan dengan Pemerintah Daerah. 24. Pelaksanaan tugas TPID (Tim Pengendalian Inflasi Daerah) ke depan perlu ditopang dengan sistem informasi harga barang strategis terutama mencakup informasi mengenai produksi dan stok secara nasional. Untuk dapat mewujudkan hal tersebut tentunya memerlukan komitmen yang kuat dan dukungan dari banyak pihak termasuk dari kementerian terkait seperti Kementerian Pertanian dan Kementerian Perdagangan, termasuk dari Pemerintah Daerah 25. Dalam rangka meningkatkan daya saing perbankan, kebijakan Suku Bunga Dasar Kredit (SBDK) akan dilanjutkan untuk memastikan mekanisme pasar berjalan dengan baik sehingga sasaran kebijakan dapat tercapai. Sebagai tindak lanjut dari sisi pengawasan bank, ditingkatkan enforcement ketentuan dengan mewajibkan Rencana Bisnis Bank (RBB) mencantumkan target-target peningkatan efisiensi dan penurunan suku bunga kredit pada level yang wajar. Bank Indonesia juga tengah "mengkaji" praktek pemberian tingkat bunga dana pihak ketiga (DPK) di atas tingkat bunga yang ditetapkan oleh Lembaga Penjamin Simpanan (LPS). Bapak dan Ibu sekalian, 26. Demikian pokok-pokok pandangan saya terhadap potensi ekonomi Indonesia pasca-investment grade. Kita mengharapkan status investment grade yang telah kita capai dapat dipertahankan, bahkan ditingkatkan kualitas ratingwya. Upaya-upaya ke arah ini sangat penting karena akan memperbaiki kualitas arus modal khususnya yang sangat diperlukan untuk menopang pertumbuhan ekonomi ke depan. 27. Saya berharap pada pertemuan hari ini kita dapat mendiskusikan dan merumuskan berbagai perspektif baru, khususnya dalam upaya mengoptimalkan potensi ekonomi yang kita miliki. Akhir kata, semoga Allah Yang Maha Pengasih dan Penyayang xx\e-ridhoi kegiatan ini dan senantiasa melimpahkan bimbingan, petunjuk, dan rahmat-Nya kepada kita sekalian. Terima kasih. Wassalamu 'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh. Dr. Darmin Nasution

Title: Penjelasan Dewan Gubernur Bank Indonesia pada Rapat Kerja Komisi IX DPR RI - 4 Maret 2002
text: EXPLANATION OF THE BOARD OF GOVERNORS OF BANK INDONESIA AT THE WORKING MEETING OF COMMISSION IX OF THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES ON 4TH MARCH 2002 Conference Time : III TahunSidang : 2001 -2002 Dear Board Members First of all, let us thank the Chairman of Commission IX of the House of Representatives and all members of the House for inviting us to attend the Working Meeting today. For us, this meeting has a very important meaning, especially in order to convey various information and explanations regarding theimplementation of Bank Indonesia's duties mandated by law as well as to obtain various inputs from Board Members that are useful for efforts to improve in the implementation of our duties in the monetary, banking and payment system sectors in the future. Moreover, we view this kind of meeting as a form of embodiment of Bank Indonesia accountability to the Dpr-RI. It is also within such a framework that, as mandated in Law No. 23 of 1999 concerning Bank Indonesia, in January 2002 we submitted a written report on the evaluation of the implementation of monetary policy in 2001 along with the monetary policy plan and the establishment of monetary targets for 2002 to An ggota Council. We have also conveyed this to the public openly. Therefore, as was the case at the last Working Meetings, beginning our explanation of the questions of the Board Members that have been submitted in writing, allow us on this good occasion to briefly present the monetary policy plan and targets of Bank Indonesia in 2002 as well as submit the latest development report on the policy measures taken by Bank Indonesia. Dear Board Members As the Board members have noted, at the beginning of 2001, Bank Indonesia predicted that in 2001 the economic restructuring process will achieve significant progress, the social conditions ofpoli tikakan improve and are conducive to economic recovery, as well as world economic developments will be quite encouraging. Based on these assumptions, at that time Bank Indonesia predicted that GDP growth in 2001 would be able to reach 4.5% - 5.5%. In addition, Bank Indonesia has set the inflation target beyond the impact of government policies in the field of prices and income at 4% - 6%, while the additional inflation which is the impact of government policy in the field of prices and income is estimated at aroundr 2% - 2.5%. In line with the inflation target, the primary money growth target for the end of 2001 has been set at 11% - 12%. But in reality, during 2001, the various problems we faced have not shown any significant progress and some of them show a worsening trend. The world economy is also showing growth that continues to slow and has even experienced a recession. Meanwhile, domestically, socio-political and security conditionshave not fully demonstrated stability, which, among other things, was marked by a change of government in mid-2001. Despite the progress, the handling of restructuring programs in the real sector still faces a number of obstacles sothat various structural problems in the country continue to persist, while business risks and uncertainties remain high. With these various problems, during 2001 economic and monetary conditions in general showed a deteriorating trend. Deteriorating economic and monetary conditions are among others indicated by slowing economic growth, weakening exchange rates, and high inflationary pressures. During 2001, indonesia's economy only grew by 3.4%, the exchange rate experienced depreciation pressures of 17.7% to an average of Rp. 10,256 per US dollar, and CPI inflation reached 12.55%. Meanwhile, the actual impact of government policies on inflation was recorded at 3.83%, higher thanwhat was estimated at the beginning of the year of 2% - 2.5%. Various efforts have been made by Bank Indonesia to achieve the targets set at the beginning of the year, both by using monetaryinstruments and regulations in the field of exchange rates and foreign exchange. However, the various problems faced above have made it more difficult to achieve the inflation target and control primary money by Bank Indonesia. Apart from the impact of government policies in the field of prices and incomes, high inflation is mainly also driven by the depreciation of the rupiah exchange rate and increasing inflation expectations in the community. Meanwhile, the high amount of primary money is mainly due to the increasing demand for uang kartal both for transaction needs and for vigilance motives. Under such circumstances, we are of the view that drastic and excessive monetary tightening will lead to even higher interest rates, and it is feared thatit may exacerbate the risks to banking restructuring measures and economic recovery efforts. Observing macroeconomic developments in 2001, the high risks and uncertainties to be faced, as well as the projected inflation generated by government policies in the field of prices and income, as well as high inflation expectations, Bank Indonesia set the CPI inflation target which is considered in line with economic conditions in 2002, at 9%-10%. However, in the medium term, Bank Indonesia will gradually reduce inflation so that it can reach the range of 6% - 7%. To achieve this target, Bank Indonesia's monetary policy is directed at controlling primary money with a focus on absorbing excess liquidity to remain in line with the real needs of the economy. This step will be carried out in a prudent and measured manner while still paying attention to the impact on the ongoing economic recovery process. In the financial sector, Bank Indonesia's policy will be directed at strengthening banking system resilience as well as accelerating the recovery of banking intermediation. Meanwhile, policy in the payment system sector will be directed at developingpayment system monitoring mechanisms to promote a safe and efficient payment system and maintain financial system stability from possible systemic failures. Dear Councillors, With the inflation target framework and thedirection of the monetary policy for 2002 as we have stated earlier, in 2002 monetary policy remained directed towards achieving price stability by maintaining primary money as needed by the economy. We have witnessed that, in the early months of 2002, economic-monetary conditions were relatively under control, the rupiah exchange rate was moving relatively stable, the development of primary money had also returned to normal levels, and interest rates had also shown a decline. However , we are of the view that vigilance still needs to be increased, especially with regard to the strengthening of inflationary pressures at the beginning of the year and the months ahead. In terms of inflation, it shows that the inflation rate, especially until February 2002, remained high, namely on a monthly basis of 1.50% (m-t-m) or on an annual basis (y-o-y) reaching 15.13%. As is understandable, the main factors that drove the continued high inflation at the beginning of this year mainly came from the impact of the implementation of an increase in a series of government policies in the field of prices and incomes such as an increase in the retail price of fuel, gradual adjustment of the basic electricity tariff (TDL); provincial minimum wage (UMP), telephone tariffs and due to flood disasters that disrupted the smooth running of the dis attribution of goods and services. The Government's policy ultimately boosted high public inflation expectations - which was previously also influenced by the high inflation of the previous month. In addition, due to the postponement of the announcement of the price increase BBM has caused psychological effects that have prompted many cases of hoarding and smuggling, causing disruptions in supply and distribution which in turn further aggravated price developments. Meanwhile, the rupiah exchange rate also moved relatively stable where until the third week of February 2002, the rupiah exchange rate continued to show a tendency to strengthen until it reached the range of Rp10. 213,- per US dollar. Fundamentally, the demand for foreign exchange for import needs and repayment of foreign debtmade by the corporate sector is still occurring. The supply of foreign exchange is also quite well maintained as indicated by the increase in exports in December 2001 and January 2002 and the tendency of market participants to sell foreign exchange. In line with the development of inflation and the exchange rate, our monetary controls are still aimed at absorbing excess liquidity to suit the real needs of the economy so as not to put new pressure on inflation and the rupiah exchange rate. We carry out monetary control with open market operations, rupiah intervention and foreign exchange sterilization. In its development, primary money is still below the indicative targets that have been set. The impact of the flood, which was previously feared to increase demand for currency, was not significant enough. With conducive monetary economic conditions, the 1-month SBI interest rate has tended to decline in January and February 2002, from 17.5% in early January to 16.89% in the third week of February. Nevertheless, monetary policy easing will be carried out prudently taking into account various developments in solving structural economic problems. Especially for the coming months, we expect inflationary pressures to remain high. Meanwhile, the exchange rate is still quite risky and tends to be sensitive to market sentiment factors. Therefore, monetary control in the short term will still be directed at absorbing excess liquidity so that primary money can be maintained at the indicative target that has been set by optimizing existing instruments. Dear Councillors, In the banking sector, at the beginning of 2002, the performance of the national banking industry showed several improvements as indicated by an increase in fund raising and lending, improvements in capital aspects, improvements in non-performing loans (NPL) and an increase in net interest margin (NIM). Nevertheless, the banking industry still faces challenges in the form of an intermediation function that has not recovered as quickly as expected to support the economic recovery process. Therefore, in 2002 Bank Indonesia will continue to implement banking policy measures directed at the banking restructuring strategy framework, which includes two major parts, namely (i) the banking restructuring program which includes government guarantees, commercial bank recapitalization programs, and bank loan restructuring; (ii) and resilience strengthening programs that include infrastructure development and improving good corporate governance and strengthening the bank supervision system. In 2002, the main policy priority was directed at strengthening the resilience of the banking system through maximizing the implementation of the 25 Basle Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision , the description of which is outlined in the Master Plan for Improving the Effectiveness of Bank Supervision. Efforts to maintain the CAR of banks that have reached 8% continue to be carried out, especially for banks whose capital structure is still vulnerable to the influence of rising interest rates and weakening exchange rates as well as declining loans. On the other hand, to restore the banking intermediation function, we will encourage banks to channel more credit to sectors that have been deemed ready and have relatively low risks such as export credit and SME credit. In addition, efforts to improve bank health are also supported by efforts to reduce the number of non-performing loans (NPLs) of national banks by requiring banks to achieve the NPL target of 5% by the end of 2002. Furthermore, steps to strengthen banking infrastructure will continue to be taken by encouraging the development of Islamic banks and rural banks and together with the government to prepare for the establishment of the Deposit Insurance Corporation and the Financial Services Authority. Dear Members of the Council, To support the effective implementation of monetary policy and efforts to create a sound banking system, in the field of payment system, in 2002 Bank Indonesia continues to make various efforts to improve to create an efficient, fast, safe and reliable national payment system. In the field of cash payment systems, the policy is directed at providing money that is fit for circulation and meets the needs of the community both in terms of nominal and type of fractions. Meanwhile, in the field of cashless payment systems, policy measures are directed at reducing payment risk, improving the quality and service capacity of payment systems as well as regulating payment system supervision in order to encourage the realization of a fast, safe and efficient payment system. Dear Members of the Council, We can also convey that the policy to be adopted by Bank Indonesia is highly dependent on policies in other fields and the development of various risk factors and uncertainties. Thus, policy coordination is a very important factor in supporting the success of the overall economic recovery. In this regard, we have coordinated policy implementation with the Government several times either through Coordination Meetings at the Ministerial level or coordination at the technical level. On several occasions, we have also proposed to the Government some efforts that can be taken in the context of economic revitalization through the formulation of an integrated Economic Policy package. The proposed breakthrough policy measures in the economic-monetary and banking sectors are generally aimed at answering various real economic problems such as empowering Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) and to provide new optimism to the public towards economic recovery efforts. The move is expected to produce a credible economic policy package so that it will regenerate the confidence of economic actors in the economic recovery process. Next, let us provide an explanation of the Board Members' questions that have been submitted in writing. 1. ASSUMPTION OF INFLATION RATE, EXCHANGE VALUE AND INTEREST RATE OF SBI Pertanvaan: a. Please be able to convey some assumptions regarding the inflation rate, rupiah exchange rate and SBI interest rate in 2003. Please also convey the supporting factors and background of Bank Indonesia's forecast regarding the magnitude of these assumptions. c. To achieve a single-digit inflation rate, what efforts will be made by Bank Indonesia in 2003 and to what extent is the coordination with the Minister of Finance as fiscal manager and the Minister of Industry and Trade responsible in the real sector. Answer: Dear Members of the Council, Given that the questions la and 1c are interrelated, let me summarize both of the answers. For Board Members, please note that since the beginning of 2002, in addition to announcing the CPI inflation target for 2002, Bank Indonesia has also announced medium-term inflation for the next 5 years. This step is taken so that the process of reducing inflation (disinflation) can be carried out gradually, so that the inflation target set will be realistic. The announcement of medium-term inflation is also intended to provide a reference for the public and business actors in planning their economic activities in the medium and long term. Thus, medium-term inflation expectations can be directed at a lower inflation rate without compromising the viability of economic recovery or in other words, this berthap disinflationary processwill prevent the implementation of extra-tight monetary policies that can negatively impact the economic recovery process. Through a cautious monetary policy, the move is expected to take the inflation rate in a more lace directiongradually, so that in the next five years it will be around 6.0%-7.0%. Nevertheless, achievement of the inflation target is also dependent on the amount of administered price pressure going forward in connection with the government's efforts to gradually reduce subsidies. Furthermore, in order to achieve the inflation target, monetary policy is directed at controlling primary money by absorbing excess liquidity to suit the real needs of the economy. This policy is taken bykeeping in mind that the real interest rate is in the range of 4.0%-5.0%. In addition, to be more effective in monetary policy, Bank Indonesia will continue to pay attention to the factors behind the formation of inflation, namely whether it originated from thesupply side or the demand side. With this step, the excessive response that results in the increase in interest rates can be avoided. In this regard, operationally, monetary control will be carried out by optimizing available monetary instruments, in particular through open market operations and foreign exchange sterilization to reduce excess liquidity that can exert new pressures on exchange rates and inflation. Meanwhile, with regard to the prospects for the average exchange rate a year, we can put forward as follows. In 2002 the rupiah exchange rate is expected to reach the range of Rp9,500-Rp10,500 per USD. Meanwhile, for 2003, the rupiah exchange rate isexpected to move in a stronger direction, if socio-political stability can continue to improve, supported by improving security conditions and legal certainty. The chances of rupiah appreciation will be even higher if it is barredwith improvements in macro and microeconomic fundamentals that can reduce the gap in demand and supply of foreign exchange in the market. The improvement of macroeconomic fundamentals will largely depend on the Government's efforts to maintain fiscal sustainability and maintain monetary stability so that it can help the wheels of economic activity run. Meanwhile, microeconomic fundamentals can improve if several structural problems such as debt and corporate restructuring, as well as revitalization of the banking sector can be resolved more quickly, so that the banking intermediation process can run normally again. Improving microeconomic conditions will also largely depend on the Government's efforts tosupport the creation of an efficient business world. The improvement in macro and microeconomic fundamentals can also improve public confidence or market confidence both domestically and internationally, which in turn will have a positive effect onthe stability and strengthening of the rupiah. Furthermore, improving investor confidence in macro and microeconomic fundamentals and also improving the global economy are expected to attract foreign investors to investin Indonesia, which in turn will support the stability and strengthening of the rupiah. In order to stabilize prices, Bank Indonesia will also continue to coordinate with relevant departments, particularly the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Industry and Trade. From the fiscal side, efforts to reduce the budget deficit are important factors in efforts to help the effectiveness of monetary policy in reducinginflation. Among them is the need for consistent government measures with clearer stages in the implementation of administered price increases, so that the announcement effect can be minimized. Meanwhile, considering that inflationis not caused by conditions in the real sector as we have experienced in recent years, efforts to improve on this side need attention, for example in the form of improvements in the distribution of goods. In addition, with the banjir disaster that has hit our homeland recently, efforts to improve infrastructure, have become very important. Therefore, the measures taken by the Ministry of Industry and Trade and other relevant departments towards improvement are very helpfulin an effort to suppress inflation. In order to coordinate with the ministers of economic affairs, including the Minister of Finance and the Minister of Industry and Trade, regular coordination meetings are held between Bank Indonesia and the Minister of Finance Economy. The coordination meeting has been held periodically since October 1999 until now. Meanwhile, for topics related to the duties of Bank Indonesia, the Governor of Bank Indonesia was also invited to the CabinEt Limited Session chaired by the President of the Republic of Indonesia, in the Coordination Meeting and Cabinet Session, the latest economic developments and steps needed to be taken to overcome the existing problems. In addition to the above Coordination Meeting forum, inorder to synchronize monetary sector policy with the fiscal and real sectors, Bank Indonesia has also invited ministers for economic affairs several times to discuss the Monthly Board of Governors' Meetings (RDG). Pertanvaan: b. In order to pursue a favorable exchange rate for Indonesia's economic development, what efforts will be made by Bank Indonesia in 2003. Answer: Dear Dewart members, In order to achieve a favorable exchange rate for the development of economists, Bank Indonesia will continue to strive to maintain rupiah stability through monetary policy that is implemented consistently, directedly and measurably. In a floating exchange rate system, the price balance that occurs in the salt exchange marketwill be determined by the market mechanism. Thus, the main role of Bank Indonesia in this regard is to reduce excessive rupiah exchange rate volatility so as to provide certainty for the business world and in turn can reduce the gangguan of the ongoing economic recovery process. Basically, rupiah depreciation pressures are caused by the gap between the amount of demand and supply in the market, due to the large need to repay foreign debt and import needs while the amount of supply tends to be slowed down bythe US - especially with the global recession that affects the performance of Indonesia's non-oil and gas exports. In addition, various fundamental problems in the economy and the still large uncertainty factors as reflected in Indonesia's country risk also influenced theperception of the rupiah, thereby exacerbating pressures on the rupiah exchange rate. Thus, ideally, an integrated and fundamental policy is needed so that in turn it can create a conducive business climate and encourage the inflow of capital back into the country. These measures include domestic and foreign debt restructuring policies, corporate restructuring in IBRA, efforts to improve banking health and restore the intermediation function of perbankan, in which implementation Bank Indonesia requires coordination with various parties, especially the government. In conjunction with such recovery measures, Bank Indonesia in the short term continues to strive for rupiah exchange rate stabilityamong others through sterlization/intervention policies. It is hoped that this step can help the stability of the rupiah by reducing the acceleration of depressive/appreciative pressures. In addition, Bank Indonesia directly or indirectly monitors the developmentin the foreign exchange market so that it is expected to reduce price fluctuations through policy measures resulting from the analysis. For example, giving advice to banks that have foreign exchange obligations on a regular basis tomeet their needs in a planned manner. Periodically, Bank Indonesia also holds communication forums with market participants so that they can get direct input on the latest market conditions. From the combination of these measures, namely short-term policies andefforts to improve economic fundamentals in the long term, it is expected to achieve rupiah exchange rate stability. How is the development of the implementation of the Customer Fund Guarantee Program to date, especially in bpr-bpr that have been liquidated related to the must be accompanied by counter-guarantees from the receiving banks? Answer: Distinguished Councillors, In order to regulate the bpr industry that is healthy and able to play a role in economic development in the future, the suspension of business activities (BBKU) is astrategic step from Bank Indonesia that needs to be carried out. The suspension of business activities is only carried out on rural banks whose business conditions cannot be saved and advised anymore because it will interfere with the running of the banking system, so thatthe BBKU steps are expected to run better. The suspension of BPR's business activities can take place properly by the Government Guarantee Program which provides guarantees for recorded public deposit funds and is supported by valid evidence. The Government Guarantee Program has been started since January 1998, which hopes that the restoration of public confidence in the RURAL BANK industry will increase as a result of the monetary crisis that occurred in early June 1997. This guarantee program is still ongoing with the provision of guarantee funds by the Government and has been allocated for guarantee needs until 2002. In relation to the presence of counter-guarantees for BPR-BPR recipients of guarantee funds, the Minister of Finance Rl through his letter No. S-3 / MK.06 / 2002 dated January 9, 2002 has agreed with Bank Indonesia that the implementation of the BPR obligation guarantee program is still based on the Joint Agreement(MoU) dated January 31, 2001 which basically needs to be pursued as much as possible counter-guarantee. In line with this, Bank Indonesia through in-depth research since mid-2001 and after providing sufficient time for BPR owners/administrators to nourish their rural banks, has suspended business activities on 82 rural banks throughout Indonesia. The suspension of business activities was carried out in 2 (two) phases of each phase I of 38 RURAL BANKS carried out inmid-December 2001 and Phase II of 44 RURAL BANKS was carried out in early January 2002. The determination of the business freeze of 82 rural banks was carried out through an in-depth study process in accordance with Bank Indonesia Regulation No. 3/15/PBI/2001 dated 21 September2002 and has been refined through PBI No. 3/24/PBI/2001 dated December 24, 2001. The criteria for BPR that is frozen for business activities are: 95 A BPR that has not carried out business activities and or its management and or owner is no longer known, or 95 Rural Banks that have a Minimum Capital Provision Adequacy ratio (KPMM) equal to or less than 0%, and or the average cash ratio for the last 6 (six) months is less than 1%. The 82 rural banks in question meet the requirements of the Government Guarantee Program so that public deposits at the BPR will be paid through the Government guarantee fund. However, the implementation of payments is carried out if the Temporary Manager (PS) of the BPR has verifiedthe existence of public deposits (savings and time deposits) and the results of the verification of the said PS have been thoroughly re-examined by the Public Accounting Firm that has been appointed by the Minister of Finance Rl. Because the duties of the Temporary Manager require along time, especially the verification of bpr assets and liabilities, it is hoped that people who have their deposits in the BPR can be patient and not panic and can maintain security and order to wait for the announcement of the payment process from the Seme Ntara Managerin due course. It should also be stated that Bank Indonesia is conducting research on BPR managements who have frozen their business activities. This is done in order to find out whether the cause of the bank's collapse is due to pure business factors, or there is an element of deviation or carelessness carried out by the BPR management. On this occasion, we can report several other problems related to the settlement of third party funds of BPR customers who have had their legal licenses revokedbefore the enactment of the guarantee program (before January 1998): 95 There were 60 rural banks that were revoked business licenses (including balido group BPR) before the enactment of the guarantee program with a total of third party funds of IDR 141.4 billion. Answer: Dear Members of the Council, In connection with the aforementioned question, we can inform you that there was an increase in the collection of public funds from Rp699.1 trillion in December 2000 to Rp797.4 trillion in December 2001, or an increase of Rp98.3 trillion (14.1%). In disbursing its funds, banks not only channel their funds to credit, but also invest in other productive pr assetssuch as SBI, interbank placements, securities and participation. The banking intermediation function of banking intermediation has begun to show signs of improvement, although not as fast as expected. This condition is reflected in the loans disbursed by banks which during 2001 amounted to Rp56.8 trillion orapproximately Rp4.7 trillion per month. When viewed in outstanding loans, there was an increase from Rp320.6 trillion in December 2000 to Rp358.6 trillion or grew by around 12% while in 2000 it grew by around 15%. Meanwhile, in terms of demand for new loans by debtors, it looks quite high, but the high risk factors for business activities make debtors have not made optimal credit withdrawals, which is reflected in the high credit commitments that have been provided by banks but have not been withdrawn by debtors, amounting to Rp70.5 trillion as of December 2001. The number of new loan disbursements during 2001 is shown in the following table: In Billion Rp Tw-I/01 Tw-II/01 Tw-in/oi Tw-IV/01 SOEs 1,479 2,597 3,424 5,394 Recap 528 910 586 795 BTO 1,321 3,116 3,339 5,293 Category A 3,410 3,647 4,564 5,795 Foreign Banks 1,572 1,509 1,477 1,819 Mixed Banks 579 884 678 514 BPD 211 226 681 466 Total 9,100 12,890 14,750 20,077 Some of the problems faced by banks in lending include : 95 Internally, the bank is still consolidating and trying to comply with the provisions of the prudential principle. In addition, the real sector itself is still not doing well, although most of the micro and small real sector groups are still doing well and can be financed by banks. In relation to the provision of credit to the middle and large groups, banks are still waiting because the large group of companies is still in the process of being restructured by IBRA. 95 In the development of small and medium enterprises (SMEs), there are obstacles to the lack of guarantees from customers. Some of the efforts made by Bank Indonesia are related to improving the bank's intermediation function, including: 95 The extension of the deadline for the settlement of the Maximum Credit Limit (BMPK) due to exchange rate fluctuations-and/or a decrease in bank capital during the economic crisis, is extended to no later than the end of December 2002. In addition, to accelerate the intermediation function of the banking bank, Bank Indonesia will take steps to: a. Adjusting the calculation of the colletibility of productive assets which is temporarily more focused on the accuracy of interest payments and cashflow projections. b. Reducing the risk weight in the calculation of ATMR for export loans guaranteed by the Indonesian Export Bank (IDX). c. Encouraging the expansion of bank branch offices associated with the development of SMEs, especially for areas that need to be encouraged by economic development. Pertanvaan : 5. Answer: Dear Dewart members, In line with Act No. 23 of 1999 concerning Bank Indonesia article 60, Bank Indonesia does not distinguish between the operational budget and the non-operational budget, as stated in the 2002 Bank Indonesia Annual Budget (ATBI) which we submitted to the House of Representatives on December 10, 2001. In order to answer the questions of the esteemed members of the Board, on this occasion we can put forward the grouping of costs commonly incurred by a central bank, namely the costs of determining and implementing monetary policy, the cost of arranging and maintaining the smooth running of the payment system, the cost of setting up and supervising banks and the costs of managing internal resources. In the cost of determining and implementing monetary policy, there are monetary control operating costs (SBI discount fees) and foreign exchange management costs (interest on foreign loans) whose realization amounts cannot be fully predicted by Bank Indonesia. In 2002, the total costs of Bank Indonesia in order to carry out its duties amounted to Rp24,963 billion and is expected to increase to Rp26,193 billion by the end of 2003. The possible increase in costs incurred by Bank Indonesia in 2003 was caused, among others, by changes in the massive monetary economy such as the amount of primary money, the volume of SBI, the inflation rate, the foreign interest rate, the SBI discount rate and the exchange rate. Pertanvaan: 6. Is Bank Indonesia in fiscal year 2003 going to issue or print money, if yes how much it is and what fractions. Answer: Dear Board Members In accordance with article 20 of Law No.23/1999, Bank Indonesia is the only institution authorized to issue and circulate rupiah currency and revoke, withdraw and destroy money from circulation. In carrying out each of these activities in abag, it begins with a plan in the form of routine (short-term) planning and long-term planning.
