Partisipasi aktif tersebut tidak begitu terasa di saat kondisi normal namun akan sangat terasa di saat krisis keuangan terjadi, dimana kemampuan Bank Sentral dalam mengantisipasi potensi krisis dan mengatasi krisis yang sesungguhnya secara critical sangat bergantung dari kelengkapan-kecepatan- keakuratan informasi, kedalaman pemahaman serta seberapa besar kewenangan yang dimiliki di dalam menjalankan tugasnya baik sebagai pengawas bank maupun sebagai Bank Sentral. Hadirin yang saya hormati, Kategori ketiga, persoalan institutional building dalam reformasi sektor keuangan Indonesia terkait proses pengembangan dan pendalaman pasar keuangan. Dengan kepastian peraturan dan upaya pengawasan di sektor keuangan yang optimal, maka terbuka lebar pintu untuk pengembangan dan pendalaman pasar keuangan lebih lanjut. Pendalaman pasar keuangan diarahkan untuk mendorong pengembangan produk-produk keuangan yang sekaligus dapat digunakan bank dan institusi keuangan sebagai alternatif penyaluran dan penempatan dana secara produktif bagi sektor riel khususnya pembiayaan infrastruktur. Dengan demikian diharapkan pasar uang menjadi lebih likuid dan bank tidak terlalu bergantung terhadap pendapatan dari penempatan pada instrumen Bl. Di sisi lain, hal tersebut akan menambah banyak pilihan bagi pelaku ekonomi untuk memperoleh sumber pendanaan dari penerbitan berbagai instrumen dan produk keuangan sehingga akan semakin mendorong naik efisiensi sektor keuangan. Sumber pendanaan kredit akan terpacu untuk mulai bersaing dengan instrumen pasar keuangan, sehingga secara keseluruhan akan menekan turun "biaya" memperoleh pendanaan bagi pelaku ekonomi. Selain itu dengan pendalaman pasar akan dapat timbul peluang bagi terciptanya kebutuhan tenaga kerja dengan skills khusus sehingga membuka kesempatan kerja. Namun saya ingin ada sebuah catatan penting, bahwa jalan menuju pendalaman pasar, perlu kajian yang dalam. Hal ini harus menjadi agenda ke depan bagi Pemerintah, Bank Indonesia, bekerjasama dengan pelaku ekonomi di sektor keuangan. Para hadirin yang saya hormati, Ketiga kategori permasalahan dalam reformasi sektor keuangan di atas menyangkut institutional building yang notabene tidak dapat ditunda lagi untuk dimulai. Hal ini sejalan dengan semangat di dunia internasional yang tengah bergairah untuk mencetak ulang sektor keuangan internasional, kembali kepada khittah keberhati- hatian. Walaupun secara relatif dibandingkan negara lain, kita memiliki sektor keuangan yg tetap solid dalam keadaan krisis 2008/09 kemarin namun Indonesia tidak bisa ketinggalan dalam proses reformasi keuangan global ini. Para Hadiri yang saya muliakan, Demikian yang dapat saya sampaikan beberapa pokok pemikiran ini. Saya meyakini bahwa hanya dengan kebersamaan dan kerja keras dari kita semua, industry keuangan kita akan lebih maju dan memberikan kontribusi yang optimal bagi perekonomian nasional. Saya berharap diskusi dan perdebatan di sini akan melahirkan sintesa yang baik bagi bangsa kita. Akhirul kalam, saya mengucapkan selamat berseminar kepada semua peserta, semoga segala upaya kita dalam membangun bangsa ini melalui seminar pagi ini memperoleh ridho dari Allah SWT. Sekian dan terima kasih Wassalamualaikum Warrahmatullahi \A/a Barakatuh Jakarta, 8 Juli 2010 BANK INDONESIA Darmin Nasution

Title: Pidato Deputi Gubernur, Muliaman D. Hadad Pada Grand Launching BRI Syariah
text: POINTERS REMARKS BY THE DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF BANK INDONESIA AT THE GRAND LAUNCHING OF BRI SYARIAH JAKARTA, 1st JULY 2009 Assalamu'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh Introduction 1. Thank God, let's pray for the presence of Allah SWT because tonight I and all of us can attend here and witness the inauguration / grand launching of BRI Syariah. I am really happy, because this event marks the presence of one sharia commercial bank (BUS) in Indonesia, namely BRI Syariah, so that currently we have 5 BUSes (note: 4 other BUSes: Bank Muamalat Indonesia, Bank Syariah Mandiri, Bank Mega Syariah Indonesia, Bank Bukopin Syariah) 2. Spin off and previously bri Sharia Business Unit (UUS) to bus - BRI Syariah is certainly a form of BRI business transformation in strengthening a more dedicated business structure and more focused on bus nis operations Islamic banks. With the establishment of BRI Syariah, BRI will have greater potential to achieve its business goals, especially by providing greater flexibility and business autonomy to BRI Syariah as its subsidiary. 3. Sya believes, with the combination of resources and the accumulation of long business experience owned by BRI, coupled with various achievements and other strengths that belong to it, the presence of BRI Syariah can be further strengthen our Islamic banking industry, so that it can support the Indonesian financial system and contribute to the Indonesian economy. Therefore, I would like to say "thank you and congratulations on the establishment of BRI Syariah " 4. We should also express our deep gratitude, because in the midst of the impact of the global financial crisis that continues today, from time to time the development of shariah finance in Indonesia, it continues to show progress that has not even hindered the expansion, especially in the Islamic banking industry. In terms of industry, our Sharia industry is still 'attractive', this can be seen from the number of 'players' in the industry continues to increase. Currently, there are 30 Islamic banks consisting of BUS, UUS, and BPRS with a total number of offices reaching 895 offices. The average growth of the number of Islamic banking offices over the past 4 years has reached up to 24%. 5. The increasing attractiveness of our Islamic bank industry is also followed by encouraging financial performance indicators, both as indicated by the growth of assets, deposits, and financing/'financing which on average per year reaches above the 30% mark (Note, Assets: 36%, Deposits: 32% and financing: 37%). Similarly, the fund disbursement ratio (FDR) reached 104%, while roe reached 62% per year. And We know that the share of Islamic banking (April 2009) also continues to increase gradually and definitely, namely 2.2% of the share of national banking assets. 6. If we speak in the context of the global Islamic financial industry, data from various sources shows that although the share of islamic financial assets in the world is currently still around 1% of the total global financial assets and the market of more than 1.4 billion Muslims in the world, the Islamic financial industry has made it a fast-growing and competitive alternative to financial services. The world Islamic financial market continues to develop and grow high at 30% since 2000 and is expected to continue to increase. (Note: at the end of 2007, total assets were USD660 billion with revenue of USD53 billion). In the midst of a relatively volatile short-term market condition, global Islamic finance continues to grow massively and is projected to reach USD 1.6 trillion and total revenue of USD 120 billion in 2012. Islamic Finance and Financial System Stability 7. We have learned that the domestic and international economic environment, which encompasses the financial business including Islamic finance today, has turned into a formidable challenge. In an open and integrated financial market like today, the dynamics of the world market and the financial crisis resolution measures taken by developed countries have a rapid and sharp impact on market developments and the economies of emerging countries such as Indonesia. Therefore, concerted action between monetary policy and fiscal stimulus continues to be pursued in various countries to increase confidence. Nevertheless, this was only achieved, when the crisis in the financial system -especially conventional finance- was corrected and subsequently maintained stability, as well as when the flow credit/financing can flow back, when financial markets return to function efficiently, and when prices reflect the real value of an asset. 8. In this challenging peri ode, financial institutions, especially Islamic financial institutions, have an important role to build confidence in the stability of the financial system and ensure continued access to financing in the real sector. The power of Islamic financial institutions by default prohibits the transaski of economists i without a clear, non-speculative economic underlying, and reduces the decoupling of the expansion of financial transactions and the growth of the real sector this has led to the hope that the growth of Islamic finance, including banking, can be one of the solutions for KRIsis. 9. Even the Islamic banking and financial system can take a greater role to create a more efficient, stable and equitable financial system. This is supported by the basic characteristics of the Islamic financial system which highlight aspects of fairness and honesty in transactions, ethical investment, prioritizing the values of togetherness and brotherhood in production and avoiding speculative activities in financial transactions, making its expediency d apat enjoyed not only by Muslims but also by all Indonesian society. 10. The presence of the Islamic financial system and economy is expected to provide the color and resilience of the current economic system. Sharia regulation has a focus on financial activities on the real sector is actually the essence of the concept of governance and increasing stability in the financial system. In many ways, the concept of sharia economy has actually lived in Indonesian society since several centuries ago. The tradition of mutual aid and sharing of agricultural production is not new. Future Agenda : Indonesian Sharia Financial Architecture and Human Capital Investment 11. On this occasion, I would like to emphasize on two other aspects that are important in the development of Islamic finance, especially Islamic banking in the future. The first aspect is clarity in the vision and objectives of the development of the Islamic financial system in the future. As is known, we already have an Indonesian Banking Architecture and also the Indonesian Sharia Banking Development Blueprint as a frame of reference in carrying out national banking and also Islamic banking. However, with the enormous concern in the creation of financial system stability in general, as well as the great demands and expectations of the Islamic financial system as a system that can reduce thestability of the financial system, bank Indonesia, the Ministry of Finance, and related agencies are gradually developing an architecture or landscape of Indonesian Islamic finance (AKSI) which later part of the Indonesian Financial System Architecture a (ASKI). In this ACTION, the design and proram will be integrated in developing the Islamic financial system both from the banking industry, capital market, and takaful both in terms of legal and regulatory frameworks, infrastructure, and contextually condusive. 12. The second aspect is the need for investment in the development of human resources in islamic finance. The rapid development of the sharia industry in the country, especially sharia development, is absolutely supported by the availability of competent human resources and in adequate terms. As an illustration, if calculated on average with an HR growth rate of 23% then every year no less than 1,000 new employees will be needed per year. the year. (note: as of April 2009 The number of HUMAN RESOURCES BUS is 8,383 org, UUS is 2,169 org, and BPRS is 2,833 org). This number does not include the number of human resources in Islamic financial institutions and other supporting institutions. A fairly large amount while on the other hand the supply of ready-to-use energy in sharia bi dang from Lembaga Pendidikan is still limited. 13. Alhamdulillah, we witnessed that with the market push (market driven) has been responded by our higher education institutions with the opening of many new programs in the field of Islamic economics, both in strata D3, SI, S2, even S3. Some time ago, Al Azhar University Indonesia has inaugurated the opening of its sharia economy program, also ITB in collaboration with LPPI also opened an MBA program in the field of sharia economics. 14. In the future, continuous efforts in the development of human capital and expertise to enlarge the pool of experts and add professionals with high skilled quality are important agenda for us including support and synergy from industry players and educational institutions. Cover 15. Finally, with the various steps taken by Bank Indonesia and the Government in building financial system stability as I stated above, then at the micro-industry level, I hope that players will Islamic banking industry, especially BRI Syariah, perlu continues efforts to significantly strengthen its capacity and capabilities in order to respond to the challenges and environment faced current and future. 16. With the various points above, I would like to close my remarks and once again congratulate the launching of BRI Syariah, hopefully BRI Syariah can be successful and persistently committed to contribute its business to the development of Indonesia's Islamic banking industry . May Allah Almighty always be pleased to give His mercy and blessings to all of us. That's it and thank you/ Billahittaufiq wal hidayah Wassalamu'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh Jakarta, 1st July 2009 Bank Indonesia Muliaman D. Hadad Deputy Governor
text_original: POINTERS SAMBUTAN DEPUTI GUBERNUR BANK INDONESIA PADA GRAND LAUNCHING BRI SYARIAH JAKARTA, 1 JULI 2009 Assalamu'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh Pendahuluan 1. Syukur ahamdulillah mari kita panjatkan kehadirat Allah SWT karena pada malam ini saya dan kita semua dapat hadir disini dan menyaksikan acara peresmian/grand launching BRI Syariah. Saya sungguh berbahagia, karena acara ini menandai hadirnya satu bank umum syariah (BUS) di Indonesia yakni BRI Syariah, sehingga saat ini kita memiliki 5 BUS (catatan : 4 BUS lain : Bank Muamalat Indonesia, Bank Syariah Mandiri, Bank Mega Syariah Indonesia, Bank Bukopin Syariah) 2. Spin off dan sebelumnya Unit Usaha Syariah (UUS) BRI menjadi BUS - BRI Syariah ini tentu menjadi satu bentuk transformasi bisnis BRI dalam memperkuat struktur bisnis yang lebih dedicated dan lebih fokus di operasi bisnis bank syariah. Dengan pembentukan BRI Syariah, BRI akan memiliki potensi yang lebih besar untuk mencapai tujuan-tujuan bisnisnya, terutama dengan memberikan fleksibilitas dan otonomi bisnis yang lebih besar pada BRI Syariah sebagai anak perusahaannya. 3. Saya yakin, dengan kombinasi resources serta akumulasi pengalaman bisnis yang panjang yang dimiliki BRI, ditambah dengan berbagai prestasi dan kekuatan lain yang dipunyai, kehadiran BRI Syariah dapat lebih memperkuat industri perbankan syariah kita, sehingga dapat menopang sistem keuangan Indonesia dan berkontribusi pada perekonomian Indonesia. Karenanya, saya ucapkan "syukur dan selamat atas berdirinya BRI Syariah ini " 4. Rasa syukur yang mendalam ini juga patut kita panjatkan, karena di tengah imbas krisis finansial global yang masih berlanjut hingga saat ini, dari waktu ke waktu perkembangan shariah finance di Indonesia terus memperlihatkan kemajuan/progress yang sagat berarti, bahkan tidak menghalangi adanya ekspansi khususnya di industri perbankan syariah. Dari sisi industri, industri syariah kita masih 'atraktif', ini terlihat dari jumlah 'pemain' di industri terus meningkat. Saat telah ada 30 bank syariah yang terdiri dari BUS, UUS, dan BPRS dengan total jumlah kantor mencapai 895 kantor. Pertumbuhan rata-rata jumlah kantor perbankan syariah selama 4 tahun terakhir mencapai hingga 24%. 5. Meningkatnya attractiveness industri bank syariah kita juga diikuti dengan indikator kinerja keuangan yang menggembirakan, baik yang ditunjukkan dari growth aset, DPK, dan pembiayaan/'financing yang rata-rata per tahun mencapai di atas angka 30% (Catatan, Aset: 36%, DPK : 32% dan pembiayaan : 37%). Demikian pula dengan rasio penyaluran dana (FDR) mencapai 104%, sedangkan ROE mencapai 62% per tahun. Dan kita tahu, bahwa share perbankan syariah (April 2009) juga terus meningkat secara bertahap dan pasti, yakni 2,2% terhadap pangsa aset perbankan nasional. 6. Apabila kita berbicara dalam konteks industri keuangan syariah global, data dari berbagai sumber menunjukkan bahwa meskipun share aset keuangan syariah dunia saat ini masih di sekitar 1% dari total aset keuangan global dan market lebih dari separo 1,4 miliar muslim dunia, industri keuangan syariah telah menjadikan alternatif jasa keuangan yang tumbuh pesat dan kompetitif. Pasar keuangan syariah dunia terus berkembang dan tumbuh tinggi yakni 30% sejak tahun 2000 dan diperkirakan terus meningkat. (Catatan : akhir tahun 2007, total aset USD660 miliar dengan revenue USD53 miliar). Di tengah kondisi short-term market yang relatif masih volatile, keuangan islam global terus tumbuh masif dan diproyeksikan mencapai USD 1,6 triliun dan pendapatan total USD 120 miliar di tahun 2012. Keuangan Syariah dan Kestabilan Sistem Keuangan 7. Kita telah mafhum bahwa lingkungan ekonomi domestik dan internasional, yang melingkupi bisnis keuangan termasuk keuangan syariah saat ini, telah berubah menjadi sebuah tantangan yang berat. Dalam pasar keuangan yang terbuka dan terintegrasi seperti saat ini, dinamika pasar dunia dan langkah resolusi krisis keuangan yang ditempuh negara maju memberikan dampak yang cepat dan tajam pada perkembangan pasar dan perekonomian negara emerging seperti Indonesia. Karenanya concerted action antara kebijakan moneter dan stimulus fiskal terus ditempuh di berbagai negara untuk meningkatkan confidence. Namun demikian, hal ini baru tercapai, ketika krisis di sistem keuangan -khususnya keuangan konvensional- diperbaiki dan selanjutnya dipertahankan kestabilannya, serta ketika arus kredit/pembiayaan dapat mengalir kembali, ketika pasar keuangankembali berfungsi efisien, dan ketika harga-harga merefleksikan real value dari suatu aset. 8. Pada peri ode yang penuh tantangan ini, lembaga keuangan khususnya lembaga keuangan syariah memiliki peran yang penting untuk membangun confidence kestabilan sistem keuangan tersebut serta memastikan berlanjutnya akses pembiayaan pada sektor riil. Kekuatan lembaga keuangan syariah yang by default melarang transaski ekonomi tanpa underlying economic yang jelas, non-speculative, dan mengurangi decoupling ekspansi transaksi keuangan dan pertumbuhan sector riil ini menyebabkan besamya harapan agar tumbuhnya keuangan syariah termasuk perbankan dapat menjadi salah satu solusi krisis. 9. Bahkan sistem sistem perbankan dan keuangan syariah dapat mengambil peran yang lebih besar untuk menciptakan sistem keuangan yang lebih efisien, stabil dan berkeadilan. Hal ini didukung oleh karakteristik dasar sistem keuangan syariah yang menonjolkan aspek keadilan dan kejujuran dalam bertransaksi, investasi yang beretika, mengedepankan nilai-nilai kebersamaan dan persaudaraan dalam berproduksi dan menghindari kegiatan spekulatif dalam bertransaksi keuangan, menjadikan kemanfaatannya akan dapat dinikmati tidak saja oleh umat Islam tetapi juga oleh semua masyarakat Indonesia. 10. Kehadiran sistem keuangan dan ekonomi syariah diharapkan dapat memberikan warna dan ketahanan dari sistem perekonomian yang telah ada pada saat ini. Pengaturan syariah terhadap fokus kegiatan keuangan terhadap sektor riil sebenarnya merupakan intisari dari konsep governance dan peningkatan stabilitas dalam sistem keuangan. Dalam banyak hal, konsep ekonomi syariah sebenarnya telah hidup dalam masyarakat Indonesia sejak beberapa abad yang lalu. Tradisi gotong royong dan berbagi hasil produksi pertanian bukanlah suatu hal yang baru. Agenda ke Depan : Arsitektur Keuangan Syariah Indonesia dan Human Capital Investment 11. Dalam kesempatan ini, saya ingin menekankan pada dua aspek lain yang penting dalam pengembangan keuangan syariah khususnya perbankan syariah ke depan. Aspek pertama adalah kejelasan dalam visi dan tujuan pengembangan system keuangan syariah ke depan. Sebagaimana diketahui, kita telah memiliki Arsitektur Perbankan Indonesia dan juga Blueprint Pengembangan Perbankan Syariah Indonesia sebagai kerangka acuan dalam mengembangkan perbankan nasional dan juga perbankan syariah. Namun dengan adanya concern yang sangat besar pada terciptanya kestabilan system keuangan secara umum, serta tuntutan dan harapan yang besar pada sistem keuangan syariah sebagai sistem yang dapat menyokong kestabilan sistem keuangan maka Bank Indonesia, Departemen Keuangan, dan instansi terkait secara bertahap sedang mengembangkan satu arsitektur atau landskap keuangan syariah Indonesia (AKSI) yang nantinya bagian dari Arsitektur Sistem Keuangan Indonesia (ASKI). Dala AKSI ini akan diintegrasikan rancangan dan proram dalam mengembangkan sistem keuangan syariah baik dari industri perbankan, pasar modal, maupun takaful baik dari sisi kerangka legal dan pengaturannya, infrastruktur, dan lingkuingan yang kondusifnya. 12. Aspek kedua, adalah pada kebutuhan investasi pada pengembangan SDM di bi dang keuangan syariah. Pesatnya perkembangan industri syariah di tanah air, khususnya perbaankan syariah, mutlak ditunjang dengan tersedianya SDM yang kompeten dan dalam jumlah yang memadai. Sebagai ilustrasi, apabila dihitung secara rata-rata dengan tingkat pertumbuhan SDM sebesar 23% maka setiap tahun akan dibutuhkan tidak kurang dari 1.000,- orang pegawai baru per tahunnya. (catatan : per April 2009 Jumlah SDM BUS 8.383 org, UUS 2.169 org, dan BPRS 2.833 org). Jumlah tersebut belum termasuk jumlah SDM dilembaga-lembaga keuangan syariah dan lembaga pendukung lainnya. Suatu jumlah yang terbilang besar sementara disisi lain supply tenaga siap pakai dalam bi dang syariah dari Lembaga Pendidikan masih terbatas. 13. Alhamdulillah kita menyaksikan bahwa dengan dorongan pasar {market driven) tersebut telah direspons lembaga perguruan tinggi kita dengan pembukaan banyak program baru di bidang ekonomi syariah, baik pada strata D3, SI, S2, bahkan S3. Beberapa waktu lalu, Universitas Al Azhar Indonesia telah meresmikan pembukaan program ekonomi syariahnya, juga ITB bekerjasama dengan LPPI juga membuka program MBA di bidang ekonomi syariah. 14. Ke depan, upaya berkelanjutan dalam pengembangan human capital dan keahlian untuk memperbesar pool of experts dan menambah profesional dengan high skilled quality menjadi agenda penting bagi kita termasuk dukungan dan sinergi dari pelaku industri dan lembaga pendidikan. Penutup 15. Akhirnya dengan berbagai langkah Bank Indonesia dan Pemerintah dalam membangun kestabilan sstem keuangan yang seperti yang saya kemukakan di atas, maka di level mikro industri, saya berharap agar pelaku industri perbankan syariah, khususnya BRI Syariah, perlu terus melanjutkan upaya penguatan capacity dan capabilities nya secara signifikan agar dapat merespon tantangan dan lingkungan yang dihadapi saat ini dan ke depan. 16. Dengan berbagai point di atas, saya ingin menutup sambutan saya ini dan sekali lagi menyampaikan selamat atas launching BRI Syariah, semoga BRI Syariah dapat sukses dan secara persisten committed untuk mengkontribusikan bisnisnya pada pengembangan industri perbankan syariah Indonesia. Semoga Allah SWT senantiasa berkenan memberikan rahmat dan ridha-Nya kepada kita sekalian. Sekian dan terima kasih/ Billahittaufiq wal hidayah Wassalamu'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh Jakarta, 1 Juli 2009 Bank Indonesia Muliaman D. Hadad Deputi Gubernur

Title: Sambutan dan Ceramah Ekonomi, Dr. Darmin Nasution Gubernur Bank Indonesia pada Halal Bihalal Ikatan Sarjana Ekonomi Indonesia (ISEI) - 5 Nopember 2010
text: Economic Celebrations and Talks Dr. Darmin Nasution Halal Bihalal Indonesian Economic Scholars Association (ISEI) 5 November 2010 Which I respect Seniors and Elders of ISEI, ISEI Central Board, Management of ISEI Branches Throughout Indonesia, ISEI Members, Ladies and gentlemen , Assalamu'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh, Good afternoon and greetings to all of us, On this occasion let's say together we offer praise of gratitude to the presence of Allah Almighty because it is by His grace alone that we can gather here, sharing stories and experiences, in a Halal Bihalal Family event The Great Association of Indonesian Ecomy Scholars (ISEI) in 1431 H. Although it is already some time away from the holiday of Iedul Fitri 1431 H, but The spirit of gratitude to God should not have been get to know the time. Father and Mother whom I respect, Gratitude should also be expressed when we examine performance Indonesia's economy these days. We have both followed how the turmoil of the currently ongoing global crisis has been 1 making many countries experience a fairly deep contraction. In the middle such unfavorable conditions, the Indonesian economy in in 2009 it was still able to grow by 4.5%. Our more economic base much supported by domestic demand, especially consumption, turned out to be more resilient to the propagation of the global crisis. Indonesia too aligned with China and India as three countries that are still posted positive growth throughout 2009. In 2010 , Bank Indonesia predicted the economy we will grow by 6.1%, still a fairly high achievement on a regional scale. In 2011 and beyond, if supported by an adequate increase in investment, Bank Indonesia predicts that the domestic economy can continue to grow above 6.0%. In line with the strengthening of economic activity, the rate of inflation shows an increasing tendency. But the increase in inflation in the last few months have been more due to the push of the material group food. The last monitoring shows we still have hope that inflation will be within the target range of 51%. The strength of our economy is also supported by trade performance that stay solid. The balance of payments this year is expected to record surplus of USD 27.4 billion, so that the accumulated foreign exchange reserves will continue to increase. Our foreign exchange reserves as of October 28th have reached USD 91.1 billion. The growing hope of improving the economy can also be achieved by us look at the financial markets. The Composite Stock Price Index (JCI) continues increased and had reached 3,640 by the end of last October. Ini is the highest level in the history of stock distribution in Indonesia. 2 Father and Mother whom I respect, In the midst of the various positive achievements of our economy today, the challenges ahead are not light. The structure of the industry shows dynamics to be observed. On the one hand, the share of industry-based manufacturing appears to be getting smaller, as a result of resource-based industries an increasingly prominent nature. If left unchecked, this issue can be leads to deindustrialization that can have an impact on declining the added value of the national industry and the erosion of economic productivity. In addition, in the midst of unemployment and poverty problems which Indonesia still faces, the presence of extensive labor-intensive industries is still needed. On the other hand, our domestic manufacturing industry is still thick with import load. This makes high economic growth will coupled with a significant increase in imports, which has an impact on the decrease in the current account surplus. If our high import-charged industrial structure is not change, then there is a risk that we will have a deficit. Under conditions deficit, if the source of financing continues to rely on capital inflows short-term ones that have high volatility, as it happens now, it will create vulnerabilities. Industrial structure links with balance of payments vulnerability still an issue that we must both review and find a solution. In terms of composition, capital and financial balance (capital and financial account) we are indeed still unbalanced. In 2009, inflows capital to our portfolio investment of USD 10.3 billion, much larger from a long-term direct investment (FDI) of only USD 1.9 billion. Bank Indonesia projects that in 2010, conditions will be slightly improved, with portfolio investment set to reach USD 15.5 billion while FDI increased to USD 9.4 billion. When viewed more in, the background of the entry of FDI into Indonesia turns out to tend to oriented domestic market rather than for export. Incoming FDI 3 it also requires additional imports as a complement to capital. This condition makes an increased FDI can make imports increase, which again can lead to a current account deficit and disruption of the external balance. Our rapidly heating economy on the balance of payments side also apparently also followed on the internal side. The condition of the infrastructure that is still inadequate, combined with our geographical challenges have, making the seemingly increasingly serious obstacles in production and distribution. This supply side constraint has been in the consistently keeping our inflation higher than countries region. Bank Indonesia's latest projections show that core inflation is already again crawled up, in the direction of 4.5% in 2010 and 5.0% in 2011. High economic growth, which is accompanied by potential high inflation increases, mainly spurred from the supply side, indicates a problem with the internal balance. The existence of potential internal and external imbalances, behind the success story of the Indonesian economy during the face of the crisis, is a real challenge for all of us that must be answered immediately. Father and Mother whom I respect, The highly dynamic global environment does make the management of macroeconomic policies is increasingly complex. This is because our economy cannot shy away from the effects of change a constellation of post-crisis global economic policies, particularly those that pursued by developed countries. For some developed countries, the past global crisis is indeed enough destructive impact, where there was interaction between sectors finance and the real sector are no longer working as they should. This condition is related to the circle of crisis problems that runs so fast because of the work of a known mechanism 4 as a financial accelerator, which is a condition where the financial sector amplify what is happening in the real sector so that it has more impact extremes. This mechanism appears to have worked in the past boom period (early 2000s), as well as in the current crisis. The financial sector became pro- cyclical or causing amplification to the economic cycle. This financial accelerator works as follows. In the boom period or positive shock, the increase in asset prices is usually accompanied by increased bank capital and reduced leverage, which encourages the bank is expanding. Rising asset prices also make it easier for the sector households and businesses obtain loans from banks, which on turn to spur consumption and investment. Conversely, in periods of crisis or negative shock, prices fall assets caused the bank's capital to slump and bank leverage to rise. Because in times of crisis it is very difficult for banks to reach new capital, banks tends to liquidate assets, thus making asset prices more slumped. The impact on the real sector and the economy will be felt more severely when the negative shock hits major banks simultaneously, or there is a systemic effect of a deteriorating bank balance sheet. With the working of the financial accelerator mechanism earlier, in crisis conditions, conventional monetary policy becomes difficult relied on its effectiveness. In America and Japan for example, interest rates which is close to zero percent has not been able to stimulate activities economy. Non-ongoing transmission of monetary policy through tribes interest in turn requires the central bank to go through various non-conventional programs, including quantitave easing (QE), i.e. buying financial instruments directly, by pouring liquidity to financial markets. For example, on November 3rd, America launches QE volume II where it is decided to buy assets of USD 600 billion. 5 Father and Mother whom I respect, On a global scale, we also look at how the economy recovers in different countries running in multispeed recovery, mainly marked with the widening disparity of economic growth between developed and emerging market countries. Disparities are also visible from the side policies, e.g. America continuing to expand temporarily India and Australia on November 2 raised policy rates. Economic recovery momentum in many developed countries is indeed looks weakened. This condition is clearly illustrated by the high unemployment rate, re-weakening of household consumption accompanied by the strengthening of the threat of deflation in the Americas, Europe, and Japan. On the other hand, the economic recovery of emerging market countries particularly in Asia and Latin America , it accelerated rapidly, accompanied by the start of the emergence of inflationary pressures. From the description above, it can be seen that in terms of capital flows, there is indeed a push factor, namely the abundance of liquidity and low interest rates in developed countries, which at the same time are accompanied by a pull factor, that is, improving economic fundamentals, high interest rates, and improving perception of risk to emerging markets. Both factors are in terms of simultaneously, it is causing a torrent of capital flows to emerging market, including to Indonesia. At this time, Indonesia is indeed a magnet for investment destinations for international portfolio capital managers. Current intensity portfolio capital entry to Indonesia in the last three months even getting stronger as those global investors anticipate the move- further steps of monetary policy in America. Regarding the recently announced QE volume II, the Fed is expected will reactivate the large-scale asset purchase program (large-scale asset purchases/LSAP). This program will certainly be more 6 putting pressure on long-term interest rates in the US again, which in turn further reducing capital flows to emerging market countries. Father and Mother whom I respect, We are both witnessing how the wave of intervention in the foreign exchange market, to dampen the pressure of appreciation, has become a menu daily tactical policy in a number of emerging market countries lately. The aftermath of the phenomenon that people temporarily call This currency-war, the accumulation of foreign exchange reserves by emerging market countries also increased rapidly. Dollar depreciation is also accelerating, in addition to the pace of QE volume II, also by the move of a number of emerging market central banks that repositioning their accumulated foreign exchange reserves to non-financial instruments dollar, including other emerging market instruments. Intervention can indeed help withstand the pressure of appreciation, however, it cannot be continuously carried out due to the burden of sterilization costs which is quite large. Therefore, many emerging market countries are starting to thinking seriously about the various policies that belong to the class macroprudential. Even a number of countries responded to the rapid flow of capital enter with capital control, for example the Brazilian government which taxing foreign parties' transactions in the bond market. Solutions to the global capital flow problem circle and The management of this exchange rate policy certainly requires coordination multilateral, and therefore today continues to be a central theme in various international fora, such as in the G-20, ASEAN, IMF, and BIS. 7 Father and Mother whom I respect, The rapid inflow of global capital into our economy brings benefits, but also pose complex problems. Entry foreign capital increases the supply of foreign exchange in the domestic financial market, encouraging rupiah appreciation, and lowering the yield on letters sovereign debt (SUN). A stronger rupiah helps suppress inflation through falling prices of imported goods. Meanwhile, with the decline in yields SUN also lowered the cost of financing the government's budget. On the other hand, the current capital inflows pose problems as it is mostly short-term, easily reverses, triggers asset bubble, and the potential to suppress the value of the rupiah away from its fundamental value (overshoothing). In addition, the torrent capital flows are currently felt to be greater than the capabilities of the real sector and our financial markets to be able to absorb them. In terms of depth as well as the availability of instruments, our financial markets do not seem ready to accept such a rapid inflow of short-term capital. The lack of depth in our financial markets relative to the magnitude of foreign capital makes the domestic financial system vulnerable to sudden change in global investor sentiment. Last May we witnessing how negative sentiments emerge in the form of peaking concerns over the economic crisis in Greece have triggered a withdrawal foreign funds on a large and sudden scale (large and sudden reversal) from the Indonesian economy which is putting strong pressure on Rupiah. Father and Mother whom I respect, In responding to the rapid inflow of capital while mitigating potential risks that can be caused if the capital reverses, Bank Indonesia has taken several policy measures. The issuance of the policy is nothing but to maintain 8 macro stability and maintaining sustainable growth our economy. As the first line of defence, Bank Indonesia continues to prioritize prudent monetary and banking policy management carried out Consistently. This is expected to further strengthen credibility policies that contribute to creating an environment conducive to investment for any kind of investment. Meanwhile, at the operational level, Bank Indonesia has take steps in the form of a policy mix, i.e. by: 1) Accommodating flexible exchange rates i.e. letting the Rupiah experience appreciation, but also keep it from overshooting and not too volatile, that is, through intervention in order to maintain macroeconomic stability, financial stability, and continuity of the current account balance. 2) Cultivate foreign exchange reserves, which are indispensable as an effort to strengthen the shield (as insurance) when facing capital reversal. 3) Selectively take a number of macroprudential policies, to manage capital flows that tend to fluctuate. I need to emphasize here that although a policy instrument conventional such interventions in the foreign exchange market have so far been quite effectively, we still face complexities in policy management Monetary. Liquidity expansion as a direct impact of intervention in the market foreign exchange needs to be reabsorbed through monetary operations so as not to triggering inflation; this has caused the SBI's outstanding to continue to increase. Therefore, realizing the increasing complexity of the problem that in the future, Bank Indonesia will also take non-bank steps conventional in the form of macroprudential policies. On June 16 , 9 a provision of obligation has been issued for the purchaser of the SBI to withhold its holdings for one month in both the primary and secondary markets, which applies to both domestic and foreign actors. The policy quite effective in preventing the occurrence of capital reversals on the scale large and sudden, because investors can no longer cash out the SBI every time. We have witnessed that recently the rupiah exchange rate can be maintained stably. Bank Indonesia also complements liquidity management instruments by introducing a Rupiah Term Deposit (TD) that cannot traded (non-transfarable). This will further narrow down the opportunity of foreign parties in accumulating SBI. Father and Mother whom I respect, Many of us hear the view of the need for us to take capital control policy. However, I see so far some steps the policies we have taken have been quite effective. Nevertheless, certainly only the space for other additional policy options remains open. At the level of international discussions, capital control policy is no longer forbidden if all conventional macro policy options are available deemed no longer adequate to mitigate the adverse effects of the past extreme cross capital. Capital control has good reason to be a part of policy tools in managing capital inflows in case of pressure inflation increases, if the adequacy of foreign exchange reserves is more than optimal, when the value of the domestic currency is overvalued, and when the current the capital that enters the majority is temporary (transitory). Looking at the current conditions, there are indeed more and more authorities in a number of emerging market countries are beginning to consider for designing and implementing capital control policies but in specific and targeted . In order for capital control policy 10 it is effective then it is very important to be able to distinguish between sources and types of capital flows, carefully considering the choice instruments to be used, strengthening communication and capacity institutional, as well as designing entry/exit mechanisms and adjustments against predetermined instruments. In general, capital control instruments that require change the minimum of the already available system will be easier to adjust, communicated, and implemented. However, capital control instruments that requires a fundamental change of an existing system can give rise to greater psychological repercussions and possibly the risk of failure. In short, capital control can be likened to a sword double-edged that should be kept until a once-emergency occurs. Father and Mother whom I respect, Before I ended my remarks, there was one other policy issue that it is good that we take it seriously and immediately, in responding to the rapid flow this incoming capital, that is, how can we reap the greatest benefit- as much as from these capital inflows to drive growth a sustainable economy. In other words, the fundamental issue that what we need to answer together is how we are able to take advantage of this capital flow to a longer period of time. There are a number of steps we can take. First, we should be able to encourage the use of these capital flows to financing for companies and deepening of domestic financial markets. Conveniences and stimulus in the capital market can be provided both to encourage initial/secondary public offering and bonds (bond issuance) for corporations. Even the magnitude of interest such investments from abroad can also be used to support efforts to issue shares and corporate bonds- our state-owned enterprises. 11 Secondly, which is also very important and urgent, we should able to encourage the improvement of the investment and development climate infrastructure by taking advantage of opportunities from the magnitude of investment interest such foreign. The discussion on this subject we have both followed and various policy recommendations have also been submitted and formulated. Now it's just a matter of how we are firmly and consistently implement it. Encouraging investment is critical to increasing capacity Economy. Spurring economic growth without being balanced with increased production capacity will only result in inflationary pressures which mainly arises due to supply-side limitations. Going forward, God willing, with our economic fundamentals improving, interest foreigners to invest in Indonesia will be huge. Moreover, Indonesia has the opportunity to enter the investment grade ranking next year. Father and Mother whom I respect, These are the points of thought in responding to the magnitude of the current capital is coming in from abroad today. We must be able to take advantage of such capital flows for the benefit of economic development Sustainable. The point is that we must indeed be able to maintain stability macroeconomics amid the openness of our economy. Absence of error macro policies do not guarantee that we remain safe from the effects of outside turmoil. Last but not least, may Allah, the Most Compassionate and Merciful me- ridhoi our activities today and always bestow guidance, Guidance, and His mercy to us all. Thank you. Wassalamu 'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh. Dr. Darmin Nasution 12
text_original: Sambutan dan Ceramah Ekonomi Dr. Darmin Nasution Halal Bihalal Ikatan Sarjana Ekonomi Indonesia (ISEI) 5 November 2010 Yang saya hormati Para Senior dan Sesepuh ISEI, Pengurus Pusat ISEI, Pengurus ISEI Cabang Seluruh Indonesia, Para Anggota ISEI, Bapak-Ibu undangan lainnya, Assalamu'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh, Selamat siang dan salam sejahtera bagi kita semua, Pada kesempatan ini mari bersama-sama kita panjatkan puji syukur ke hadirat Allah SWT karena atas rahmatNya sajalah kita dapat berkumpul di sini, berbagi cerita dan pengalaman, dalam acara Halal Bihalal Keluarga Besar Ikatan Sarjana Ekoomi Indonesia (ISEI) tahun 1431 H. Walaupun sudah berjarak beberapa waktu dari hari raya Iedul Fitri 1431 H, namun semangat bersyukur kepada Tuhan memang sudah seharusnya tidak mengenal waktu. Bapak dan Ibu yang saya hormati, Rasa syukur juga patut kita ungkapkan apabila kita menelaah kinerja perekonomian Indonesia akhir-akhir ini. Kita telah sama-sama mengikuti bagaimana gejolak krisis global yang saat ini masih berlangsung telah 1 membuat banyak negara mengalami kontraksi yang cukup dalam. Di tengah kondisi yang tidak menguntungkan tersebut, perekonomian Indonesia pada tahun 2009 lalu masih dapat tumbuh 4.5%. Basis ekonomi kita yang lebih banyak ditopang permintaan domestik, terutama konsumsi, ternyata lebih berdaya tahan terhadap rambatan krisis global tersebut. Indonesia pun disejajarkan dengan China dan India sebagai tiga negara yang masih membukukan pertumbuhan positif sepanjang 2009. Pada tahun 2010 ini Bank Indonesia memperkirakan perekonomian kita akan tumbuh 6.1%, masih merupakan pencapaian yang cukup tinggi dalam skala kawasan. Pada tahun 2011 dan selanjutnya, apabila didukung oleh peningkatan investasi yang memadai, Bank Indonesia memprediksi bahwa ekonomi domestik dapat terus tumbuh di atas 6.0%. Sejalan dengan semakin menguatnya kegiatan ekonomi, laju inflasi menunjukkan kecenderungan meningkat. Namun peningkatan inflasi dalam beberapa bulan terakhir lebih diakibatkan dorongan kelompok bahan makanan. Pemantauan terakhir menunjukkan kita masih memiliki harapan bahwa inflasi akan berada dalam kisaran sasaran 5+1%. Kekuatan ekonomi kita juga didukung oleh kinerja perdagangan yang tetap solid. Neraca pembayaran pada tahun ini diperkirakan akan mencatat surplus sebesar USD 27.4 miliar, sehingga akumulasi cadangan devisa akan terus meningkat. Cadangan devisa kita per 28 Oktober telah mencapai USD 91.1 miliar. Tumbuhnya harapan semakin membaiknya ekonomi juga dapat kita lihat di pasar keuangan. Indeks Harga Saham Gabungan (IHSG) terus meningkat dan telah mencapai 3.640 pada akhir Oktober lalu. Ini merupakan level tertinggi dalam sejarah parsar saham di Indonesia. 2 Bapak dan Ibu yang saya hormati, Di tengah berbagai capaian positif perekonomian kita saat ini, tantangan ke depan tidaklah ringan. Struktur industri menunjukkan dinamika yang harus dicermati. Di satu sisi, pangsa industri berbasis manufaktur tampak semakin mengecil, akibat industri berbasis sumber daya alam yang semakin menonjol. Apabila dibiarkan, persoalan ini dapat mengarah pada deindustrialisasi yang dapat berdampak pada menurunnya nilai tambah industri nasional dan tergerusnya produktivitas perekonomian. Disamping itu, ditengah-tengah persoalan pengangguran dan kemiskinan yang masih dihadapi Indonesia, kehadiran industri padat karya yang luas masih dibutuhkan. Di sisi lain, industri manufaktur domestik kita masih kental dengan muatan impor. Ini membuat pertumbuhan ekonomi yang tinggi akan dibarengi dengan naiknya impor secara cukup signifikan, yang berdampak pada menurunnya surplus pada neraca transaksi berjalan (current account). Apabila struktur industri kita yang bermuatan impor tinggi tersebut tidak berubah, maka terdapat risiko kita akan mengalami defisit. Dalam kondisi defisit, apabila sumber pembiayaan tetap mengandalkan arus modal masuk jangka pendek yang memiliki volatilitas tinggi, seperti yang terjadi sekarang, maka akan menimbulkan kerentanan. Kaitan struktur industri dengan kerentanan neraca pembayaran masih merupakan persoalan yang harus sama-sama kita kaji dan cari solusinya. Dari sisi komposisi, neraca modal dan keuangan (capital and financial account) kita memang masih kurang berimbang. Pada 2009, arus masuk modal ke investasi portofolio kita sebesar USD 10,3 milyar, jauh lebih besar dari investasi langsung jangka panjang (FDI) yang hanya sebesar USD 1.9 milyar. Bank Indonesia memproyeksikan bahwa di tahun 2010, kondisi akan sedikit membaik, dengan investasi portofolio akan mencapai USD 15.5 milyar sementara FDI meningkat menjadi USD 9.4 milyar. Bila dilihat lebih dalam, latar belakang masuknya FDI ke Indonesia ternyata cenderung berorientasi pasar domestik ketimbang untuk ekspor. FDI yang masuk 3 tersebut juga membutuhkan impor tambahan sebagai komplemen modal. Kondisi ini membuat FDI yang meningkat dapat membuat impor meningkat, yang kembali dapat mengarah pada defisit transaksi berjalan dan terganggunya keseimbangan eksternal. Perekonomian kita yang cepat memanas di sisi neraca pembayaran juga ternyata juga diikuti pada sisi internal. Kondisi infrastruktur yang masih belum memadai, dikombinasikan dengan tantangan geografis yang kita miliki, menjadikan kendala yang tampak semakin serius dalam produksi dan distribusi. Kendala di sisi penawaran (supply side constraint) ini telah secara konsisten membuat inflasi kita tetap lebih tinggi dari negara-negara kawasan. Proyeksi terakhir Bank Indonesia menunjukkan inflasi inti sudah kembali merangkak naik, ke arah 4.5% di 2010 dan 5.0% di 2011. Pertumbuhan ekonomi yang tinggi, yang diiiringi dengan potensi peningkatan inflasi yang tinggi, utamanya dipacu dari sisi penawaran, menunjukkan adanya persoalan pada keseimbangan internal. Adanya potensi ketidakseimbangan internal dan ekternal, di balik kisah sukses perekonomian Indonesia selama menghadapi krisis, merupakan tantangan nyata bagi kita semua yang harus segera dijawab. Bapak dan Ibu yang saya hormati, Lingkungan global yang sangat dinamis memang membuat pengelolaan kebijakan ekonomi makro semakin kompleks. Ini karena perekonomian kita tidak dapat menghindar dari dampak perubahan konstelasi kebijakan ekonomi global paska krisis, khususnya kebijakan yang ditempuh negara-negara maju. Bagi beberapa negara maju, krisis global lalu memang cukup berdampak destruktif, dimana sempat terjadi interaksi antar sektor keuangan dan sektor riil tidak berjalan lagi sebagaimana mestinya. Kondisi tersebut terkait dengan lingkaran permasalahan krisis yang berjalan demikian cepat karena bekerjanya suatu mekanisme yang dikenal 4 sebagai financial accelerator, yaitu kondisi dimana sektor keuangan mengamplifikasi apa yang terjadi di sektor riil sehingga berdampak lebih ekstrem. Mekanisme ini tampak telah bekerja pada periode boom yang lalu (awal 2000-an), maupun pada krisis saat ini. Sektor keuangan menjadi pro- cyclical atau menyebabkan amplifikasi terhadap siklus ekonomi. Financial accelerator ini berkerja sebagai berikut. Pada periode boom atau positive shock, kenaikkan harga aset biasanya dibarengi dengan bertambahnya modal bank dan berkurangnya leverage, yang mendorong bank melakukan ekspansi. Kenaikkan harga aset juga memudahkan sektor rumah tangga dan bisnis memperoleh pinjaman dari bank, yang pada gilirannya memacu konsumsi dan investasi. Sebaliknya, pada periode krisis atau negative shock, jatuhnya harga aset menyebabkan modal bank merosot dan leverage bank naik. Karena dalam masa krisis sangat sulit bagi bank meraih modal baru, bank cenderung melikuidasi asset, sehingga membuat harga aset lebih merosot. Dampak terhadap sektor riil dan ekonomi akan terasa lebih berat saat negative shock tersebut menimpa bank-bank besar secara serentak, atau terjadi efek sistemis dari neraca bank yang memburuk. Dengan bekerjanya mekanisme financial accelerator tadi, dalam kondisi krisis, kebijakan moneter yang konvensional menjadi sulit diandalkan efektivitasnya. Di Amerika dan Jepang misalnya, suku bunga yang mendekati nol persen pun belum mampu menstimulasi kegiatan ekonomi. Tidak berjalannya transmisi kebijakan moneter melalui suku bunga pada gilirannya mengharuskan bank sentral melalui berbagai program non-konvensional, diantaranya quantitave easing (QE), yaitu membeli instrumen keuangan secara langsung, dengan menggelontorkan likuiditas ke pasar keuangan. Sebagai contoh pada 3 November kemarin Amerika meluncurkan QE jilid II dimana diputuskan untuk membeli aset sebesar USD 600 milyar. 5 Bapak dan Ibu yang saya hormati, Dalam skala global, kita juga melihat bagaimana pemulihan ekonomi di berbagai negara berjalan dalam multispeed recovery, terutama ditandai dengan semakin melebarnya disparitas pertumbuhan ekonomi antara negara maju dan emerging market. Disparitas juga tampak dari sisi kebijakan, misalnya Amerika yang terus melanjutkan ekspansi sementara India dan Australia pada 2 November lalu menaikkan suku bunga kebijakan. Momentum pemulihan ekonomi di banyak negara maju memang terlihat melemah. Kondisi tersebut tergambar jelas dari masih tingginya tingkat pengangguran, melemahnya kembali konsumsi rumah tangga yang disertai dengan menguatnya ancaman deflasi di Amerika, Eropa, dan Jepang. Di pihak lain, pemulihan ekonomi negara-negara emerging market khususnya di Asia dan Amerika Latin melaju pesat, disertai dengan mulai munculnya tekanan inflasi. Dari uraian tadi, terlihat bahwa dari sisi arus modal memang terdapat push factor, yaitu berlimpahnya likuiditas dan rendahnya suku bunga di negara maju, yang pada saat bersamaan disertai pull factor, yaitu membaiknya fundamental ekonomi, tingginya suku bunga, dan membaiknya persepsi risiko ke emerging market. Kedua faktor tersebut secara bersamaan telah, sedang menyebabkan derasnya aliran modal ke emerging market, termasuk ke Indonesia. Pada saat ini Indonesia memang menjadi magnet tujuan investasi bagi kalangan pengelola modal portofolio internasional. Intensitas arus masuk modal portfolio ke Indonesia dalam tiga bulan terakhir bahkan semakin kuat karena para investor global tersebut mengantisipasi langkah- langkah lanjutan kebijakan moneter di Amerika. Terkait QE jilid II yang baru saja diumumkan, the Fed diperkirakan akan mengaktifkan kembali program pembelian aset dalam skala besar (large-scale asset purchases/LSAP). Program ini dipastikan akan semakin 6 menekan lagi suku bunga jangka panjang di AS, yang pada gilirannya semakin memperderas arus modal ke negara emerging market. Bapak dan Ibu yang saya hormati, Kita sama-sama menyaksikan bagaimana gelombang intervensi di pasar valuta asing, untuk meredam tekanan apresiasi, telah menjadi menu harian kebijakan taktis di sejumlah negara-negara emerging market belakangan ini. Akibat fenomena yang sementara orang menyebut currency-war ini, akumulasi cadangan devisa oleh negara emerging market pun meningkat pesat. Depresiasi dollar juga semakin terakselerasi, disamping oleh langkah QE jilid II, juga oleh langkah sejumlah bank sentral emerging market yang mereposisi akumulasi cadangan devisa mereka ke instrumen keuangan non- dollar, termasuk instrumen negara emerging market lain. Intervensi memang dapat membantu menahan tekanan apresiasi, namun tidak dapat terus menerus dilakukan karena beban ongkos sterilisasi yang cukup besar. Oleh karenanya, banyak negara emerging market mulai memikirkan dengan serius berbagai kebijakan yang termasuk kelas macroprudential. Bahkan sejumlah negara merespon derasnya arus modal masuk dengan capital control, misalnya pemerintah Brazil yang mengenakan pajak terhadap transaksi pihak asing di pasar obligasi. Solusi atas lingkaran permasalahan arus modal global dan pengelolaan kebijakan nilai tukar ini tentunya memerlukan koordinasi multilateral, dan oleh karenanya saat ini terus menjadi tema sentral di berbagai fora internasional, seperti di G-20, ASEAN, IMF, dan BIS. 7 Bapak dan Ibu yang saya hormati, Derasnya arus masuk modal global ke perekonomian kita membawa manfaat, tetapi juga menimbulkan permasalahan yang kompleks. Masuknya modal asing meningkatkan pasokan devisa di pasar keuangan domestik, mendorong penguatan rupiah, dan menurunkan imbal hasil (yield) surat utang negara (SUN). Rupiah yang menguat membantu menekan inflasi melalui turunnya harga barang impor. Sementara itu, dengan turunnya yield SUN juga menurunkan ongkos pembiayaan anggaran pemerintah. Di sisi lain, arus modal masuk saat ini menimbulkan permasalahan karena sebagian besar berjangka pendek, mudah berbalik arah, memicu penggelembungan aset (asset bubble), dan berpotensi menekan nilai rupiah menjauh dari nilai fundamentalnya (overshoothing). Selain itu, derasnya arus modal saat ini dirasa sudah lebih besar dari kemampuan sektor riil dan pasar keuangan kita untuk dapat menyerapnya. Dari segi kedalaman maupun ketersediaan instrumen, pasar keuangan kita tampak belum siap untuk menerima begitu derasnya arus masuk modal jangka pendek. Kurang dalamnya pasar keuangan kita relatif terhadap besarnya modal asing menjadikan sistem keuangan domestik rentan terhadap perubahan mendadak sentimen investor global. Pada Mei lalu kita menyaksikan bagaimana munculnya sentimen negatif berupa memuncaknya kekhawatiran terhadap krisis ekonomi di Yunani telah memicu penarikan dana asing dalam skala besar dan mendadak (large and sudden reversal) dari perekonomian Indonesia yang menimbulkan tekanan kuat terhadap Rupiah. Bapak dan Ibu yang saya hormati, Dalam menyikapi derasnya arus masuk modal sekaligus memitigasi potensi risiko yang dapat ditimbulkan apabila modal tersebut berbalik arah, Bank Indonesia telah menempuh beberapa langkah kebijakan. Dikeluarkannya kebijakan tersebut tidak lain adalah untuk menjaga 8 stabilitas makro dan mempertahankan kesinambungan pertumbuhan perekonomian kita. Sebagai first line of defence, Bank Indonesia tetap mengedepankan pengelolan kebijakan moneter dan perbankan yang pruden yang dijalankan secara konsisten. Ini diharapkan dapat semakin memperkuat kredibilitas kebijakan sehingga turut menciptakan lingkungan yang kondusif bagi investasi untuk segala jenis investasi apapun. Sementara itu dalam tataran operasional, Bank Indonesia telah mengambil langkah-langkah dalam bentuk bauran kebijakan (policy mix), yaitu dengan: 1) Mengakomodasi nilai tukar yang fleksibel yaitu membiarkan Rupiah mengalami apresiasi, namun juga tetap menjaga agar tidak overshooting dan tidak terlalu fluktuatif, yaitu melalui intervensi guna memelihara stabilitas ekonomi makro, stabilitas keuangan, dan kesinambungan neraca transaksi berjalan. 2) Memupuk cadangan devisa, yang sangat diperlukan sebagai upaya untuk memperkuat perisai (sebagai insurance) ketika menghadapi pembalikan modal. 3) Mengambil sejumlah kebijakan macroprudential secara selektif, guna mengelola arus modal yang cenderung fluktuatif. Perlu saya tekankan di sini bahwa walaupun instrumen kebijakan konvensional seperti intervensi di pasar valuta asing sejauh ini cukup efektif, kita tetap menghadapi kompleksitas dalam pengelolaan kebijakan moneter. Ekspansi likuiditas sebagai dampak langsung intervensi di pasar valuta asing perlu diserap kembali melalui operasi moneter agar tidak memicu inflasi; ini menyebabkan outstanding SBI terus meningkat. Oleh karena itu, menyadari semakin kompleknya permasalahan yang akan dihadapi ke depan, Bank Indonesia juga menempuh langkah non- konvensional dalam bentuk kebijakan macroprudential. Pada 16 Juni lalu, 9 telah dikeluarkan ketentuan kewajiban bagi pembeli SBI untuk menahan kepemilikannya selama satu bulan baik di pasar primer maupun sekunder, yang berlaku baik bagi pelaku domestik maupun asing. Kebijakan tersebut cukup efektif dalam mencegah terjadinya pembalikan modal dalam skala besar dan mendadak, karena investor tidak dapat lagi mencairkan SBI setiap saat. Kita menyaksikan akhir-akhir ini nilai tukar rupiah dapat terjaga dengan stabil. Bank Indonesia juga melengkapi instrumen pengelolaan likuiditas dengan memperkenalkan Term Deposit (TD) Rupiah yang tidak dapat diperdagangkan (non-transfarable). Ini akan semakin mempersempit peluang pihak asing dalam mengakumulasi SBI. Bapak dan Ibu yang saya hormati, Banyak kita mendengar pandangan perlunya bagi kita mengambil kebijakan capital control. Namun, saya melihat sejauh ini beberapa langkah kebijakan yang telah kita ambil telah cukup efektif. Meski demikian, tentu saja ruang untuk opsi-opsi kebijakan tambahan lainnya tetap terbuka. Dalam tataran diskusi internasional, kebijakan capital control tidak lagi diharamkan apabila seluruh opsi kebijakan makro konvensional yang tersedia dirasa tidak lagi memadai untuk memitigasi dampak buruk dari lalu lintas modal yang ekstrem. Capital control memiliki alasan kuat untuk menjadi bagian dari perangkat kebijakan dalam mengelola arus masuk modal apabila tekanan inflasi meningkat, apabila kecukupan cadangan devisa sudah lebih dari optimal, apabila nilai mata uang domestik overvalued, dan apabila arus modal yang masuk mayoritas bersifat sementara (transitory). Melihat kondisi sekarang, memang semakin banyak otoritas di sejumlah negara emerging market yang mulai mempertimbangkan untuk menrancang dan menerapkan kebijakan capital control namun secara specifik dan tepat sasaran (targeted). Agar kebijakan capital control 10 tersebut efektif maka sangat penting untuk dapat menbedakan antara sumber dan jenis aliran modal, mempertimbangkan secara hati-hati pilihan instrumen yang akan digunakan, memperkuat komunikasi dan kapasitas institusional, serta merancang mekanisme entry/exit dan penyesuaian terhadap instrumen yang telah ditetapkan. Secara umum, instrumen capital control yang memerlukan perubahan minimal dari sistem yang sudah tersedia akan lebih mudah disesuaikan, dikomunikasikan, dan diimplementasikan. Namun, instrumen capital control yang memerlukan perubahan mendasar dari sistem yang sudah ada dapat menimbulkan dampak psikologis yang lebih besar dan mungkin risiko gagal. Singkatnya, capital control dapat saya ibaratkan sebagai pedang bermata dua yang sebaiknya disimpan sampai kondisi darurat sekali terjadi. Bapak dan Ibu yang saya hormati, Sebelum saya akhiri sambutan saya, ada satu isu kebijakan lain yang baiknya kita kaji secara serius dan segera, dalam menyikapi derasnya arus modal masuk ini, yaitu bagaimana kita bisa meraup manfaat sebesar- sebesarnya dari arus modal masuk tersebut guna mendorong pertumbuhan ekonomi yang berkelanjutan. Dengan kata lain, persoalan fundamental yang perlu kita jawab bersama adalah bagaimana kita mampu memanfaatkan aliran modal ini ke jangka waktu yang lebih panjang. Terdapat sejumlah langkah yang dapat kita tempuh. Pertama, kita seyogyanya mampu mendorong pemanfaatan aliran modal tersebut untuk pembiayaan bagi perusahaan dan pendalaman pasar keuangan domestik. Kemudahan-kemudahan dan stimulus di pasar modal dapat diberikan baik untuk mendorong penerbitan saham (initial/secondary public offering) maupun obligasi (bond issuance) bagi korporasi. Bahkan besarnya minat investasi dari luar negeri tersebut juga dapat dimanfaatkan untuk mendukung upaya-upaya untuk penerbitan saham dan obligasi perusahaan- perusahaan BUMN kita. 11 Kedua, yang juga sangat penting dan mendesak, kita sebaiknya mampu mendorong perbaikan iklim investasi dan pembangunan infrastruktur dengan memanfaatkan peluang dari besarnya minat investasi asing tersebut. Diskusi tentang hal ini sudah sama-sama kita ikuti dan berbagai rekomendasi kebijakan juga sudah disampaikan dan dirumuskan. Kini tinggal bagaimana kita secara kokoh dan konsisten mengimplementasikannya. Mendorong investasi sangatlah penting untuk meningkatkan kapasitas perekonomian. Memacu pertumbuhan ekonomi tanpa diimbangi dengan peningkatan kapasitas produksi hanya akan menghasilkan tekanan inflasi yang utamanya muncul akibat keterbatasan sisi penawaran. Ke depan, Insya Allah, dengan fundamental ekonomi kita yang semakin baik, minat asing untuk berinvestasi di Indonesia akan sangat besar. Apalagi, Indonesia memiliki peluang untuk memasuki peringkat investment grade tahun depan. Bapak dan Ibu yang saya hormati, Demikian pokok-pokok pemikiran dalam menyikapi besarnya arus modal masuk dari luar negeri dewasa ini. Kita harus mampu memanfaatkan aliran modal tersebut untuk kepentingan pembangunan ekonomi berkelanjutan. Intinya kita memang harus mampu menjaga stabilitas ekonomi makro ditengah keterbukaan ekonomi kita. Ketiadaan kesalahan kebijakan makro tidak menjamin kita tetap aman dari dampak gejolak luar. Akhir kata, semoga Allah Yang Maha Pengasih dan Penyayang me- ridhoi kegiatan kita hari ini dan senantiasa melimpahkan bimbingan, petunjuk, dan rahmat-Nya kepada kita sekalian. Terima kasih. Wassalamu 'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh. Dr. Darmin Nasution 12

Title: Penjelasan Dewan Gubernur Bank Indonesia Pada Rapat Kerja Dengan Komisi IX DPR RI Tanggal 26 Juni 2001
text: EXPLANATION OF THE BOARD OF GOVERNORS OF BANK INDONESIA AT THE WORKING MEETING WITH COMMISSION IX OF THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES ON JUNE 26, 2001 Conference Time: IV Year of Session: 2000 - 2001 Dear Members of the Council, First of all, let me thank the Chairman of Commission IX and the esteemed Members of the Board, who have invited us to attend the Working Meeting today. For us, this Working Meeting has a very important meaning because it is a form of our accountability to the public through this House Session. In addition, this Working Meeting is very useful, especially to convey information on the extent of the implementation of Bank Indonesia's duties as mandated by law, as well as to obtain input for us to continue to strive for improvements in the implementation of future tasks. Secondly, as was the case at the last Working Meetings, before we present answers to the questions of the esteemed members of the Board, let us briefly present the latest developments on the policy measures taken by Bank Indonesia. Dear Board Member, As of May 2001, in general, monetary economic conditions showed that they were likely to have not shown any significant improvement, especially when compared to the original forecast at the beginning of 2001. The optimistic mood for the economic outlook turned into concerns of rising various risk factors and uncertainties. Economic growth is expected to be lower than originally expected, while inflationary and exchange rate pressures increase. The progress of the banking and business sector restructuring process, which is expected to further increase economic activity in 2001, has not been as fast as expected. Investor confidence in the prospect of economic recovery has also deteriorated as a result of political- domestic security conditions and relations with the IMF. Meanwhile, the global economy, especially the US, is also likely to deteriorate even though it is expected to be short-term. In general, the Board of Governors considers that until May 2001, the intensity of pressure on price increases in general has strengthened. Monthly inflation (m-t-m) in May 2001 reached 1.13%, higher than april inflation of 0.46%. With this monthly inflation rate, the cumulative inflation rate (y-t-d) reached 3.73%, while the annual inflation (y-o-y) reached 10.82%. All groups of goods and services in the CPI basket experienced an increase in prices, where the group 1 clothing recorded the highest inflation followed by the foodstuffs group and the health group. Exchange rate depreciation coupled with government policies in the field of prices and income has increased inflation expectations, both on the consumer and producer sides, thereby encouraging an increase in prices in general. Meanwhile, developments throughout May 2001 indicate that the rupiah exchange rate is still facing depreciation pressures. The warming political temperature accompanied by violence and riots gave rise to negative sentiments which resulted in heavy pressure on the rupiah. On the other hand, the political agenda leading to the Special Session of the MPR began to cause optimism among market participants. The rupiah, which has been weakening since the beginning of the month, has strengthened in the last week so that it closed on June 25, 2001 at a level of Rpl 1,350 per US dollar. The weakening of the exchange rate and the increasing inflation rate have prompted Bank Indonesia to implement a tight monetary policy. As a result, the SBI interest rate increases and is followed by the deposit rate. As an illustration, the 1-month SBI rate increased by 24 bps to reach 16.33% at the last auction in May 2001. Meanwhile, the interest rate on other opt instruments, namely rupiah intervention, was raised by 50 bps. However, the increase in the interest rate of the instrument that serves as a floor in the money market was only carried out towards the end of the month, so the impact on the increase in interest rates in the money market will be more widely seen in June. Meanwhile, the 3-month SBI rate increased gradually by around 100bps from 14.79 in January 2001 to 15.79 in June 2001. Thus the average interest rate of the 3-month SBI in the first 6 months of 2001 was about 15.3%. Going forward, with high inflationary pressures and weakening of the exchange rate, interest rates are expected to continue to rise, then decline again in line with improving inflation expectations and exchange rates, so that the average 3-month SBI interest rate in 2001 will be around 14-16%. However, the increase in the SBI interest rate has not been followed by a commensurate increase in the deposit rate. In real terms, the interest rate on banking deposits is currently at around 3%. This figure is still much lower than the real interest rate in the pre-crisis period, which was about 10-11% in the first quarter of 1997, and also not very high compared to neighboring countries. Based on the results of a survey conducted by Bank Indonesia, demand conditions show a weakening trend in line with the trend of real GDP growth in the 1st quarter of 2001. GDP growth in Q1-2001 reached only 4.01% (y-o-y), which is down compared to the growth in the fourth quarter of 2000 of 5.23%, and even lower than the growth in quarter 1-2000 of 4.24%. Meanwhile, a low real exchange rate does not guarantee a significant improvement in boosting Indonesia's overall exports. Non-oil and gas exports only recorded an annual growth of 0.67% in the January-April 2001 period. In contrast, non-oil and gas imports increased high in the period with annual growth reaching 49.29%. The increase in non-oil and gas imports primarily occurred in the imports of raw material groups. In general, the performance of The Indonesian banking industry in April 2001 showed several improvements, such as increasing lending, increasing funds. Third Parties (DPK) and capital. On the other hand, non-performing loans (NPLs) increased by 0.4% to 18.5% mainly due to the increase in NPLs of foreign exchange loans, while net interest margin (NIM) remained relatively positive at Rp3 trillion. In unstable social and security conditions, banks have begun to increase lending. This is certainly quite a relief for all of us. To speed up the process of restoring the bank's intermediation function, credit restructuring and company restructuring need to be further improved. Considering the developments that have occurred, especially in the development of the inflation rate, exchange rate, and economic activities, the Board of Governors believes that in the coming months there is still a possibility of an increase in the inflation rate both from the depreciation of the rupiah and from policies to increase the prices of administered goods (administered prices). and other factors. For this reason, the Board of Governors considers the need to take disciplined and consistent measures to maintain the money supply, especially the base money as needed. The achievement of the base money target will mainly be carried out through the absorption of liquidity in Open Market Operations (OPT). In addition, Bank Indonesia will also continue to intervene in the foreign exchange market where it is deemed necessary, in a measured manner as needed. Dear Members of the Council, In particular, we would like to thank you for the questions that have been submitted in writing by the honourable Members of the Board to Bank Indonesia. These questions have covered several aspects of the implementation of Bank Indonesia's duties and authorities, ranging from bank regulation and supervision, BLBI issues, predictions of monetary policy programs, and procurement of banknotes. The discussion in this Working Meeting is expected to provide a comprehensive overview of these various aspects and their implications for developments and policies adopted in the future. Next, let us provide an explanation of the written questions that the Councillor has previously presented to us. Question : 1. In order to anticipate the CAR provisions targeted at the end of 2001 of 8%, how can the target be achieved or there are other things that will affect the target in relation to macroeconomic circumstances that have not recovered before. To explain in detail the regulatory and supervisory programs of Bank Indonesia in order to increase the role of national banks in 2001. Answer : Dear Members of the Council, To answer the question of the anticipation of the CAR provision of 8% at the end of 2001, we can say that economic conditions that have not been conducive to economic recovery, especiallya industry banks caused several banks to experience obstacles in meeting various business and prudential targets, including the fulfillment of 8% CAR by the end of 2001. In order to anticipate this problem, several approaches have been taken to these banks, including exploring the possibility of increasing capital. Based on the results of the last stress test conducted by Bank Indonesia, there are 9 banks that are expected to be difficult to achieve a CAR of 8% by the end of 2001. This number decreased when compared to the results of the stress test in the previous period which produced 12 banks. Of the 9 banks, 5 of them are banks that are currently in the process of restructuring at IBRA, while for the other 4 banks, Bank Indonesia will ask its shareholders to make a capital deposit, find a new investor, or explore the possibility of a merger. In order to increase banking resilience and achieve a healthy banking system by the end of 2002, Bank Indonesia has and will continue to make various efforts related to the improvement of licensing provisions , improvement of banking arrangements based on the principle of prudence, as well as improvement of procedures for restructuring and settling problem banks (exit policy). Improvements to the licensing provisions that have been carried out include interviews with prospective controlling shareholders, requirements for submitting a corporate plan, risk management guidelines, system plans internal control, information technology system plan, as well as the entire business group structure. The improvement of banking regulations (prudential regulations) will include : - improvement of capital adequacy provisions that include other elements of risk other than credit risk, as well as improvement of the calculation of risk-weighted assets (ATMR) - increase transparency to the public through publication reporting, which includes several financial performance indicators - mewajibkan bank implement risk management in controlling the risks faced, as well as implementing an internal control system - implementing risk-based banking supervision on a consolidated basis, including consolidated reporting of bank charges with affiliated companies - prevention of money laundering practices carried out through banks by issuing regulations relating to the obligation of banks to apply the principles of customer recognition (know your customer principles) In relation to the procedures for restructuring and settling non-performing banks, Bank Indonesia will make improvements, especially regarding the criteria and procedures for determining banks in special supervision, banks in restructuring at IBRA, as well as frozen business banks (BBKU). Question : 2. In the report on the Results of the BPK Investigation Audit regarding BLBI, it was found that there was an additional BLBI of Rp14.5 trillion which occurred after January 29 , 1999. How is the clarification of the BLBI tammaterial between Bank Indonesia and the Ministry of Finance and when it will be resolved because it affects the 2002 State Budget. Please explain in detail. Answer : Dear Members of the Council, Fulfilling the answers to the questions of Commission IX of the DPR-RI mentioned above, we can state the following: 1. Additional BLBI of Rp.14,447.7 billion was given to: a. Bank Frozen Operations (BBO) amounting to Rp.0.5 billion b. Bank Frozen Operating Activities (BBKU) amounted to Rp.14,447.2 billion. 2. The additional BLBI arising in the period after January 29, 1999 until the banks were frozen on March 13, 1999 with the following details: a. The debit balance amounted to Rp. 13,899.6 billion (30 BBKU and 1 BBO). b. Special Money Market Securities (SBPUK) amounting to Rp. 106.7 billion (1 BBKU) c. Discount Facility of Rp.441.4 billion (1 BBKU), details in appendix 1. 3. The additional amount of the BLBI: a. Included in Government Bond (SUP) No.4 amounting to Rp. 53.7 trillion were provided for payments in the framework of additional BLBI after January 1999. In order to avoid an unequal understanding, we may suggest that as detailed in the letter of the Minister of Finance referred to from the outset of the expenditure of SUP No.4, it has been realized that the amount of amounting to Rp.53.7 trillion is intended for the purposes of: 1) The provision of down payment to IBRA for guarantee payments in accordance with Presidential Decree No.26 of 1998 amounted to Rp.35.3 trillion. 2) Completion of other guarantees (Presidential Decrees No. 120 and 193 of 1998, trade finance - exchange offer) worth Rp.4.0 trillion. 3) Additional blbi payments after January 1999 amounted to Rp. 14.447 trillion. Thus, since the beginning, it has been realized that the amount of Rp. 14.447 trillion is not a free fund. SUP No.4 referred to and the letter of the Minister of Finance No.SR- 176 / MK.01 / 1999 dated May 31, 1999 is as in appendix 2. b. In accordance with the Joint Agreement between the Governor of Bank Indonesia and the Minister of Finance on 6 February 1999, article 2 is explained as follows (appendix 3): 1) . The right to charge the first party (Governor of Bank Indonesia) against Commercial Banks the recipient of the BLBI who is taken over by the second party (the Minister of Finance) and who is paid to the first party as contemplated in Article 1 is the type of BLBI in accordance with the applicable provisions. 2) . Acceptance of the BLBI takeover as referred to in paragraph 1) is only carried out by the second party for the BLBI whose distribution has been recorded in the books of the first party and has been billed by the first party to the second party in accordance with applicable regulations. 3) . Upon the takeover of the right to charge as referred to in paragraph 1) verification will be carried out as agreed by both parties. c. It has been reported by the CPC-RI in the audit (lampiran 4): 1) Initial Balance Sheet Report of Bank Indonesia as of May 17, 1999 in Sub Post 2.a.2.) Bills on special government agencies. 2) Annual Financial Statements as of December 31 , 1999 in SUP No.4. 3) Interim Financial Statements as of June 30, 2000 and Annual Financial Statements per December 31, 2000 in SUP No.4. 4.
