Distinguished Guest, Ladies and Gentlemen Nevertheless, on our view there are some key elements that have been absent of market consideration. First, crisis is not isolated to our economy only. It is a worldwide phenomenon. Second, amidst such inauspicious surroundings, Indonesia is certainly not in the worst position compared to other countries. In general, our macro posture is not bad. Our banking industry also remains robust in the midst of heavy pressures. 2 On our view, economic slowdown will be more obvious in 2009, particularly during the first semester. Amidst of the crisis, our economy would still able to grow around 4%. However, the downside risk is still high. Along with the declining domestic demand and the fall of commodity prices, inflation pressures would be milder around the range of 5%-7%. The restrained domestic demand would also slash demand for imports that help to rebalance the BoP, mainly in the second semester. We project, the current account deficit to be below 1% of GDP. Regarding the capital account, there are worries concerning the burden of private sector foreign debt matured in 2009. I would like to confirm that the burden is within our reach. The outstanding of debt mature in 2009 is US17.4 billion. However, our consolidated data shows that the debt is dominantly consist of trade financing and revolving type of foreign loan agreement, that embed relatively low default risk. Some of non-revolving debt are also affiliated and connected to parent companies that are expected to have more opportunity to be rolled-over. Concerning our international reserve adequacy, currently Bank Indonesia and the Government are working hand in hand to negotiate a financial arrangement both bilateral and multilateral, such as under Bilateral Swap Arrangement (BSA) and under Chiang-May Initiatives. We are sure that these features will support the stability of rupiah exchange rate in the near future. In the banking sector, the resilience of our domestic banking industry is sufficient. Though decreasing, the capital adequacy ratio (CAR) is projected well above its minimum limit. Slow economic growth will precipitate a rise in NPL in 2009. However, we are sure that the level would still consider within safe boundaries. Considering the recent speculation concerning the settlement of structured products involving a number of banks, let be briefly assure you that the risk of potential loss due to unwinding process, both for customer and for banks, is low. Our data shows that the notional amount of outstanding structured product has been drop significantly from around US3.5 billion in Dec-2008 to US2.6 billion in Jan-2009 and the actual potential lost should be lower. Bank Indonesias new regulations that restrict banks from such practices have been proven effective. Further potential lost has also been limited, as the new regulation is also put provision of contract restructuring and our mediation effort has also been effective in resolving a number of cases. 3 Distinguished Guest, Ladies and Gentlemen It is impossible to know how protracted or severe the crisis would be. Nevertheless, what we do know is that economic downturns dont last forever. So despite the gloomy circumstances, its important to ask the question: what are the factors that can contribute to an upturn in due course? So let me counterbalance with factors that, over time, can be expected to contribute to an upturn. A great deal depends on the success of the policy responses. Countries experiences have shown that a structural financial crisis such as is occurring now will have lasting impacts on the real sector. Sluggish economic growth will continue for several periods despite liquidity returning to normal. It suggests that a sustained economic recovery will not be possible until the financial sectors functionality is restored and credit markets are unclogged. Market liquidity is at the heart of central banks financial stability concerns because it is a precondition for market efficiency and also because its sudden disappearance from markets may degenerate into systemic crisis, as evidenced by the recent turbulence, which resulted in the abrupt drying up of liquidity on the bond markets. Furthermore, fiscal stimuli have to be introduced concomitantly with financial sector strengthening. They will not catalyze sustainable economic growth if not bolster by a reawakening of private and business sector activities. Furthermore, the private sector will only be roused if supported by a fully functioning financial sector. As such, measures to repair and reinforce our financial sector must be taken along with the introduction of fiscal stimuli. Fiscal stimuli are a key step in preventing the further deterioration of economic activities in the short term. Within its authority but constrained by capacity limits, Bank Indonesia will take any and all measures required. In our great nation, banks remain a reliable source of financing for the business sector, and thus, tidying up and strengthening our banking sector must remain a priority for continuous implementation. Distinguished Guest, Ladies and Gentlemen On the back of this reasoning, substantial set of expansionary measures have been taken through conventional monetary and fiscal policies. Bank Indonesia has 4 responded forcefully to the negative impact of the crisis. Bank Indonesia began to ease monetary policy since December 2008 by reducing the BI Rate. The reduction has been reached a cumulative of 125 basis points by the February 2008 at 8.25%. However, as I mentioned earlier, a widening credit spreads, segmentation in banking industry, more-restrictive lending standards, and credit market dysfunction have worked against the monetary easing and led to tighter financial conditions overall. Thus, in addition to easing monetary policy, Bank Indonesia has made use of a range of additional tools to ease credit conditions and support the broader economy. These are closely tied to the central bank's traditional role of provider of shortterm liquidity to sound financial institutions. Over the course of the crisis, Bank Indonesia has taken a number of extraordinary actions to ensure that financial institutions have adequate access to short-term credit. In fulfilling its traditional lending function, Bank Indonesia enhances the stability of our financial system, increases the willingness of financial institutions to extend credit, and helps to ease conditions in interbank lending markets, thereby reducing the overall cost of capital to banks. Distinguished Guest, Ladies and Gentlemen Extraordinary times call for extraordinary measures. Responding to the very difficult economic and financial challenges we face, Bank Indonesia has gone beyond traditional monetary policy making to develop new policy tools to address the dysfunctions in the nation's credit markets. Once global credit flows have returned to normal, fund flows to developing countries will gradually return to normal too. We have to assure ourselves that we can be among the first to benefit from the global financial awakening. In my view, the key lies in positioning Indonesia to be considered as a safe and convenient place to conduct business and investment. We have to affirm investors that our macro economy is properly managed and sustainable, and that our financial sector is robust. This is our joint responsibility. Thank you very much for your kind attention. May you have a fruitful discussion. Billahi taufiq wal hidayah wassalamu alaikum wa Rahmatullah wa Barakatuh. Jakarta, 26 February 2008 5

Title: Pidato Deputi Gubernur BI, Erwin Rijanto pada Seminar Pengawasan Bank Indonesia di Bidang Makroprudensial, Moneter dan Sistem Pembayaran di Kantor Bank Indonesia Provinsi NTT, Kamis 24 Agustus 2017
text: Closing Remarks "Bank Indonesia Supervision Seminar in the Macroprudential , Monetary and Development System Fields" Dear: a6 Mr. M. Edhie Purnawan, Member of the Supervision Board of Bank Indonesia, a6 Member of Muspida of East Nusa Tenggara Province, a6 Mr. Fredrik Lukas Benu, Rector of Nusa Cendana University, a6 Leaders and Officials at Bank Indonesia, a6 Leaders and Officials at the OJK East Nusa Tenggara Regional Office, a6 Head of Banking in NTT Province and Academics, a6 The Seminar Participants and Ladies and Gentlemen were happy. Assalamu'alaikum Warahmahtullah Wabarakatuh, Good Afternoon and Peace be upon us all 1. On this happy occasion, we should be grateful to the presence of Allah SWT, God Almighty, because for His mercy and grace, we were able to complete the seminar "Supervision of Bank Indonesia in the Macroprudential, Monetary and Payment System Fields". 2. We believe that there has been a lot gained in the implementation of this seminar even though the implementation was relatively short. The diversity of viewpoints obtained from many speakers during the seminar certainly complements Bank Indonesia in carrying out its duties in the future. 3. In accordance with Law No.23 of 1999 concerning Bank Indonesia, it is stated that Bank Indonesia has the main objective of achieving and maintaining rupiah stability. For this purpose, Bank Indonesia is equipped with the pillar of authority to determine and implement monetary policy, the pillar of payment system regulation, and the macroprudential pillar to promote financial system stability. Happy audience Supervision at the National and Regional Levels 4. Today's seminar has explored various aspects of macroprudential, monetary and payment system supervision implemented by Bank Indonesia in accordance with the authority granted by the Law. As stated in the discussion, the authority referred to is not limited to national-scale policy supervision, but also policies whose implementation needs to be monitored at the regional level. 5. To that end, Bank Indonesia is present in all regions of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia through its representative offices, one of which aims to supervise and ensure the effectiveness of Bank Indonesia's policies. carried out in order to achieve regional welfare. 6. The presence of Bank Indonesia in East Nusa Tenggara is also inseparable from the intended purpose. Through the strategic advisory function, regional financial surveying and payment system supervision as well as money circulation, the Bank Indonesia East Nusa Tenggara Representative Office will strive to oversee the achievement of controlled inflation in the range of 3%, a stable financial system with credit growth above 12% and NPLs below 5% and contribute to the regional economic growth prospects of 5.1 - 5.5% during 2017. 7. To achieve bank Indonesia's policy objectives nationally. Bank Indonesia needs to ensure policy implementation not only at the national level but also at the regional level. Rupiah Use Policy and foreign exchange transaction policy are some examples of Bank Indonesia policies that have an impact directly on the regional economy that needs to be supervised its implementation. Of course, the implementation of this supervision requires support and cooperation from the Regional Government and the community as parties who are in direct contact with the implementation of the policy. Seminar participants we are proud of Key Point Seminar Material 8. Taking into account the ongoing discussions and the thoughts that originated from all participants, let me take a few important aspects that were produced in today's semin ar. 9. First, the formulation of macroprudential, monetary and payment system sector policies is based on the Law which is the highest mandate on legal construction in Indonesia. To that end, Bank Indonesia is obliged to achieve the objectives formulated by the Law through strategic policy implementation measures, including the implementation of supervision of the policies issued. 10. The second aspect that needs to be considered is the measurement of the effectiveness of policies issued by Bank Indonesia harus implemented properly so that the policy is felt to be beneficial to the community. Evaluation of the effectiveness of the policy in question, one of which can be obtained through supervisory activities carried out by Bank Indonesia. For example, the penerapan of the Loan To Value ratio policy needs to be supervised in its operationalization, so that the purpose of controlling excessive property credit growth {excessive} can be achieved. 11. The next aspect of Bank Indonesia supervision is the active role of the public in implementing Bank Indonesia's policies. An example is the increase in usage Rupiah currency throughout the territory of the Republic of Indonesia is not only the result of Bank Indonesia's encouragement through the Rupiah Currency Use (PUR) policy, but also because of the increasing public awareness to love more Rupiah as a symbol of state sovereignty that must be respected and proud of by all Negara Indonesians. 12. This awareness raising is key in achieving the effectiveness of Bank Indonesia's policies and supervision considering that Indonesia is a country with more than 17,000 islands, stretching from Sabang to Merauke in the expanse of the h ampir area of 2000 million km2 and with a population of more than 260 million people, so the operationalization of supervision will incur very high costs if is not accompanied by public awareness support. 13. Furthermore, aspects of cooperation between authorities also play an important role in the supervision of Bank Indonesia. Bank Indonesia's cooperation with the Financial Services Authority (OJK), the Ministry of Finance, and the Deposit Insurance Corporation formalized in Law No. 9 of 2016 concerning Crisis Prevention and Handling Financial System (PPKSK), strengthens coordination for the four authorities to provide mutual support in order to prevent and deal with financial system crises. In particular, Bank Indonesia and OJK consistently continue to build strong and solid coordination so as to create a culture of healthy and complementary supervision. 14. Meanwhile, at the regional level, Bank Indonesia's cooperation with local governments and other relevant agencies strengthens Bank Indonesia's ability to carry out its duties. I would like to express my deepest appreciation to the Ntt Regional Government and all relevant agencies, who have worked hand in hand to support the implementation of Bank Indonesia's duties, among others through the Team Monitoring and Controlling Regional Inflation (TPID) as well as MSME clustering programs. This good coordination can be seen in the inflation rate of NTT as of July 2017 which is quite sufficient well maintained at 2.61% {year on yea?), or below national inflation of 3.88% {year on yea?). Hopefully, this good coordination and cooperation can be maintained and further improved in the future. 15. Another important aspect that is key in Bank Indonesia's role as a supervisor in the macroprudential, monetary and payment system sectors is Bank Indonesia's readiness to control the economy in conditions. a pa also, both at a time when the economy is experiencing growth and at a time when the economy is in a state of slowdown. Bank Indonesia as a lender of the last resort is the last defense for the condition of banking liquidity to maintain the financial system. To that end. Bank Indonesia will continuously strive to improve its capabilities to become a credible and better central bank in the region. Ladies and gentlemen of the happy audience, Recoverers 16. Currently, Indonesia's opportunity to maintain economic growth momentum is increasingly open with the improvement of Indonesia's investment rating into an investment grade category by institutions inter-national as well as the existence of national infrastructure development that is running quickly and evenly throughout Indonesia. 17. In this context, Bank Indonesia needs to increase its role in supporting Indonesia's economic progress through various policies in the macroprudential, monetary and payment system fields, which of course needs to be supported by strong and quality supervision so that bankIndonesia's goal of achieving and maintaining rupiah stability can be achieved. 18. For this reason, the public needs to understand that Bank Indonesia supervision is not aimed at limiting the space for economic actors to move, but to provide direction for eco-nomi actors so that growth. the economy is running on the right corridor. 19. I believe that this understanding has been initiated through seminars that have been carried out well today and subsequently to be disseminated by the participants in the scope of the broader, so that the understanding received will have a positive impact on the Indonesian economy and especially this beloved 'BumiI Flobamora'. 20. To end this speech, I would like to express my gratitude to the organizers of this seminar and the greatest appreciation to all the speakers and participants who have been pleased taking time in the midst of busyness to share his knowledge, thoughts, information and experiences during this seminar. 21. Finally , may God Almighty be meridhoi and always bestow His guidance and mercy on all of us, towards a better future. That's it and thank you. Wa billahi taufiq Wai Hidayah. Wasalamu'alaikum Warahmatullahi wabarakatuh Erwin Rijanto Deputy Governor I Flores, Sumba, Timor, Alor --------------- ------------------------------------------------------------
text_original: Closing Remarks "Seminar Pengawasan Bank Indonesia di Bidang Makroprudensial, Moneter dan Sistem Pemba ya ran" Yang terhormat: <a6> Bp. M. Edhie Purnawan, Anggota Badan Supervisi Bank Indonesia, <a6> Anggota Muspida Provinsi Nusa Tenggara Timur, <a6> Bp. Fredrik Lukas Benu, Rektor Universitas Nusa Cendana, <a6> Pimpinan dan Pejabat di Bank Indonesia, <a6> Pimpinan dan Pejabat di Kantor Regional OJK Nusa Tenggara Timur, <a6> Pimpinan Perbankan di Provinsi NTT dan Para Akademisi, <a6> Para Peserta Seminar dan Hadirin sekalian yang berbahagia. Assalamu'alaikum Warahmahtullah Wabarakatuh, Selamat Sore dan Salam Sejahtera untuk kita semua 1. Dalam kesempatan yang berbahagia ini, kita patut bersyukur ke hadirat Allah SWT, Tuhan Yang Maha Kuasa, karena atas rahmat dan anugerah-Nya, kita dapat menyelesaikan seminar "Pengawasan Bank Indonesia di Bidang Makroprudensial, Moneter dan Sistem Pembayaran". 2. Kami meyakini bahwa telah banyakyang diperoleh dalam pelaksanaan seminar kali ini meski pelaksanaannya relatif singkat. Keragaman sudut pandang yang diperoleh dari banyak narasumber selama seminar berlangsung tentu semakin melengkapi Bank Indonesia dalam melaksanakan tugasnya kedepan. 3. Sesuai dengan Undang-Undang No.23 tahun 1999 tentang Bank Indonesia, disebutkan bahwa Bank Indonesia memiliki tujuan utama yaitu mencapai dan memelihara kestabilan nilai Rupiah. Untuk tujuan dimaksud Bank Indonesia dilengkapi dengan pilar kewenangan untuk menetapkan dan melaksanakan kebijakan moneter, pilar pengaturan sistem pembayaran, serta pilar makroprudensial untuk mendorong terjaganya stabilitas sistem keuangan. Hadirin yang berbahagia < Pengawasan di Tingkat Nasional dan Daerah> 4. Seminar hari ini telah mengupas berbagai aspek mengenai pengawasan makroprudensial, moneter dan sistem pembayaran yang dilaksanakan Bank Indonesia sesuai dengan kewenangan yang diberikan Undang-Undang. Sebagaimana diungkapkan pada diskusi sebelumnya, kewenangan dimaksud tidak terbatas kepada pengawasan kebijakan yang berskala nasional, tetapi juga kebijakan yang pelaksanaannya perlu dipantau di tingkat regional. 5. Untuk itu, Bank Indonesia hadir di seluruh wilayah Negara Kesatuan Republik Indonesia melalui kantor perwakilannya, yang salah satunya bertujuan untuk melakukan pengawasan dan memastikan efektivitas kebijakan Bank Indonesia terlaksana demi mencapai kesejahteraan daerah. 6. Kehadiran Bank Indonesia di Nusa Tenggara Timur juga tidak terlepas dari tujuan dimaksud. Melalui fungsi strategic advisory, regional financial surveiiance dan pengawasan sistem pembayaran serta pengedaran uang, Kantor Perwakilan Bank Indonesia Nusa Tenggara Timur akan berupaya untuk mengawal pencapaian inflasi yang terkendali di kisaran 3%, sistem keuangan yang stabil dengan pertumbuhan kredit di atas 12% dan NPL di bawah 5% serta turut mendorong prospek pertumbuhan ekonomi regional sebesar 5,1 - 5,5% selama tahun 2017. 7. Untuk mencapai tujuan kebijakan Bank Indonesia secara nasional. Bank Indonesia perlu memastikan pelaksanaan kebijakan bukan hanya pada level nasional tetapi juga pada level regional. Kebijakan Penggunaan Rupiah dan kebijakan transaksi valuta asing adalah beberapa contoh kebijakan Bank Indonesia yang berdampak langsung pada perekonomian daerah yang perlu diawasi pelaksanaannya. Tentunya, pelaksanaan pengawasan tersebut membutuhkan dukungan dan kerjasama dari Pemerintah Daerah dan masyarakat selaku pihak yang bersentuhan langsung dengan penerapan kebijakan dimaksud. Peserta seminar yang kami banggakan < Key Point Materi Seminar> 8. Dengan memperhatikan diskusi yang berjalan serta pemikiran yang bersumber dari seluruh peserta, perkenankan saya mengambil beberapa aspek penting yang dihasilkan pada seminar hari ini. 9. Pertama, penyusunan kebijakan sektor makroprudensial, moneter dan sistem pembayaran dilandaskan Undang- Undang yang merupakan amanat tertinggi pada konstruksi hukum di Indonesia. Untuk itu, Bank Indonesia wajib mencapai tujuan yang dirumuskan oleh Undang-Undang melalui langkah-langkah strategis pelaksanaan kebijakan termasuk pelaksanaan pengawasan dari kebijakan yang dikeluarkan. 10. Aspek kedua yang perlu diperhatikan adalah pengukuran efektivitas kebijakan yang dikeluarkan oleh Bank Indonesia harus dilaksanakan dengan baik agar kebijakan tersebut dirasakan manfaatnya bagi masyarakat. Evaluasi atas efektivitas dari kebijakan dimaksud salah satunya dapat diperoleh melalui aktivitas pengawasan yang dilakukan oleh Bank Indonesia. Sebagai contoh, penerapan kebijakan rasio Loan To Value perlu mendapat pengawasan dalam operasionalisasinya, agar tujuan pengendalian pertumbuhan kredit properti yang berlebihan {excessive} dapat tercapai. 11. Aspek berikutnya dalam pengawasan Bank Indonesia adalah adanya peran aktif masyarakat dalam pelaksanaan kebijakan Bank Indonesia. Sebagai contoh adalah adanya peningkatan penggunaan uang Rupiah di seluruh wilayah Republik Indonesia bukan semata- mata hasil dorongan Bank Indonesia melalui kebijakan Penggunaan Uang Rupiah (PUR), tetapi juga karena adanya peningkatan kesadaran masyarakat untuk semakin mencintai Rupiah sebagai simbol kedaulatan negara yang harus dihormati dan dibanggakan oleh seluruh Warga Negara Indonesia. 12. Peningkatan kesadaran ini menjadi kunci dalam mencapai efektivitas kebijakan dan pengawasan Bank Indonesia mengingat Indonesia adalah negara yang memiliki lebih dari 17.000 pulau, terbentang dari Sabang sampai Merauke dalam hamparan wilayah hampir 2000 juta km2 dan dengan jumlah penduduk lebih dari 260 juta jiwa, sehingga operasionalisasi pengawasan akan menimbulkan biaya yang sangat tinggi apabila tidak disertai dengan dukungan kesadaran masyarakat. 13. Selanjutnya aspek kerjasama antar otoritas juga memainkan peran penting dalam pengawasan Bank Indonesia. Kerjasama Bank Indonesia dengan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan, Kementerian Keuangan, dan Lembaga Penjamin Simpanan yang diformalkan dalam Undang- Undang No. 9 tahun 2016 tentang Pencegahan dan Penanganan Krisis Sistem Keuangan (PPKSK), memperkuat koordinasi bagi keempat otoritas untuk saling memberikan dukungan dalam rangka mencegah dan menangani krisis sistem keuangan. Secara khusus, Bank Indonesia dan OJK secara konsisten terus membangun koordinasi yang kuat dan solid sehingga dapat tercipta kultur pengawasan yang sehat serta saling melengkapi. 14. Sementara itu, pada tingkat regional, kerjasama Bank Indonesia dengan Pemerintah Daerah serta instansi terkait lainnya memperkokoh kemampuan Bank Indonesia dalam pelaksanaan tugasnya. Saya ingin menyampaikan apresiasi yang sebesar-besarnya kepada Pemerintah Daerah NTT dan seluruh instansi terkait, yang telah bahu-membahu mendukung pelaksanaan tugas Bank Indonesia, antara lain melalui Tim Pemantauan dan Pengendalian Inflasi Daerah (TPID) maupun program clustering UMKM. Koordinasi yang baik ini dapat terlihat pada angka inflasi daerah NTT per Juli 2017 yang cukup terjaga dengan baik di angka 2,61% {year on yea?), atau di bawah inflasi nasional sebesar 3,88% {year on yea?). Semoga koordinasi dan kerjasama yang baik ini dapat tetap dijaga dan lebih ditingkatkan lagi di masa mendatang. 15. Aspek penting lain yang menjadi kunci dalam peranan Bank Indonesia sebagai pengawas di bidang makroprudensial, moneter dan sistem pembayaran adalah kesiapan Bank Indonesia dalam mengawal perekonomian pada kondisi a pa pun, baik pada saat ekonomi mengalami pertumbuhan maupun pada saat ekonomi dalam kondisi perlambatan. Bank Indonesia sebagai lender of the last resort adalah pertahanan terakhir bagi kondisi likuiditas perbankan agar sistem keuangan tetap terjaga. Untuk itu. Bank Indonesia akan terus menerus berusaha untuk meningkatkan kapabilitasnya menjadi bank sentral yang kredibel dan terbaik di regional. Bapak-Ibu hadirin sekalian yang berbahagia, <Penutup> 16. Saat ini peluang Indonesia dalam menjaga momentum pertumbuhan ekonomi semakin terbuka dengan perbaikan rating investasi Indonesia menjadi kategori investment grade oleh lembaga inter nasional serta adanya pembangunan infrastruktur nasional yang berjalan dengan cepat dan merata di seluruh Indonesia. 17. Dalam konteks ini, Bank Indonesia perlu meningkatkan perannya dalam mendukung kemajuan perekonomian Indonesia melalui berbagai kebijakan di bidang makroprudensial, moneter dan sistem pembayaran, yang tentunya perlu didukung dengan pengawasan yang kuat dan berkualitas agar tujuan Bank Indonesia untuk mencapai dan memelihara kestabilan nilai Rupiah dapat tercapai. 18. Untuk itu, masyarakat perlu memahami bahwa pengawasan Bank Indonesia bukan ditujukan untuk membatasi ruang gerak pelaku ekonomi, tetapi untuk memberikan arah bagi pelaku ekonomi agar pertumbuhan ekonomi berjalan pada koridor yang tepat. 19. Saya percaya bahwa pemahaman ini telah terinisiasi melalui seminar yang telah terlaksana dengan baik hari ini dan selanjutnya untuk dapat di-diseminasi-kan oleh para peserta dalam lingkup yang lebih luas, sehingga pemahaman yang diterima akan memberikan dampak yang positif bagi perekonomian Indonesia dan khususnya 'Bumi Flobamora'I tercinta ini. 20. Untuk mengakhiri sambutan ini, saya ingin menyampaikan terima kasih kepada penyelenggara seminar ini serta apresiasi sebesar- besarnya kepada seluruh narasumber dan peserta yang telah berkenan meluangkan waktu di tengah kesibukan untuk berbagi ilmu, pemikiran, informasi dan pengalamannya selama seminar ini. 21. Akhir kata, semoga Tuhan Yang Maha Kuasa meridhoi dan senantiasa melimpahkan bimbingan dan rahmat-Nya kepada kita semua, menuju masa depan yang lebih baik. Sekian dan terima kasih. Wa billahi taufiq Wai Hidayah. Wasalamu'alaikum Warahmatullahi wabarakatuh Erwin Rijanto Deputi Gubernur I Flores, Sumba, Timor, Alor --------------- ------------------------------------------------------------

Title: Pandangan Gubernur Bank Indonesia Pada Rapat Kerja Panitia Anggaran DPR RI Mengenai Laporan Semester I Dan Prognosis Semester II APBN TA 2006, 5 Juli 2006
text: VIEWS OF THE GOVERNOR OF BANK INDONESIA AT THE WORKING MEETING OF THE BUDGET COMMITTEE of the House of Representatives Rl REGARDING THE FIRST SEMESTER REPORT AND THE PROGNOSIS OF THE SECOND SEMESTER State Budget FY 2006 9595959595959595959595959595 Dear Members of the Council, 1. First of all, let us express our gratitude to the Budget Committee of the House of Representatives for inviting us to attend a Working Meeting with the Ministry of Finance today which will discuss the Report on the First Semester and Prognosis of the Second Semester of the FY 2006 State Budget. Before we express our views on the macro asumsi in the 11th-2006 state budget and the realization of the 2006 state budget, let us first convey the latest macroeconomic developments. A. Recent Macroeconomic Developments Dear Board Members, 2. In the quarter of 11-2006, economic growth is expected to increase slightly from the previous quarter which reached 4.59%. Entering the quarter of 111-2006, the increase in economic activity is expected to be high so that overall in 2006 the economy is expected to grow in the range of 5.0-5.7%. This is supported by the recovery of macroeconomic stability, thus creating opportunities for increased economic activity. The forecast is also based on a number of developments in external and internal factors, as well as the dynamics of economic developments up to the quarter of 11-2006. From the external side, world economic growth in 2006 is predicted to be relatively stable, while still being supported by economic expansion in the industrialized group, amid the high world oil demand and the resilience of a relatively tight monetary policy cycle. From the internal side, pressure on growth, which mainly comes from the weakening of people's purchasing power after the fuel price increase , is expected to continue, especially until the first half of 2006. 3. In relation to the rupiah exchange rate, although it still depreciated quite sharply until it reached the level of Rp9,263 per USD at the end of June 2006 for the whole of 2006 the rupiah exchange rate is estimated to move deeply stable tendency. Currently , the average rupiah exchange rate is from January to January. June 30th reached Rp9,207 per USD. Fundamentally, the rupiah exchange rate's stable forecast is related to the improving BOP performance. The improvement in BOP performance was mainly supported by a surplus in the capital and financial account, in line with improving private capital inflows in the form of FDI and portfolio investment. The increase in fund flows is supported by domestic factors, including high yields with an acceptable level of risk. However, there are some downside risks that need to be be wary, such as the lack of improvement in the investment climate and the existence of obstacles to the implementation of infrastructure projects, reversals in the flow of short-term portfolio funds, and uncertainty in world oil prices also have the potential to provide negative impact on the balance of payments. Overall, the rupiah exchange rate is still possible in the range assumed in the 2006 State Budget. 4. Meanwhile, future inflationary pressures are expected to ease. Inflation, which is currently at 15.53%, isexpected to gradually decline. The easing of inflationary pressures was caused by the delay in the increase in TDL and rupiah exchange rates as well as weak inflation stemming from the interaction between demand and supply. Price pressures due to fuel price hikes in October 2005 are expected to cause the CPI inflation rate to remain at a high level until the quarter of 111-2006. In the fourth quarter of 2006 the impact of price pressure is expected to end, and taking into account the lack of strong domestic demand for inflation, at the end of 2006 CPI inflation is expected reaching below the level of 8%, or still within the inflation range set by the Government, namely 8% b1 1.0%. 5. Taking into account the above developments, monetary policy is directed at maintaining macroeconomic stability. If the trend of positive developments such as in recent months continues, it is open to the possibility of a gradual reduction in interest rates as has been done in the past May. Furthermore, to increase the effectiveness of monetary policy in controlling inflation. Bank Indonesia will continue policy coordination and strategic partnerships with the Government and other economic players. B. Views on Macro Assumptions in the 2006 State Budget Dear Board Members, 6. After the 1st Semester of 2006, we consider that the macroeconomic assumptions presented by the Government are still realistic enough to be used as the basis for calculating the FY 2006 State Budget, with the following notes. : Table 1. Macro Assumptions of the State Budget and the Results of the APBN-P Meeting Variable 2006 BUDGET Macro Assumptions Meeting for apbn-P 2006 1. Annual economic growth (%) 6.2 5.9 2. Inflation (%) 8 8 3. Average exchange rate (Rp/USD) 9900 9000 4. Average 3-month SBI interest rate (%) 9.5 12 5. International oil prices (USD/barrel) 57 60 6. Indonesia's oil production (million barrels/day) 1.05 1 7. Economic Growth Assumptions - The realization of economic growth in the first quarter of 2006 which reached 4.6% indicates slowing domestic demand. Meanwhile, in the second quarter of 2006 several indicators still showed a slowdown. However, the economy in the future still has the potential to increase, if there is an acceleration of investment activities, both private and government. - Stable macroeconomic conditions are expected to provide incentives for investment activities as production costs including for capital purchases and raw materials from imports are lower. In addition, assuming lower interest rates, consumption and investment activities are expected to increase. - Given that to date various indicators have not shown significant development, we are of the view that to achieve the pace of economic growth as set by the Government of 5.9% in 2006 faces quite severe challenges. For this reason, more rigorous and sustainable efforts are needed to encourage improvements in people's purchasing power, improve the investment climate, efficiency, and productivity as well as efforts to encourage exports. These efforts must also be supported by increased financing from the banking industry, capital market and government finance (APBN). 8. Assumption of Inflation Rate - The inflation rate until June 2006 (year to date) showed a downward trend, reaching 2.87% or 15.53% (yoy). Taking into account the inflation rate and the downward trend of inflation and its seasonal patterns, we are of the view that the assumption of inflation of 8.0% is realistic enough to be used as the basis for calculating the 2006 APBN-P. As is known, the Government has also set the 2006 inflation target of 8% /- 1%. 9. Exchange Rate Assumptions - The average exchange rate until the end of June 2006 reached Rp9,207/USD. To achieve an average exchange rate of Rp9,000/USD as used in the assumption of the 2006 APBN-P, it is necessary to strengthen the rupiah exchange rate in the second semester of 2006. Taking into account the fundamental factors that influence the development of the exchange rate to date, we are of the view that the assumption of the rupiah exchange rate is quite optimistic. - The assumption of the rupiah exchange rate can be achieved if fundamental factors continue to improve. From the domestic side, it needs to be supported by improvements in theinvestment climate and infrastructure that can increase investment activities including FDI, thereby increasing production and exports. From the external side, it is necessary to maintain market confidence and minimize risk perception, so that the inflow of capital in the short term continues. 10. Interest Rate Assumptions - As is known, at the Board of Governors' Meeting on May 9, 2006, Bank Indonesia decided to lower the Bl Rate to 12.50%, down 25 bps compared to the previous level. The decline was based on the assessment that macroeconomic stability conditions are getting steadier so that medium-long-term inflation is expected to be on target. Thus, room for a gradual and measurable lowering of interest rates is still possible. But demikian. Bank Indonesia will continue to monitor various risk factors, such as the development of world oil prices and the direction of global monetary policy which still tends to be tight. In line with the decline in the 1-month Bl Rate, the 3-month SBI interest rate also showed a downward trend, from an average of 12.92% in January 2006 to 12.16% at the end of June 2006. - With this in mind, we are of the view that the assumption of an average SBI interest rate of 12% is realistic enough to be used as a calculation in the 2006 APBN-P. C. Realization of the 2006 State Budget Dear Councillors, 11. With regard to the 2006 STATE BUDGET deficit which is expected to exceed the 2006 state budget deficit of 0.7% of GDP (1.2% to 1.4% of GDP), we consider that an increase in the deficit can still be considered. The increase in the deficit is expected to restrain the decline in people's purchasing power. However, the increase in the deficit is not expected to have a significant impact on economic growth because a large amount of gian is aimed at Government consumption. In terms of monetary control, we will pay close attention to the increase in the deficit so as not to disrupt monetary stability. 12. Compared to the same period in the previous year, the realization of the 2006 State Budget (January to May) showed much better developments reflected in the lower state budget surplus. However, in the midst of the weak private sector, the realization of the 2006 state budget which still recorded a surplus -- among others due to very low capital expenditure -- also affected the low economic growth. The low fiscal stimulus from the Central Government also occurs at the regional level, so it needs attention. At the regional level, the low fiscal stimulus was reflected in the increase in local government accounts in BPD of around Rp30 trillion in the first four months of 2006 in line with the large drop in spending for the regions in the period which reached Rp62.8 trillion. This indicates that the expenditure for the region has not been fully utilized by the local government, which will further have implications for the non-acceleration of regional economic activities and the return of these funds to the Center in the form of investment in SBI which is reflected in the increasing ownership of SBI by BPD resulting in high costs of monetary management. 13. Some of the factors that in our view cause the low realization of the use of the Budget at the Regional level are: a. The incompatibility between the time of dropping (allocation) of Expenditure for the Regions by the Central Government and the needs of the Regions. b. In terms of administration and institutional capacity, the approval of the regional budget is slower than the allocation of regional expenditure disbursements, causing the funds that have been disbursed to be unable to be utilized by local governments. c. In terms of numbers, the budget for regional expenditures continues to increase in line with the development of the state budget (the share of the General Allocation Fund continues to increase from 25%, to 25.5% and now 26% of net domestic revenues. The allocation of profit-sharing funds has increased along with the development of international oil prices). d. The current fund management mechanism is that the dropping of funds for local governments is carried out directly into the local government's account at a commercial bank , causing a monetary expansion when funds are transferred from Bank Indonesia. 14. Some of the recommendations that we can convey are mainly related to the absorption of regional spending as follows: a. Regional spending is adjusted to the readiness of the region, especially for investment activities. b. Accelerate the apbd approval process by the DPRD so that investment activities can be realized. c. Increase institutional capacity in the regions. d. Placing unused Local Government funds in a checking account in Bl. e. Using funds in local Government accounts to increase fiscal stimulus. Dear Councillors, 15. This is our view on macroeconomic assumptions and the realization of the 2006 State Budget presented by the Government. We believe that with close cooperation between the Government, the House of Representatives and Bank Indonesia, it is expected to achieve the economic development targets aspired to in order to create a just society and prosperous. For the attention of the honourable Board members, we thank you. Jakarta, July 5th, 2006
text_original: PANDANGAN GUBERNUR BANK INDONESIA PADA RAPAT KERJA PANITIA ANGGARAN DPR Rl MENGENAI LAPORAN SEMESTER I DAN PROGNOSIS SEMESTER II APBN TA 2006 <95><95><95><95><95><95><95><95><95><95><95><95><95><95> Anggota Dewan yang terhormat, 1. Pertama-tama perkenankanlah kami menyampaikan terima kasih kepada Panitia Anggaran DPR Rl yang telah mengundang kami untuk menghadiri Rapat Kerja bersama Depkeu pada hari ini yang akan membahas mengenai Laporan Semester I dan Prognosis Semester II APBN TA 2006. Sebelum kami menyampaikan pandangan kami mengenai asumsi makro pada APBN semester 11-2006 serta realisasi APBN 2006, ijinkanlah kami menyampaikan terlebih dahulu perkembangan ekonomi makro terkini. A. Perkembangan Ekonomi Makro Terkini Anggota Dewan Yang Terhormat, 2. Dalam triwulan 11-2006, pertumbuhan ekonomi diperkirakan sedikit meningkat dari triwulan sebelumnya yang mencapai 4,59%. Memasuki triwulan 111-2006 ini, peningkatan kegiatan ekonomi diharapkan tinggi sehingga secara keseluruhan 2006 perekonomian diperkirakan akan tumbuh pada kisaran 5,0-5,7%. Perkiraan ini didukung oleh mulai pulihnya kestabilan makroekonomi, sehingga menciptakan peluang bagi peningkatan kegiatan ekonomi. Perkiraan tersebut juga didasarkan atas sejumlah perkembangan faktor eksternal maupun internal, serta dinamika perkembangan ekonomi sampai dengan triwulan 11-2006. Dari sisi eksternal, pertumbuhan ekonomi dunia pada tahun 2006 diperkirakan relatif stabil, dengan tetap didukung oleh ekspansi ekonomi di kelompok negara industri, di tengah masih tingginya permintaan minyak dunia dan dipertahankannya siklus kebijakan moneter yang relatif ketat. Dari sisi internal, tekanan terhadap pertumbuhan yang terutama bersumber dari melemahnya daya beli masyarakat pasca kenaikan harga BBM, diperkirakan akan terus berlanjut, khususnya sampai dengan paro pertama tahun 2006. 3. Berkaitan dengan nilai tukar rupiah, kendatipun masih terdepresiasi cukup tajam hingga mencapai level Rp9.263 per USD pada akhir Juni 2006 untuk keseluruhan tahun 2006 nilai tukar rupiah diperkirakan bergerak dalam kecenderungan yang stabil. Saat ini rata-rata nilai tukar rupiah dari Januari s.d. 30 Juni mencapai Rp9.207 per USD. Secara fundamental, perkiraan stabilnya kurs rupiah ini terkait dengan membaiknya kinerja NPI. Perbaikan kinerja NPI tersebut terutama didukung oleh surplus di transaksi modal dan finansial, sejalan dengan membaiknya aliran modal masuk swasta dalam bentuk FDI dan investasi portofolio. Meningkatnya aliran dana tersebut ditopang oleh faktor domestik antara lain imbal hasil yang cukup tinggi dengan tingkat risiko yang dapat diterima. Walaupun demikian, terdapat beberapa downside risk yang perlu diwaspadai, seperti belum membaiknya iklim investasi dan adanya hambatan implementasi proyek infrastruktur, pembalikan aliran dana portfolio jangka pendek, dan ketidakpastian harga minyak dunia juga berpotensi memberikan dampak negatif terhadap neraca pembayaran. Secara keseluruhan nilai tukar rupiah masih memungkinkan pada kisaran yang diasumsikan pada APBN 2006. 4. Sementara itu, tekanan inflasi ke depan diperkirakan akan menurun. Inflasi yang saat ini sebesar 15,53% diperkirakan akan berangsur-angsur menurun. Meredanya tekanan inflasi tersebut disebabkan oleh penundaan kenaikan TDL dan nilai tukar rupiah serta masih lemahnya inflasi yang bersumber dari interaksi antara permintaan dan penawaran. Tekanan harga akibat kenaikan harga BBM pada bulan Oktober 2005 diperkirakan menyebabkan laju inflasi IHK bertahan pada level yang tinggi sampai triwulan 111-2006. Pada triwulan IV-2006 pengaruh tekanan harga tersebut diperkirakan akan berakhir, dan dengan mempertimbangkan belum kuatnya permintaan domestik inflasi, di akhir tahun 2006 inflasi IHK diperkirakan mencapai di bawah level 8%, atau masih dalam kisaran inflasi yang ditetapkan oleh Pemerintah yaitu 8% <b1> 1,0%. 5. Dengan mempertimbangkan perkembangan diatas, kebijakan moneter diarahkan untuk menjaga stabilitas makroekonomi. Apabila kecenderungan perkembangan yang positif seperti dalam beberapa bulan terakhir ini terus berlanjut maka terbuka kemungkinan penurunan suku bunga secara bertahap sebagaimana yang telah dilakukan dalam bulan Mei yang lalu. Selanjutnya untuk meningkatkan efektivitas kebijakan moneter dalam mengendalikan inflasi. Bank Indonesia akan tetap melanjutkan koordinasi kebijakan dan kemitraan strategis dengan Pemerintah dan pelaku ekonomi lain. B. Pandangan Terhadap Asumsi Makro pada APBN 2006 Anggota Dewan Yang Terhormat, 6. Setelah berlangsungnya Semester 1-2006, kami memandang bahwa asumsi-asumsi makroekonomi yang disampaikan Pemerintah masih cukup realistis untuk digunakan sebagai dasar perhitungan APBN TA 2006, dengan beberapa catatan sebagai berikut: Tabel 1. Asumsi Makro APBN dan Hasil Rapat APBN-P Variabel 2006 APBN Rapat Asumsi Makro untuk APBN-P 2006 1. Pertumbuhan ekonomi tahunan (%) 6.2 5.9 2. Inflasi (%) 8 8 3. Nilai tukar rata-rata (Rp/USD) 9900 9000 4. Suku bunga SBI 3 bulan rata-rata (%) 9.5 12 5. Harga minyak internasional (USD/barel) 57 60 6. Produksi minyak Indonesia (juta barel/hari) 1.05 1 7. Asumsi Pertumbuhan Ekonomi - Realisasi pertumbuhan ekonomi pada triwulan I 2006 yang mencapai 4,6% menunjukkan permintaan domestik yang melambat. Sementara itu, dalam triwulan II 2006 beberapa indikator masih menunjukkan perlambatan. Namun demikian, perekonomian ke depan masih berpotensi meningkat, apabila terdapat akselerasi kegiatan investasi baik swasta maupun pemerintah. - Kondisi makroekonomi yang stabil diharapkan memberikan insentif bagi kegiatan investasi karena biaya produksi termasuk untuk pembelian modal dan bahan baku dari impor menjadi lebih rendah. Selain itu, dengan asumsi suku bunga yang lebih rendah maka kegiatan konsumsi dan investasi diharapkan akan mengalami peningkatan. - Mengingat sampai saat ini berbagai indikator belum menunjukkan perkembangan yang signifikan, kami berpandangan bahwa untuk mencapai laju pertumbuhan ekonomi sebagaimana yang ditetapkan Pemerintah sebesar 5,9% pada tahun 2006 menghadapi tantangan yang cukup berat. Untuk itu, diperlukan upaya lebih keras dan berkesinambungan untuk mendorong perbaikan daya beli masyarakat, perbaikan iklim investasi, efisiensi, dan produktivitas serta upaya mendorong ekspor. Upaya-upaya tersebut harus pula didukung oleh peningkatan pembiayaan baik dari industri perbankan, pasar modal maupun keuangan pemerintah (APBN). 8. Asumsi Laju Inflasi - Laju inflasi sampai dengan Juni 2006 (year to date) menunjukkan kecenderungan yang menurun yakni mencapai 2,87% atau 15,53% (yoy). Dengan memperhatikan tingkat inflasi tersebut dan kecenderungan inflasi yang menurun tersebut serta pola musimannya, kami berpandangan bahwa asumsi inflasi sebesar 8,0% cukup realistis untuk digunakan sebagai dasar perhitungan APBN-P 2006. Sebagaimana diketahui, Pemerintah juga telah menetapkan sasaran inflasi 2006 sebesar 8% +/- 1%. 9. Asumsi Nilai Tukar - Rata-rata nilai tukar sampai dengan akhir Juni 2006 mencapai Rp9.207/USD. Untuk mencapai rata-rata nilai tukar sebesar Rp9.000/USD sebagaimana digunakan dalam asumsi APBN-P 2006 diperlukan penguatan nilai tukar rupiah pada semester II 2006. Memperhatikan faktor-faktor fundamental yang mempengaruhi perkembangan nilai tukar hingga saat ini, kami berpandangan bahwa asumsi nilai tukar rupiah tersebut cukup optimis. - Asumsi nilai tukar rupiah tersebut dapat tercapai apabila faktor-faktor fundamental terus membaik. Dari sisi domestik, perlu didukung oleh perbaikan iklim investasi dan infrastruktur yang dapat meningkatkan kegiatan investasi termasuk FDI, sehingga meningkatkan produksi dan ekspor. Dari sisi eksternal, perlu mempertahankan kepercayaan pasar dan meminimalkan persepsi resiko, sehingga aliran masuk modal jangka pendek terus berlanjut. 10. Asumsi Suku Bunga - Sebagaimana diketahui, pada Rapat Dewan Gubernur tanggal 9 Mei 2006 yang lalu Bank Indonesia memutuskan untuk menurunkan Bl Rate menjadi 12,50%, turun 25 bps dibandingkan tingkat sebelumnya. Penurunan tersebut didasarkan pada asesmen bahwa kondisi stabilitas makroekonomi semakin mantap sehingga inflasi jangka menengah panjang diperkirakan akan sesuai target. Dengan demikian, ruang untuk menurunkan suku bunga secara bertahap dan terukur masih dimungkinkan. Namun demikian. Bank Indonesia akan senantiasa mencermati berbagai faktor risiko seperti perkembangan harga minyak dunia serta arah kebijakan moneter global yang masih cenderung ketat. Sejalan dengan penurunan Bl Rate 1 bulan tersebut, suku bunga SBI 3 bulan juga menunjukkan kecenderungan menurun yaitu dari rata-rata 12,92% pada Januari 2006 menjadi 12,16% pada akhir Juni 2006. - Dengan mempertimbangkan hal ini, kami berpandangan bahwa asumsi rata-rata suku bunga SBI sebesar 12% cukup realistis untuk digunakan sebagai dasar perhitungan dalam APBN-P 2006. C. Realisasi APBN 2006 Anggota Dewan Yang Terhormat, 11. Berkaitan dengan defisit APBN-P 2006 yang diperkirakan dapat melampaui defisit APBN 2006 sebesar 0,7% dari PDB (1,2% s.d 1,4% dari PDB), kami memandang bahwa kenaikan defisit masih dapat dipertimbangkan. Peningkatan defisit tersebut diharapkan dapat menahan penurunan daya beli masyarakat. Namun demikian peningkatan defisit tersebut diperkirakan belum berdampak signifikan terhadap pertumbuhan ekonomi karena sebagian besar ditujukan untuk konsumsi Pemerintah. Di sisi pengendalian moneter, peningkatan defisit tersebut akan kami cermati sehingga tidak mengganggu stabilitas moneter. 12. Dibandingkan dengan periode yang sama tahun sebelumnya, realisasi APBN 2006 (Januari s.d. Mei) menunjukkan perkembangan yang jauh lebih baik tercermin pada lebih rendahnya surplus APBN. Namun demikian, di tengah masih lemahnya sektor swasta, realisasi APBN 2006 yang masih mencatat surplus -- antara lain karena belanja modal yang masih sangat rendah -- turut mempengaruhi rendahnya pertumbuhan ekonomi. Rendahnya stimulus fiskal dari Pemerintah Pusat juga terjadi di tingkat daerah, sehingga perlu mendapat perhatian. Di tingkat daerah, rendahnya stimulus fiskal tercermin pada meningkatnya rekening Pemerintah Daerah di BPD sekitar Rp30 triliun pada empat bulan pertama tahun 2006 seiring dengan besarnya dropping Belanja untuk Daerah pada periode tersebut yang mencapai Rp62,8 triliun. Hal ini mengindikasikan dropping Belanja untuk Daerah tersebut belum sepenuhnya digunakan oleh Pemerintah Daerah, yang selanjutnya akan berimplikasi pada belum terakselerasinya kegiatan ekonomi daerah dan kembalinya dana tersebut ke Pusat dalam bentuk investasi di SBI yang tercermin dari meningkatnya kepemilikan SBI oleh BPD sehingga mengakibatkan tingginya biaya pengelolaan moneter. 13. Beberapa faktor yang menurut pandangan kami menyebabkan rendahnya realisasi penggunaan Anggaran Belanja di tingkat Daerah tersebut adalah: a. Kekurang-sesuaian antara waktu dropping (alokasi) Belanja untuk Daerah oleh Pemerintah Pusat dengan kebutuhan Daerah. b. Di sisi administrasi dan kapasitas kelembagaan, persetujuan APBD yang lebih lambat dari alokasi pencairan belanja daerah, menyebabkan dana yang sudah cair tersebut belum dapat dimanfaatkan Pemerintah daerah. c. Di sisi jumlah, anggaran Belanja untuk Daerah terus meningkat seiring dengan perkembangan APBN (Pangsa Dana Alokasi Umum terus meningkat dari 25%, menjadi 25,5% dan kini 26% dari penerimaan dalam negeri bersih. Alokasi Dana Bagi Hasil meningkat seiring dengan perkembangan harga minyak internasional). d. Mekanisme pengelolaan dana yang berlaku saat ini adalah dropping dana untuk Pemerintah Daerah dilakukan langsung ke rekening Pemerintah Daerah di Bank Umum sehingga menyebabkan ekspansi moneter saat dana ditransfer dari Bank Indonesia. 14. Beberapa rekomendasi yang dapat kami sampaikan terutama terkait dengan penyerapan belanja daerah sebagai berikut: a. Dropping belanja daerah disesuaikan dengan kesiapan daerah, terutama untuk kegiatan investasi. b. Mempercepat proses persetujuan APBD oleh DPRD agar kegiatan investasi dapat direalisasikan. c. Meningkatkan kapasitas kelembagaan di daerah. d. Menempatkan dana Pemerintah Daerah yang belum terpakai di rekening giro di Bl. e. Menggunakan dana di rekening Pemerintah daerah untuk meningkatkan stimulus fiskal. Anggota Dewan Yang Terhormat, 15. Demikian pandangan kami mengenai asumsi ekonomi makro dan realisasi APBN 2006 yang disampaikan oleh Pemerintah. Kami berkeyakinan bahwa dengan kerjasama yang erat di antara Pemerintah, DPR, dan Bank Indonesia, diharapkan dapat mencapai sasaran pembangunan ekonomi yang dicita-citakan guna mewujudkan masyakat yang adil dan sejahtera. Atas perhatian Anggota Dewan yang terhormat, kami ucapkan terima kasih. Jakarta, 5 Juli 2006

Title: Tantangan Perekonomian Indonesia di Era Pemulihan Ekonomi Global, Budi Mulya, Deputi Gubernur Bank Indonesia, 9 Februari 2011
text: Indonesia's Economic Challenges in the Era of Global Economic RecoveryBUDI MULYA1 Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia February 9, 2011 Indonesian Financial Market Community, Banking and ladies and gentlemen whom I respect, Assalamu'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh, Good afternoon and greetings to all of us, First, I would like to thank ING Securities for inviting me to the seminar this morning. This morning's seminar, which was held at the beginning of 2011 as well as the beginning of the 'rabbit' year, is certainly a valuable momentum for us to strengthen our business strategy in 2011 and the period ahead, which will still be more dynamic and full of challenges. Business strategy must remain based on optimism, but cautiously optimistic accompanied by strengthening business risk management practices. In particular, I would like to emphasize the importance of strengthening risk management practices, so that all financial industry players do not panic easily in the midst of the future situation which still tends to be covered by high volatility, especially in global financial markets. In this regard, the tendency of the behavior of global financial market participants, to change drastically over time as we can see in recent times, is expected to still occur. This is considering that the sustainability of the global economic recovery has not been convincing enough, although indications of economic recovery in developed countries have begun to be seen. The global economy is expected to grow 4.5% in 2011, up from the previous forecast of around 4.2%. Nevertheless, 2downside risk, especially from developed economies, remains high. In addition, the uncertainty factor is also further magnified by the protracted debate over efforts to resolve the crisis in the European region, and finally, the turmoil that has hit several countries in the Middle East region (Tunisia, Egypt and Yemen). On the other hand, economic growth in China and emerging markets, especially in Asia, is running faster and has even now begun to be marked by the threat of high inflation. This is also a reflection of the difference in the speed of economic recovery globally (two-speed economic recovery). The threat of inflation is mainly driven by the sharp increase in food commodity prices and global energy, which among others is related to the ongoing global extreme climate. If not handled carefully, it is feared that it will be a rollout of inflation expectations that are strengthening, given that perception factors still dominate today. Figure 1: World Economic Growth Projections The difference in the speed of economic recovery has its own implications for developing countries, especially through the pressure of capital inflows, including those that are quite large in the short term (hot money), and of course, it adds to the complexity of the macroeconomic policy in emerging markets. The capital inflows are not only an implication of expansive monetary policy in developed countries through quantitative easing and low interest rates, but also come from funds from the Asian region was transferred from the original placement in the European and American regions to other developing countries, including to Indonesia to find the level of returns that higher. The Insitute of International Finance (IIF) estimates that capital inflows to emerging markets will increase and exceed 1 trillion US Dollars starting in 2011. Chart 2: Capital Inflows to Emerging Market Forecast Sumber: Institute of International Finance (IIF), 24 Januari 2011 Another thing that must be observed is the increasingly visible differences in interests between countries, which is reflected in the differences in views of state leaders who came to the fore at the G-20 forum in Seoul on November 11-12, 2010 . On the one hand, the 2008 crisis has incurred tremendous costs in some developed countries, so that domestic political interference has become deeper and deeper. On the other hand, regional and international policy coordination and harmonization in the process of global economic recovery are increasingly realized its importance. It is clearly a challenge to deliver on the previous G-20 deal, in Pittsburgh 2009, which is 'strong, sustainable and balance growth'. Indeed, it must be realized that this is obviously not easy and takes time considering that banyak state has to carry out an unpopular step in the form of 'tightening the tie 'in its various forms of policy amid demands for expansion from the fiscal side to boost economic growth. The global situation is a picture of the conditions we will face in the coming years. In such a situation, for the authorities, especially the central bank, measures to prevent excessive risk taking in the financial industry and efforts to maintain macroeconomic stability will be a priority. In addition, policy measures will also be faced with an increasingly dilemmatic situation and tend to be costly. Going forward, policy challenges will be even greater considering that, on the one hand, policy transmission, including monetary policy, after the 2008 crisis tends to slow down, while on the other hand, economic actors and the public tend to demand faster results. This condition will make the credibility of the authorities, including Bank Indonesia, even more important considering the increasingly strong role of perception factors in driving financial markets today. Indonesia's Economy : Economic Growth and Inflation We should be grateful that in the midst of the challenging dynamics of the global economy and financial markets in recent years, the Indonesian economy was still able to grow 4.5% in 2009. The Central Bureau of Statistics (BPS) also just announced the realization of Indonesia's economic growth in 2010 of 6.1%, with growth in the last quarter of 6.9%. The encouraging thing is that although the main driving factor for economic growth is domestic consumption, the contribution of investment and exports showed an increase in 2010. In line with the positive export performance, the3 current account also recorded a considerable surplus, namely 6.3 billion US Dollars. Strong foreign capital inflows, both in the form of direct investment (FDI) and portfolio investment, contributed to the strong performance of Indonesia's Balance of Payments (BOP) in 2010, which experienced a surplus of 30.2 billion US Dollars. With the strong BOP performance, the position of reserve assets until the end of December 2010 was recorded at USD 96.2 billion, equivalent to 7.1 months of imports and servicing government external debt4 This will certainly be a conducive foundation in the coming years. Bank Indonesia estimates that economic growth in 2011 will be slightly higher than 6%, in the range of 6%-6.5%. Similarly, in the next few years. However, Indonesia's economic growth is currently still relatively lower than some neighboring countries. This needs to be a common concern and agenda, so that Indonesia does not lose momentum. Domestic economic capacity must be further increased so that the economy does not overheat quickly. Strengthening economic capacity must really be a common priority to accommodate a fairly high, healthy and quality economic growth, as well as being the key to efforts to reduce poverty and employment. In this regard, at least some positive indications have begun to be seen from the data on investment realization, both foreign (FDI) and domestic (PMDN) in 2010 which was quite high, namely Rp 208.5 trillion (/- 23 billion US Dollars), an increase of almost 50% from 2009. We all certainly hope that these investment projects can be smooth and completed soon, so that they can really increase economic capacity.5 Figure 3: Indonesia's GDP Development (%, y-o-y) Meanwhile , in terms of prices, in line with the strengthening of economic activity, the inflation rate shows an increasing trend, mainly due to the encouragement of volatile foods prices, especially due to climate change and distribution disruptions, as is also the case in some countries in the region. This condition has the potential to drive up inflation expectations amid the dominance of current perceptions, as reflected in several expectation indicators, both based on consumer surveys and producers, as well as indicators of expectations in financial markets. Figure 4: Inflation Indicators and Inflation Expectations Inflation in 2010 was recorded at 6.96% (yoy), exceeding the Bank's inflation target Indonesia was 5% /-1% in 2010. As I mentioned earlier, this fairly high inflation is mainly due to the volatile foods component which experiences inflation of 17.74%. Inflationary pressures are maintained at present, as reflected by inflation in January 2011 of 7.02% (yoy) and inflation of volatile foods of 18.25% (yoy). Observing the development of inflation, and to strengthen the Government's policy aimed at reducing food price pressures, especially through the policy of exempting import duties on several foodstuffs, Bank Indonesia in the RDG on 4th February 2011 took pre-emptive steps by raising the Bl Rate by 25 bps from 6.50% to 6.75%.6 Figure 5: Indonesia Inflation Development (%, y-o-y) Basically, the increase in the Bl Rate is a commitment by Bank Indonesia to anchor public inflation expectations to remain in line with achievement of the inflation target in 2011 of 5% b11%. Bank Indonesia strives to ensure that the development of volatile foods inflation does not worsen inflation expectations of economic actors. Especially when considering that the increasing inflation of volatile foods is a phenomenon that also occurs in other developing countries. In addition, policy measures are also aimed at preventing potential inflationary pressures from the demand side, in line with the continued economic expansion in 2011. One early indication is an increase in the growth rate of the money supply (Ml7), which usually signals potential future inflationary pressures from the demand side. I should also emphasize that the increase in the Bl Rate is also a step by Bank Indonesia to strengthen the policy 'mix' that has been taken since 20108, especially through bandage liquidity control measures, both in the form of improving the operational strategy of liquidity management (OPT) and increasing the reserve requirement ratio9 With the policy steps as I stated, Bank Indonesia is optimistic that inflation will be controlled and within the range of inflation targets set by the Government, namely 5% /- 1% (2011) and 4.5% /- 1% (2O12)10. Going forward. Bank Indonesia will continue to monitor the turmoil in inflationary pressures and is ready to take policy that it is needed in a measured manner to ensure that inflation is on target, given that controlled inflation is a prerequisite for the sustainability of economic development and to protect the purchasing power of the wider community. In relation to exchange rate policy, Bank Indonesia will continue to take steps to prevent excessive exchange rate fluctuations and to minimize speculative transactions. In the current strengthening exchange rate tendency. Bank Indonesia will provide reasonable strengthening in line with economic fundamentals and improving risk perceptions to support achievement of the inflation target and to maintain balance of the external side of the economy. In this connection. Bank Indonesia will also emphasize on regulating foreign exchange liquidity, as well as to stimulate risk management related to exchange rate exposure, particularly for banks. . The commitment to maintain reasonable exchange rate fluctuations, in accordance with dinamika and interactions in the foreign exchange market, is becoming increasingly important going forward for stability in the domestic financial market In general, it can be optimally maintained, in a situation where the risk of global financial market volatility is expected to remain high. Singkatnya, so as not to add to the uncertainty and so that domestic economic actors do not easily panic in the midst of quite strong domestic economic fundamentals. Financial Market Deepening Before ending my presentation this morning, I would like to re-emphasize theneed for deepening of domestic financial markets. The thing that must really be in the common interest is concretely, both the authorities and the market participants. This effort must be realized immediately although it must still be carried out gradually, to provide forging tan adjustments and as a "learning process'. We certainly still remember, the impact of the turmoil that continued to occur in the domestic financial market when the global crisis hit in 2008, although in general the economy and financial markets were in a state of disrepair . can be said to be relatively able to survive well. In the money market, the perception of tight liquidity still occurs even though the liquidity stocks of banks are still very large. Liquidity stocks are indeed very large, but they are not flowing due to the decline in interbank trust. This happens because inter-bank transactions are still dominated by transactions that are 'un-collateralized'. Such a habit would tend to override the importance of increasing the liquidity of the SUN market. In other words, SUN 8 which are liquid assets are not part of the daily liquidity management of banks. Currently, SUN is really treated as a risk-free investment, even though as a risk-free asset, of course, the return is also the lowest. Thus, the portfolio composition of banks and other financial institutions will certainly tend to be sub-optimal. In addition, this trend also makes market participants tend to ignore the market risk inherent in SUN as a securities instrument. As a result, SUN holders will quickly panic when the price of SUN is in a downward trend because all will react the same, namely selling SUN. With the number of SUN getting bigger at this time, the deepening of the SUN market should be a common agenda, because all parties clearly have similar interests with the increasing liquidity of the SUN market. In this regard, several initiatives have been carried out by Bank Indonesia, especially through strengthening bank liquidity management in the implementation of OPT, including making SUN an eligible asset of OPT since February 2008. This step begins with gradually reducing excess liquidity in the banking industry every day, through the absorption of excess liquidity into SBI instruments with a longer tenor and term deposit. This is intended so that when there is a lack of liquidity at a certain time, banks can repo-kan their SUN to obtain temporary liquidity. Bank Indonesia remains committed to providing sufficient liquidity every day, although not with an approach to allowing excessive liquidity and only absorbing the rest at the end of the day. Gradually. Bank Indonesia will take a different approach, namely absorbing excess liquidity first, and then temporarily increasing the shortfall through repo SUN purchase transactions. This is in addition to strengthening the daily liquidity management of the banking industry, as well as so that banks are accustomed to transacting on a repo basis. In relation to efforts to deepen the financial market, what is currently in the preparation stage is the activation of repo 'try-party' transactions in Bank Indonesia's OPT to absorb excess liquidity. In this regard, Bank Indonesia will borrow SUN from various financial institutions (pension and insurance funds) to further use the SUN in reverse repo transactions to banks to absorb excess liquidity. Related to the 'try-party' repo transaction, pension and insurance funds will get a fee for SUN borrowed by Bank Indonesia, so that they can get additional income to compensate for the custodion fee. Pension and insurance funds will not face counterparty risk considering that the counterparty of the transaction is Bank Indonesia. This includes the risk of non-return of SUN lent (lending) to Bank Indonesia, when there are banks that cannot return SUN purchased in a repo from Bank Indonesia, Bank Indonesia Indonesia will bear this risk by finding a replacement for SUN with the same series. Cover In closing, I would like to affirm Bank Indonesia's commitment to maintain inflation in accordance with the target set, even in conditions that are often increasingly dilemmatic and optional. increasingly complex policies. Thus, there will be necessary conditions for economic development that not only grows higher, but also that is of higher quality and sustainability. In the positions and angles of interest of each one, we all have a responsibility for it. We still have to be optimistic, but always be vigilant and continue to improve our ability to manage risks considering that the situation in the future will still be very dynamic and full of challenges.
