text_original: Tantangan Perekonomian Indonesia di Era Pemulihan Ekonomi Global1 BUDI MULYA Deputi Gubernur Bank Indonesia 9 Februari 2011 Komunitas Pasar Finansial Indonesia, Perbankan dan hadirin sekalian yang saya hormati, Assalamu'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh, Selamat siang dan salam sejahtera bagi kita semua, Pertama, saya sampaikan terima kasih kepada ING Securities yang sudah mengundang saya dalam seminar pagi ini. Seminar pagi ini, yang diselenggarakan di awal tahun 2011 sekaligus awal tahun 'kelinci', tentunya merupakan momentum yang berharga bagi kita untuk memantapkan strategi bisnis di tahun 2011 dan periode kedepan, yang masih akan semakin dinamis dan penuh tantangan. Strategi bisnis harus tetap dilandasi optimisme, namun penuh kewaspadaan (cautiously optimist) disertai dengan penguatan praktik manajemen risiko bisnis. Secara khusus, saya ingin menekankan pentingnya penguatan praktik manajemen risiko, agar segenap pelaku industri keuangan tidak mudah panik ditengah situasi ke depan yang masih cenderung diliputi volatilitas yang tinggi, khususnya di pasar finansial global. Dalam hal ini, kecenderungan perilaku pelaku pasar finansial global, untuk berubah secara drastis dari waktu ke waktu sebagaimana dapat kita cermati dalam beberapa waktu terakhir, diperkirakan masih akan terjadi. Hal tersebut mengingat kelangsungan pemulihan ekonomi global belum cukup meyakinkan, meskipun indikasi pemulihan ekonomi di negara maju sudah mulai terlihat. Perekonomian global diperkirakan tumbuh 4.5% di tahun 20112, meningkat dari perkiraan sebelumnya sekitar 4.2%. Namun demikian, downside risk, terutama dari perekonomian negara maju masih cukup tinggi. Selain itu, faktor ketidakpastian juga semakin diperbesar oleh berlarutnya perdebatan atas upaya penyelesaian krisis di kawasan Eropa, dan yang terakhir, gejolak yang melanda beberapa negara di kawasan Timur Tengah (Tunisia, Mesir dan Yaman). Di sisi lain, pertumbuhan ekonomi di China dan negara-negara berkembang (emerging market), khususnya di Asia berjalan lebih cepat dan bahkan kini sudah mulai diwarnai ancaman inflasi yang tinggi. Hal ini sekaligus menjadi refleksi dari perbedaan kecepatan pemulihan ekonomi secara global (two-speed economic recovery). Ancaman inflasi utamanya didorong oleh meningkat-tajamnya harga komoditi pangan dan enerji global, yang antara lain terkait dengan berlangsungnya iklim ekstrim global. Hal ini bila tidak ditangani secara cermat, dikhawatirkan akan menjadi guliran ekspektasi inflasi yang semakin menguat, mengingat faktor persepsi masih mendominasi dewasa ini. Grafik 1: Proyeksi Pertumbuhan Ekonomi Dunia Perbedaan kecepatan pemulihan ekonomi tersebut membawa implikasi tersendiri bagi negara-negara berkembang, khususnya melalui tekanan capital inflows, termasukyang sifatnya jangka pendek (hot money) yang cukup besar, dan tentunya menambah kompleksitas kebijakan makroekonomi di emerging market. Capital inflows tersebut bukan saja sebagai implikasi kebijakan moneter yang ekspansif di negara-negara maju melalui quantitative easing dan suku bunga rendah, melainkan juga berasal dari dana-dana dari kawasan Asia yang dialihkan dari semula berupa penempatan di kawasan Eropa dan Amerika ke negara-negara berkembang lainnya, termasuk ke Indonesia untuk mencari tingkat imbal hasil yang lebih tinggi. Insitute of International Finance (IIF) memperkirakan bahwa capital inflows ke emerging market akan meningkat dan melampui 1 triliun US Dollar mulai tahun 2011 ini. Grafik 2: Perkiraan Capital Inflows ke Emerging Market Sumber: Institute of International Finance (IIF), 24 Januari 2011 Hal lain yang harus dicermati adalah semakin terlihatnya perbedaan kepentingan antar negara, yang diantaranya tercermin dari perbedaan pandangan para pemimpin negara yang mengemuka pada forum G-20 di Seoul 11-12 November 2010 lalu. Di satu sisi, krisis 2008 telah menimbulkan biaya yang luar biasa besar di beberapa negara maju, sehingga campur tangan politik domestik menjadi semakin dalam. Di sisi lain, koordinasi dan harmonisasi kebijakan secara regional dan internasional dalam proses pemulihan ekonomi global semakin disadari arti pentingnya. Hal ini jelas merupakan tantangan tersendiri untuk mewujudkan kesepakatan G-20 sebelumnya, di Pittsburgh 2009 lalu, yaitu 'strong, sustainable and balance growth'. Memang harus disadari bahwa hal tersebut jelas tidak mudah dan memerlukan waktu mengingat banyak negara harus menjalankan langkah yang tidak popular berupa 'pengetatan ikat pinggang' dalam berbagai bentuk kebijakannya di tengah tuntutan ekspansi dari sisi fiskal untuk mendorong pertumbuhan ekonomi. Situasi global tersebut merupakan gambaran kondisi yang akan kita hadapi di tahun- tahun mendatang. Dalam situasi tersebut, bagi otoritas, utamanya bank sentral, langkah untuk mencegah excessive risk taking di industri keuangan dan upaya menjaga stabilitas makro ekonomi akan menjadi prioritas. Selain itu, langkah kebijakan juga akan dihadapkan pada situasi yang semakin dilematis dan cenderung costly. Ke depan, tantangan kebijakan akan semakin besar mengingat, disatu sisi, transmisi kebijakan, termasuk kebijakan moneter, pasca krisis 2008 cenderung melambat, sementara di sisi lain, pelaku ekonomi dan masyarakat cenderung menuntut hasil yang lebih cepat. Kondisi ini akan membuat kredibilitas otoritas, termasuk Bank Indonesia, menjadi semakin penting mengingat semakin kuatnya peran faktor persepsi dalam menggerakkan pasar finansial dewasa ini. Perekonomian Indonesia : Pertumbuhan Ekonomi dan Inflasi Kita harus bersyukur bahwa di tengah dinamika perekonomian dan pasar finansial global yang penuh tantangan dalam beberapa tahun terkahir ini, ekonomi Indonesia masih mampu tumbuh 4.5% pada tahun 2009 lalu. Biro Pusat Statistik (BPS) juga baru mengumumkan realisasi pertumbuhan ekonomi Indonesia di tahun 2010 sebesar 6,1%, dengan pertumbuhan di kuartal terakhir sebesar 6.9%3. Hal yang menggembirakan adalah bahwa meskipun faktor pendorong utama pertumbuhan ekonomi adalah konsumsi domestik, namun kontribusi investasi dan ekspor menunjukkan peningkatan di tahun 2010 ini. Sejalan dengan kinerja ekspor yang positif, neraca transaksi berjalan (current account) juga masih mencatat surplus yang cukup besar, yaitu 6,3 milyar US Dollar. Kuatnya aliran masuk modal asing, baik dalam bentuk investasi langsung (PMA) dan investasi portofolio, berkontribusi terhadap kuatnya kinerja Neraca Pembayaran Indonesia (NPI) tahun 2010, yang mengalami surplus 30,2 milyar US Dollar4. Dengan kinerja NPI yang cukup kuat tersebut, posisi cadangan devisa sampai dengan akhir Desember 2010 tercatat USD 96,2 miliar, setara 7.1 bulan impor dan pembayaran utang luar negeri pemerintah Hal ini tentu akan menjadi pondasi yang kondusif di tahun-tahun mendatang. Bank Indonesia memperkirakan pertumbuhan ekonomi di tahun 2011 akan sedikit lebih tinggi dari 6%, dalam rentang 6%-6.5%. Demikian pula pada beberapa tahun berikutnya. Meski demikian, pertumbuhan ekonomi Indonesia saat ini masih relatif lebih rendah dibandingkan beberapa negara tetangga. Hal ini perlu menjadi perhatian dan agenda bersama, agar Indonesia tidak kehilangan momentum. Kapasitas perekonomian domestik harus lebih ditingkatkan agar perekonomian tidak cepat memanas (overheating). Penguatan kapasitas perekonomian harus benar-benar menjadi prioritas bersama untuk mengakomodasi petumbuhan ekonomi yang cukup tinggi, sehat dan berkualitas, sekaligus menjadi kunci bagi upaya mengurangi tingkat kemiskinan dan penyerapan tenaga kerja. Terkait hal ini, paling tidak beberapa indikasi positif sudah mulai terlihat dari data realisasi investasi, baik asing (PMA) maupun domestik (PMDN) di tahun 2010 yang cukup tinggi, yaitu Rp 208.5 triliun5 (+/- 23 milyar US Dollar), meningkat hampir 50% dari tahun 2009. Kita semua tentu berharap agar proyek-proyek investasi ini dapat lancar dan segera selesai, sehingga benar-benar dapat meningkatkan kapasitas perekonomian. Grafik 3 : Perkembangan PDB Indonesia (%, y-o-y) Sementara dari sisi harga, sejalan dengan menguatnya kegiatan ekonomi, laju inflasi menunjukkan kecenderungan yang meningkat terutama akibat dorongan kenaikan harga kelompok bahan pangan (volatile foods), terutama akibat perubahan iklim dan gangguan distribusi, sebagaimana juga terjadi di beberapa negara di kawasan. Kondisi ini berpotensi mendorong kenaikan ekspektasi inflasi di tengah dominasi persepsi saat ini, sebagaimana tercermin pada beberapa indikator ekspektasi, baik berdasarkan survey konsumen dan produsen, maupun indikator ekspektasi di pasar keuangan. Grafik 4 : Indikator Inflasi dan Ekspektasi Inflasi Inflasi tahun 2010 tercatat sebesar 6,96% (yoy), melampaui target inflasi Bank Indonesia sebesar 5% +/-1% di tahun 2010. Sebagaimana saya singgung sebelumnya, inflasi yang cukup tinggi ini terutama disebabkan oleh komponen volatile foods yang mengalami inflasi sebesar 17,74%. Tekanan inflasi masih berlanjut saat ini, tercermin dari inflasi bulan Januari 2011 sebesar 7,02% (yoy) dan inflasi volatile foods sebesar 18.25% (yoy). Mencermati perkembangan inflasi tersebut, dan untuk memperkuat kebijakan Pemerintah yang ditujukan untuk mengurangi tekanan harga pangan, khususnya melalui kebijakan pengecualian bea masuk impor beberapa bahan pangan, Bank Indonesia dalam RDG tanggal 4 Februari 2011 lalu mengambil langkah pre-emptive dengan menaikkan Bl Rate 25 bps dari 6,50% menjadi 6,75%6. Grafik 5 : Perkembangan Inflasi Indonesia (%, y-o-y) Pada dasarnya, kenaikan Bl Rate tersebut merupakan komitmen Bank Indonesia untuk menjangkar ekspektasi inflasi masyarakat agar tetap sejalan dengan pencapaian sasaran inflasi di tahun 2011 sebesar 5%<b1>1%. Bank Indonesia berupaya agar perkembangan inflasi volatile foods tidak memperburuk ekspektasi inflasi pelaku ekonomi. Terlebih bila mengingat bahwa meningkatnya inflasi volatile foods merupakan fenomena yang juga terjadi di negara-negara berkembang lainnya. Selain itu, langkah kebijakan juga ditujukan untuk mencegah potensi tekanan inflasi dari sisi permintaan, seiring dengan berlanjutnya ekspansi ekonomi di tahun 2011. Salah satu indikasi awal adalah kenaikan laju pertumbuhan uang beredar (Ml)7, yang lazimnya menandakan potensi tekanan inflasi ke depan dari sisi permintaan. Perlu juga saya tegaskan bahwa kenaikan Bl Rate tersebut juga merupakan langkah Bank Indonesia untuk memperkuat 'bauran' kebijakan yang sudah ditempuh sejak tahun 2010 yang lalu8, khususnya melalui langkah pengendalian likuiditas perbankan, baik berupa penyempurnaan strategi operasional manajemen likuiditas (OPT) maupun kenaikan rasio GWM9 Dengan langkah kebijakan sebagaimana saya sampaikan, Bank Indonesia optimis bahwa inflasi akan terkendali dan berada dalam kisaran target inflasi yang ditetapkan Pemerintah, yaitu 5% +/- 1% (2011) dan 4,5% +/- 1% (2O12)10. Ke depan. Bank Indonesia akan terus mencermati gejolak tekanan inflasi dan siap mengambil kebijakan yang diperlukan secara terukur untuk memastikan agar inflasi sesuai target, mengingat inflasi yang terkendali menjadi prasyarat bagi kesinambungan pembangunan ekonomi dan untuk melindungi daya beli masyarakat luas. Terkait dengan kebijakan nilai tukar, Bank Indonesia akan tetap menempuh langkah untuk mencegah fluktuasi nilai tukar yang berlebihan serta untuk meminimalkan transaksi yang sifatnya spekulatif. Dalam tendensi nilai tukar yang menguat saat ini. Bank Indonesia akan memberikan ruang penguatan yang wajar sejalan dengan fundamental perekonomian dan membaiknya persepsi risiko, untuk mendukung pencapaian target inflasi dan dengan tetap menjaga keseimbangan sisi eksternal perekonomian. Dalam kaitan ini. Bank Indonesia juga akan menekankan pada langkah pengaturan likuiditas valuta asing, sekaligus untuk mendorong pengelolaan manajemen risiko terkait dengan eksposure nilai tukar, khususnya bagi perbankan. Komitmen untuk menjaga fluktuasi nilai tukar yang wajar, sesuai dengan dinamika dan interaksi di pasar valuta asing, menjadi semakin penting ke depan agar stabilitas di pasar finansial domestik secara umum dapat tetap optimal terjaga, dalam situasi risiko volatilitas pasar finansial global yang diperkirakan masih akan tinggi. Singkatnya, agar tidak menambah ketidakpastian dan agar pelaku ekonomi domestik tidak mudah panik di tengah cukup kuatnya kondisi fundamental ekonomi domestik. Pendalaman Pasar Finansial Sebelum mengakhiri paparan saya pagi ini, saya ingin kembali menekankan perlunya pendalaman pasar finansial domestik. Hal yang harus benar-benar menjadi kepentingan bersama secara konkrit, baik otoritas maupun para pelaku pasar. Upaya ini harus segera terwujud meski harus tetap dilakukan secara bertahap, untuk memberikan kesempatan penyesuaian dan sebagai "learning process'. Kita tentu masih ingat, imbas gejolak yang tetap terjadi di pasar finansial domestik ketika krisis global melanda tahun 2008 lalu, meski secara umum perekonomian dan pasar finansial domestik bisa dikatakan relatif dapat bertahan dengan baik. Di pasar uang, persepsi ketatnya likuiditas masih terjadi meskipun stok likuiditas perbankan masih sangat besar. Stok likuiditas memang sangat besar, namun tidak mengalir karena merosotnya kepercayaan antar bank. Hal ini terjadi karena transaksi antar-bank masih didominasi transaksi yang sifatnya 'un-collateralized'. Kebiasaan seperti ini akan cenderung mengesampingkan pentingnya meningkatkan ke-likuid-an pasar SUN. Dengan kata lain, SUN 8 yang merupakan aset likuid tidak menjadi bagian pengelolaan likuiditas harian perbankan. Saat ini, SUN benar-benar diperlakukan sebatas sebagai risk-free investment, padahal sebagai risk-free asset tentunya return-nya juga yang paling rendah. Dengan demikian, komposisi portfolio perbankan dan institusi keuangan lainnya tentu akan cenderung sub- optimal. Selain itu, kecenderungan ini juga menjadikan pelaku pasar cenderung abai terhadap market risk yang melekat dalam SUN sebagai suatu instrumen surat berharga. Akibatnya, pemegang SUN akan cepat panik manakala harga SUN dalam tendensi yang turun karena semua akan bereaksi sama, yaitu menjual SUN. Dengan jumlah SUN yang semakin besar saat ini, maka pendalaman pasar SUN sudah seharusnya menjadi agenda bersama, karena semua pihak jelas memiliki kesamaan kepentingan dengan semakin likuid-nya pasar SUN. Terkait hal ini beberapa inisiatif sudah dilakukan Bank Indonesia, terutama melalui penguatan manajemen likuiditas perbankan dalam pelaksanaan OPT, termasuk menjadikan SUN sebagai eligible asset OPT sejak Februari 2008. Langkah ini dimulai dengan secara bertahap mengurangi kelebihan likuiditas perbankan setiap harinya, melalui penyerapan kelebihan likuiditas ke dalam instrumen SBI dengan tenor yang lebih panjang dan term deposit. Hal ini dimaksudkan agar manakala terjadi kekurangan likuiditas pada saat tertentu, perbankan dapat me-repo-kan SUN-nya untuk memperoleh likuiditas sementara. Bank Indonesia tetap berkomitmen untuk menyediakan likuditas yang cukup setiap harinya, meskipun bukan dengan pendekatan membiarkan likuiditas berlebihan dan baru menyerap sisanya di akhir hari. Secara bertahap. Bank Indonesia akan mengambil pendekatan yang berbeda, yaitu menyerap terlebih dahulu kelebihan likuiditas, baru kemudian menambah secara temporer kekurangannya melalui transaksi pembelian SUN secara repo. Hal ini selain untuk memperkuat manajemen likuiditas harian perbankan, sekaligus agar perbankan terbiasa bertransaksi secara repo,. Terkait dengan upaya pendalaman pasar keuangan, hal yang saat ini sedang dalam tahap penyiapan adalah aktivasi transaksi 'try-party' repo dalam OPT Bank Indonesia untuk menyerap kelebihan likuiditas. Dalam hal ini, Bank Indonesia akan meminjam (borrow) SUN dari berbagai institusi keuangan (dana pensiun dan asuransi) untuk selanjutnya menggunakan SUN tersebut dalam transaksi reverse repo kepada perbankan untuk menyerap kelebihan likuiditas. Terkait dengan transaksi 'try-party'repo tersebut, dana pensiun dan asuransi akan memperoleh fee atas SUN yang dipinjam Bank Indonesia, sehingga dapat memperoleh tambahan income untuk mengkompensasi custodion fee. Dana pensiun dan asuransi tidak akan menghadapi counterparty risk mengingat counterparty transaksi adalah Bank Indonesia. Termasuk terhadap risiko tidak kembalinya SUN yang dipinjamkan (di-lending- kan) ke Bank Indonesia, manakala terdapat bank yang tidak dapat mengembalikan SUN yang dibeli secara repo dari Bank Indonesia, Bank Indonesia yang akan menanggung risiko tersebut dengan mencarikan pengganti SUN dengan seri yang sama. Penutup Sebagai penutup saya ingin menegaskan komitmen Bank Indonesia untuk menjaga inflasi sesuai dengan sasaran yang sudah ditetapkan, meskipun dalam kondisi yang seringkali semakin dilematis dan pilihan kebijakan yang semakin kompleks. Dengan demikian, akan terwujud kondisi yang diperlukan bagi pembangunan ekonomi yang tidak saja tumbuh lebih tinggi, namun juga yang lebih berkualitas dan berkesinambungan. Dalam posisi dan sudut kepentingan masing-masing, kita semua memiliki tanggung jawab untuk itu. Kita tetap harus optimis, namun senantiasa waspada dan terus meningkatkan kemampuan dalam mengelola risiko mengingat situasi ke depan masih akan sangat dinamis dan penuh tantangan. Terima kasih dan semoga Allah SWT senantiasa melindungi dan membimbing kita semua. Wassalamu'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh. Title: Penjelasan Gubernur Bank Indonesia Pada Rapat Kerja Dengan Komisi XI DPR RI, 14 Maret 2006
text: EXPLANATION BY THE GOVERNOR OF BANK INDONESIA AT A WORKING MEETING WITH COMMISSION XI of the House of Representatives on MARCH 14, 2006 9595959595959595959595959595 1. Introduction Dear Members of the Council, 1. First of all, let us express our gratitude to the Chairman and Members of Commission XI of the House for inviting us to the Working Meeting today. For us, this meeting has a very important meaning , especially in order to convey various information and explanations regarding the implementation of Bank Indonesia's duties mandated by law as well as to get a variety of inputs from Board Members that are useful for improvement efforts in the implementation of our duties in the field of monetary, banking, and payment systems going forward. Moreover, we view this kind of meeting as a form of embodiment of Bank Indonesia accountability to the Dpr-RI. 2. In accordance with the agenda we obtained, in the Working Meeting this time will be discussed regarding the Report on the performance and implementation of bl tasks in 2005, the plan for action andjut API and intermediation developments banking through MSMEs. We can say that the first topic was raised on the occasion of the Meeting on February 20, 2006. Similarly, at the end of January 2006 we have submitted the Triwulan Iv-2005 Report which is a report on the progress of the implementation of Bank Indonesia's duties and authorities in the monetary, banking and system sectors. payments for the period of the fourth quarter of 2005 (October - December 2005). The report is basically to comply with theiban Bl obligation as per article 58 paragraphs (1) and (2) of Law No. 23 of 1999 concerning Bank Indonesia as amended by Law No. 3 of 2004. 3. Therefore, on the occasion of today's Meeting, before we listen to the input, questions, and views of the Board Members, allow us to briefly explain the important points of evaluation of the performance and implementation of Bl tasks in 2005, followed by a presentation on the API follow-up plan and the development of banking intermediation through thedevelopment of MSMEs. 2. Performance and Performance of Bl Duties in 2005 Dear Members of the Council, 4. At the beginning of 2005, Bank Indonesia predicted that in 2005 the momentum of economic recovery that had been achieved in 2004 would continue continued and became a strong foothold for economic growth in later periods. This optimism is based on various efforts to improve the investment climate and accelerate infrastructure development by the Government as well as positive support from economic actors for the new government. Based on these assumptions, at that time Bank Indonesia predicted that GDP growth in 2005 would be able to reach 5% - 6%, with the CPI inflation rate estimated at 6% 1%. 5. In fact, efforts to strengthen the momentum of economic recovery i experienced quite significant obstacles, both externally and internally. From the external side, rising oil prices, slowing economic growth and world trade volume , as well as rising global interest rates have had a negative impact on developments. stability of the monetary economy. From the internal side, the handling of various structural problems, such as the infrastructure development acceleration program , which is still not optimal, also provides obstacles to the domestic economy. 6. The negative impact of external turmoil on economic stability in 2005 was reflected in the deteriorating development of the balance of payments, a weakening exchange rate and sharply increasing inflation. Indonesia's Balance of Payments (BOP) recorded a deficit of USD533 million, with the rupiah depreciating 8.6% and on average reaching Rp9,713 per USD, while CPI inflation increased to 17.11% (yoy). Nevertheless, overall economic growth in 2005 of 5.6% continued to show an increase compared to the previous year of 5.1%, which was mainly supported by economic performance. which was quite good in the quarter of 1-2005 by 6.12%. This is also due to the fact that the negative impact of the increase in world oil prices has only been transmitted significantly inthe real sector through the increase in domestic fuel prices in the quarter IV-2005. Dear Members of the Council, 7. Observing the pressures of macroeconomic stability, we are of the view that monetary policy, which tended to be tight during 2005, with minimal emphasis on sustainable growth, remains necessary. The policy is also intended as an anticipatory measure to prevent a persistent increase in inflation going forward. 8. In the quarter of 1-2005, monetary policy tended to be tight in the form of an indicative determination of base money growth for the whole year of about 11.5- 12.5%, lower than the realization of test growth date base money in the previous year, at 15.1%. In the quarter of 1-2005, the level of base money was maintained in the range of indicative estimates and was followed by the movement of the weighted average of the 1-month SBI which was relatively unchanged as it was still high excesses of banking liquidity. 9. In the quarter of 11-2005, in order to overcome the deteriorating condition of NPI which led to further weakening of the exchange rate, a tighter monetary policy was pursued by the absorption of liquidity in a more optimally, namely by maintaining the base money so that it can grow in line with the projected economic maxim and inflation target set by the Government. In addition, to reduce pressure on the rupiah, efforts to absorb excess liquidity were followed by a fairly high increase in the 1-month SBI interest rate, which was around 82bps compared quarter-triwulan before. Furthermore, in an effort to reduce excess liquidity in the banking industry and reduce the weakening of the rupiah exchange rate. Bank Indonesia also issued a rupiah exchange rate stabilisation package through PBI No.7/14/2005 concerning Restrictions on Rupiah Transactions and Foreign Exchange Credit Deposits by Banks that could reduce pressures on rupiah depreciation. from short-term foreign capital flows (especially in the form of buy swaps) because foreign exchange transactions with foreign parties that do not have a basis for economic transactions are reduced. at the same time. Bank Indonesia also continues to implement measured foreign exchange sterilization to reduce rupiah exchange rate volatility in the market. With the monetary policy that has been adopted, the inf Iasi pressure stemming from inflation expectations is relatively restrained in line with the increase in the SBI interest rate. Nevertheless, the rupiah stabilization package has not been fully able to withstand further rupiah depreciation, due to weak economic fundamentals and the US dollar strengthened against almost all of theworld's strong currencies . 10. Furthermore, in order to improve the effectiveness of monetary policy, in early July 2005 Bank Indonesia implemented measures to strengthen the monetary policy framework consistent with the Inflation Targeting Framework (ITF). This framework is characterized by the use of the Bl Rate as a monetary policy signal to replace the use of base money to make monetary policy signals more transparent. The implementation of this framework is believed to be able to improve the effectiveness and governance of monetary policy in achieving the ultimate goal of price stability to support sustainable economic growth and improving the welfare of society. 11. In the period July-December 2005, Bank Indonesia still considers it necessary to continue its strict moneter policy to keep the acceleration of rising inflation expectations from being excessive and may lead to its medium-term inflation target. This is because the planned increase in fuel prices has triggered an increase in inflation expectations which is quite strong. The policy was pursued by raising the Bl Rate gradually and measurably, 3 times during the fourth quarter of 2005 to reach 12.75% in early December 2005. This policy is strengthened by increasing the effectiveness of quality li management in the money market - among others by reactivating the Overnight (O/N) Fine Tune Contraction (FTK) instrument, increasing the Mandatory Demand Deposit Minimum (RR), raising the FASBI 7-day interest rate and maximum deposit guarantee rate-, stabilization efforts in the interbank money pa sar O/N and improving the interest rate structure. Meanwhile, in an effort to reduce rupiah depreciation pressures, several policies that had been adopted in the previous period were also strengthened by the ban on 'margin trading' on all foreign exchange, theavailability of investment swap facilities, the implementation of foreign exchange swap interventions, and the improvement of PDN provisions. 12. Apart from the monetary side, efforts to control inflation throughout 2005 were also accompanied by strengthening policy coordination with the Government through the Target Setting, Monitoring and Control Team. Inflation, in particular, minimizes the impact of rising inflation in terms of administered prices and volatile foods. Dear Members of the Council, 13. In the banking sector, banking performance until the end of FY 2005 was still quite good despite pressures on the macroeconomic balance. The banking intermediation function during 2005 was able to proceed as planned. Credit (including channeling) grew according to the target of reaching the range of 22.7%. On the other hand, the ability of banks to raise Third Party Funds also continued to experience moderate growth in the range of 15%. With the acceleration of credit growth that is higher than the growth of the third party fund (DPK) collection, the bank's LDR is until the end of the year. 2005 rose quite significantly to reach about 65%. The total assets of the banking industry also experienced almost as large growth as deposit growth of 12%. Bank profitability increased slightly as reflected in the Return on Asset (ROA) ratio increasing from 2.6% to 2.8%, while net interest income (Nil) rose from Rp5.9 trillion to IDR 6.2 trillion. With the improvement in profitability and not too much increase in loans, the capital adequacy ratio (CAR) also increased from 19.4% to 19.6%. This figure is the highest CAR compared to banking CAR in other Asian countries. 14. The banking performance is inseparable from the policies adopted by Bank Indonesia in the banking sector during 2005 which remained focused on strengthening banking system stability in order to create system stability. financial and encourages the intermediation function of banks. The policy is pursued through several steps, among others, through the implementation of programs that have been launched in the Indonesian Banking Architecture (API) in increasing the effectiveness of bank supervision and resilience banking system, regulatory regulation and banking supervision system aligned with the basic principles of basel as well as the implementation of good governance, risk management and effective and efficient internal control, as well as the development of banking human resources through thecertification of risk management. 15. To support the effective implementation of monetary policy and efforts to create a sound banking system, in the field of payment system, in 2005 Bank Indonesia continued to make various efforts improvements to implement an efficient, fast, secure, and reliable national payment system. In the field of cash payment systems, the policy is directed at efforts to meet the needs of kart a I in society in a sufficient nominal amount, the appropriate type of denomination, tep at time and in a condition worthy of circulation. Meanwhile, in the field of non-cash payment systems, policy measures are directed at efforts to reduce risk, increase payment system efficiency and consumer protection of users. payment system through the expansion of the implementation of the National Clearing System (SKN). 2. Follow-up Plan of Indonesian Banking Architecture Dear Members of the Council, 16. As is understandable, the Indonesian Banking Architecture (API) launched in early 2004 is aimed at realizing a healthy, strong and efficient banking system in order to create system stability finance in order to encourage national economic growth. We can reiterate that the API consists of 6 pillars, namely: - pillar I - Strengthening the National Banking Structure - Pillar 2 - Banking Regulatory Quality Improvement Program - Pillar 3 - Supervisory Function Improvement Program - Pillar 4- Banking Management and Operational Quality Improvement Program - pillar 5 - Banking Infrastructure Development Program - Pillar 6 - Customer Protection Improvement Program 17. Until the end of 2005, API has begun to give another color to the national banking system, both in terms of banking consolidation, partiality to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), an increase in the ability of banking human resources, infrastructure and customer protection. 18. In terms of banking consolidation, which is the Pillar 1 API program, Bank Indonesia has set the direction of banking consolidation policy through the regulation of Bank Indonesia on the Minimum Core Capital in force since July 1 , 2005 and the announcement of the criteria for good performance banks (BKB) and the criteria of anchor banks (anchor banks). In addition, it is also carried out to strengthen the institutional, financial and operational joints of the banking industry by improving the capital conditions of the national banking industry, the implementation of risk management, and governance. 19. We further realize that to create a healthy, strong and efficient banking industry in order to stability the financial system that is useful for national economic growth, it is necessary to close coordination with the Government, especially the financial department. On this occasion, we inform you that bl is currently conducting identification and diagnosis of tax incentives and banking regulatory incentives without eliminating the precautionary principle . This incentive is expected to be useful as a sweetener within the framework of accelerating banking consolidation. Furthermore, the special taxation of the banking industry in the context of mergers and consolidations is expected to provide added value in the future when the k-bank tires are produced mergers are able to increase economies of scale and encourage banks to be better able to compete in the era of globalization. 20. Meanwhile, partiality for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) is manifested in the form of financing programs to MSMEs through a linkage program between commercial banks and RURAL BANKS. The financing program is manifested in the form of announcing the direction of policy and signing a linkage program between several commercial banks and a number of rural banks. The policy direction of this program is expressed in the form of establishing a generic model of the linkage program in the form of a model of providing working capital (executing) and credit forwarding (chanelling) from commercial banks to rural banks as well as a joint financing model between commercial banks and rural banks. The success of the linkage program was marked, among others , by the signing of financing cooperation between 10 commercial banks and 38 rural banks worth IDR 103 billion, most of which were provision of working capital for rural banks. 21. Another form of increasing financing to MHMes is also realized by increasing access to banking credit through the establishment of regional credit guarantee schemes . This credit guarantee scheme involves Bank Indonesia as a facilitator, PT Askrindo, Regional Government, and Regional Development Bank and is intended to help MSMEs in the regions get convenience in obtaining credit from banking. Dear Councillors, 22. Within the framework of improving the process of formulating the direction of banking policy and regulation, through the program contained in the Pilar 2 API, we have taken the initiative to hold regular meetings with a panel of experts banking (expert panel). The meeting of the panel of banking experts aims to align the direction of banking policy carried out by Bank Indonesia with the development of economists and finance nationally and globally. For this reason, the composition of the panel of banking experts is structured in such a way that both domestic banking experts and foreign banking experts are represented in it. During 2005 , two banking expert panel meetings were held in January and December 2005. 23. We also inform you that on December 30, 2005 , a Joint Decree (SKB) was signed concerning the Establishment of the Financial System Stability Forum (FSSK). The establishment of the FinancialSystem Stability Committee is a means of cooperation, coordination and exchange of information in the context of creating and maintaining financial system stability, and is part of improved coordination program with other supervisory agencies which is a program of pillar 3 of api. 24. In line with the implementation of coordination with other supervisory agencies. Bl has also carried out internal consolidation in the form of reorganization of the banking sector at Bank Indonesia, especially the consolidation of supervision and inspection work units. With this consolidation, a dedicated organization will be created at the team level (dedicated team) where the supervisory and inspection functions currently carried out by different Task Forces will be unified so that it is hoped that coordination will increase and problems related to banking can be identified and resolved more quickly. Meanwhile, measures to improve the supporting infrastructure of bank supervision continue to be carried out through increasing the competence of Bank Supervision Human Resources, establishing Specialist Supervisors, improving bank supervision information technology and improving supervisory document management in Bl. 25. In relation to the program in Pillar 4 of the API to improve the quality of banking management and operations, on August 3, 2005, provisions on Risk Management Certification were issued for management and officials of commercial banks. In essence, this regulation aims to provide competency standards for management and officials of commercial banks in managing the risks faced in daily operational activities. This competency standard is important considering that the intermediation function carried out by banks requires adequate skills and expertise in managing the collection and distribution of funds so that the risks associated with the implementation of bank business activities can be anticipated and managed properly. 26. As an implementation of the risk management certification program, on December 5, 2005 for the first time, a level 1 risk management certification exam was held, attended by 1,635 participants from bank management. Of these, as many as 1,193 participants or 73% were declared to have passed the risk management certification exam. The obligation to have a risk management certificate for bank administrators and officials will be effective on August 3, 2010 and it will be one of the administrative requirements in the fit &proper test for the management and executive officers of commercial banks. 27. To support the development of a healthy banking industry. Bank Indonesia through Pillar 5 API seeks to complement supporting infrastructure, which among others is realized by refining the system and database regarding debtor performance information to improvethe quality of credit decisions made by banks. 28. The improvement of this system is carried out based on Bank Indonesia Regulation Number 7/8/PBI/2005 dated January 20, 2005 concerning the Debtor Information System. Basically, the improvement of dilakukan by expanding the scope of credit data provided to debtors which was originally only for credit with a nominal value of IDR 50 million and above to all credit given by the bank regardless of face value. In addition, the banks that are required to provide data to the Debtor Information System are also expanded to include RURAL BANKS that have total assets above IDR BILLION. Another important thing in this Debtor Information System is that each debtor customer will have a special identification number (debtor identification number) so that it will facilitate credit analysis that performed by a bank. Dear Councillors, 29. In terms of the relationship between banks and their customers, banking arrangements in Indonesia starting in 2005 experienced a new balance with the beginning of the coverage of aspects of customer protection and empowerment in Bank Indonesia Regulation. In the January 2005 policy package, 2 related provisions have been issued. The first provision is regarding transparency of bank product information and use of customer personal data. This provision came into effect on July 20, 2005 which in principle provides for: - the bank's obligation to provide complete, accurate, up-to-date and complete information regarding the characteristics of the products it offers - The use of customer personal data for the commercial benefit of other parties outside the bank's legal entity must be supported by the written consent of the customer concerned. It is intended to protect the personal rights of customers in addition to juga to reduce the negative impact of dissemination of customer personal data. 30. The second provision is regarding the Settlement of Customer Complaints, where the bank is obliged to resolve any complaints related to the potential financial losses of the customer within a certain period of time . To support this complaint resolution effort, banks are required to establish a special unit and or function of handling customer complaints at each bank office and submit quarterly reports on settlements customer complaints to Bank Indonesia. 31. Furthermore, Bank Indonesia realizes that efforts to resolve customer complaints by banks will not always be able to satisfy customers. After banks are required to establish units to handle customer complaints, Bank Indonesia is currently also pursuing the establishment of a Banking Mediation Institution as the expected institution can facilitate the settlement of disputes between customers and banks in a simple, cheap, and fast manner. 3. Development of banking intermediation through MSMEdevelopment Dear Councillors, 32. Micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in the national economy have an important and strategic role. In addition to the large number of industries and contained in every economic sector, MSMEs also have great potential in employment. Each unit of investment in the MSME sector can create more job opportunities when compared to the same investment in large businesses. Furthermore, in line with the conducive macroeconomics and the change in the banking paradigm in looking at MSMEs, in recent years there has been a change in banking business behavior. which is more towards the MSME segment. This condition is very different from the past era where the orientation of bank lending was too focused on corporations that were considered to provide large profits economically. Meanwhile, the MSME sector often experiences obstacles in obtaining access to funds and is often financed through government programs that tend to have subsidies or sources of funds relatively inexpensive from donors. 33. In line with the changes in banking business behavior, the development of MSME loans during 2005 shows that the net expansion of MSME loans has reached Rp86.3 trillion or 142.7% of t otal business plan banking for MSME loans in 2005 amounted to Rp60.4 trillion. Meanwhile, the share of MSME loans to bank loans in 2005 reached 51.0%, higher than the previous year's share of 48.5%. The increase is related to the government's support for MSME lending in line with the declaration of 2005 as the Year of Indonesian Microfinance . In addition, the increase in MSME lending cannot be separated from the role of Bank Partner Financial Consultants (KKMB) as a liaison between MSMEs and banks , which in a few years the latter was vigorously developed by the government. Dear Member De wan, 34. With the enactment of Law No.23/1999 concerning Bank Indonesia, Bank Indonesia's policy in assisting the development of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) has undergone a fairly basic paradigm shift. Bank Indonesia can no longer provide financial assistance or Bank Indonesia Liquidity Credit (KLBI), so the role of Bank Indonesia in developing MSMEs is indirect. The approach to MSMEs, especially the role of the central bank , has shifted from a developmental role to a promotional role. The approach that provides credit subsidies and low interest has shifted to an approach that is more than facilitation, promotion, research development, surveys and innovation. 35. With these conditions. Bank Indonesia continues to provide support, but Bank Indonesia's policy is focused more on improving the intermediation function of perbankan as well as to support a sound banking system. . Several policies of Bank Indonesia can be broadly divided into two, namely from the supply side, namely policies that are more related to the banking sector and from the demand side which is more related to the development of MSMEs. 36. From the supply side, Bl has issued several policies that encourage the development of MSMEs, including provisions regarding Small Business Loans which in principle are to encourage and encourage banks to me expand MSME loans; provisions on the Provision of Technical Assistance in the development of MSMEs, namely training for banks and accompanying institutions, as well as the provision of information that supports the development of MSMEs; and provisions regarding the business plan of commercial banks in disbursing MSME loans. In addition, regulations were also issued regarding the quality of productive assets, which for quality loans up to Rp.500 million (MSMEs) are only assessed from the accuracy of principal and interest payments, and the assessment of credit collateral up to Rp. 5 billion is sufficient for the bank's internal appraisal. Similarly, Bl gave special treatment to Commercial Bank Loans after the National Disaster in Aceh and North Sumatra, namely determining credit quality and providing other funds sd. Rp. 5 billion (MSMEs) is only based on the accuracy of principal and interest payments. 37. In addition to these provisions. Bl has also developed a BPR development strategy to support the sustainable growth of the BPR industry in order to be able to fulfill its function as a provider of financial services, especially to micro and small enterprises (MSEs). The preparation of the strategy cannot be separated from the fact that the development of MSME activities cannot be separated from the development of microfinance itself, especially rural banks considering that the main market segments of rural banks are micro-enterprises and small businesses. 38. In terms of demand, Bank Indonesia's policy is more focused on strengthening MSME companion institutions through increasing capacity building in the form of training and research activities that support the provision of credit to MSMEs. Some of the efforts made by a.I through trainings to MSME companion institutions, intermediation bazaar activities with the aim of bringing each other closer and improving communication between banks and MSMEs, the development of an Integrated Information System for Small Business Development (SIPUK) and the establishment of an SME Companion Development Center (P3UKM) as a pilot project in Bandung. 39. Furthermore, in order to accelerate the realization of banking loans to MSMEs, in the last two years and is also a strategy going forward. Bank Indonesia through cooperation with various parties seeks to make a breakthrough by cooperating with Swisscontact and IFC (International Finance Corporation) in establishing PEAC (Promoting Enterprise Access to Credit). Peac was established to increase credit flow from financial institutions to MSMEs by strengthening Business Development Services Providers (BDSP). Currently , PEAC Bromo has been established in Surabaya and PEAC Monas in Jakarta. In addition, cooperation with Swisscontact is also carried out to carry out the KasKu (Financial Access Coupon) program. 40. One of the obstacles faced by banks in financing MSMEs is that banks do not have sufficient information about MSMEs that have the potential to be financed, while on the other hand MSMEs are difficult to get information about perbankan products, especially those related to financing. Through this KasKu program, which in the early stages has only been implemented in West Java, banks participating in the KasKu program can access through the internet MSMEs that have the potential to be financed. For this, banks and msMEs who are prospective bank debtors pay a certain amount of fees. The assessment of MSMEs is carried out by BDSP which has been accredited by P3UKM. 9. Final words Dear Members of the Council, 41. Such are the honourable Mr. and Mrs. Board Members, our brief address regarding the performance evaluation and implementation of Bl's duties in 2005, the API follow-up plan and the development of banking intermediation through the development of MSMEs. Jakarta, March 14th, 2005

Pendahuluan Anggota Dewan yang terhormat, 1. Pertama-tama perkenankanlah kami menyampaikan terima kasih kepada Pimpinan dan Anggota Komisi XI DPR yang telah mengundang kami dalam Rapat Kerja pada hari ini. Bagi kami, pertemuan ini memiliki arti yang sangat penting terutama dalam rangka menyampaikan berbagai informasi dan penjelasan mengenai pelaksanaan tugas Bank Indonesia yang diamanatkan oleh Undang-undang sekaligus untuk mendapatkan berbagai masukan dari Anggota Dewan yang berguna bagi upaya perbaikan dalam pelaksanaan tugas kami di bidang moneter, perbankan, dan sistem pembayaran ke depan. Lebih dari itu, pertemuan semacam ini pada hakikatnya kami pandang sebagai salah satu bentuk perwujudan dari akuntabilitas Bank Indonesia kepada DPR-RI. 2. Sesuai dengan agenda yang kami peroleh, dalam Rapat Kerja kali akan dibahas mengenai Laporan kinerja dan pelaksanaan tugas Bl tahun 2005, Rencana tindak lanjut API serta Perkembangan intermediasi perbankan melalui UMKM. Dapat kami sampaikan bahwa topik pertama telah kami utarakan pada kesempatan Raker tanggal 20 Februari 2006 yang lalu.
