Soebandono and Mr. Bambang Sarengat;  Academic Senat of STIE IBS;  Founders of STIE IBS: o Mr. Burhanuddin Abdullah o Dr. Maman Soemantri o Dr. Siswanto o Dr. Muchlis  Managing Director and member of Board Directors of LPPI, Mr. Hartadi A. Sarwono;  Chairman of YPPI  Mr. Abdul Aziz and YPPI Board of Management  Managing Director of PT. Bank Mandiri (Persero), Tbk, Mr. Budi Gunadi Sadikin;  Chairman of ASBISINDO, Mr. Yuslam Fauzi;  Messrs. & Madam Managing Director, Board of Directors and Leadership of Banks and Financial Services;  Chairman of Indonesias Banker Association  Executive Director of LSPP;  Chairman of BARa;  Leadership of Pondok Pesantren Darunnajah, Madrasah Aliyah Negeri and Al Izhar Senior High School;  Academic Community of STIE IBS, Lecturers, Students;  Attendees and Invitees, Good Morning and Greetings to us all  First of all to start this morning meeting, allow me to ask you all to praise and thank God the Almighty, for His blessing we are able to gather here in a good atmosphere to have a friendly get-together and attend the Tenth Anniversary of STIE Indonesia Banking School (IBS);  We welcome various cooperation arranged in this event, as an effort of good collaboration between banking industry, educational institution, banking development institution, and other related institutions in order to enhance banking human resources leadership and managerial competence; Ladies and Gentlemen,  As a component in the economic system, the dynamic and performance of banking industry certainly cannot be separated from the dynamics of global and domestic economy. Even, this economic condition which eventually will forge banking leaders in formulating the best strategy, to maintain business continuity and bank profitability;  Together, we have witnessed how the fluctuation of global economic uncertainties in the half of last decade continuously creating new uncertainty pendulum. In the midst of the still weak domestic economic structure, drastic change of the world economic structure has provided quite significant additional pressure to the domestic economy;  The year 2013 was not an easy year for us all. The national economic activities indicated a deceleration with a growth lower than predicted previously. Nevertheless, amidst the world economic turbulence, we should be grateful that in year 2013 our economy was able to survive at a fairly high level with 5.78% growth, far above the average growth of peer countries at 3.6%. Ladies and Gentlemen,  If in 2013 the macroeconomic policy was directed to the effort of stabilization to support a healthy and balanced economic growth, in this year 2014 we have entered a different policy nuance, namely a policy and structural reform to sustainable economic growth. This is based on the global economic situation that is still surrounded by uncertainties and the still decelerating domestic economy.  Different from the previous prediction, the trend of recovery and the rate of economic growth inter-regions and inter-countries move with various acceleration. The economy of European countries finally is free from the shackles of recession, whereas USAs economy continues to show further strengthening of recovery momentum;  On the other hand, emerging markets economy especially China, is entering an acceleration phase as the impact of rebalancing of macro-economic policy. IMF has predicted that this trend of economic growth deceleration of China will continue, i.e. down to 7.5% from the previous of 7.7%. Even, some emerging market countries experience the increasing pressure of susceptibility increase indication, including risk of unsustainable current account balance and accumulation of increasing private sector overseas loans;  Such various developments certainly will highly influence the condition of financial market in the region. Pressures in the financial markets of several ASEAN countries continue to increase. In line with this, the pressure of Rupiah depreciation that had subsided in the Q1-2014 again experiences an increase, especially influenced by reposition of financial assets from emerging market related to the possibility of monetary stimulus adjustment by the Fed and sentiment to fiscal deficit and current account in the country. Ladies and Gentlemen,  We are aware that the challenges which need to be addressed are increasingly felt sooner or later. In my opinion, at this point our capability to read and anticipate this economic movement ahead is tested. The rapidity in responding to that challenge will affect our ability to maintain the continuity of growth;  We believe that process of economic adjustment still runs quite smoothly, although there are a number of risks that needs attention and watched out for. Therefore, anticipative policy needs to be focused to ensure that the inflation target can be achieved and the performance of current account remains controlled. With that consideration, Bank Indonesia decides to maintain the BI Rate at 7.5%, with interest rate of Lending Facility and interest rate of Deposit Facility respectively at 7.5% and 5.75%;  Further, to support that policy, Bank Indonesia will constantly strengthen the monetary policy mix and macro-prudential as well as the policy to strengthen domestic economic structure and Foreign Loans (ULN) management, especially corporations ULN. Besides, Bank Indonesia also will improve coordination the Government in controlling inflation and current account deficit. Ladies and Gentlemen, invitees and attendees,  Facing the hard challenges ahead that will have to be addressed by Indonesias economy, we consider that sharia financial industry, already proven to be immune to crisis, has the opportunity to take a bigger role in the national economy through its contribution to economic activities based on sharia principle;  Although the national economic problems also bring influences to sharia banking industry, we see that up to today the performance of sharia banking is still pretty good. Sharia banking services continue to grow bringing positive impact on the increase of the number of fund accounts in sharia banks from 10 million accounts in 2012 to 12 million accounts in 2013. Meanwhile, the ratio of financing to deposit (FDR) already at the level of 100% with financing priorities channeled to the financing of micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSME);  From the perspective of sharia banking industry, the challenges that currently arise, among others, are limitations of human resources both quality and quantity to support industry acceleration, limitations of product development and services of sharia financial services, and also optimization of sharia financial market development. Those challenges have a long term time dimension and require consistency of policy to face them;  With the transferring of sharia banks governance and supervision to OJK, it does not mean that Bank Indonesia has no role in the development of sharia financial industry. Bank Indonesia with its macro-prudential governance and supervision will conduct monitoring toward institutions or financial markets in order to maintain stability of the financial system, including institutions and financial markets based on sharia principle. Apart from that, Bank Indonesia also has interest to implement sharia-based monetary policy in maintaining economic stability.  The role of Bank Indonesia in sharia financial development will be conducted through the regulation of money market and various funding instruments of financial institution liquidity management, such as sharia-based inter-banks repo transactions;  Besides, Bank Indonesia will conduct harmonization and coordination of policy inter-authorities more closely and improve socialization & education to stakeholders that is more integrated, among others through the implementation of Sharia Economic Movement. Ladies and Gentlemen, invitees and attendees,  Such various challenges need to be examined in line with the approaching commitment of ASEAN Economic Community (AEC) in 2015. On one hand, the AEC commitment will open more liberal market opportunities with the flow of goods, services, investments, manpower and capital. On the other hand, however, this will also provide consequences of higher competition in the domestic markets of the respective country;  With the massive market potential, I see that the most fundamental substance from the AEC commitment is our ability to create a competitive competitiveness. Are we able to utilize AEC as the main actor in the global production chain, or we just become the market target and marginalized? In my opinion, at this point our capabilities to read and anticipate the economic movement ahead will be tested. Survivors arent always the strongest; theyre the smartest;  In this condition, bankers should equip themselves as best as possible so as to have high professionalism and competitiveness in order not to become second class bankers. We must be able to show that Indonesian bankers are the best in ASEAN region by becoming professional bankers and their competence, expertise and professionalism are accounted for by the neighboring countries;  Currently, Indonesias economic scale dominates 40% of the ASEAN countries economy, with a total population of approximately 50% from the total ASEAN population. But certainly, this demands various revamping that need to be met, such as the existence of structural reform;  We notice there are at least 3 (three) structural challenges that needs to get priorities immediately. First, basic capital of development such as infrastructure of physical and digital connectivity, human resources, and capacity of technology application, and also business climate and institutional that requires further strengthening. Second, the condition of real sector that still requires increased competitiveness and reliability from the production perspective. Third, financing of development that is still not optimal resulted from domestic financial market that is still not deep;  To respond to the structural challenge, it requires a structural reform policy that focuses on three main pillars, i.e. (i) self-reliance of domestic economy, (ii) competitiveness of industrial sector, and (iii) continuity of development financing. Ladies and Gentlemen, invitees and attendees,  In line with the policy on structural reform and preparation in facing the approaching formation of AEC, we observe that consolidation of various institutions engaging in financial sector and educational industry have important roles to enhance competitiveness, especially from the perspective of banking human resources quality;  Various institutions contribute actively in the development of knowledge, skill, and attitude of the human resources of banking and financial services, in order to support the realization of quality banking industry;  Cooperation inter-institutions both locally and abroad that have good reputations is an integrative and synergic effort that must constantly be developed in improving quality human resources development. However, we believe that knowledge and skills realized by mastering the standard of competence and expertise will not be meaningful without good integrity, for banking business is a business of trust. Ladies and Gentlemen, invitees and attendees,  Finally, we would like to congratulate STIE Indonesia Banking School for its Tenth Anniversary. Hopefully the positive collaboration that has been arranged in this years event is able to boost the creation of qualified human resources development system and to provide equipment of managerial competence and leadership in order to enhance the resilience and competitiveness of the banking industry;  Hopefully our good intentions to build a nation and state through the development of quality banking human resources that has integrity will constantly be blessed by God the Almighty. Thank you! Jakarta, June 2014 Ronald Waas

Title: Opening Remarks by Ronald Waas Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia at Pilot Project of Less Cash Society (LCS) Area (University of Indonesia, Jakarta 2 October 2013)
text: OPENING REMARKS DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF BANK INDONESIA AT PILOT PROJECT OF LESS CASH SOCIETY (LCS) AREA, AT UNIVERSITAS INDONESIA Jakarta, 2 October 2013 Honorable, Vice-Rector of Universitas Indonesia, Mr. Dr. Adi Zakaria Affif Talk Show Resource Persons, - Mrs. Rosmaya Hadi, Executive Director of Payment System Policy Department, Bank Indonesia - Mr. Budi Gunadi Sadikin, Managing Director of Bank Mandiri and also former Chairman of Indonesias Payment System Association (ASPI) - Mr. Suwignyo Budiman, Director of BCA - Mr. Faisal Basri, Economist and Academician of Universitas Indonesia - and Mrs. Niniek L. Karim, as moderator Academic Community of Universitas Indonesia Invitees, Media Partners, and Audiences Good Morning and Greetings to us all  First, lets praise the God Almighty, for His blessing we are able to gather here in a healthy condition and good atmosphere for the Seminar (Talk Show) of Less Cash Society at Universitas of Indonesia with topic of Opportunities and Challenges in Realizing Less Cash Society.  I happily welcome the organizing of this Talk Show, which constitutes part of a series of Trials of Less Cash Society Area at Universitas Indonesia. This talk show naturally becomes a meeting event and important discussion for the development of Less Cash Society in Indonesia. Todays discussion also becomes more complete and sharp, due to the presence of Resources from various background representing the Regulator (Mrs. Maya), Industrial Association (represented by Mr. Budi G. Sadikin), Banking Practitioner (Mr. Suwignyo), Economic and Politic Observer and also academician (Mr. Faisal Basri), and Mrs. Ninik L. Karim who is certainly familiar looking to all of us. Ladies and Gentlemen,  At present we together are witnessing how the change in the global economic order has impacted the space and vision of various entities, both in financial and non-financial institutions. The Government and Bank Indonesia as the central bank are also not immune to the changes.  Such thing becomes more real following the adjustment of domestic economic fundamental condition that we are currently experiencing. This condition naturally needs proactive response from all of us, especially Bank Indonesia as the Monetary Authority, Banking and Payment System.  First is the importance of awareness on the roles of financial system stability, monetary stability, and payment system that is secure, efficient, and smooth in supporting the sustainability of economic growth. This brings consequences on the more strategic mixture of the three policies in guarding Indonesias economy.  Second, the role of central bank that becomes increasingly critical amidst the change of business needs that increasingly widespread, the rapid technological development and product innovation, up to the increasingly complex payment instruments. Bank Indonesia as the Payment System Authority is required to direct the industry so as to move efficiently; to encourage climate that is conducive for payment system and settlement of financial transactions; and also to strengthen consumers protection by maintaining the principle of leaning toward the national interest, namely providing access that is more extensive and reachable for all people.  Changes and challenges that we encounter, of course must be addressed with the strengthening of human resources capability in every sectors and industry. In my point of view, at this point our capability to read and anticipate economic movement for the future is further tested. Distinguished Attendees,  Technological development should provide added values for all of us, especially in making transactions. It is time for us all to utilize this technological development by willing to make transactions electronically; currently all transactions are real time, borderless. Using electronic transactions also support economic growth of a country.  Bank Indonesia in cooperation with the industry strives to motivate the society to perform transactions electronically or non-cash to realize Less Cash Society.  There are three fundamental advantages from less cash society. First, EASE, whereas non-cash transactions are easier as everyone does not need to bother carrying cash everywhere in performing business transactions. Second, EFFICIENT, as non-cash transactions are relatively not costly. Money management, starting from money printing, distribution, to its destruction requires high cost. Third, SAFE, non-cash transaction is easier to be traced if a criminal offence is occurred and it minimizes the risk of counterfeit money, although currently its ratio is still very low, i.e. only 5 pieces of counterfeit money from 1 million bills UYD (money in circulation), decreasing compared to year 2012 of 8 pieces of counterfeit money from 1 million bills UYD.  Currently, there are quite many media provided by the industry to perform transactions electronically, among others, started from credit cards, ATM/Debit cards, and finally electronic money. Until now the utilization of e-money is relatively still low, as it is the most current being introduced to the society, i.e. below 3%, with the average nominal usage up to July 2013 amounting to Rp7 billion/month. Moreover, its utilization is still concentrated in certain areas, although its potential is still very high.  Therefore, this trial is one of the efforts to promote the use of Electronic Money to the society. We expect this series of activities will provide direct experiences in using electronic money so that it can create a custom in transacting afterwards; provide education of electronic money so that the society are drawn to using it; and increase the use of electronic money in payment of transactions.  The selection of UI as a prototype certainly also by taking into account the large potential market, i.e. with a population up to 60,000 people. With such large population, I hope that daily activities of employees, students and the surrounding community who using cards also can be integrated with modes of transport, i.e. Trains, so that with just one card they can perform various types of transactions. Ladies and Gentlemen,  The realization of this less cash society naturally is an effort from various parties. From regulation perspective, Bank Indonesia has issued several regulations, especially in Payment Instrument Using Cards and Electronic Money. In the near future, we also will issue a regulation concerning protection to consumers. From media perspective, I think electronic money products issued already varies and innovative. Thanks to BCA, Mandiri, Permata, CIMB Niaga, BRI, BNI, that are willing to participate in this activity.  I also would like to express my appreciation to the Rector, and all Academic Community of Universitas Indonesia for their willingness to support this program, which will be replicated in various universities in Indonesia. Yogyakarta, Bandung, Surabaya should become the next targets.  Considering that from the perspectives of regulations and products have already been fulfilled, the next question for all of us is why the utilization of electronic money in the society is still relatively low, i.e. below 3%. Maybe, it is about time for us to sit down and study the behavior of consumers, and find out what can make them willing to use Electronic Money. Therefore, this activity should not only be directed to communicate Electronic Money, but at once as feedbacks in understanding the actual needs of consumers. Banking is no longer somewhere they go, its something they do, changes of consumers behavior are very fast, not like before; this is the time for us all to get on board or get out of the way.  So, Thank You, and Enjoy the Discussion! Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Ronald Waas

Title: Pidato Deputi Gubernur Senior : Kebijakan Bank Indonesia Dalam Mendorong Kredit Agro Bisnis
text: (c)I KEYNOTE SPEECH BY SENIOR DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF BANK INDONESIAI "BANK INDONESIA POLICY IN ENCOURAGING AGRO-BUSINESS CREDIT" Dear: Rector Ul Prof. Dr. Gumilar R. Somantri, Sdr. Dr. Ruslan Prijadi, Head of Postgraduate Program in Management llmu FEU I, Sdri. Dr. Rofikoh Rokhim, economist of Bisnis Indonesia daily, The Invitees and Panelists I honor, as well as Happy ladies and gentlemen, Good morning and greetings to all of us, First of all, let us give thanks to the presence of God Almighty who has given His grace and gift to all of us, so that on this happy morning we can gather in a scientific meeting, namely "The 3rd MRC Doctoral Journey in Management, which was held in collaboration with the Faculty of Economics Ul, especially the Management Research Center (MRC) of the Postgraduate Program in Management and The Daily Business of Indonesia. With the theme ''Optimizing Local Resources for Competitiveness", this Journey or scientific meeting in my opinion is an important vehicle for exchanging information and seeking scientific breakthroughs in the realm of management science, in order to improve the competitiveness of this nation in the future. For me, the theme of this meeting is also a strategic momentum. The issue of the competitiveness of this nation should indeed become a serious concern for all of us, especially those of you who are present here, who in fact have above-average intellectual provisions (with the doctoral and master's degrees owned). As we know, from the 2007-2008 Global Competitive Index report, Indonesia's ranking still has not moved from 54th, still the same as the previous year's report (2006-2007). For the ASEAN region, we are still better than Vietnam (68), the Philippines (71), or Cambodia (110), but still far below Singapore (7), Malaysia (21), or Thailand (28). I'm sure we're all very aware, that with the resources and potential we have, we are actually capable and deserving of being ranked much better. Nevertheless, I will not talk about such efforts to increase competitiveness on this day. In accordance with the request in the committee's invitation to the Governor of Bank Indonesia, which I represent, I will give a presentation on Bank Indonesia Policy in Encouraging Agro-Business Credit. Before moving further into the topic, allow me to begin by giving a glimpse of the latest developments in our economy. Happy brothers, GENERAL ECONOMIC ASSESSMENT As we all understand, our economy is currently facing several challenges stemming from global economic uncertainty. The three factors influencing the uncertainty are first related to the prospect of declining world economic growth. The IMF in the April 2008 WEO revised down its 2008 global economic growth outlook from 4.2% to 3.7%. As we know, the global economic slowdown was triggered by the impact of the accumulated subprime mortgage problem in the US which then through the "wealth effect" channel has reduced the US and global economy. The second is stemming from the increased vulnerability of global financial markets. This vulnerability is partly influenced by the impact of declining financial market investor confidence in the global economic growth prospects, which further affects the development of global commodity prices. The third is related to the high price of global commodities, both energy commodities and food commodities, in line with the phenomenon of climate change which has serious impacts and policy implications for future global economic developments. Oil prices are still quite high when compared to the end of 2007 of 95/barrel, although currently it has begun to decline in the range of US118/barrel in line with weakening demand from developed countries. Meanwhile, the prices of food commodities such as rice, corn, CPO and wheat are also relatively high. These unfavorable global conditions disrupted economic performance, especially in 2008. Economic growth in 2008 is expected to be in the range of 6% or slightly lower than initially estimated. Meanwhile, with annual inflation as of July 2008 reaching 11.90%, as well as taking into account several risk factors and inflationary pressures that will still arise, we expect CPI inflation at the end of this year to be in the range of 11.5%-12.5% (y-o-y). In relation to these inflationary pressures, our latest observations indicate that there are still risks of future inflationary pressures that need to be responded to with appropriate policies. The inflation risk is related to the impact of the turmoil in world oil and food prices as well as domestic demand pressures. This risk was considered by Bank Indonesia 2 days ago to raise the Bl Rate by 25 bps to 9%. In order to further streamline monetary policy, the increase in the Bl Rate is also accompanied by the optimization of the use of other monetary policy instruments such as controlling exchange rate volatility and absorbing excess liquidity through Open Market Operations (OPT). Thus, it is expected that inflation next year in the range of 6.5%-7.5% can be achieved. Meanwhile, on the banking side, industrial resilience was maintained, supported by the implementation of a good intermediation function, although there was little pressure in the real sector. Bank loans still grew 31.6% (y-o-y) with NPLs declining to 4.08% (gross) and CAR levels at 16.4%. Meanwhile, foreign exchange reserves, until the end of July 2008 reached USD60.56 billion or equivalent to 4.7 months of imports and servicing government external debt. Happy audience, BANK INDONESIA'S ROLE IN ENCOURAGING AGRO-BUSINESS LOANS Moving on from the journey of our economy in the past year, as well as the high global uncertainty today, one important lesson that can be drawn in efforts to strengthen the national economy in the future is the importance of appropriate and responsive strategies in the management and development of the agricultural sector in order to have better resilience. The increasing resilience of the agricultural sector not only encourages the agricultural sector to be able to absorb the risks of the impact of global price increases as it is today, but can also contribute strategically to increasing the potential for future economic growth. I am sure that all of us present here agree on this, especially the geographical characteristics and natural resources we have to support efforts to strengthen this agricultural sector. Nevertheless, indeed, the challenges in the agricultural sector faced in plain sight are still quite heavy. Allow me to express these challenges, which I quote from what was conveyed by Mr. Bayu Krisnamurthi, Deputy Coordinating Minister for The Economy for Agriculture and Marine Affairs in a seminar a few days ago (Kompas, August 6, 2008): ? To restore the carrying capacity of the north coast of Java as the basic infrastructure of national agriculture, a long-term reinvestment of around RplOO trillion is needed for the next 5-10 years; ? The same investment is also needed for the opening of agricultural areas outside Java; ? For this reason, in addition to a multi-year budget, it is also a multi-commitment from the government (which changes every 5 years) as a provider of agricultural infrastructure; ? Investments are needed to repair weir, build irrigation networks, and improve human resources (PU Department data: 50 out of 106 weir in the country are in a damaged condition); ? Local governments are also expected to be committed to allocating adequate budgets to the agricultural sector; ? Land productivity in Indonesia is still low. Of the 7.4 million hectares of land, it can only be planted 1.6 times a year, which indicates a low cropping index. The brothers I respect, From the picture above, we can see that the provision of agricultural infrastructure is a very important aspect and cannot be delayed. Of course, this is the responsibility of the Government with the support of high commitment and the provision of an adequate budget. On the other hand, we see that in general business actors in the agro-business industry (especially medium and large-scale ones) have no difficulty in obtaining financing from banks. This can be seen from the data on bank loans to the agricultural sector which grew rapidly over the past year (June 2007-2008), reaching 30.7%. In credit statistics at Bank Indonesia, the agricultural sector is divided into 8 sub-sectors, namely food crops, plantation crops, fisheries, animal husbandry, forestry and logging, hunting, agricultural facilities, and others. However, if you look further, this rapid growth turned out to only occur in large-scale loans while MSME loans which include micro (up to Rp50 million), small (Rp50 million - Rp500 million), and medium (Rp500 million - Rp5 billion) loans channeled to the agricultural sector only grew 20% during the same period. The development of credit to the agricultural sector is suspected to be the influence of the increase in agricultural commodity prices in the international market that has occurred over the past almost 2 years, which has encouraged a surge in the expansion of lending to large debtors in the agricultural sector. With regard to this condition, I would like to remind the banking community that the "euphoria" of lending to this rising sector does not come at the expense of the principles of prudential banking and environmental sustainability, considering that the largest portion of the credit is taken by large debtors. Returning to the role of Bank Indonesia in this sector, I need to emphasize that since the enactment of Law No. 23/1999 concerning Bank Indonesia (as amended by Law No.3/2004), Bank Indonesia's policy in supporting the improvement of the business climate or the real sector has undergone fundamental changes. The change is that Bank Indonesia can no longer provide financial assistance or liquidity credit directly as in the past, but the assistance provided is more indirect, among others through regulation and facilitation in strategic roles. In other words, Bank Indonesia does not specifically design a policy in the field of credit sectorally. Bank Indonesia's policy is directed towards supporting the development of MSMEs, especially those based on superior commodities, so that they can be financed by the banking industry. The policy is outlined in the form of regulations (provisions) and the provision of technical assistance (especially through banking) as well as cooperation with stakeholders (departments, donor agencies and institutions related to the empowerment of MSMEs). In this cross-sectoral policy, there are activities that seek to support the development of the agribusiness sector. In general, if I may say that "we no longer give fish, but give hooks". What are the "hooks"? Let's take a look at it one by one 1. Indonesian Business Data and Information (DIBI) DIBI presents website-based data and information and can be accessed through the Bank Indonesia ( ) website. The information presented in the DIBI is based on research conducted by Bank Indonesia, including data and information on regional economic potential, potential export commodities, and lending models for agribusiness commodities. 2. MsME lending model Bank Indonesia conducts research on the pattern of financing/lending models of various commodities that have the potential tobe financed by banks. Currently, there are 88 conventional financing patterns and 21 Sharia financing patterns, most of which are for agribusiness commodities. 3. MSME Development through Cluster Development This program is designed to develop MSMEs through an integrated cluster model from upstream to downstream. MSMEs will benefit from cooperation with medium and large businesses that act as local champions in a large business community. In 2007, the development of leading commodity clusters was carried out in 6 areas of Bank Indonesia Offices, including seaweed, emping melinjo, paprika, and opak commodities. This program is carried out in collaboration with various stakeholders in the regions, both local government and banks and related agencies. 4. Research on Partnership Patterns This study aims to see various patterns of partnership between Medium Enterprises / Large Enterprises and MSMEs in order to potentially increase accessto redit to banks. In the partnership, medium and large businesses can act as recommendations, avalis and also provide cash collateral guarantees for MSMEs who are partners in the partnership business relationship. The agribusiness sector is one of the sectors that is heavily involved in partnership relationships with medium and large enterprises. 5. Core-Plasma Development Program Bank Indonesia has long been (sejak before the 1999 Bl Law) financing Core Plasma activities, especially for palm oil commodities with Bank Indonesia Liquidity Credit . Currently, even though there is no financing with the Financial System stability Committee, Bank Indonesia is still paying attention to the process of stockpilingthe core-plasma relationship, especially with various post-reform social problems. Bank Indonesia acts as a mediator for conflicts of interest from various parties involved in the core-plasma program. This model of solving the dal am problemof core-plasma relationship in palm oil commodities is expected to be a guide in the partnership relationship between core and plasma in the future. In addition, in order to encourage the provision of plantation loans with this plasma core pattern, Bank Indonesia has relaxed the provisions on the Maximum Credit Limit, namely the provision of credit with a plasma core partnership pattern where core companies that guarantee credit to plasma are excluded from the definition of borrowers, as stated inmoney in PBI No. 7/3/PBI/2005 concerning the Maximum Limit of Commercial Bank Credit Provision. 6. Facilitation of Regional Economic Acceleration and Empowerment This program is an effort by Bank Indonesia to develop the regional economy, especially the real sector, which is still felt to be hampered by its development. Bank Indonesia through its network of Bank Indonesia Offices is moving to support various programs from agencies/agencies that are still felt to be hampered by financing by banks in the regions. We hope that Bank Indonesia's role in it can more or less facilitate the financing of activity projects in the regions. Some of the activities that have been carried out include supporting the revitalization of plantations/agriculture such as oil palm and rubber, as well as financing for vanilla, jagung, rice, seaweed, oranges, cane sugar and others. Through the various efforts made by Bank Indonesia, namely by taking the role of regulator and facilitator, we hope that improvements in the real sector can run more efficientlyand significantly. However, of course, the efforts we make still require criticism and suggestions for improvement and improvement, besides of course we need support from all parties concerned and care about efforts toimprove the business climate which in general is still far from satisfactory. Happy audience, RECOMMENDATIONS AND STEPS FORWARD Entering the final part of this speech, I hope that the government and other policy authorities need to evaluate, coordinate policies, and breakthrough efforts, both in terms of regulation and reorientation of achieving goals that are more focused on the welfare of the people by encouraging the creation of a conducive investment climate in the real sector, especially the agricultural sector. It is also necessary to have policies in the agricultural sector with a clear scale of priorities and implementation stages, so that agro-business actors can be more accurate in making decisions in a predictable business environment. I also hope that the scientific forum initiated by FEU I can help find breakthroughs that are beneficial for efforts to optimize the resources we have in order to increase the competitiveness of the nation, efforts and of course the competitiveness of each of us as individuals in this era of globalization and borderless world. Happy living your journey , that's it and thank you. I Presented on The 3rd MRC Doctoral Journey in Management in conjunction with The 1st Master Journey in Management, with the theme "Optimizing Local Resources for Competitiveness", a collaboration between FEUI and Bisnis Indonesia daily, Thursday, August 7, 2008 in Jakarta. --------------- ------------------------------------------------------------ --------------- ------------------------------------------------------------
text_original: (c)I KEYNOTE SPEECH DEPUTI GUBERNUR SENIOR BANK INDONESIAI "KEBIJAKAN BANK INDONESIA DALAM MENDORONG KREDIT AGRO BISNIS" Yth: Rektor Ul Prof. Dr. Gumilar R. Somantri, Sdr. Dr. Ruslan Prijadi, Ketua Program Pascasarjana llmu Manajemen FEU I, Sdri. Dr. Rofikoh Rokhim, economist harian Bisnis Indonesia, Para Undangan dan Panelis yang saya muliakan, serta Hadirin sekalian yang berbahagia, Selamat pagi dan salam sejahtera bagi kita semua, Pertama-tama marilah kita panjatkan puji syukur kehadirat Tuhan Yang Maha Kuasa yang telah memberikan rahmat dan karuniaNya kepada kita semua, sehingga pada pagi yang berbahagia ini kita dapat berkumpul dalam pertemuan ilmiah, yaitu "The 3rd MRC Doctoral Journey in Management, yang terselenggara atas kerjasama Fakultas Ekonomi Ul, khususnya Management Research Center (MRC) Program Pascasarjana llmu Manajemen dan Harian Bisnis Indonesia. Dengan tema ''Optimizing Local Resources for Competitiveness", Journey atau temu ilmiah ini menurut hemat saya merupakan wahana yang penting untuk bertukar informasi dan mencari terobosan ilmiah dalam ranah ilmu manajemen, guna meningkatkan daya saing bangsa ini ke depan. Bagi saya, tema pertemuan ini juga merupakan momentum yang strategis. Isu daya saing bangsa ini memang selayaknya semakin menjadi perhatian serius kita semua, terlebih lagi anda yang hadir disini, yang notabene memiliki bekal intelektual di atas rata-rata (dengan titel doktor dan master yang dimiliki). Sebagaimana kita ketahui, dari laporan Global Competitive Index 2007-2008, peringkat Indonesia masih belum beranjak dari peringkat 54, masih sama dengan report tahun sebelumnya (2006-2007). Untuk kawasan ASEAN, kita memang masih lebih baik dari Vietnam (68), Filipina (71), atau Kamboja (110), namun masih jauh di bawah Singapura (7), Malaysia (21), atau Thailand (28). Saya yakin kita semua sangat sadar, bahwa dengan sumber daya dan potensi yang kita miliki, sesungguhnya kita mampu dan layak berada di peringkat yang jauh lebih baik. Namun demikian, saya tidak akan berbicara tentang upaya peningkatan daya saing tersebut pada hari ini. Sesuai permintaan dalam undangan panitia kepada Gubernur Bank Indonesia yang saya wakili, saya akan memberikan paparan tentang Kebijakan Bank Indonesia dalam Mendorong Kredit Agro Bisnis. Sebelum beranjak lebih jauh ke topik tersebut, perkenankan saya untuk mulai dengan menyampaikan sekilas perkembangan terakhir perekonomian kita. Saudara-saudara yang berbahagia, ASESMEN PEREKONOMIAN SECARA UMUM Sebagaimana kita pahami bersama, perekonomian kita saat ini sedang menghadapi beberapa tantangan yang bersumber dari ketidakpastian perekonomian global. Tiga faktor yang mempengaruhi ketidakpastian itu pertama terkait dengan prospek pertumbuhan ekonomi dunia yang menurun. IMF pada WEO April 2008 merevisi prospek pertumbuhan ekonomi global tahun 2008 dari 4,2% menjadi 3,7%. Sebagaimana kita ketahui, perlambatan ekonomi global ini dipicu oleh dampak akumulasi permasalahan subprime mortgage di AS yang kemudian melalui jalur "wealth effect" telah menurunkan perekonomian AS dan global. Kedua bersumber dari peningkatan kerentanan pasar keuangan global. Kerentanan ini antara lain dipengaruhi juga oleh dampak menurunnya keyakinan investor pasar keuangan terhadap prospek pertumbuhan ekonomi global, yang selanjutnya mempengaruhi perkembangan harga komoditas global. Ketiga terkait dengan harga komoditas global baik komoditas energi maupun komoditas pangan yang masih tinggi, sejalan dengan fenomena climate change yang memberikan dampak dan implikasi kebijakan yang serius bagi perkembangan ekonomi global ke depan. Harga minyak masih cukup tinggi jika dibandingkan akhir 2007 sebesar $95/barel, meski saat ini sudah mulai menurun pada kisaran US118/barrel seiring melemahnya permintaan dari negara maju. Sementara harga komoditi pangan seperti beras, jagung, CPO dan gandum juga relatif pada level yang tinggi. Berbagai kondisi global yang kurang menguntungkan tersebut mengganggu kinerja perekonomian terutama pada tahun 2008. Pertumbuhan ekonomi pada 2008 diperkirakan pada kisaran 6% atau sedikit menurun dibandingkan perkiraan awal. Sementara inflasi, dengan inflasi tahunan per Juli 2008 yang mencapai 11,90%, serta memperhitungkan beberapa faktor risiko serta tekanan inflasi yang masih akan timbul, kami memprakirakan inflasi IHK pada akhir tahun ini akan berada pada kisaran 11,5%-12,5% (y-o-y). Terkait dengan tekanan inflasi ini, pengamatan terakhir kami mengindikasikan masih adanya risiko tekanan inflasi ke depan yang perlu direspon dengan kebijakan yang tepat. Risiko inflasi tersebut terkait dengan dampak gejolak harga minyak dan pangan dunia tersebut serta tekanan permintaan dalam negeri. Risiko tersebut menjadi pertimbangan Bank Indonesia 2 hari yang lalu untuk kembali menaikkan Bl Rate sebesar 25 bps menjadi 9%. Agar lebih mengefektifkan kebijakan moneter, kenaikan Bl Rate juga diiringi optimalisasi penggunaan instrumen kebijakan moneter lain seperti pengendalian volatilitas nilai tukar dan penyerapan ekses likuiditas melalui Operasi PasarTerbuka (OPT). Dengan demikian diharapkan inflasi tahun depan pada kisaran 6,5%-7,5% dapat dicapai. Sementara di sisi perbankan, ketahanan industri masih terjaga dengan didukung pelaksanaan fungsi intermediasi yang baik, meski terdapat sedikit tekanan di sektor riil. Kredit perbankan masih tumbuh 31,6% (y-o-y) dengan NPL yang menurun menjadi 4,08% (gross) dan level CAR pada 16,4%. Sementara cadangan devisa, hingga akhir Juli 2008 mencapai USD60,56 miliar atau setara 4,7 bulan impor dan pembayaran utang luar negeri pemerintah. Hadirin yang berbahagia, PERAN BANK INDONESIA DALAM MENDORONG KREDIT AGRO BISNIS Beranjak dari perjalan perekonomian kita satu tahun terakhir ini, serta masih tingginya ketidakpastian global dewasa ini, satu pelajaran penting yang dapat ditarik dalam upaya memperkuat perekonomian nasional ke depan adalah pentingnya strategi yang tepat dan responsif dalam pengelolaan dan pengembangan sektor pertanian agar semakin memiliki ketahanan yang baik. Ketahanan sektor pertanian yang semakin baik tidak hanya mendorong sektor pertanian untuk akan dapat menyerap risiko dampak kenaikan harga global seperti terjadi dewasa ini, namun juga dapat berkontribusi strategis pada peningkatan potensi pertumbuhan ekonomi ke depan. Saya yakin bahwa kita semua yang hadir disini sepakat akan hal ini, apalagi karakteristik geografis dan sumber daya alam yang kita miliki mendukung upaya memperkuat sektor pertanian ini. Namun demikian, memang, tantangan di sektor pertanian yang dihadapi di depan mata masih cukup berat. Izinkan saya untuk mengungkapkan tantangan tersebut, yang saya kutip dari apa yang disampaikan oleh Bp. Bayu Krisnamurthi, Deputi Menko Perekonomian Bidang Pertanian dan Kelautan dalam sebuah seminar beberapa hari yang lalu (Kompas, 6 Agustus 2008): ? Untuk mengembalikan daya dukung pantai utara Jawa sebagai infrastruktur dasar pertanian nasional, dibutuhkan reinvestasi jangka panjang sekitar RplOO triliun untuk 5-10 tahun ke depan; ? Investasi yang sama juga diperlukan untuk pembukaan wilayah pertanian di luar Jawa; ? Untuk itu selain diperlukan anggaran multi-tahun, juga multi-komitmen dari pemerintah (yang berganti tiap 5 tahun) sebagai penyedia infrastruktur pertanian; ? Investasi diperlukan untuk memperbaiki bendung, membangun jaringan irigasi, dan membenahi SDM (data Departemen PU: 50 dari 106 bendung di tanah air dalam kondisi rusak); ? Pemerintah daerah pun diharapkan komitmennya untuk mengalokasikan anggaran yang memadai kepada sektor pertanian; ? Produktivitas lahan di Indonesia masih rendah. Dari 7,4 juta hektar lahan, hanya dapat ditanami 1,6 kali dalam setahun, yang menunjukkan indeks pertanaman yang rendah. Saudara-saudara yang saya hormati, Dari gambaran tadi, kita dapat melihat bahwa penyediaan infrastruktur pertanian menjadi aspek yang sangat penting dan tidak dapat ditunda-tunda. Tentunya hal ini menjadi tanggung jawab Pemerintah dengan didukung komitmen tinggi dan penyediaan anggaran yang memadai. Di sisi lain, kami melihat bahwa secara umum pelaku usaha di industri agro bisnis (terutama yang berskala menengah dan besar) tidak mengalami kesulitan dalam memperoleh pembiayaan dari perbankan. Hal ini terlihat dari data kredit perbankan ke sektor pertanian yang tumbuh pesat selama setahun terakhir (Juni 2007-2008), yakni mencapai 30,7%. Dalam data statistik perkreditan di Bank Indonesia, sektor pertanian dibagi ke dalam 8 sub-sektor, yakni tanaman pangan, tanaman perkebunan, perikanan, peternakan, kehutanan dan pemotongan kayu (logging), perburuan, sarana pertanian, dan lainnya. Namun jika ditelaah lebih jauh, pertumbuhan yang pesat tersebut ternyata hanya terjadi pada kredit berskala besar sedangkan kredit UMKM yang meliputi kredit mikro (s.d. Rp50 juta), kecil (Rp50 juta - Rp500 juta), dan menengah (Rp500 juta - Rp5 miliar) yang disalurkan ke sektor pertanian hanya tumbuh 20% selama periode yang sama. Perkembangan kredit ke sektor pertanian ini ditengarai merupakan pengaruh kenaikan harga komoditas pertanian di pasar internasional yang terjadi selama hampir 2 tahun terakhir, yang mendorong lonjakan ekspansi penyaluran kredit ke debitur besar di sektor pertanian. Berkenaan dengan kondisi ini saya ingin mengingatkan kepada kalangan perbankan agar "euphoria" penyaluran kredit ke sektor yang sedang naik daun ini tidak mengorbankan prinsip prudential banking dan kelestarian lingkungan, mengingat porsi terbesar kredit tersebut diambil oleh para debitur besar. Kembali ke peran Bank Indonesia di sektor ini, perlu saya tekankan bahwa sejak berlakunya UU No. 23/1999 tentang Bank Indonesia (sebagaimana diamandemen dengan UU No.3/2004), maka kebijakan Bank Indonesia dalam mendukung peningkatan iklim usaha atau sektor riil telah mengalami perubahan mendasar. Perubahan tersebut adalah bahwa Bank Indonesia tidak dapat lagi memberikan bantuan keuangan atau kredit likuiditas secara langsung seperti di masa lalu, namun bantuan yang diberikan lebih bersifat tidak langsung, antara lain melalui regulasi dan fasilitasi dalam peran-peran strategis. Dengan kata lain, Bank Indonesia tidak secara khusus mendesain suatu kebijakan dalam bidang perkreditan secara sektoral. Kebijakan Bank Indonesia lebih diarahkan untuk mendukung pengembangan UMKM, terutama yang berbasis komoditas unggulan, agar dapat dibiayai oleh perbankan. Kebijakan tersebut dituangkan dalam bentuk pengaturan (ketentuan) dan pemberian bantuan teknis (khususnya melalui perbankan) serta kerjasama dengan pemangku kepentingan (departemen, lembaga donor dan lembaga terkait pemberdayaan UMKM). Di dalam kebijakan yang bersifat lintas sektoral tersebut, terdapat kegiatan-kegiatan yang berupaya mendukung pengembangan sektor agribisnis. Secara umum, kalau boleh saya katakan bahwa "kami tidak lagi memberikan ikan, namun memberikan kail". Apa saja "kail-kail" itu ? Mari coba kita lihat satu persatu 1. Data dan Informasi Bisnis Indonesia (DIBI) DIBI menyajikan data dan informasi berbasis website dan dapat diakses melalui website Bank Indonesia (www.bi.go.id). Informasi yang disajikan dalam DIBI didasarkan atas penelitian yang dilakukan Bank Indonesia, antara lain data dan informasi mengenai potensi ekonomi daerah, komoditas ekspor potensial, serta pola pembiayaan (lending model) untuk komoditi agrobisnis. 2. Pola Pembiayaan (lending model) UMKM Bank Indonesia melaksanakan penelitian mengenai pola pembiayaan/lending model berbagai komoditi yang potensial untuk dibiayai oleh bank. Saat ini telah terdapat 88 pola pembiayaan konvensional dan 21 pola pembiayaan syariah, yang mana sebagian besar dari pola pembiayaan tersebut adalah untuk komoditas agribisnis. 3. Pengembangan UMKM melalui Pengembangan Klaster Program ini didesain untuk mengembangkan UMKM melalui model klaster yang terintegrasi dari hulu ke hilir. UMKM akan memperoleh manfaat dari kerjasama dengan usaha menengah maupun besar yang berperan sebagai local champion dalam suatu komunitas usaha yang sejenis. Pada tahun 2007 telah dilaksanakan pengembangan klaster komoditas unggulan di 6 wilayah Kantor Bank Indonesia, antara lain untuk komoditas rumput laut, emping melinjo, paprika, dan opak. Program ini dilaksanakan bekerjasama dengan berbagai pemangku kepentingan di daerah baik Pemda maupun perbankan dan instansi terkait. 4. Penelitian tentang Pola Kemitraan Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk melihat berbagai pola kemitraan antara Usaha Menengah/Usaha Besar dengan UMKM dalam rangka potensi peningkatan akses kredit kepada perbankan. Dalam kemitraan tersebut, usaha menengah maupun usaha besar dapat berperan sebagai pemberi rekomendasi, avalis dan juga memberikan jaminan cash collateral bagi UMKM yang menjadi mitra dalam hubungan usaha kemitraan. Sektor agribisnis merupakan salah satu sektor yang banyak terlibat dalam hubungan kemitraan dengan usaha menengah dan besar. 5. Program Pengembangan Inti-Plasma Bank Indonesia telah cukup lama (sejak sebelum UU Bl 1999) membiayai kegiatan Inti Plasma terutama untuk komoditas kelapa sawit dengan Kredit Likuiditas Bank Indonesia. Saat ini, meskipun sudah tidak ada pembiayaan dengan KLBI, Bank Indonesia masih memberikan perhatian pada proses kesinambungan hubungan inti-plasma, terutama dengan berbagai masalah sosial pasca reformasi. Bank Indonesia berperan menjadi mediator bagi adanya konflik kepentingan dari berbagai pihak yang terlibat dalam program inti-plasma tersebut. Model penyelesaian masalah dalam hubungan inti-plasma pada komoditi kelapa sawit ini diharapkan dapat menjadi pedoman dalam hubungan kemitraan antara inti dan plasma ke depan. Disamping itu, dalam rangka mendorong pemberian kredit perkebunan dengan pola inti plasma ini, Bank Indonesia telah melakukan relaksasi ketentuan tentang Batas Maksimum Pemberian Kredit, yakni pemberian kredit dengan pola kemitraan inti plasma dimana perusahaan inti yang menjamin kredit kepada plasma dikecualikan dari pengertian kelompok peminjam, sebagaimana tertuang dalam PBI No. 7/3/PBI/2005 tentang Batas Maksimum Pemberian Kredit Bank Umum. 6. Fasilitasi Percepatan dan Pemberdayaan Ekonomi Daerah Program ini merupakan upaya Bank Indonesia untuk mengembangkan ekonomi daerah terutama sektor riil yang masih dirasakan terhambat perkembangannya. Bank Indonesia melalui jaringan Kantor Bank Indonesia bergerak mendukung berbagai program dari dinas/instansi yang dirasakan masih terhambat pembiayaannya oleh perbankan di daerah. Kami berharap peran Bank Indonesia di dalamnya sedikit banyak dapat memperlancar pembiayaan proyek-proyek kegiatan di daerah. Beberapa kegiatan yang telah dilakukan antara lain mendukung revitalisasi perkebunan/pertanian seperti kelapa sawit dan karet, serta pembiayaan untuk komoditi vanili, jagung, padi, rumput laut, jeruk, gula tebu dan lainnya. Melalui berbagai upaya yang dilakukan Bank Indonesia tersebut, yaitu dengan mengambil peran sebagai regulator dan fasilitator, kami berharap agar perbaikan di sektor riil dapat berjalan dengan lebih cepat dan signifikan. Namun demikian tentu saja, upaya yang kami lakukan tersebut masih memerlukan kritik dan saran demi perbaikan dan penyempurnaannya, disamping tentunya kami membutuhkan dukungan dari semua pihak yang terkait dan peduli terhadap upaya peningkatan iklim usaha yang secara umum dirasakan masih jauh dari memuaskan. Hadirin yang berbahagia, REKOMENDASI DAN LANGKAH KE DEPAN Memasuki bagian akhir dari sambutan ini, saya berharap pemerintah dan otoritas kebijakan lainnya perlu melakukan evaluasi, koordinasi kebijakan, dan upaya terobosan, baik dari sisi regulasi maupun reorientasi pencapaian tujuan yang lebih difokuskan pada kesejahteraan rakyat banyak dengan cara mendorong terciptanya iklim investasi yang kondusif di sektor riil, khususnya sektor pertanian. Kiranya juga diperlukan kebijakan di sektor pertanian dengan skala prioritas dan stages implementasi yang jelas, sehingga para pelaku usaha agro bisnis dapat lebih akurat dalam mengambil keputusan di lingkungan bisnis yang predictable. Saya juga berharap forum ilmiah yang digagas FEU I ini dapat membantu mencari terobosan yang bermanfaat bagi upaya mengoptimalkan sumber daya yang kita miliki demi meningkatkan daya saing bangsa, usaha dan tentu saja daya saing kita masing- masing sebagai individu di era globalisasi dan borderless world ini. Selamat menjalani journey anda, sekian dan terima kasih. I Disampaikan pada The 3rd MRC Doctoral Journey in Management in conjunction with The 1st Master Journey in Management, dengan tema "Optimizing Local Resources for Competitiveness", kerjasama FEUI dan harian Bisnis Indonesia, Kamis, 7 Agustus 2008 di Jakarta. --------------- ------------------------------------------------------------ --------------- ------------------------------------------------------------

Title: Penjelasan Dewan Gubernur Bank Indonesia pada Rapat Kerja Komisi IX DPR RI Tanggal 20 September 2001
text: EXPLANATION OF THE BOARD OF GOVERNORS OF BANK INDONESIA AT THE WORKING MEETING OF COMMISSION IX OF THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES ON 20 SEPTEMBER 2001 Trial Period : I Year of Session : 2001 - 2002 Dear Members of the Council, First of all, let me thank the Chairman of Commission IX and the esteemed Members of the Board, who have invited us to attend the Working Meeting today. For us, this Working Meeting has a very important meaning because it is a form of our accountability to the public through this House Session. In addition, this Working Meeting is very useful, especially to convey information on the extent of the implementation of Bank Indonesia's duties as mandated by the Law, as well as to obtain input for us tomake efforts to make improvements in the implementation of future tasks. Secondly, as was the case at the last Working Meetings, before we present answers to the questions of the honourable members of the Board, let us brieflypresent the latest developments on the policy measures taken by Bank Indonesia. In detail, economic developments and the implementation of Bank Indonesia's duties in the monetary, banking and payment system sectors have been presentedin the Quarterly Report which is a quarterly report on the implementation of duties and authorities to the Honorable Board. Dear Members of the Council, In the first half of 2001, a number of macroeconomic and monetary indicatorsshowed an unfavorable development of n. After growing by 4.8% in 2000, Indonesia's economic growth fell to 3.21% during the first half of 2001. Meanwhile, monetary stability faces threats from the weakening of the rupiah exchange rate and the increasingright tee of inflation. The exchange rate weakened from Rp9,485 in January 2001 to Rpl 1,314 per US dollar in June 2001. Meanwhile, the CPI inflation rate increased to 12.11% (y-o-y) in June 2001. This condition has also made it difficult for Bank Indonesia to maintain monetary stability with the high number of currency circulating in the community. Therefore, monetary stabilization efforts will continue to be pursued by Bank Indonesia to control liquidity in the economy, with consequences for the increasing SBI interest rate. Further developments until August 2001 of economic-monetary conditions were marked by various positive developments, as reflected in the continued strengthening of the rupiah exchange rate and the occurrence of deflation in August, which was the first deflation in 2001. Meanwhile, economic activity, albeit slowly, also began to move in an improving direction. This is the case with function 1 of banking intermediation where there are indications of improvement. Nevertheless, this positive development needs to be watched out for considering that there are still several risk factors that cause new pressures on inflation and the exchange rate. General price pressures in August showed a decline and even deflation. The inflation rate reached minus 0.21% (m-t-m) much lower than the inflation rate in July (2.12%). Cumulatively, the inflation rate for eight months in 2001 has reached 7.48% (y-t-d), while on an annual basis (y-o-y) it has reached 12.23%. The deflation in August 2001 was caused by lower prices in the food group, which was partly due to the smooth supply of various basic necessities. The strengthening of the exchange rate also had a positive impact on the decline in some prices of clothing group goods, especially gold. Other groups continue to experience inflation, especially in the education, recreation and sports groups. Meanwhile, the strengthening of the rupiah exchange rate was also reflected in the decline in the group of traded goods which reached -0.76% (m-t-m) in August 2001, while the group of non-traded goods recorded a price increase of 0.8%. Meanwhile, the development of the rupiah exchange rate throughout August 2001 also showed improvement. The comparison at the end of the month shows that the rupiah exchange rate against the US dollar showed a strengthening from the level of Rp9,500 at the end of July 2001 to Rp8,850 at the end of August 2001 or appreciated by 7.34%. Even during August 2001, the strongest level in August was recorded at the level of Rp8,200 per US dollar, which was the lowest point since the beginning of 2001. However, towards the end of the month, the rupiah exchange rate was corrected and weakened again to reach Rp9,000, - which was caused by high demand from corporations for the benefit of debt repayment and for the needs of considerable fuel imports. If calculated on an average monthly basis, the rupiah exchange rate reached Rp8,966 in August, or strengthened 21.3% compared to the previous month. The appreciation of the rupiah exchange rate was also followed by an increase in average volatility which reached 8.3% much higher than the previous month which was only 3.6%. The thin market, which only reaches an average of USD200 million per day, is seen as very vulnerable, allowing large financiers who want to take advantage (speculation) from the fluctuating movement of the rupiah. Nevertheless, the strengthening of the exchange rate has not been followed by the prospect of long-term strengthening, as reflected by the high swap premium and risk premium. On a monthly average basis, the 1-month swap premium increased, from 14.5% in July to 15.2% in August. The tendency to continue to increase the SBI interest rate is a monetary policy response in absorbing excess liquidity, which is feared to put pressure on inflation and the exchange rate. In August, the increase in SBI interest rates was followed by money market interest rates and deposit rates and interest rates on working capital loans. The weighted average (PRC) 1-month SBI discount rate, which rose by 13 bps to 17.67%, while the rupiah intervention rate, which did not increase compared to the previous month, was responded to by the daily average interbank rate in the morning and afternoon with a fairly high increase to 16.67% and 15.78%. Meanwhile, the PRC's 1-month deposit rate in the banking industry (July) rose to 14.25% from the previous month's position. In July, the difference between the PRC's 1-month SBI discount rate (17.17%) and the PRC's 1-month deposit rate (14.25%) reached 292 bps further widening compared to last month (264 bps). The positive spread between deposit rates and the increasingly large SBI interest rate is a symptom that has recently occurred because banks are still dependent on planting in SBI. This has resulted in banks tending to maintain a positive spread between their fund rates and SBI rates. Judging from the development of base money, in August 2001 the position of base money was still above its indicative target. The position of test date base money slightly increased from Rpl 11.4 trillion in July to Rpl 11.8 trillion at the end of August 2001 or slightly above the revised indicative target of Rpl 11.5 trillion. Meanwhile, banking conditions showed slight improvement, as indicated by improving deposits, and increasing bank lending. In July 2001, rupiah third party funds (DPK) increased by Rp2.43 trillion due to an increase in savings and current accounts, which increased by Rp2.08 trillion and Rp3.90 trillion, respectively. In contrast, deposits in rupiah decreased by IDR 3.54 trillion. This shifting phenomenon indicates the growing need for transactions and vigilance carried out by depositors. Meanwhile, there are indications of slight improvement in the intermediation function as reflected in the continued expansion of credit growth in July 2001 amounting to Rp2.7 trillion. The increase in credit was mostly channeled to the industrial, trade, business and social services sectors. Based on the results of the evaluation and monetary economic projections, Bank Indonesia considers that monetary policy is still aimed at reducing the growth of base money in a direction that is more in line with the real needs of economic activity. However, in absorbing excess liquidity, monetary control strategies need to be carried out in a prudent and measured manner by reducing the impact of excessive interest rate increases. For this reason, Open Market Operations as the main monetary control tool will be sought not to give signals of interest rate hikes that are too strong. In addition, rupiah intervention policy is still used as "fine tuning" to absorb excess liquidity that is not absorbed in the OPT. Another instrument that will be used by Bank Indonesia is to sterilize the foreign exchange market to assist the absorption of rupiah liquidity while increasing the supply in the thin foreign exchange market so as to reduce pressure and fluctuations in the rupiah exchange rate. To that end, let us provide an explanation of the written questions that the Councillors have previously presented to us. Question: 1. After the filling of kembali Account No. 502,000,002 is agreed, the next issue is how will the BLBI issue continue? Is this matter by itself resolved as well? This needs to be clarified because during the reign of President Abdurrahman Wahid, there were 2 (two)conflicting katans, namely: 95 On 17th November 2000, Bank Indonesia and the Government (Menko Rizal Ramli) agreed to jointly bear the BLBI bailout of Rpl44.5 trillion, of which Bank Indonesia is obliged to bear the BLBI of Rp24.5 trillion. Bank Indonesia itself has deposited the funds into the Government's account and has an interest and has been used by the Government. 95 The agreement between the Government and Bank Indonesia has not received approval from the Dpr Rl (commission IX). Even now the BLBI Pansus has been formed and the Pansus itself has not worked until Abdurahman Wahid stepped down. In this regard, it is necessary to be clear about this case, and how Bank Indonesia itself responds to this case. Jawaban : Dear Members of the Council, Fulfilling the answers to the questions of Commission IX of the DPR-RI mentioned above, we can state the following: 1. As is known that in the Working Meeting between the Government, Bank Indonesia and Commission IX of the House of Representatives on 10th October 2000, among others, it was stipulated that the Government and Bank Indonesia immediately resolve the BLBI issue within 30 days from 10th October 2000. For this reason, a Working Team has been formed whose members are appointedfrom officials representing the Ministry of Finance, Bank Indonesia and the Attorney General's Office which is coordinated by the Coordinating Minister for the Economy (Mr. Rizal Ramli). 2. As an implementation of the decision of the House of Representatives, several meetings have been held at the Departmentof Finance, and finally at Bank Indonesia on November 17, 2000. In the meeting, which was attended by the Minister of Finance and the Attorney General as well as the Coordinating Minister for the Economy, an agreement was reached as outlined in the Principles of Agreement between the Governmentand Bank Indonesia regarding the Settlement of BLBI. The points of agreement have also been signed by the Minister of Finance and Senior Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia and witnessed by the Coordinating Minister for the Economy. As a follow-up to the terse agreement, Bank Indonesia issued Debt Securities to the Government amounting to Rp24.5 trillion and fulfilled related obligations such as periodic interest payments, as Bank Indonesia's financial responsibility for BLBI amounting to Rp144.5 trillion. 3. From the Bank Indonesia side, with the principal agreement signed on November 17, 2000 and Bank Indonesia has issued Debt Securities to the Government and has paid interest periodically, the BLBI problem of Rp144.5 trillion has been resolved. However, if the agreement between the Governor of Bank Indonesia and the Minister of Finance regarding the issuance of Government Bonds (SUP) No. 6/2001 on September 6, 2001 is to be used, then we expect it to beresolved in the near future.
