In addition, the implementation of monetary policy that is too tight will cause the SBI interest rate to increase high and it is feared that it may threaten the economic recovery. Under such conditions, despite efforts to be controlled, the position of base money in the third quarter of 2000 was still above its indicative target. Meanwhile, performance criteria based on factors affecting the base money, namely Net Domestic Asset (NDA) and Net International Reserve (NIR), are still within the set limits. The growth of base money, both nominal and real, continues to show an upward trend in line with the increase in economic activity. In the third quarter of 2000, the average growth of real base money was 14.9.% (yoy) higher than the previous quarter of 12.3%. The development of base money is mainly due to the high demand for currency to meet economic activities. This is shown by the increase in currency to deposit ratio (C/D) since April 2000 from 0.65 to 0.69 in August 2000, although it has decreased slightly compared to the previous month of July 2000). The sign of the beginning of the decline in C /D is in line with the increasing use of giral money to meet the needs of investment activities. The implementation of tight monetary policy has pushed interest rates up. This was marked by an increase in the average interest rate of the 1-month SBI from 11.7% at the end of June to 13.62% in September 2000. The increase in the SBI interest rate was not immediately followed by an increase in the bank deposit rate due to the large excess liquidity of the banking industry and the relatively small spread of the guarantee interest rate, which is 100 basis points above JIBOR. The average interest rate on 1-month deposits began to increase since July from 9.7% to 10.5% in September 2000 after the underwriting rate spread was raised to 200 basis points above JIBOR. Meanwhile, the real interest rate (calculated annualized) of the 1-month SBI is still positive at around 7%, while the average 1-month deposit rate is around 3.7%. Dear Members of the Council. Next, let us explain the developments and policy steps in the field of banking. In general, we have stated that improvements have been achieved in the banking industry as seen in the increase in capital, decrease in Non-Performing Loans (NPLs), increasing Net Interest Margin (NIM) in all bank groups, increasing profit generation which shows an increase and credit that is starting to show an increase. The improvements achieved are the fruit that is closely related to the ongoing banking restructuring program that we have carried out since the beginning of 1998. In relation to the development of the banking restructuring program, we can say that until the third quarter of 2000 the Government had issued bonds in the framework of the recapitalization program for 26 banks consisting of 4 state-owned banks, 7 National Private Commercial Banks (BUSN) participants in the recapitalization program, 3 Take Over Banks (BTO) and 12 Regional Development Banks (BPD). Government Bonds for BRI and BTN were issued in two phases, the first phase was implemented in July 2000 and the next phase will be implemented in October 2000 together with Bank Bali's recapitalization plan. If the bond issuance has been carried out, the recapitalization program of the banks has been completed according to the plan. Meanwhile, related to the guarantee program, as the Board members understand, since November 1999 the guarantee program of commercial banks has been entirely the responsibility of IBRA. However, to maintain international trust, Bank Indonesia for and on behalf of the Government still implements guarantee programs related to international trade (trade finance arrears) and interbank debt exchange offers. In connection with the implementation of the guarantee, during the third quarter of 2000, principal and interest payments on the interbank debt exchange offer amounted to USD236.69 million, resulting in accumulated payments up to the third quarter of 2000 amounting to USD473.94 million. Meanwhile, for trade finance, there were no payments until the third quarter of 2000. Dear Dezwan members, In relation to efforts to implement good corporate governance to improve the strengthening of banking system resilience, until the third quarter of 2000, a fit and proper assessment for owners and administrators has been completed, interviews with prospective owners and pew entry\ management and approval of the appointment of a compliance director (compliance director) on some commercial banks. Meanwhile, in terms of improving banking regulations, during the third quarter of 2000 Bank Indonesia has issued a Bank Indonesia Regulation (PBI) regulating the Requirements and Procedures for Granting Orders or Written Permits to Open Bank Secrets, Short-Term Funding Facilities for Commercial Banks and Monthly Statements of Commercial Banks. In addition, a Circular Letter (SE) of Bank Indonesia was also issued which regulates the Determination of Government Bonds Series FR0003, FR0004 and FR0005 To Trade on the Secondary Market and on Increasing The Percentage of Tradable Government Bond Portfolios For Commercial Banks Participating in the Banking Recapitalization Program. In order to further strengthen the bank supervision function, the implementation of bank supervision is not only focused on compliance supervision but also directed at risk-based supervision and forward looking. In this regard, Bank Indonesia has placed on-site permanent supervision (OSP) personnel in several banks that are considered systemic banks. Until now, several OSP workers have been placed in 4 state-owned banks and 5 BUSN banks. Furthermore, in order to increase the fulfillment of the 25 Basel Core Principles on increasing supervision as stated in the Letter of Intent (Lol) of September 2000, Bank Indonesia has formulated an Action Plan for the next 2 years (until 2002). The action plan includes, among others: (i) the terms/conditions in licensing for the establishment of banks, bank owners and administrators; (ii) coordination between supervisory authorities in the financial sector; (iii) the expansion of the scope of the examination not only in terms of bank operations but also includes policies, procedures and internal controls; and (iv) supervision based on risk-based and consolidated supervision. Dear Dezwan members, Please allow us on this occasion to inform the development of banking lending. Although still in relatively small numbers some banks have begun to channel new loans to business sectors. Although there is still a transfer of credit to IBRA related to the recapitalization program, especially for state-owned banks, the new credit distribution shows that the process of restoring the bank's intermediation function is beginning to take place. We realize that the incomplete implementation of banking restructuring and the slow completion of the corporate restructuring process so far have resulted in the banking intermediation function not being as fast and large as we expected, even thoughpublic confidence in the banking industry has recovered. For this reason, we believe that the settlement of non-performing loans is a crucial agenda to be resolved immediately considering that non-performing loans are a burden on banks and their resolutionwill affect the success of the overall banking restructuring program. Credit restructuring basically aims to normalize the business function of the debtor so that it is able to return to fulfill its obligations to the bank, as well as improve the qualityof the bank's credit portfolio. Furthermore, we can convey to the honorable members of the Board that until August 2000 the settlement of non-performing loans through the credit restructuring program facilitated by the Bank Indonesia Credit Restructuring Task Force Team as well as those carried out by the banks themselves showed an increase. Total loans that had been restructured until August 2000 increased by Rp3.4 trillion to Rp54.l trillion with the number of debtors increasing by 1,754 debtors to16,996 debtors compared to the position in June 2000. These results reflect that credit restructuring is able to make an adequate contribution to the process of reducing NPLs and at the same time improving credit quality. Taking into accountthese content, we continue to strive to accelerate the completion of credit restructuring, among others, by increasing an active role in credit restructuring through the Credit Restructuring Task Force Team which handles the loans of banks outside IBRA and improves coordination with relevant agencies, including the Jakarta Initiative, IBRA and INDRA. Dear Dezwan members, As members of the Board of Indonesia know, Bank Indonesia's policy in the field of payment system is directed towards the development of a fast, efficient, reliable and safe payment system to reduce payment risks that may disrupt monetary stability and support the development of a sound payment system. In the field of money circulation, in addition to providingsufficient amounts of money, Bank Indonesia also always maintains that the quality of money held by the public is always maintained in quality by implementing a policy of destroying money that is no longer fit for circulation or Giving No Valuable Signs (PTTB) andwaiting for the destroyed money. In relation to efforts to overcome the circulation of counterfeit money, one of the efforts made by Bank Indonesia is to revoke and withdraw the types of banknotes that are widely counterfeited. Since the third quarter of 2000, Bank Indonesia will continue its withdrawal efforts from the circulation of denomination banknotes of Rp 10,000 in 1992, Rp20,000 in 1992/1995 and Rp50,000 in 1993/1995. In the field of payment traffic, the policy taken during the third quarter of 2000 is to continue the policy that had been taken in the previous quarter, namely continuing the steps to develop the Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system which at this time has reached the final stage to be implemented at the end of December 2000. Dear Members of the Council. At the end of this introduction, let us share our views on the economic outlook and the future policy direction. Observing the development of several important economic indicators until the third quarter of 2000, we consider that indonesia's economic outlook going forward, especially in the fourth quarter of 2000, still shows the ongoing economic recovery process. Economic growth in the fourth quarter of 2000 is expected to be higher than the previous quarter. The source of growth comes from the continued increase in investment, exports and consumption, as well as the rampant economic activity at the end of the year in connection with Christmas, Eid al-Fitr and New Year. Investment is expected to continue to increase although not as high asin the quarter. Consumption will continue to grow positively but at a slowing pace. On the supply side, the manufacturing, trade and transportation sectors are the main drivers of the economy. Overall economic growth in 2000 is expected to grow in the range of 4%-5%. Nevertheless, such developments were overshadowed by high pressures on the inflation rate at the end of the year as a result of government policies in the field of prices and income, as well as seasonal factors, namelythe religious holidays that will occur simultaneously at the end of 2000. The Government's policy of increasing prices and income, namely the increase in fuel prices, the plan to increase the phase II salary of civil servants/TNI/Polri, increase in use and increase inflation expectations in the first quarterof V/2000, is expected to encourage an increase in the inflation rate. As we have previously stated, we expect the inflation rate in 2000 to reach about 1% above the set target. Taking into account the magnitude of inflationary pressures on the one hand and the increase in economic activity on the other, we are of the view that the direction of monetary policy in the future will be carried out prudently. This policy is also carried out considering the vulnerability of the economic recovery process with the ongoingprocess of restructuring corporate and banking debt. Under current conditions, monetary conditions need to be directed to reduce the amount of inflationary pressure while still providing sufficient liquidity to support the economic recovery process. In this context, Bank Indonesia is currently conducting a study to change the base money target in 2000 to be more realistic with the current development of economic activity. In the banking sector, the direction of banking policy going forward will be pursued by considering (i) efforts to encourage the recovery of the banking intermediation function, (ii) follow-up of banks that fall into special supervision of thellance survey) (iii) implementation of the Master Plan according to the established schedule in order to increase the effectiveness of banking supervision and regulation, and (v) follow-up action plan to the fulfillment of the 25 Basel Core Principles, especially those relating to risk based supervision studies for the preparation of the implementation of consolidated supervision and the scope of examinations. Dear Members of the Council, Henceforth allow us to give an explanation of the written questions that the Councillor had previouslypresented to us. Pertanvaan: 1. Bank Indonesia Certificate (SBI) is an instrument to attract liquidity from the public, how much is the monthly burden, how much money comes in is used for operations, and where is the source of theaan interest for the SBI interest in question? Answer: Dear Members of the Council, SBI is securities in rupiah issued by Bank Indonesia as a recognition of short-term debt (1 month and 3 months) used as a monetary instrument. In saat issuance, SBI serves as a monetary contraction tool to absorb excess rupiah liquidity in the money market and at the time of repayment/falling time SBI becomes an automatic monetary expansion. Therefore, the implementation of the SBI auction needs to be carried out in asustainable way so that on the one hand it can neutralize the impact of monetary expansion from the SBI which is falling in time and on the other hand can absorb excess rupiah liquidity in the money market. Based on Bank Indonesia's Annual Budget (ATBI) of 2000, the discounted expense for SBI transactions for 2000 is budgeted at Rp 10.25 trillion or Rp0.85 trillion per month. As of August 2000, the realization of discounted expenses that have been issued for SBI transactions is Idr 7.80 trillion or Rp0.98 trillion per month. The increase in realization (compared to the budget) was mainly due to the relatively high interest rate of the SBI in 2000 compared to the original estimate in preparing the budget, which was only 11.0%. As is known, in early 2000, the average 1-month SBI rate was 11.64% and fell to 10.88% (the lowest in 2000) in late April and early May 2000. Since then, the average interest rate of the 1-month SBI has continued to rise and since the second week of July2000 the level has been above 13.00%. Finally, as of October 4, 2000, the average 1-month SBI rate was 13.63%. The source of funding in paying the SBI discount mainly comes from the management of foreign exchange reserves controlled by BI which are plantedin the form of current accounts, deposits, securities and other forex transactions. As is known, based on atbi BI in 2000, receipts from foreign exchange management are estimated at Rpl4.77 trillion or Rpl.23 trillion per month. Asof August 2000, the realization of foreign exchange management has reached Rp22.37 trillion or Rp2.80 trillion per month. Question: 2. What is and how is Bank Indonesia's responsibility in following up with banks after recapitalization? Answer: Dear Members of the Council , As is known, the recapitalization program aims to improve the capital structure of banks, especially banks that have prospects for viable banks. Efforts to improve the capital structure arecarried out through capital deposits by the owners and participation by the government. Participation by the government has been carried out through the issuance of bonds which until now reached Rp. 412.16 trillion. Efforts to improve the bank's capital structure were also followed by improvements in asset quality through credit restructuring and the transfer of non-performing loans to IBRA. With better quality of assets and capital, it is expected that the performance of banks will improve and in turn the banking system will be sehat. As a further step towards the restructuring of the national banking system, Bank Indonesia has also undertaken a series of efforts to strengthen the resilience of the banking system through the development of banking infrastructure, the implementation of good corporate governance as well as the improvementof governance and increased supervision. In relation to infrastructure development, banks that carry out activities with sharia principles and People's Credit Banks have been developed. The implementation of good corporate governance is carried out through the implementation of fit and proper tests on bank administrators and owners, interviews with prospective administrators and owners, requiring banks to appoint compliance directors and the establishment of a Special Banking Investigation Unit at Bank Indonesia. Efforts to improve the provisions andsupervision committees carried out by referring to international standards. In order to improve the effectiveness of supervision , various efforts are taken including: 95 Monitoring the realization of the business plan of banks, where the supervisor early asks the bank owners and management to take the necessary steps, such as increasing capital and accelerating the settlement of non-performing loans. 95 Cooperation with public accounting firms in conducting bank checks. 95 The application of On-site Supervisory Presence through the placement of supervisors in banks that are considered to have a large share of national banks. 95 Placement in special surveillance status forbank banks that do not meet the banking prudence requirements . 95 The implementation of enforcement of exit policy provisions for banks that can no longer be maintained is in the banking system. Pertanvaan: 3. How is the implementation of the Foreign Debt Restructuring program, both government external debt and private external debt? Answer: Dear Members of the Council, As is known, efforts to restructure government debt are carried out through two mechanisms, namely the Paris Club and the London Club, respectively forthe restructuring of bilateral loans and commercial loans of the Government of Indonesia. Efforts to restructure these obligations are carried out by the Government in the framework of reducing fiscal deficit pressures and pressures on Indonesia's Balance of Payments. This program has also implicitly obtained the approval of the House of Representatives as reflected in the approval of the Council Session on the State Budget submitted by the Government. The restructuring program is reflected in the expenditure post for the payment of the principal installment of the loan on the state budget in theud. The implementation of the program through each of these mechanisms can be explained as follows: 1. Paris Club I: Negotiations with the 17 member countries of the Paris Club have been intensive since August 1998. The government sought restructuring of bilateral loans maturing during FY. 1998 and 1999. The terms of the restructured loan refer to the original agreement. These loans generally have a term of between 20 to 24 years for ODA and 10 to 15 years for Non-ODA. The restructuring agreement with creditors is contained in an MOU signed by both parties on September 23 1998, with the points of agreement: (first) restructuring of the principal payment obligations of bilateral loans due between 06/08/98 and 31/03/00 worth USD4.2 billion. (second) ODA loans restructured for a period of 20 years including a 5-year grace period, and Non-ODA loans are restructured for a period of 11 years including a 3-year grace period. (third) The Government of Indonesia is obliged to provide comparable treatment for other bilateral loan repayment obligations (excluding PC members) and obligations for commercial loans received by the Government. As an implementation of the MOU, the Government submitted a request for restructuring bilaterally to each of the creditors concerned. The total restructured loans were USD4.66 billion. This amount includes syndicated loan obligations worth USD210 million y yang carried out through the London Club mechanism. As an implementation of the PC I MOU, the Government has signed an agreement to restructure the obligation to pay principal installments to 17 PC member donor countries, valued at USD4.38 billion at the end of March 2000. Itcan be informed that the difference between this amount and the value contained in the MOU is due solely to changes in the exchange rate. In addition, the Government has also signed an obligation restructuring agreement to 2 non-member countries (Saudi Arabiaand Brunei) and 5 commercial banks, worth USD 70.85 million. Efforts to resolve negotiations are still being carried out against 3 non-PC member countries (Taiwan, Kuwait and China) with a total obligation of USD 18 million. The delay in completing this restructuringof the asi does not hinder or derail the implementation of the program as a whole. This is mainly based on the consideration that the Paris Club MOU agreement is non-binding for non-PC member creditors. Nevertheless, the Government continues to seek restructuring obligations to these non-member states. 2. Paris Club II. Considering the severity of the fiscal deficit and Balance of Payments pressures; The government is conducting phase II restructuring efforts. Restructuring is proposedfor obligations due in FY 2000 and FY. 2001 (economic recovery period), and with the condition that it refers to the original agreement. Intensified negotiations were conducted in March/April 2000, and a restructuring agreement with the 17 member countries of the Paris Club was set out on the MOU of April 13, 2000. The main points of the MOU agreement are: (first) restructuring of the principal payment obligations of bilateral loans due between 01/04/00 and 31/03/02 worth USD5.8 billion. (second) ODA loans are restructured for a period of 20 years including a 7-year grace period and Non-ODA loans are restructured for a period of 15 years including a 3-year grace period. (third) The Government of Indonesia shall make comparable treatment on other bilateral loan repayment obligations (excluding PC members) and obligations on commercial loans received by the Government. In the MOU, it was also agreed that the limit for holding negotiations was the end of November 2000. As an implementation of the PC II MOU, the Government has submitted a restructuring proposal to creditors with a total obligation of USD5.86 billion consisting of USD5.8 billion in obligations to 17 PC member donor countries and USD425 million is an obligation to 5 member countriesand commercial loans outside of syndicated loans. As of October 10, 2000, the New Government signed a restructuring agreement with Saudi Arabia worth USD 19.8 million. The government has accepted and approved the draftagreements submitted by the 15 PC member states with a total value of USD2.84 billion. We need to point out that the 15 countries that have submitted the draft restructuring agreement do not include Japan. The obligation to Japan to be restructuredreferring to PC II is USD3 billion. Discussions with Japan are still intensively carried out both through correspondence and directly within the framework of the visit of the JBIC Delegation (institution as a result of the merger betweenJEXIM and OECF) to Indonesia. 3. London Club I: As an implementation of the agreement contained in the Paris Club MOU; Bank Indonesia as a debtor on behalf of the Government of The Republic of Indonesia seeks to restructure syndicated loan obligations maturing during the period 06/08/98 to 31/03/00 worth USD210 million. Negotiations were carried out with the Steering Committee consisting of the Bank of Tokyo Mitsubishi as the syndicate agent of the bank and 5 banks as representatives of creditors. Negotiations began intensively in January/F1999. Bank Indonesia submits a restructuring proposal with reference to the restructuring requirements as stated in the PC MOU dated 23rd September 1998. The USD210 million loan obligation restructuring agreement that felltemp o in the period 06/08/98 to 31/03/00 became a 10.5-year term-term obligation, set forth in the London Club MOU Term-sheet, February 1999. The signing of the obligation restructuring agreement was carried out on March 28, 1999. 4. London Club II\ As an implementation of the agreement required by creditors for the implementation of the PC II restructuring programme; Bank Indonesia seeks restructuring of 2 syndicated loans worth USD340 million due between 01/04/00 to 31/03/02. The restructuring proposal refers toa Paris Club II MOU for Non-ODA loans. Intensive discussions with the Steering Committee began in May 2000 which resulted in a restructuring agreement for a period of 12.5 years including a grace period of 3 years The signing ofthe syndicated loan restructuring agreement was carried out after obtaining the approval of all creditors. The signing of the manuscript was held on September 28, 2000. With this success, Standard & Poors - one of the international rating agencies based in London, has raised Indonesia's sovereign rating from SD/Selective Default to B- on October 2, 2000. Besides paris club as an effort to restructure government debt; in order to reduce pressure on the national balance of payments, the Government supports efforts to restructure private debt. This effort was stated in the form of a joint press release/release of the Frankfurt agreement on June 4, 1998 by Indonesia with representatives of the kreditur. The agreement includes two things, namely the Exchange Offer for debt restructuring of the national banking sector and INDRA for the debt restructuring of the Indonesian corporate sector. The implementation of each program can be explained asberikut: 1. Restructuring of sector debt: Conducted through the implementation of the Exchange Offer Program. The program is held in addition to reducing pressure on the balance of payments, also paying attention to the difficulties in foreign exchange liquidity experiencedby the national economy. The program is carried out in two stages as follows: a. Exchange Offer I: The program was marked by the signing of a Master Loan Agreement by Bank Indonesia on behalf of national banks as debtors with bank creditors on August 18, 1998. The points of agreement are: (first) restructuring the principal installment obligations of national banking loans to foreign banks that mature up to the point of March 31, 1999. (second) The obligation is restructured for a period of 4 yearswith the payment of principal installments made on an annual basis starting from August 25, 1999. As an implementation of the program, USD3 billion of national banking obligations to foreign banks have been restructured. The outstanding position of the restructured loan as of October 10, 2000 was USD 1.45 billion. Usd 1.56 billion has been settled as a principal installment obligation which fell on August 25, 1999 and August 25, 2000, as well as prepayments carried out by 4 banks , namely BCA, Danamon, Lippo Bank and BPD Central Java. b. Exchange Offer II: The program was proposed taking into account the liquidity difficulties still faced by national banks and efforts to continue to suppress the difficulties in the balance of payments needed to workout the economic recovery program. Negotiations began intensively in February/March 2000 with the Steering Committee. Points of agreement such are: (first) restructuring the principal installment obligations of national bankingloans to foreign banks due between 01/04/99 and 31/03/02. (second) The obligation was restructured for a period of 4 years with the payment of the first principal installment falling on June 2002. The agreement was then stated inthe form of signing a Master Loan Agreement on May 25, 1999 by Bank Indonesia as a debtor on behalf of national banks with bank creditors participating in the program. The program successfully restructured obligations worth USD3.3 billion into obligations with aperiod of 4 years. 2. Debt restructuring of the non-bank szwasta sector In contrast to the successful Exchange Offer program; the implementation of the INDRA program only da pat withdrawing the restructuring agreement of 1 private debtor, namely PT. Danareksa worth USD96 million. The government has closed the registration period for the INDRA program starting from the last ljuni date. Thus, the hope and efforts to restructure private debt fully now lie in the successful implementation of the Prakarsa Jakarta programs. Based on information from the Jakarta Initiative, to date USD5.3 billion in private sector loans have been restructured through the JITF program. According to JITF, the restructuring in 2000 is targeted at USD 10 billion. Pertanvaan: 4. Theestimated cost of foreign exchange reserves until the end of 2000? Answer: Dear Members of the Council, The gross reserves at the beginning of October amounted to USD 28,094.20 million. During the coming quarter beginning in October,the amount will increase by USD 1,363.80 million so that by the end of the fourth quarter of 2000, the amount of gross foreign exchange reserves will be USD 29,458.00 million. The increase in the amount of foreign exchange reserves is due mainly to theestimated receipt of oil and gas exports, the estimated withdrawal of foreign loans. Meanwhile, the increase in the amount of foreign exchange reserves has also taken into account the payment of the government's foreign obligations. The estimate of the receipt of exportproceeds mentioned above, is carried out using the assumption that the price of oil on the world market is still improving, which is an increase from the average price per year during 1999 of USD 17.40 per barrel to an average per year during 2000 of USD26.90 per barrel. Meanwhile, the fulfillment of the government's foreign obligations in the preparation of the estimate of foreign exchange reserves mentioned above, has taken into account the scheduling of foreign debt in the framework of Paris Club I and II. The estimated payment of foreign obligations includes to multilateral institutions such as ibrd, ADB and IDB; as well as bilateral payment of Indonesia's foreign obligations. Meanwhile, the payment of obligations to the IMF will only be made from2001, and for interest payments it has been included in the estimated calculation of foreign exchange reserves above. For information, the assessment of government debt in the framework of The London Club II, dated September 28, 2000 has succeeded in re-equalizing government debt of USD 340 million for a period of 12.5 years including a grace period of 3 years. So the debt repayment in the London Club ranka will only be carried out from 2003. The assumptions used in thesecalculations are in line with the estimates used in preparing the 2001 state budget.With the estimate of gross reserves as above, using a fixed exchange rate; the net foreign exchange reserves or Net International Reserve (NIR) of Indonesia by theend of 2000 are expected to be USD 18.1 billion. When compared to the performance criteria of the IMF in the Letter of Intent dated July 31, 2000, where the performance criteria for NIR were set at USD 15.7 billion; thisfigure still meets the minimum target of the safe limit of foreign exchange reserves agreed with the IMF. What efforts are being made by Bank Indonesia so that the Government is immediately free from the Guarantee Program. Answer: In accordance with the Decree of the Minister of Finance No. 179 / KMK.017 / 2000 dated May 26, 2000 concerning the Terms, Procedures and Conditions for the Implementation of Government Guarantees against Payment Obligations of Commercial Banks, currently the implementation of the Guarantee Program for commercial banks is fully carried out by the National Banking Restructuring Agency (IBRA). With the Decree of the Minister of Finance, Bank Indonesia will no longer be directly involved in the Guarantee Program. Given the large costs incurred for the implementation of the program, namely until September 2000, it has reached Rp53.8 trillion, it is necessary to consider efforts to reduce the potential burden that will be borne by the Government. From Bank Indonesia's side, various measures have been and will be taken to reduce the burden on the Government, including through: a. Seeking the creation of national banking, yesng healthy, as an industry and individual banks, so as to maintain public trust in banks which in turn will be able to reduce the burden of guarantee costs; b. Conducting studies on guarantee skims as an effort to reduce the burden that must be borne by the Government. The results of the study will be presented to the Government as input to review the scope of the guarantee program which currently seems too broad. c. While waiting for the establishment of the Deposit Insurance Corporation (LPS) which isin accordance with the Letter of Intent to be rolled out no later than 2004, Bank Indonesia considers providing inputs to the Government in order to gradually reduce the scope of guarantees. d. The study of LPS whichconcerns various aspects that include institutions, funding, rights and authorities as well as organizations. The results of the study as input to the Government will be conveyed through a working group for the establishment of lps chaired by the Minister of Finance. Pertanvaan: 6. What is the projected inflation at the end of Fiscal Year 2000 and what efforts are being made by Bank Indonesia to suppress inflation? Answer: Dear Members of the Council, As is known, the cumulative CPI inflation rate from January to September 2000 has reached 4.65%, or closer to the lower limit of the target range of the overall inflation rate for the year of 5%-7%. Government policies in the field of administered prices and income policies such as fuel price increases, angkul an tariffs,basic electricity tariffs, cigarette excise, civil servant salaries and UMR were the main causes of the high inflation rate until September 2000. Of the overall CPI inflation rate, around 1.73% came from the impact of government policies in the field of prices and impermeability, both direct and indirect impacts. With this calculation, the cumulative CPI inflation rate in the first 9 months of 2000 excluding the impact of government policies in the field of prices and income has reached 2.85%, or has approached the lower limitof the 3%-5% inflation range targeted by Bank Indonesia. Inflationary pressures are expected to persist in the fourth quarter of 2000. The government's policy in the field of transportation tariffs and fuel price increases are expected to cause a severe impactboth directly and indirectly on inflation in October and November. In addition, seasonal factors, namely religious holidays that will occur simultaneously (Eid, Christmas and New Year) at the end of 2000 are expected toincrease prices in December. These price pressures are expected to push the CPI inflation rate in the fourth quarter around 3%-4% (q-t-q). Looking at the aforementioned developments, the inflation rate during 2000 isexpected to be around 1% above the target. The CPI estimate also takes into account the impact of government policies in the field of prices and income on the CPI which is estimated to be above the original projection of 2%. Increasingpressures on inflation and the rupiah exchange rate require Bank Indonesia to pursue a tight-biased monetary policy by pursuing the primary money target set. Several factors were considered in the implementation of such a tight monetary policy. First, it is necessary to realize that the weakening of the rupiah exchange rate (and its direct impact on inflation) is more due to non-economic factors. This is mainly reflected in the increase in risk premiums, measured by swap premiums or yield spreads between Yankee Bond Indonesia and T-bills, which have tended to increase for all tenors since April 2000. Second, the increasing pressure on inflation is largely influenced by government policies in the field of prices and income (electricity tarfi , premix prices, transportation tariffs, salaries of civil servants and UMR). Third, excess liquidity in the banking industry has been driven by the lack of recovery in the real sector, especially due to the ongoing debt and corporate restructuring process. In this condition, the portfolio of banking assets is more in SBI and government bonds. Fourth, the high growth of primary money is more driven by an increase in demand for currency by the public both for transaction needs and for beijaga-jaga. Economic activity that was faster than the original assumptions caused the primary money target set at the end of 1999 to become too tight. At that time economic growth, inflation and the rupiah exchange rate for 2000 were assumed to beng at 2.50 percent, 5 percent, and Rp7000 per US dollar, respectively. Under the above conditions, it is not rational for efforts to stabilize macro through monetary policy to be carried out excessively. Stabilization of the rupiah exchange rate and control of inflation witha drastic tightening of monetary policy will cause interest rates to soar and threaten the economic recovery process. In this connection, monetary tightening still needs to be carried out with the framework of achieving the primary money target, taking into accountthe higher economic growth compared to the original assumption, as a work benchmark. This strategy is accompanied by measures that directly minimize the volatility of the rupiah exchange rate , especially those derived from speculation, with stricter enforcementof prudential rules in the field of foreign exchange (including net foreign exchange positions and restrictions on forward selling transactions to non-residents). In other words, monetary policy that tends to be tight needs to be viewed asa temporary effort to increase market confidence. Once confidence returns to normal and the risk premium begins to decline, room for a rate cut is expected to be looser to stimulate economic recovery. Pertanvaan: 7. In order to increase real sector activities, it is necessary to disburse banking loans both for business restructuring and for investment capital for new businesses. The problem is whether the banks have funds for that purpose? Please be given an overview of the public funds in the banking industry and their distribution in the use of these funds. Pertanvaan: 9. Why is there a still large increase in third depository funds (PDK) in state-owned banks? Are private banks very liquid because they have the courage to makecredit? What is the projected interest rate of SBI at the end of Fiscal Year 2000? Answer: Dear Members of the Council, Given that questions number 7 and 9 are interrelated, let us answer them all at once, In line with the increasing public confidence in banks, third party funds raised by commercial banks continue to show an increase. By the end of August 2000, rupiah third party funds raised by commercial banks from the public had reached Rp 525.40 trillion, anincrease of Rp 32.53 trillion when compared to the position at the end of 1999. The increase in rupiah deposits came from an increase in current accounts of IDR 22.36 trillion and savings of IDR 25.09 trillion. Meanwhile, deposits collected by commercial banks decreased by IDR 14.92 trillion. Judging from the bank group, the increase in rupiah deposits in the banking industry has increased in all groups except foreign banks. The largest increase in rupiah deposits was experienced by the group of persero banks which increased by RP 22.72 trillion. The high increase in deposits of persero banks is likely due to the high level of public trust in the persero bank group. The rapid collection of funds was not followed by distribution in the form of credit by banks. Total loans that have been disbursed by commercial banks until August 2000 have only reached Rp 267.61 trillion. This amount is still very low when compared to the fund raising carried out. This condition shows that the distribution of funds raised by therbankan has not been carried out optimally, which is also reflected in the very low loan-to-deposit (LDR) ratio. The value of the banking LDR decreased from 78.31% in December 1996 to 32.24 in August 2000. Judging from the type of bank, the highest increase in lending was owned by the private bank group which reached IDR 11.50 trillion. On the other hand, the increase in lending by persero banks experienced the largest decrease of IDR 10.59 trillion. The higher credit disbursed by private banks than persero banks, among others, is related to the recapitalization process for private banks which is carried out earlier than for persero banks. This can be seen from the higher CAR of private banks than persero banks. In August 2000, the CAR of the private bank group was 8.25% while the CAR of the persero bank was 4.25%. We can state that the low level of bank lending is due to both external and internal banking. On the external side, especially the real sector, the current crisis has caused the financial quality of the business world to be very low. This makes banks reluctant to channel danany in the form of credit, even though it is alleged that there is demand for credit by the real sector. On the internal side, the bank's cooperation to disburse loans is influenced by the adjustment process to the fulfillment of minimum capital (CAR). This development can be said to give an indication of the occurrence of a credit crunch. The tendency to become a credit crunch is strengthened by the declining value of LDR and portfolio adjustments made by banks into other investments such as securities, interbank money markets, and SBI. In order to stimulate lending, the government and Bank Indonesia have made efforts to recover banking conditions from the crisis through recapitalization and restructuring of the banking industry, which is planned to be completed in October 2000. In addition, Bank Indonesia has also refined the provisions and increased banksupervision measures, among others, through re-regulation of the respective provisions (relaxation) on the Maximum Credit Limit (BMPK), assessment of Productive Assets in the calculation of Risk-Weighted Assets (ATMR), and criteria for capital participationthat must be withdrawn. The development of commercial bank lending, which is smaller than its fund raising, has caused excess liquidity on the banking side. In order to control excess liquidity in the banking industry so that rupiah exchange rate and macroeconomic stability remain under control, Bank Indonesia has sterilized through the sale of SBI instruments. Conditions where banks are still experiencing excess liquidity, while business risks in the real sector are still increasing, causing SBI portfolios in commercial bank assets to increase. By the end of August 2000, the investment of commercial bank funds in the SBI had reached Rp 79.52 trillion, an increase of Rp 7.28 trillion compared to the end of 1999. Judging per group of banks, in addition to foreign banks planting in SBI, the entire group of banks has increased. The largest increase was owned by the group of persero banks which increased by IDR 5.91 trillion, while foreign banks decreased by IDR 5.53 trillion. In relation to the development of the SBI interest rate, it can be stated that the determination is carried out through market mechanisms by considering the target of primary money (base money). Taking into account macroeconomic conditions, especially price developments, which areexpected to continue towards the end of the year, Bank Indonesia is of the view that the SBI interest rate, which currently ranges from 13% to 14%, still needs to be maintained. Answer: Dear Members of the Council, Based on data from July 1999, it is estimated that the projected figures for bank loans up to December 2000 are as follows: - State-owned banks RP. 162,639 trillion - Recapitalization Program Participating Banks IDR 43,359 trillion - Private Banks (excluding foreign banks) IDR 48,288 trillion - Sum IDR 254,286 trillion Some of the dominant factors that affect the level of credit development provided by banks to customers will depend on several factors, namely: (1) Credit Requests If you look at the data in the table in question number 7, the number of loans in December 1998 amounting to Rp. 545 trillion dropped to Rp. 277 trillion in December 1999. This decrease was due to the transfer of bad category loans to IBRA as one of the conditions for banks to participate in the recapitalization program. Future credit demand is expected to come from the following alternatives: - Providing credit to new customers, - Provision of additional kredit for old debtors in the context of business expansion, - Providing additional credit to customers who have been restructured by IBRA. Loans for new customers have been carried out by banks, but most of them are consumer loans and small and medium enterprise loans where the impact on the overall credit portfolio is still relatively small. The demand for additional credit from debtors who are already bank customers has also not increased because the market absorption is still relatively low. Requestsfor additional loans for restructured customers are still relatively small considering that the bank restructuring process has not been completely completed and there are internal constraints in the bank because the restructured loans cannot be directly categorized into Lancar (maximum Less Current) so the bank needs to form a Receivables Write-off Reserve that can burden the bank's CAR. (2) Credit Non-Payment Risk (default risk) Most banks think that the risk of non-payment of credit is still relatively high considering that economic conditions have not recovered due to various factors (politics and security). This is especially true for corporate customers who are not well known by banks. Although credit can be given, banks charge a higher risk premium y ang will burden the debtor. (3) Alternatives to Fund Planting There is still an alternative to investing bank funds in the form of SBI where default risk does not exist and is not required to form reserves and is not included in the risk calculation in the CAR. Under conditions of relatively high default risk, SBI is the safest temporary planting alternative even though the bank does not obtaina large enough margi n. (4) Internal Constraints (CAR, BMPK, and adequate liquidity available) There are still some banks that have limited CAR to reach 8% in 2001 so that banks face CAR constraints in increasing their creditportfolios with plans to achieve 8% CAR in the year 2001. In addition, there are still several banks that are ready to disburse loans to former customers who have been restructured by IBRA but face obstacles related to BMPK violations. There arealso some banks that are experiencing liquidity difficulties so they have not been able to increase their credit portfolios. Question: 11. text_original: PENJELASAN GUBERNUR BANK INDONESIA PADA RAPAT KERJA KOMISI IX DPR RI TANGGAL 11 OKTOBER 2000 Masa Persidangan : II Tahun Sidang : 2000 - 2001 Anggota Dewan yang terhormat. Pertama-tama kami mengucapkan terima kasih kepada Pimpinan Komisi IX DPR RI beserta seluruh Anggota Komisi yang telah mengundang kami pada Rapat Kerja hari ini. Bagi kami, pertemuan dengan Anggota Dewan yang terhormat seperti ini mempunyai arti yang sangat penting untuk menyampaikan informasi mengenai pelaksanaan tugas Bank Indonesia yang telah diamanatkan oleh Dewan. Pertemuan ini juga penting sekaligus untuk mendengarkan masukan Anggota Dewan kepada kami dalam mengupayakan berbagai perbaikan dalam perumusan dan pelaksanaan tugas Bank Indonesia ke depan. Sebagaimana Anggota Dewan telah maklumi bersama, Rapat Kerja rutin terakhir yang kami hadiri adalah pada tanggal 19 Juni 2000. Dalam pertemuan tersebut kami telah menjelaskan mengenai perkembangan ekonomi dan moneter serta langkah-langkah kebijakan yang ditempuh Bank Indonesia hingga periode Juni 2000. Selanjutnya kami juga telah menghadiri beberapa pertemuan dan Rapat Kerja dengan Anggota Dewan untuk membahas hal-hal khusus dimana yang terakhir diadakan kemarin hari Selasa 10 Oktober 2000 untuk membahas mengenai permasalahan BLBI. Pada kesempatan Rapat Kerja hari ini, perkenankanlah kami menyampaikan perkembangan terakhir atas langkah-langkah kebijakan yang telah ditempuh Bank Indonesia selama triwulan III/2000. Anggota Dezwanyang terhormat Secara umum, beberapa indikator penting ekonomi makro sampai dengan akhir triwulan III/2000 menunjukkan proses pemulihan ekonomi kita terus berlangsung. Pertumbuhan ekonomi pada triwulan III/2000 diperkirakan pada kisaran 4%-5%, setelah mencatat 4,13% pada triwulan sebelumnya. Peningkatan kegiatan investasi dan ekspor yang teijadi pada dua triwulan sebelumnya diperkirakan akan terus berlanjut, sedangkan konsumsi diperkirakan masih mengalami 1 pertumbuhan positif meskipun semakin melambat. Secara sektoral, peningkatan kegiatan ekonomi terutama ditunjang oleh sektor industri pengolahan, perdagangan, bangunan dan pengangkutan. Terus membaiknya perekonomian juga didukung oleh mulai berlangsungnya penyaluran kredit baru oleh perbankan meskipun masih dalam jumlah yang relatif kecil. Sementara itu, nilai tukar Rupiah dalam triwulan III/2000 cenderung melemah dan rata-rata mencapai Rp 8.737,- atau terdepresiasi sebesar 5,8% dibandingkan triwulan sebelumnya. Melemahnya nilai tukar rupiah tersebut adalah sebagai akibat dari perkembangan beberapa faktor ^perti meningkatnya permintaan valuta asing khususnya untuk membiayai impor dan melunasi utang luar negeri yang jatuh tempo, terbatasnya penawaran valuta asing terutama karena relatif kecilnya devisa ekspor yang masuk ke dalam negeri dan masih negatifnya lalu lintas modal swasta bersih, serta kurang kondusifnya faktor-faktor sentimen pasar terhadap perkembangan sosial-politik dalam negeri. Di sisi lain, tekanan terhadap harga yang terjadi sejak triwulan I dan II/ 2000 masih berlanjut hingga triwulan III/2000. Laju inflasi IHK selama triwulan III-2000 meningkat sebesar 1,74%, lebih rendah dibandingkan triwulan sebelumnya sebesar 1,91%. Dengan perkembangan ini, secara kumulatif untuk periode Januari hingga September 2000 laju inflasi IHK telah mencapai 4,65%. Angka ini berarti mendekati batas bawah dari kisaran sasaran inflasi dengan memperhitungkan kebijakan Pemerintah di bidang harga dan pendapatan yang ditetapkan pada awal tahun 2000 sebesar 5-7%. Salah satu faktor yang menyebabkan tingginya inflasi sampai cfengan triwulan III/2000 adalah terkait dengan dampak dari kebijakan Pemerintah di bidang harga dan pendapatan. Sebagaimana Anggota Dewan maklumi, Pemerintah mulai April telah melakukan penyesuaian harga pada beberapa sektor ekonomi seperti kenaikan gaji PNS, harga BBM, TDL, cukai rokok serta terakhir kenaikan tarif angkutan pada tanggal 1 September 2000. Pada awal tahun 2000, berdasarkan informasi yang tersedia waktu itu, kebijakan tersebut diperkirakan akan berdampak pada kenaikan inflasi sebesar 2%. Akan tetapi, hingga September 2000 kebijakan tersebut telah memberikan pengaruh baik secara langsung maupun tidak langsung terhadap inflasi sebesar 1,73%. Dengan perhitungan tersebut, laju inflasi IHK kumulatif 9 bulan pertama tahun 2000 di luar dampak kebijakan pemerintah di bidang harga dan pendapatan telah mencapai 2,85%, atau telah mendekati batas bawah dari kisaran sasaran inflasi 3%-5% yang ditetapkan pada awal tahun 2000. Inflasi pada triwulan laporan juga dipengaruhi oleh melemahnya nilai tukar rupiah. Kecenderungan depresiasi nilai tukar rupiah telah meningkatkan harga barang-barang yang dapat diperdagangkan secara internasional (traded goods). Inflasi kelompok traded goods pada triwulan III-2000 mencapai 0,86% atau lebih rendah dari triwulan sebelumnya sebesar 1,87%. Hal ini didorong oleh lebih rendahnya depresiasi rupiah pada triwulan ini dan bahkan cenderung menguat setelah melemah bulan Juli 2000. Untuk kelompok non-traded goods, inflasi pada triwulan III-2000 mencapai 3,40% atau lebih tinggi dari triwulan sebelumnya sebesar 1,84%. Anggota Dezwanyang terhormat, Untuk triwulan IV/2000 ini kami perkirakan tekanan terhadap inflasi masih akan cukup besar. Hal ini terutama berkaitan dengan dampak kenaikan harga BBM per 1 Oktober 2000, kenaikan tahap II gaji PNS, TNI dan POLRI dan pengaruh inflasi musiman di akhir tahun sehubungan dengan Hari Raya, Natal, Tahun Baru yang akan datang secara bersamaan. Di samping itu, pengeluaran pemerintah dalam jumlah besar menjelang tutup tahun anggaran diperkirakan juga akan berdampak pada tekanan laju inflasi. Dengan mempertimbangkan faktor-faktor ini, laju inflasi IHK laju inflasi hingga akhir tahun 2000 diprakirakan akan melampaui sasaran yang telah ditetapkan di awal tahun, yaitu sekitar 1% di atas sasaran. Berkaitan dengan hal tersebut, maka perkenankan kami dalam kesempatan ini menjelaskan mengenai beberapa faktor yang menurut hemat kami berpotensi menyebabkan tidak tercapainya sasaran inflasi pada tahun ini. Pertama^ dampak kenaikan harga dan pendapatan yang dikendalikan Pemerintah untuk keseluruhan tahun 2000 yang sebelumnya diproyeksikan sebesar 2% diprakirakan akan terlampaui. Hal ini terutama karena sulitnya untuk memperkirakan dengan tepat, kapan dan besarnya implementasi kenaikan berbagai harga dan pendapatan yang dikendalikan oleh Pemerintah, meskipun Bank Indonesia telah melakukan koordinasi dengan Pemerintah sebelum sasaran inflasi ditetapkan. Sebagai contoh, penundaan kenaikan harga BBM selain Premix dan Super dari April menjadi Oktober, misalnya, tidak diperhitungkan dalam perkiraan awal. Meski kenaikannya ditunda, harga-harga telah sempat naik pada awal April. Demikian pula persentasi kenaikan harga yang terjadi tidak seluruhnya sama dengan asumsi yang digunakan dalam perkiraan awal, antara lain kenaikan UMR Jabotabek yang diasumsikan naik satu kali sebesar 25% dalam realisasinya naik dua kali sebesar total 45%. Hal lain yang diprakirakan berpotensi mendorong laju inflasi dari sisi fiskal adalah kemungkinan pengeluaran pemerintah dalam jumlah besar yang akan dilakukan menjelang berakhirnya tahun anggaran pada bulan Desember tahun 2000. Kedua^ nilai tukar Rupiah rata-rata yang sebelumnya diperkirakan dapat mencapai Rp7.000 per USD, sampai bulan September 2000 sudah mencapai Rp8.125 per USD. Secara umum, melesetnya perkiraan asumsi ini disebabkan karena lebih sensitifnya perkembangan nilai tukar rupiah terhadap sentimen negatif pasar terhadap faktor nonekonomi dibandingkan sensitivitas sentimen positif pasar terhadap membaiknya faktor ekonomi. Melemahnya nilai tukar rupiah tersebut selanjutnya akan meningkatkan laju inflasi melalui kenaikan harga barang-barang yang diperdagangkan di pasar internasional. Ketiga, beberapa perkembangan di sisi penawaran sampai kuartal III/2000, baik berupa dampak positif atau negatif terhadap pencapaian sasaran inflasi, juga sangat sulit untuk diperkirakan dengan baik. Membanjirnya beras impor dibarengi musim panen kedua dalam bulan September 2000 telah memberikan dampak positif berupa deflasi, sedangkan kelangkaan BBM dan terganggunya saluran distribusi BBM pada bulan Juli 2000 memberikan dampak negatif berupa inflasi. Keempat, pertumbuhan PDB tahun 2000 diprakirakan akan melampui asumsi proyeksi pertumbuhan ekonomi yang digunakan dalam inflasi sebesar 3% - 4%. Meningkatnya kegiatan ekonomi yang lebih cepat dari yang diprakirakan sebelumnya menyebabkan kelebihan kapasitas perekonomian yang ada saat ini mulai berkurang serta jumlah base money riil dan Ml riil meningkat. Dapat diinformasikan, sampai bulan Agustus 2000 rata-rata Ml riil mengalami pertumbuhan sebesar 19,7%, jauh lebih tinggi dibandingkan negatif 8,8% pada Desember 1999. Meningkatnya kegiatan ekonomi tersebut juga sejalan dengan kenaikan laju inflasi dari sisi permintaan (core inflation) yang telah terjadi sejak akhir triwulan 1/2000. Anggota Dewan yang terhormat. Pertanvaan: 3. Bagaimana pelaksanaan Program Restrukturisasi atau Rescheduling Hutang Luar Negeri, baik hutang luar negeri Pemerintah maupun hutang luar negeri swasta? Jawaban: Anggota Dewan yang terhormat, Sebagaimana diketahui, upaya restrukturisasi hutang Pemerintah dilakukan melalui dua mekanisme yakni Paris Club dan London Club, masing-masing untuk restrukturisasi pinjaman bilateral dan pinjaman komersiil Pemerintah Indonesia. Upaya restrukturisasi kewajiban tersebut dilakukan Pemerintah dalam kerangka mengurangi tekanan defisit atas fiskal maupun tekanan terhadap Neraca Pembayaran Indonesia. Program ini secara implisit juga telah memperoleh persetujuan DPR sebagaimana tercermin pada persetujuan Sidang Dewan atas RAPBN yang diajukan oleh Pemerintah. Program restrukturisasi tercermin pada pos pengeluaran pembayaran angsuran pokok pinjaman pada RAPBN dimaksud. Pelaksanaan program melalui masing-masing mekanisme tersebut dapat dijelaskan sebagai berikut: 1. Paris Club I: Negosiasi dengan 17 negara anggota Paris Club intensif dilakukan sejak Agustus 1998. Pemerintah mengupayakan restrukturisasi atas pinjaman bilateral yang jatuh tempo selama FY. 1998 dan 1999. Persyaratan pinjaman yang direstrukturisasi merujuk pada peijanjian asal. Pinjaman-pinjaman tersebut umumnya berjangka waktu antara 20 s.d 24 tahun untuk ODA dan 10 sampai 15 tahun untuk Non-ODA. Kesepakatan restrukturisasi dengan kreditur tertuang dalam MOU yang ditandatangani kedua belah pihak pada tanggal 23 September 1998, dengan pokok-pokok kesepakatan: (pertama) restrukturisasi atas kewajiban pembayaran pokok pinjaman bilateral jatuh tempo antara tgl.06/08/98 s.d 31/03/00 senilai USD4,2 milyar. (kedua) Pinjaman ODA direstrukturisasi untuk jangka waktu 20 tahun termasuk 5 tahun masa tenggang, dan pinjaman Non -ODA direstrukturisasi untuk jangka waktu 11 tahun termasuk 3 tahun masa tenggang. (ketiga) Pemerintah Indonesia wajib melakukan comparable treatment atas kewajiban pembayaran pinjaman bilateral lainnya (diluar anggota PC) dan kewajiban atas pinjaman komersiil yang diterima oleh Pemerintah. Sebagai implementasi kes epakatan MOU tersebut, Pemerintah mengajukan permintaan restrukturisasi secara bilateral kepada masing-masing kreditur yang bersangkutan. Total pinjaman yang direstrukturisasi adalah USD4,66 milyar. Jumlah ini termasuk kewajiban pinjaman sindikasi senilai USD210 juta yang dilakukan melalui mekanisme London Club. Sebagai implementasi MOU PC I, Pemerintah telah menandatangani perjanjian restrukturisasi kewajiban pembayaran angsuran pokok kepada 17 negara donor anggota PC, senilai USD4,38 milyar pada akhir Maret 2000. Dapat diinformasikan bahwa perbedaan jumlah ini dengan nilai yang terdapat dalam MOU semata disebabkan oleh perubahan nilai tukar. Disamping itu Pemerintah juga telah menandatangani perjanjian restrukturisasi kewajiban kepada 2 negara bukan anggota (Saudi Arabia dan Brunei) dan 5 bank komersiil, senilai USD 70,85 juta. Upaya penyelesaian negosiasi masih terus dilakukan terhadap 3 negara non- anggota PC (Taiwan, Kuwait dan China) dengan total kewajiban senilai USD 18 juta. Berapa proyeksi inflasi akhir Tahun Anggaran 2000 dan upaya apa yang dilakukan Bank Indonesia untuk menekan inflasi tersebut? Jawaban : Anggota Dewan yang terhormat, Sebagaimana diketahui, laju inflasi IHK kumulatif bulan Januari hingga September 2000 telah mencapai 4,65%, atau semakin mendekati batas bawah dari kisaran sasaran laju inflasi secara keseluruhan tahun sebesar 5%-7%. Kebijakan Pemerintah di bidang harga dan pendapatan (administered price and income policy) seperti kenaikan harga BBM, tarif angkulan, tarif dasar listrik, cukai rokok, gaji PNS dan UMR merupakan penyebab utama dari tingginya laju inflasi hingga September 2000. Dari keseluruhan laju inflasi IHK tersebut, sekitar 1,73% berasal dari dampak kebijakan pemerintah di bidang harga dan pendapatan, baik dampak langsung maupun tidak langsung. Dengan perhitungan tersebut, laju inflasi IHK kumulatif 9 bulan pertama tahun 2000 di luar dampak kebijakan pemerintah di bidang harga dan pendapatan telah mencapai 2,85%, atau telah mendekati batas bawah dari kisaran inflasi 3%-5% yang menjadi sasaran Bank Indonesia. Tekanan inflasi ini diperkirakan masih akan berlangsung pada triwulan keempat tahun 2000. Kebijakan pemerintah di bidang tarif angkutan dan kenaikan harga BBM diperkirakan akan menimbulkan dampak baik secara langsung maupun tidak langsung terhadap inflasi bulan Oktober dan November mendatang. Selain itu adanya faktor musiman yaitu hari raya keagamaan yang akan terjadi bersamaan (Lebaran, Natal dan Tahun Baru) di akhir tahun 2000 diperkirakan akan meningkatkan harga-harga pada bulan Desember mendatang. Tekanan-tekanan harga tersebut diperkirakan akan mendorong laju inflasi IHK pada triwulan IV sekitar 3%-4% (q-t-q). Melihat perkembangan tersebut di atas, maka laju inflasi selama tahun 2000 diperkirakan akan berada sekitar 1% di atas sasaran. Dalam perkiraan IHK tersebut telah pula memperhitungkan dampak kebijakan pemerintah di bidang harga dan pendapatan terhadap IHK yang diperkirakan di atas proyeksi semula sebesar 2%. Meningkatnya tekanan terhadap inflasi dan kurs rupiah mengharuskan Bank Indonesia untuk menempuh kebijakan moneter yang cenderung ketat (tight-bias) dengan mengupayakan sasaran uang primer yang ditetapkan. Beberapa faktor dipertimbangkan dalam implementasi kebijakan moneter yang cenderung ketat tersebut. Pertama, perlu disadari bahwa melemahnya kurs rupiah (dan dampaknya secara langsung terhadap inflasi) lebih banyak disebabkan oleh faktor-faktor non- ekonomi. Ini terutama tercermin dari meningkatnya premi resiko, diukur dengan premi swap atau yield spread antara Yankee Bond Indonesia dengan T-bills, yang cenderung meningkat untuk semua tenor sejak April 2000. Kedua, meningkatnya tekanan terhadap inflasi banyak dipengaruhi oleh kebijakan pemerintah di bidang harga dan pendapatan (tarfi listrik, harga premix, tarif angkutan, gaji PNS dan UMR). Ketiga, ekses likuiditas pada perbankan selama ini didorong oleh belum pulihnya sektor riil khususnya karena proses restrukturisasi utang dan perusahaan yang masih berlangsung. Dalam kondisi demikian, portofolio aset perbankan lebih banyak pada SBI dan obligasi pemerintah. Keempat, pertumbuhan uang primer yang cukup tinggi lebih banyak didorong oleh peningkatan permintaan uang kartal oleh masyarakat baik untuk kebutuhan transaksi maupun untuk beijaga-jaga. Kegiatan ekonomi yang lebih cepat dari asumsi-asumsi semula menyebabkan sasaran uang primer yang ditetapkan akhir tahun 1999 menjadi terlalu ketat. Pada waktu itu pertumbuhan ekonomi, inflasi dan kurs rupiah untuk tahun 2000 diasumsikan masing-masing sebesar 2,50 persen, 5 persen, dan Rp7000 per US dollar. Dengan kondisi seperti di atas, tidaklah rasional apabila upaya stabilisasi makro melalui kebijakan moneter dilakukan secara berlebihan. Stabilisasi kurs rupiah dan pengendalian inflasi dengan pengetatan kebijakan moneter secara drastis akan menyebabkan suku bunga melambung tinggi dan mengancam proses pemulihan ekonomi. Dalam hubungan ini, pengetatan moneter tetap perlu dilakukan dengan kerangka pencapaian sasaran uang primer, dengan mempertimbangkan lebih tingginya pertumbuhan ekonomi dibandingkan dengan asumsi semula, sebagai patokan kerja. Strategi ini dibarengi dengan langkah-langkah yang secara langsung meminimalkan volatilitas kurs rupiah, khususnya yang berasal dari spekulasi, dengan penegakan ketentuan yang lebih tegas atas aturan-aturan prudensial di bidang devisa (antara lain posisi devisa neto dan pembatasan transaksi forward jual kepada non- residen). Dengan kata lain, kebijakan moneter yang cenderung ketat tersebut perlu dipandang sebagai upaya temporer untuk meningkatkan kepercayaan pasar. Setelah kepercayaan kembali normal dan premi resiko mulai menurun, ruang gerak untuk penurunan suku bunga diharapkan dapat lebih longgar untuk mendorong pemulihan ekonomi. Pertanvaan: 7. Mengapa terjadi peningkatan yang masih besar atas Penyimpanan Dana Ketiga (PDK) pada bank-bank BUMN? Apakah bank swasta sangat likuid karena telah berani mengucurkan kredit? Berapa proyeksi bunga SBI pada akhir Tahun Anggaran 2000? Jawaban : Anggota Dewan yang terhormat, Mengingat pertanyaan nomor 7 dan 9 saling berkaitan, perkenankanlah kami menjawabnya sekaligus, Sejalan dengan semakin membaiknya kepercayaan masyarakat kepada perbankan dana pihak ketiga yang dihimpun bank umum terus menunjukkan peningkatan. Sampai dengan akhir Agustus 2000, dana pihak ketiga rupiah yang berhasil dihimpun bank umum dari masyarakat telah mencapai Rp 525,40 triliun, atau meningkat sebesar Rp 32,53 triliun bila dibandingkan dengan posisi pada akhir tahun 1999. Peningkatan DPK rupiah tersebut bersumber dari peningkatan giro Rp 22,36 triliun dan tabungan Rp 25,09 triliun. Sementara itu, deposito yang berhasil dikumpulkan bank umum mengalami penurunan sebesar Rp 14,92 triliun. Dilihat dari kelompok bank, peningkatan DPK rupiah perbankan icrjadi pada semua kelompok kecuali bank asing. Peningkatan DPK rupiah terbesar dialami oleh kelompok bank persero yang naik sebesar Rp 22,72 triliun. Peningkatan yang tinggi dari DPK bank persero kemungkinan disebabkan masih tingginya tingkat kepercayaan masyarakat terhadap kelompok bank persero. Pesatnya penghimpunan dana tidak diikuti oleh penyaluran dalam bentuk kredit oleh perbankan. Total kredit yang telah disalurkan bank umum sampai dengan Agustus 2000 baru mencapai Rp 267,61 triliun. Jumlah tersebut masihlah sangat rendah jika dibandingkan dengan penghimpunan dana yang dilakukan. Kondisi ini menunjukkan penyaluran dana yang dihimpun perbankan belum dilakukan secara optimal yang juga tercermin dari sangat rendahnya rasio loan to deposit (LDR). Nilai LDR perbankan menurun dari 78,31% pada Desember 1996 menjadi 32,24 pada Agustus 2000. Dilihat dari jenis bank, peningkatan penyaluran kredit tertinggi dimiliki oleh kelompok bank swasta yang mencapai Rp 11,50 triliun. Di sisi lain, peningkatan penyaluran kredit oleh bank persero mengalami penurunan terbesar yaitu sebesar Rp 10,59 triliun. Lebih tingginya kredit yang disalurkan oleh bank swasta dibanding bank persero antara lain berkaitan dengan proses rekapitalisasi terhadap bank swasta yang dilakukan lebih dulu dibandingkan terhadap bank persero. Hal ini terlihat dari CAR bank swasta yang lebih tinggi dibanding bank persero. Pada Agustus 2000, CAR dari kelompok bank swasta sebesar 8,25% sementara CAR bank persero sebesar 4,25%. Dapat kami kemukakan bahwa masih rendahnya penyaluran kredit perbankan disebabkan baik oleh sisi eksternal maupun internal perbankan. Di sisi eksternal, khususnya sektor riil, krisis yang teijadi menyebabkan kualitas finansial dunia usaha menjadi sangat rendah. Hal ini membuat perbankan enggan untuk menyalurkan danany dalam bentuk kredit, meskipun disinyalir terdapat permintaan kredit oleh sektor riil. Di sisi internal, keengganan perbankan utuk menyalurkan kredit dipengaruhi oleh proses penyesuaian terhadap pemenuhan modal minimum (CAR). Perkembangan tersebut dapat dikatakan memberi indikasi terjadinya credit crunch. Kecenderungan teijadinya credit crunch diperkuat dengan nilai LDR yang semakin menurun dan adanya penyesuaian portofolio yang dilakukan oleh perbankan ke dalam penanaman lain seperti surat berharga, pasar uang antar bank, dan SBI. Guna mendorong penyaluran kredit, pemerintah dan Bank Indonesia telah melakukan upaya untuk memulihkan kondisi perbankan dari krisis melalui rekapitalisasi dan restrukturisasi perbankan yang menurut rencana akan selesai pada bulan Oktober 2000. Selain itu, Bank Indonesia juga telah melakukan penyempurnaan ketentuan dan peningkatan pemantapan pengawasan bank, antara lain melalui pengaturan kembali ketentuan (relaksasi) masing-masing tentang Batas Maksimum Pemberian Kredit (BMPK), penilaian Aktiva Produktif dalam penghitungan Aktiva Tertimbang Menurut Resiko (ATMR), dan kriteria penyertaan modal yang harus ditarik kembali. Perkembangan penyaluran kredit bank umum yang lebih kecil dari penghimpunan dananya menyebabkan terjadinya kelebihan likuiditas di sisi perbankan. Dalam rangka mengendalikan kelebihan likuiditas perbankan tersebut agar kestabilan nilai tukar rupiah dan perekonomian makro tetap dapat terkendali, Bank Indonesia melakukan sterilisasi melalui penjualan instrumen SBI. Kondisi dimana perbankan masih mengalami kelebihan likuiditas, sementara risiko usaha di sektor riil masih tinggi menyebabkan portofolio SBI dalam aset bank umum mengalami peningkatan. Sampai dengan akhir Agustus 2000, penanaman dana bank umum di dalam SBI telah mencapai Rp 79,52 triliun atau meningkat sebesar Rp 7,28 triliun dibanding akhir tahun 1999. Dilihat per kelompok bank, selain bank asing penanaman dalam SBI seluruh kelompok bank mengalami peningkatan. Peningkatan terbesar dimiliki oleh kelompok bank persero yang meningkat sebesar Rp 5,91 triliun, sementara bank asing menurun sebesar Rp 5,53 triliun. Berkaitan dengan perkembangan suku bunga SBI dapat dikemukakan bahwa penentuannya dilakukan melalui mekanisme pasar dengan mempertimbangkan target uang primer (base money). Dengan memperhatikan kondisi ekonomi makro khususnya perkembangan harga yang diperkirakan masih akan cenderung mningkat menjelang akhir tahun, bank Indonesia berpandangan bahwa suku bunga SBI yang saat ini berkisar antara 13% - 14% masih perlu dipertahankan. Peningkatan outflow karena penggantian terhadap Uang Kertas yang dicabut dari peredaran (pecahan Rp50.000 seri Soeharto, Rp20.000,- seri Cendrawasih dan Rpl 0.000,- seri Sri Sultan Hamengkubuwono) a.iii. Bank BUMN b. Bank Rekap Swasta c. Bank Swasta Harap dijelaskan faktor dominan yang mempengaruhi tingkat perkembangan tersebut. Jawaban : Anggota Dewan yang terhormat, Atas dasar data sejak bulan Juli 1999 diperkirakan angka proyeksi kredit perbankan sampai dengan bulan Desember 2000 adalah sebagai berikut: - Bank BUMN Rp. 162.639 triliun - Bank Peserta Program Rekapitalisasi Rp. 43.359 triliun - Bank Swasta (tidak termasuk bank asing) Rp. 48.288 triliun - Jumlah Rp. 254.286 triliun Beberapa faktor dominan yang mempengaruhi tingkat perkembangan kredit yang diberikan oleh bank kepada nasabah akan tergantung beberapa faktor, yakni: (1) Permintaan Kredit Apabila dilihat data dalam tabel pada pertanyaan nomor 7, jumlah kredit pada bulan Desember 1998 sebesar Rp. 545 triliun turun menjadi Rp. 277 triliun pada bulan Desember 1999. Penurunan ini sebagai akibat pengalihan kredit kategori macet ke BPPN sebagai salah satu syarat bagi bank untuk ikut program rekapitalisasi. Permintaan kredit di masa yang akan datang diperkirakan akan berasal dari alternatif sebagai berikut: - Pemberian kredit kepada nasabah baru, - Pemberian tambahan kredit untuk debitur lama dalam rangka expansi usaha, - Pemberian kredit tambahan kepada nasabah yang sudah direstrukturisasi oleh BPPN. Kredit untuk nasabah baru sudah dilakukan oleh bank-bank, namun sebagian besar adalah kredit konsumsi dan kredit usaha kecil serta menengah dimana pengaruhnya terhadap portfolio kredit secara keseluruhan masih relatif kecil. Permintaan tambahan kredit dari debitur yang sudah menjadi nasabah bank juga belum begitu meningkat karena daya serap pasar masih relatif rendah. Permintaan tambahan kredit untuk nasabah yang sudah direstrukturisasi masih relatif kecil mengingat proses restrukturisasi bank belum seluruhnya selesai dan adanya kendala intern di bank karena kredit yang direstruktur tidak dapat langsung dikategorikan menjadi Lancar (maksimum Kurang Lancar) sehingga bank perlu membentuk Cadangan Penghapusan Piutang yang dapat membebani CAR bank. (2) Risiko Tidak Terbayarnya Kredit {default risk) Sebagian besar bank beranggapan bahwa risiko tidak terbayarnya kredit masih relatif tinggi mengingat kondisi ekonomi belum pulih karena berbagai faktor (politik dan keamanan). Hal ini terutama untuk nasabah-nasabah korporasi yang belum dikenal baik oleh bank. Meskipun kredit dapat diberikan namun bank mengenakan risk premium yang lebih tinggi yang akan memberatkan debitur. (3) Alternatif Penanaman Dana Masih terdapat alternatif penanaman dana bank dalam bentuk SBI dimana default risk tidak ada dan tidak diharuskan untuk membentuk cadangan serta tidak masuk dalam perhitungan risiko dalam CAR. Dalam kondisi default risk relatif tinggi maka SBI merupakan alternatif penanaman sementara yang paling aman meskipun bank tidak memperoleh margin yang cukup besar. (4) Kendala Intern (CAR, BMPK, dan tersedianva likuiditas yang memadai) Masih terdapat beberapa bank yang mempunyai CAR terbatas untuk mencapai 8% tahun 2001 sehingga bank menghadapi kendala CAR dalam meningkatkan portofolio kreditnya berkaitan dengan rencana pencapaian CAR 8% pada tahun 2001. Disamping itu masih terdapat beberapa bank yang siap mengucurkan kredit kepada eks nasabah yang telah direstrukturisasi oleh BPPN namun menghadapi kendala yang berkaitan dengan pelanggaran BMPK. Juga terdapat beberapa bank yang mengalami kesulitan likuiditas sehingga belum dapat meningkatkan portofolio kreditnya. Pertanyaan : 11.
