Title: Pidato Deputi Gubernur, Muliaman D. Hadad Pada Forum Komunikasi Perbankan Syariah (FKPS)
text: KEYNOTE POINTERS ADDRESS OF THE DEPUTY GOVERNOR ON SHARIA BANKING COMMUNICATION FORUM (FKPS) OF BANK INDONESIA. JAKARTA, August 3rd, 2009 Topics: Windows of Opportunity Islamic Banking : It's Time to Actualize the Potential and Advantages Bismillahirrahmanirrahim. Which I respect, - The leadership of Sharia banking, BUS, UUS including BPD Syariah, and BPRS - Members of the Islamic Banking Committee - Happy invitees and ladies and gentlemen Assalamu'alaikuni warahmatullahi wa barakatuh and peace be upon you, Introduction : expressions of gratitude, shalawat, and hope 1. An invitation to always be grateful to the hadlirat of Allah SWT, which only with His permission can we meet at the Islamic Banking Communication Forum (FKPS) at noon today, which alhamdulillah was also attended by members Sharia Banking Committee (PPP). 2. It is a joy for me andpat to be present in the midst of the islamic banking leaders , experts in PPP, as well as Islamic banking activists , through the regularly FKPS forum to: to be continued, exchange thoughts, share information, and discuss issues in the Islamic banking industry. To jointly advance Islamic banking, turn all ''potentials", opportunities, and advantages into "actual", so that its benefits can be increasingly felt by all Indonesians without exception. 3. Previously, at the first PPP meeting, I was also present at the Begawan Lounge accompanying Mrs. Fadjrijah to participate in discussions and discussions on the issues raised by PPP members in develop Islamic banking going forward. Encouragement to actualize potential, advantages and work on opportunities 4. Gradually, the level of public awareness and curiosity about the presence of shari'a banks we have witnessed has increased. This is a capital and at the same time an opportunity for the Islamic banking industry, to turn awareness into enthusiasm to try the wealth of Islamic banking iB (ai-Bi) products and feel the advantages ''More than Just a Bank" (beyond banking). 5. This is the time for, is the window of opportunity for Islamic banks to show their advantages. And proved his promises, as many were socialized through various electronic and print media, in newspapers, radio and television. This is the time for Islamic banks to prove: - Are Islamic banks "mutually beneficial to customers and banks"? - Do Islamic banks have more diverse products? - Are Islamic banks able to provide services as well as other bank services? - Are Islamic banks "more than just banks"? 6. Good opportunities demand a timely response and the strength of commitment to overcome any challenges that come their way. The opportunity will not come twice, and only with seriousness and hard work, the opportunity will turn into a concrete result as expected, that is, the increase in the number of accounts in Islamic banks from the current 5.3 million accounts (position in June 2009) - accelerate the growth and share of the industry even greater. 7. The implementation of the ''Grand Strategy for The Development of the Islamic Banking Market" needs to be carried out seriously by all Islamic bank actors and Islamic bank activists. Several things need to continue to be done by Islamic banks, so that this golden opportunity can be utilized to expand the market so as to enlarge its role in the national financial system, namely: - The commitment to carry out universal, inclusive and open communication for all segments of society about Islamic banks needs to continue to be carried out, so that the benefits of Islamic banks can be understood and enjoyed by all groups of Indonesian society without exception. - Positioning Islamic Banks as " mutually beneficial banking for both parties" which is supported by the uniqueness of iB (ai-Bi), namely more diverse products with more varied schemes . And it displays the new branding of Islamic banks as ''more than just a bank" (beyond banking). - Develop innovative products in exploring the wealth / variation of sharia-based financial schemes, so that they can meet the needs of modern society that continues to develop issues: revitalization peran DSN and PPP. - Commitment to Improve the reliability and quality of service, as a manifestation of sharia values that value others, help and facilitate the affairs of others, and especially humanize others (nge-wong ke). - Commitment toUK to improve the hr competence of Islamic banks, so as to have multi-dimensional, multi-disciplinary competencies. Islamic bank human resources should have a complete knowledge of Islamic banking and finance, knowledge of the latest progress in banking and finance, and knowledge of strategies marketing and service excellence issues: industry commitment to set aside costs for HR development. Only by taking these steps and the commitment of all Islamic bank actors, the iB (ai-Bi) of Islamic banking will be able to prove all its promises as an alternative to the banking system that fairer, more profitable and more than just a bank. Some agendas ahead: The context of the KSSK and the potential for voluntary funds 8. In the context of the benefits of Islamic banks for the national economy, Bank Indonesia has a high commitment to continue to participate in developing the Islamic financial and banking industry in Indonesia. Development is carried out by always referring to other strategic plans that are nationwide, such as the Indonesian Financial System Architecture (ASKI), the dual banking system framework banking architecture Indonesia (API), the National Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMN) and the National Long-Term Development Plan (RPJPN). Thus, efforts to develop Islamic banking are part and activities that support the achievement of strategic plans on a larger scale at the national level, so that the benefits will be able to be enjoyed oleh all Indonesian people without exception. 9. Another benefit and advantage of the presence of Islamic banks is the role of Islamic banks in supporting the national economy through the empowerment of the social sector (voluntary sector), both in the form of management and distribution of funds Zakat, Infaq, Shadaqoh and Waqaf. This role is the more value of Islamic banks, which is the embodiment of the value of their concern for the empowerment of the poor and weak members of society. Bank Indonesia highly appreciates the role of Islamic banks in carrying out these social procedures, either carried out individually or in collaboration with institutions managing the voluntary sector. This is the positive role of the Islamic bank industry in supporting the Government's efforts to improve the welfare of the Indonesian people. Cover 10. Finally, I hope that this Islamic Banking Communication Forum (FKPS) activity can be successful and can be utilized optimally as a two-way communication forum between banking actors. sharia with Bank Indonesia selaku regulator. In order to jointly develop the Islamic banking industry in this Indonesian homeland that we both love. Thank you and happy discussion. Billahittaufiq wal hidayah Assalamu'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh
text_original: POINTERS KEYNOTE ADDRESS DEPUTI GUBERNUR PADA FORUM KOMUNIKASI PERBANKAN SYARIAH (FKPS) BANK INDONESIA. JAKARTA, 3 AGUSTUS 2009 Topik: Windows of Opportunity Perbankan Syariah : Saatnya Mengaktualisasikan Potensi dan Kelebihan Bismillahirrahmanirrahim. Yang saya hormati, - Jajaran pimpinan perbankan syariah, BUS, UUS termasuk BPD Syariah, dan BPRS - Para anggota Komite Perbankan Syariah - Para undangan dan hadirin sekalian yang berbahagia Assalamu'alaikuni warahmatullahi wa barakatuh dan salam sejahtera, Pendahuluan : ungkapan syukur, shalawat, dan harapan 1. Ajakan untuk senantiasa bersyukur ke hadlirat Allah SWT, yang hanya dengan izin-Nya kita dapat bertemu pada Forum Komunikasi Perbankan Syariah (FKPS) pada siang hari ini, yang alhamdulillah juga dihadiri oleh anggota Komite Perbankan Syariah (KPS). 2. Merupakan sebuah kebahagiaan bagi saya dapat hadir di tengah-tengah Bapak/Ibu para pimpinan perbankan syariah, para pakar dalam KPS, serta para penggiat perbankan syariah, melalui forum regularly FKPS untuk : saling bersambung rasa, bertukar fikirart, sharing informasi, dan berdiskusi seputar permasalahan industri perbankan syariah. Untuk bersama-sama memajukan perbankan syariah, mengubah semua ''potential", opportunity, dan kelebihan menjadi "actual", sehingga kemanfaatannya dapat semakin dirasakan oleh seluruh masyarakat Indonesia tanpa terkecuali. 3. Sebelumnya, pada pertemuan KPS yang pertama, saya juga ikut hadir di Begawan Lounge mendampingi Ibu Fadjrijah mengikuti diskusi dan pembahasan mengenai beberapa isu yang dikemukakan oleh anggota KPS dalam mengembangkan perbankan syariah ke depan. Dorongan untuk mengaktualisasikan potensi, kelebihan dan menggarap peluang 4. Secara bertahap, tingkat awareness dan keingintahuan masyarakat akan kehadiran bank syariah kita saksikan telah semakin meningkat. Hal tersebut merupakan modal dan sekaligus peluang bagi industri perbankan syariah, untuk mengubah awareness menjadi antusiasme untuk mencoba kekayaan produk iB (ai-Bi) perbankan syariah dan merasakan kelebihan bank syariah yang ''Lebih dari Sekedar Bank" (beyond banking). 5. Inilah saatnya bagi, adalah window of opportunity bagi bank syariah untuk menunjukkan kelebihannya itu. Dan membuktikan janji-janjinya, sebagaimana ramai disosialisasikan melalui berbagai media elektronik dan cetak, di koran, radio dan televisi. Inilah saatnya bagi bank syariah membuktikan : - Apakah bank syariah "saling menguntungkan nasabah dan bank"? - Apakah bank syariah memiliki produk yang lebih beragam? - Apakah bank syariah mampu memberikan pelayanan sebaik pelayanan bank lainnya? - Apakah bank syariah "lebih dari sekedar bank"? 6. Peluang yang baik menuntut respon yang tepat waktu dan kekuatan komitmen untuk mengatasi segala tantangan yang menghadang. Peluang tidak akan datang dua kali, dan hanya dengan keseriusan serta kerja keras, maka peluang tersebut akan berubah menjadi hasil konkrit sebagaimana yang diharapkan, yaitu bertambahnya jumlah rekening di bank syariah dari 5,3 juta rekening pada saat ini (posisi Juni 2009) -> mengakselerasi growth dan share industri lebih besar lagi. 7. I mpiementasi ''Grand Strategy Pengembangan Pasar Perbankan Syariah" perlu dilakukan secara sungguh-sungguh oleh segenap pelaku bank syariah dan penggiat bank syariah. Beberapa hal perlu terus dilakukan oleh bank syariah, agar peluang emas ini dapat dimanfaatkan untuk melakukan ekspansi pasar sehingga memperbesar perannya dalam sistem keuangan nasional, yaitu : - Komitmen untuk melakukan komunikasi yang universal, inklusif dan terbuka bagi semua segmen masyarakat tentang bank syariah perlu terus dilakukan, sehingga kemanfaatan bank syariah dapat dipahami dan dinikmati oleh seluruh golongan masyarakat Indonesia tanpa terkecuali. - Melakukan positioning Bank Syariah sebagai "perbankan yang saling menguntungkan kedua belah pihak" yang ditunjang oleh keunikan khas iB (ai-Bi) yaitu produk yang lebih beragam dengan skema lebih variatif. Dan menampilkan branding baru bank syariah sebagai ''lebih dari sekedar bank" (beyond banking). - Melakukan pengembangan produk yang inovatif dalam mengeksplorasi kekayaan/variasi skema keuangan berbasis syariah, sehingga dapat memenuhi kebutuhan masyarakat modern yang terus berkembang isu : revitalisasi peran DSN dan KPS. - Komitmen untuk Meningkatkan reliabilitas dan kualitas pelayanan, sebagai perwujudan nilai-nilai syariah yang menghargai orang lain, membantu dan mempermudah urusan orang lain, dan terutama memanusiakan orang lain (nge-wong ke). - Komitmen untuk meningkatkan kompetensi SDM bank syariah, sehingga memiliki kompetensi yang multi dimensi, multi disiplin ilmu. SDM bank syariah seyogianya memiliki pengetahuan yang lengkap tentang perbankan dan keuangan syariah, pengetahuan tentang kemajuan terkini produk perbankan dan keuangan, maupun pengetahuan tentang strategi marketing dan service excellence isu : komitmen industri untuk menyisihkan biaya untuk pengembangan SDM. Hanya dengan melakukan langkah-langkah tersebut dan komitmen dari segenap pelaku bank syariah, maka iB (ai-Bi) perbankan syariah akan dapat membuktikan segala janji-janjinya sebagai alternatif sistem perbankan yang lebih adil, lebih menguntungkan dan lebih dari sekedar bank. Beberapa agenda ke depan : Konteks KSSK dan potensi voluntary fund 8. Dalam konteks kemanfaatan bank syariah bagi perekonomian nasional, maka Bank Indonesia memiliki komitmen yang tinggi untuk terus ikut mengembangkan industri keuangan dan perbankan syariah di Indonesia. Pengembangan dilakukan dengan selalu mengacu kepada rencana-rencana strategis lainnya yang bersifat nationwide, seperti Arsitektur Sistem Keuangan Indonesia (ASKI), kerangka dual banking system Arsitektur Perbankan Indonesia (API), Rencana Pembangunan Jangka Menengah Nasional (RPJMN) dan Rencana Pembangunan Jangka Panjang Nasional (RPJPN). Dengan demikian upaya pengembangan perbankan syariah merupakan bagian dan kegiatan yang mendukung pencapaian rencana strategis dalam skala yang lebih besar pada tingkat nasional, sehingga manfaatnya akan dapat dinikmati oleh seluruh masyarakat Indonesia seluruhnya tanpa terkecuali. 9. Kemanfaatan dan kelebihan lain dari hadirnya bank syariah adalah peran bank syariah dalam mendukung perekonomian nasional melalui pemberdayaan sektor sosial (voluntary sector), baik berupa pengelolaan dan penyaluran dana-dana Zakat, Infaq, Shadaqoh dan Waqaf. Peran ini adalah nilai lebih dari bank syariah, yang merupakan perwujudan dari value kepeduliannya terhadap pemberdayaan masyarakat miskin dan anggota masyarakat yang lemah. Bank Indonesia sangat mengapresiasi peran bank syariah dalam menjalankan fungsi sosial ini, baik yang dilakukan sendiri-sendiri ataupun bekerjasama dengan lembaga-lembaga pengelola voluntary sector. Inilah peran positif dari industri bank syariah dalam mendukung upaya Pemerintah meningkatkan kesejahteraan masyarakat Indonesia seluruhnya. Penutup 10. Akhirnya, saya berharap bahwa kegiatan Forum Komunikasi Perbankan Syariah (FKPS) ini dapat berlangsung sukses dan dapat dimanfaatkan secara maksimal sebagai forum komunikasi dua arah antara pelaku perbankan syariah dengan Bank Indonesia selaku regulator. Dalam rangka secara bersama-sama mengembangkan industri perbankan syariah di tanah air Indonesia yang sama-sama kita cintai ini. Terima kasih dan selamat berdiskusi. Billahittaufiq wal hidayah Assalamu'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh

Title: Keynote Speech Dr. Halim Alamsyah, Deputi Gubernur Bank Indonesia Pada Acara "Seminar Akhir Tahun Tentang Outlook Perbankan Syariah 2011" 24 November 2010
text: KEYNOTE SPEECH BY Dr. HALIM ALAMSYAH, DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF BANK INDONESIA AT THE "YEAR-END SEMINAR ON THE OUTLOOK OF ISLAMIC BANKING 2011" 24 NOVEMBER 2010 I respect the Leaders of Banking, Leaders of Government Institutions, Chamber of Commerce, Business Associations, Resource Persons, Academics, and happy invited Attendees Assalamu'alaikum Wr. Wb., Good Morning and Peace be upon you all. 1. First of all, let us pray for the praise and gratitude of Allah Almighty who for His permission we can gather in these four tfour to take part in the "Year-End Seminar on the Outlook of Islamic Banking 2011". On this occasion, on behalf of Bank Indonesia, I would like to express my deep sympathy and concern to the victims of natural disasters in Mentawai, Wasior andan area eruption of Mount Merapi in Yogyakarta and its surroundings. 2. The implementation of this seminar certainly has an important meaning and can be used as one of the momentums to maintain and improve the development of Islamic banking which in the last five years is very encouraging with an average growth in total assets above 33% per annum. By the end of October 2010, total Islamic banking assets had reached Rp 86 trillion. We are optimistic that this high growth rate will continue along with the increasing number of Islamic banks. Institutionally, currently the number of Islamic banks has reached 11 BUS, 23 UUS, and 146 BPRS with an office network of 1,625 offices at the end of September 2010. Geographically, the distribution of the Islamic banking network has currently reached people in more than 89 regencies/cities in 33 provinces. 3. The increasing number of Islamic banks, both the establishment of new and conversion banks, along with their service networks, including office channeling, which is supported by increasingly public socialization and education programs . it is believed that it will improve the performance of Islamic banking. The collection of third party funds (DPK) of Islamic banking in 2011 is expected to exceed the previous year, especially if sharia banks are able to take advantage of the momentum of capital inflows. Meanwhile, the increasingly solid economic fundamentals in 2011, the strengthening of the global economic recovery process, and the support of more conducive tax regulations will boost p performance. Islamic banking costs. 4. It is necessary to realize that Bank Indonesia cannot work alone in developing Islamic banking, it needs support and cooperation with various parties, such as the House of Representatives (DPR) in the preparation of the foundation of the ang-invitation negotiator; The National Sharia Council (DSN) in product innovation; and the Government in its role in the field of taxation and policy strengthening in the real sector. The birth of the Sharia Banking Law and the new Tax Law in 2009, is believed to make the climate of usaha Islamic banks more conducive, thereby increasing investor interest in entering the Islamic bank business in Indonesia. Ladies and Gentlemen, Happy Ladies and Gentlemen 5. In order to capture the opportunities of 2011 which are quite prospective, the development of the islamic banking industry in general is directed at mastering the domestic market with quality of service of international standard. The domestic-oriented development paradigm is in line with the huge potential of the domestic market and has not been fully explored. The domestic market is also an attractive investment destination in the Asian region in line with indonesia's improved rating and efforts towards investment grade in 2011. 6. Meanwhile, the policy direction for islamic banking development in 2011 was focused on the following: 95 First, improving the quality of the surveillance system in line with the rapid growth of the industry, increasingly controlled risk supervision, and the latest developments in regulatory compliance both originating from the IFSB, BIS and other international commitments, such as the G-20 and the ASEAN Economic Community (AEC). 95 Second, the development of Islamic banking human resources where in the perspective of modern management, human capital is the most important and decisive element in achieving the vision and competitive advantage of the organization. 95 Third, a co-opetition strategy to improve capacity and quality of service. Co-opetition is a combination of cooperation and competition that synergizes resources between BUS or UUS and its parent BUK. Synergy in various operational activities, such as the use of ATM networks and promotions is aimed at capturing market opportunities and winning the competition because it is proven to be able to improve quality Islamic bank services. to the community. 95 Fourth, there is a level of playing field that allows Islamic banks to provide a wide level of service and is as modern as what has been provided by conventional banks. 95 Kelima, public education in an innovative and integrated manner. The public has increasingly recognized and felt the benefits of the presence of Islamic banks so that enthusiasm for using Islamic banking products and services is increasing. This shows that a new, more universal and inclusive image of the Islamic banking industry, now popularly known as iB (ai-Bi), has succeeded in positioning Islamic banks as alternative banking system that can be enjoyed by all circles of society. 7. Meanwhile, to foster the development of Islamic banking more quickly and sustainably, Bank Indonesia has issued various long-term policies as stated in the Blue Print of Sharia Banking Development The year 2011-2015 which in general includes 7 pillars or focuses of development, namely: human resource development, effective regulation and supervision, infrastructure that support, effective banking structure, synergistic strategic alliances, effective customer empowerment, and product innovation. The implementation of the seven development focuses in the Blue Print will be described in the form of implementation programs for the next 5 years. These programs are currently in the process of being finalized and in due course they will be delivered to all stake holders. Mr., Mrs., Happy seminar attendees 8. I can say that in addition to the trade, manufacturing, transportation, agribusiness, and housing sectors, recently Islamic banking has begun to actively become a financing partner for franchise activities (franchise) as a manifestation of profit-sharing business. Islamic banking must indeed be innovative and continue to increase competitiveness in providing fund-raising and financing products so that the hope of becoming a modern Islamic banking, being professional and understanding the needs of society can become a reality. 9. Based on these developments, there are several important issues that can be discussed together in this seminar so that Islamic banking cannot be better prepared in grasping the opportunities of 2011. 95 First, what business strategies does Islamic banking need to prepare to seize the opportunities of 2011? Is it able to realize islamic banking that is modern, professional and understands the needs of the community tobe a reality? 95 Second, how is the readiness of human resources both in quantity and quality, or will there be another phenomenon of "piracy"? What is the strategy for preparing, developing and fulfilling human resources in the future? 95 Third, is islamic banking infrastructure ready , such as office networks, hedging facilities and liquidity, to offset growth and competition? 95 Fourth, is Islamic banking ready to provide services on par with conventional banks and what strategies will be used? Ladies and Gentlemen, Happy Ladies and Gentlemen 10. Towards 2011, in the midst of increasingly fierce business competition, amid the severe challenges of implementing regional free markets , amid the test of natural disasters in various parts of Indonesia, as well as various regions of Indonesia Another challenge, let's together a line-up and strengthen the determination to work together and work hard to develop Islamic banking, so that in the future Islamic banking will has a significant contribution in the banking system as well as the national economy. 11. Before ending this speech, I would like to express my appreciation to all levels of the committee for the implementation of this seminar and thank you to the panelists, hopefully the results of the seminar this can provide optimal benefits for Islamic banking, all Islamic economic activists and the Indonesian people in general. 12. Finally , I congratulate the seminar participants and by saying "Bismillahirrahmannirrahiim" with this "Year-End Seminar on the Outlook of Islamic Banking 2011" I officially opened . Billahitaufiq wal hidayah wassalamu'alaikum warrahmatullahi wabarakaatuh Jakarta, 24 November 2010 Dr. Halim Alamsyah
text_original: KEYNOTE SPEECH Dr. HALIM ALAMSYAH, DEPUTI GUBERNUR BANK INDONESIA PADA ACARA "SEMINAR AKHIR TAHUN TENTANG OUTLOOK PERBANKAN SYARIAH 2011" 24 NOVEMBER 2010 Yang saya hormati Para Pimpinan Perbankan, Pimpinan Lembaga Pemerintah, Kadin, Asosiasi Usaha, Para Narasumber, Akademisi, dan Hadirin undangan yang berbahagia Assalamu'alaikum Wr. Wb., Selamat Pagi dan Salam Sejahtera buatkita semua. 1. Pertama-tama marilah kita panjatkan puji dan syukur kehadirat Allah SWT yang atas izin-Nya kita dapat berkumpul di tempat ini untuk mengikuti "Seminar Akhir Tahun Tentang Outlook Perbankan Syariah 2011". Pada kesempatan ini, atas nama Bank Indonesia, saya ingin menyampaikan rasa simpati dan keprihatinan yang mendalam kepada para korban bencana alam di mentawai, Wasior dan daerah letusan gunung merapi di Yogyakarta dan sekitarnya. 2. Pelaksanaan seminar ini tentunya mempunyai makna penting dan dapat dijadikan sebagai salah satu momentum untuk menjaga dan meningkatkan perkembangan perbankan syariah yang dalam lima tahun terakhir sangat menggembirakan dengan rata-rata pertumbuhan total aset di atas 33% per tahun. Sampai dengan akhir Oktober 2010, total aset perbankan syariah telah mencapai Rp 86 triliun. Kami optimis tingkat pertumbuhan yang tinggi ini akan terus berlanjut seiring dengan semakin bertambahnya jumlah bank syariah. Secara kelembagaan, saat ini jumlah bank syariah telah mencapai 11 BUS, 23 UUS, dan 146 BPRS dengan jaringan kantor sebanyak 1.625 kantor pada akhir September 2010. Secara geografis, sebaran jaringan kantor perbankan syariah saat ini telah menjangkau masyarakat di lebih dari 89 kabupaten/kota di 33 propinsi. 3. Bertambahnya jumlah bank syariah, baik pendirian bank baru maupun konversi, berikut jaringan pelayananannya, termasuk office channeling, yang didukung dengan program sosialisasi dan edukasi publik yang semakin gencar diyakini akan meningkatkan kinerja perbankan syariah. Penghimpunan dana pihak ketiga (DPK) perbankan syariah pada tahun 2011 diperkirakan akan melebihi tahun sebelumnya, terlebih jika perbankan syariah mampu memanfaatkan momentum capital inflow. Sementara kondisi fundamental ekonomi tahun 2011 yang semakin kokoh, proses pemulihan ekonomi global yang semakin menguat, dan dukungan aturan perpajakan yang lebih kondusif akan mendorong kinerja pembiayaan perbankan syariah. 4. Perlu disadari bahwa Bank Indonesia tidak dapat bekerja sendirian dalam mengembangkan perbankan syariah, perlu dukungan dan kerjasama dengan berbagai pihak, seperti Dewan Perwakilan Rakyat (DPR) dalam penyusunan landasan perundang-undangan; Dewan Syariah Nasional (DSN) dalam inovasi produk; dan Pemerintah dalam perannya di bidang perpajakan dan penguatan kebijakan di sektor riil. Lahirnya UU Perbankan Syariah dan UU Perpajakan yang baru pada tahun 2009, diyakini membuat iklim usaha bank syariah semakin kondusif sehingga meningkatkan minat investor untuk masuk ke dalam bisnis bank syariah di Indonesia. Bapak, Ibu, Hadirin yang berbahagia 5. Agar dapat menangkap peluang tahun 2011 yang cukup prospektif, maka pengembangan jangka menengah industri perbankan syariah secara umum diarahkan pada penguasaan pasar domestik dengan kualitas pelayanan berstandar internasional. Paradigma pengembangan yang berorientasi domestik sesuai dengan potensi pasar domestik yang sangat besar dan belum sepenuhnya dieksplorasi. Pasar domestik juga menjadi tujuan investasi yang menarik di kawasan Asia sejalan dengan perbaikan rating Indonesia dan upaya menuju investment grade pada 2011. 6. Sementara arah kebijakan pengembangan perbankan syariah tahun 2011 difokuskan kepada beberapa hal berikut: <95> Pertama, peningkatan kualitas sistem pengawasan yang sejalan dengan pertumbuhan industri yang pesat, pengawasan risiko yang semakin terkendali, dan perkembangan terkini kepatuhan regulasi baik yang berasal dari IFSB, BIS maupun komitmen-komitmen internasional lainnya, seperti G-20 dan ASEAN Economic Community (AEC). <95> Kedua, pengembangan sumber daya manusia perbankan syariah dimana dalam perspektif manajemen modern, human capital merupakan elemen terpenting dan penentu dalam mencapai visi dan keunggulan bersaing organisasi. <95> Ketiga, strategi co-opetition untuk meningkatkan kapasitas dan kualitas layanan. Co-opetition merupakan kombinasi dari cooperation dan competition yang mensinergikan sumber daya antara BUS atau UUS dengan BUK induknya. Sinergi dalam berbagai aktivitas operasional, seperti pemanfaatan jaringan ATM dan promosi ditujukan untuk menangkap peluang pasar dan memenangkan persaingan karena terbukti mampu meningkatkan kualitas layanan bank syariah. kepada masyarakat. <95> Keempat, adanya level of playing field yang memungkinkan bank syariah untuk memberikan tingkat pelayanan yang luas dan sama modern-nya dengan apa yang telah disediakan oleh bank konvensional. <95> Kelima, edukasi publik secara inovatif dan terintegrasi. Masyarakat telah semakin mengenal dan merasakan kemanfaatan dari kehadiran bank syariah sehingga antusiasme untuk menggunakan produk dan jasa perbankan syariah semakin meningkat. Hal ini menunjukkan bahwa citra baru yang lebih universal dan inklusif dari industri perbankan syariah, yang kini populer dikenal sebagai iB (ai-Bi), telah berhasil menempatkan bank syariah sebagai alternatif sistem perbankan yang dapat dinikmati oleh semua kalangan masyarakat. 7. Sementara itu untuk menumbuh kembangkan perbankan syariah secara lebih cepat dan berkesinambungan, Bank Indonesia telah menerbitkan berbagai kebijakan jangka panjang yang tertuang dalam Blue Print Pengembangan Perbankan Syariah Tahun 2011-2015 yang pada dasarnya mencakup 7 pilar atau fokus pengembangan, yakni: pengembangan sumber daya manusia, pengaturan dan pengawasan yang efektif, infrastruktur yang mendukung, struktur perbankan yang efektif, aliansi strategis yang sinergis, pemberdayaan nasabah yang efektif, dan inovasi produk. Pelaksanaan ketujuh fokus pengembangan dalam Blue Print tersebut akan dijabarkan dalam bentuk program-program pelaksanaan selama 5 tahun ke depan. Program-program tersebut saat ini dalam proses finalisasi dan pada waktunya nanti akan disampaikan kepada seluruh stake holders. Bapak, Ibu, Hadirin peserta seminar yang berbahagia 8. Dapat saya sampaikan bahwa selain sektor perdagangan, manufaktur, transportasi, agribisnis, dan perumahan, baru-baru ini perbankan syariah telah mulai aktif menjadi mitra pembiayaan untuk kegiatan waralaba (franchise) sebagai perwujudan usaha bagi hasil. Perbankan syariah memang harus inovatif dan terus meningkatkan daya saing dalam menyediakan produk penghimpunan dana maupun pembiayaan sehingga harapan untuk menjadikan perbankan syariah yang modern, profesional dan memahami kebutuhan masyarakat dapat menjadi kenyataan. 9. Berdasarkan perkembangan tersebut terdapat beberapa isu penting yang dapat didiskusikan bersama dalam seminar ini sehingga perbankan syariah dapat menjadi lebih siap dalam menangkap peluang 2011. <95> Pertama, strategi bisnis apa yang perlu disiapkan perbankan syariah untuk menangkap peluang 2011? Apakah mampu mewujudkan perbankan syariah yang modern, profesional dan memahami kebutuhan masyarakat menjadi kenyataan? <95> Kedua, bagaimana kesiapan SDM baik secara kuantitas maupun kualitas, atau akan terjadi lagi fenomena "pembajakan"? Bagaimana strategi penyiapan, pengembangan dan pemenuhan SDM ke depan? <95> Ketiga, siapkah infrastruktur perbankan syariah, seperti jaringan kantor, fasilitas hedging dan likuiditas, untuk mengimbangipertumbuhan dan persaingan? <95> Keempat, siapkah perbankan syariah menyediakan pelayanan yang setara dengan bank konvensional dan apa strategi yang akan digunakan? Bapak, Ibu, Hadirin yang berbahagia 10. Menuju tahun 2011, di tengah persaingan usaha yang semakin ketat, di tengah tantangan berat penerapan pasar bebas kawasan regional, di tengah ujian bencana alam di berbagai wilayah Indonesia, serta berbagai tantangan lainnya, marilah bersama-sama merapatkan barisan dan mengukuhkan tekad untuk bekerjasama dan bekerja keras untuk mengembangkan perbankan syariah, sehingga ke depan perbankan syariah akan memiliki kontribusi yang signifikan dalam sistem perbankan maupun perekonomian nasional. 11. Sebelum mengakhiri sambutan ini, saya ingin menyampaikan apresiasi kepada seluruh jajaran panitia atas pelaksanaan seminar ini dan ucapan terima kasih kepada para panelis, semoga hasil seminar ini dapat memberikan kemaslahatan yang optimal bagi perbankan syariah, seluruh pegiat ekonomi syariah dan masyarakat Indonesia pada umumnya. 12. Akhir kata, saya ucapkan selamat berdiskusi kepada para peserta seminar dan dengan mengucapkan "Bismillahirrahmannirrahiim" dengan ini "Seminar Akhir Tahun tentang Outlook Perbankan Syariah 2011" secara resmi saya buka. Billahitaufiq wal hidayah wassalamu'alaikum warrahmatullahi wabarakaatuh Jakarta, 24 November 2010 Dr. Halim Alamsyah

Title: Keynote Speech Gubernur Bank Indonesia Pada Seminar Nasional Big Data "Globalisasi Digital : Optimalisasi Pemanfaatan Big Data Untuk Akselerasi Pertumbuhan Ekonomi" Jakarta, 9 Agustus 2017
text: Keynote Speech by the Governor of Bank Idonesia National Seminar on Big Data "Digital Globalization: Optimizing The Use of Big Data to Accelerate Economic Growth" Jakarta, 9th August 2017 What we respect: - Members of the Board of Governors of Bank Indonesia - Head of Financial Transaction Reporting and Analysis Center - Chairman and members of the Supervisory Board of Bank Indonesia (BSBI) - Governor of DKI Jakarta Province, Mr. Djarot Saiful Hidayat - Mayor of Makassar, Mr. M. Ramdhan Pomanto - The Panel is and moderators of the seminar - Ladies and gentlemen, Hadirin all who are happy Assaiamu'aiaikum Wr Wb Morning Mat and Greetings to all of us, 95 First of all, let us offer praise and gratitude to the presence of Allah Almighty, God Almighty, because only by His consent can we all be present in good health and good condition to jointly attend the National Big Data Seminar with the theme "Digital Globalization: Optimization of Big Data Concentration to Accelerate Economic Growth" Ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen we respect, 95 Today we are entering the era of the digital revolution, which is also referred to as the fourth industrial revolution. If the first industrial revolution was marked by the birth of the steam engine, the second industrial revolution with the emergence of electrification and mass production, and the third industrial revolution marked by the emergence of internet technology, then the fourth industrial revolution is a phase in which almost all aspects of our lives have been touched by digital services. In this phase digital services have influenced the way we make decisions, the way we interact with others, and at the same time have driven the emergence of new business models that are much more efficient and innovative. 95 We look at at least 3 main factors driving the wave of the digital revolution. First, the development of mobile phones. Nowadays, mobile phones have become the main device for accessing the internet. The majority of the world's online traffic today comes from mobile phone devices. Second, the Internet of Things (IoT). In 2016, nearly 18 billion1 internet-based devices were interconnected which resulted in the creation of innovative concepts such as smart homes. Third, Big Data which is supported by the ability of computers to perform complex analysis {advance analytics}. In 2016, global internet traffic has reached at least 1.2 zetabytes or 1.2 trillion2 gigabytes, yes ng mainly triggered by the increasing trend of social use m edia through gadgets. In 2013 alone there were at least 1.85 billion active users of social media, which then increased to 2.8 billion in 2016.3 95 The expanding activity of social media and digital services has encouraged the creation of new data massively. Data which is very large, varied and produced very quickly frea/f/777ejini is what is known as Big Data. Along with the rapid development of computing technology, today we have been able to sift through information and perform in-depth analysis {advance analytics) of the data, so that it can be used for productive purposes. 95 The three factors above are part of a technological breakthrough phenomenon known as a disruptive technologies. This phenomenon illustrates how technological breakthroughs are able to change many things in people's lives. The emergence of various social media applications for example, has led to a change in the way humans interact, e- commercete\ah shifting people's preferences from shopping in the center shopping to online shopping , cloud computing technology has changed conventional data storage methods, and so on. Together, these disruptive technologies are the main driving force for the rolling out of the digital revolution globally. Ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen we respect, 95 The unavoidable digital revolution has also hit Indonesia. In recent years, we have seen tremendous growth in digital-based start-ups , both in the trade in goods and services {e-commerce}, payment modes, and financing. The number of internet users shopping online in the country in 20 164 has reached 24.74 million people. Over the past year, these internet users have spent around USD5.6 billion (around Rp75 trillionun) on various e-commerce sites. In other words, every e-commerce user in Indonesia spends an average of IDR 3 million per year. This high on/ineyanq shopping activity is in line with the activeness of Indonesians on various social media. Jakarta is even known as the "Twitter capital of the world" 95 In addition to e-commerce, the digital revolution in Indonesia has also touched the financial sector. This can be seen, among others, from the number of fintech players in Indonesia which in the last 2 years (2015-2016) has grown rapidly by 78%. Ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen we respect, 95 Indonesia's great potential in utilizing this digital era is unfortunately still not optimized. This means that internet penetration5 in Indonesia is still quite low, which is around 51%6 (2016). This figure is still relatively far below our neighboring countries, such as Malaysia (71%) and Thailand (67%). In comparison, the internet penetration rate in countries such as the UK and Japan has reached above 90%. 95 The main problem that causes the non-optimal use of digital technology in Indonesia comes from the quality of internet services which are relatively lagging behind compared to other countries. 95 Another obstacle is investment spending in information technology (IT), which is also relatively lagging behind other countries. IT investment in key sectors contributing to economic growth such as manufacturing and mining remains relatively low, even tending to be lower than countries in the same group. However, a fairly high investment was recorded in the tertiary sector such as fintech e-commerce which in 2016 was estimated to reach USD1.7 billion. 95 If these barriers in the use of digital technology can be overcome, it is estimated that economic digitalization will be able to provide an added value of USD150 billion to Indonesia's GDP by 2025 (around 10% of GDP), which is accompanied by an increase in employment reaching nearly 4 million people (Study me Kinsey Indonesia: McKinsey Indonesia- 2016, Unlocking Indonesia's Digital Opportunity) Ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen we respect, 95 The digital revolution that has triggered more widespread digital-based activities has created an explosion of information and a flood of data. In addition to its very large number and produced quickly, the variety of data created is also very diverse, so that Big Data has characteristics known as 3V, namely : volume, variety, and velocity. This characteristic then develops to 5V, with the addition of value and veracity (confidence in the correctness of the data). 95 This huge amount of data is unfortunately still very little that has been utilized. Studies by IBM show that 80% of all data in the world, whether in the form of text, images, video or sound, cannot be used, mainly because its unstructured nature. On the other hand, it is realized that such huge data actually stores so much deeper information and knowledge, which, if processed properly, can provide benefits which is amazing. 95 Observing the phenomenon, this seminar specifically raised the theme: "Digital Globalization: Optimizing the Use of Big Data to Accelerate Economic Growth". Ladies and Gentlemen, hadin'n whom we respect, 95 In our observation, the use of Big Data in the country in the last 5 years has become more widespread. The commercial industry, including the financial sector industry, has relatively utilized Big Data to support its business activities, among others, to improve services to customers more efficiently and effectively, reducing distribution costs and strengthening business risk analysis in the financial sector. 95 Several government agencies/authorities in Indonesia have also started using Big Data in policy making or supporting their work processes. Local governments through the smart c/Zy application have also proactively begun to utilize Big Data to improve the quality of public services such as education, health, transportation andn city security. 95 The rise of smart city development in various cities also gives rise to potential data sources that are further utilized. If the data stored in every s/77a/tc/Zy can be connected to each other, it could be that the problem in one city is found a solution in another. For example, careful mapping of surplus data or commodity deficits between cities can be synergized to reduce supply volatility and price inequality. 95 Meanwhile, central banks, including Bank Indonesia, have also started to utilize Big Data in recent years to support the decision-making process. Ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen we respect, 95 The utilization of Big Data at Bank Indonesia began in October 2014, in line with the launch of the Transformation Program Towards Bank Indonesia 2024. 95 One of the themes of such transformation is the state of the art technology, which in essence is to encourage Bank Indonesia to utilize the latest technology and approaches that will help Bank Indonesia in achieving the vision and its mission effectively and efficiently. 95 In particular, the utilization of Big Data at Bank Indonesia is expected to strengthen the decision-making process in the Monetary, Financial Market, Financial System Sta bi litas (SSK), Payment System and Rupiah Currency Management (SP-PUR) sectors. 95 Through in-depth observation, the benefits of Big Data for Bank Indonesia will at least be obtained from several areas as follows: (1) First, the availability of new indicators isfaster and more frequent (high frequency) to overcome the issue of data lag that is often faced in policy formulation. (2) Second, the relationship between financial actors (including banks, non-bank financial institutions, and corporations) can be better monitored through strengthening network analytics in order to mitigate systemic risks. (3) Third, public perceptions of Bank Indonesia's policies can be monitored more accurately through sentiment analysis to improve Bank Indonesia's policy communication strategy. 95 We formulated the development of Big Data at Bank Indonesia into three phases, namely (i) establishing foundation 2015-2018, (ii) empowering2019-2021 and (iii) executing innovative a3/se2022 -etc. 95 In the process of building a solid foundation for the utilization of Big Data, Bank Indonesia has carried out a number of pilot projects that have produced a number of new indicators sourced from various online portals, such as indices job vacancy and index harga property. In addition, Big Data analytics began to be used regularly as part of the assessment of payment system supervision frameworks. To support it all, new capabilities are constantly being built to process and analyze Big Data. 95 In the final slag phase (starting in 2022), the utilization of Big Data at Bank Indonesia is expected to be real-time so that it can support the creation of innovations in providing new data/indicators by utilizing data sources that more varied so that it can support a high-quality decision-making process. Ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen we respect, 95 We consider that in general there are 3 main challenges faced in the use of Big Data. First, the availability and access to data sources. The availability of real-time data is the basis for policy formulation that is able to answer the current situation. 95 On the other hand, data accessibility also often clashes with aspects of data confidentiality. Therefore , it is necessary to build a mechanism that can challengethe interests of data owners so that they are willing to share data without causing concern about the confidentiality aspect. 95 The second challenge is data quality. One of the characteristics of Big Data is veracity (belief in the correctness of data), considering that the information contained in Big Data is raw data that still contains a lot of "noise". The data cleansing process thus becomes critical to ensure that the data obtained is valuable for further analysis. 95 The next challenge is the limitations of human resources with data scientist qualifications. The digital revolution has not been balanced with the adequacy of the output of universities that have the expertise to process Big Data. For this reason, close collaboration with the world of academia is needed so that the capability of Big Data can also be built gradually in the internal institutions. Ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen we respect, 95 We believe that this ongoing digital revolution, if it can be put to good use, will be able to bring Indonesia is on an economic growth trajectory of around 7% per year. The World Bank (2016) illustrates this using the terminology of digital dividends, where the digitalization of the economy is believed to be able to provide breakthroughs in the form of increasing efficiencyin various sectors an economy born of more accurate targets and business decisions , encourages the creation of new innovations, while creating a more inclusive economic ecosystem. All of this will eventually increase the productivity of the economy significantly, which in turn will lead the economy to a higher trajectory of economic growth and sustainable, which is accompanied by increased employment opportunities and better public services. 95 The breakthrough of the digital economy to increase employment opportunities and productivity is a common homework. In this case, it is very important for public policy makers, business actors, and academics to collaborate with each other. 95 In closing, through this seminar we want to invite all elements of society to share knowledge and experiences with each other in terms of the use of Big Data which is an inseparable phenomenon from digital economy, as well as encouraging the creation of collaboration between institutions in order to encourage more optimal use of Big Data. 95 This national seminar is also an offering of "BI's Real Work in Every Meaning of Indonesia" in order to inflame the spirit of mutual cooperation to build a better Indonesia to ahead, in line with the theme of the commemoration of the 72nd Anniversary of Indonesian Independence, namely "Indonesia Kerja Bersama". 95 This is to ensure that Indonesia's huge digital potential can be transformed to ultimately contribute concretely to the acceleration of national economic growth. Thank you and thank you Wassalamu'alaikum Wr Wb Agus D.W. Martowardojo Governor of Bank Indonesia 1 Source: Statista (2016) Statista is a data provider company online statistics, based in Germany 2 Source: Cisco (2016) 3 Source: We are Social (2017). We are Social is global agency in the field of social media, based in New York. 4 Source: Statista (2016) 5 Internet penetration rate is the ratio between number of internet users and number of inhabitants 6 Source: We are Social (2017) --------------- ------------------------------------------------------------ --------------- ------------------------------------------------------------

Djarot Saiful Hidayat - Walikota Makassar, Bpk. M. Ramdhan Pomanto - Para Panel is dan Moderator Seminar - Bapak/Ibu, Hadirin sekalian yang berbahagia Assaiamu'aiaikum Wr Wb Sela mat Pagi dan Salam Sejahtera bagi kita semua, <95> Pertama-tama, marilah kita panjatkan puji dan syukur ke hadirat Allah SWT, Tuhan Yang Maha Kuasa, karena hanya atas perkenan- Nya kita semua dapat hadir dalam keadaan sehat dan baik untuk bersama-sama mengikuti Seminar Nasional Big Data dengan tema "Globalisasi Digital: Optimalisasi Pemanfatan Big Data untuk Akselerasi Pertumbuhan Ekonomi" Bapak/Ibu, hadirin yang kami hormati, <95> Saat ini kita memasuki era revolusi digital, yang juga disebut sebagai revolusi industri keempat. Jika revolusi industri pertama ditandai dengan lahirnya mesin uap, revolusi industri kedua dengan munculnya elektrifikasi dan produksi massal, dan revolusi industri ketiga ditandai dengan munculnya teknologi internet, maka revolusi industri keempat adalah fase dimana hampir semua sendi kehidupan kita telah tersentuh layanan digital. Pada fase ini layanan digital telah mempengaruhi cara kita membuat keputusan, cara kita berinteraksi dengan orang lain, dan sekaligus telah mendorong munculnya model-model bisnis baru yang jauh lebih efisien dan inovatif. <95> Kami mencermati paling tidak terdapat 3 faktor utama pendorong gelombang revolusi digital. Pertama, perkembangan telepon seluler. Dewasa ini, telepon seluler telah menjadi perangkat utama untuk mengakses internet. Mayoritas lalu lintas online dunia saat ini berasal dari perangkat telepon seluler. Kedua, Internet of Things (IoT). Di 2016, hampir 18 miliar1 piranti berbasis internet telah saling terkoneksi yang mengakibatkan terciptanya konsep-konsep inovatif seperti smart homes. Ketiga, Big Data yang didukung oleh kemampuan komputer melakukan analisis yang kompleks {advance analytics}. Di 2016, lalu lintas internet global setidaknya telah mencapai 1,2 zetabyte atau 1,2 triliun gigabytes2,ya ng terutama dipicu oleh peningkatan tren penggunaan media sosial melalui perangkat gawai (gadget). Pada 2013 saja terdapat setidaknya 1,85 miliar pengguna aktif media sosial, yang kemudian meningkat menjadi 2,8 miliar pada 20163. <95> Aktivitas media sosial dan layanan digital yang makin meluas tersebut telah mendorong terciptanya data baru secara masif. Data yang berjumlah sangat besar, bervariasi dan dihasilkan secara sangat cepat frea/f/777ejinilah yang dikenal sebagai Big Data. Seiring dengan perkembangan teknologi komputasi yang pesat, saat ini kita telah dapat menyaring informasi dan melakukan analisa yang mendalam {advance analytics) terhadap data tersebut, sehingga dapat digunakan untuk keperluan yang produktif. <95> Ketiga faktor diatas merupakan bagian dari fenomena terobosan teknologi yang dikenal dengan nama disruptive technologies. Fenomena ini menggambarkan bagaimana terobosan teknologi mampu merubah banyak hal dalam kehidupan masyarakat. Munculnya berbagai aplikasi sosial media misalnya, telah menyebabkan perubahan dalam cara manusia berinteraksi, e- commercete\ah menggeser preferensi masyarakat dari berbelanja di pusat perbelanjaan menjadi belanja secara online, teknologi cloud computing telah merubah metode penyimpanan data secara konvensional, dan lain sebagainya. Secara bersama-sama, disruptive technologies inilah yang menjadi motor penggerak utama bergulirnya revolusi digital secara global. Bapak/Ibu, hadirin yang kami hormati, <95> Revolusi digital tak dapat dihindari juga telah melanda Indonesia. Dalam beberapa tahun terakhir, kita melihat pertumbuhan perusahaan-perusahaan start-ups berbasis digital yang luar biasa, baik di perdagangan barang dan jasa {e-commerce}, moda pembayaran, maupun pembiayaan. Jumlah pengguna internet yang berbelanja secara online di tanah air pada 20 164 telah mencapai 24,74 juta orang. Selama setahun terakhir, para pengguna internet tersebut telah membelanjakan uang sekitar USD5,6 miliar (sekitar Rp75 triliun) di berbagai e-commerce. Dengan kata lain, setiap pengguna e-commerce di Indonesia rata-rata membelanjakan Rp3 juta per tahun. Aktivitas belanja on/ineyanq tinggi ini sejalan dengan keaktifan orang Indonesia di berbagai media sosial. Jakarta bahkan dikenal sebagai "Twitter capital of the world" <95> Selain e-commerce, revolusi digital di Indonesia juga telah menyentuh sektor keuangan. Hal ini antara lain terlihat dari jumlah fintech player di Indonesia yang dalam 2 tahun terakhir (2015-2016) tumbuh pesat sebesar 78%. Bapak/Ibu, hadirin yang kami hormati, <95> Potensi besar Indonesia dalam memanfaatkan era digital ini sayangnya masih belum kita optimalkan. Hal ini mengingat penetrasi internet5 di Indonesia tergolong masih cukup rendah, yaitu sekitar 51%6 (2016). Angka ini masih relatif jauh dibawah negara-negara tetangga kita, seperti Malaysia (71%) dan Thailand (67%). Sebagai perbandingan, angka penetrasi internet di negara seperti Inggris dan Jepang sudah mencapai di atas 90%. <95> Persoalan utama yang menyebabkan belum optimalnya pemanfaatan teknologi digital di Indonesia berasal dari kualitas layanan internet yang relatif masih tertinggal dibandingkan negara lain. <95> Hambatan lain adalah pengeluaran investasi di bidang teknologi informasi (TI) yang juga relatif tertinggal dibanding negara lain. Investasi TI di sektor-sektor utama pemberi kontribusi ke pertumbuhan ekonomi seperti manufaktur dan pertambangan relatif masih rendah, bahkan cenderung lebih rendah dibandingkan negara- negara da lam kelompok yang sama. Namun investasi yang cukup tinggi tercatat di sektor tersier seperti e-commerce fintech yang pada 2016 diperkirakan mencapai sebesar USD1,7 miliar. <95> Apabila hambatan-hambatan dalam pemanfaatan teknologi digital tersebut dapat diatasi, maka diperkirakan bahwa digitalisasi ekonomi mampu memberikan nilai tambah sebesar USD150 miliar terhadap PDB Indonesia pada 2025 (sekitar 10% terhadap PDB), yang dibarengi dengan peningkatan penyerapan tenaga kerja mencapai hampir 4 juta orang (Studi Me Kinsey Indonesia: McKinsey Indonesia- 2016, Unlocking Indonesia's Digital Opportunity) Bapak/Ibu, hadirin yang kami hormati, <95> Revolusi digital yang memicu aktivitas berbasis digital yang makin meluas telah menciptakan ledakan informasi maupun banjir data. Selain jumlahnya yang sangat besar dan dihasilkan dengan sangat cepat, variasi data yang tercipta juga sangat beragam, sehingga Big Data memiliki karakteristik yang dikenal dengan 3V, yaitu : volume, variety, dan velocity. Karakteristik ini kemudian berkembang menjadi 5V, dengan tambahan value dan veracity (keyakinan terhadap kebenaran data). <95> Data yang berjumlah sangat besar ini sayangnya masih sangat sedikit yang telah termanfaatkan. Studi oleh IBM menunjukkan bahwa 80% dari semua data di dunia baikyang berupa teks, gambar, video ataupun suara, belum dapat dimanfaatkan, terutama karena sifatnya yang tidak terstruktur. Di sisi lain, disadari bahwa data yang sangat besar tersebut sesungguhnya menyimpan begitu banyak informasi dan pengetahuan yang lebih dalam, yang apabila diolah dengan baik, dapat memberikan manfaat yang luar biasa. <95> Mencermati fenomena, ini maka seminar kali ini secara khusus mengangkattema: "Globalisasi Digital: Optimalisasi Pemanfaatan Big Data untuk Akselerasi Pertumbuhan Ekonomi". Bapak/Ibu, hadin'n yang kami hormati, <95> Dalam pengamatan kami, pemanfaatan Big Data di tanah air dalam 5 tahun terakhir telah semakin meluas. Industri komersial, termasuk di dalamnya industri sektor keuangan, relatif telah lebih dahulu memanfaatkan Big Data mendukung aktivitas bisnisnya, antara lain untuk meningkatkan pelayanan kepada pelanggan secara lebih efisien dan efektif, mengurangi biaya distribusi serta memperkuat analisis risiko bisnis di sektor keuangan. <95> Beberapa instansi pemerintah/otoritas di Indonesia juga sudah mulai menggunakan Big Data dalam pengambilan kebijakan ataupun mendukung proses kerjanya. Pemerintah daerah melalui aplikasi smart c/Zyjuga secara proaktif telah mulai memanfaatkan Big Data bagi peningkatan kualitas layanan publik seperti pendidikan, kesehatan, transportasi dan keamanan kota. <95> Maraknya pengembangan smart city di berbagai kota memunculkan pula sumber data yang potensial dimanfaatkan lebih lanjut. Apabila data yang tersimpan pada setiap s/77a/tc/Zydapat saling terhubung, bisa jadi persoalan di satu kota ditemukan solusinya di kota lain. Contohnya, pemetaan secara cermat mengenai data surplus atau defisit komoditas antar kota dapat disinergikan untuk mengurangi volatilitas pasokan dan ketimpangan harga. <95> Sementara itu, kalangan Bank Sentral, termasuk Bank Indonesia, dalam beberapa tahun terakhir juga sudah mulai memanfaatkan Big Data guna mendukung proses pengambilan keputusan. Bapak/Ibu, hadirin yang kami hormati, <95> Pemanfaatan Big Data di Bank Indonesia dimulai pada bulan Oktober 2014, sejalan dengan dicanangkannya Program Transformasi Menuju Bank Indonesia 2024. <95> Salah satu tema transformasi tersebut adalah state of the art technology, yang pada intinya adalah mendorong Bank Indonesia untuk memanfaatkan teknologi dan pendekatan mutakhir yang akan membantu Bank Indonesia dalam mencapai visi dan misinya secara efektif dan efisien. <95> Secara khusus, pemanfaatan Big Data di Bank Indonesia diharapkan dapat memperkuat proses pengambilan keputusan di sektor Moneter, Pasar Keuangan, Sta bi litas Sistem Keuangan (SSK), Sistem Pembayaran dan Pengelolaan Uang Rupiah (SP-PUR). <95> Melalui pengamatan yang mendalam, manfaat Big Data bagi Bank Indonesia setidaknya akan diperoleh dari beberapa area sebagai berikut: (1) Pertama, tersedianya indikator-indikator baru secara lebih cepat dan lebih sering (high frequency) untuk mengatasi isu data lag yang seringkali dihadapi dalam perumusan kebijakan. (2) Kedua, keterkaitan antar pelaku keuangan (termasuk di dalamnya bank, lembaga keuangan non bank, maupun korporasi) dapat dipetakan secara lebih baik melalui penguatan network analytics guna memitigasi risiko sistemik. (3) Ketiga, persepsi publik atas kebijakan Bank Indonesia dapat dipantau secara lebih akurat melalui sentiment analysis guna perbaikan strategi komunikasi kebijakan Bank Indonesia. <95> Kami merumuskan pengembangan Big Data di Bank Indonesia menjadi tiga fase, yaitu (i) establishing foundation 2015-2018, (ii) empowering2019-2021 dan (iii) executing innovative <a3>/se2022 -dst. <95> Dalam proses membangun pondasi yang kokoh untuk pemanfaatan Big Data, Bank Indonesia telah melaksanakan sejumlah pilot projects yang menghasilkan sejumlah indikator baru yang bersumber dari berbagai portal online, seperti indeks job vacancy dan indeks harga properti. Selain itu, Big Data analytics mulai digunakan secara rutin sebagai bagian dari asesmen framework pengawasan sistem pembayaran. Untuk mendukung itu semua, terus dibangun kapabilitas baru untuk mengolah dan menganalisis Big Data. <95> Pada fase terakhir (mulai 2022), pemanfaatan Big Data di Bank Indonesia diharapkan telah bersifat real time sehingga dapat mendukung terciptanya inovasi penyediaan data/indikator baru dengan memanfaatkan sumber data yang lebih bervariasi sehingga dapat mendukung proses pengambilan keputusan yang berkualitas tinggi. Bapak/Ibu, hadirin yang kami hormati, <95> Kami memandang bahwa secara umum terdapat 3 tantangan utama yang dihadapi dalam pemanfaatan Big Data. Pertama, ketersediaan dan akses terhadap sumber data. Ketersediaan akses data secara real-time merupakan basis bagi perumusan kebijakan yang mampu menjawab situasi terkini. <95> Di sisi lain, aksesibilitas data juga sering berbenturan dengan aspek kerahasiaan data. Oleh karena itu, perlu dibangun sebuah mekanisme yang dapat menjembatani kepentingan pemilik data agar bersedia untuk sharing data tanpa menimbulkan kekuatiran akan aspek kerahasiaannya. <95> Tantangan kedua adalah kualitas data. Salah satu karakteristik Big Data yaitu veracity (keyakinan akan kebenaran data), mengingat informasi yang terkandung dalam Big Data adalah data mentah yang masih banyak mengandung "noise". Proses data cleansing dengan demikian menjadi hal yang kritikal guna memastikan data yang diperoleh bernilai untuk dianalisis lebih lanjut. <95> Tantangan selanjutnya adalah keterbatasan SDM dengan kualifikasi data scientist. Revolusi digital ternyata belum diimbangi dengan kecukupan keluaran perguruan tinggi yang memiliki keahlian memroses Big Data. Untuk itu, diperlukan kolaborasi erat dengan dunia akademisi agar kapabilitas Big Data dapat juga dibangun secara bertahap di internal institusi. Bapak/Ibu, hadirin yang kami hormati, <95> Kami meyakini bahwa revolusi digital yang tengah berlangsung ini, apabila dapat dimanfaatkan dengan baik, akan mampu membawa Indonesia pada lintasan pertumbuhan ekonomi sekitar 7% per tahun. World Bank (2016) menggambarkan hal ini dengan menggunakan terminologi digital dividens, dimana digitalisasi perekonomian diyakini mampu memberikan terobosan da lam bentuk peningkatan efisiensi di berbagai sektor ekonomi yang lahir dari target maupun keputusan-keputusan bisnis yang lebih akurat, mendorong terciptanya inovasi-inovasi baru, sembari menciptakan ekosistem perekonomian yang lebih inklusif. Kesemuanya ini pada akhirnya akan meningkatan produktivitas perekonomian secara signifikan, yang pada gilirannya akan membawa perekonomian kepada lintasan pertumbuhan ekonomi yang lebih tinggi dan berkesinambungan, yang diiringi dengan peningkatan kesempatan kerja dan pelayanan publik yang lebih baik. <95> Terobosan ekonomi digital guna peningkatan kesempatan kerja dan produktivitas merupakan pekerjaan rumah bersama. Dalam hal ini, pengampu kebijakan publik, pelaku usaha, dan akademisi sangat penting untuk saling berkolaborasi. <95> Sebagai penutup, melalui seminar ini kami ingin mengajak semua elemen masyarakat untuk saling berbagi pengetahuan dan pengalaman dalam hal pemanfaatan Big Data yang merupakan fenomena tak terpisahkan dari perekonomian digital, sekaligus mendorong terciptanya kolaborasi antar institusi guna mendorong pemanfaatan Big Data secara lebih optimal. <95> Seminar nasional ini juga merupakan persembahan "Karya Nyata BI di Setiap Makna Indonesia" dalam rangka menggelorakan semangat gotong royong untuk membangun Indonesia yang lebih baik ke depan, sejalan dengan tema peringatan Hari Ulang Tahun ke-72 Kemerdekaan RI yaitu "Indonesia Kerja Bersama". <95> Hal ini untuk memastikan potensi digital Indonesia yang sangat besar dapat ditransformasikan untuk pada akhirnya berkontribusi secara konkrit dalam akselerasi pertumbuhan ekonomi nasional. Sekian dan terima kasih Wassalamu'alaikum Wr Wb Agus D.W. Title: Challenges and Opportunities in Public Relation as a Profession in Welcoming The 2015 ASEAN Community (Ronald Waas Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia on Perhumas Awarding Night 2014, 24 February 2014)
text: HONORABLE SPEECH OF THE DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF BANK INDONESIA IN THE NATIONAL CONVENTION OF INDONESIA PUBLIC RELATIONS ASSOCIATION CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES IN PR AS A PROFESSION IN WELCOMING THE 2015 ASEAN COMMUNITY Jakarta, 24 February 2014 The Honourable Board and Members of Indonesia Public Relations Association, Ladies and Gentlemen, Good evening and greetings to all of us, Please allow me to invite all of you to praise God the Almighty for the blessings bestowed upon us so that we have the opportunity to gather today in a healthy and favourable condition for the Perhumas Awarding Night 2014. It is a great honour for me to attend this event for the Perhumas Award 2014. I would also like to extend my appreciation of the hard work for organizing this covention as a joint learning event to strengthen the public relations society of Indonesia. Ladies and gentlemen, and distinguished guests, As introduced by Alvin Toffler (futurologist), globalization is a series of human civilization journey on earth marked into three waves: The first wave is agriculture. The second is industrial revolution, and the third is communication technology and transportation advancement. Communication technology advancement has produced a new civilization revolution as information becomes a commodity determining interaction between humans. Those predominating information will become winners in every competition, including business competition. We are now living in this era and striving to survive in the endless whirlpool of information and communication gravity. In the context of economy, within the last half decade we also experience a strong uncertainty in the global economy. This condition results in the so called New Normal, a period when economic landscape extremely shifts before adjoining a new equilibrium. The drastic change of global economic structure continuously creates a new uncertainty pendulum, thereby generating new New Normal phases implicating domestic economy. Ladies and gentlemen, and distinguished guests, 2013 was not an easy year for us. National economy slowed down with lower growth than expected. On the external side, national economic pressure intensified, particularly boosted by a deficit in the Current Transactions. Rupiah exchange rate was significantly adjusted, while inflation surpassed the target of 4.51% due to fuel subsidy reduction and sharp increase in volatile food. Amidst the consistently revolving global economic turbulence, we must be grateful that we survive at a quite high growth level of 5.7%, far above the average growth of peer countries at an estimated level of 3.6%. In 2014, an increasing export is expected to influence the decrease in current transaction deficit and support improving performance of Indonesias Balance of Payment. The improving economic foundation of Indonesia will pose a positive impact to stop the pressure of rupiah exchange rate depreciation. In the meantime, various internal and external challenges are not trivial and potentially diminish positive sentiments to our economy. On the internal side, various economic shocks due to natural disasters potentially disturb distribution as well as balance of supply and demand. On the external side, the Feds tapering off policy becomes more crucial amidst structural improvement of developing countries. Ladies and gentlemen, and distinguished guests, The diverse challenges must be observed in line with the approaching commitment to the 2015 ASEAN Economic Community (AEC). AEC serves as the embodiment of ASEAN communal strategy to become the key player within the global production chain. Deeper integration to ASEAN will consolidate ASEAN centrality to allow shifting the worlds economic activity gravity to ASEAN (Plummer & Yue, 2009). On one hand, AEC commitment will open market opportunities with freer flow of goods, services, investment, manpower, and capital. However, on the other hand, it also brings the consequence of stronger competition in the domestic market of respective countries. With the massive market potential, we observe that the most fundamental substance of AEC commitment is our ability to create competitiveness. Are we capable of using AEC as the key player of global production chain, or do we only become the market target and marginalized? In my opinion, it is at this point our ability to read and anticipate economic movements ahead will be more proven. Survivors are not always the strongest; they are the smartest. Ladies and gentlemen, and distinguished guests, In connection with the 2015 AEC, I notice several socioeconomic facts, which will significantly influence Indonesias economy. First, Indonesia has abundant natural resources and the largest population of 240 million people in South East Asia. IMFs GDP data by purchasing power parity (PPP) also indicates that Indonesias GDP in this year has reached USD 1.2 trillion, and it is predicted that Indonesia will overtake some big countries like Australia and Canada. With such a massive economic magnitude, our economic growth rate in the last few years is even far ahead of the average economic growth of peer countries. Second, the profit margin of Indonesias financial industry market structure is quite wide, which is attractive to foreign investors in the world. Goldman Sachs Asset Management, which previously introduced the acronym of BRIC, now introduces a new acronym, i.e. MIST, standing for Mexico, Indonesia, South Korea and Turkey; four country members of G-20 rising as new stars for international investors. Third, middle class society is estimated to grow to 150 million people in 2014, which means more than 50% of Indonesias population is the potential market for payment system. In 2020, the number of Indonesias middle class society is estimated to grow twice from now. Fourth, the largest portion of our population today is at the age of 0-24 years; therefore, within 20-25 years they will be at their productive age. Such demographic dividend springs more obvious amidst the aging society phase in other countries like Japan and European countries. Expansion of Indonesias middle class society within the next decade will continue and our domestic market will consistently grow. Ladies and gentlemen, and distinguished guests, The above facts must open our eyes that the role of PR as a communication tool becomes more vital to open the worlds eyes to know us better. By so doing, we will be able to make a better acquaintance with stakeholders to gain more understanding on our products and contribute positively as our expectation.The history of PR is a history of a battle for what reality is and how people will see and understand reality ... (Stuart Ewen). We, in Bank Indonesia, are fully aware that the various strategic policies of BI will not be realized without any collaboration with BIs strategic partners and maintained communication with stakeholders, the general public, and media. Such close cooperation will eventually promote effectiveness of BIs policy. Good communication of policies will reduce uncertainty and increase predictability. The role of PR here is essential. Communication by the Central Bank generally focuses on 3 main elements, namely building accountability, strengthening policy effectiveness, and increasing credibility. When achieved, the central banks policy is expected not only to be recognized by the general public (awareness), but also to be accepted and understood (acceptance) and to eventually stimulate expectation of the general public and market actors (behaviour). Ladies and gentlemen, and distinguished guests, As professional PR, there are at least three most important challenges. The first is internal challenges related to the competence of communication technology device. The second is rapid advancement of information and communication technology. Ten years ago, no one predicted that most of our lives will always relate to electronic and digital communication. Social media (Facebook, Twitter, blog) even now dominates as the biggest stopover in the world. Communication technology development has restructured internal and external communication pattern of a company. The third pertains to political reform. Communication effectiveness is highly determined by the boldness and creativity of PR in communicating an institutions stance. In the era of more open reform and democracy, the general public becomes more critical to any news spread by various media. Ladies and gentlemen, and distinguished guests, In addressing such challenges, I would like to invite all of us to adapt to the change and create communication innovations to win the hearts of people and stakeholders in a positive way. Through such positive value only will our role and position as PR be effective and timeless as nicely put by Joseph Pulitzer: Publicity is the greatest moral factor and force in our public life ... Finally, I would like to extend my appreciation of the hard work for organizing Perhumas National Convention. Congratulations to those who win the prestigious awards. The achievements will hopefully accelerate and trigger us all to work better. I also hope this meeting can strengthen interaction and communication of Perhumas Indonesia and will consistently produce fresh ideas as breakthroughs in the information and communication technology. Thank you. Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Ronald Waas

Title: Indonesia as an Emerging Economic Powerhouse : Challenges and How to Move Forward (Opening Address at Indonesia Career Expo (ICarE), The University of Melbourne, 16 May 2014)
text: Indonesia as an Emerging Economic Powerhouse : Challenges and How to Move Forward Agus D.W. Martowardojo Governor, Bank Indonesia Opening Address at Indonesia Career Expo (ICarE), The University of Melbourne 16 May 2014 Good evening Distinguished guest, ladies and gentlemen I am delighted to be here at the opening of Indonesia Career Expo and thank you to the expo-organizer, Melbourne University Indonesia Students Association (MUISA), for the kind invitation to address you tonight. It gives me a warm feeling to see such of a good crowd of distinguished guests and committed students attending this opening ceremony. In this opening ceremony, the expo-organizer have put together a distinguished array of speakers to discuss the critically important issue, on how Indonesia as emerging economic powerhouse can move forward and how the quality human resources and diverse talents could lead the way in transforming Indonesia into the better future. I am pleased to be able to participate in the discussions which hopefully provide a great time to take a fresh look at the opportunities in Indonesia at this challenging juncture. 1 To give you the background, I will share my view on how the challenges that the Indonesian economy is facing today and in the future, and at the same time I will attempt to delineate a path on how should we respond and move forward. Ladies and gentlemen The world economy now appears to be recovering from its worst post-war recession but only very slowly and at a different pace across regions and countries. Uncertainty as to future growth prospects remains still high as the legacy of the global financial crisis has cast a long shadow. The euro zone has finally exited from a recession while the US has been one of the more convincing bright spots when it comes to stronger underlying momentum in economic growth.. In contrast, slower growth rates in China, lower commodity prices, and moderating growth in emerging market economies are some of the downside risks that have materialized. On the financial stability front, the consequences of an exit from unconventional monetary policies by major central banks in particular- the US Fed have been excessively responded by global financial market. Without resolving such uncertainties and challenges, we may find ourselves for considerable time in an uncomfortable zone where global economic recovery continues to be fragile and with insufficient traction to reach a sustainable growth path. Ladies and gentlemen Now allow me to move on to the home issue. Let me started by looking Indonesia as is an unique country in many ways; as a country of some 250 2 million people, as the biggest archipelago in the world, as the worlds third largest democracy, as a leading exporter of numerous high value commodities, and by far the largest of the ten members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN). The ASEAN story is largely an Indonesian story, with much of global investor finding opportunities in Indonesia (Slide 2) From demographic structure, approximately 50% of the population is below the age of 30, is highly adaptive to new technology and has a low dependency ratio among its workforce, giving rise to a so called transitional demographic dividend. The expanding middle-class population strengthen the domestic demand of which private consumption accounts for over 60% of total GDP (Slide 3) Indonesia is also endowed with diverse natural resources. The country continues to be a major liquid natural gas (LNG) exporter. In energy and mining, Indonesia is the worlds leading thermal coal exporter, the largest tin exporter and home to vast deposits of precious metals such as gold, silver and copper (Slide 4). Ladies and gentlemen Indonesias distinct characteristics are now coupled with political and macroeconomic stability, robust economic growth and self-reliance, which saw Indonesia largely shielded from the 2008/2009 global economic crisis. Over the past five years Indonesia successfully maintain a continuous economic growth on average of 5.9% per year, one of the highest in the world, given that a few countries with a positive and stable growth during 2008-2009s crisis (Slide 5). Indonesia earned applauses from watchful eyes 3 of overseas investors and, for some time, was considered a strong contender to join the BRICs group and hence attracting huge capital inflows. The vigorous economic progress such as the one I just described earlier has been made achievable on the backdrop of fundamental strengths, which was attributable to a wide-ranging fundamental reforms following the devastating 1997 Crisis with huge economic, social and political costs. Let me cite a number of concrete examples of the fundamental reform; (i) the establishment of flexible exchange rate regimes (ii) the enhancement of the degree of autonomy of central banks, with primary mandate of price stability, (iii) consciousness about the relevance of fiscal discipline and the preservation of public debt sustainability; and (iv) the restructuring of the banks that began two decade ago which now produced much healthier financial sector balance sheets (Slide 6). All things considered, Indonesia has sailed through the global financial crisis relatively well, notwithstanding the bumpiness in the ride. Required policy responses have been implemented on a timely basis in most cases, and the underlying fundamentals are still strong. With such strong economic resilience and fundamental strengths, Indonesia was rewarded in with an upgrade that took the sovereign rating to investment grade in early 2012 (Slide 7). Now the debate is about whether Indonesia is realizing its huge potential? Ladies and gentlemen Given the vigorous economic progress has been observed, it is not all rosy. Under the surface, problems were looming where some indicators depicted the 4 economic expansion (demand side) was not sufficiently backed by adequate domestic capacity (supply side). Since early 2012 commodity prices has shown a declining trend and therefore adversely impacted our exports amidst strong import to meet burgeoning domestic demand. This has resulted in growing current account deficits which in turn deteriorates our balance of payment posture (Slide 8). Such development has raised concern to the sustainability of our economy. Despite inflation is kept check at relatively low level, current account deficit has been widening and induced slowing down economic growth. There has been repeated warnings about Indonesia fall victim to middle-income trap which occurs when a rapidly growing economies stagnating at middle-income levels and failing to maintain their growth momentum to graduate into the ranks of high-income countries (Slide 9). As we moved deeper into 2013, some of the global headwinds contributing to macro and financial instability did indeed materialize. The U.S. Feds statements related to exit of monetary stimulus provoked a tumble in asset prices in emerging market economies alike which also had a profound impact on Indonesia financial markets. Given the shallow domestic financial market, during June 2013 we witnessed a net outflow of USD 4,1 billion causing Indonesia rupiah weakened, yields on fixed income instruments spiked. and the equity markets sold off (Slide 10) In responses, we (Bank Indonesia and Government) geared policy mix to put priority on the stabilization over the growth. We increased the policy rate by 175 bps to the level of 7.50%, in stages starting from June 2013.
