This was an 5 upfront, bold decision to address the macro instability and was taken place when most other emerging markets were not in the contraction mode. Early signs are positive, including a resilient GDP growth rate, improving external sector indicators, controlled inflation rate, rebuilding international reserve as buffer, as well as acknowledgment by many outside observers and investors on the progress made by Indonesia. That said, we leave no room for complacency, and instead re-emphasize our unwavering commitment to stability (Slide 11). Ladies and gentlemen While there appears to be reason for optimism overall as the global recovery gathers momentum, we will have to contend with an environment that continues to be characterized by uncertainty and volatility. The extent of the impact of the exit from the US unconventional monetary policy measures remains unclear. But, forward-looking financial markets are always to respond abruptly, no matter how transparent and gradual is the exit from the current monetary stimulus. Meanwhile, Indonesia with open capital markets will be particularly vulnerable to such negative impacts of global market uncertainty stemming from the rise in the global interest rate. As such, the future challenges are enormous (Slide 12). Given the many uncertainties in the global environment that are beyond our control, there is little room to get wrong that which is within our control, such as focused, effective and efficient implementation of reforms and policies that will improve our competitiveness. 6 Therefore, from a political economy point of view, taking a perspective that goes beyond the domain of central banks, I would say that the future challenge for Indonesian economy boils down to how to stimulate growth without compromising macro and financial stability, facing at the same time an uncertainties in global environment. The question then is, how to move forward? I shall be drawing on a theoretical framework provided by Dani Rodrik1 in his paper entitled The past, present and future of economic growth. Rodrik argues that for countries to raise incomes and living standards, they need to do two broad things, namely to build fundamental capabilities and to undertake structural transformation. So, in my mind, a three-building block approach should be followed (Slide 13). First building block. Strong macro-fundamentals and policy settings are of the essence. There should be no room for poor fundamentals. This calls for prudent fiscal policies and monetary policy should concentrate in keeping inflation under control, since this is a prerequisite for the flexible exchange rate to be able to perform as a shock absorber. Fundamentally, we should use aggregate demand management to avoid an unsustainable current account deficits. Second building block. It is very important to have a healthy and strong balance of payments posture. For Bank Indonesia, flexibility in interest and exchange rates, anchored by strong fundamentals, should 1 Dani Rodrik is Professor of Social Science at the Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, New Jersey 7 be part of the adjustment process. But, given the sheer size of capital inflows to Indonesia so far, this might not be sufficient. So to count with large international reserves and other forms of backstops, like Bilateral Swap Arrangement (BSA) with other central bank is highly required. Also, the public and private sectors should pursue proactive debt management strategies, avoiding bunching of maturities, lengthening durations, and keeping an eye on foreign exchange rate mismatches. Third building block. Promote economic growth by making the economy more competitive, increasing total factor productivity and thus potential GDP growth. This takes us down the road of structural reforms, which have huge potential in Indonesia. Whether or not we can seize these potential depends critically on our infrastructure. Indeed, building infrastructure is the hard way for Indonesia to grow and break into the high-income level bracket, but is the only reliable one that is left. Please note that I am using a broad definition of infrastructure here, consisting of both hard and soft infrastructure. To make an analogy, I am proposing that we need to build a staircase with four steps: (i) physical infrastructure, (ii) financial infrastructure, (ii) institutional infrastructure, and (iv) human capital infrastructure (Slide 14). But, looking back at our recent experience with infrastructure, I find it difficult to escape the conclusion that Indonesia is are falling short in many areas. As we all aware, most policy responses so far have been focused on demand-side management through monetary or fiscal policy, 8 while the real lift of potential growth of the economy must essentially come from supply-side progress. Without a flexible supply side, an external shock would always require substantial adjustment in the demand side that will only intensify boomand-bust cycle in the economy. Therefore, we have to give serious consideration on the need to address structural issues to be very pressing. So, the first and second pillars are meant to guarantee macro and financial stability, not necessarily inhibiting economic growth. The real lever for a sustainable long term growth lies in the third pillar. Its my firm believe that the next administration will ensure quality public policy that can enhance the countrys competitiveness and sustain long-term growth. Ladies and gentlemen Let me conclude by saying that I am an optimist, even though my remarks might not visualize that. As you know, we as central bankers, by design, should be overly cautious. But, Indonesia is really confronted with a significant challenge over the coming years. While our domestic demand are set to grow strongly, we will need to lift our rate of productivity growth substantially if we are to continue to enjoy the type of increases in our living standard. Thank you for listening and I look forward to your questions. Governor of Bank Indonesia Agus D.W. Martowardojo 9

Title: Keynote Speech by Ronald Waas Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia in Banking Service Excellence Awards 2014, Jakarta 13 June 2014
text: KEYNOTE SPEECH OF THE DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF BANK INDONESIA IN SERVICE EXCELLENCE AWARDS 2014 Jakarta, 13 June 2014 The Honourable,  Editor in Chief of Infobank,  Head of Marketing Research Indonesia,  Economic, Bank, and Insurance Observers,  Board of Commissioners and Board of Directors and Priority Customers of Conventional Banks in Indonesia,  Distinguished guests, Good evening and greetings to all of us.  To begin this meeting, allow me to invite all of you to praise God the Almighty for the blessings bestowed upon us so that we have the opportunity to meet in healthy and good condition to witness Banking Service Excellence Awards 2014. Ladies and gentlemen, and distinguished guests,  We feel a wave of uncertainty for the last half decade has been dominating the global economic condition. Such drastic change of global economic structure continuously creates a new uncertainty pendulum, so that the new normal phase is finally considered imaginary. A few years ago, the phase is marked with two-speed world recovery, namely economic recovery acceleration divergence between advanced and emerging economies. However, the declining performance of emerging markets with the soft landing of China, and the rising of American and European economy creates three-speed world recovery.  Such global economic condition adjustment continuously affects the heartbeat of domestic economy. We feel that 2013 was not an easy year for us. National economy slowed down with lower growth than expected. On the external side, national economic pressure intensified, particularly boosted by a deficit in the Current Transactions. Rupiah exchange rate was significantly adjusted, while inflation surpassed the target of 4.51% due to fuel subsidy reduction and sharp increase in volatile food.  Amidst the consistently revolving global economic turbulence, we must be grateful that we survive at a quite high growth level of 5.7%, far above the average growth of peer countries at an estimated level of 3.6%.  With such achievement, the economy of Indonesia is considered to be able to survive amidst the constantly turbulent global economy, and many parties are of the opinion that Indonesia is able to mitigate credit risk and prevent capital flight. It is reflected from the portion of foreign investor subscription to BI Certificate and Government Securities surviving at a quite high level of 31.5%.  Such challenges must certainly be addressed and responded immediately so as not to increase the risk of disturbing the sustainability of Indonesias economic growth. Therefore, in order to face the challenges, Bank Indonesia takes several anticipatory measures. First, Bank Indonesias policy mix is strengthened to ensure inflation to return to the target of 4.51% in 2014. Second, Bank Indonesia consistently makes efforts to direct the current transaction deficit to a more balanced and sound condition. In addition, Bank Indonesia also reinforces coordination with the government and increase cooperation with central banks.  We see that the anticipatory Policy Mix of Bank Indonesia has yielded a good result to start the economy in 2013 and give a more resilient economy direction in 2014. Ladies and gentlemen, and distinguished guests,  Behind the success record, we also realize that the challenges we are addressing are slowly rising.  In 2014, global economic growth is predicted to improve, particularly due to the rising economy of USA and European countries. On the contrary, Chinese production activities are predicted to be limited and IMF has predicted Chinese economic growth slowdown trend will continue to fall to 7.5% from 7.7%. Such condition also affects the speed of Indonesias export performance recovery as one of the major trade partners of China.  At the same time, the economy of the USA shows an improving signal. The number of unemployment in the USA, primarily in manpower sector, has strengthened the speculation to accelerate stimulus reduction and even termination.  Such progress certainly affects financial market in the region. We have also witnessed an increasing pressure in financial markets of some ASEAN countries. In line with this, the once decreasing Rupiah depreciation pressure at the Q1-2014 increases again, especially as affected by financial asset re-position of emerging markets related to possible monetary stimulus adjustment by the Fed and sentiment to deficit in fiscal and domestic current transactions.  The urgent challenge today is how we can allocate economic resources in a more effective manner with a more minimum distortion. In my opinion, it is at this point that our ability to read and anticipate economic movements ahead becomes more proven.  The speed in addressing such challenges will affect our ability to be able to maintain sustainable economic growth in a balanced manner. The balance may be defined as internal balance, namely growth and inflation balance as well as external balance, namely a balanced balance of payment.  Fundamentally, we think that the present dynamics of balance of payment results from issues how our industry has competitiveness, independent in raw materials and supporting materials, improvement of innovation capacity and technology preparedness, as well as efficient economic resource allocation.  Observing the present dynamics, we evaluate that economic adjustment process still runs well despite some risks to be noted and cautious about. Therefore, an anticipatory policy must be focused on ensuring achievable inflation target and controlled current transactions. By such considerations, Bank Indonesia decides to maintain BI rate of 7.5% at a lending facility interest rate and deposit facility interest rate of 7.5% and 5.75% respectively.  Thereafter, to support the policy, Bank Indonesia will consistently strengthen a mix of monetary and macroprudential policy as well as the policy to strengthen domestic economic structure and external debt management (EDM), particularly corporate EDM. In addition, Bank Indonesia will also improve coordination with the Government in controlling inflation and current transaction deficit. Ladies and gentlemen, and distinguished guests,  Global financial crisis has given a valuable lesson on the importance of maintaining financial system stability. With interconnectedness of financial system, crisis out of financial sector poses negative impacts not only on the financial sector itself but also on wider sector affecting macroeconomic performance and resulting in high recovery cost in some countries. In Indonesia, the management cost required during the financial crisis in 1997/1998 was estimated to reach around 51% of national GDP.  Maintained financial system stability is an important factor to reach macroeconomic stability, and on the other hand, an enabling macroeconomic condition is a prerequisite to achieve financial system stability. From a stable financial system, it is expected to create a condition allowing effective and efficient national financial system and survival against internal and external turbulence; therefore, funding source allocation may contribute to national economic growth and stability.  Bank Indonesia maintain financial system stability by macroprudential approach, among others through surveillance, research, and policy making. With such tools, Bank Indonesia is able to monitor fragility and volatility in financial sector, thereby allowing to detect potential pressure posing impacts on financial system. Meanwhile, policy making by Bank Indonesia is expected to be able to affect the behaviour of agents in a financial system, thus allowing to mitigate risks and maintain financial system stability.  I realize that successful macroprudential surveillance highly depends on the level of supervisors understanding on financial system stability. It includes understanding on the structures of financial market, capital market, financial industry, and the financial condition of individual financial institutions.  We observe that presently financial system performance indicators may be well maintained as supported by banking system resilience and financial market performance. Growth of credit extended to the private sector in April 2014 slows down to 18.5% (yoy) from 19.1% (yoy) in the previous month, in line with adjustment process in the economy. To maintain the strength of banking industry resilience against risks of credit, liquidity and market and strong capital support, Bank Indonesia will coordinate with the Financial Services Authority (OJK) to direct credit growth ahead to be able to support economic growth towards a more sound and balanced direction.  Despite the well maintained general financial system performance indicators, rapid changing dynamics demand us to consistently develop by improving resilience, competitiveness, and good governance. Ladies and gentlemen, and distinguished guests,  Changes in the global economic order affects the movement space and vision of various entities, in global and local financial and non-financial institutions. The Government and Bank Indonesia, as a central bank, closely relate to such changes.  The role as a circulation bank is a classic function of central banks throughout the world inherent and part of the long history of Bank Indonesia since 1828 (formerly, De Javasche Bank). In line with economic development, the function of Bank Indonesia expands and deepens to escort Monetary Stability, Financial System Stability, and Payment System Stability.  The identity evolution, which moves in line with the dynamics, must be wisely addressed because it will undoubtedly happen to any entities, either public or private. It is at this point corporate/organization culture plays an important role as a captain promoting the roles of an organization in its essential function and identity, strengthening intraorganizational and inter-organizational cohesiveness, and directing individuals in the organization to move according to their vision and mission.  On this occasion, I represent Mr. Agus D.W. Martowardojo to extend our appreciation of the honor given for Lifetime Achievement Corporate Culture. Ladies and gentlemen, and distinguished guests,  Banking industry must always provide service excellence to customers in order to maintain their trust and loyalty as well as keep banks credibility as the basic principle of corporate culture. However, it is not enough because there are other important factors to be observed.  To be able to survive from global crisis, to fairly compete with banks of neighbouring countries, and to meet national economic funding requirements, the present condition of national banks must be improved. The fine performance of banks in recent years can be a momentum to strengthen resilience and increase competitiveness and improve governance in banking industry in particular and financial system in general.  Awards for service excellence provided by banks is something good and will be able to encourage banks to consistently improve their service quality for their customers. However, it will be much better if customers are proportionally positioned and their rights are respected in order to minimize the number of customer complaints. If it is done, customer loyalty will not be an issue and public trust in banks may improve. In turn, it will support efforts to maintain financial system stability.  Bank Indonesia realizes that banks supervisory role will also determine the quality of a bank in providing the best service for customers through supervisory mechanism directing banks to operate in a sound and efficient manner.  Bank Indonesia will also do surveillance from payment and macroprudential system to ensure that economic transaction settlements run safe, efficient, quick, and easy, and financial system is within a stable and enabling condition for the economy.  We are confident that synergy of macroprudential surveillance by Bank Indonesia and microprudential surveillance by OJK will encourage sufficient resilience of the banking system. Layered resilience through protection and empowerment of financial service customers and payment system is also expected to be able to improve service quality by banks.  Finally, we wish to congratulate all winners of the Banking Service Excellence Awards 2014 and we expect that the awards may always improve performance to provide the best services for customers. Thank you. Jakarta, June 2014 Ronald Waas

Title: Meningkatkan Efektivitas Kebijakan Ekonomi melalui Pengembangan Sistem Informasi yang Berkualitas Keynote Address Gubernur Bank Indonesia, Agus D.W. Martowardojo Pada Acara Pertemuan Gubernur Bank Indonesia dengan Pelapor, Jakarta, 2 November 2014
text: Improving the Effectiveness of Economic Policy through the Development of Quality Information Stem Keynote Address Agus D.W. Martowardojo Governor of Bank Indonesia At the Meeting between the Governors of Bank Indonesia and the Jakarta Rapporteurs , 2nd November 2014 Which we respect, 95 Minister of Finance Mr. Bambang Brodjonegoro 95 Minister of ESDM, Father Sudirman Said 95 Head of SKK Migas, Mr. Amien Sunaryadi 95 Director General of Customs, Mr. Agung Kuswandono 95 Minister of State-Owned Enterprises, represented by Mr. Sahala Lumban Gaol 95 Coordinating Minister for Maritime Affairs, represented by Mr. Safri Burhanudin 95 Member VII of the CPC, Mr. Achsanul Qosasi 95 Member II of the CPC, Mr. Agus Joko Pramono Assalamu'alaikum Warahmatullahi Wabarakatuh, Sa lam Sejahtera for all of us 1. First of all let us give thanks to the presence of Allah Almighty, God Almighty , because for His favor we can gather this morning in a very good atmosphere. 2. On this happy occasion, we, on behalf of all members of the Board of Governors of Bank Indonesia, would like to thank you for the presence of you, ladies and gentlemen, who have spent time on the sidelines of their busy schedule. which is quite dense to attend our meeting with you as a partner of Bank Indonesia. 3. It is our great hope that this meeting will be useful as a wadah to strengthen the relationship and communication between us as policymakers in the monetary, macroprudential, and payment system, with the main actors of the business world such as ladies and gentlemen who play a big role in turning the wheels ofeconomic economy. Dear Father/mother we respect 4. We are currently at the end of 2014, and it won't be long before we will open a new page in 2015. While there is still a lot of burden of structural issues that have not been completely addressed, we can say 2014 was a year full of records of success. 5. 2014 was the culminating year of the political transition process in which we managed to conduct very democratic elections peacefully, honestly, and fairly. We believe that democracy has become increasingly consolidated and the system of Government and various bureaucratic devices will be more effective in carrying out their duties. 6. Slide 3 This year is also the year we have achieved macro stability again, after during the second half of 2013 , our capability in managing economic stability has been severely tested. due to the start of the monetary policy normalization process in the US, along with rising inflation as a result of the continued increase in fuel prices. In June 2013, there was a usd 4.1 billion ca pital outflows 7. Slide 4 We should be grateful, the firm, proactive and consistent policy steps taken by the Government in reforming fiscal and Bank Indonesia, in pursuing a consistently pro-stability monetary policy, has fostered the confidence of economic and market participants in the quality of macroeconomic policy management, and directs the economy to a more balanced structure, and preventing a deep economic downturn or hard landing 8. Slide 5. In carrying out its mandate as a stability guard, Bank Indonesia must always be consistent in its attitude and be proactive and firm in taking steps. Consistency and being proactive, both of which are key to building public trust, thus building the credibility of the policy, which in turn will increase the effectiveness of the policy alone, with minimal trade-offs 9. Slide 6 On November 18, 2014, we even reaffirmed our consistency and proactive steps to achieve a pro-stability-oriented monetary policy, namely by raising the benchmark interest rate to 7.75%. This policy is a pre-emptive measure to minimize the continued impact of fuel price hikes on November 17, on future inflationary pressures. We would like to point out that inflationary pressures due to rising fuel prices are only temporary, and the rate of inflation and expectations going forward remains anchored in the medium-term inflation target range of 4b11% 10. Slide 7 We believe that, with inflation and expectations anchored at a low rate, real savings and people's purchasing power are not will be eroded, thus becoming the foundation for economic growth and a stronger pace of poverty alleviation going forward. In addition, low and stable inflation relative to the exchange rate of peer countries will make the rupiah exchange rate on a real (Real Effective Exchange Rate) become more competitive thus increasing the competitiveness of our export performance in the world market 11. Slide 8. The policy of raising interest rates is also to ensure that the current account deficit, which has been going on for along time for three years, remains under control at around 2.5 - 3 percent of GDP and not enlarged. A manageable current account deficit is essential to ensure that the national economy can grow strongly and balanced, and that job creation can continue. 12. Moreover, we want to ensure investor confidence - about the overall consistency and quality of Indonesia's macroeconomic policy management - remains strong, amid the approach of rising rates. global interest goingforward. Dear Father /Mother we respect 13. We hope that macro stability maintained throughout 2014 as a prerequisite for the continuity of economic growth sustainability in the future will be maintained. This is remembering the year 2015 we're about to enter is a stormy year of challenges. 14. It seems quite possible that the changes in the constellation of the global economy since the 2008 crisis, which felt so broad and profound, have given rise to new challenges, which are increasingly complex in the management of macroeconomic stability. External shock and uncertainty seem to be a constant dimension that constantly follows our steps. 15. In the midst of the strong currents of globalization where countries and regions are intertwined in increasingly complex relations, any formulation and implementation of economic policies will inevitably face inevitability about "certainty and uncertainty". The sure thing is that any open economy like Indonesia will face shock global with type, which is not always the same as it is. Meanwhile, the "uncertain thing" is about when the global shock will occur, how big it will be, and how it will shape. 16. Slide 9 Although the global economy is cyclically recovering (cyclical expansion), it is still too low and unbalanced, and prone to shock. The U.S. and U.K. economies are indeed experiencing a solid recovery, but the Euro and Japanese economies on the contrary are still caught in stagnation and the threat of deflasi. In the US and UK, the restructuring of the banking sector and the decline in the debt burden (deleveraging) of the household sector are taking place faster than in the Euro area. Similarly, the fiscal drag in the US, can be handled more cepat. The delayed effect of the long-running episode of low interest rates and wider fiscal space, will make the wheels of the US economy turn faster 17. Meanwhile, China's economy is undergoing a structural transition from an era of slowing double-digit economic growth to a "new normal" era of around 7.0 percent. This is due to the aging of the population and the correction of government policies to rebalancing the structure of economic growth by reducing investment in infrastructure and industrial infrastructure, as well as controlling the expansion of the housing sector very rapidly. 18. Slide 10 The logical consequence of the change in the constellation of the global economy will color the "main global theme" in 2015, namely the divergence of global monetary policy, where the US Federal Reserve will normalize interest rates, while the European Central Bank and the Bank of Japan will stay afloat with accommodative ulta monetary policy 19. Slide U The episode of normalization of a rates in the US is expected to last quite a long and gradual period, to ensure that rising interest rates do not interfere with the ongoing economic expansion. This divergence in monetary policy has been represented in the form of the strengthening of the US dollar currency since mid-2014. In line with the long episodes of future interest rate normalization, the strengthening of the US dollar will take place in the next few years. Tightness of liquidity the dollar is expected to be experienced in developing countries with weak economic fundamentals 20. The strengthening of the US dollar was also supported by the decreasing US trade deficit due to the increase in domestic oil production as a result of the latest technological innovations in oilfield exploration. The decline in oil prices in recent months is a symptom of the shrewdness of technological innovation rather than due to the weakening of the global economy. Dear Father /Mother we respect 21. How will the strong global winds in the future affect Emerging Market including Indonesia? We expect Emerging Market countries, which are building on the capabilities of fundamental economic strengths through structural reforms, to be expected to have a fairly good macro stability resilience. 22. Slide 12. In addition, global investors are expected to be intolerant of Emerging Market countries with many fundamental problems, such as the current account deficit, deficit in the primary balance of the budget, and weak ability to assess foreign debt and inflation 23. The overall change in the geo-monetary constellation that has the potential to cause global shock in the future cannot be underestimated. Our economy's ability to continue to grow continuously and its strong risilience to global shock will depend on concrete and rapid steps in addressing some structural constraints, which have already settled from year to year. 24. Slide 13 The three-year current account deficit, which has been going on for three years , and is a binding constraint for our economy to grow higher, is also a big mirror that reflects some structural flaws, including weaknesses in the structure of domestic production. So far, our high dependence on exports of low value-added natural resources has made export performance vulnerable to price fluctuations. In addition, our ability to export high value-added goods , both by utilizing domestic production factors and by importing intermediate goods, is also very much weak 25. As a developing country, we realize that the technological deficit causes us to still have to import capital goods and intermediate goods. However, the import of these technologies is not an obstacle if we are able to become a production center for export-oriented touring manufak. 26. Slide 14 We also note that measures to reduce the level of micro-risks in the business world are urgent, so that the investment climate in all corners of the country will be better in the future, as a result of improvements in (i) ease of doing business, (ii) quality of public services and their governance, and (iii) strengthening the quality of human resources in the bureaucracy 27. Therefore, we welcome and fully support the determination of the "Working Cabinet", in accelerating the pace of reform structural to build a stronger enabler environment for increased investment. The improvement in overall economic efficiency will make Indonesia very attractive, not only because of the large size of the domestic market, but also as a global production base . Happy ladies and gentlemen 28. Some of the crises of the past have taught valuable lessons, that amid the strong currents of globalization, we are required to be faster and more proactive in recognizing problems and taking judgments. Our delay in responding to the global shock, often makes us lose momentum which has consequences for the magnitude of the costs that the economy has to bear. 29. Slide 15 In an era where global funds flow without knowing cross-border capital flows, an economic crisis in one country can spread rapidly to another. This has caused the frequency of global economic crises to become more and more frequent, with cycles shortening in the past two decades or so. In this context, proactive attitude and speed in making decisions are increasingly important given that the shock of global turmoil always has the opportunity to reappear Dear Father /Mother we respect 30. Some episodes of past crises also provide lessons that the unavailability of statistical data and information with a wide scope, timely ,and accurately weakens the capacity of policymakers to respond and take effective policy making. 31. However, an effective policy response also requires not only structured but also unstructured data, including data and information to capture some of the coolchallenges that have come to the fore. excessive risk-taking and stacking "leverage" in several sectors of the economy. In this regard we are pioneering the development of the national balance sheet, to capture the various vulnerabilities inherent in the balance sheets of financial and non-financial institutions, corporations, and sectors the public and households need to. 32. Considering the importance of providing complete, accurate, and timely data and information as a foundation in conducting economic assessments and formulating monetary, macroprudential, and system policies payment, Bank Indonesia also continues to strive to improve the quality of data/information. This is achieved, among others, through the development of increasingly advanced and erintegrative data collection systems and methodologies. 33. Various data and information in the form of structured and unstructured data, anecdotal will continue to be strengthened and improved. In addition, data sources or whistleblowers also continue to be sought to be expanded, so that it includes not only business actors in the financial sector but also increasingly expanded so that it includes business actors (corporations) and the general public (individuals). 34. In the future, the overall data and information we obtain both in the form of structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data will become part of an information system based on "big data" I Dear Father/Mother we respect 35. We would like to express our appreciation to all of you as whistleblowers in submitting reports to Bank Indonesia that continue to show improvement. This is due to the good synergy between Bank Indonesia and the whistleblowers, through socialization and bilateral consultations (coaching and clinic) to help the whistleblowers understand the reporting provisions. 36. We will continue to strive for whistleblowers to pay attention to and implement two important things in reporting, namely timely and quality-appropriate. We do this considering that the good quality of data from the whistleblower will determine the quality of information and statistics presented by Bank Indonesia. Furthermore, good data quality will also improve the quality of Bank Indonesia's policies. As we can say, may God always protect, meridhoi and ease our steps. Amin. Thank you. Wassaiamu'aiaikum warahmatuiiahi wabarakatuh Agus DW Martowadojo Governor of Bank Indonesia
text_original: Meningkatkan Efektivitas Kebijakan Ekonomi melalui Pengembangan Si stem Informasi yang Berkualitas Keynote Address Agus D.W. Martowardojo Gubernur Bank Indonesia Pada Acara Pertemuan Gubernur Bank Indonesia dengan Pelapor Jakarta, 2 November 2014 Yang kami hormati, <95> Menteri Keuangan Bapak Bambang Brodjonegoro <95> Menteri ESDM, Bapak Sudirman Said <95> Kepala SKK Migas, Bapak Amien Sunaryadi <95> Dirjen Bea Cukai, Bapak Agung Kuswandono <95> Meneg BUMN, diwakili Bapak Sahala Lumban Gaol <95> Menko Kemaritiman, diwakili Bapak Safri Burhanudin <95> Anggota VII BPK, Bapak Achsanul Qosasi <95> Anggota II BPK, Bapak Agus Joko Pramono Assalamu'alaikum Warahmatullahi Wabarakatuh, Sa lam Sejahtera untuk kita semua 1. Pertama-tama marilah kita panjatkan puji syukur kehadirat Allah SWT, Tuhan Yang Maha Kuasa, karena atas perkenan-Nya kita dapat berkumpul pada pagi hari ini dalam suasana yang sangat baik. 2. Dalam kesempatan yang berbahagia ini, kami atas nama seluruh anggota Dewan Gubernur Bank Indonesia, menghaturkan terimakasih atas kehadiran Bapak/Ibu sekalian, yang telah meluangkan waktu di sela-sela kesibukannya yang cukup padat untuk menghadiri acara pertemuan kami dengan Bapak/Ibu sekalian sebagai mitra kerja Bank Indonesia. 3. Harapan besar kami, acara pertemuan ini akan bermanfaat sebagai sebuah wadah untuk memperat jalinan silaturahmi dan komunikasi antara kami sebagai pemangku kebijakan di bidang moneter, makroprudensial, dan sistem pembayaran, dengan pelaku utama dunia usaha seperti Bapak/ibu sekalian yang berperan besar dalam memutar roda perekonomian. Bapak/ibu sekalian yang kami hormati 4. Kita saat ini berada dipenghujung tahun 2014, dan tidak lama lagi akan membuka lembaran baru tahun 2015. Meskipun masih banyak beban persoalan struktural yang belum tuntas dibenahi, kita boleh mengatakan tahun 2014 adalah tahun penuh catatan-catatan keberhasilan. 5. Tahun 2014 adalah tahun puncak proses transisi politik dimana kita berhasil melaksanakan pemilu yang sangat demokratis dengan damai, jujur, dan adil. Kita meyakini demokrasi yang terbangun sudah semakin terkonsolidasi dan sistem Pemerintahan dan berbagai perangkat birokrasi akan semakin efektif dalam menjalankan tugasnya. 6. <Slide 3> Pada tahun ini juga adalah tahun kita kembali meraih stabilitas makro, setelah selama semester kedua tahun 2013 lalu kapabilitas kita dalam mengelola stabilitas ekonomi memperoleh ujian berat akibat dimulainya proses normalisasi kebijakan moneter di AS, bersamaan dengan meningkatnya inflasi sebagai dampak lanjutan kenaikkan harga BBM. Pada Juni 2013 tercatat capital outflows sebesar USD 4,1 miliar 7. <Slide 4> Kita patut bersyukur, langkah kebijakan tegas, proaktif, dan konsisten yang ditempuh Pemerintah dalam mereformasi fiskal dan Bank Indonesia dalam menempuh kebijakan moneter yang konsisten pro-stabilitas, telah menumbuhkan kepercayaan pelaku ekonomi dan pasar terhadap kualitas pengelolaan kebijakan makroekonomi, mengarahkan ekonomi pada struktur yang lebih berimbang, dan mencegah kemerosotan ekonomi yang dalam atau hard landing 8. <Slide 5>. Dalam menjalankan mandatnya sebagai pengawal stabilitas, Bank Indonesia harus senantiasa konsisten dalam bersikap dan proaktif dan tegas dalam mengambil langkah. Konsistensi dan proaktif, keduanya menjadi kunci untuk membangun kepercayaan masyarakat, sehingga terbangun kredibilitas kebijakan, yang pada gilirannya akan meningkatkan efektivitas kebijakan itu sendiri, dengan trade-off yang minimal 9. <Slide 6> Pada 18 November 2014 lalu, kami bahkan menegaskan kembali konsistensi dan langkah proaktif untuk menempuh kebijakan moneter berorientasi pro-stabilitas, yaitu dengan menaikkan suku bunga acuan menjadi 7,75%. Kebijakan ini sebagai langkah preemptive untuk meminimalkan dampak lanjutan kenaikan harga BBM pada 17 November, pada tekanan inflasi kedepan. Kami ingin memastikan, bahwa tekanan inflasi akibat kenaikan harga BBM hanya bersifat sementara, dan laju inflasi serta ekspektasinya kedepan tetap terjangkar pada kisaran sasaran inflasi jangka menengah yaitu 4<b1>1% 10. <Slide 7> Kami meyakini, dengan inflasi dan ekspektasinya yang terjangkar pada laju yang rendah, tabungan riil dan daya beli masyarakat tidak akan tergerus, sehingga menjadi fondasi bagi pertumbuhan ekonomi dan laju pengentasan kemiskinan yang lebih kuat kedepan. Selain itu, inflasi yang terjaga rendah dan stabil relatif terhadap nilai tukar negara peers akan membuat nilai tukar rupiah secara real (Real Effective Exchange Rate) menjadi lebih kompetitif sehingga meningkatkan daya saing kinerja ekspor kita di pasar dunia 11. <Slide 8>. Kebijakan menaikkan suku bunga juga untuk memastikan bahwa defisit neraca transaksi berjalan yang sudah berlangsung selama tiga tahun, tetap terkendali di sekitar 2.5 - 3 persen dari PDB dan tidak membesar. Defisit neraca transaksi berjalan yang terkendali sangatlah penting untuk memastikan perekonomian nasional dapat tumbuh kuat dan berimbang, serta penciptaan lapangan kerja dapat terus berlanjut 12. Lebih dari pada itu, kami ingin memastikan kepercayaan investor - tentang keseluruhan konsistensi dan kualitas pengelolaan kebijakan ekonomi makro Indonesia - tetap kuat, ditengah semakin dekatnya peningkatan suku bunga global kedepan. Bapak/Ibu sekalian yang kami hormati 13. Kita berharap kestabilan makro yang terpelihara sepanjang 2014 sebagai prasyarat penopang (element of continuity) kesinambungan pertumbuhan ekonomi ke depan, akan tetap terjaga. Ini mengingat tahun 2015 yang akan kita masuki adalah tahun yang sarat badai tantangan. 14. Rasanya kita cukup mahfum bahwa perubahan konstelasi ekonomi global sejak krisis 2008 lalu yang terasa begitu luas dan mendalam, telah memunculkan berbagai tantangan baru, yang semakin komplek dalam pengelolaan stabilitas makroekonomi. Kejutan eksternal dan ketidakpastian seakan-akan adalah sebuah dimensi konstan yang terus menerus mengikuti langkah kita. 15. Di tengah kuatnya arus globalisasi dimana negara dan kawasan saling terkait dalam hubungan yang semakin kompleks, setiap perumusan dan implementasi kebijakan ekonomi pasti akan berhadapan dengan keniscayaan tentang "kepastian dan ketidakpastian". Hal yang pasti adalah bahwa setiap perekonomian yang terbuka seperti Indonesia akan menghadapi shock global dengan tipe, yang tidak selamanya sama-sebangun. Sedangkan, "hal yang tidak pasti" adalah tentang kapan shock global tersebut akan terjadi, berapa besarnya, dan bagaimana bentuknya. 16. <Slide 9> Meskipun perkenomian global secara siklikal sedang pulih (cyclical expansion), namun masih terlalu rendah dan tidak berimbang, serta rentan terhadap shock. Ekonomi AS dan Inggris memang tengah mengalami pemulihan yang solid, namun ekonomi Euro dan Jepang sebaliknya masih terperangkap dalam stagnasi dan ancaman deflasi. Di AS dan Inggris, penyehatan sektor perbankan dan penurunan beban utang (deleveraging) sektor rumah tangga berlangsung lebih cepat dibandingkan dengan kawasan Euro. Demikian pula, kebuntuan politik fiskal (fiscal drag) di AS, mampu ditangani lebih cepat. Efek tunda dari episode suku bunga rendah yang sudah berlangsung lama dan ruang fiskal yang lebih luas, akan menjadikan roda perekonomian AS berputar lebih cepat 17. Sementara itu, ekonomi Tiongkok tengah mengalami transisi struktural dari era pertumbuhan ekonomi dua digit melambat ke era "new normal" sekitar 7,0 persen. Ini disebabkan oleh menuanya populasi penduduk dan koreksi kebijakan pemerintah untuk menyeimbangkan kembali (rebalancing) struktur pertumbuhan ekonomi dengan menurunkan investasi di bidang infrastruktur dan prasarana industri, serta pengendalian ekpansi sektor perumahan yang sangat pesat. 18. <Slide 10> Konsekuensi logis dari perubahan konstelasi ekonomi global tersebut akan mewarnai "tema utama global" pada tahun 2015, yaitu divergensi kebijakan moneter global, dimana the US Federal Reserve akan melakukan normalisasi suku bunga, sedangkan European Central Bank dan Bank of Japan akan tetap bertahan dengan kebijakan moneter ulta akomodatif 19. <Slide U> Episode normalisasi suku bunga di AS diperkirakan akan berlangsung cukup lama dan bertahap, untuk memastikan peningkatan suku bunga tidak mengganggu ekspansi ekonomi yang tengah berlangsung. Divergensi kebijakan moneter ini sudah direpresentasikan dalam bentuk menguatnya mata uang dollar AS sejak pertengahan 2014 lalu. Sejalan dengan panjangnya episode normalisasi suku bunga ke depan, penguatan dollar AS akan berlangsung dalam beberapa tahun ke depan. Keketatan likuiditas dollar diperkirakan akan di alami di negara berkembang dengan dengan fundamental ekonomi yang lemah 20. Penguatan dollar AS juga ditopang oleh menurunnya defisit perdagangan AS karena meningkatnya produksi minyak domestik sebagai buah dari inovasi teknologi terkini dalam eksplorasi ladang minyak. Menurunnya harga minyak dalam beberapa bulan terakhir merupakan symptom dari keberhailan inovasi teknologi tersebut ketimbang karena melemahnya ekonomi global. Bapak/Ibu sekalian yang kami hormati 21. Bagaimana angin haluan global yang kencang ke depan berpengaruh terhadap Emerging Market termasuk Indonesia? Kami memperkirakan negara Emerging Market yang lebih awal membangun kapabilitas kekuatan fundamental ekonomi melalui reformasi structural, diperkirakan akan memiliki daya risiliensi stabilitas makro yang cukup baik. 22. <Slide 12>. Sebaliknya, investor global diperkirakan tidak akan toleran terhadap negara Emerging Market dengan banyak permasalahan fundamental, seperti defisit neraca transaksi berjalan, defisit pada keseimbangan primer anggaran, serta lemahnya kemampuan dalam mengedalikan utang luar negeri dan inflasi 23. Perubahan keseluruhan konstelasi geo-moneter tersebut yang berpotensi menimbulkan shock global ke depan tidak dapat kita pandang remeh. Kemampuan ekonomi kita untuk terus tumbuh bersinambung dan risiliensinya yang kuat terhadap shock global akan tergantung pada langkah konkrit dan cepat dalam mengatasi beberapa kendala struktural, yang sudah menetap dari tahun ke tahun. 24. <Slide 13> Defisit neraca transaksi berjalan yang sudah berlangsung tiga tahun ini, dan menjadi penghambat (binding constraint) bagi ekonomi kita untuk tumbuh lebih tinggi, juga merupakan cermin besar yang merefleksikan beberapa kelemahan struktural, termasuk kelemahan pada struktur produksi domestik. Selama ini, ketergantungan kita yang tinggi pada ekspor SDA bernilai tambah rendah telah membuat kinerja ekspor rentan terhadap fluktuasi harga. Selain itu, kemampuan kita untuk mengekspor barang bernilai tambah tinggi, baik dengan memanfaatkan faktor produksi domestik maupun dengan impor barang antara, juga masih sangat lemah 25. Sebagai negara berkembang, kita menyadari bahwa defisit teknologi menyebabkan kita masih harus mengimpor barang modal dan barang antara. Namun, impor teknologi tersebut bukanlah kendala jika kita mampu menjadi sentra produksi bagi manufaktur berorientasi ekspor. 26. <Slide 14> Kami juga mencatat langkah-langkah untuk menurunkan tingkat risiko mikro dunia usaha sudah sangat mendesak, agar iklim investasi di seluruh pelosok negeri akan lebih baik kedepannya, sebagai hasil dari perbaikan pada (i) kemudahan berusaha, (ii) kualitas layanan publik serta tata kelolanya, dan (iii) penguatan kualitas SDM di birokrasi 27. Oleh karena itu, kami menyambut baik dan mendukung sepenuhnya tekad "Kabinet Kerja", dalam mempercepat langkah reformasi struktural untuk membangun lingkungan pendukung (enabler) yang lebih kuat bagi peningkatan investasi. Perbaikan efisiensi perekonomian secara keseluruhan akan menjadikan Indonesia sangat menarik, tidak hanya karena ukuran pasar domestik yang besar, tapi juga sebagai basis produksi global. Bapak/Ibu sekalian yang berbahagia 28. Beberapa krisis di masa lalu memberikan pelajaran berharga, bahwa ditengah kuatnya arus globalisasi, kita dituntut semakin cepat dan proaktif dalam mengenali permasalahan dan mengambil keputusan. Keterlambatan kita dalam merespon shock global, seringkali membuat kita kehilangan momentum yang membawa konsekuensi pada besarnya biaya yang harus ditanggung oleh perekonomian. 29. <Slide 15> Di era dimana dana-dana global mengalir tanpa mengenal batas negara (cross border capital flows), krisis ekonomi di suatu negara dapat merambat dengan cepat ke negara lain. Ini menyebabkan frekuensi krisis ekonomi global menjadi semakin sering, dengan siklus yang memendek dalam dua dekade terakhir ini. Dalam kondisi demikian, sikap proaktif dan kecepatan dalam mengambil keputusan semakin penting mengingat shock gejolak global selalu berpeluang untuk muncul kembali Bapak/Ibu sekalian yang kami hormati 30. Beberapa episode krisis di masa lalu juga memberikan pelajaran bahwa ketidak-tersediaan data statistik dan informasi dengan cakupan yang luas, tepat waktu (timely), dan akurat melemahkan kapasitas pemangku kebijakan untuk merespon dan mengambil kebijakan yang tepat waktu dan efektif (effective policy making). 31. Namun, respon kebijakan yang efektif juga tidak hanya memerlukan data yang terstruktur tapi juga yang tidak terstruktur, termasuk data dan infomasi untuk menangkap beberapa kerentanan yang mengemuka akibat pengambilan risiko yang berlebihan (excessive risk-taking) dan penumpukkan "leverage" pada beberapa sektor ekonomi. Terkait ini kami sedang merintis pengembangan neraca nasional, untuk menangkap berbagai kerentanan yang melekat pada neraca lembaga keuangan dan non-keuangan, korporasi, serta sektor publik dan rumah tangga perlu. 32. Mempertimbangkan pentingnya ketersediaan data dan informasi yang lengkap, akurat, dan tepat waktu sebagai fondasi dalam melakukan asesmen ekonomi dan perumusan kebijakan moneter, makroprudensial, dan sistem pembayaran, Bank Indonesia juga terus berupaya untuk meningkatkan kualitas data/informasi. Ini ditempuh antara lain melalui pengembangan sistem dan metodologi pengumpulan data yang semakin maju dan terintegratif. 33. Berbagai data dan informasi baik yang berupa data yang terstruktur maupun tidak terstruktur, anekdotal akan terus diperkuat dan ditingkatkan. Selain itu, sumber data atau pelapor juga terus diupayakan untuk diperbanyak, sehingga mencakup tidak hanya pelaku usaha di sektor keuangan tetapi juga semakin diperluas sehingga mencakup pelaku usaha (korporasi) dan masyarakat umum (individu). 34. Ke depan keseluruhan data dan informasi yang kami peroleh baik dalam bentuk data terstruktur, semi terstruktur, dan tidak terstruktur akan menjadi bagian dari sistem informasi yang berbasis "big data" io Bapak/Ibu sekalian yang kami hormati 35. Kami menyampaikan apresiasi kepada Bapak/Ibu sekalian sebagai pelapor dalam penyampaian laporan kepada Bank Indonesia yang terus menunjukkan perbaikan. Ini terjadi karena adanya sinergi yang baik antara Bank Indonesia dan para pelapor, melalui sosialisasi maupun konsultasi secara bilateral {coaching and clinic) untuk membantu para pelapor memahami ketentuan pelaporan. 36. Kami akan terus berupaya agar para pelapor memperhatikan dan menerapkan dua hal penting dalam pelaporan, yaitu tepat waktu dan tepat kualitas. Hal ini kami lakukan mengingat kualitas data yang baik dari pelapor akan menentukan kualitas informasi maupun statistik yang disajikan oleh Bank Indonesia. Selanjutnya, kualitas data yang baik akan meningkatkan pula kualitas kebijakan Bank Indonesia. Demikian yang dapat kami sampaikan, semoga Tuhan YME senantiasa melindungi, meridhoi dan meringankan langkah kita. Amin. Sekian dan terima kasih. Wassaiamu'aiaikum warahmatuiiahi wabarakatuh Agus DW Martowadojo Gubernur Bank Indonesia

Title: Keynote Speech: IIFM Industry Seminar on Islamic Financial Market, Bahrain 1st December 2014, Dr. Halim Alamsyah, Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia
text: Keynote Speech: IIFM Industry Seminar on Islamic Financial Market, Bahrain 1st December 2014 Dr. Halim Alamsyah Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia *** The Legacy of Islamic Finance : A Path to Financial Stability and Sustainable Economic Development Bismillahi rahmani rahiim,  His Excellency: Mr. Khalid Hamad, Chairman, International Islamic Financial Market (IIFM);  His Excellency: Mr. Elgaili Mohamed Albashir, Deputy Governor, Central Bank of Sudan;  Honorable Board of Directors of IIFM;  Mr. Ijlal Ahmed Alvi, CEO of International Islamic Financial Market (IIFM);  Prominent speakers; and,  All participants, Excellencies, Honorable Speakers, Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen Assalamu alaikum Warrahmatullahi Wabarokatuh, very good morning to all of us [Greeting] 1. It is both a pleasure and an honor for me to be here today, to speak before such a distinguished audience. Let me first thank you to the Central Bank of Bahrain for providing excellent support and hospitality to the success of this event. Against the backdrop of increasingly challenging global environment, this seminar is a strategic avenue to enhance our common understanding on the situation that we are all currently facing with and possibly to discuss some strategies to benefit from them in developing the global Islamic financial markets. Excellencies, ladies and gentlemen [The overview of Islamic finance in the context of global economy] 2. It has been six years since the peak of the 2008 global financial crisis. Signs of economic recovery have indeed materialized, but growth is still low and volatile. Although the United States, the locomotive of the worlds economy, has begun to demonstrate consistent indications of recovery, its medium and long term growth trend has declined compared to the pre-crisis period. 3. In other parts of the world, growth of Euro area and Japan remain fragile. Threats of deflation still overshadow both economies. China  the worlds manufacturing center  is also experiencing slower economic growth. Such grim development have even prompted a question, is this slow growth the new normal? 1 of 5 4. In the global financial market, the imminent risk is the normalization of US monetary policy. Following the increase of Fed Fund rate, re-pricing the risk investment appetite and financial asset valuation by investors may generate a shifting of global portfolio flows. 5. We see more challenging economic environment in the near future. Nevertheless, this situation also offers more opportunities in the context of Islamic finance development. We believe that there will be increasing need of safer and more stable instrument, including Islamic financial products, in time of rising uncertainty. Islamic financial market demonstrated a stronger resiliency based on the experience of previous global financial crisis. Because of that fact, we believe that Islamic finance has continued to become new frontier and offer more prospective financial model in this challenging global economic landscape. 6. Moreover, salient characteristic of Islamic finance to require a close link between real sector activities and financial markets has positioned Islamic finance to be well-anchored in serving the real economy, manifested into broadening strong production base, unemployment reduction and greater inclusion of economic development. With pro-growth, pro-poor, and financial stability characteristics, an internationalisation of Islamic finance may unleash country true economic growth potential. Excellencies, ladies and gentlemen [Recent development of Islamic Financial Market] 7. In the midst of global economic slowdown, the performance of Islamic financial market is delightful. Islamic capital and money markets, driven by sukuk grow rapidly in a number of jurisdictions. Until recently, there have been several countries as those in Europe and Asia dedicatedly reviewed their legislations and tax regime in order to offer sukuk and develop the Islamic sukuk market. As a result, some of the sukuk were issued in multi-currencies for tapping a wider investor base and to finance variety of government and private projects. 8. Based on IIFMs sukuk report that will be released today, it is found that the global sukuk issuance has reached US668 billion (BHD252 billion) with sukuk outstanding reaching US303 billion until July 2014, and this year the total sukuk issuance has also been growing positively as per July 2014 to over US68 billion (BHD26 billion). In line with that, Kuwait Finance House (KFH) Research Report revealed that the global Islamic banking assets have also gone up US1.8 trilion by the end of 2013 or increased by 16% yoy1. Excellencies, ladies and gentlemen [The importance of liquidity and risk management] 9. Responding to the growing Islamic financial market, liquidity management plays a pivotal role in assuring the operational sustainability of the Islamic financial institutions, while completing the sufficient infrastructures and comprehensing instruments available in the 1 Source: IIFM, Moodys, KFH Research 2 of 5 markets. Empirical evidences showed that severe liquidity shortfall may be able to throw illiquid but solvent banks into insolvency. 10. However, the effectiveness of Islamic liquidity management instruments, currently is rather questioned, as the inter-bank liquidity management with instruments like mudharabah, wakalah, commodity murabahah and sukuk repurchase agreement are relatively shallow. In addition, liquidity of sukuk in secondary market is relatively low because sukuk are treated by most market players as an investment instrument as opposed to a tradable instrument for a liquidity purpose. Moreover, most of the sovereign sukuk issuance is to finance budget deficit as opposed to finance large scale investment projects. 11. As such, in cooperation with IIFM, the International Islamic Liquidity Management (IILM) comes to enhancee liquidity management in Islamic financial institutions through periodic issuance of short-term shariah compliant financial instruments. With its unique business model, the IILM opens the possibility for the Islamic financial institutions either to invest in Islamic liquid instruments or to issue the global sovereign sukuk in a broader market and more efficient way. By doing so, it will open opportunities for countries to enhance Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) that contributes to the real economic growth. 12. Within Indonesian context, the Indonesian Authority in banking and finance sectors namely Bank Indonesia, Indonesian FSA (OJK), and Ministry of Finance have cooperatively had some efforts to deepen the Indonesian Islamic financial markets especially sukuk and Islamic money markets through islamic financial market development framework. 13. Related to this issue, Bank Indonesia has significant role to promote Islamic money market development. So far, Bank Indonesia has provided repurchase facilities for Islamic money market instruments particularly with SBIS (Central Bank Islamic Certificate), reverse repo of SBSN (government sukuk), repurchase facilities for Islamic money market instruments particularly with SBIS, and recently term deposit FX for liquidity management in domestic market. Now Bank Indonesia is about to issue regulation pertaining shariah compliant repurchase agreement. Other Islamic financial instruments are also in the pipeline to be developed. 14. With regard to the development of Islamic hedging instruments (tahawwut), the development is still low due to regulatory and legal challenges faced by many countries. Not all Islamic hedging can be implemented in different countries due to differences in fatwa. In Indonesia for example, National Shariah Council only allows if the hedging product is not for speculative purposes and based on productive sectors as an underlying asset. Whereas, hedging instrument could be crucial for risk management in the midst of global economic uncertainty. 3 of 5 Excellencies, Ladies and gentlemen, [Importance of IIFM roles] 15. Given the importance of liquidity and risk management, and financial deepening for Islamic financial industry that I have ben highlighting, IIFM, as one of the international Islamic standard setting bodies, has played an impressive role in an effort to standardize the Islamic capital and money market documentations along with the products. Up until now, IIFM has been sucessfully able to highlight and address very essential and complicated issues related to the Islamic financial services industry such as Islamic hedging (tahawwut) master agreement along with certain Islamic hedging products, Islamic collateralisation (rahn), inter-bank unrestricted master wakalah agreement, and other instruments as liquidity management tools. 16. Recently, IIFM has just launched a template of standardized contract namely collateralised murabaha transactions, aiming to boost the usage of liquidity management instruments for Islamic financial institutions. This is imperative development made by IIFM to help Islamic financial industry meeting its liquidity requirements and addressing the scarce shariah compliant repos. For that reason, I would like to appreciate and congratulate IIFM for initiating such a notable development. 17. I am also glad to know that IIFM also has an ongoing initiative for Islamic financial deepening through developing new shariah compliant products such as FX forward, Islamic cross currency swap, market risk participation agreement in addressing market needs and risk management tools. Initiatives that have been taken by IIFM so far are very selective and based on the recommendation of the industry and tailor made practical solutions in consultation with all stakeholders. The main objective of the initiatives is to facilitate unification, shariah harmonisation and legal reforms in Islamic financial industry across jurisdictions. 18. In achieving IIFM initiatives, IIFM develops strategic plans whereby IIFM addresses the very selective product and documentation standardisation needs of the Islamic financial industry based on its recommendations through a well-established procedure. Apart from that, IIFM provides universal platform by bringing regulatory bodies, financial institutions, law firms, stock exchanges, industry associations, infrastructure service providers and other market participants on a common platform through the creation of project specific global working groups and committees. Excellencies, Ladies and gentlemen, [Key challenges ahead for Regulatory Authorities] 19. Moving forward, there are four identified major challenges ahead to be coped in order to make Islamic financial industry more competitive and continuously flourish within the right trajectory. Firstly, regulatory clarity and legal certainty whereby the standards for Islamic finance, especially for Islamic banking, are relatively fragmented across jurisdictions due to different fatwas interpretation and legal enforcement in each respective jurisdiction. For 4 of 5 that reason, there is a need for harmonisation of perception as well as unison standard and regulation across jurisdictions, which can be achieved by cross border collaboration between key players, regulators, and international standard setting bodies. 20. Secondly, human capacity development in the Islamic financial industry across all sectors. The central issue in this particular challenge is that a dichotomy between shariah and finance skills. People who are well versed in shariah skills do not necessarily possess finance skill, and vice versa. In light of that issue, academic institutions and Islamic financial institutions are critical to work hand-in-hand in order to pursue initiatives in fostering a set of skillful Islamic finance talent in the industry. 21. Thirdly, there are missing gaps between Islamic finance theory and actual practices as reflected gaps between academicians and practitioners. These gaps should be bridged by more practical and pragmatic research conducted by academicians in collaboration with practitioners with the objective of bringing feasible solutions for the inherent gaps in Islamic financial industry and also shariah awareness for market participants. 22. Lastly, low technological difussion in Islamic financial market development. To accelerate Islamic financial market, the development should incorporate technology advancement such as digital mobile banking technology, big data management, IT interfaces with a third party, in order to be more competitive and to anticipate disruptive megatrends in the future. Excellencies, Ladies and gentlemen, [Conclusion and closing remark] 1. To conclude, I, as one of the founding members of IIFM, would like to point out some of the IIFM concerns with regard to its efforts and the level of participation and support required to fully achieving IIFMs objectives. I strongly encourage all stakeholders to take an active role in IIFM efforts to promote global standardisation of Islamic capital markets and money market products. I also urge all the main standard setting organisations to collaborate and come up with more practical shariah compliant solutions to cater the economic and financial needs of the ummah. I believe that all we do will be our legacy as path to promote financial stability and support sustainability in the economic development to deliver more prosperity in our economy. 2. Finally, please allow me to express my sincere appreciation to all committee, event organizers, and parties for arranging this important and useful seminar. My appreciation and sincere gratitude also to distinguished speakers for their willingness to share their expertise and knowledge for the betterment of Islamic financial industry. May Allah almighty bestow us the strength and patient to persevere in fulfilling our duty for a better future. Thank you very much and I wish you all very successful and fruitful deliberations in todays seminar. *** Wa billahi tawfiq wal hidayah, Wasalamualaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh *** 5 of 5

Title: Keynote Speech Gubernur Bank Indonesia, Agus Martowardojo "Bersinergi Mengawal Stabilitas, Mewujudkan Reformasi Struktural" pada Diskusi dan Peluncuran Buku Laporan Perekonomian Indonesia (LPI) 2015, Jakarta 28 April 2016
text: Keynote Speech by the Governor of Bank Indonesia "Synergize to Safeguard Stability, Realize Structural Reforms" Jakarta, 28 April 2016 What we respect: 95 Ladies and gentlemen of our predecessors as Governor of Bank Indonesia, 95 Chairman of the Board of Commissioners of the Financial Services Authority, 95 Minister of Finance of the Republic of Indonesia, 95 Mr. Members of the House of Representatives and the CPC Rl, 95 Mr.-lbu Member of BSBI, 95 Mr. Member of the Board of Governors of Bank Indonesia, and 95 Mr.-lbu Speakers, Responders, and Moderators, as well as 95 Invitees, Happy Attendees, Assalamu'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh, Good morning and greetings to all of us, 1. First of all, let us invite the audience to offer thanksgiving to the presence of Allah Almighty because only by His grace and approval we have the opportunity to attend this event. God willing, soon we will witness together the launch of the Indonesian Economic Report Book (LPI) 2015 which was continued with a discussion with the theme "Synergize to Control Stability, Realize Structural Reform". 2. The LPI book is an annual routine publication of Bank Indonesia that comprehensively contains the dynamics of the national economy in the relevant year. In addition to documenting Indonesia's economic journey, LPI also seeks to convey a number of lessons that can be learned during this period of time. Efforts to explore lessons from the economic journey are quite important because they can be the foundation for strengthening and improving policies in the future. [Slide #2: Global Challenge 2015] Parents of the audience whom I respect 3. Indonesia's economy during 2015 was faced with a series of external pressures stemming from the global economy. The world economic recovery turned out to be not as expected, slow, unbalanced, and still full of uncertainty. On the one hand, developed countries, especially the United States economy, showed a more solid recovery. On the other hand, emerging economies, especially China, experienced a structural slowdown that did not trigger a slump in commodity prices, which in turn continued to suppress export performance. Indonesian. 4. The imbalance in the global economic recovery has resulted in a divergence in the monetary policy cycle between various countries. The monether policy in the United States began to enter a period of normalization, after within a period of six years interest rates were kept low. On the other hand, monetary policy in Europe, Japan, and developing countries has been further relaxed to restrain the pace of economic growth from slowing down. 5. In financial markets, turmoil arose due to the continued decline in commodity prices and uncertainty regarding the speed and magnitude of interest rate hikes in the United States, as well as currency devaluation The yuan that the market did not anticipate. This turmoil in turn resulted in a decrease in capital inflows to developing countries, including to Indonesia. [Slide #3: Domestic Challenges 2015] Parents of the audience whom I respect 6. The situation at the global level has a bad impact on the Indonesian economy due to a number of structural problems in the domestic economy. 7. Indonesia's export structure is more source-based , resulting in a slump in commodity prices, which in turn affects the slowdown in performance in various sectors of the economy. . 8. In addition, the high level of guidance on imports of raw materials / baranq between products or export activities causes the export-oriented industrial sector tonot be able to in a optimally utilizing rupiah depreciation to improve export performance. 9. On the other hand, the carrying of domestic sources of financing has led to a high dependence on sources of financing from abroad, especially in the flow of portfolio capital and external debt. private public. Whereas we all know that portfolio capital flows and external debt are strongly influenced by global dynamics and are vulnerable to exchange rate fluctuations. [Slide #4: Bank Indonesia Policy Mix] Parents of the audience whom I respect 10. Responding to these external and domestic challenges, Bank Indonesia together with the Government and financial services authority strengthen policy synergy aimed at safeguarding macroeconomic stability and boosting momentum economic growth. 11. Efforts to control macroeconomic stability are pursued by directing inflation to the target corridor for 2015 of 4b1.1%, reducing the current account deficit to a healthier level, and maintaining stability. the value of tukar rupiah that corresponds to its fundamentals. 12. To that end, Bank Indonesia has consistently and cautiously continued the strictly biased monetary policy adopted from mid-2013 to October 2015. This policy it was also strengthened by exchange rate stabilisation measures to ease excessive pressures on the rupiah that could disrupt economic stability. The implementation of policies in the management of private external debt also continues to be strengthened so that the ability of the business world is better andthe nature of managing risks, especially those caused by risk of exchange rate fluctuations. 13. Meanwhile, in an effort to stimulate economic recovery momentum, Bank Indonesia has relaxed macroprudential policy selectively and relaxed the minimum reserve requirement for rupiah. The policy is synergized with government policies to increase economic stimulus, as fiscal space becomes increasingly open as a positive impact of energy subsidy reforms . 14. In the real sector itself, efforts to accelerate the implementation of structural reforms are also continuously carried out, through the launch of a series of government policy packages, which are supported by several policy measures Bank Indonesia in deepening financial markets. [Slide #5: Structural Reform Throughout 2015] Parents of the audience whom I respect 15. In an effort to stimulate structural reforms in 2015, Bank Indonesia has coordinated with relevant authorities, focusing on the financial sector, real sector, and payment system as well as money management. rupiah. In the financial sector, reforms related to financial market deepening are aimed at strengthening economic fundamentals, among others, by maintaining the availability of liquidity, increasing ease of transactions, and maintaining price discovery. In the real sector, coordination in the context of implementing structural reforms is also carried out to increase the competitiveness of the national industry and also reforms in two leading fields, namely maritime affairs. and tourism. On the payment side, coordination is realized by establishing the Indonesian payment system forum (FSPI) as a means of communication and harmonization of strategic policy directions between authorities in the field of payment system. In terms of rupiah money management, coordination between the Government is carried out to expand the scope of money distribution in the territory of the Republic of Indonesia and improve the quality of money circulating in the community. [Slide #6: Policy Results] Mr. Mrs. happy audience 16. As we have seen together, the various policy mix responses pursued by Bl and the Government have succeeded in dampening pressures on macroeconomic stability and supporting economic growth momentum. The creation of macroeconomic stability is reflected in inflation in 2015 which was constrained byli, a narrowing current account deficit at a healthy level, the return of capital flows to domestic financial markets, as well as a more stable rupiah exchange rate. 17. The inflation rate can be controlled to the target range of 4b11%. This achievement was supported by managed domestic demand, anchored inflation expectations, and maintained adequate food supply. The current account deficit also narrowed to around 2.1% of GDP in line with managed domestic demand. Meanwhile, the capital and financial account improved in the fourth quarter of 2015 on the back of easing turmoil in global financial markets as well as improving market participants' perceptions of the outlook. Indonesian economy. In line with this, the rupiah exchange rate also began to be under control, even appreciated in the fourth quarter of 2015. 18. In terms of economic growth, the fiscal stimulus adopted by the Government and the return of market confidence were able to create momentum for increasing economic growth since the second half of 2015. In 2015, Indonesia was one of the emerging markets whose economy remained stable and relatively high growth compared to other emerging markets. [Slide #7: Lessons Learned] Parents of the audience whom I respect 19. The dynamics of the economy during 2015 gave birth to several important arrangements, which can strengthen the principles of policy implementation in managing the Indonesian economy in the future. 20. The first lesson: macroeconomic policies that are applied in a disciplined, prudent, consistent, and timely manner, both fiscal and monet, are key in maintaining stability macroeconomics and promote sustainable economic growth. 21. Second, the macroeconomic policy discipline also needs to be supported by strong policy synergy between policymakers, both Bank Indonesia, the Central and Regional Governments, and other relevant authorities. The right policies with strong synergy, not only bring the Indonesian economy through the shock, but also put the economy in the right position to mget the momentum of growth. 22. Lesson Three: the cycle of the national economy in recent years teaches about the importance of implementing structural reforms and diversifying the sources of economic growth, including downstreaming, which can be strengthen the foundation of the economy, so that the economy becomes more resilient (resilient) and grows sustainably. 23. These lessons are important because we believe that there is nothing coincidental about the economic dynamics of a nation. Our ability to draw lessons from the past will determine the economic future we are capable of forming. [Slide #8: Prospects and Challenges] Ladies and gentlemen, 24. Going forward, various challenges and risks need to be continuously anticipated and responded to with well-coordinated policies. On the external side, the possibility of a sluggish and unbalanced global economic recovery, the continued slowdown in the Chinese economy and the policy implications it has on the condition of world financial markets, as well as the decline in commodity prices, are three major risks that need to be mitigated. 25. In the neqeri, structural reform policies need to be implemented consistently and purposefully to encourage potential output and increase economic productivity and competitiveness. 26. To that end, coordination between Bank Indonesia and the Government in implementing monetary, fiscal and structural reform policies that synergize and strengthen each other will be continued. Bank Indonesia will implement a policy mix that remains directed at maintaining macroeconomic and financial system stability, while taking advantage of prudential and measured policy easing space, if various parameters in the economy permit. 27. With a mix of monetary, fiscal, and structural reform policies carried out in a disciplined, prudent, consistent, and measurable manner, within a synergistic coordination framework, indonesia's economy will grow stronger, more balanced, and sustainable in the future. 28. In 2016, Indonesia's economy is projected to grow 5.2-5.6% and continue to be on an upward trend in the medium term, in line with increasing economic capacity. With the increasing economic capacity, inflation is predicted to be maintained in line with the target corridor of 4b1.1% for 2016-2017 and 3.5b1.1% in the medium term. With a better economic structure and more diversified sources of growth, the current account deficit is expected to remain under control at a safe level and with a healthier structure. 29. In the medium term, the domestic economic outlook is on an increasing trajectory supported by a recovering global economy and the Government's structural policies in the real sector that are increasingly able to overcome various structural challenges. [Slide #9: Forward Recommendations Regarding Structural Reforms] Ladies and Gentlemen of the audience whom I respect 30. Going forward, coordination between Bank Indonesia and the Government in realizing structural reforms will need to be carried out continuously. This coordination is expected to strengthen synergy in responding to various structural issues, such as (1) food, energy and water security, (2) increasing the competitiveness of the national industry and also improving the maritim and tourism sectors, (3) financing sustainable development, (4) the economy more inclusive, and (5) strengthening the basic capital of development. Here we will briefly describe the concrete steps of structural reform in the future. 31. The agenda for structural reforms in the areas of food security, energy and water is still long and winding. Good coordination among policymakers is needed in an effort to increase agricultural productivity and overcome problems that arise in terms of production, distribution, marketing, and institutions. We welcome the Government's commitment and efforts in maintaining the availability of frugal food we are essential in keeping inflation low and stable. In the energy sector, we also still need to encourage an increase in primary energy production and reserves, energy mix, expansion of accessibility and efficiency of energy and electricity use, as well as more transparent and targeted management of fuel subdivisions. No less important and also related to food and energy, are our efforts in strengthening national water security combined with the conservation of water resources. 32. Structural reforms are time to be directed at efforts to increase the competitiveness of national industries, including downstreaming, which if left unchecked will tend to be eroded by new economic forces in the region. Coordinated policies are needed in the development of national industries that have an important role in encouraging growth and equity. We need to encourage an increase in the industrial population with a better distribution, especially outside Java, and integrated in the global value chain. Related to the maritime and tourism sectors, we need to continue to strengthen the development of maritime connectivity, increase the promotion of tourism potential, and strengthen institutional and human resource capacity. 33. The development efforts that we continue to make must be supported by the ability of sustainable financing. In this context, we are faced with the challenge of strengthening sources of financing, especially long-term ones. Reformative policies are needed to increase the availability of funds based on long-term financing from domestic and foreign countries, as well as encourage financial market deepening. 34. We certainly agree on the need to create an inclusive economy. Economic policy is not only continuously focused on growth, but must also put forward the aspek of equity. The equity is not only related to the distribution of development results, but also related to efforts to increase and expand public access to financial services. To support this, Bank Indonesia together with the Government and other relevant authorities are committed to continuing to encourage the implementation of the National Financial Inclusion Strategy (SNKI), among others, by disbursing non-cash social assistance. By distributing social assistance in a non-cash manner, in addition to being able to meet the prinsip on time, on quantity and on target, it can also expand and increase access society towards formal financial kites. 35.
