Something probably new in this presentation is electronic money. How is it different from the currently existing money? By definition, Electronic Money Cash Money changed to an electronic form. There are 4 characteristics of electronic money: initial deposit, saved in a particular medium (either cards or communication devices), the main function as a means of payment, and non-deposit making it ineligible for deposit insurance and interest. The currently circulating types of electronic money are presented in slide 28. Electronic money saved in cards is usually issued by banks, while non-cards are usually issued by telco companies. 39. In principle, electronic money is money. Therefore, electronic money can be used for shopping and purchases. However, there is something better than traditional money: electronic money can be used to pay bills, transfer between individuals, or withdraw cash. It is similar to a bank account. There are 2 types of electronic money: unregistered which does not require user data registration, and registered which requires the electronic money holder's identity data to be recorded with an issuer. For registered electronic money, there are 3 advantages, namely maximum balance is Rp 5 million, transfer is permitted, and cash withdrawal is possible. Expansion of financial inclusion: Synergy of Electronic Money and DFS 40. To expand financial access to unbanked and underbanked people in remote areas, Bank Indonesia opens a space for banks and non- banks to provide Digital Financial Services (DFS).For Bank Indonesia, DFS not only serves as a gate to open financial access, but is in line with Non-Cash National Movement since its launch in 2014. Through provision of DFS, efficiency is expected to increase, primarily in retail payment system from the provider and user sides.41. As 12 Public Lecture on the Central Bank - Bank Indonesias Policies on Financial Inclusion through Non-Cash National Movement an embodiment of Bank Indonesias financial inclusion initiative, DFS is an innovation to bring financial access closer to the community in remote areas. Through DFS, payment system and financial services no longer depend on the existence of branch offices of banks. Such service is provided by providers in cooperation with third parties by using mobile and web-based technology devices and facilities. 42. The product used in DFS is server-based electronic money transacted online. Third parties in such services expansion are called DFS in the form of legal entities or individuals. DFS individual agents are companies with no legal personality and individuals. DFS agents function to provide facilities of electronic money registration, top up, payment, cash withdrawal, and distribution of governments aid to the community. 43. For the community, DFS offers various benefits: no need to come to branch offices of banks, save money and time, has a medium to temporarily save money in a safe manner, learn to save and be recognized by banks, and serve as the first step to recognize other financial services. Therefore, the overall transformation process of public culture and paradigm in financial transactions is in line with the road map of financial inclusion and electronification designed by Bank Indonesia. At present, DFS serves at least 5 functions, namely facilitating registration, top up, cash withdrawal, payment of bills, and distribution of governments aids. Islamic Boarding School-Based DFS: Financial Inclusion Development Model 44. Bank Indonesia has also observed Islamic boarding schools as the target of financial inclusion development through DFS. In relation to this, Bank Indonesia and the Ministry of Religious Affairs have signed a 13 Public Lecture on the Central Bank - Bank Indonesias Policies on Financial Inclusion through Non-Cash National Movement Memorandum of Understanding on Development of Economic Independence of Islamic Boarding Schools and Improvement of Non-Cash Services for Financial Transactions in the Ministry of Religious Affairs in Surabaya. Such memorandum signing is one of the series of events of Sharia Economic Festival (ISEF) held from 3 to 9 November 2014 in Surabaya. 45. This Memorandum of Understanding is first implemented in East Java because there are approximately 6,000 Islamic boarding schools there and it is in line with the governments plan to make Surabaya the Center of National Sharia Economic Development. The initial movement in East Java is expected to inspire other areas to accelerate financial inclusion in the community. 46. The cooperation between Bank Indonesia and the Ministry of Religious Affairs is triggered by the huge number of muslim population in Indonesia. Accordingly, the existence of educational institutions becomes more widespread, and the number of Islamic boarding school students also increases. With the huge potential, financial education provided to such students will encourage economic independence, resulting in financial inclusion in the wider community. 47. What is the business model of the Islamic boarding school-based DFS? In this model as shown in slide 35, Islamic boarding schools will act as DFS agents interacting with banks. The users in such DFS are the students and the surrounding community. Islamic boarding schools as DFS will provide financial products and services to users. For example, DFS can provide the needs of the students, such as receiving transfer from their parents, making payment of tuition fees, buying cell phone credit, and purchasing daily necessities in the schools cooperatives/convenience stores. The added value of this model is the presence of third parties, namely experts in Islam, teachers, or heads of 14 Public Lecture on the Central Bank - Bank Indonesias Policies on Financial Inclusion through Non-Cash National Movement Islamic boarding schools who will act as influencers and agents of change in financial education, money saving culture, and establishment of SOP on non-cash tuition fee receipt. 48. Slide 36 presents a pilot project, where Bank Indonesia is now establishing BMT Sidogiri in Pasuruan, East Java. BMT Sidogiris assets in financial year 2013 reached Rp 1 trillion and it is presently the biggest cooperative in East Java. 49. In this model, BMT Sidogiri Cooperative acts as a DFS agent interacting with the electronic money issuer. As a DFS agent, BMT Sidogiri can provide services to pay tuition fees, deposit and withdraw cash, and remit and receive money. The students and the community can also shop in Basmallah convenience store owned by BMT Sidogiri by using electronic money. 50. To conclude my presentation, I emphasize that in addition to the business model, services, and instruments, the most important factor in guaranteeing successful financial inclusion is financial education. Its all about changing the mindset. And such mindset change cannot be done overnight. Therefore, the roles of influencers, such as experts in Islam, community leaders, students like you, and the government as well as the central bank must be synergized and consistently conducted. I do hope this public lecture will not stop here, but it will revolve as a part of sharing the knowledge you have for the communitys economic development. I conclude my presentation to continue to question and answer session. Wassalaamualaikum warahmatullaahi wabarakaatuh 15 Public Lecture on the Central Bank - Bank Indonesias Policies on Financial Inclusion through Non-Cash National Movement

Title: Navigating through Volatility, Agus D.W. Martowardojo, Governor of Bank Indonesia, (as prepared for delivery, Indonesia Fixed Income and High Yield Bond Forum 2015) 22 September 2015, Jakarta, Indonesia
Subtitle: as prepared for delivery, Indonesia Fixed Income and High Yield Bond Forum 2015
text: Navigating through Volatility Agus D.W. Martowardojo Governor of Bank Indonesia (as prepared for delivery, Indonesia Fixed Income and High Yield Bond Forum 2015) 22 September 2015, Jakarta, Indonesia Mr. Sumit Dutta, Chief Executive Officer, HSBC Indonesia Mr. Scenaider C.H. Siahaan, Director for Strategy & Portfolio Financing, Ministry of Finance Republic Indonesia Distinguished participants from both domestic and international institutions, Ladies and gentleman Good morning and a very warm welcome to all of you at this respectful event, 1. First of all, I would like to thank Euromoney Institutional Investor for inviting me to give a keynote address at the 4th Indonesia Fixed Income and High Yield Bonds Forum. 2. It is always a pleasure to gather with you and have this valuable opportunity to talk to investors, about the current Indonesias economic challenges and policy respond. Distinguished Guest, Ladies and Gentlemen 3. Since the outbreak of the financial and economic crisis in 2008, we live in an increasingly uncertain world. In the last few months, global financial markets have suffered repeated shocks, with a number of them due to diverging monetary policies among advanced countries, 1 Greek crisis, a continued fall in commodity prices, and a surprise change to China renminbis exchange rate arrangements. 4. With policy rates close to zero, the Bank of Japan and the ECB continued their respective asset purchase programmes seeking to stimulate economic activity and lift inflation closer to target. At the same time, the US Federal Reserve and the Bank of England continued to prepare market participants for an eventual increase in their policy rates 5. Although the timing of the Federal Reserves first move has become more uncertain, interest rate differentials between the United States and many other countries have remained wide, with important consequences for foreign exchange markets, where the US dollar has been on an appreciating trend since mid-2014 6. Meanwhile, after a brief recovery in the second quarter of 2015, the prices of most commodities continued their plunge, putting additional pressure on commodity producers exchange rates. Perceptions of weaker global demand due to the fall in Chinas investment growth and, in the case of oil, persistently high supply played a key role. 7. As price drops in commodity markets accelerated, investors grew increasingly concerned about growth prospects for Emerging Market Economies more broadly, and the impact on the global economy. 8. On the heels of the Greek crisis, global financial markets were again roiled following a sharp drop in the Chinese equity market and a surprise change to the renminbis exchange rate arrangements. 9. Currencies in the region including Indonesian Rupiah depreciated sharply in response to the weakening of the Chinese currency. In particular, the Malaysian ringgit as a commodity exporter- reacted strongly depreciating by more than 6% since the announcement. 2 10. On 20 August, Kazakhstan, also as a commodity exporter whose main trading partners are Russia and China, announced that it would let its currency trade freely; the Kazakhstan currency immediately lost more than a fifth of its value against the US dollar. 11. Chinas economic slowdown and the US dollars appreciation have confronted Emerging Market with a double challenge: growth prospects have weakened, especially for commodity exporters, and the burden of dollar-denominated debt has risen in local currency terms. 12. Against this backdrop, a number of emerging market economy and commodity-exporting central banks eased monetary policy, including those of China, Hungary, India, Russia and Thailand. 13. In Brazil, where a recession coincided with rising inflation and political tensions, the central bank increased its key policy rate from 12.75% in early March to 14.25%, citing above-target inflation as its primary concern, but signalled a pause in further tightening. Ladies and Gentlemen 14. As a small open economy, Indonesia is certainly not insulated from the several bout of volatility in the global financial market. We might presume that risks of further surges in global financial market volatility remain. 15. Divergence path of the global monetary policy, US dollar super cycle, a slowdown in China and a continued fall in commodity prices, represent key risks to the Indonesian economic stability and outlook. 16. In recent times, several concern in the media stand out in this respect, by comparing 1997/1998 crisis and current market pressure. As far as Im concerned, in the face of an uncertain scenario with very 3 high potential costs, it is far better for us to remain vigilance, but there no any reason to be panic. 17. First, Indonesia is financially more sound today than it was a decade or two ago, when financial fragilities led to currency, banking, and sovereign-debt crises. The restructuring of the nonperforming loans of Indonesia banks that began a decade or so ago, now produced much healthier financial sector balance sheets. 18. These reflected from banks capital adequacy ratio (CAR) much higher than the minimum requirements, relatively high industrial liquidity, relatively low ratio of non-performing loans, sustained profitability, good risk management, and rigorous supervision. 19. Second, Indonesias vastly improved fiscal positions, both debts and deficits, should ensure that Indonesia were able to take a strong policy response, when needed. Under the budget law, the cumulative amount of the budget deficit and the regional budget is limited to maximum of 3% of GDP, while total government debt outstanding is restricted to maximum 60% of GDP. 20. In November 2014, we are applaud the decisive actions have been taken by the current administration to remove most fuel subsidies -to a more targeted system- with a policy to freeing up space in the government budget for more growth-critical infrastructure spending. 21. Third, the adoption of inflation targeting framework (ITF) since 2005 ensure a discipline, transparent, and accountable monetary policy framework. This combined with macro-prudential policy warrant that macroeconomic and financial stability are maintained stable. The key role of ITF framework was evidently reflected from the trajectory of core inflation which have been hovering in the range of 4,5-5,0% in the last six years. 4 22. We believe that credible monetary and fiscal policy framework would continue to underpin investors confidence on the quality of Indonesias macroeconomic policies management. This represented in form of portfolio capital inflows to Indonesia that remain supportive in the last three years. 23. Forth, Indonesia has flexible exchange rates, which leave us less vulnerable to a disruptive collapse of currency pegs, as well as adequate foreign exchange reserves to shield Indonesia against a run on our currencies and bank deposits. 24. In this respect, we remain unwavering to adopt more market-based practices in the domestic foreign exchange and money market, as well as hedging practices and transaction based market pricing. Ladies and Gentlemen, 25. We understand that the fundamental reform I mentioned earlier has made Indonesia currently in a better footing compared to 1997/1998. However, Indonesia remain exposed to vulnerability risk as a group of Emerging Market Economies (EMs) which require policymakers to err on the side of caution. 26. Several elements have been obvious in this respect. First, at the onset of an external shock of this nature, markets respond rather indiscriminately towards emerging market economies as a group, with differentiation following after a relatively short time span. 27. Second, differentiation is made on the basis of the strength of economic fundamentals. In particular, economies with stronger external and fiscal accounts, lower inflation, more international reserves, and sound and deep financial sectors, normally experience more subdued market reactions. This also underlines the importance of building policy buffers during favorable times. 5 28. Third, markets reward timely and credible policy action, as economies that respond to emerging challenges in a flexible way and with appropriate instruments generally fare better. 29. Fourth, even though using the foreign exchange rate as a shock absorber has proved effective in helping emerging economies to better endure a tightening of global financial conditions, intervention in this market may be useful to cope with temporary bouts of volatility in a situation of adequate international reserves and an exchange rate which is not overvalued; However, the effectiveness of intervention tends to disappear when the degree of market uncertainty reaches very high levels. 30. Finally, growth potential is another major element of differentiation during episodes of turbulence; more specifically, the better the prospects for growth the less severe the likely consequences of financial turmoil. Ladies and Gentlemen, 31. Allow me to focus a bit on the recent initiative of Bank Indonesia. First and foremost, I would like to reiterate that Bank Indonesia continues to maintain a tight monetary stance, in order to anchor inflation expectations and manage external pressures in light of current vulnerabilities. As needed, we continue to use macro prudential policies as a balancing role in supporting credit growth while maintaining financial stability. 32. As for exchange rate, we continue the policy to ensure the exchange rate movement along its fundamental value and allow the exchange rate flexibility to play as a shock absorber role in the economy. We do a measured intervention policy in the FX market to 6 smoothing volatility and ensuring orderly market conditions, in line with the existing practice. 33. We will further make improvements in the monetary operations framework, complemented by BIs ongoing financial market deepening efforts, to strengthen the monetary policy transmission mechanism. 34. We recognize some pockets of vulnerabilities exist owing to rising corporate indebtedness and un-hedged foreign currency debt. Although around 70 percent of non-SOE foreign currency debt is estimated to have been incurred by companies with FDI-related funding and/or with FX cash flows, some companies are still subject to FX risk. 35. Hence, to minimize the risks, we have issued a regulation requiring the corporation to maintain some minimum of hedge and liquidity ratio to reduce currency and liquidity mismatch. This policy is not intended to impede the inflow of private foreign debt but to ensure adequate risk management by the business sector. Distinguished Guest, Ladies and Gentlemen 36. Let me close by leaving you with some final thoughts. Indonesia is now challenged by both external and internal risks. These are not necessary unfavorable, as they also come with opportunities to urge us to prepare ourselves collectively to cope with uncertainty in the global economy. 37. In an increasingly volatile world, we must do more. Our efforts should not be just about coping with short-term fluctuations, but also about laying long-term foundation for Indonesias future. That requires a forward-looking plan of action by all stakeholders. Bank Indonesia, for our part, will continue to ensure a stable financial and 7 economic environment, so that businesses can continue to thrive and individuals can enjoy better standards of living on a sustainable basis. Thank you. Agus D.W. Martowardojo Governor of Bank Indonesia 8

Title: Opening Remarks on The International Conference on Economic Modeling (Bali  Indonesia, 16 - 18 July 2014)
text: Opening Remarks The International Conference on Economic Modeling Agus D W Martowardojo Governor of Bank Indonesia Bali - Indonesia, 16 -18 July 2014  Honorable Governor Made Mangku Pastika  Professor Ali Bayar, the President the Global Economic Modeling Network  Dr. Perry Warjiyo, the Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia  Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen Om Swastiastu, Good morning and Welcome to Bali 1. I am delighted to welcome you to this international conference on "Economic Modeling 2014". And, I would like to especially thank our international guests who have travelled a long way to be with us today. For those of you visiting Bali for the first time, I would like to give you a quick look. Bali is a premier tourist destination, sometimes is called the "Island of Gods" and famous for its natural beauty as well as cultural rich and hospitality of its people. 2. In addition, you would see first hand the diversity and religious tolerance in Indonesia. While some of the incoming tourists and locals enjoy the beauty and culture of Bali, others and maybe some of you with moslem background observe fasting during this holy month of Ramadhan. So let me extend our best wishes for you who observe fasting and at the same time I encourage others to enjoy Bali during your free time. 3. Bank Indonesia is most honoured to host and to jointly organise this International Conference with EcoMod Network, the world's leading research, advisory, and Non-Profit Educational Network. 4. This conference will promote the exchange of ideas among economists conducting quantitative analysis, for policy and decision- making in the public and private sector. The conference will cover all areas of applied modeling in economics. I am told that here some 120 papers have been prepared and would be presented in plenary and various parallel sessions. Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, 5. The world economy now appears to be recovering from its worst post-war recession, but only very slowly, and at a different pace across regions and countries. The recovery is driven by stronger outturns in advanced economies as softer fiscal consolidation and relaxed financial conditions should support growth this year. 6. Meanwhile in many emerging markets, in the shadow of the scaling down of ultra-easy monetary policy by the Fed, despite benefited from stronger exports, domestic demand has been weaker than expected, following in part of tighter financial conditions. Emerging economies with relatively high inflation and high current account deficits suffered the most. 7. Capital outflows, higher interest rates, and sharp currency depreciation in emerging economies remain a key concern, and a persistent tightening of financial conditions could undercut investment and growth in some countries given corporate vulnerabilities. Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, 8. Now allow me to move on to the home issue. Over the past five years Indonesia successfully maintain a continuous economic growth on average of 5.9% per year, one of the highest in the world, given that a few countries with a positive and stable growth during 2008-2009's crisis. 9. The vigorous economic progress such as the one I just described earlier has been made achievable on the backdrop of fundamental strengths, which was attributable to a wide-ranging fundamental reforms following the devastating 1997 Asian Crisis, with huge economic, social and political costs. All things considered, Indonesia has sailed through the global financial crisis relatively well, notwithstanding the bumpiness in the ride. Required policy responses have been implemented on a timely basis in most cases, and the underlying fundamentals are still strong. 10. However, given the vigorous economic progress has been observed, it is not all rosy. Since early 2012 commodity prices has shown a declining trend and therefore adversely impacted our exports amidst strong import to meet burgeoning domestic demand. This has resulted in growing current account deficits which in turn deteriorates our balance of payment posture. 11. In responses, we (Bank Indonesia and Government) geared policy mix to put priority on the stabilization over the growth. We increased the policy rate by 175 bps to the level of 7.50%, in stages starting from June 2013. This was an upfront, bold decision to address the macro instability and was taken place when most other emerging markets were not in the contraction mode. 12. Early signs are positive, including a resilient GDP growth rate, improving external sector indicators, controlled inflation rate, rebuilding international reserve as a buffer, as well as acknowledgment by many outside observers and investors on the progress made by Indonesia. That said, we leave no room for complacency, and instead re- emphasize our unwavering commitment to stability Ladies and Gentlemen, 13. While there appears to be reason for optimism, many emerging market economies including Indonesia will have to contend with global environment that continues to be characterized by uncertainty and volatility. Therefore, given the many uncertainties in the global environment that are beyond our control, there is little room to get wrong that which is within our control, such as focused, effective and efficient implementation of reforms and policies that will improve our competitiveness. 14. I would argues that for many emerging market economies, including Indonesia, to raise competitiveness they need to undertake structural transformation. Promote economic growth by making the economy more competitive, increasing total factor productivity and thus potential GDP growth. 15. This takes us down the road of structural reforms, which have huge potential in Indonesia. Whether or not we can seize these potential depends critically on our infrastructure. Please note that I am using a broad definition of infrastructure here, consisting of both hard and soft infrastructure. To make an analogy, I am proposing that we need to build a staircase with four steps: (i) physical infrastructure, (ii) financial infrastructure, (ii) institutional infrastructure, and (iv) human capital infrastructure. Respected ladies and gentlemen, 16. This brings me to the final part of my opening address, what is Bank Indonesia policy focus going forward? Upon assessing the changing global and domestic environment, Bank Indonesia remains resolute in commitment to safeguard economic resiliency and sustainable growth path. 17. We believe that our monetary policy framework will continue to serve us well. And, in implementing monetary policy, Bank Indonesia has been using intensively economic or econometric model in various forms. I am a strong believer that monetary policy should be built on sound research, survey and of course quality data. Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, 18. For the formulation of monetary policy, in the early of 1980, Bank Indonesia employed a Macro-Econometric Model, known as MODBI (Macro-econometric Model of Bank Indonesia). As its name implies, this model adopts econometric approach using annual data. This model is also widely used in determining the direction of monetary policy in the form setting money supply target, in the environment of managed floating exchange rate regime. 19. In light of our experiences, econometric models need to be continuously improved and strengthened in anticipation of unexpected shocks unaccounted in the existing models. 20. With the onset of the 1997 Asian economic crisis, and the passing of the new Central Bank Law No. 23/1999, Bank Indonesia is mandated to achieve its single objective of price stability. The law provided the basis for setting Inflation Targeting as a policy framework, replacing quantity targeting (money targeting). 21. The implementation of ITF was officially declared in July 2005, which raises the need for a new model using quarterly data, that allow central bank to project, simulate and make early response and minimize the adverse impacts of various shocks. 22. In the event, such framework needs further refinements. In the past three and a half years, we have successfully adopted the so called monetary and macro prudential policy mix. This framework includes: firstly, using interest rate as a major policy instrument; secondly, smoothing exchange rate volatilities; thirdly, managing speculative capital flows; fourthly, imposing macro-prudential policy in credit allocation to make it more balanced and supportive for the economy; and lastly promoting and strengthening policy coordination and communication with the government. Ladies and gentlemen, 23. However I would like to caution that sophisticated the model, it cannot fully capture the complexity and dynamics of environment confronting the economy, and the process of economic and monetary transmission. 24. We should not be over confident to our model. Inaccurate model could lead to wrong projections and hence wrong policy and at the end it could lead to disaster. It is still fresh in our mind in 1997-98, when many hailed our economic performances in the preceding years, only to find our economy sliding to economic crisis. So in using the model we should take it with grain and salt. 25. While we admit there are some flaws with our modelling this should not discourage all of us, instead we should improve our model from time to time. And I think it is with the benefit of sharing experiences among modellers like what we do today in this conference that we could learn from each other. I believe that we would be able to deliver fruitful performance to our society out of this conference. So I think we should move forward. Honorable conference Participants, Ladies and Gentlemen 26. In closing, I underscore that academician, market players and practicioners should not work in isolation, rather they should collaborate to build better and prosperous society. We should find the answer for problems around us especially in the area of economics. 27. In conclusion, I am looking forward for the success of this seminar as it will provide opportunity to all of the participants to forward their idea, and learn from each other, to build better world. 28. Thank You and once again I look forward to the successful EcoMod conference. Wassalammu'alaikum WarahmatuHahi Wabarakatuh Om Santi Santi Om Agus D.W. Martowardojo Governor of Bank Indonesia

Title: Paparan Anggota Dewan Gubernur Bank Indonesia, Erwin Rijanto Pada Pengendalian Pembiayaan Properti dan Formulasi Alternatif Mendorong Tumbuhnya Industri Properti, Rakernas REI, 14 September 2017
text: Presentation of Members of the Board of Governors of Bank Indonesia: "Controlling Property Financing and Alternative Formulations Encourage the Growth of the Property Industry" Rei National Meeting, 14 September 2017 Assaiamu'aiaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh, Seiamatsore and greetings to all of us, 1. First of all, let me invite all of us to give thanks to the presence of Allah Almighty, for for the abundance of His favors and gifts, on this day we are still given the opportunity to gather in good health and in a good atmosphere. 2. We welcome the national dialogue activity with the theme "Predicting the Property Industry in the Future and Strengthening the Government's Partiality to the National Property Industry in Facing Economic Turbuience" as part of the REI National Assembly in 2017. Activities like this are expected to further increase our common understanding of developments, challenges and efforts to encourage the development of the property sector in the country. Father and Mother whom I respect, 3. The long journey of 72 years in the realm of independence, has been filled by the Indonesian nation with various transformation efforts through development in all fields, in order to realize the ideals of our predecessors to make the Indonesian state an independent, sovereign, just and prosperous country. 4. On the economic front, Indonesia has risen to become a middle income country, and has the largest middle-class population in Southeast Asia, as well as the fastest growing middle class in Asia. Indonesia is even included in the G-20 group of countries and has the opportunity to develop into a high income country with the 4th economic size praise 7 largest in the world alongside China, India and the United States by 2050 .12 5. The economic journey until the third quarter of 2017 should also be grateful for making a positive performance, both in terms of economic growth, exchange rates, and inflation. These positive records of economic development are not easy things to achieve. 6. Since the beginning of the year, we are faced with a variety of external and domestic challenges that are not light. i. From the external side, we are faced with economic and political policy uncertainties in developed countries, such as the discourse of the decline in the US central bank's balance sheet, the not yet fully recovered chinese economic performance and geopolitical factors on the Korean peninsula. ii. On the domestic side, we see a slowdown in consumption in the household sector and corporate consolidation that is running longer than originally projected. A happy can Hadi, 7. In line with the high uncertainty in the global economy, the recovery that occurred in the global property market was also slow. This is also the case in the domestic property market where the pace of price growth tends to slow down although the latest developments have begun to show little improvement. 8. If we look deeper, the slowdown in the rate of growth of property prices mainly occurs in the large and middle classes which is in line with the phenomenon of "smoothing consumption?' at the class. Meanwhile, the growth rate of modest house prices actually experienced a fairly high increase. Surely this is leaving work homes for us together, are mainly related to the affordability of homeownership prices for low-income communities. 9. The smoothing consumption seems to have an impact on property financing behavior, both from the consumer and developer sides. In this case, the purchase and construction of property using cash and own funds has decreased. This was then followed by an increase in mortgage loans including mortgages for property funding. Happy Ladies and Gentlemen, 10. Observing these conditions, Bank Indonesia pays more attention to the current development of the property sector. Moreover, the property sector has great potential to be the key to the recovery ofthe national economy, given its high muitipiier effect on the economy in general. 11. However, we certainly still need to realize that the characteristics of the property sector are also one of the sources of systemic risk, both through the keuangan channel and the real sector channel. There are many lessons we can learn in the Global Financial Crisis 2008 related to this. 12. This is also in line with the book "rethinking the economics of land and housing' which emphasizes the need for good management of the property sector so as not to become a source of stagnation and productivity puzzles in the economy. . 13. With the strategic role of the property sector in the economy, Bank Indonesia considers the need to balancing between the risk-benefit of the property sector and the property sector, so that later the growth of the property sector can be more continuous. Father and Mother whom I respect, 14. In this regard, and to support the momentum of economic recovery more broadly, including in the property sector, the Bank Indonesia has lowered its policy rate by 175bps since January 2016, followed by additional liquidity to the banking system through a 150bps reduction in reserve requirements since December 2015. 15. We also made LTV adjustments in August 2016 to provide greater incentives for the property sector to grow higher without compromising the principle of banking prudence. We hope that lighter LTV requirements, especially in Sharia mortgages, can be utilized to support the development of the national property sector. 16. The results of the series of policies began to appear with a reduction in interest rates on funds and loans. In June 2017, mortgage growth increased to 7.51%. The increase is still limited but at least it can withstand the slowdown in credit growth. Happy Ladies and Gentlemen, 17. In terms of the follow-up LTV policy, the direction will still be aimed at encouraging a balanced and quality intermediation function. Currently, we are conducting a study on the possibility of implementing spatial-based LTV policies given the very diverse characteristics between regions in Indonesia. 18. In order to strengthen the macroprudential policy formulation process, including LTV, Bank Indonesia is currently developing Big Data as a leading indicator in the property sector; so it is hoped that the macroprudential policy making process in the property sector can be more anticipatory and forward looking. 19. We are also concerned about the low share of property credit to GDP compared to regional countries. For example, Indonesia's position (2.8%) lags far behind Malaysia (37.8%) and Thailand (22.3%). We view this as not fully comparable directly given the high position of unbanked people in the country. We hope that this lag can be pursued through the Financial Inclusion program. 20. Bank Indonesia also certainly pays close attention to various complaints3 in the public regarding the mortgage application process, one of which is also due to the feasibility assessment procedure for prospective debtors carried out by banks. On this good occasion, we convey that the existence of the Debtor Information System which is often called BI-Checking is actually to make it easier for banks to manage credit risk so it is expected that the credit distribution process will also be faster than if the Bank had to admita credit risk assessment from the beginning. Father and Mother whom I respect, 21. Moving forward, Bank Indonesia will continue to strengthen its monetary, macroprudential and payment system policy mix in order to maintain economic and financial system stability. Furthermore, Bank Indonesia will also continue to strengthen coordination with the Government and other authorities to ensure that inflation control, growth stimuli and structural reforms are well underway, thereby supporting quality and sustainable economic growth. 22. We support the Government's measures in the package of economic policies, including in the property sector. As one example of such a form of support is the exclusion of the LTV rule for Government programs. In addition, we see the need for policy synchronization with taxation to reduce the motive for speculation from mortgage transactions. 23. We also carried out coordination together with the OJK to formulate several policy options in responding to the high NIM in the banking system, which in turn burdens the national economy. The audience, 24. With these policies , Indonesia's economic growth in the future is expected to improve, supported by an increase in investment and consumption in line with the continued impact of more government spending expansive as well as the utilization of space for monetary policy easing. Bank Indonesia estimates that overall economic growth in 2017 will remain in the range of 5.0-5.4% and will increase to 5.1-5.5% in 2018. 25. Deposit growth in 2017 is predicted to grow in the range of 9-11%, while credit in the same year grows lower than originally estimated , namely in the range of 8-10%. Bank intermediation is expected to be higher in 2018 with projected credit growth of 10-12% and deposit growth of 9-11%. 26. In line with these projections, the prospects for the property sector are also expected to increase, in accordance with the conducive demand and supply profile in the sector. i. In terms of requestn: Based on the McKinsey Report and the Global Property Guide, it is projected that there will be an increase of around 90 million middle class by 2030. In this case, the expenditure of the middle class on housing reaches 10-15% of income. In between that, investment in the domestic property sector is also quite competitive when compared to the regional. ii. Meanwhile, the supply side is marked by the availability of land bank developers and Infrastructure development programs, such as MRT and road construction that can provide incentives for property area development around the development area. Father and Mother whom I respect, 27. That's all we can say. We hope that this National Dialogue can broaden horizons on developments, challenges and aspects of public policy in the properti sector. Finally, we would like to express our gratitude and appreciation to the 2017 REI National Meeting Committee for organizing the National Dialogue activities today, so that it can be carried out properly. Wassalamu 'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh. Erwin Rijanto Deputy Governor 1 PWC Research(2016) 2 of 7 3 Rumah.com Survey stated that 86% of respondents stated that the cost and process of mortgages in Indonesia are convoluted 5 of 7 --------------- ------------------------------------------------------------
text_original: Paparan Anggota Dewan Gubernur Bank Indonesia : "Pengendalian Pembiayaan Properti dan Formulasi Alternatif Mendorong Tumbuhnya Industri Properti" Rakernas REI, 14 September 2017 Assaiamu'aiaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh, Seiamatsore dan salam sejahtera bagi kita semua, 1. Pertama-tama, ijinkan saya mengajak kita semua untuk memanjatkan puji syukur kehadirat Allah Yang Maha Kuasa, karena atas limpahan nikmat dan karunia-Nya, pada hari ini kita masih diberi kesempatan untuk berkumpul dalam keadaan sehat dan dalam suasana yang baik. 2. Kami menyambut baik adanya kegiatan dialog nasional yang mengangkat tema "Prediksi Industri Properti ke Depan dan Memperkuat Keberpihakan Pemerintah kepada Industri Properti Nasional dalam Menghadapi Turbuiensi Ekonomi" sebagai bagian dalam Rakernas REI pada tahun 2017. Kegiatan seperti ini diharapkan akan semakin meningkatkan pemahaman kita bersama mengenai perkembangan, tantangan dan upaya- upaya untuk mendorong perkembangan sektor properti di tanah air. Bapak dan Ibu yang saya hormati, 3. Perjalanan panjang selama 72 tahun di alam kemerdekaan, telah diisi oleh Bangsa Indonesia dengan berbagai upaya transformasi melalui pembangunan di segala bidang, demi mewujudkan cita-cita para pendahulu kita untuk menjadikan negara Indonesia sebagai negara yang merdeka, berdaulat, adil dan makmur. 4. Di bidang ekonomi, Indonesia telah naik menjadi negara middle income country, dan memiliki penduduk kelas menengah terbesar di Asia Tenggara, serta pertumbuhan kelas menengah tercepat di Asia. Indonesia bahkan masuk dalam kelompok negara G-20 dan berkesempatan untuk berkembang menjadi high income country dengan ukuran ekonomi ke-4 lof 7 terbesar di dunia bersama China, India dan Amerika Serikat pada tahun 20501 2. 5. Perjalanan ekonomi sampai dengan triwulan III tahun 2017 juga patut kita syukuri karena menorehkan kinerja yang positif, baik dari sisi pertumbuhan ekonomi, nilai tukar,maupun inflasi. Berbagai catatan positif perkembangan ekonomi tersebut bukanlah hal yang mudah untuk dicapai. 6. Sejak awal tahun, kita dihadapkan pada berbagai tantangan eksternal dan domestik yang tidak ringan. i. Dari sisi Eksternal, kita dihadapkan pada ketidakpastian kebijakan ekonomi maupun politik di negara-negara maju, seperti wacana penurunan neraca bank sentral AS, belum sepenuhnya pulih kinerja perekonomian Tiongkok dan faktor geopolitik di semenanjung Korea. ii. Di sisi domestik, kami melihat terjadinya perlambatan konsumsi di sektor rumah tangga dan konsolidasi korporasi yang berjalan lebih lama dari prakiraan semula. Hadi tin yang berbahagia, 7. Sejalan dengan tingginya ketidakpastian perekonomian global, recovery yang terjadi pada pasar properti global juga berjalan lambat. Hal ini juga terjadi pada pasar properti domestik dimana laju pertumbuhan harga cenderung melambat meski pada perkembangan terakhir mulai sedikit menunjukan perbaikan. 8. Jika kita bedah lebih dalam, perlambatan laju pertumbuhan harga properti terutama terjadi pada kelas besar dan menengah yang sejalan dengan fenomena "smoothing consumption?' pada kelas tersebut. Sementara itu, laju pertumbuhan harga rumah sederhana justru mengalami kenaikan yang cukup tinggi. Tentunya hal ini meninggalkan pekerjaan rumah bagi kita bersama, terutama terkait dengan keterjangkauan harga kepemilikan rumah bagi masyarakat berpenghasilan rendah. 9. Smoothing consumption tersebut tampaknya berdampak juga pada perilaku pembiayaan properti, baik dari sisi konsumen maupun developer. Dalam hal ini, pembelian dan pembangunan properti dengan menggunakan dana tunai dan dana sendiri mengalami penurunan. Hal tersebut kemudian diikuti oleh kenaikan pinjaman bank termasuk KPR untuk pendanaan properti. Bapak dan Ibu yang berbahagia, 10. Mencermati kondisi tersebut, Bank Indonesia memberi perhatian yang lebih terhadap perkembangan sektor properti saat ini. Terlebih sektor properti berpotensi besar menjadi kunci bagi pemulihan perekonomian nasional, mengingat efek muitipiier-nya yang tinggi terhadap perekonomian secara umum. 11. Namun kita tentunya tetap perlu menyadari bahwa karakteristik sektor properti juga merupakan salah satu sumber risiko sistemik, baik melalui jalur keuangan maupun jalur sektor riil. Banyak pelajaran yang dapat kita petik pada Global Financial Crisis 2008 terkait hal tersebut. 12. Hal ini juga sejalan dengan Buku "rethinking the economics of land and housing' yang menekankan perlunya pengelolaan sektor properti secara baik agar tidak menjadi sumber terjadinya stagnasi dan productivity puzzle dalam perekonomian. 13. Dengan peran strategis sektor properti dalam perekonomian, Bank Indonesia memandang perlunya balancing antara risk-benefit pengem ba ngan sektor properti, agar nantinya pertumbuhan sektor properti dapat lebih berkesinambungan. Bapak dan Ibu yang saya hormati, 14. Berkaitan dengan hal tersebut, dan untuk turut mendukung momentum pemulihan ekonomi secara lebih luas, termasuk di sektor properti, Bank Indonesia telah melakukan penurunan policy rate sebesar 175 bps sejak Januari 2016 yang diikuti dengan penambahan likuiditas ke sistem perbankan melalui penurunan GWM sebesar 150 bps sejak Desember 2015. 15. Kami juga melakukan penyesuaian LTV pada Agustus 2016 untuk memberikan insentif yang lebih besar bagi sektor properti untuk tumbuh lebih tinggi tanpa mengorbankan prinsip kehati-hatian perbankan. Harapan kami, persyaratan LTV yang lebih ringan, khususnya pada KPR syariah, dapat dimanfaatkan untuk mendukung perkembangan sektor properti nasional. 16. Hasil dari rangkaian kebijakan tersebut mulai tampak dengan penurunan suku bunga dana dan kredit. Pada Juni 2017, KPR tumbuh meningkat menjadi 7,51%. Peningkatan tersebut memang masih terbatas namun setidaknya dapat menahan laju perlambatan pertumbuhan kredit. Bapak dan Ibu yang berbahagia, 17. Dari sisi kebijakan lanjutan LTV, arahnya akan tetap ditujukan untuk mendorong fungsi intermediasi yang seimbang dan berkualitas. Saat ini, kami sedang melakukan kajian mengenai kemungkinan penerapan kebijakan LTV berbasis spasial mengingat karakteristik antar daerah di Indonesia yang sangat beragam. 18. Guna memperkuat proses perumusan kebijakan makroprudensial termasuk LTV, Bank Indoensia saat ini sedang mengembangkan Big Data sebagai leading indicator di sektor properti; sehingga diharapkan proses pengambilan kebijakan makroprudensial di sektor properti nantinya dapat lebih antisipatif dan forward looking. 19. Kami juga menaruh perhatian terhadap masih rendahnya porsi kredit properti terhadap PDB dibandingkan dengan negara kawasan. Sebagai contoh, posisi Indonesia (2,8%) jauh tertinggal dibandingkan Malaysia (37,8%) dan Thailand (22,3%). Kami memandang hal tersebut tidak dapat sepenuhnya diperbandingkan secara langsung mengingat masih tingginya posisi unbanked people di Tanah Air. Kami berharap ketertinggalan tersebut dapat terkejar melalui program Financial Inclusion. 20. Bank Indonesia juga tentunya mencermati berbagai keluhan3 di masyarakat mengenai proses pengajuan KPR yang salah satunya juga disebabkan adanya prosedur penilaian kelayakan calon debitur yang dilakukan oleh bank. Dalam kesempatan yang baik ini, kami sampaikan bahwa keberadaan Sistem Informasi Debitur yang sering disebut BI- Checking sejatinya adalah untuk memudahkan bank dalam pengelolaan risiko kredit sehingga diharapkan proses penyaluran kredit juga lebih cepat dibandingkan jika Bank harus melakukan penilaian risiko kredit dari awal. Bapak dan Ibu yang saya hormati, 21. Kedepan, Bank Indonesia akan terus memperkuat bauran kebijakan moneter, makroprudensial, dan sistem pembayaran guna menjaga stabilitas ekonomi dan sistem keuangan. Bank Indonesia juga akan terus memperkuat koordinasi dengan Pemerintah dan otoritas lainnya untuk memastikan pengendalian inflasi, penguatan stimulus pertumbuhan, dan reformasi struktural berjalan dengan baik sehingga mampu menopang pertumbuhan ekonomi yang berkualitas dan berkelanjutan. 22. Kami mendukung langkah-langkah Pemerintah dalam paket kebijakan ekonomi, termasukdi bidang properti. Sebagai salah satu contoh bentuk dukungan tersebut adalah pengecualian aturan LTV untuk program-program Pemerintah. Selain itu, kami memandang perlu adanya sinkronisasi kebijakan dengan perpajakan untuk mengurangi motif spekulasi dari transaksi KPR. 23. Koordinasi juga kami lakukan bersama-sama dengan OJK untuk merumuskan beberapa opsi-opsi kebijakan dalam menjawab masih tingginya NIM di sistem perbankan yang pada gilirannya membebani perekonomian nasional. Hadirin yang berbahagia, 24. Dengan berbagai kebijakan tersebut, pertumbuhan ekonomi Indonesia kedepan diperkirakan akan membaik, ditopang oleh peningkatan investasi dan konsumsi seiring dengan berlanjutnya dampak belanja Pemerintah yang lebih ekspansif serta pemanfaatan ruang pelonggaran kebijakan moneter. Bank Indonesia memperkirakan pertumbuhan ekonomi secara keseluruhan pada tabun 2017 tetap dalam kisaran 5,0- 5,4% dan akan meningkat menjadi 5,1-5,5% pada tabun 2018. 25. Pertumbuhan DPK pada tahun 2017 diperkirakan tumbuh dalam kisaran 9- 11%, sementara kredit di tahun yang sama tumbuh lebih rendah dari perkiraan semula yaitu menjadi dalam kisaran 8-10%. Intermediasi perbankan diperkirakan akan lebih tinggi pada tahun 2018 dengan perkiraan pertumbuhan kredit sebesar 10-12% dan pertumbuhan DPK sebesar 9-11%. 26. Sejalan dengan proyeksi tersebut, prospek sektor properti diyakini juga akan meningkat, sesuai dengan profil permintaan dan penawaran pada sektor tersebut yang cukup kondusif. i. Dari sisi permintaan : Berdasar McKinsey Report dan Global Property Guide, diproyeksikan akan terjadi peningkatan sekitar 90 juta kelas menengah di tahun 2030. Dalam hal ini, pengeluaran kelas menengah untuk perumahan mencapai 10-15% dari pendapatan. Sela in itu, investasi pada sektor properti domestik juga cukup kompetitif jika dibandingkan dengan regional. ii. Sementara, Dari sisi penawaran ditandai oleh masih tersedianya land bank developer dan program pembangunan Infrastruktur, seperti MRT dan pembangunan jalan yang dapat memberikan insentif pengembangan area properti di sekitar area pembangunan. Bapak dan Ibu yang saya hormati, 27. Demikian yang dapat kami sampaikan. Kami berharap Dialog Nasional ini dapat memperluas wawasan mengenai perkembangan, tantangan dan aspek kebijakan publik di sektor properti. Akhir kata, Kami menyampaikan terima kasih dan apresiasi kepada Panitia Rakernas REI 2017 yang telah menyelenggarakan kegiatan Dialog Nasional pada hari ini, sehingga dapat terlaksana dengan baik. Wassalamu 'alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh. Title: Growth and Stability in Challenging Global and Domestic Environment: Key Issues, Policy Mix and Indonesian Experience (Keynote Speech Deputy Governor Perry Warjiyo on Central Bank of Sri Lanka 7th International Research Conference) Colombo, 28 November 20
text: Growth and Stability in Challenging Global and Domestic Environment: Key Issues, Policy Mix and Indonesian Experience Keynote Address by Dr. Perry Warjiyo Deputy Governor, Bank Indonesia Central Bank of Sri Lanka 7th International Research Conference Colombo, 28 November 2014 I. Introduction The theme of this conference is indeed very important and timely. We are living in continuously challenging global and domestic environment. Since the taper tantrum last year, the global economy is seeking a new equilibrium with corresponding high volatile financial market in the process. The spillover impacts to the emerging economy are really unprecedented, through both the trade and financial channels. The key question posed to us especially the policy makers in the emerging economiesis how best we manage the stability while continuously supporting economic growth? The short answer build down into these mantras: make sure your economic fundamentals are sound, implement appropriate and timely policy mix, and deepen your financial market. I will discuss these mantras in more details in the following four parts. First, I will outline the key issues arising from the recent changes in the global economy and their impacts to the emerging markets. Second, I will discuss the three policy mixes that I find them become increasingly important and appropriate responses to ensure the balance between stability and growth in this challenging global and domestic environment. Third, I will share our experience in Indonesia in implementing these policy mixes that have been successful in withstanding through the global turbulences with strong economic performances. And finally, I will close with some small tips on the coordination and communication aspects when come down in formulating and implementing these policy mixes. 1 II. The Challenges: Managing Spillovers and Strengthening Fundamentals There are at least two global spillover effects to the emerging economies that have important implications to the theme of this conference i.e. stability and growth. The first relates to the global economic recovery that is still fragile and uneven. We are witnessing that the US economic recovery continues while China economy is slowing down. The implications of this rebalancing process to the growth pattern as well as stability to the emerging economies have been imminent. With its key role as in global supply hub, China slowdown have negative impacts to primary commodity exporter countries that in the past filling the inputs for manufacturing production of Chinese exports. The impacts have been severely confounded by continued decline of commodity prices. For these economies, the negative impacts have been seen in the slowdown of their economic growth (through decline in exports) and worsening macroeconomic stability (through impairment of current account balance). The US economic recovery, on the other hand, has positive impacts to the emerging economies growth, especially those with exports dominated by manufacturing products. The second challenge emerges from the normalization process of Fed monetary policy. With the US economic recovery to set apace, the Fed finally announced in May 2013 of the tapering of its unconventional monetary easing that has been adopted since the onset of 2008 global crisis. Subsequently, it also becomes clear that the Fed would ultimately start to increase its Fed Fund Rate (FFR) sometime in mid of 2015. Since this taper tantrum, there have heavy pressures of capital reversals out from emerging economies and heightened volatility in the financial markets. The impacts have been visible in the pressures on exchange rate depreciation, increasing yield and risk premium on fixed income securities, as well as equity prices. The pressures have also been perplexed by the lack of clarity of the Fed announcement at the early phase and market over-reaction to it. Confronted with these spillover effects, managing macroeconomic and financial system stability becomes priority for many emerging economies. Surely, the extent to which these spillovers impacts emerging economies depends on their domestic environment. In general, the impacts are more onerous in those countries that face problems in their economic fundamentals, lack of decisive policy responses, and incur some vulnerability in their external and financial sectors. These are often reflected in one or more weak economic and financial indicators such as: high inflation, large current account deficit, unsustainable fiscal deficit, and unsound banking 2 and financial sectors. Openness of the capital account and the depth of financial market of the country are also matter. Quite often, these countries face unfair market punishments by labelling them as vulnerable economies. These discussion lead to the central theme of this conference: how to balance between stability and growth under these unfortunate global and domestic environment? This proves the three mantras that I spoke about at the beginning matters: the problems will be less challenging if we have strong economic fundamental, decisive and appropriate policy responses, supported by sound and deep financial sector. But in real world, often we do not have this luxury. We, in many cases, have to choose between stability and growth. This is particularly true when domestic issues have accentuated the depth of the global spillovers. To make thing more difficult, the timing and magnitude of the spillovers are frequently unpredicted and unprecedented, as we witness in the global financial market following the Feds taper announcement. Under this difficult environment, the priority must be given to the stability, both macroeconomic and financial stability, over supporting growth. When we are already at the corner, never think twice to balance the stability with the growth. Under the current setting of globalized and interconnected world, market will punish us with even greater problem of instability that ultimately would even worsen the growth. The challenge is, of course, how to design and implement policy responses to maintain macroeconomic and financial stability with a minimum negative impact to growth. This will lead us to a number of policy dilemmas in front of us. Let me just outline three of them. The first relates to policies to manage monetary stability --the so-called impossible trinity for a small open economy as we often referred it. That is, how to balance between maintaining exchange rate stability and open capital flows with the independence of setting interest rate for price stability. When we face large and unpredicted capital outflows, as experienced by many emerging countries following the Fed tapering, exchange rate have been under pressures and become more volatile. As a response, we have the choice of increasing interest rate to mitigate the exchange rate pass-through effects to price stability. But relying solely on interest rate would not be effective. The root cause of exchange rate pressures largely come from heightened expectation on US interest rate and risk premium in the global financial market. Moreover, the magnitude of interest rate increase would be excessive that it would large negative impact to growth. Foreign exchange intervention could complement interest 3 response to avert excessive volatility of the exchange rate. Capital flows management could also be used to facilitate the orderly reversals. The second is dilemma between monetary stability and financial stability. Surely, large capital reversals and exchange rate depreciation will tighten domestic liquidity and market risks in the financial system. Thus, excessive interest response for price stability will cause even larger credit risk to the financial sector (and then to overall financial system stability and economic growth). Moreover, in many emerging economies, banking condition may not be homogenous while financial market is often shallow, making interest rate transmission to maintain monetary stability would not always effective while its negative impact to financial system stability would be more imminent. Under such condition, macroprudential instruments (such as reserve requirement, loan to value ratio, capital buffer, etc.) would be more appropriate to support financial stability, complementing interest rate response to maintain price stability. The third dilemma is between maintaining macroeconomic stability and supporting economic growth. The objectives of central bank monetary and macroprudential policy is to achieve price stability and supporting financial stability. It is the government fiscal policy and structural reforms to achieve high, inclusive and sustainable economic growth. Of course, there is a need for coordination of monetary and fiscal policy to manage macroeconomic stability (both in term of price stability and sustainable current account position) from aggregate demand side. Similarly, structural reforms in investment, labor, and productivity are the best policy to achieve economic growth by expanding aggregate supply. But there are many cases that large deficit inhibits fiscal instruments as policy for managing macroeconomic stability and providing stimulus for economic growth. Likewise, structural reforms may also progress slowly that create bottlenecks for supporting growth and at the same time not conducive for macroeconomic stability. III. The Responses: Three Policy Mixes The preceding section leads to a strong argument that in increasing complex world with full of dilemmas, policy makers including us in the central banks must not rely solely on one instrument and fail to coordinate with other agencies. It is the appropriate policy mixes that provide answer to our question on how to balance stability and growth. Some of these mixes have long been known, especially the mix for price stability and exchange rate stability, monetary and fiscal policy, and for macroeconomic stability 4 and structural reforms, while the mix of monetary and macroprudential policy has just recently been implemented. Formulating these mixes is more of an art than a rule. Monetary and macroprudential policy mix The objective of this mix is to make the most possible a number of instruments for achieving price stability and supporting financial stability. For achieving price stability, the inflation targeting framework is widely known as an approach whereas interest rate response (through a Taylor rule type) is set to ensure forecasted inflation in the periods ahead will be fall within the inflation target. A strong assumption underlying this simple rule is that exchange rate flexibility always behave efficiently (i.e. no market rigidity) and provides a smooth adjustment of external shocks to domestic economy (i.e. there is no economic rigidity). As this may not always be the case, foreign exchange intervention could be used to complement the interest response to smooth out excessive exchange rate volatility driven by irrationality in the market. Moreover, capital flow management could be implemented to manage the volatile and speculative shortterm capital flows. This can be done through a number of instruments, e.g. Tobin tax, unremunerated reserve requirement for foreign exchange deposits, and holding period for foreign investors in unwinding their domestic assets. A number of macroprudential tools are available to support financial system stability from both mitigating systemic risk as well as managing pro-cyclicality. To manage market or liquidity risk, for instance, instruments such as reserve requirement, liquidity coverage ratio, open FX position limit, currency mismatch, and FX lending restrictions are common practice. For mitigating leverage on bank deposit/lending, there are instruments such as capital ratio, risk weights, provisioning, loan to value ratio, and credit growth cap. And for mitigating systemic risk from inter-connectedness, capital surcharge and counterparty risk limit could be exercised. In essence, most of microprudential instruments for maintaining individual soundness of the financial institution could be used as macroprudential tools. The key difference is that macroprudential policy for managing overall systemic risk and financial system stability. The next question is how to mix monetary and macroprudential policy to achieve price stability and support financial stability. Note that monetary instruments affect financial system risks (interest and exchange, liquidity, and credit), and vice versa, macroprudential tools directly influence the effectiveness of monetary transmission channels (interest rate, liquidity or money, credit, and risk taking behavior). The 5 challenge is to work through these channels to search optimal balance of these two group instruments. Under inflation targeting framework, this can be done by expanding the policy forecasting and simulation model to encompass financial sector so that some forms of macroprudential tools (e.g. reserve requirement and loan-to-value ratio) could complement the monetary instruments (interest rate and exchange rate) in optimizing the policy response beyond the standard Taylor rule. One important advantage of using macroprudential tools is that they can be targeted to some segments of financial institution or economic sectors, and thus they can fulfill some allocative and distributive role that the monetary instruments (interest rate or exchange rate) are impossible to perform. For example, overall bank lending behavior could be influenced through interest rate policy, and this is one of the channels that monetary policy is directed toward achieving price stability. But lending to some economic sectors may not be elastic to interest rate, such as in property and housing sectors. Under such circumstances, macroprudential tools such as loan-to-value ratio can be designed to complement interest rate in reinforcing the effectiveness of bank lending channel. Thus, with the policy mix, the temptation of over-relying and excessive interest rate response for price stability could be hindered and thus would not put financial stability and economic growth at greater risks. Monetary and fiscal policy mix This policy mix has long been discussed and recommended for managing macroeconomic stability without detrimental impact to economic growth. When a country faces pressures on macroeconomic stability (high inflation and large current account deficit), monetary tightening through rising interest rate could dampen domestic demand and thus contain inflation pressures, and by complementing it with exchange rate depreciation could facilitate current account adjustment. Fiscal policy through deficit reduction is also important to manage domestic demand. Moreover, as in the case of macroprudential policy, fiscal instruments can be designed for allocative and distributive purpose to certain segments of economic growth or groups of population. For example, more fiscal expenditures could be provided to mitigate the negative impact of interest rate increase to agriculture sector and small medium enterprises. More allowances could also be distributed to mitigate the impact of inflation to the poor and near-poor. Likewise, some forms of tax incentives could be 6 given to certain manufacturing sector for export oriented products or to attract more foreign direct investment to these sectors. The more challenging condition is when fiscal deficit is so large due to a number of reasons, including expenditures for political purposes. Under such circumstance, controlling the fiscal deficit will leave little room for stimulus so that both fiscal and monetary tightening for managing macroeconomic stability would incur larger detrimental impact to economic growth. Still, fiscal instruments could be designed to target some segments of population or economic sectors so that the outcome to economic growth would be still better. Some forms of macroprudential tools could complement these fiscal instruments for allocative and distributive purposes. For instance, larger fiscal expenditure and more accommodative loan-to-value ratio could be implemented to support economic growth in the agriculture and SMEs. Macroeconomic policy and structural reforms This policy mix is a more relevant approach to balance stability and growth. Monetary and fiscal policies are directed toward managing aggregate demand while structural reforms are to expand aggregate supply. Mixing the two could deliver stability and at the same time achieve high growth. The reforms may encompass a number of key areas, including investment, infrastructure, labor, industry, as well as trade and services. Technological advantages through education, research and development is important to increase competitiveness. And if this policy mix is complemented by social programs and financial inclusion, the economic development trilogy of stability, high growth, and equality can be achieved for the welfare of the people. But this is easier said than done. Even if structural reforms are progressing well, the impacts to the expansion in the aggregate supply involve long gestation period. This is true for structural reforms in many areas of investment, labor and productivity. In the meantime, aggregate demand may already be too strong in relative to the progress of aggregate supply that necessitates monetary and fiscal response to manage the macroeconomic stability. It would be better if the design of monetary and fiscal policy from the demand side could anticipate and already incorporate the prospective impacts of structural reforms to the aggregate supply in one policy cycle ahead. This leads to the important of understanding the economic cycle from both demand as well as supply side, and how it is influenced by policies in monetary, fiscal and structural reforms. 7 Likewise, understanding the behavior of financial sector is equally important. We know that financial sector acts as accelerator in the economy. That is, financial activities would usually more bullish during the economic boom and, vice versa, more bearish during the economic downturn. This happens due to a number of reasons: wealth effect, risk premium, leveraging, asymmetric information, or moral hazard. During the economic boom, for instance, the wealth will rise and improve the creditworthiness in assessing bank lending. Better economic prospect will also ease the banks to extend their lending. The spiraling up effect of wealth effect, bank lending, and economic prospect would accelerate the boom and creating the bubbles in the economy. The opposite condition happens during the economic recession. Thus, understanding financial cycle and how this relates to the economic cycle is important in formulating the timing, magnitude, and optimality of the three policy mixes. IV. The Case: Indonesia Indonesia is weathering well the spillovers from the Fed normalization process. In fact, market confidence has resumed since September last year and there has been large portfolio inflows amounting to about USD 17 billion in 2014, stimulating equity prices to rebound, lower bond yield, and stabilize exchange. This is evidence that strengthening domestic economic fundamentals, decisive policy responses, and financial deepening prove to be effective for maintaining the macroeconomic and financial stability with minimum impact to growth. The aggressive and bold measures of policy mixes that Bank Indonesia in close coordination with the Government undertake since June 2013 have resulted in streams of positive news of benign inflation, faster than expected decline in current account deficit, and better than expected GDP growth to the markets. The current condition is far different than those at the onset of Fed tapering announcement in May 2013. At that time, there was huge capital reversals amounting to about USD 5 billion in one single month, creating panic in both foreign exchange and government bond markets, causing heavy pressures on exchange rate, bond yield and equity prices, and thus threatening both monetary and financial stability. The problem was aggravated by domestic economic problems of widening current account deficit (peaking at 4.4% of GDP in Q2-2013) due to the decline of primary commodity exports against the strong domestic demand. Inflation also increased to 8.6% in July 2013 due to the 40% hike of subsidized fuel price as the government by law needs to reduce 8 subsidy to secure a maximum of 2.5% of GDP fiscal deficit. Bank lending was also high at 23.5% in May 2013 supported by ample liquidity in the economy. Confronted with these complex challenges, Bank Indonesia in close coordination with the Government took decisive decision to put stability as the highest priority over stimulating growth. First, Bank Indonesia took a decisive monetary and macroprudential policy mix to control inflation as well as to facilitate adjustments in the current account deficit and bank lending. Second, monetary and fiscal policy mix is closely coordinated especially to manage domestic demand so that consistent with the needs to control inflation and current account deficit. The Government raised fuel price by 44% in June 2013 and another 31% in November 2014 while now is preparing the plan to move fuel price to be market determined. These fiscal policy are not only important for managing domestic demand in the short-term, but also free up substantial expenditures for more productive purposes and thus stimulating economic growth. And third, structural reforms in the real sectors such as in infrastructure, investment, and manufacturing as well as financial market deepening are also priority for securing a strong, balanced and sustainable growth over the medium-term. Let me discuss in more details Bank Indonesia monetary and macroprudential policy mix. It basically consists of the following four key instruments: interest rate response complemented by some exchange rate flexibility, capital flow management, and macroprudential measures. Clear communication, policy coordination with the government on inflation, fiscal and structural reforms, as well as central bank cooperation on strengthening regional financial arrangements also play crucial role. The interest rate policy, as in other inflation targeting countries, is the main instrument to anchor inflation expectation and forecast going forward to fall within the targeted range. Exchange rate policy is geared toward maintaining the stability along its fundamental path. Some forms of capital flows management are implemented to dampen its short-term excessive volatility. Macroprudential measures are targeted to manage procyclicality and excessive lending in some specific sectors. Overall, the policy mix is intended to reinforce the effectiveness of all monetary transmission channels (interest rate, exchange rate, money and lending, asset prices, as well as expectation channels) to manage monetary and financial stability to better withstand the spillover impacts of global factors. 9 In real practice, managing the trade-off between monetary and financial stability is a challenge. The general principle is that when we are facing pressures on inflation beyond the target (and large current account deficit) at time when bank lending growth is high (and financial activities are booming), the appropriate mix is to tighten both monetary and macroprudential policy stance, and vice versa. The challenge is when the pressures on inflation still persist but lending growth is already low and restrained. This is when monetary policy tightening is still consistent for managing monetary stability, but it needs to be complemented by a more accommodative macroprudential policy to avert the unintended consequences to the financial system stability. The two episodes of Indonesia experience since the taper tantrum provide a clear example. The first episode is from May 2013 to October 2014 when we tighten both monetary and macroprudential policy to control inflation following the 44% fuel price increase in June 2013, contain relatively high current account deficit due to the decline in commodity exports and large import related to strong domestic demand, and manage excessive bank lending and housing bubbles driven by economic buoyant. The second episode starts in November 2014 when we just formulate our policy mix to respond to the latest Government decision to raise 31% fuel price increase when at the same time bank lending and GDP growth reached at the lowest 13% and 5.1%, respectively. We are in full support the Government decision and now in close coordination to ensure the inflation will be under control and temporary, while in the medium-term will support a more higher and sustainable economic growth. Accordingly, while tight bias monetary policy is continued, we have started to adopt a more accommodative macroprudential policy. Interest rate policy We raise our policy rates decisively and aggressively to ensure that inflation continues under control to contain the short-term impact of 44% fuel price increase in June 2013. Indonesia is among the first central bank that ahead of the curve raised its policy rate in the aftermath of Fed announcement on planned tapering in May 2013. We started to raise the BI policy rate by 25 bps in June 2013. We then aggressively raised the policy rate by 50 bps in July, another 50 bps in August, and 25 bps in September 2013. After pausing in October, we raised again the policy rate by 25 bps in November 2013. In total, the policy rate was increased by 175 bps to 7.50% within six months. We hold the policy rate since then until recently when we raise our policy rate by another 25 10 bps to 7.75% in November 18, 2014 to anchor inflation expectation following the latest 31% fuel price increase. We maintain our tight bias monetary policy stance. The primary objective of this aggressive interest rate policy is to preemptively anchor inflation to fall within our target ranges of 4.5%1% in 2014 and 4.0%1% in 2015-2017. Inflation expectation initially arose from food price shocks and subsequently driven by the impact of fuel price hike, causing the CPI inflation to reach its peak at 8.6% in July 2013. The large increase in policy rate is also to slow down the domestic demand at the back of declining exports so as to dampen the current account deficit that peaks at 4.4% of GDP in Q2-2013. The timing of the aggressive increases in policy rate is important as they help in mitigating the capital reversals and increasing global interest rate and risks following the Fed tapering announcement. We believe bold and aggressive response in interest rate is a key to send a strong and clear signal to the market in our monetary policy deliberation. The bold response in interest rate has succeeded in containing the inflation pressures and helped in reducing current account deficit faster than initially forecasted. The CPI inflation returned to its normal path since September and downed to 8.3% in December 2013, much lower than our earlier forecast of 9.0%-9.8%. The inflation decelerated further to 4.8% in October 2014, but it is forecasted to be at 7.7%-8.1% at the end of 2014 following the recent fuel price increase. Trade balance turns into surplus and current account deficit is falling from 4.4% of GDP in Q2-2013 to 3.3% of GDP for the overall 2013 and estimated at 3.1% of GDP in 2014. We are aiming to lower the current account deficit to below 3.0% of GDP in 2015 and trending down to 2.5% of GDP over the next three years. We believe this level of current account deficit is more sustainable in the longer term for Indonesia. Overall, macroeconomic stability has resumed and can be achieved with manageable moderation in economic growth. GDP growth recorded at 5.8% in 2013 and it is forecasted to moderate to 5.1%-5.5% in 2014 following the stabilization policies, but it is projected to rebound to 5.4%-5.8% in 2015 with improving external demand and accelerated investments.
