Exchange rate policy Even though increases in policy rate have succeeded in anchoring inflation expectation and helped in slowing down domestic demand, it could not be left alone to play all the burdens of economic adjustments, including in further reducing current account deficit and mitigating the spillover effects from the Fed normalization process. 11 It would need excessive increases in policy interest rate to do all the adjustments. Some room for exchange rate flexibility helps in facilitating the reduction of current account deficit and the transmission of global monetary normalization. For Indonesia, exchange rate policy is geared toward maintaining the stability of exchange rate movements that is consistent with its fundamental path. The path is calibrated through some methodology of determining the fundamental exchange rate and then inputted to be consistent with macroeconomic forecasting and simulation when determining the policy interest rate. Real Effective Exchange Rate (REER) is one approach to check the consistency of exchange rate movements to the fundamental. To achieve this objective, symmetric intervention in the foreign exchange market is conducted to smooth out the short-term volatility of day to day exchange rate movements in the market with the path that is consistent with the fundamental equilibrium exercises. The objective is not to target a certain level or range of exchange rates, but merely to avoid too excessive volatility that may give rise to panics and disruptions in the smooth functioning of foreign exchange market. Capital flow management Volatile capital flows, especially those of short-term and speculative natures, increase the risks of instability to both monetary and financial system stability. The carry trade flows often give rise to excessive volatility in the exchange rate movements beyond implied by fundamentals. Dual intervention in both foreign exchange and capital market is one of strategy to smooth out volatility. But in many cases, measures of capital flows management are needed. For Indonesia, the policy on capital flows management is guided with three principles. First, the objective is to help mitigate the negative impacts of short-term volatility in capital flows to instability in exchange rate as well as overall monetary and financial system. Second, they are targeted to short-term and speculative capital flows since we welcome those flows that are of medium-longer term that benefits the economy. And third, the measures are consistent with our broad principle of maintaining free foreign exchange system. They are temporary, i.e. the measures are strengthened when too much capital inflows and relaxed when too much capital outflows, and do not differentiated to both domestic and international investors. 12 The followings provide clear examples. During heavy capital inflows from the Fed quantitative easing since the global crisis, we introduced six month holding period in 2010 for transactions in the central bank bills and imposed a maximum of 30% capital to the short-term off-shore borrowings of the banks. But following the Fed announcement of planned tapering in 2013 we relaxed the holding period for central bank bills to one month and expanded a number of transactions that are excluded from the calculation on off-shore borrowing of the banks. We view that these measures help in dampening the short-term and volatile capital flows, and thus are consistent with the objective of managing financial stability. Assessing macroprudential policy As underlined before, the interest rate transmission mechanism of monetary policy is not always smooth and fully effective in a country where financial market is not yet developed such as Indonesia. Other channels of monetary transmissions must be deployed, including the lending channel. This is where macroprudential measures play key role, including in smoothing out the procyclicality nature of bank lending behavior. Thus, both the objectives of maintaining monetary and financial system stability are taken into account when we design macroprudential measures. In Indonesia, the formulation of macroprudential measures is done as follows. We develop some methodologies to assess some sort of optimal lending growth of the banks, including what we call non-accelerating inflation lending growth model. We apply the model to aggregate lending growth as well as lending growth to each bank, certain types of lending (consumption, working capital, and investment) and per economic sectors. By comparing these optimal vs. actual lending growth, we have some ideas where excessive lending occurs and thus some instruments of macroprudential measures are justified and can be applied. This is the approach that we applied when introducing loan-to-value (LTV) ratio to lending to automotive and property sectors in 2012. We then strengthened the LTV ratio to lending to property sectors in 2013, especially to mortgages for the second, third, and so on purchases of certain types of housing and apartments. The measures are also complemented by supervisory actions to banks that we viewed exhibit excessive lending behavior. Our experience shows that these measures help in reinforcing the effectiveness of monetary transmission mechanism and supporting the financial system stability. Bank lending growths for mortgage on housing and apartments have declined 13 substantially in relatively short-period and help in mitigating the risks of property price bubbles. In addition, the automotive and property sectors contain substantially large import content, and thus managing lending growths to these two sectors help in reducing the current account deficit. Financial market deepening The stage and depth of domestic financial market influence the transmission mechanism and policy response to global monetary factors, in both the Fed easing period as well as the normalization process. Preceding discussions clearly show the challenges that we face in Indonesia. Interest rate transmission is lagging in the absence of domestic money and fixed income markets that provide efficient mechanism interest rate and term-structure determination. The shallowness of domestic foreign exchange market often causes excessive volatility and overshooting of exchange rate movements in responding to global monetary and financial shocks. This is the rationale for our focus and priority on financial market deepening, as an integral part of our policy responses to the Fed normalization process. In addition to strengthening the economic fundamentals, sound macroeconomic and financial system stability, the best defense for withstanding the spillover effects of such global monetary and financial factors is to make our financial market more conducive and resilience to swings in the international investors preferences. We embark on a series of policy initiatives to deepen our financial market, especially domestic money and foreign exchange markets, by establishing market mechanisms for interest and exchange rate determination, more financial products such as FX swap and interbank repo, as well as introducing best practices of market conducts. V. Final Remarks Managing stability and growth in current challenging global and domestic environment is not always straightforward. We face a number of dilemmas beyond the well-known macroeconomic stability and high economic growth to encompass the trade-off between price stability and exchange rate stability in one hand and with financial system stability in the other hand. Relying solely to one instrument on interest rate will be erroneous and onerous. Thus, we need to design three policy mixes: monetary-macroprudential, monetary-fiscal, and macroeconomic-structural reforms. Our experience in Indonesia shows that this approach provides better outcomes. 14 Formulating and implementing these policy mixes require comprehensive knowledge on our economy supported by rigorous methodology as well as strong determination. Understanding the behavior of economic cycle from both demand and supply side, as well as how it interacts with different behavior of financial cycle is also important. It is a challenge for policy makers to deliver appropriate response to achieve stability and growth, and for academician to develop theoretical and empirical that underpins them. Policy coordination is another challenge, particularly in countries where the authorities of the policies rest on a number of agencies. In Indonesia, we have close policy coordination between the central bank and the government both at the central and local levels in a number of areas, including in inflation control, fiscal and monetary policies, as well as in gauging structural reform agendas. Coordination between the central banks macroprudential policy with individual financial institution microprudential and supervision by Financial Sector Agency (FSA) is also conducted. At the national level, Financial System Stability Coordination Forum (FKSSK) has been established to conduct policy coordination for overall financial system stability. Finally, clear communication is important as well. We need to be clear on what our policy objective and policy responses, as well as the instruments to achieve the objectives. This is easier said than done. For instance, when communicating monetary and macroprudential policy mix, we need to deliver clear signal that interest rate response is always for price stability, while macroprudential policy is for financial system stability. They are in many cases complemented, but certainly they could not be perceived as substitutes. In addition, if there is conflict between the two, it is important to signal that price stability should be the ultimate objective for monetary policy. Colombo, 28 November 2014 15

Title: "SEACEN High Level Seminar on Integrating Monetary Policies with Macroprudential Framework" Opening Remarks by Dr. Perry Warjiyo Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia (Bali, November 7th 2013)
text: SEACEN High Level Seminar on Integrating Monetary Policies with Macroprudential Framework  Opening Remarks by Dr. Perry Warjiyo Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Bali, November7th 2013 Distinguished Speakers, Participants, Ladies and Gentlement. 1. Good morning. Let me start by welcoming all of you to SEACEN High Level Seminar on Integrating Monetary Policies with Macroprudential Framework, at this beautiful island Bali. I am very delighted to provide opening remarks to this seminar today. The topic of the seminar is both timely and essential. Global crisis gave us a valuable lesson that fostering financial system stability plays a key role beyond price stability as the mandate of the central bank. Macroprudential policy becomes an increasingly important new policy tool kit of the central bank to complement the already established monetary policy and microprudential supervision. Yet, we still need to rethink and design the current framework for monetary policy to include macroprudential in order to achieve both price stability as well as financial stability. 2. I will speak these issues along with the following two broad aspects. First, I will discuss the changing nature of central bank challenges since the global crisis and why we need to complement and integrate the current monetary policy with macroprudential policy.Then, I will share the experience of Indonesia in formulating and implementing monetary and macroprudential policy mix in facing the unprecedented challenges for maintaining price and financial system stability since the global crisis. Ladies and Gentlement, 3. Global crisis taught us a number of lessons and brought up new challenges to the central bank. First, there is a need to expand the mandate of central bank from price stability to encompass also a role in promoting financial system stability. The success of sound monetary policy in delivering low inflation and then low interest rate in the period preceeding global crisis was construed as giving rise to the boom and risks in the financial sector that lead to the global crisis. Certainly, strengthening regulation and supervision in the financial sector, both in the micro aspect to mitigate individual risk as well as in the 1 macro aspect to manage systemic risk, are needed to secure financial system stability. But it is clearly that monetary policy to achieve price stability need to be closely coordinated with macroprudential policy to foster financial system stability. 4. Second, we also need to put stability objective, whether it relates to price or financial system stability, into a new prospective. We need to think of stability not in static sense, i.e. year by year, but in a more dynamic and forward looking sense. This is especially true since financial activities exhibit procyclicality along with the boom and bursts in the economic cycle. Bank lending, for instance, tends to be more excessive in the boom period but restrictive when the economy slumps. Interest rate policy alone would not be effective to address this financial acceleration fenomenon in the economy. Macroprudential policy for securing financial system stability must also able to manage these procyclicality nature and allocative distribution of bank lending among sectors so as to help manage (and not accentuate) the boom and bursts cycle in the economy. Likewise, apart from investors' preference in the global financial market, capital inflows are usually high when our economy is on the rise but they will reverse when risks in the economy emerge. Some forms of capital flow management are needed to complement exchange rate policy to maintain external stability from the impacts of the volatility of capital flows. 5. Third, market mechanism does not always work efficiently in developing countries like South-East Asia. The invisible hand of Adam Smith may not always be prevailed. Inflation, for example, may be caused by non-monetary factors such as production, distribution, or market structure, and thus would not be effectively responded by interest rate alone. Likewise, financial imperfections often inhibit rigidities of interest rate and exchange rate in transmitting monetary policy to the economy. Interest rate response to monetary policy tends to be with a long lag and bank's lending tends to be less elastic to interest rate setting. Exchange rate overshooting often happen because of price rigidity in the real sector and under developed financial market. Under such circumstances, we could not only rely on standard monetary or banking policy for achieving price and financial system stability. In a number of cases, some forms of intervention policy may be needed when market failure exists. 6. The preceeding discussion leads to the need for formulating a monetary and macroprudential policy mix to achieve price and financial system stability to promote sustainable economic growth. Monetary policy to achieve price stability must also take into account non-monetary factors of inflation and the impact of financial imperfections to monetary transmission mechanism. Likewise, macroprudential policy needs to balance the objective of maintaining financial system stability with the promotion of a sustainable intermediation function and efficiency of the financial sectors for stimulating the economic 2 growth. The question is then how to formulate and integrate monetary and macroprudential policy mix. Ladies and Gentlement, 7. Let me share with you Indonesia experience in this regard. Indonesia, as a small open economy, faces a number of challenges over the past years. First, capital inflows were substantively large over the period of 2009 to 2011 from the quantitive easing of monetary policy in the advanced counties, but then they reverse because of Greek crisis in the end of 2011 and recent market over reaction to the planned tapering of Fed quantitative easing. Second, inflation was under controlled and relatively low up to 2012 but it has been under pressures since then because of increased of domestic fuel price and supply shocks on food prices. Third, current account was in relatively large surplus up to 2011 induced by strong external demand and high global commodity price, but it then turn into large deficit when the global economic condition reverse. These three challenges depict a more complex environment faced by Bank Indonesia to formulate and implement its policies to maintain price and financial system stability to promote economic growth. 8. Faced with these more complex problems, Bank Indonesia no longer just rely on one instrument, particularly, the interest rate policy. Since mid of 2010, Bank Indonesia has adopted a new approach of monetary and macroprudential policy mix, implemented through the following five instruments. 9. First, the policy interest rate is always the main instrument of monetary policy, directed to anchor future inflation to remain under controlled within the target range. Thus, when inflation declined and relatively low during 2010-2012, policy interest rate was lower 100 basis point from 6.75% to 5.75%. But the recent increased inflation pressures, coupled with relatively high current account deficit occurring when pressures on capital reversals are mounting in respond to Fed's planned tapering, the policy rate has been increased 150 basis point to 7.25%. We will continue monitor the pressures on inflation and current account deficit and readjust our policy repond to ensure price and external stability are maintained. 10. Second, Bank Indonesia continues to maintain exchange rate stability in accordance with economic fundamentals. Thus, maintaining the path and stability of exchange rate is an integral part of the efforts to achieve the inflation target based on the forward looking macroeconomic projection exercise. Thus, when inflation was low, current account was in surplus and capital inflows were large in ghe period of 2009-2011, we let exchange rate to appreciate from about Rp12.000 per USD when the global crisis erupted in 2008 to about 3 Rp9.700 per USD in 2010 and even to Rp8.500 per USD in the mid of 2011. The Rupiah was under strains because of global financial market pressures emanated from the European crisis in the end of 2011 and recent Fed's planned tapering. Rupiah is now stabilizing at around Rp11.400 per USD and we view this consistent with the economic fundamental. 11. Third, Bank Indonesia has pursued a number of measures to manage capital flows so as not to induce extreme volatility in the exchange rate and endanger the risks to financial stability. We welcome those capital flows that are long-term and benefits to financing the economy, especially FDI and to some extent portfolio inflows to government bond and equity. We targeted the measures to "put sand in the wheel" those capital inflows that are short-term and speculative. Thus, we introduced 1 month and then lengthend to 6 monthholding-period for Bank Indonesia Certificates (SBI) in 2010-2011 as we regarded capital inflows were excessive during that time, but it was shortened to 1 month recently as a part of policy mix to withstand from the impact of Fed's planned tapering. We also introduced maximum of 30% capital to the short-term offshore borrowing of the banks in 2011, but it was relaxed recently with exluding divestment of equity portfolio flows and capital participation from parent companies. We also continue to deepen domestic financial market with introducing a number of new products such as negotiable securities and hedging instruments. 12. Fourth, Bank Indonesia also introduced a number of macroprudential policies to manage ovesll lending and the allocation of bank credit to various sectors to be more balanced and support the economy. The measures are also geared toward dampening the procyclicality nature of bank lending in the economy. In the past, we rely very much the instruments for managing liquidity and lending of the banks through a number of reserve requirements. We strengthened our macroprudential policies last year with introduction of Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio on lending to automotive and property sectors. Recentley, we amended the LTV regulation due to excessive credit growth in the property sector, particularly for houses and high-rises (flats and apartments). On the other hand, accommodative macroprudential measures are deployed to stimulate lending to a number of sectors which are supporting sustainable and equitable economic growth. For example, Bank Indonesia has issued a policy requiring lending to MSMEs by each bank a minimum of 20% of their total lending within the next five year. 13. Fifth, Bank Indonesia continues to strengthen policy coordination with the Government at central and local levels to manage inflalion, macroeconomic and financial system stability for promoting economic growth. To curb inflation pressures especially from volatile foods prices because of production, distribution and market structure, we established Inflation Control Team (ICT) at the national, as well as in all of the 33 provinces and 76 4 cities/counties. Coordination on monetary - fiscal - and structural policies are conducted through Bank Indonesia involvement in the government budget process as well as regular coordination meering between Bank Indonesia, Ministry of Finance, and other related line ministries. For maintaining financial system stability, a forum called Financial System Stability Coordination Forum (FKSSK) involving Ministry of Finance, Bank Indonesia, Financial Service Authority (FSA), and Indonesian Deposit Insurance Company (IDIC) has been formed and meet regularly to discuss overall financial system condition and coordinated policy responses that are needed. 14. Our experience over the past three years shows that this new framework has been more effective in maintaining price and financial system stability for promoting exonomic growth. The policy mix, however, is not always easy to design and implement, and it needs to be appropriately and continuously calibrated according to the evolving dynamics of the global and domestic economic environment. Communicating the policy mix is also a challenge. We need to be clear which instrument is directed to which specific objective, and we must avoid substituting the interest rate policy for other instruments in the mix. Even when we are successful in these aims, there is always a risk that the market may perceive the policy mix differently, given that the monetary policy response is generally (and often only) associated with interest rate adjustments. Ladies and Gentlement, 15. In closing, once again, I am delighted to give opening remarks to this important seminar today. I am particularly hopeful that the next two-day seminar will provide ample opportunities for all of us to enrich our understanding and able to give inputs to improve the integration of monetary policies and macroprudential framework for policy making in our respective central bank. We appreciate it very much to the SEACEN Centre for organizing this Seminar and commend this important topic will be further enriched and deepened in the future. With that, I declare this seminar officially opened. Thank You. 5

Title: Macroeconomic Policy Mix for Promoting Sustainable and Inclusive Growth (Keynote Speech by Dr. Perry Warjiyo Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia at the ESCAP High Level Policy Dialogue and Eleventh Bank Indonesia Annual International Seminar) Yogyakarta, Ma
text: Macroeconomic Policy Mix for Promoting Sustainable and Inclusive Growth Keynote Speech by Dr. Perry Warjiyo Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia At the ESCAP High Level Policy Dialogue and Eleventh Bank Indonesia Annual International Seminar Yogyakarta, May 15th 2013 Introduction 1. Let me start by welcoming all of you to this high level policy dialogue, jointly organized by the ESCAP, Bank Indonesia, and the Ministry of Finance, at this cultural city of Yogyakarta. I am very delighted to be here at least for two reasons. First, this is my hometown and I used to live here when I took my bachelor degree at Gadjah Mada University. I know very well that promoting sustainable and equitable growth has been and always be the philosophy of teaching in this university, including in economics. 2. Second, the topic of the seminar is timely and provoking. We need to rethink and find a new approach of macroenomic policies for promoting sustainable and equitable growth in East Asia. Looking at what happen over the past decade, I have a strong believe that the rise of Asia will be here to stay and leap forward as the engine of global economic growth. What we need is to make sure that the high economic growth will be sustainable and inclusive to benefit to all the people. East Asia Economic Challenges 3. But we need to be aware that the challenges of East Asia economy to continue to leap forward are many and a number of them are complex. First, the global economic recovery seems to be protracted, giving rise to downward pressures on world trade volume and commodity prices (excluding oil price). We could not rely only on export promotion to sustain our economic growth. We need to boost our domestic demand, be it consumption and investment, to compensate the declining exports as our engine of growth. 4. Second, global excess liquidity will continue to linger with all of its positive and negative ramifications. Capital flows will continue to pour in to our region. But not all of them are good for our economy, especially those of short-term and speculative capital flows. We need to limit this type of capital flows while continue attracting those capital flows that are longer-term and benefit to our economic development, such as FDI and longer-term portfolio investment and offshore borrowings. 1 5. Third, we need to continue to develop infrastructure and technology to expand our domestic production capacity and competitiveness. Most of Asia economies are experiencing demographic bonus, with increasing middle income group demanding carious goods and services. Without increasing our domestic production capacity and competitiveness, our region will only be a target of market for other region goods and services. Moreover, our economy will easily be trapped into overheating and short-lived economic cycle, which ultimately limits our capability to sustain economic growth. 6. Fourth, we also need to work harder to tackle the problem of poverty. Even though East Asia is experiencing high economic growth, many people are still living below poverty line, including in my own country Indonesia. The trickle down effects of high economic growth are slow progressing in this region. We need to spend more on education, health, and other social welfare programs to address this problem of inclusive economic development. The Tale of Two Fallacies 7. These complex economic challenges need a new approach of macroeconomic policy making which well integrated and coordinated for securing stability and at the same time promoting sustainable and equitable growth in Asia. But I must confess that the conventional thinking and practice of macroeconomic policies may not always be suitable to our region. Let me cite just the following two fallacies. 8. First, market mechanism does not always work efficiently in developing countries like East Asia. The invisible hand of Adam Smith may not always be prevailed. Thus, financing public expenditures through bond issuance would not always the same with by increasing taxes as the Ricardian equivalence predicted. Inflation may be caused by non-monetary factors such as production, distribution, or market structure, and thus would not be effectively be responded by increasing interest rate. Likewise, financial imperfections often inhibit the flexibility of interest rate and exchange rate in transmitting monetary policy to the economy. Under such circumstances, we could not only rely on standard fiscal, monetary or banking policy for a stable, sustainable and equitable growth. In a number of cases, some forms of intervention policy may be needed when market failure exists. 9. Second, we also need to put stability-growth-equity nexus as objectives of macroeconomic policies into a new prospective. We need to think of stability and growth nexus not in static sense, i.e. year by year, but in a more dynamic and forward looking sense. We need to put this issue along with the need to extend our economic cycle, or we risk that maintaining the stability could have detrimental effects to growth. Thus, we need to address fiscal and debt sustainability not merely by limiting fiscal deficit, but also taking into account how boom and burst cycle in our economy would influence our capacity to raise taxes, increase public 2 expenditure, and issue government bond and borrowings. We need to design a countercyclical fiscal policy to balance stability with growth. Likewise, in the financial sector, bank lending often exhibit procyclicality along with the boom and bursts in the economic cycle. Macroprudential policy for securing financial system stability must also able to manage these procyclicality nature and allocative distribution of bank lending among sectors so as to help manage (and not accelerate) the boom and bursts cycle in the economy. The Need for Macroeconomic Policies Mix 10. The preceding discussions lead to the need for formulating macroeconomic policy mix to balance the stability with sustainable and equitable economic growth. Fiscal policy need not be geared only toward maintaining fiscal and debt sustainability, but also find a way to act as a counter cyclical policy to sustain the economic growth. Monetary policy to achieve price stability must also take into account non-monetary factors of inflation and the impact of financial imperfections to monetary transmission mechanism. Likewise, macroprudential policy needs to balance the objective of maintaining financial system stability with the promotion of a sustainable intermediation function and efficiency of the financial sectors for stimulating the economic growth. 11. The question is then how to formulate and coordinate fiscal-monetary policymacroprudential policy mix in this new approach of macroeconomic policy making. Let me share with you our experience in Indonesia. On national level, we have a close coordination between fiscal policy of Ministry of Finance with monetary policy of Bank Indonesia. In formulating government budget, for example, the central bank provides its views to the parliament on macroeconomic projections and its monetary policy direction. For Indonesia, the issue in fiscal and monetary policy coordination center on their capability to maintain macroeconomic stability while at the same time promoting sustainable and equitable economic growth. In this regard, I must say that with the heavy burden of subsidy has severely limited the capacity of fiscal policy to stimulate and acts as counter-cyclical measures in the economy. Conversely, through a monetary and macroprudential policy mix which I will talk shortly, the central bank has been able to maintain the monetary and financial system stability while at the same time help in promoting sustainable and equitable growth in Indonesia. 12. Policy coordination between fiscal, monetary and financial sectors policies has been strengthened with the establishment of Financial System Stability Coordination Forum among the Ministry of Finance, Bank Indonesia, Financial Services Authority, and Deposit Insurance Institution since last year. This forum is an integral part of national crisis 3 prevention and resolution protocol. The four institutions share their assessment on macroeconomic conditions and policy issues that need to be addressed and coordinated to maintain macroeconomic and financial system stability. The forum meets regularly, i.e. monthly at the deputies level and quarterly at the ministerial level. Monetary and Macroprudential Policy Mix 13. Let me share with you Bank Indonesia experience in formulating and implementing monetary and macroprudential policy. Faced with more complex problems above, Bank Indonesia no longer just rely on one instrument, particularly, the interest rate policy in controlling inflation and promoting sustainable economic growth. Since mid of 2010, Bank Indonesia took a new approach through monetary and macroprudential policy mix, implemented through the following five instruments. First, the policy interest rate is always directed to ensure that future inflation remained under control and within the range of the target of 4.5% 1% in 2013 and 2014. Under current condition, the policy interest rate (BI Rate) has been maintained at 5.75% as it deems consistent with the inflation forecast over the next two years that will fall within the target. 14. Second, Bank Indonesia continues to maintain exchange rate stability is maintained in accordance with economic fundamentals. Thus, maintaining the path and stability of exchange rate is an integral part of the efforts to achieve the inflation target based on the a forward looking macroeconomic projection exercise. To that end, Bank Indonesia intervened to supply the foreign exchange market as needed. This effort is supported by the adequacy of foreign exchange reserves, which today is approximately USD 107 billion, or about 6 months of imports and government foreign debt payments. 15. Third, Bank Indonesia has pursued a number of measures to manage capital flows, especially those of short-term and speculative nature. This has been done through a number of measures such as six-month holding period for investing on central bank bills, limits on banks short-term off-shore borrowing to a maximum of 20 percent of capital. At the same time, capital flows that are of medium-and long-term nature, such as in the form of FDI, long-term bonds and off-shore borrowings, are continuously welcome as these benefits to the economy. 16. Fourth, Bank Indonesia also introduced a number of macroprudential policies to manage the allocation of bank credit to various sectors to be more balanced and support the economy. The measures are also geared toward dampening the procyclicality nature of bank lending in the economy. In this regard, last year the central bank issued the new regulations on Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio ranging from 70 to 80 per cent to dampen the excessive lending growth to property and automotive sectors. On the other hand, 4 accommodative macroprudential measures are deployed to stimulate lending to a number of sectors which are supporting sustainable and equitable economic growth. For example, Bank Indonesia has issued a policy requiring lending to MSMEs by each bank a minimum of 20% of their total lending within the next five years. Bank Indonesia is also considering macroprudential policies to encourage lending to the agricultural sector, particularly in support of food security. 17. Fifth, Bank Indonesia continues to strengthen policy coordination with the Government at central and local levels to curb inflation pressures especially from volatile foods prices because of production, distribution and market structure. In addition to Inflation Control Team (ICT) at the national, we have established as many as 88 ICTs through the country, i.e. in all of the 33 provinces and 55 cities/counties. An instruction has been issued by the central government for the establishment of the ICT in every cities and counties. The Team has played key role in identifying and solving problems of production and distribution that often give rise to pressures on volatile food prices. 18. Our experience over the past three years shows that this new framework has been effective. The policy mix, however, is not always easy to design and implement, and it needs to be appropriately and continuously calibrated according to the evolving dynamics of the global and domestic economic environment. Communicating the policy mix is also a challenge. We need to be clear at all times which instrument is directed to which specific objective, and we must also avoid substituting the interest rate policy for other instruments in the mix. Even when we are successful in these aims, there is always a risk that the market may perceive matters differently, given that the monetary policy response is generally (and often only) associated with interest rate adjustments. Closing Remark 19. In closing, once again, I am delighted that we are here today. I hope the next two-days policy dialogue provides ample opportunities for all of us to enrich our understanding and able to formulate a new approach of macroeconomic policies making for promoting sustainable and equitable growth in East Asia. Thank You 5

Title: Sambutan Gubernur Bank Indonesia Pada Upacara Peringatan Hari Ulang Tahun Kemerdekaan RI ke-69 17 Agustus 2014
text: AT THE MEMORIAL SERVICE 69TH ANNIVERSARY OF INDONESIA'S INDEPENDENCE AUGUST 17, 2014 95 Whom we respect our predecessors as Governor, Deputy Governor and Board of Directors of Bank Indonesia 95 To which we respect the Members of the Board of Governors, 95 Heads of Work Units, as well as Bank Employees / Employees Indonesia at head offices and representative offices, 95 Management and Members of PIPEBI, Management and Members of PPBI, 95 Management and Members of the Indonesian Veterans Corps at Bank Indonesia, 95 Management of YKK-BI and Dapenbi, as well as the entire audience Happy Assalamu'alaikum Warahmatullahi Wabarakatuh, Greetings to all of us, 1. First of all let us offer praise and thanksgiving to the presence of God The Almighty, because of the blessing of His mercy and gift, we can gather to perform a ceremony commemorating the Day Proclamation of the 69th Independence of the Republic of Indonesia. 2. Still in the atmosphere of the peak of the victory of ramadan fasting, allow us on behalf of the Board of Governors and as a person wishing you a happy Eid al-Fitr 1 Syawal 1435 H for brothers/sisters who celebrated it, apologies for birth and mercy. 3. Today, we together commemorate the victory of the Nation Indonesian. A victory that has been fought for and proclaimed by our predecessors with the sacrifice of souls, bodies and treasures. We should be grateful for the blessing of the warriors 2 we can breathe the air of independence and this country is free from Colonization. 4. After 69 years of independence, we are sure that the founders of the nation will grateful and happy to see the transformation of the Indonesian nation in 21st century. The achievement of this transformation can be seen from the education system which is better and enjoyed by the wider community. In addition, Indonesia has also risen to become a middle income country and is included in the category of the top 10 world economies if calculated from Purchasing Power Parity, has the largest middle class population in Southeast Asia and the fastest growing middle class in Asia, as well as being the third largest democracy in the world. Nutshell Indonesia today continues to grow into an increasingly diverse nation united, peaceful, prosperous and democratic. 5. Such achievements should certainly not be underestimated and should be taken for granted value. In the absence of the services of the founders of the republic and contributions and the hard work of the leaders of the nation, what we enjoy today is not will materialize. We can see examples of tragedies experienced by the people other countries that are in conflict. This of course reminding our nation of how expensive the price of independence is, unity and peace. Dear brothers, 6. Commemoration of the anniversary of the independence of the Republic of Indonesia this year took the theme: "In the Spirit of the Proclamation of August 17, 1945, We Support The Succession of National Leadership of the 2014 Election Results For The Sake of Continuation of Development Towards an Increasingly Advanced And Increasingly Developed Indonesia Prosperous." 7. The theme is very relevant to the current condition of Indonesia, for we have just organized a democratic party, for 3 elected a national leader during the 2014 - 2019 period. We should grateful that the direct election process has gone smoothly, safe, and peaceful. 8. The success of direct elections is a necessity for smooth transition of national leadership 2014 - 2019. Electoral process The past July 9 , 2014 showed that the Indonesian people have maturity and maturity in democracy and having a sense of ke-Bhinneka Tunggal Ika-an which is high. Nevertheless, we realizing that though presidential and vice presidential candidates with the most votes have been set by the Election Commission, currently there is still legal follow-up in the relevant Constitutional Court determination of the results of the election. 9. Therefore, let us all work together to continue overseeing this process to take place constitutionally and peace, and always puts interests and the future first the people of Indonesia. This condition is an absolute prerequisite for the creation of a strong and solid economic foundation due to stability macroeconomics will not be achieved without political stability. 10. During this transition period, Bank Indonesia needs to have a role that strategic in the life of the nation and state. Bank Indonesia as a monetary, macroprudential and payment system authority who are government partners should be able to be a bridge liaison between the old government and the new government, in order to the national economy continues to run on the right track (on-track), towards an economy that grows sustainably in medium-long term. 11. The role is realized , among others , by communicating and coordination in order to ensure the continuation of the reform agenda 4 Structural. Bank Indonesia and the central government and government the regions will continue to coordinate and cooperate in order to increased competitiveness, acceleration of infrastructure development, improvement of investment climate, improvement of bureaucracy and governance and licensing, including regulatory synchronization and application of e- Government. 12. Bank Indonesia and the government also need to pay close attention to various risks and Indonesia's future economic challenges, including those related to with planned rate hikes in the United States on of 2015. We need to anticipate these potential risks so that Indonesia's macroeconomic and financial system stability can remain awake. Happy brothers, 13. Macro and financial system stability that we achieve today is the result of long reforms that have been carried out post-mortem economic crisis in 1997/1998. Within 17 years after crisis, Indonesia's economy has entered a new era where our economic fundamentals are believed to have been much better. Therefore that, we need to change the paradigm in the way we view it our economy today, compared to 17 years ago. Stigma the monetary crisis that still lingers in society is no longer relevant again with the current condition of the Indonesian economy. 14. In the future, we certainly still need to pay attention to various challenges that exists, mainly to prevent the national economy from being avoiding pitfalls in middle-income countries (middle income trap), otherwise it can transform into A country that is getting more developed and prosperous. 5 15. In line with such efforts, Bank Indonesia will always directing policies to create an environment stable macroeconomics, that is, mainly by controlling inflation rate towards the set target and lowers current account deficit to a more sustainable level. Dear brothers, 16. To face various challenges in the long run, the Bank Indonesia also needs to transform, so that it can realize vision of becoming a credible and best central bank in the region. Deep this connection, there is still ample room to do strengthening the main functions of Bank Indonesia. 17. In the monetary function, Bank Indonesia will pursue policy credible and consistent monetary. Bank Indonesia will implement initiatives to strengthen the policy framework monetary, including strengthening monetary operations and deepening financial markets. Bank Indonesia also encourages the running of functions monetary, fiscal and real sector coordination in the regions, strengthening the role of TPID and advisory role to local governments through support for regional economic and financial studies and power analysis regional competitiveness. In this regard, Bank Indonesia has initiated the coordination meeting in Padang, West Sumatra, at 9pm June 2014; in Makassar, South Sulawesi, on June 23, 2014, and in Manado, North Sulawesi, on August 11, 2014. 18. In macroprudential function and financial stability, Bank Indonesia will strive for a strong and stable financial system. Policy Bank Indonesia will be directed to mitigate systemic risks in financial sector and controlling credit and liquidity on financial system in an effort to support the realization of 6 a healthy and productive economy. This policy will be strengthened with crisis strengthening management protocols to support maintained and maintained financial system stability, as well as strengthening coordination and cooperation with authorities and institutions other finance, especially between Bank Indonesia and the Authority Financial Services. 19. In the payment system function, Bank Indonesia will strive payment system that is innovative and meets governance standards which is good. Bank Indonesia will further optimize management Rupiah currency, strengthening payment system infrastructure, encouraging the realization of a less cash society, as well as strengthening regulation and supervision of payment systems. 20. Regarding the implementation of the functions of the payment system, there are two a significant event in August 2014. First, in order to fulfill the mandate of the Currency Law Number 7 of 2011, Rupiah banknotes denominated at Rp100,000 emission year 2014 starting enacted, issued, and circulated in Indonesia simultaneously with the 69th Anniversary of the Independence of the Republic of Indonesia on August 17, 2014. 21. Second, Bank Indonesia together with relevant agencies (Ministry of Ministry Economic Coordinator, Ministry of Finance, Government DKI Province, and the Association of Provincial Governments throughout Indonesia) as well as industry players in the payment system, who are members of The Indonesian Payment System Association (ASPI) has launched The National Non-Cash Movement (GNNT) on August 14, 2014. 22. This GNNT initiative aims to encourage and expand the use of cashless transactions so as to increase economic efficiency, security and convenience of transactions, 7 strengthen transparency and accountability, and support efforts prevention of corruption, money laundering and terrorism financing. Efforts to expand the use of non-cash transactions are not only for retail transactions, but also for transactions that are high value in order to facilitate the activities of receiving transactions and corporate and government financial expenditures. Happy brothers, 23. Before concluding the remarks, we on behalf of the Board of Governors would like to express high appreciation and appreciation for the contribution, hard work and dedication that the brothers and sisters have give to race and country. 24. We want to invite all of us to continue to improve devotion and devotion to the beloved nation and country by always building an atmosphere of mutual respect and trust each other, maintain professionalism, make contributions best, putting the interests of the nation and the state first, and build excellent cooperation and coordination. 25. The end of the word, in the spirit of the Day of the Proclamation of Independence of the Republic 69th Indonesia, let us support the succession of national leadership the results of the 2014 elections, for the continuation of development towards Indonesia who are getting ahead and prospering. May Allah SWT make us including people who can appreciate and thank, and can carry out the mandate of heroes and martyrs to fill independence and development in order to realize the country which is fair and prosperous. Thank you. Wassalamu'alaikum Warahmatullahi Wabarakatuh Agus D.W. Martowardojo Governor of Bank Indonesia
text_original: SAMBUTAN GUBERNUR BANK INDONESIA PADA UPACARA PERINGATAN HARI ULANG TAHUN KEMERDEKAAN RI KE-69 17 AGUSTUS 2014 ??Yang kami hormati para pendahulu kami sebagai Gubernur, Deputi Gubernur, dan Direksi Bank Indonesia ??Yang kami hormati para Anggota Dewan Gubernur, ??Para Pimpinan Satuan Kerja, serta Karyawan/Karyawati Bank Indonesia di Kantor Pusat dan Kantor Perwakilan, ??Pengurus dan Anggota PIPEBI, Pengurus dan Anggota PPBI, ??Pengurus dan Anggota Korps Veteran RI di Bank Indonesia, ??Pengurus YKK-BI dan Dapenbi, serta seluruh hadirin yang berbahagia, Assalamu'alaikum Warahmatullahi Wabarakatuh, Salam sejahtera bagi kita semua, 1. Pertama-tama marilah kita panjatkan puji dan syukur ke hadirat Tuhan Yang Maha Esa, karena atas berkat rahmat dan karunia-Nya, kita dapat berkumpul untuk melaksanakan upacara memperingati Hari Proklamasi Kemerdekaan Republik Indonesia ke-69. 2. Masih dalam suasana puncak kemenangan ibadah puasa Ramadhan, perkenankan kami atas nama Dewan Gubernur dan selaku pribadi mengucapkan selamat Idul Fitri 1 Syawal 1435 H bagi saudara/saudari yang merayakannya, mohon maaf lahir dan bathin. 3. Hari ini, kita bersama-sama memperingati kemenangan Bangsa Indonesia. Sebuah kemenangan yang telah diperjuangkan dan diproklamirkan oleh para pendahulu kita dengan pengorbanan jiwa, raga dan harta. Kita patut bersyukur karena berkat para pejuanglah 2 kita dapat menghirup udara kemerdekaan dan negara ini terbebas dari penjajahan. 4. Setelah 69 tahun merdeka, kami yakin para pendiri bangsa akan bersyukur dan bergembira melihat transformasi bangsa Indonesia di abad-21. Pencapaian transformasi ini terlihat dari sistem pendidikan yang lebih baik dan dinikmati oleh masyarakat luas. Selain itu, Indonesia juga telah naik menjadi negara middle income country dan masuk dalam kategori 10 besar ekonomi dunia jika dihitung dari Purchasing Power Parity, memiliki penduduk kelas menengah terbesar di Asia Tenggara dan pertumbuhan kelas menengah tercepat di Asia, serta menjadi negara demokrasi ketiga terbesar di dunia. Singkatnya, Indonesia saat ini terus tumbuh menjadi bangsa yang semakin bersatu, damai, makmur dan demokratis. 5. Pencapaian tersebut tentunya jangan kita anggap remeh dan patut kita hargai. Tanpa adanya jasa para pendiri republik dan sumbangsih serta kerja keras para pemimpin bangsa, apa yang kita nikmati saat ini tidak akan terwujud. Kita bisa melihat contoh tragedi yang dialami rakyat negara lain yang sedang mengalami konflik. Hal ini tentunya mengingatkan bangsa kita akan betapa mahalnya harga kemerdekaan, persatuan dan perdamaian. Saudara-saudara sekalian, 6. Peringatan hari ulang tahun kemerdekaan Republik Indonesia tahun ini mengambil tema: "Dengan Semangat Proklamasi 17 Agustus 1945, Kita Dukung Suksesi Kepemimpinan Nasional Hasil Pemilu 2014 Demi Kelanjutan Pembangunan Menuju Indonesia yang Makin Maju dan Sejahtera." 7. Tema tersebut sangat relevan dengan kondisi Indonesia saat ini, karena kita baru saja menyelenggarakan pesta demokrasi, untuk 3 memilih pemimpin nasional masa bakti 2014 - 2019. Kita patut bersyukur karena proses pemilihan langsung telah berlangsung lancar, aman, dan damai. 8. Suksesnya pemilihan langsung merupakan keniscayaan bagi kelancaran transisi kepemimpinan nasional 2014 - 2019. Proses pemilu 9 Juli 2014 yang lalu menunjukkan bahwa rakyat Indonesia memiliki kematangan dan kedewasaan dalam berdemokrasi serta memiliki rasa ke-Bhinneka Tunggal Ika-an yang tinggi. Namun demikian, kita menyadari bahwa meskipun calon Presiden dan Wakil Presiden dengan suara terbanyak telah ditetapkan oleh Komisi Pemilihan Umum, saat ini masih terdapat tindak lanjut hukum di Mahkamah Konstitusi terkait penetapan hasil pemilu tersebut. 9. Oleh karena itu, marilah kita semua bekerjasama untuk terus mengawal proses ini agar berlangsung secara konstitusional dan damai, serta selalu mengedepankan kepentingan dan masa depan rakyat Indonesia. Kondisi ini merupakan prasyarat mutlak bagi terciptanya fondasi ekonomi yang kuat dan kokoh karena stabilitas makroekonomi tidak akan tercapai tanpa adanya stabilitas politik. 10. Pada masa transisi ini, Bank Indonesia perlu memiliki peran yang strategis dalam kehidupan berbangsa dan bernegara. Bank Indonesia sebagai otoritas moneter, makroprudensial dan sistem pembayaran yang merupakan mitra pemerintah harus dapat menjadi jembatan penghubung antara pemerintahan lama dan pemerintahan baru, agar perekonomian nasional tetap berjalan pada jalur yang tepat (on-track), menuju sebuah perekonomian yang tumbuh berkesinambungan dalam jangka menengah-panjang. 11. Peran itu diwujudkan antara lain dengan melakukan komunikasi dan koordinasi dalam rangka menyakini berlanjutnya agenda reformasi 4 struktural. Bank Indonesia dan pemerintah pusat serta pemerintah daerah akan terus berkoordinasi dan bekerjasama dalam rangka peningkatan daya saing, percepatan pembangunan infrastruktur, perbaikan iklim investasi, perbaikan birokrasi dan tata kelola serta perizinan, termasuk sinkronisasi peraturan dan penerapan e- Government. 12. Bank Indonesia dan pemerintah juga perlu mencermati berbagai risiko dan tantangan perekonomian Indonesia kedepan, termasuk berkaitan dengan rencana peningkatan suku bunga di Amerika Serikat pada tahun 2015. Potensi risiko tersebut perlu kita antisipasi sehingga stabilitas makroekonomi dan sistem keuangan Indonesia dapat tetap terjaga. Saudara-saudara yang berbahagia, 13. Stabilitas makro dan sistem keuangan yang kita raih saat ini merupakan hasil dari reformasi panjang yang telah dilakukan paska krisis ekonomi pada 1997/1998. Dalam kurun waktu 17 tahun setelah krisis, ekonomi Indonesia telah memasuki era baru dimana fundamental ekonomi kita diyakini sudah jauh lebih baik. Oleh karena itu, kita perlu merubah paradigma dalam cara memandang perekonomian kita saat ini, dibandingkan 17 tahun silam. Stigma krisis moneter yang masih melekat di masyarakat sudah tidak relevan lagi dengan kondisi perekonomian Indonesia saat ini. 14. Kedepan, kita tentunya tetap perlu mencermati berbagai tantangan yang ada, terutama untuk mencegah agar perekonomian nasional terhindar dari perangkap dalam negara berpendapatan menengah (middle income trap), sebaliknya dapat bertransformasi menjadi negara yang semakin makin maju dan sejahtera. 5 15. Sejalan dengan upaya tersebut, Bank Indonesia akan senantiasa mengarahkan kebijakan untuk menciptakan lingkungan makroekonomi yang stabil, yaitu terutama dengan mengendalikan tingkat inflasi menuju sasaran yang ditetapkan dan menurunkan defisit transaksi berjalan ke tingkat yang lebih sustainable. Saudara-saudara sekalian, 16. Untuk menghadapi berbagai tantangan dalam jangka panjang, Bank Indonesia juga perlu bertransformasi, sehingga dapat mewujudkan visi menjadi bank sentral yang kredibel dan terbaik di regional. Dalam kaitan ini, masih terdapat ruang yang cukup luas untuk melakukan penguatan fungsi-fungsi utama Bank Indonesia. 17. Di fungsi moneter, Bank Indonesia akan mengupayakan kebijakan moneter yang kredibel dan konsisten. Bank Indonesia akan menjalankan inisiatif-inisiatif untuk memperkuat kerangka kebijakan moneter, termasuk penguatan operasi moneter dan pendalaman pasar keuangan. Bank Indonesia juga mendorong berjalannya fungsi koordinasi moneter, fiskal dan sektor riil di daerah, penguatan peran TPID dan peran advisory kepada pemerintah daerah melalui dukungan kajian ekonomi dan keuangan regional serta analisis daya saing daerah. Terkait hal ini, Bank Indonesia telah menginisiasi pertemuan koordinasi tersebut di Padang, Sumatera Barat, pada 9 Juni 2014; di Makassar, Sulawesi Selatan, pada 23 Juni 2014, dan di Manado, Sulawesi Utara, pada 11 Agustus 2014. 18. Di fungsi makroprudensial dan stabilitas keuangan, Bank Indonesia akan mengupayakan sistem keuangan yang kuat dan stabil. Kebijakan Bank Indonesia akan diarahkan untuk memitigasi risiko sistemik di sektor keuangan serta mengendalikan kredit dan likuiditas pada sistem keuangan dalam upaya mendukung terwujudnya 6 perekonomian yang sehat dan produktif. Kebijakan ini akan diperkuat dengan penguatan krisis manajemen protokol untuk mendukung terjaga dan terpeliharanya stabilitas sistem keuangan, serta penguatan koordinasi dan kerjasama dengan otoritas dan lembaga keuangan lainnya, khususnya antara Bank Indonesia dengan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan. 19. Di fungsi sistem pembayaran, Bank Indonesia akan mengupayakan sistem pembayaran yang inovatif dan memenuhi standar tata kelola yang baik. Bank Indonesia akan lebih mengoptimalkan pengelolaan uang Rupiah, memperkuat infrastruktur sistem pembayaran, mendorong terwujudnya less cash society, serta memperkuat pengaturan dan pengawasan sistem pembayaran. 20. Terkait pelaksanaan fungsi sistem pembayaran tersebut, terdapat dua peristiwa penting di bulan Agustus 2014. Pertama, dalam rangka memenuhi amanat Undang-Undang Mata Uang Nomor 7 tahun 2011, uang Rupiah kertas pecahan Rp100.000 Tahun Emisi 2014 mulai diberlakukan, dikeluarkan, dan diedarkan di Indonesia bertepatan dengan Hari Ulang Tahun ke-69 Kemerdekaan Republik Indonesia pada 17 Agustus 2014. 21. Kedua, Bank Indonesia bersama dengan instansi terkait (Kementrian Koordinator Perekonomian, Kementrian Keuangan, Pemerintah Provinsi DKI, dan Asosiasi Pemerintah Provinsi Seluruh Indonesia) serta pelaku industri di sistem pembayaran, yang tergabung dalam Asosiasi Sistem Pembayaran Indonesia (ASPI) telah mencanangkan Gerakan Nasional Non Tunai (GNNT) pada 14 Agustus 2014 yang lalu. 22. Inisiatif GNNT ini bertujuan untuk mendorong dan memperluas penggunaan transaksi non tunai sehingga dapat meningkatkan efisiensi perekonomian, keamanan dan kenyamanan bertransaksi, 7 memperkuat transparansi dan akuntabilitas, serta mendukung upaya pencegahan korupsi, pencucian uang dan pembiayaan terorisme. Upaya perluasan penggunaan transaksi non-tunai tidak hanya untuk transaksi ritel, namun juga untuk transaksi yang bersifat high value dalam rangka fasilitasi kegiatan transaksi penerimaan dan pengeluaran keuangan korporasi dan pemerintah. Saudara-saudara yang berbahagia, 23. Sebelum mengakhiri sambutan, kami atas nama Dewan Gubernur ingin menyampaikan penghargaan dan apresiasi yang tinggi atas kontribusi, kerja keras dan dedikasi yang telah saudara-saudari berikan kepada bangsa dan negara. 24. Kami ingin mengajak kita semua untuk terus meningkatkan pengabdian dan karya bakti kepada bangsa dan negara tercinta dengan senantiasa membangun suasana saling menghormati dan saling percaya, menjaga profesionalisme, memberikan kontribusi terbaik, mengutamakan kepentingan bangsa dan negara, serta membangun kerjasama dan koordinasi yang prima. 25. Akhir kata, dengan semangat Hari Proklamasi Kemerdekaan Republik Indonesia ke-69, marilah kita dukung suksesi kepemimpinan nasional hasil pemilu 2014, demi kelanjutan pembangunan menuju Indonesia yang makin maju dan sejahtera. Semoga, Allah SWT menjadikan kita termasuk orang-orang yang dapat menghargai dan berterimakasih, serta dapat mengemban amanat para pahlawan dan syuhada untuk mengisi kemerdekaan dan pembangunan demi mewujudkan negara yang adil dan makmur. Sekian dan terima kasih. Wassalamu'alaikum Warahmatullahi Wabarakatuh Agus D.W. Martowardojo Gubernur Bank Indonesia

Title: Speech of the Governor of Bank Indonesia Issuance of New Rp100,000 Banknote for 2014 18th August 2014
text: Speech of the Governor of Bank Indonesia Issuance of New Rp100,000 Banknote for 2014 18th August 2014 Respected guests,  Honourable representatives of MPR/DPR/DPD of the Republic of Indonesia  Honourable representatives of Commission XI of the House of Representatives of the Republic of Indonesia  The Minister of Finance of the Republic of Indonesia, Hon. Muhammad Chatib Basri, S.E., M.Ec.  The Chairman of the OJK Board of Commissions, Dr Muliaman D. Hadad  Members of the BI Board of Governors  Representatives of Bank Indonesia  Representatives of Perum Peruri  Representatives of the Banking Industry  Representatives of Perbanas Institute, Perbarindo and Himbara  Descendants of our national heroes, Dr (H.C.) Ir. Soekarno and Dr (H.C.) Drs Mohammad Hatta  Ladies and gentlemen Assalamualaikum Warahmatullahi Wabarakatuh Good day to you all. 1. Let me begin by expressing praise to God Almighty for His bounty and blessings that we may gather here today to officially issue a new Rp100,000 banknote for 2014. 2. Yesterday, on 17th August 2014, we celebrated the 69th anniversary of the Proclamation of Independence of the Republic of Indonesia. Long live the Republic of Indonesia! May the sovereignty of the Republic of Indonesia be respected and live on in us all. Ladies and gentlemen, 3. The sovereignty of the Republic of Indonesia did not just appear; it was achieved through a long struggle with lives and possessions lost. As the nations next generation, we have duly expressed our gratitude, appreciation and respect for the sacrifices of our national heroes. 4. As a form of respect and appreciation to our national heroes we must honour our symbols of sovereignty, one of which is the rupiah. 5. Pursuant to Act Number 7 of 2011, the Currency Act, the rupiah is the official currency of the Republic of Indonesia and legal tender throughout the archipelago. 6. Notwithstanding, we are concerned that there remain certain parties who do not fully implement or comply with the provisions stipulated in the Currency Act. We regularly encounter disrespectful behaviour towards the rupiah within the territory of the Republic of Indonesia. 7. For example, transactions in border areas are regularly conducted using foreign currencies. Of greater concern is that the use of non-rupiah currencies has spread beyond border towns and villages. In other areas of the country certain parties list prices and tariffs of goods and services in currencies other than the rupiah. 8. Such actions have at least three arresting implications. First, legal implications. The use of non-rupiah currencies within Indonesian borders can harm the legal mandate of the Currency Act. Consequently, those who violate the mandate will face the legal consequences. 9. Second, national implications. The use of non-rupiah currencies is not aligned with the spirit of nationalism and idealism. In other words, the use of non-rupiah currencies can be viewed as disrespectful behaviour towards national sovereignty. 10. Third, economic implications. The use of non-rupiah currencies in the economy exacerbates exchange rate volatility. Left unchecked, demand for non-rupiah currencies could soar, thereby undermining rupiah stability. Ladies and gentlemen, 11. Bank Indonesia, as the monetary, macroprudential policy and payment system authority, is mandated with creating and maintaining rupiah stability. Today, as part of its task implementation with respect to the payment system, Bank Indonesia will issue and circulate a new Rp100,000 banknote for 2014. 12. We are grateful because after a lengthy process the new Rp100,000 banknote is ready to be issued. On this joyous occasion, we would like to express our gratitude and appreciation to the Government and all related parties who supported and assisted the issuance and circulation of the new banknote. 13. The new 2014 issue Rp100,000 banknote fully satisfies all stipulations contained in the Currency Act, which mandates that the rupiah banknote with special features must be issued and circulated throughout the Indonesia archipelago on 17th August 2014. 14. Accordingly, on 14th August 2014, Bank Indonesia in conjunction with the Government issued a press release concerning the imminent launch of a new Rp100,000 banknote. Furthermore, on 15th August 2014, the President announced the issuance of a new banknote with special characteristics during his national address at the 69th Anniversary of the Proclamation of Independence of the Republic of Indonesia. 15. In addition, Bank Indonesia also undertook extraordinary efforts to ensure an adequate supply of the new banknote was available at Bank Indonesia Representative Offices throughout the archipelago, thereby enabling the new banknote to be circulated on 17th August 2014. 16. In general, the design of the new Rp100,000 banknote is not significantly different from the existing banknote. The two most salient differences are (i) the inclusion of the phrase Negara Kesatuan Republik Indonesia (The Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia) and (ii) the signatures of the Governor of Bank Indonesia and the Minister of Finance. 17. Inclusion of the phrase Negara Kesatuan Republik Indonesia (The Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia) as well as the signatures of the Governor of Bank Indonesia and the Minister of Finance emphasise the philosophy of the rupiah as a symbol of national sovereignty that must be respected by all Indonesians. Ladies and gentlemen, 18. Before closing my speech, I would like to once again express gratitude and utmost appreciation to the Government and all relevant parties who supported and assisted the issuance of the new Rp100,000 banknote, 2014 issue. 19. We sincerely expect all parties to promote the use of the rupiah for all domestic economic transactions. Such support will bolster the sovereignty of the rupiah in the territory of the Republic of Indonesia. 20. Finally, may Allah always protect us and bless our goodwill. Amen. Thank you. Wassalamualaikum Warahmatullahi Wabarakatuh Agus D.W. Martowardojo Governor of Bank Indonesia

Title: Sambutan Deputi Gubernur Bank Indonesia Hendar dalam Dewan Kurator Wisuda Stie Indonesia Banking School Tahun 2015 Jakarta, 14 November 2015
text: REMARKS BY THE BOARD OF CURATORS OF STIE INDONESIA BANKING SCHOOL GRADUATION IN 2015 Jakarta, November 14, 2015 Which I respect, 95 Chief Commissioner of the Financial Services Authority, Dr. Muliaman D. Hadad; 95 Chairman of STIE Indonesia Banking School (IBS), Dr. Subarjo Joyosumarto; 95 Coordinator of Kopertis Region III, Dr. Ir. Illah Sailah 95 Honorable faculty STIE IBS; o Drs. Rachmat Saleh o Prof. Adrianus Mooy o Dr. Darmin Nasution o Dr. KH. (HC) Ma'ruf Amin Binhadi MSc o Prof. Dr. H. Djokosantoso Moeljono 95 Members of the Academic Senate of STIE IBS; 95 The Founders of STIE IBS; 95 President Director of LPPI Dr. Hartadi A. Sarwono and the board of directors of LPPI; 95 YPPI Chairman Bp Abdul Azis; 95 The Academic Community of STIE IBS, lecturers, and students; 95 Happy Attendees and Invitees, Assalamualaikum Wr. Wb. l.Starting this speech, let me invite you all to jointly express praise and gratitude to the presence of God Almighty, because only with His approval can we meet in a good atmosphere to jointly attend and witness the Graduation of STIE Indonesia Banking School (IBS) in 2015. On behalf of ourselves and the Board of Governors of Bank Indonesia, we congratulate the graduates of STIE IBS and the parents who attended today's graduation ceremony. 2.Before we read the remarks of the Governor of Bank Indonesia as Chairman of the Board of Curators, let us express our apologies from the Governor of Bank Indonesia, Mr. Agus Martowardojo, who was unable to attend the STIE IBS graduation ceremony today. From Thursday to Sunday tomorrow, all Members of the Board of Governors of the Bank Indonesia is in Yogyakarta in a series of activities on the Board of Seminars on Regional Economic and Financial Studies as well as coordination between Bank Indonesia and the Central Government-Regional Government in Yogyakarta. This activity has been a routine agenda since the beginning of 2015 as part of Bank Indonesia's efforts to encourage structural reforms at both the central and regional levels. Mr./lbu and the happy audience, The latest economic challenges 3. Soon we will leave 2015, a year full of challenges for the Indonesian economy. I noted at least 4 challenges faced by the Indonesian economy in 2015. First is the uncertainty of the global economy. Global economic conditions this year turned out to be not as bright as originally thought. The global economic recovery is indeed continuing in various major economies of the world, but at a pace that is not according to expectations and unevenly. This is indicated by several downward revisions to the projections of world economic growth by various international institutions. World commodity prices continued to slump due to weakening demand, especially from China. As a country with an open economy and financial system, Indonesia cannot be separated from the constellation of the global economy. Especially in the midst of the divergence of world monetary policy and changes in the perception of external risks that caused the US dollar on a global scale to continue to strengthen. These external pressures in turn caused instability in the domestic economy, including rupiah depreciation, capital outflows in both the capital market and stock markets, as well as rising SBN yields. 4. Second is the slowdown in economic growth. As is known that until the final quarter of 111-2015, the economy Indonesia is growing below 5%. The first quarter grew by 4.71%, the second quarter grew by 4.67%, while the newly announced third quarter last week rose slightly to 4.73%. The slowdown was caused by declining export performance due to the continued decline in prices of a number of major primary commodities such as CPO, rubber, coal and petroleum. This decline in commodity prices has caused economic growth in most provinces, whose economies are based on natural resources, especially in Sumatra and Kalimantan, to decline dramatically. Even in some provinces experienced negative growth such as Kaltim-Kaltara, Riau, and Aceh Provinces. This economic slowdown has begun to have an impact on the increase in the unemployment rate. The August 2015 Open Unemployment Rate announced on November 5, 2015, showed an increase from 5.9% to 6.2% due to a decrease in the number of workers in the sector. agriculture, industry, and services. Even the increase in the open unemployment rate in Riau and East Kalimantan has increased beyond the 7% mark. 5. Tantanqan ketiqa is the implementation of the ASEAN Economic Community (AEC) vang will begin at the end of December 2015. On the one hand, the AEC's commitment will open up market opportunities with a freer flow of goods, services, investment, labor and capital. But on the other hand, this also has the consequence of increasing competition in the domestic market of each country. With the massive market potential, I see the most fundamental challenge of the MEA's commitment is our ability to create competitiveness. Can we afford to use the AEC as an opportunity to play a role as a major actor in the global production chain, or will we become the target market and audience? In my view, it is at this point that the capability we to read and anticipate future economic movements are increasingly tested. 6. The fourth tantanqan is the normalization of the bunqa rate of the Central Bank of the United States. This issue has dominated financial market dynamics in both the advanced economy and emerging markets since May 2013. This normalization of interest rates results in uncertainty that often changes the risk on-risk off behavior of investors so quickly. Following the release of improving U.S. labor data in October 2015, a Bloomberg survey showed market expectations for a rate hike by the U.S. central bank, the Fed Fund Rate, in December 2015 increased from 56% to 68%. Mr/lbu and the happy audience, The Latest Bank Indonesia Policy 7. Facing these severe economic challenges, various policies have been carried out. In midwifeq moneter, Bl remains maintain a tight biased monetary policy to boost market confidence and reduce the current account deficit. Although pressures on macro stability have begun to ease, leaving room for monetary policy easing, weneed to pay close attention to the high risk of global uncertainty, especially the planned increase in the Fed Fund Rate in December and the readiness to mitigate risks. 8.In line with this, the focus of Bl's policy in the short ianqka remains directed at lanqkah-lanqkah value stabilization Change strengthening liquidity management rupiah and strengthening management supply- forex demand. Bank Indonesia also welcomes and appreciates the series of policy packages of the Government and OJK in supporting growth. economic and structural reforms necessary to strengthen the foundations of the Indonesian economy. These various policy measures are expected to be able to create an increasingly conducive investment climate which in turn canimprove the outlook for the Indonesian economy. 9-Some of these policy measures have had a positive impact although they have not fully met expectations. Good news was published last week where Fitch Rating affirmed Indonesia's souverign rating with a stable outlook (BBB-). We need to be grateful for this in the midst of increasing global volatility. However, pressures on the rupiah will still not ease even though Bank Indonesia has stabilised quite a lot in the foreign exchange market. Recognizing the complexity of the challenges faced, we will continue and strengthen policy coordination between institutions. Confidence and Positive Perception 10. We realize that it is not easy for us to go through the various challenges facing the economy. But we must remain optimistic because history proves that we have a good experience in carrying out economic reforms. Pertamaj in the period before the old order, Indonesia has been recorded in the book Economics Development written Beniamin Higgins in 1963 sebagai "the chronic drop out" dan expressed as an example of a failure in managing the economy. However, within 30 hours year, IMF and World Bank declare Indonesia as one of the "Asian" Miracle", with economic growth high and stable, successful structural transformations, as well as controlled inflation. 11. Second, at the time of the 1997 Asian financial crisis, we, along with Thailand and Korea, were the countries that suffered the most severe impacts, leading to political crises and power changes. However, with the various reforms we carried out, inthe 2008 global financial crisis, Indonesia along with China and India became the few countries that survived the vortex of the largest world economic crisis after the 1930 economic crisis, with economic growth still growing above 4%. 12. The experience conveys a message to all of us that no matter how tough the challenges will be, we will be able to go through as long as we maintain confidence and conveying a positive perception that we have, are, and will undertake structural reforms. This requires the synergy of Indonesia Incorporated, both the government, central bank, OJK and the business world, including the financial and financial sectors. Ladies and gentlemen, happy invitees and attendees, 13. In dealing with this tantanqan, especially in the face of the 2015 AEC, actors in the financial sector must prepare themselves as well as possible to have dava sainq and professionalism vang tinqqi so as to become first-class bankers. We must be able to show that indonesian banking personnel and financial sector professionals are the best in the ASEAN region. 14. We need to prepare the following things to increase the dava sainq of thep rofesional in the keuanqan sector. First, standardization of the quality of human resources that link and match the needs of the market. Academic education is required to have a curriculum and teaching methods that can produce ready-made graduates. Therefore, the academic world needs to continue to update itself with the latest developments in the growing world of finance. It is necessary to give special time for students to discuss with professionals and policy makers in the field of finance. 15. Second,the existence of competency certification in the financial sector is a necessity. To compete with the skilled workforce of other ASEAN countries, a bachelor's degree is simply not enough. Now there are more and more new professions that have not beenwidely implemented and require certifications, both those that is global as well as national. An accounting and management scholar could have been a financial, management, and operational auditor, but not necessarily all could have audited the information, software, and application systems. Whereas in the next 5 years, we have to compete with human resources from MEA member countries. 16. Ketiqa, the importance of assessing the sainq power of human resources in banking and svariah finance. After the issuance of Law No. 21 of 2008 concerning Islamic Banking and the rise of Islamic financial instruments such as sukuk and the Islamic capital market, it has triggereda very large need for work opportunities. In addition to having skills in the field of finance, Islamic financial human resources are required to have an understanding of sharia principles. Although the ratio of Islamic banking assets to banking assets is currently still below 5%, the supply of human resources in the field of Islamic banking and finance is still limited. Facing the 2015 AEC, especially with the advantages of our neighboring countries in Islamic banking and finance, it feels like we need to sit down together to address this. 17. Last but not least, as good as the runway from tiqa the above, sava menqqarisbawahi pentinqnya education towards inteqritas. I believe that knowledge and skills are realized by mastery of competency standards and professional expertise will be meaningless without good integrity, because business in the financial sector is a business of trust. Ladies and gentlemen, happy invitees and attendees, 18. Finally, we congratulate STIE IBS who successfully graduated around 120 alumni at the 2015 graduation. Hopefully this will be an even better motivation to produce graduates- better STIE IBS graduates the following year. I also pronounce congratulations to the graduates STIE IBS. The bachelor's degree or master's degree that you achieved today is a provision for you all to enter a new world. After being equipped with banking and finance knowledge at the STIE IBS campus, now is the time for you to create value. I always remember Einstein's words, "Try not to become a man of success, but rather try to become a man of value." 19. May our goodwill to build the nation and state through the development of quality and integrity banking and financial sector personnel will always get ridho from Allah SWT. That's it and thank you. Wassalamualaikum Wr Wb. Jakarta, 14th November 2015 Deputy Governor Hendar
text_original: SAMBUTAN DEWAN KURATOR WISUDA STIE INDONESIA BANKING SCHOOL TAHUN 2015 Jakarta, 14 November 2015 Yang saya hormati, <95> Ketua Komisioner Otoritas Jasa Keuangan, Dr. Muliaman D. Hadad; <95> Ketua STIE Indonesia Banking School (IBS), Dr. Subarjo Joyosumarto; <95> Koordinator Kopertis Wilayah III, Dr. Ir. Illah Sailah <95> Honorable faculty STIE IBS; o Drs. Rachmat Saleh o Prof. Adrianus Mooy o Dr. Darmin Nasution o Dr. KH. (HC) Ma'ruf Amin o Drs. Binhadi o Prof. Dr. H. Djokosantoso Moeljono <95> Para Anggota Senat Akademik STIE IBS; <95> Para Pendiri STIE IBS; <95> Direktur Utama LPPI Dr. Hartadi A. Sarwono beserta jajaran direksi LPPI; <95> Ketua YPPI Bp Abdul Azis; <95> Civitas Akademika STIE IBS, para Dosen, dan para mahasiswa; <95> Para Hadirin dan Undangan yang berbahagia, Assalamualaikum Wr.
