Area strategis kedua adalah menjadikan Bank Indonesia Institute sebagai lembaga riset dan studi terkemuka tingkat dunia di bidang ekonomi dan keuangan. Bank Indonesia Institute dalam hal ini akan memfasilitasi diskusi kebijakan moneter, fiskal, keuangan, dan perdagangan internasional, serta memberikan alternatif solusi atas berbagai permasalahan ekonomi yang mengemuka. 20. Pada area strategis kedua ini, Bank Indonesia Institute menjalankan fungsinya dengan mengundang dan memberikan kesempatan yang luas kepada para pakar, akademisi, maupun tokoh ekonomi dan keuangan, untuk mengasah dan menunjukkan keunggulannya dalam memberikan pemikiran dan solusi terbaik bagi pembangunan ekonomi. Bapak/Ibu dan para hadirin yang kami hormati, 21. Di hadapan kita masih terbentang jalan yang berliku. Dinamika perekonomian global yang tidak menentu, revolusi teknologi digital di bidang keuangan yang semakin cepat, serta belum merata dan inklusifnya pembangunan ekonomi, hanyalah sebagian kecil dari tantangan besar yang harus dihadapi. 22. Permasalahan perekonomian yang sedemikian kompleks tentu menuntut kehadiran sumber daya manusia yang unggul dan mampu menunjukkan kepemimpinan yang prima. Disini, Bank Indonesia Institute harus berada pada posisi yang tepat dan menunjukkan kelasnya dalam mem ba ng un kapasitas dan ka pa bi litas sumber daya manusia yang berkualitas tinggi, serta menjadi lembaga terkemuka dunia yang mampu memberikan pemikiran maupun alternatif solusi terbaik bagi bangsa dan negara. 23. Namun, upaya itu tentu tidak mudah dilaksanakan. Terlebih, fungsi strategis yang diamanatkan tidak hanya untuk mengembangkan keunggulan sumber daya manusia internal Bank Indonesia, namun juga memberikan dharma bhakti yang prima untuk turut membentuk kepemimpinan ekonomi yang unggul. 24. Kami meyakini cita-cita pendiri bangsa yang menjadi landasan berpijak bagi Bank Indonesia Institute, akan mendorong terbangunnya keteguhan dalam memberikan kerja nyata terbaik, serta menjadi bekal perjuangan tanpa lelah untuk mewujudkan sumber daya manusia yang berkualitas. Bank Indonesia Institute didirikan tidak hanya untuk 10, 20, atau 30 tahun kedepan, namun akan terus hadir mengawal dan memberikan kontribusi terbaik bagi terwujudnya sumber daya manusia yang unggul. 25. Keberadaan Dewan Kehormatan yang didukung oleh tokoh-tokoh bangsa dan para pakar nasional dan internasional yang tidak diragukan lagi wawasan maupun keahliannya, niscaya akan dapat mewujudkan Bank Indonesia Institute sebagai lembaga berkelas dunia yang memiliki kredibilitas dan reputasi tinggi. 26. Demikian pula dengan kehadiran Dewan Penasehat yang diketuai oleh Deputi Gubenur Dr. Perry Warjiyo, serta faculty members eksternal dan internal Bank Indonesia yang memiliki kemampuan dan keahlian dibidangnya, kami meyakini hal tersebut akan membawa Bank Indonesia Institute untuk terus bergerak, melangkah maju, dan mampu beradaptasi dengan dinamika lingkungan yang berubah, serta memberikan kontribusi terbaiknya secara efektif. 27. Kemitraan stategis yang dibangun dengan berbagai lembaga di dalam dan luar negeri juga akan memperkaya wawasan dalam proses pembelajaran, studi, maupun riset yang berlangsung di Bank Indonesia Institute. 28. Selain itu, secara khusus kemitraan strategis dengan lembaga-lembaga di luar negeri akan memfasilitasi perwujudan Bank Indonesia Institute sebagai lembaga terkemuka yang memiliki kontribusi strategis dalam membentuk pemimpin-pemimpin ekonomi kelas dunia. Bapak/Ibu dan para hadirin yang kami muliakan, 29. Mengakhiri sambutan kami, perkenankan kami atas nama Dewan Gubernur Bank Indonesia menyampaikan apresiasi dan penghargaan kepada Dewan Kehormatan, Dewan Penasehat, Faculty Members, serta para undangan yang telah memberikan perhatian besar kepada peresmian Bank Indonesia Institute pada hari ini. 30. Semoga dengan peresmian Bank Indonesia Institute dan dijalankannya kegiatan studi dan riset secara penuh mulai hari ini, kelak akan membawa Bank Indonesia Institute menjadi lembaga pembelajaran, studi, dan riset terkemuka tingkat dunia yang memberikan kontribusi strategis bagi terwujudnya sumber daya manusia yang berkualitas, berintegritas, dan mampu mewujudkan bangsa yang makmur, sejahtera, dan berkeadilan. 31. Akhir kata, dengan memohon ridho Allah SWT, Bank Indonesia dengan rasa bangga dan penuh suka cita mempersembahkan Bank Indonesia Institute kepada Indonesia untuk menjadi bagian dari keselarasan gerak pengembangan sumber daya manusia yang unggul, demi terwujudnya pemimpin-pemimpin ekonomi masa depan bangsa yang handal dan berkualitas tinggi. 32. Semoga Allah SWT senantiasa melindungi, meridhoi dan meringankan setiap langkah perjuangan kita membangun negara dan memakmurkan negeri. Sekian dan terima kasih. Wassalamu'alaikum Wr. Wb Agus D.W. Martowardojo Gubernur Bank Indonesia

Title: Sambutan Pembukaan Halim Alamsyah, Deputi Gubernur BI Seminar Nasional Keuangan Inklusif: "Pentingnya Keuangan Inklusif dalam Meningkatkan Akses Masyarakat dan UMKM terhadap Fasilitas Jasa Keuangan Syariah" Surabaya, 7 November 2014
text: Opening Remarks by Dr. Halim Alamsyah, Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia National Seminar on Financial Inclusion: "The Importance of Financial Inclusion in Improving Public and MSME Access to Islamic Financial Services Facilities" Surabaya, 7 November 2014 Bismillahhirrohmannirrohim, Alhamdulillahhirobbil aalamin, asholatuwassholaamuala asyrofil anbiya iwal mursalin wa ala aalihi washohbihi ajmain Which I respect, Leader of Bank Indonesia Representative Office Surabaya or who represents Mr/mrs. Authoritative Officials bag Financial Services both from the Head Office and Surabaya Regional Office Officials from various ministries who attended and have supported the implementation of this activity (Ministry of Manpower and Transmigration and BNP2TKI, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Social Affairs, Ministry of Agriculture, Ministry of Religious Affairs, Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs and Iain-Iain that cannot be mentioned one by one) Elements of the regional leadership of East Java province and surabaya municipality Mr/ mrs officials from national and regional banks, colleagues from universities, associations, Amil Zakat institutions, BMT, ladies and gentlemen who are blessed by Allah SWT Assalammualaikum warohmatullahhi wabarakatuh First of all, let us pray all praise and gratitude to Allah SWT, for His rakhmat and gift, we can all attend this National Seminar on Financial Inclusion in the City of Surabaya. Do not forget the shalawat and greetings to the Great Prophet Muhammad SAW and His family, friends and followers until the end of time. Happy audience, Background of Public Financial Access Conditions in Indonesia 1. In the last five years, Indonesia's economic growth has been in the range of 6%, a proud achievement amidst the uncertainty of global economic conditions. However, it seems that the benefits of this growth have not had an evenly distributed impact on the poor. Although the number of poor people has decreased (BPS data in March 2014), from 32 million people (2009) to 28 million people (2014), the delta decline is getting smaller. One of the factors identified by Bl is the low public access to financial services. 2. Based on the results of the Bl household balance survey (2012), only 48% of the total households in Indonesia have savings in banks, non-bank financial institutions and non-financial institutions. In other words, there are 52% of households in Indonesia that do not have any savings at all. This is in line with the World Bank Survey (2010) which states that in Indonesia, access to formal financial services is only available to half of the Indonesian population. 32% of the Indonesian population does not even have savings (both in the formal and informal sectors), and falls into the category of financially excluded. 3. There are many factors behind why there are still groups of people who do not have access to banks or financial institutions, both in the form of savings and credit acquisition. Some of them are a long distance from the place of residence to the bank office, the products offered are not suitable, product information that is not understood, low income, identity documents that do not exist, and the perception that banks / financial institutions are not for small communities. From the banking side, there are also obstacles, including related to the establishment of branch offices with segmentation to unbanked people requiring expensive costs, so banks prefer large customers who can meet the requirements. Bl's Role in Promoting Financial Inclusion in Indonesia 4. On the other hand, we realize that Indonesia has great potential to improve people's welfare through economic growth. To that end, as with most central banks in developing countries, Bank Indonesia has long been actively involved in stimulating economic activities, including the development of MSMEs in an effort to eradicate poverty, both in conventional ways such as technical assistance, marketing and capital, as well as with a breakthrough covered in the Financial Inclusion Policy. 5. Financial inclusion is defined as an effort aimed at reducing all forms of barriers that are price and non-price, to public access to financial services. The policy needs to be carried out by the national secara, involving relevant ministries, authorities, and institutions to obtain optimal results. 6. Related to this, Bl actively collaborates with the Ministry of Finance (BKF), OJK, and the National Team for the Acceleration of Poverty Reduction (TNP2K), in the form of yes, developing a comprehensive financial access improvement strategy , namely, The National Financial Inclusion Strategy (SNKI) which is a national commitment and has been launched by the Vice President of Rl in June 2012. In its implementation, SNKI requires the support of various parties, namely ministries, authorities, and related institutions or institutions including the private sector to create collaboration and synergy in order to encourage economic growth through poverty alleviation and income equality while maintaining financial system stability. 7. Within the framework of the SNKI, Bank Indonesia is fully committed and has implemented various programs and breakthroughs, including: a. Financial Education Program that is national, comprehensive and sustainable which aims to increase public knowledge about finance. The target of the implementation of this education is students from elementary, junior high, high school to students, migrant workers, and certain community groups, a.I. farmers, fishermen, traders, homeworkers, communities in the border areas and islands. b. Increasing the utilization of TabunganKu is related to the Indonesia Savings Movement. As of August 2014, there were 12.34 million TabunganKU accounts, an increase of 1.72 million accounts (16.2%) compared to the position at the end of 2013. c. Encouraging public access in remote areas connected to financial services through the implementation of Digital Financial Services (DFS) for individual agents LKD is a breakthrough program that aims to expand the community's acceptance to financial services by utilizing today's technology such as mobile phones and involving the services of LKD agents. LKD uses registered electronic money (registered e-money) with the help of a mobile phone or card (the number of registered e-money b1 2.7 million). LKD can be used to make bill payments or cash withdrawals and can even be used for the distribution of government assistance to the public (G2P) in a non-cash manner. d. The development of the G2P (government to person) program went through trials of the distribution of the Family Hope Program (PKH) and social assistance using Electronic Money The G2P program has officially been started through the launch of the Prosperous Family Card (KKS), Smart Indonesia Card (KIP), and Healthy Indonesia Card (KIS) by the President of Rl, Joko Widodo on November 3, 2014 in Jakarta. This is in line with the National Non-Cash Movement (GNNT) launched by Bl which is expected to accelerate the implementation of LKD in Indonesia to support financial inclusion. - Previously, Bl together with the government had also conducted a trial distribution of Conditional Cash Direct Assistance to participants of the Family Hope Program (PKH) using Electronic Money through LKD Agents in DKI Jakarta, West Java, East Java and East Nusa Tenggara pexisted last October 2014. e. Developing the Financial Identity Number (FIN) project aims to provide a database of unbanked people that can be accessed by financial institutions in order to reduce assymetric information. Since 2012, Bl has gradually carried out the development of FIN. In the early stages, it has collected baseline survey and comprehensive survey data, and until now it is still making efforts to improve FIN infrastructure. In its future development, the FIN project will use the Ministry of Home Affairs' e-KTP database, a list of recipients of the Family Hope Program funds and a survey of Bl's household balance sheet. f. Empowerment of UIVIKM through the provision of technical, production and marketing assistance. Bl also launched several initiative programs, including an entrepreneurship program aimed at supporting the National Entrepreneurship Movement in the context of creating new entrepreneurs through continuous mentoring. As we know, MSMEs are one of the main targets in the financial inclusion program, considering the strategic role of MSMEs in the Indonesian economy, namely as the main contributor to GDP (around 57.84%), and the absorption of 97.2% of the total Indonesian workforce. Ladies and gentlemen Happy audience The Potential of Islamic Financial Inclusion in Indonesia 8. Judging from its history, Islamic financial institutions in Indonesia have existed since 20 years ago, which was marked by the issuance of Law N0.7 of 1992 concerning Banking, which became the gateway to the establishment of financial institutions operating based on sharia principles. 9. Although currently the market share of Islamic banking is still small (around 5%), Indonesia has a very large potential to develop Islamic finance, especially retail mass banking, as reflected in the total Muslim population of 207 million people or reaching 87% of all Indonesians (BPS Population Census, 2010). This potential is supported by the increasingly visible changes in the behavior and lifestyle of the Indonesian Muslim community, who are increasingly actively looking for financial products that are able to provide a good mix of functional and spiritual benefits. 10. To increase the share of the Islamic financial market, integrated efforts are needed in various fields, ranging from product innovation, expansion of distribution channels, improvement of services and quality of human resources, communication strategies including continuous education programs. Sharia Financial Inclusion and Poverty Alleviation 11. Islamic finance and financial inclusion policies have the potential to synergize well considering the similar concepts, namely: financial inclusion aims to provide easy, cheap access to finance, safe and appropriate for unbanked communities, and aims to improve people's capabilities to be able to live more prosperously and get out of the poverty line, while the principle of shari'a aims to prosper the community through the principles of partnership and profit sharing. 12. The concept of partnership is needed by unbanked groups considering the low level of financial literacy, while the concept of mentoring through partnerships will improve the economic conditions of unbanked people so that able to get out of the poverty line. 13. In the OIC Experts Group Workshop on November 5, 2014, Bank Indonesia and OIC member central banks have also discussed a lot about Islamic Financial Inclusion, by utilizing the huge financing potential of sosiai (social finance) activities, including zakat and waqf to accelerate economic development and support financial stability. This needs to be responded by the authority by developing strategies and business models that are able to capture product innovation, processes and distribution channels. 14. Therefore, this seminar is very important as one of the vehicles for us to give birth to or enrich the strategies that can be done. Happy audience, By saying Bismillahhirohmannirrohim, I declare that the national seminar on financial inclusion with the theme "The Role of Islamic Financial Inclusion in Encouraging Economic Development and Poverty Alleviation Efforts" was officially opened. God willing, this seminar can produce strategic thoughts and can be implemented in order to achieve the improvement of the welfare of Muslims in particular and the Indonesian nation by and large. Wabillahitaufik walhidayah, wassalammualaikum warohmatullahhiwabarakatuh Surabaya, 7 November 2014 DR. Halim Alamsyah Deputy Governor
text_original: Sambutan Pembukaan Dr. Halim Alamsyah, Deputi Gubernur Bank Indonesia Seminar Nasional Keuangan Inklusif: "Pentingnya Keuangan Inklusif dalam Meningkatkan Akses Masyarakat dan UMKM terhadap Fasilitas Jasa Keuangan Syariah" Surabaya, 7 November 2014 Bismillahhirrohmannirrohim, Alhamdulillahhirobbil aalamin, asholatuwassholaamuala asyrofil anbiya iwal mursalin wa ala aalihi washohbihi ajmain Yang saya hormati, Pemimpin Kantor Perwakilan Bank Indonesia Surabaya atau yang mewakili Bapak/ibu Pejabat Otoritas Jasa Keuangan baik dari Kantor Pusat maupun Kantor Regional Surabaya Bapak/ibu Pejabat dari Berbagai Kementerian yang hadir dan telah mendukung pelaksanaan kegiatan ini (Kementerian Tenaga Kerja dan Transmigrasi dan BNP2TKI, Kementerian Keuangan, Kementrian Sosial, Kementerian Pertanian, Kementerian Agama, Kementerian Koordinator Perekonomian dan Iain-Iain yang tidak bisa disebutkan satu persatu) Unsur pimpinan daerah provinsi Jawa Timur dan kotamadya Surabaya Bapak/ibu pejabat dari Perbankan nasional dan daerah, Rekan-rekan dari Perguruan Tinggi, Asosiasi, Lembaga Amil Zakat, BMT, Hadirin yang dirakhmati Allah SWT Assalammualaikum warohmatullahhi wabarakatuh Pertama-tama marilah kita panjatkan segala puji dan syukur kepada Allah SWT, atas rakhmat dan karunia Nya, kita semua dapat menghadiri Acara Seminar Nasional Keuangan Inklusif di Kota Surabaya ini. Tak lupa shalawat dan salam kepada Nabi Besar Muhammad SAW beserta keluarga Beliau, para sahabat dan pengikut sampai akhir zaman. Hadirin yang berbahagia, Latar Belakang Kondisi Akses Keuangan Masyarakat di Indonesia 1. Dalam lima tahun terakhir ini pertumbuhan ekonomi Indonesia berada pada kisaran 6%, sebuah pencapaian yang cukup membanggakan di tengah ketidakpastian kondisi perekonomian global. Namun sepertinya manfaat pertumbuhan ini belum begitu berdampak secara merata pada kelompok masyarakat miskin. Meskipun jumlah penduduk miskin mengalami penurunan (data BPS Maret 2014), yakni dari 32 juta jiwa (2009) menjadi 28 juta jiwa (2014), namun delta penurunannya semakin kecil. Salah satu factor yang diidentifikasikan oleh Bl adalah masih rendahnya akses masyarakat kepada layanan keuangan. 2. Berdasarkan Hasil survey neraca rumah tangga Bl (2012), hanya 48% dari total rumah tangga di Indonesia yang memiliki tabungan di bank, lembaga keuangan non bank dan non lembaga keuangan. Dengan kata lain terdapat 52% rumah tangga di Indonesia yang belum memiliki tabungan sama sekali. Hal ini sejalan dengan Survey World Bank (2010) yang menyatakan bahwa di Indonesia, akses terhadap jasa keuangan formal hanya tersedia bagi setengah penduduk Indonesia. 32% dari penduduk Indonesia bahkan tidak memiliki tabungan (baik di sektor formal maupun informal), dan masuk ke dalam kategori financially excluded. 3. Banyak faktor yang melatarbelakangi mengapa masih terdapat kelompok masyarakat yang belum memiliki akses kepada perbankan atau lembaga keuangan, baik dalam bentuk tabungan maupun perolehan kredit. Beberapa diantaranya adalah jarak yang jauh dari tempat tinggal ke kantor bank, produk yang ditawarkan tidak sesuai, informasi produk yang tidak dipahami, pendapatan yang rendah, dokumen identitas yang tidak ada, dan adanya persepsi bahwa bank/lembaga keuangan bukan untuk masyarakat kecil. Dari sisi perbankan juga terdapat kendala diantaranya terkait pendirian kantor cabang dengan segmentasi kepada unbanked people membutuhkan biaya mahal, sehingga bank lebih memilih nasabah besar yang dapat memenuhi persyaratan. Peran Bl dalam Mendorong Keuangan Inklusif di Indonesia 4. Disisi lain kita menyadari bahwa Indonesia memiliki potensi yang besar untuk peningkatan kesejahteraan masyarakat melalui pertumbuhan ekonomi. Untuk itu, sebagaimana umumnya bank sentral di negara berkembang, Bank Indonesia sudah sejak lama terlibat aktif dalam mendorong kegiatan perekonomian termasuk pengembangan UMKM dalam upaya untuk memberantas kemiskinan, baik dengan cara-cara yang konvensional seperti bantuan teknis, pemasaran dan permodalan, juga dengan suatu terobosan yang dicakup dalam Kebijakan Keuangan Inklusif. 5. Keuangan inklusif didefinisikan sebagai upaya yang bertujuan mengurangi segala bentuk hambatan yang bersifat harga maupun non harga, terhadap akses masyarakat dalam memanfaatkan layanan jasa keuangan. Kebijakan tersebut perlu dilakukan secara nasional, melibatkan kementerian, otoritas, dan institusi terkait untuk memperoleh hasil yang optimal. 6. Terkait dengan hal itu, Bl secara aktif bekerjasama dengan Kemenkeu (BKF), OJK, dan Tim Nasional Percepatan Penanggulangan Kemiskinan (TNP2K), berupaya menyusun strategi peningkatan akses keuangan yang komprehensif yaitu, Strategi Nasional Keuangan Inklusif (SNKI) yang merupakan komitmen nasional dan telah di launching Wakil Presiden Rl pada Juni 2012. Dalam implementasinya, SNKI memerlukan dukungan berbagai pihak yaitu kementerian, otoritas, dan institusi atau lembaga terkait termasuk sektor swasta untuk menciptakan kolaborasi dan sinergi dalam rangka mendorong pertumbuhan ekonomi melalui pengentasan kemiskinan dan pemerataan pendapatan sambil tetap menjaga stabilitas sistem keuangan. 7. Dalam kerangka SNKI tersebut, Bank Indonesia berkomitmen penuh dan telah melaksanakan berbagai program dan terobosan antara lain: a. Program Edukasi Keuangan yang bersifat nasional, komprehensif dan berkelanjutan yang bertujuan untuk meningkatkan pengetahuan masyarakat mengenai keuangan. Sasaran dari pelaksanaan edukasi ini adalah pelajar mulai tingkat SD, SMP, SMA sampai mahasiswa, TKI, dan kelompok masyarakat tertentu, a.I. petani, nelayan, pedagang, buruh rumah tangga (homeworkers), masyarakat di wilayah perbatasan dan kepulauan. b. Meningkatkan pemanfaatan TabunganKu terkait dengan Gerakan Indonesia Menabung. Sampai dengan Agustus 2014, tercatat sebanyak 12,34 juta rekening TabunganKU, atau meningkat 1,72 juta rekening (16,2%) dibandingkan posisi akhir tahun 2013. c. Mendorong akses masyarakat di remote area terhubung dengan layanan keuangan melalui implementasi Layanan Keuangan Digital (LKD) untuk agen individu LKD merupakan program terobosan yang bertujuan memperluas akses masyarakat kepada layanan keuangan dengan memanfaatkan teknologi masa kini a.I telepon genggam dan melibatkan jasa agen-agen LKD. LKD menggunakan uang elektronik yang terdaftar (registered e-money) dengan bantuan telepon genggam ataupun kartu (jumlah registered e-money <b1> 2,7 juta). LKD dapat digunakan untuk melakukan pembayaran tagihan atau penarikan tunai bahkan dapat digunakan untuk penyaluran bantuan pemerintah kepada masyarakat (G2P) secara non tunai. d. Pengembangan program G2P (government to person) melalui ujicoba penyaluran Program Keluarga Harapan (PKH) dan bantuan sosial menggunakan Uang Elektronik Program G2P secara resmi telah dimulai melalui peluncuran Kartu Keluarga Sejahtera (KKS), Kartu Indonesia Pintar (KIP), dan Kartu Indonesia Sehat (KIS) oleh Presiden Rl, Joko Widodo tanggal 3 November 2014 di Jakarta. Hal ini sejalan dengan Gerakan Nasional Non Tunai (GNNT) yang dicanangkan Bl yang diharapkan dapat mempercepat implementasi LKD di Indonesia untuk mendukung keuangan inklusif. - Sebelumnya Bl bersama pemerintah juga telah melakukan uji coba penyaluran Bantuan Langsung Tunai Bersyarat kepada peserta Program Keluarga Harapan (PKH) menggunakan Uang Elektronik melalui Agen LKD di DKI Jakarta, Jawa Barat, Jawa Timur dan Nusa Tenggara Timur pada Oktober 2014 lalu. e. Mengembangkan proyek Financial Identity Number (FIN) bertujuan untuk menyediakan database unbanked people yang dapat diakses lembaga keuangan dalam rangka mengurangi assymetric information. Sejaktahun 2012, Bl secara bertahap melakukan pengembangan FIN. Pada tahap awal, telah melakukan pengumpulan data baseline survey dan comprehensive survey, dan hingga saat ini masih terus melakukan upaya penyempurnaan infrastruktur FIN. Dalam pengembangannya ke depan, proyek FIN ini akan mempergunakan basis data e-KTP milik Kemendagri, daftar penerima dana Program Keluarga Harapan dan survei neraca rumah tangga Bl. f. Pemberdayaan UIVIKM melalui pemberian bantuan teknis, produksi dan pemasaran. Bl juga meluncurkan beberapa program inisiatif, diantaranya program kewirausahaan yang bertujuan mendukung Gerakan Kewirausahaan Nasional dalam rangka penciptaan wirausaha baru melalui pendampingan yang berkesinambungan. Sebagaimana kita ketahui, UMKM menjadi salah satu sasaran utama dalam program keuangan inklusif, mengingat peran strategis UMKM dalam perekonomian Indonesia a.I. sebagai kontributor utama PDB (sekitar 57.84%), dan penyerapan 97.2% dari total tenaga kerja Indonesia. Bapak/ibu Hadirin yang berbahagia Potensi Islamic Financial Inclusion di Indonesia 8. Dilihat dari historisnya, lembaga keuangan syariah di Indonesia telah ada sejak 20 tahun yang lalu, yakni ditandai oleh terbitnya Undang-Undang N0.7 Tahun 1992 tentang Perbankan, yang menjadi pintu gerbang berdirinya lembaga keuangan yang beroperasi dengan berlandaskan prinsip-prinsip syariah. 9. Meskipun saat ini pangsa pasar perbankan syariah masih kecil (sekitar 5%), namun Indonesia memiliki potensi yang sangat besar untuk mengembangkan keuangan syariah terutama retail mass banking, tercermin dari jumlah penduduk muslim sebanyak 207 juta jiwa atau mencapai 87% dari seluruh masyarakat Indonesia (Sensus Penduduk BPS, 2010). Potensi tersebut didukung oleh mulai terlihatnya perubahan perilaku dan gaya hidup masyarakat muslim Indonesia, yang semakin aktif mencari produk keuangan yang mampu memberikan bauran manfaatfungsional dan spiritual yang baik. 10. Untuk meningkatkan pangsa pasar keuangan syariah diperlukan upaya yang terintegrasi dalam berbagai bidang, mulai dari inovasi produk, perluasan saluran distribusi, peningkatan pelayanan dan kualitas SDM, strategi komunikasi termasuk program edukasi yang berkesinambungan. Keuangan Inklusif Syariah dan Pengentasan Kemiskinan 11. Keuangan syariah dan kebijakan keuangan inklusif memiliki potensi untuk bersinergi dengan baik mengingat kesamaan konsep yaitu: keuangan inklusif bertujuan memberikan akses keuangan yang mudah, murah, aman dan sesuai bagi masyarakat unbanked, serta bertujuan untuk meningkatkan kapabilitas masyarakat agar mampu hidup lebih sejahtera dan keluar dari garis kemiskinan, sementara prinsip syari'ah bertujuan untuk mensejahterakan masyarakat melalui prinsip partnership dan profit sharing. 12. Konsep partnership sangat dibutuhkan oleh kelompok unbanked mengingat rendahnya tingkat literasi keuangan, sementara konsep pendampingan melalui kemitraan akan meningkatkan kondisi ekonomi masyarakat unbanked sehingga mampu keluar dari garis kemiskinan. 13. Dalam kegiatan Experts Group Workshop OIC pada tanggal 5 November 2014 yang lalu, Bank Indonesia beserta bank sentral anggota OKI juga telah banyak berdiskusi mengenai Islamic Financial Inclusion, dengan memanfaatkan potensi pembiayaan yang sangat besar dari kegiatan sosiai (social finance), diantaranya zakat dan wakaf untuk mempercepat pembangunan ekonomi dan mendukung stabilitas keuangan. Hal ini perlu direspon oleh otoritas dengan penyusunan strategi dan model bisnis yang mampu menangkap inovasi produk, proses maupun saluran distribusi. 14. Oleh karena itu, Seminar ini sangat penting sebagai salah satu wahana bagi kita untuk melahirkan atau memperkaya strategi-strategi yang dapat dilakukan. Hadirin yang berbahagia, Dengan mengucap Bismillahhirohmannirrohim, saya nyatakan Seminar nasional keuangan inklusif dengan tema "Peranan Islamic Financial Inclusion dalam Mendorong Pembangunan Ekonomi dan Upaya Pengentasan Kemiskinan" resmi dibuka. Insya allah Seminar ini dapat menghasilkan pemikiran-pemikiran yang strategis dan dapat diimplementasikan dalam rangka mencapai peningkatan kesejahteraan umat muslim pada khususnya dan Bangsa Indonesia pada umumnya. Wabillahitaufik walhidayah, wassalammualaikum warohmatullahhiwabarakatuh Surabaya, 7 November 2014 DR. Halim Alamsyah Deputi Gubernur

Title: The Transformation of Payment System for Inclusive Growth (Keynote Speech Deputi Gubernur Ronald Waas padaIndonesia Financial Services Summit 2013) Jakarta, 3 September 2013
text: 3 BANK INDONESIA Regulatory Keynote Speech By Ronald Waas Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia At The Indonesia Financial Services summit 2013 "The Transformation of Payment System for Inclusive Growth" Jakarta, September 3rd 2013 Honorable Speakers and Heads of Institutions, Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlement, Good Morning and May God bless us All, Introduction  It is such a great pleasure to be here today in the Indonesian Financial Services Summit 2013. Thank you IDC for excellent arrangements made for this summit. All of you from the networking, the private sector, and business leader are our important partners in achieving national economic integration in financial services.  It is a high time for all of us to enhance the exchange information and cooperation on all issues relating to financial services, especially the payment system. The collaborative and intensive communication among us, such as what we have today is needed, as a new episode of prosperity and opportunity seems to unfold incessantly before us.  I am glad that the Financial Services Summit theme for this year's seminar captures the spirit of the moment, pursuing a growth story in 2014. However, I would like to emphasize that it's not merely pursuing a growth, but a sustainable and inclusive growth. It is in this spirit I would like to share some thought about payment system, the role and transformational step towards sustainable and inclusive growth. The Spirit of inclusive growth  Before I begin, let me share you one inspire thought about the uniqueness spirit of inclusive growth. At a time when half of the world was still in the dark ages, this part of Indonesia, the java island, was already building harmonious religious structures and art. These were represented by two amazing world heritage coming from two different dynasties, a largest Buddhist temple in the world, Borobudur, and one of the biggest Hindu Temple, Prambanan. 1  By the unification of these two amazing temple, central java spirituality and artistic endeavor continues to exist side by side up until now. The two dynasty allusion to create prosperity among society also captures the sense of our dream to have an inclusive growth not only in the economy, but in the mundanities of everyday life.  The questions are What and Why do we need financial services in an inclusive growth? As a country, it's not merely the pace, but the quality of growth that matter the most, and therefore should be addressed together. The pace symbolizes the power to produce and optimize the sources of allocation among the society. Nevertheless, the quality of growth takes it to another level beyond physical appearance in creating a lasting and prosperity for all.  In order to have a quality growth, the implementation of the payment system as the financial system's infrastructure is an important factor to support monetary and financial system stability. It also plays an important role to facilitate economic activity and the business community. Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlement, Lesson Learned from The Crises  After the crises in 1997, many people feared that we are going to suffer and the economy will fade away and took a while before it can begin to stimulate back to normal. Instead, we bounced back a lot more rapidly then people could imagine. We started to grow swiftly by mending the economy that once contracted by 13,5% to made it one of the largest and fastest growing emerging economy.  We also witness the changes in the constellation of the global economy ever since the financial crisis of 2008 had left a profound and widespread anxiety. By mid 2012 we came to realize that the global crisis barely has subsided. Unfortunately, despite signs of a growing global economic recovery, some uncertainties remain very high.  Indonesia is a land of enormous opportunities. Massive population of 240 million people, abundant natural resources, and one of the largest and fastest growing middle class, we have a huge domestic market. For the last decade, Indonesia has been able to make a difference because of our high growth and economic size.  Our economic resilience is inseparable from the strong support of stable macroeconomic conditions and favorable financial system. To maintain conducive financial system, it therefore necessary for the payment system to ensure smoothness, efficiency, and security of economic transaction. The recent financial crisis has emphasized the importance of sound risk management policies and practices in the maintenance of a safe and efficient payment system. 2 Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlement, The Path of Transformational Phase in Payment System: Some Priorities  Bank Indonesia has pursued several payment system policies to enhance the stability of financial system and boosting the implementation of financial inclusion within the society. It lies in four key areas: (1) Investing the sources (people), (2) developing the infrastructure, (3) ensuring the development of payment system by protecting the environment, and (4) be a part of competitive global system.  The first, investing the people. Investing in human capital has and always been an important part of any transformational journey to success. An intensified focus on human resources capacity building will bolster the knowledge depth and needed skilled in the industry.  Secondly, strengthening the infrastructure and continued seeking interconnection infrastructure of existing payment system in an effort to ensure the safety and efficiency of the payment system. The quality of payment systems determines the stability of economy, the efficiency and reliability of intermediation, the possibility for the private sector to innovate and provide new services to consumer.  Some of the infrastructure includes the developing of Bank Indonesia Real Time Gross Settlement (BI-RTGS) and Bank Indonesia Scriptless Securities Settlement System (BI-SSSS), interconnection of retail payment systems through the development of the Gate National Payments (JPN), organizing interconnection of electronic money as well as implementation of the national standard ATM card/chip based debit gradually, and implements Electronic Credit Transfer System among Rural Banks.  The development of second generation is aimed to guarantee that such high level operational effectiveness in the payment system infrastructure ensures the payment and settlement in the financial system. These will also help enhancing banking and financial institution resilience so that they will remain strong and sound in confronting competition.  Payment system should mitigate financial crises by reducing settlement risks. An efficient, secure and reliable payment system reduces the cost of exchanging goods and services, enhances the stability of the financial sector, and expands access to financial services. As the participation of non-bank stakeholders in the clearing system and other formal management structures improving, we need to continue evaluating further domestic access to the National Payment System. 3  We would also need to facilitate access to financial services that is part of financial inclusion. The policy is aimed to promote access of low income community to financial services.  Third, the regulator and the industry need to enhance the supervisory function through better implementation of macro prudential surveillance. These are needed to develop especially in terms of early warning system that the payment system can provide. Learning from our major crises in the last decade, the turbulence has given us guidance on how important the protocol management crisis is.  Furthermore, Bank Indonesia also continues to strengthen legal aspects of the implementation of the payment system in order to ensure consumer protection in using payment system.  Lastly, We should be prepared to be a part of global system. It is always not enough to be a king in our own territory, especially when the definition of territory has been blurred by borderless financial approach. Therefore enhancing communication among our peer countries in the region will be very important as we are facing multifaceted nature of payments system. In order to be competitive, we need to ensure that our system is robust and be competitive to facilitate the regional and international payment system infrastructure integration. Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlement,  The very existence of government at all, infers inequality. As the new equilibrium is on the rise, I believe that the great humanity must come first in the dynamic change of global economy. It is not the size of economy that makes a country flourished, but the spirit of equality that bring the reaped of prosperity worth it.  A national payment system does not only entail settlement between entities, it encompassed the total payment process, which includes all the mechanism, agreements, procedures, rules, and laws that come into play. It is therefore essential that the regulator ensure a safe and smooth, competitive, efficient, and widely used payment system across all levels that lies within the national interest.  As closing remarks, I am delighted that we are here today. I have nothing but high hopes that the lucrative collaborations and thoughts about how payment system role in supporting sustainable and inclusive growth should become an international wisdom in creating a better place for all of us. Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Ronald Waas 4

Title: Speech of the Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Ronald Waas in Educational Wayang Puppet Performance and the MSME Bazaar, Pacitan, 10th October 2015
Subtitle: Educational Wayang Puppet Performance and the MSME Bazaar, Pacitan
text: Speech of the Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Educational Wayang Puppet Performance and the MSME Bazaar Pacitan, 10th October 2015 Distinguished guests: Vice-regent of Pacitan, Seodjono and his delegation; Regional Secretary, Suko Wiyono Komandan Korem, Colonel Czi M. Reza Utama Komandan Kodim, Lieutenant Colonel Yudi Diliyanto Chairman of the Regional Development Planning Agency, Heru Wiwoho Supadi Putra Representatives from Bank Indonesia Bank Indonesia Representative of Region II, Java, Dwi Pranoto Bank Indonesia Representative of East Java, Benny Siswanto Bank Indonesia Representative of Yogyakarta, Arif Budi Laksono Bank Indonesia Representative of Malang, Dudi Herawadi Bank Indonesia Representative of Kediri, Djoko Raharto Ladies and Gentlemen: Good evening, 1. Let me begin my expressing thanks to the Lord God Almighty for bestowing His blessings that we can all congregate here today to witness the charms of the setting sun in the city of Pacitan, nicknamed the city of 1000 caves, and take in the educational puppet performance and MSME bazaar. 2. I have noted four main activities to make this a seminal moment for the residents of Pacitan, local government and Bank Indonesia alike. The activities include socialising the characteristics of genuine rupiah banknotes (CIKUR), enforcing mandatory rupiah utilisation, launching the national Non-Cash Movement (GNNT) as well as arranging the MSME bazaar to introduce and promote the leading commodities of Pacitan. 3. The range of activities will reinforce Bank Indonesias efforts to strengthen the role and function of domestic representative offices, particularly in terms of the payment system, namely to boost the efficacy of cash and non-cash payment system services, while safeguarding the availability of currency fit for circulation, especially in remote and border areas. Ladies and Gentlemen: 4. One task of Bank Indonesia in terms of rupiah management is to determine rupiah authenticity. To that end, Bank Indonesia constantly strives to provide the public insightful information concerning the characteristics of genuine rupiah banknotes. It is clear that such an activity cannot be successfully achieved alone but requires the help of all those involved, including the local community. 5. The phrase Tak kenal maka tak sayang" also applies to the rupiah, the official currency of our beloved Republic of Indonesia. Recognising genuine rupiah currency is becoming increasingly important in the fight against counterfeit money, the consequences of which are harmful to the public. 6. Socialising the characteristics of genuine rupiah banknotes is achieved through various media, through formal meetings on education, bazaars and other communication media, including local culture, such as the puppet show we are set to enjoy this evening. Activities such as this also represent a tangible form of cooperation between local governments and Bank Indonesia to provide consumer protection against counterfeit money in circulation. Ladies and Gentlemen: 7. Enforcing mandatory rupiah utilisation within the territory of the Republic of Indonesia is a joint endeavour to preserve the rupiah as a symbol of sovereignty of the Republic of Indonesia. 8. I would like to relay an analogy on nationality delivered by Jokowi in his inaugural address as President of the Republic of Indonesia. In a maritime context, he stated we have turned our backs on the oceans for too long. Indonesia must determine its own destiny as a maritime nation. 9. With respect to rupiah enforcement, we especially do not want to hear a future President of the Republic of Indonesia say We have turned our backs on the rupiah for too long. 10. I would also like to remind everyone of an important note from our recent history as a lesson, namely the territorial dispute centred on the islands of Sipadan and Ligitan. One consideration of the international community when awarding the islands to Malaysia was the minimal number of transactions and economic activity on the islands that actually used the rupiah. 11. In terms of the economy, we have all felt the pressures constantly experienced by the rupiah. Furthermore, a high number of domestic transactions using the dollar is one trigger of rupiah depreciation. We have noted that transactions between residents using dollars to purchase goods and services on the domestic market have become dominant, accounting for more than 50%. 12. Widespread use of foreign currencies has escalated depreciatory pressures on the rupiah and left our economy exposed to shocks. Therefore, I urge all of you in attendance to love the rupiah; to make the rupiah a proud host of its own nation. International and domestic confidence in the rupiah will bolster national economic resilience, giving the rupiah prestige at home and abroad. Ladies and Gentlemen: 13. As the payment system authority, Bank Indonesias mission is to realise secure, efficient and uninterrupted cash and non-cash payment systems. In terms of the noncash payment system, Bank Indonesia is currently striving towards a Less Cash Society (LCS), where residents favour non-cash payment instruments. To that end, Bank Indonesia launched the National Non-Cash Movement (GNNT) in August 2014. 14. GNNT is vital to realise a more efficient economy with good governance in terms of financial management amongst the public, business community and government institutions. Program efficacy will be boosted through synergy with government programs throughout Indonesia and the expected implementation of e-government and e-payment. 15. Micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) are no less important, representing a leading pillar of the Indonesian economy. The MSME sector contributes 57.8% of GDP, absorbs 97.7% of the labour force and accounts for 99.9% of all business units in Indonesia. 16. Over the past five years, Indonesia has been one of the very few countries in the world that has consistently achieved economic growth in the 6% range. Such tenacious economic resilience stems from a large domestic demand base, supported by a flourishing middle class as well as micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to keep the wheels of the economy turning. 17. Notwithstanding, against an increasingly dynamic global economic backdrop and tighter competition, the role of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) needs to be transformed to strengthen the competitiveness of local leading products. 18. Therefore, the MSME bazaar here today is expected to motivate MSME advocates to become more productive and innovative in terms of product marketing, to fix the distribution channels as well as to create a more conducive climate in Pacitan and the environs. 19. Through a combination of financial education for students and the public, socialisation of genuine rupiah characteristics, the non-cash campaign and the MSME bazaar, we hope to improve public understanding in Pacitan of the financial system and payment system, thereby supporting financial system stability as well as a secure, efficient and smooth payment system. Ladies and Gentlemen: 20. Before closing, I would like to extend my appreciation to the Pacitan Government, banking industry and residents for your attendance here today, support and cooperation with Bank Indonesia to ensure this event was a success. 21. Kindly enjoy the puppet performance, which I hope will benefit us all and provide value added. The Lord God Almighty is always by our side, blessing our endeavours towards a brighter future. Thank you. Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Ronald Waas

Title: Speech Of Deputy Governor Of Bank Indonesia, Ronald Waas, Concerning Cooperation Between Bank Indonesia And Ministry Of Law And Human Rights Independence Enhancement Of Correctional Prisoners And Clients In Class IIA Correctional Facility Of Palangkaraya,
Subtitle: Independence Enhancement Of Correctional Prisoners And Clients In Class IIA Correctional Facility Of Palangkaraya
text: SPEECH OF DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF BANK INDONESIA CONCERNING COOPERATION BETWEEN BANK INDONESIA AND MINISTRY OF LAW AND HUMAN RIGHTS INDEPENDENCE ENHANCEMENT OF CORRECTIONAL PRISONERS AND CLIENTS IN CLASS IIA CORRECTIONAL FACILITY OF PALANGKARAYA Palangkaraya, 6 March 2015 The honorable,  Minister of Law and Human Rights of RI, Mr. DR. Yasonna Hamonangan, SH, M.Si, and staff of the Ministry of Law and Human Rights RI,  Governor of Central Kalimantan Province, Mr. A. Teras Narang, SH, the staff and the Regional Work Unit of Central Kalimantan Province,  Chairman of DPRD (Regional Parliament) of Central Kalimantan Province,  Regional Leadership of Communication Forum elements of Central Kalimantan Province,  Regencies/Mayors of Central Kalimantan,  Head of Regional Office of Ministry of Law and Human Rights, Central Kalimantan Province,  Head of KPw BI of Central Kalimantan Province, Mr. Muhamad Nur,  Head of Correctional Facility/Penitentiary of Central Kalimantan,  Banking Leaders,  Rectors of Universities and Academicians  Fellow Entrepreneurs and Associations,  Mass Media Leaders and Journalists,  Invitees and Attendees. Good Morning and Greetings to us all, 1. To begin this morning speech, please allow me to ask all attendees to praise our gratitude to God the Almighty, for His grace and blessing in this opportunity, where we together can be present in this Beautiful city as the nickname of Palangkaraya, in order to realize a cooperation between Ministry of Law and Human Rights RI and Bank Indonesia in the Page 1 of 6 Independence Enhancement of Correctional Prisoners and Clients in IIA Correctional Facility of Palangkaraya. 2. This cooperation is intended to enhance capabilities and skills, to encourage independence of correctional prisoners/inmates and clients, to support regional inflation control through demplot (demonstration plot) of commodities of crops and horticulture contributors of inflation, or other commodities that can support the regional economy, and also support the strengthening of food resilience through food diversification with cluster replication. 3. This cooperation program is at once a derivative from the memorandum of understanding between Ministry of Law and Human Rights and Bank Indonesia signed in 28 October 2014. 4. We welcome and express our gratitude to the Government of Central Kalimantan Province that has facilitated the implementation of cooperation program between the Ministry of Law and Human Rights and Bank Indonesia. I also would like to convey our appreciation to the Kanwil (Regional Office) of Ministry of Law and Human Rights of Central Kalimantan Province as well as Correctional Facility of Class IIA, Palangkaraya, upon their cooperation with the Representative Office (KPw) of Bank Indonesia of Central Kalimantan Province in rolling this program. As individuals and a Member of the Board of Governors of Bank Indonesia, I welcome the initiative of this program, as it has many positive values both from social and economic aspects. 5. We see that this cooperation between Bank Indonesian and the Ministry of Law and Human Rights is not only important, but also has a noble meaning. Macro wise, the enhancement of prisoners independence is a part of our efforts to build the nation, since development, essentially, must involve all elements of the society, as what we do today. Micro wise, this independence enhancement is a process to prepare the prisoners, so that when they are free later, they can live independently and improve the quality of relationship with their family and also with the society. Ladies and Gentlemen, and attendees, 6. In accordance with Law No. 23 Year 1999, as amended lastly with the Law No. 6 Year 2009, Bank Indonesia is the central bank which has been given mandate to realize the stability of Rupiah value. In the context of domestic internal balance, a stable Rupiah shall be reflected by the controlled price level in general or known as inflation. 7. To achieve the target of inflation is certainly not easy, and in guarding the inflation, Bank Indonesia cannot do it alone. Therefore, it requires more or extra efforts to control the Page 2 of 6 sources of inflationary pressures, i.e., by involving cooperation, coordination, and synergy with the central and regional governments, economic actors and the public at large. 8. Inflation or Price Stability in general is a very vital component for economic development of a nation. First, low inflation will be able to enhance competitiveness of the economy, both at the regional level and national level. Second, low inflation will be able to help us in reducing poverty level, as it directly related to the buying power of the society. 9. Poverty will be suppressed rapidly if inflation on foodstuffs group can be controlled. The effect of food inflation to poverty level can occur, considering the poor spends their income more for food and foodstuffs. The study of Banerjee (2009) in various countries indicates that around 56% up to 78% consumption of less advantaged communities were used to buy food. Ladies and Gentlemen, attendees, 10. As we all know, the inflation of fluctuating foodstuff group or known as volatile food, is one of the primary contributors of inflation in Indonesia. The profile of Indonesia as archipelago which is vulnerable to natural disaster both from tectonic and volcanic earthquake, to a sharp climate change can easily disturb foodstuff supplies. Therefore, inflation pressure from this component of volatile food is more vulnerable in Indonesia. 11. With that consideration, regional food commodity development needs to be improved, so that each region is able to be self-reliant on their food needs, and even able to become a food self-sufficiency region. 12. In our observation, the role of Central Kalimantan seen from the economic growth in general is relatively good. This is reflected by the growth rate of 6.21% (yoy) in 2014, higher than the national economic growth estimated at 5.02%, and it was the highest economic growth compared to the other provinces in Kalimantan. However, I am convinced that the excellent growth can be further optimized to encourage its contribution at national level, or in improving the welfare of the Central Kalimantan community. 13. In line with the performance of its economic growth, Central Kalimantan also has an inflation rate that tends to be stable and low. In 2014, inflation rate in Central Kalimantan was 7.07% (yoy), or lower compared to the national inflation of 8.36% (yoy) and also was the lowest inflation compared to the other provinces in Kalimantan. The lower rate of inflation certainly is a potential supporter that can enhance the acceleration of economic growth in Central Kalimantan. 14. In order to strengthen food resilience and to enhance supplies of the said foodstuff group, Bank Indonesia through its Representative Office and in cooperation with the local Page 3 of 6 stakeholders has developed food resilient cluster, focusing on food commodities to support inflation control, such as rice, red chili, beef, shallot and garlic. 15. And since last year, we also established cooperation with the Ministry of Law and Human Rights to empower correctional prisoners and clients in Correctional Facilities, by utilizing land of the concerned Correctional Facility in the development of food resilient commodities. Ladies and Gentlemen, attendees, 16. The cooperation of the Ministry of Law and Human Rights and Bank Indonesia for the enhancement of prisoners independence had already been initiated its implementation in the KPw of Bank Indonesia in West Kalimantan Province, which was also conducted in cooperation with the Class IIA Correctional Facility of Pontianak. 17. This program has already been running well, among others through the implementation of skills training facilitated by Bank Indonesia. The inmates have been able to make a demplot of shallots and horticulture cultivation, tilapia and catfish aquaculture, to produce coconut coir mats which in the future will be directed to meet the need of the local hospitality industry, and also to produce banana chips with various innovation in taste and processing. Even, wooden mats produced by the Inmates in Class IIA Pontianak had already penetrated the export market. 18. Other than technical skills training, Bank Indonesia also provides entrepreneurship training using business incubator approach, so that the prisoners are expected to have comprehensive knowledge to start business, production, marketing, financial and also networking. The training is also expected to motivate and change the mindset of the prisoners, that they are able to become entrepreneurs. 19. We see that the success of the program in West Kalimantan needs to be spread to other areas, surely, by still considering the unique characteristic of the area in question. I am very happy to hear various progresses and development of cooperation programs conducted by the Kanwil of the Ministry of Law and Human Rights of Central Kalimantan, KPw Bank Indonesia, and Correctional Facility of Palangkaraya. We need to welcome and support extensive cooperation program and type of activities which are conducted creatively, so as to be able to give benefits in accordance with the community needs. Attendees, Ladies and Gentlemen, 20. Having the status of ex-prisoners brings consequences of its own for the inmates, starting from self-adjustment to return to the family and the community, to the need of finding a Page 4 of 6 job. Therefore, guidance or coaching to the prisoners is required absolutely, so that after they are free they can start a better new life for their future. 21. As citizens that still have productive potency for nation building, we believe that the prisoners need to be equipped with certain skills and entrepreneurship, so that they can live independently and provide contribution in the development. 22. The efforts of mental development and skills training certainly must be conducted in a planned and systematic way. Equipped with the above, it is expected that after finished serving their sentences, the ex-prisoners are able to diffuse again and even contribute positively in the community, to become human beings useful for the community, the country and the nation. 23. I expect that the model of independence enhancement of correctional prisoners and clients that will be implemented through the synergy of Ministry of Law and Human Rights and Bank Indonesia becomes an inspiration for coaching prisoners in Indonesia, tools for prisoners to survive and their responsibilities in the national development through active roles in the community, when they have finished serving their sentences. 24. Therefore, supports from all parties both in central and regional are very much expected for the success of the program. We also will continue to develop similar model in the 41 Representative Offices of Bank Indonesia through cooperation with the local Correctional Facility, which is expected to support the efforts of food self-sufficiency and the national entrepreneurship movement proclaimed by the Government. Attendees, 25. The program of Independence Enhancement of Correctional Prisoners and Clients is one of the example forms of synergy between institutions or agencies in Central Kalimantan. We believe that with the maintained synergy, the sustainability of this program will run properly. In the future, the program will continue to be developed and it is expected to be applied immediately to all Correctional Facilities in Indonesia. 26. With this speech, I at once open the program of Training of Trainers (ToT), which will be participated by the heads and officials of Correctional Facility/Penitentiary of Central Kalimantan. This training is expected to equip the Heads & Officials of the Correctional Facility/Penitentiary with several matters related to entrepreneurship and motivation, so that the program replication target of independence enhancement of correctional inmates & clients can be realized sooner, as the same understanding has already created on the benefits of the program. Page 5 of 6 27. Thus, that is all that I can convey. May God the Almighty always bless our steps in enhancing the independence of the correctional inmates and clients. Thank you. Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Ronald Waas Page 6 of 6

Title: Closing Remarks Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia, Ronald Waas at The 17th Technical Meeting of Mints in Asean (TEMAN) Conference, Yogyakarta, 12 June 2015
text: CLOSING REMARKS DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF BANK INDONESIA THE 17th TECHNICAL MEETING OF MINTS IN ASEAN {TEMAN) CONFERENCE Yogyakarta, 12 June 2015 Excellencies, Distinguished speakers, Honorable guests, Ladies and gentlemen, Good morning and may God bless us all, 1. First of all, I would like to invite all of you to join me in expressing thanks and praises to God Almighty, who has blessed us with the opportunity to come here together at The 17th Technical Meeting of Mints in ASEAN (TEMAN) Conference in two beautiful cities, Jakarta and Yogyakarta, that has started on Monday, June Th, 2015 and will be closed today on Friday, June 12th , 2015. 2. On behalf of Bank Indonesia, I would like to extend our gratitude for the honor that all of you have given to participate in this conference. I believe that many of you have to travel a long distance, and spend your valuable times in order to be here at this conference, to share ideas, perspectives and knowledge in what we believed to be very fruitful discussions during this 5 days seminar. 3. I would also like to express my gratitude to The Indonesian Government Security Printing and Minting Corporation (Peruri), who has organized this conference excellently. Distinguished Ladies and Gentlemen, 4. I feel so glad that at the end of the day the conference that involving important people in central bank, printing and minting company, and also industrial company as partners, all of you, has gone successfully. It is because the contribution and participation with heart that all of you have given during the conference. 5. I believed that all of the presentations delivered by the speakers, and also the information, knowledge, experiences, inputs, and views that was shared and discussed formally inside this conference room, or even discussed informally outside of this room by all of us here during this 5 days seminar, will be an enrichment to our knowledge, while giving us new insights about the coins management. 6. I am convinced that those valuable inputs will be greatly used in developing the central banks, or issuing authorities regarding the currency policy, especially the ones related to currency operation, design, quality, distribution, and processing, which at the end will bring the central banks or issuing authorities to be more credible. Ladies and gentlement 7. George Bernard Shaw, an Irish novelist, short story writer, and a co-founder of the London School of Economics who received the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1925 said, "Progress is impossible without change, and those who cannot change their minds cannot change anything". I believed that organizations must continue to evolve to keep up with changes in order to survive and continue to grow in this dynamic world. 8. Bank Indonesia is currently running a transformation program which is based on the Architecture of Bank Indonesia Strategic Function (AFSBI) 2024. The architecture is developed to enhance the strength and dexterity of Bank Indonesia in dealing with the implication of dynamics of change, and a medium-long term challenge especially in monetary, finance and economy whether it is global, regional and national. 9. Important areas of substance that will be the scopes of transformation are : i) the functions of monetary; ii) financial system stability including macro-prudential; iii) the functions of payment system; iv) supporting internal capabilities; iv) and also the enforcement of coordination mechanism with partner institutions. 10. This Transformation Program will accelerate the pace of Bank Indonesia to enhance its ability in controlling inflation, and to support the achievement of Financial System Stability. This Transformation Program will also enhance Bank Indonesia innovation in the areas of Payment System and Currency Management. 11. With regard to currency management, transformation program is focused to encourage 3 (three) pillars of Bank Indonesia's currency management. First pillar, The availability, realiability and quality of cash; second pillar, The cash distribution and cash processing which are optimum and secure; and third pillar, The excellence cash services. Distinguished participants, 12. Indonesia is an archipelago comprising approximately 17,000 islands, about 6,000 of which are inhabited, scattered along the equator covering a vast land area of nearly 1.9 million square kilometers. With nearly 2 50 million in population, vary in ethnics and tribes, Indonesia is considered as one of the most populous country in the world. Along with its geographical and demographical features, Indonesia is considered as one of the emerging market economies of the world with an average economic growth of 5% - 6% per annum. 13. In its capacity as central bank, Bank Indonesia is in charge of regulating and ensuring a smooth payment system which includes both non-cash and cash payment instruments. For cash payment instruments, Bank Indonesia currency management policy is built around its mission to fulfill public needs for banknotes and coins in terms of amount and denomination in a timely manner, fit for circulation condition and safe from counterfeiting. 14. In Indonesian case and maybe the same to other ASEAN countries, the usage of cash for everyday transactions is still high despite the steadily increased trend of less cash society. In line with the positive economic and population growth of Indonesia, the currency in circulation also increases with an average of 15% - 20% per year. For your information, by the end of 2014, the currency in circulation reached the total amount of 528,5 trillion Rupiah or equivalen with USD 40,6 billion, with number of banknotes and coins circulated amounting 15,3 billion and 17, 1 billion respectively. 2 15. As mandated by the Currency Act No. 7/2011, Bank Indonesia appoints the state owned printing company, Peruri, to carry out the printing of Indonesian banknotes and coins. Every year, Bank Indonesia asks Perum Peruri to print and mint banknotes/coins based on the estimation which is addressing the macro economic assumptions such as economic growth (GDP), inflation, exchange rate and interest rate. Ladies and gentlement, 16. Regarding with the coin currency, in general, almost all countries in the world have the same problems in terms of coins recirculation. For your information in Indonesian case, during 2014, Bank Indonesia has issued coins as many as 1,6 billion pieces with nominal value of 776,7 billion Rupiah. As for 2015, since January until May 2015, Bank Indonesia has issued coins as many as 487 million pieces with a nominal value of 234,05 billion Rupiah. Nevertheless, the amount of coins that came back to Bank Indonesia only reached 8% - 10% of total coins issued each year. 17. Although the coins have been issued and circulated in large numbers by Bank Indonesia, but there are still complaints in society regarding a lack of coins. Therefore Bank Indonesia continues to make improvements in the management of coins, including appealed to the public good as well as the banking industry to utilize coins optimally. In addition, Bank Indonesia together with the related partner institutions such as Peruri, will also continue to coordinate and cooperate to make coins management becomes better and better. Dear guests, ladies and gentlement, 18. We are approaching to the end of the 17th TEMAN conference, I was little bit indecisive whether I am going through all the traditional way of conference to give you a summary, or give a summing up the whole discussion in the last one, and give my several salient points, and try to gather all comments from all the distinguished guest speakers at this forum, but then I decided not to do so. I know all of you or some of us want to do a city tour, to enjoy the beautiful and exotic scenery of Yogyakarta. 19. In this occasion, let me encourage you to make the best of your stay here in Yogyakarta, one of the major tourist destinations in Indonesia. Yogyakarta is known for showcasing Javanese culture and history, and also home to invaluable historical sites and spectacular period architecture. In Yogyakarta, we have the largest budhist temple in the world "Borobudur" that was built in 8th - 9th century, and the largest hinduist temple in Indonesia "Prambanan" that was built in 9th century, and also we have the royal palace "Kraton Yogyakarta". 20. Beside that, in this ancient city you can also enjoy the stunning cultural dance performance, celebrate the arts, or go visit a batik or silver-smithing workshop. I do hope that you will experience an unforgettable memories during your stay here in our beautiful country. 21. So finally, I wish you a safe and pleasant journey back to your homes. May God Almighty be with you throughout your journey. 22. Good morning, and with that I close this conference officially. Thank you, thank you, thank you. 3 Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Ronald Waas

Title: Speech of the Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Ronald Waas at Seminar on Non-Cash Services for Wakaf, Infak and Shadaqah Payments, Surabaya, 30th October 2015
Subtitle: Seminar on Non-Cash Services for Wakaf, Infak and Shadaqah Payments
text: Speech of the Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Seminar on Non-Cash Services for Wakaf, Infak and Shadaqah Payments Surabaya, 30th October 2015 Distinguished speakers: o Pungky P. Wibowo, Head of the Electronification and Financial Inclusion Program, o Sepyan Uhyandi, SEVP of Bank Rakyat Indonesia, o Andy Kristianto, SVP of Business Planning at Telkomsel, o Muhammad Taufik, Director of Yayasan Dana Sosial Al-Falah Payment system industry players, Leaders of pesantren, Leaders and employees from Bank Indonesia Ladies and Gentlemen: Good morning, 1. Let me begin my expressing thanks to the Lord God Almighty for bestowing His blessings that we can all congregate here today for this seminar on Non-Cash Services for Wakaf, Infak and Shadaqah Payments. 2. This event is part of the 2015 Indonesia Sharia Economic Festival (ISEF), which is an annual event organised by Bank Indonesia since 2014. 3. I sincerely expect this seminar to facilitate constructive and interactive discussions, along with information sharing, thereby broadening insight and enriching the knowledge of us all, particularly in the area of non-cash services as well as advancing implementation amongst Muslim communities in Indonesia. Ladies and Gentlemen: 4. At several recent socialisation events with industry players and the public, I have cited a quote from the early 19th Century by an American author named James F. Cooper, The very existence of government at all, infers inequality. The real essence of authority is to manage socioeconomic imbalances in the public interest. 5. In the context of the payment system, we feel the adage expressed by James F. Cooper should be taken into consideration by Bank Indonesia when formulating policy. 6. The complexity of social diversity, accompanied by rapid technological development, has made the control of the authorities over society increasingly strategic, especially in terms of creating a payment system that is actually secure, uninterrupted and efficient. Ladies and Gentlemen: 7. As the payment system authority, the mission of Bank Indonesia is to Manage and Maintain a Secure, Efficient and Uninterrupted Payment System and Currency Management through broader access in the national interest. 8. We will accomplish the mission through two salient approaches, namely by strengthening the payment system and also by proactively pioneering cooperation and collaboration. 9. We have translated strengthening the payment system into four pillars as follows: (i) an effective and efficient currency management system; (ii) large-scale payment electronification; (iii) reliable and secure payment infrastructure; and (iv) rigorous supervision and oversight. 10. In terms of expanding payment electronification, one non-cash vision of Bank Indonesia is to foster a Less Cash Society, where the public has a greater propensity for non-cash payment instruments. 11. The realisation of a less cash society is pivotal in the creation of a more efficient economy, while also enhancing aspects of financial management governance amongst the public, business community and government institutions. 12. As a form of BI commitment to promoting non-cash transactions, Bank Indonesia initiated the National Non-Cash Movement (GNNT) in August 2014, through Memorandums of Understanding (MoU) between Bank Indonesia, the Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, local government as well as provincial government associations throughout Indonesia. Ladies and Gentlemen: 13. According to the most recent national census conducted by BPS-Statistics Indonesia in 2010, Muslims account for around 87% of the total population, making Indonesia the most populous Muslim country in the world. 14. Unfortunately, however, the dominant Muslim population in Indonesia remains unsupported by the weak market penetration of the Islamic banking industry, accounting for just 4.7% of the banking industry in Indonesia as of August 2015. 15. We firmly believe that many Muslim communities in Indonesia remain unbanked. On the other hand, demand for retail transactions amongst the Muslim public is increasing, especially for wakaf, infak and shadaqah payments. 16. Consequently, we feel that the development of non-cash services to broaden access to financial services in Muslim communities is inevitable. 17. Congruous with the financial inclusion policy of Bank Indonesia, we have also prepared an Islamic Financial Inclusion (IFI) strategy as part of the grand design to expand financial access. IFI serves to extend the Digital Financial Services (DFS) ecosystem through participation of the informal sector, including the Islamic Centre, mosque networks as well as Islamic boarding schools (pesantren) and their respective business units. 18. The informal sector plays a decisive role in creating public interest for the non-cash services available, while slowly persuading the public to try the available services. 19. Furthermore, public willingness to open up and try financial transactions will serve as a strategic entry point to offer financial education, particularly on non-cash transactions, towards a technology/digital-based economy. Looking ahead, the public is not only expected to master financial transactions but also master reliable financial management. Ladies and Gentlemen: 20. We focused on three main aspects when developing the non-cash concept to support Islamic financial transactions. First, develop non-cash instruments/services in compliance with Islamic principles and tailored to the characteristics of the Muslim population. 21. Second, pursue innovation-driven development and third, support the e-payment ecosystem to maintain the sustainability of non-cash payment services that make financial transactions more accessible and efficient. 22. Consequently, non-cash services are expected to facilitate more efficient Islamic financial transactions, including wakaf, infak and shadaqah, while adhering to sharia principles. Furthermore, the availability of non-cash payment services for wakaf, infak and shadaqah payments is also expected to expand public knowledge and experience of non-cash transactions. 23. As a tangible outcome of our efforts to provide non-cash services to the Muslim population, we are launching Digital Financial Services (DFS) today at pesantren through collaboration with telecommunications companies and Islamic boarding schools (pesantren). We sincerely hope that DFS will be expanded through the participation of other pesantren. 24. We also expect the full support of all parties to ensure the implementation of non-cash services in sharia retail transactions is a success. Through transparent communication, intensive coordination and synergic collaboration between Bank Indonesia, the Government, relevant authorities, amil zakat institutions, pesantren and payment system players we expect public awareness and uptake of non-cash services to proliferate. 25. In closing, I would like to express my sincere appreciation to all attendees for their active participation and support of this seminar for the mutual benefit of us all. Thank you. Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Ronald Waas

Title: Sambutan Deputi Gubernur Bank Indonesia Ronald Waas dalam Seminar Layanan Non Tunai Untuk Pembayaran Wakaf, Infak Dan Shadaqah, Surabaya, 30 Oktober 2015
text: REMARKS BY THE DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF BANK INDONESIA SEMINAR ON NON-CASH SERVICES FOR WAQF, INFAK AND SHADAQAH PAYMENTS SURABAYA, 30 OCTOBER 2015 Which we respect, A Seminar Speaker: 95 Mr. Pungky P. Wibowo, Head of BI Electronification and Financial Inclusion Program, 95 Mr. Sepyan Uhyandi, SEVP of Bank Rakyat Indonesia, 95 Mr. Andy Kristianto, SVP Bussiness Planning Telkomsel, 95 Mr. Muhammad Taufik, Administrator of Al-Falah Social Fund Foundation, J Indonesian Payment System Industry Player, J Leaders of Islamic Boarding Schools, J Leaders and Employees of Bank Indonesia, as well as A Happy Audience and Invitees. Morning and Greetings to all of us 1. Starting this morning's remarks, I would like to invite the audience to express praise and gratitude to the presence of God Almighty, because only for His approval, on this occasion we can be present in good health, in order to take part in the Seminar "Non-Cash Services for Waqf, Infak, and Shadaqah Payments". 2. This event is part of the series of activities of the Indonesia Sharia Economic Festival 2015, which is an annual agenda of Bank Indonesia since it was first started in 2014. 3. In this seminar, it is hoped that an interactive and constructive discussion will be created, accompanied by sharing information and views, so that in the end it will add insight and enrich the treasures of science for all of us, especially regarding cashless services and the development of their implementation for the Muslim community in Indonesia. Ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen whom we respect, 4. On several occasions socializing with industry players and the wider community, I often quote the ucapan of one of America's most famous writers in the early 19th century, James F. Cooper, who said "The very existence of government at all, infers inequality". The most essential essence of the existence of authority is, to guarantee that the imbalance of social and economic institutions that occur in society, can be managed for the benefit of society at large. 5. In the context of the payment system, we consider that the adagium expressed by James F. Cooper should be considered by Bank Indonesia in formulating a policy. 6. The complexity of today's social plurality, which is accompanied by the rapid dynamics of the development of digital technology, causes the control of authority as a control tool to regulate the order of people's lives in the increasingly strategic, in particular to achieve a truly secure, smooth, and efficient payment system. Ladies and Gentlemen, Ladies and Gentlemen whom we respect, 7. As the payment system authority, Bank Indonesia's mission is to Manage and Maintain a safe, efficient and smooth Payment System and Money Management, through expanding access and considering national interest. 8. We will achieve this mission through two important aspects, namely the first: strengthening the Payment System, and second: active homework in pioneering cooperation and collaboration. 9. In terms of strengthening the Payment System, we describe it through four pillars, namely first: Effective and Efficient Money Management System, second: Expansion of Payment Electronification, ketiqa: Paymentinfrastructure is reliable and secure, and the fourth pillar is Strong and Sharp Supervision and Oversight {Rigorous}. 10. Regarding the Expansion of Payment Electronification, one of Bank Indonesia's visions in the non-cash sector is to realize a society that has a high preference in using payment instruments and facilities. non-cash in making transactions, or what is known as the Less Cash Society. 11. The realization of the Less Cash Society is important to encourage a more efficient economy, as well as improve governance aspects in financial management by the community, business people and institutions government. 12.
