As a form of Bank Indonesia's commitment to encourage an increase in non-cash transactions, in August 2014 Bank Indonesia initiated the launching of the National Non-Cash Movement (GNNT), which was marked by the signing of a Memorandum of Note Agreementbetween Bank Indonesia and the Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, Regional Governments, and the Association of Provincial Governments throughout Indonesia. Ladies and Gentlemen, Ladies and Gentlemen whom we respect, 13. Based on the terakhir population census conducted by the Central Statistics Agency in 2010, the Muslim population in Indonesia reaches 87%, which is spread throughout the archipelago. 14. But unfortunately, the existence of the Muslim population as the majority in Indonesia has not been supported by the penetration of Islamic banking in facilitating public financial transactions. This condition is due to the low share of Islamic banking in Indonesia, which was 4.7% as of August 2015. 15. We believe that there are still many Muslim residents in Indonesia who are unbanked. Meanwhile, on the other hand, the need for retail financial transactions among the Muslim community is increasing, especially for waqf, infak and shadaqah payments. 16. Observing these factors, we consider that the development of cashless services as part of efforts to expand financial access among Muslims, is a necessity. 17. Within the framework of Bank Indonesia's financial inclusion policy, we have developed an Islamic Financial Inclusion (IFI) strategy, as part of the grand design of expanding financial access. IFI can play a role as a means of expanding the Digital Financial Services (LKD) ecosystem, through the role of the informal sector such as islamic centers, mosque networks, and Islamic boarding schools including u nit units a business owned by a pesantren. 18. The informal sector has a big role in creating public interest in the non-cash services available, and slowly begins to get to know and then try to transact with dimaks services ud. 19. In addition, the willingness of the public to open up and try financial transactions is expected to be a strategic entry point for conducting financial education, especially related to non-transaction transactions. cash that leads to a techno-based economy. In the future, people are expected to not only be proficient in financial transactions, but also have reliable financial management. Ladies and Gentlemen, Ladies and Gentlemen whom we respect, 20. In developing the cashless concept to support Islamic financial transactions , we focus on three main aspects. First, the development of non-cash instruments/services is carried out by referring to sharia principles, and in accordance with the characteristics ofthe Muslim community. 21. Second, development is carried out based on innovation as an {innovative driven) motor. And ketiqa, the support of the e-payment ecosystem is an important factor to maintain the sustainability of non-cash services, because it can make keuangan transactions more accessible and efficient. 22. With these three aspects, it is hoped that non-cash services will be able to facilitate Islamic financial transactions including Waqf, Infak and Shadaqah, to be more efficient but still in accordance with the principles sharia. Furthermore, the provision of non-cash services for waqf, infak and Shadaqah payments is expected to increase people's understanding and experience in non-cash transactions. Ladies and Gentlemen, Ladies, and Ladies and Gentlemen whom we respect, 23. As a tangible manifestation of our efforts in facilitating cashless payment transactions for the Muslim community segment, at noon today, the launching of LKD will be carried out at islamic boarding schools, which is a collaboration between islamic boarding schools and telecommunications companies. We hope that the implementation in the future will be further expanded, by involving other islamic boarding school communities. 24. Furthermore, we expect support from all relevant parties in order to succeed in implementing cashless services for Sharia retail transactions. Through good communication, intensive coordination, and synergistic collaboration between Bank Indonesia, the Government, relevant authorities, amyl zakat institutions, Islamic boarding schools and payment system industry players, we believe that public awareness and willingness to use non-cash services in accordance with sharia principles in daily economic activities will increase. 25. Before concluding this remark, let me thank you to you, ladies and gentlemen all who have been willing to spend the precious time they have, to attend this morning's seminar. Hopefully, with the active participation and contributions made during this seminar, it can ultimately bring benefits to all of us. Happy seminar, thank you. Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Ronald Waas
text_original: (c) BANK INDONESIA SAMBUTAN DEPUTI GUBERNUR BANK INDONESIA SEMINAR LAYANAN NON TUNAI UNTUK PEMBAYARAN WAKAF, INFAK DAN SHADAQAH SURABAYA, 30 OKTOBER 2015 Yang kami hormati, J Para Pembicara Seminar: <95> Bp. Pungky P. Wibowo, Kepala Program Elektronifikasi dan Keuangan Inklusif BI, <95> Bp. Sepyan Uhyandi, SEVP Bank Rakyat Indonesia, <95> Bp. Andy Kristianto, SVP Bussiness Planning Telkomsel, <95> Bp. Muhammad Taufik, Pengurus Yayasan Dana Sosial Al-Falah, J Pelaku Industri Sistem Pembayaran Indonesia, J Para Pimpinan Pondok Pesantren, J Pimpinan dan Pegawai Bank Indonesia, serta J Hadirin dan Undangan yang Berbahagia. Seiamat Pagi dan Salam Sejahtera untuk kita semua 1. Mengawali sambutan pagi ini, saya ingin mengajak hadirin sekalian untuk memanjatkan puji dan syukur ke hadirat Tuhan Yang Maha Kuasa, karena hanya atas perkenan-Nya, pada kesempatan ini kita dapat hadir dalam keadaan sehat walafiat, dalam rangka mengikuti Seminar "Layanan Non Tunai untuk Pembayaran Wakaf, Infak, dan Shadaqah". 2. Acara ini merupakan bagian dari rangkaian kegiatan Indonesia Sharia Economic Festival 2015, yang merupakan agenda tahunan Bank Indonesia sejak dimulai pertama kalinya pada tahun 2014 yang lalu. 3. Dalam seminar ini, diharapkan akan tercipta diskusi yang interaktif dan konstruktif, disertai dengan sharing informasi dan pandangan, sehingga pada akhirnya akan menambah wawasan dan memperkaya khazanah ilmu pengetahuan kita semua, utamanya mengenai layanan non tunai serta pengembangan implementasinya untuk komunitas muslim di Indonesia. Bapak, Ibu, hadirin yang kami hormati, 4. Dalam beberapa kesempatan bersosialisasi dengan pelaku industri dan masyarakat luas, saya sering mengutip ucapan dari salah seorang penulis ternama Amerika di awal abad ke-19, James F. Cooper, yang mengatakan "The very existence of government at all, infers inequality". Esensi yang paling hakiki dari keberadaan otoritas adalah, untuk menjamin bahwa ketidakseimbangan pranata sosial dan ekonomi yang terjadi di masyarakat, dapat dikelola untuk kemaslahatan masyarakat luas. 5. Dalam konteks sistem pembayaran, kami memandang adagium yang diutarakan James F. Cooper ini patut dijadikan pertimbangan bagi Bank Indonesia dalam merumuskan suatu kebijakan. 6. Kompleksitas kemajemukan sosial saat ini, yang diiringi dengan pesatnya dinamika perkembangan teknologi digital, menyebabkan kendali otoritas sebagai alat kontrol untuk mengatur tatanan kehidupan masyarakat menjadi semakin strategis, khususnya untuk mencapai sistem pembayaran yang benar-benar aman, lancar, dan efisien. Bapak, Ibu, Hadirin yang kami hormati, 7. Sebagai otoritas sistem pembayaran, misi Bank Indonesia adalah Mengelola dan Memelihara Sistem Pembayaran dan Pengelolaan Uang yang aman, efisien, dan lancar, melalui perluasan akses dan mempertimbangkan kepentingan nasional. 8. Capaian misi tersebut akan kami tempuh melalui dua aspek penting, yaitu yang pertama: melakukan Penguatan Sistem Pembayaran, dan kedua: proaktif dalam memelopori kerjasama dan kolaborasi. 9. Dalam hal penguatan Sistem Pembayaran, kami menjabarkannya melalui empat pilar, yaitu pertama: Sistem Pengelolaan Uang yang Efektif dan Efisien, kedua: Perluasan Elektronifikasi Pembayaran, ketiqa: Infrastruktur Pembayaran yang handal dan aman, dan pilar keempat adalah Pengawasan dan Oversight yang Kuat dan Tajam {Rigorous}. 10. Terkait Perluasan Elektronifikasi Pembayaran tersebut, salah satu visi Bank Indonesia di bidang non tunai adalah, mewujudkan masyarakat yang memiliki preferensi tinggi dalam menggunakan instrumen dan sarana pembayaran non- tunai dalam melakukan transaksi keuangan, atau yang dikenal dengan Less Cash Society. 11. Perwujudan Less Cash Society ini penting untuk mendorong perekonomian yang lebih efisien, serta meningkatkan aspek governance dalam pengelolaan keuangan oleh masyarakat, pelaku bisnis maupun lembaga-lembaga pemerintah. 12. Sebagai bentuk komitmen Bank Indonesia dalam mendorong peningkatan transaksi non tunai, pada bulan Agustus 2014 yang lalu Bank Indonesia menginisiasi pencanangan Gerakan Nasional Non Tunai (GNNT), yang ditandai dengan penandatanganan Nota Kesepahaman antara Bank Indonesia dengan Kementerian Koordinator Bidang Perekonomian, Kementerian Keuangan, Pemerintah Daerah, serta Asosiasi Pemerintahan Provinsi Seluruh Indonesia. Bapak, Ibu, Hadirin yang kami hormati, 13. Berdasarkan sensus penduduk terakhir yang dilakukan oleh Badan Pusat Statistik pada tahun 2010, populasi penduduk muslim di Indonesia mencapai 87%, yang tersebar di seluruh wilayah Nusantara. 14. Namun sayangnya, keberadaan penduduk muslim sebagai mayoritas di Indonesia, belum didukung dengan penetrasi perbankan syariah dalam memfasilitasi transaksi keuangan masyarakat. Kondisi ini disebabkan karena masih rendahnya pangsa perbankan syariah di Indonesia, yakni sebesar 4,7% per Agustus 2015. 15. Kami meyakini, masih banyak penduduk muslim di Indonesia yang merupakan unbanked. Sementara di sisi lain, kebutuhan transaksi keuangan ritel dikalangan masyarakat muslim semakin meningkat, khususnya untuk pembayaran Wakaf, Infak dan Shadaqah. 16. Mencermati berbagai faktor tersebut, kami memandang bahwa pengembangan layanan non tunai sebagai bagian dari upaya perluasan akses keuangan di kalangan umat muslim, merupakan suatu keniscayaan. 17. Dalam kerangka kebijakan keuangan inklusif Bank Indonesia, kami telah menyusun strategi Islamic Financial Inclusion (IFI), sebagai bagian dari grand design perluasan akses keuangan. IFI dapat berperan sebagai sarana perluasan ekosistem Layanan Keuangan Digital (LKD), melalui peranan sektor informal seperti Islamic Center, jaringan mesjid, serta pondok pesantren termasuk unitunit usaha yang dimiliki oleh pesantren. 18. Sektor informal tersebut mempunyai peran besar dalam menciptakan ketertarikan masyarakat terhadap layanan non tunai yang tersedia, dan perlahan mulai mengenal untuk kemudian mencoba bertransaksi dengan layanan dimaksud. 19. Selain itu, kemauan masyarakat untuk membuka diri dan mencoba bertransaksi keuangan, diharapkan dapat menjadi entry point yang strategis untuk melakukan edukasi keuangan, khususnya terkait transaksi non tunai yang mengarah kepada ekonomi berbasis teknologi/digital. Ke depannya, masyarakat diharapkan tidak hanya mahir bertransaksi keuangan, melainkan juga memiliki pengelolaan keuangan yang handal. Bapak, Ibu, Hadirin yang kami hormati, 20. Dalam pengembangan konsep non tunai untuk mendukung transaksi keuangan syariah, kami memfokuskan pada tiga aspek utama. Pertama, pengembangan instrumen/layanan non tunai dilakukan dengan mengacu pada prinsip syariah, dan sesuai dengan karakteristik masyarakat muslim. 21. Kedua, pengembangan dilakukan dengan berbasis pada inovasi sebagai motor {innovative driven). Dan ketiqa, dukungan ekosistem e-payment merupakan faktor penting untuk menjaga keberlangsungan layanan non tunai, karena dapat membuat transaksi keuangan menjadi lebih mudah diakses dan efisien. 22. Dengan ketiga aspek tersebut, diharapkan layanan non tunai mampu memfasilitasi transaksi keuangan syariah diantaranya Wakaf, Infak dan Shadaqah, agar semakin efisien namun tetap sesuai dengan prinsip syariah. Lebih jauh, penyediaan layanan non tunai untuk pembayaran Wakaf, Infak dan Shadaqah diharapkan dapat meningkatkan pemahaman dan pengalaman masyarakat dalam bertransaksi non tunai. Bapak, Ibu, dan Hadirin yang kami hormati, 23. Sebagai perwujudan nyata dari upaya kami dalam memfasilitasi transaksi pembayaran non tunai bagi segmen masyarakat muslim, pada siang hari ini akan dilakukan launching LKD di pondok pesantren, yang merupakan kolaborasi antara pondok pesantren dengan perusahaan telekomunikasi. Kami mengharapkan implementasi kedepan semakin diperluas, dengan melibatkan komunitas pondok pesantren lainnya. 24. Selanjutnya, kami mengharapkan dukungan dari seluruh pihak terkait dalam rangka mensukseskan upaya implementasi layanan non tunai terhadap transaksi retail syariah. Melalui komunikasi yang baik, koordinasi yang intensif, serta kolaborasi sinergis antara Bank Indonesia, Pemerintah, otoritas terkait, lembaga amil zakat, pondok pesantren dan pelaku industri sistem pembayaran, kami meyakini awareness dan kesediaan masyarakat untuk menggunakan layanan non tunai yang sesuai dengan prinsip syariah dalam aktivitas ekonomi sehari- hari, akan meningkat. 25. Sebelum mengakhiri sambutan ini, perkenankanlah saya mengucapkan terimakasih kepada Bapak, Ibu, serta hadirin semuanya yang telah bersedia meluangkan waktu berharga yang dimiliki, untuk hadir pada seminar pagi ini. Semoga dengan partisipasi aktif dan kontribusi yang diberikan selama berlangsungnya seminar ini, pada akhirnya dapat membawa kemaslahatan bagi kita semua. Selamat mengikuti seminar, terima kasih. Deputi Gubernur Bank Indonesia Ronald Waas

Title: Speech of Deputy Governor, Ronald Waas of Bank Indonesia at the Signing of Work Guidelines Between BI and POLRI: Procedure For Implementation of Guidance and Supervision to Security Business Services Agencies Conducting Business Activities in Escorting Mo
text: SPEECH OF DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF BANK INDONESIA AT THE SIGNING OF WORK GUIDELINES BETWEEN BI AND POLRI: PROCEDURE FOR IMPLEMENTATION OF GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION TO SECURITY BUSINESS SERVICES AGENCIES CONDUCTING BUSINESS ACTIVITIES IN ESCORTING MONEY CONVEYANCES AND RUPIAH PROCESSING AS A FOLLOW-UP OF: THE SIGNING OF MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING ON COOPERATION IN ORDER TO SUPPORT THE IMPLEMENTATION OF DUTIES AND AUTHORITIES OF BANK INDONESIA Jakarta, 26 February 2015 The honorable, Head of Security Maintenance Agency (Baharkam) of Polri, Komjen Pol. Drs. Putut Eko Bayuseno, S.H.; Head of Legal Division of Polri, Irjen Pol. Drs. Moch Giyarto, S.H., M.Hum; Head of Baharkam Administrative Planning Bureau of Polri, Brigjen Pol. Dr. Achmadi, S.H., MAP; Director of Baharkam Community Development of Polri, Brigjen Pol. Hengki Kaluar; Director of Baharkam Vital Object Security of Polri, Brigjen Pol. Drs. Yohanes Agus Mulyono; Chairman of Cash Conveyance Services Company Association (APJATIN), Mrs. Inne Yuaniza; Chairman of Indonesian Business Services of Security Agency Association (ABUJAPI) or his representative Management and staff of Baharkam and Legal Division of POLRI; Department Leadership of Bank Indonesia, attendees and invitees. Good day and Greetings to us all.  First of all, I would like to ask us all to praise our gratitude to God the Almighty, for His grace we could be present in this good atmosphere for the Signing of Work Guidelines between Bank Indonesia and the State Police of the Republic of Indonesia, in this case the Security Maintenance Agency (Baharkam), in relation to the Procedure for Implementation of Guidance and Supervision to Security Business Services Agencies Conducting Business Activities in Escorting Money Conveyances and Rupiah Processing. Page 1 of 4  The signing of this Work Guidelines constitutes a follow-up of the Memorandum of Understanding on Cooperation in Order to Support the Implementation of Duties and Authorities of Bank Indonesia and the State Police of the Republic of Indonesia, already signed by the Governor of Bank Indonesia and the Head of the State Police of the Republic of Indonesia on 1 September 2014.  In the Memorandum of Understanding signed by the Governor of Bank Indonesia and the Head of POLRI referred to, some duties have already been agreed, which implementation would be synergized, specifically in the field of Law Enforcement. Broadly, the scope of cooperation built includes: Exchanging data and/or information; Securing and escorting; Supervision; Law Enforcement; Human Resources Enhancement; and Socialization Attendees,  In accordance with the mandate of Law concerning Bank Indonesia, BI duties as the payment system authority is to govern and maintain the smoothness of the payment system, including cash and non-cash payment system.  In the cash payment system or what we call money management, Bank Indonesia through Department of Money Management has a mission to meet the need of rupiah in the society in sufficient nominal amounts, appropriate types of fraction, timely and in fit for circulation condition. In order to achieve that mission, Department of Money Management of Bank Indonesia applies 3 strategy pillars, namely: Availability of Reliable and Quality Rupiah; Secured and Optimal Money Management and Distribution; and Excellent Cash Service.  In the implementation of the three pillars of strategy, besides, naturally, involving banking in it, there are also other parties which are during this time have roles that are quite strategic, among others, Badan Usaha Jasa Pengamanan-BUJP (Security Business Service Agency) conducting money conveyance escorting activities and Rupiah processing, or known as Cash in Transit (CIT).  This Security Business Service Agency conducts its duties in accordance with the cooperative contract agreed with banks, among others, covering: cash distribution; Page 2 of 4 calculation, sorting, and cash processing; cash in safe; and replenishing ATM with cash and/or withdrawing cash from Cash Deposit Machine (CDM) or other similar devices, including monitoring of cash adequacy in ATM and/or CDM (cash replenishment). Ladies and Gentlemen,  Considering the strategic role of Security Business Service Agency (BUJP) conducting business activities of escorting money conveyance and processing of Rupiah, Bank Indonesia sees the need for guidance and supervision toward the BUJP, in order to protect the society in association to Rupiah circulation.  Naturally, with the limitation of authority and expertise owned, in providing guidance and supervision to the Security Business Service Agency, Bank Indonesia needs help and cooperation from the institution that has authority and expertise in this field, namely POLRI. Strong coordination and consolidation between authorities and law enforcer, is expected to prevent and minimize various risks that might arise in the implementation of money circulation activities in Indonesia, so that the society can be prevented from loss.  This good cooperation and coordination, naturally needs to be embedded into a clear and transparent mechanism, in accordance with the duties and authorities of BI and POLRI, as well as to refer to the applicable laws and regulations by taking into account the principle of justice, principle of utility, and principle of legal certainty.  We welcome the signing of the Work Guidelines on the Procedure for Implementation of Guidance and Supervision to Security Business Service Agency that Conducting Money Conveyance Escorting Business Activities and Rupiah Processing, which is also part of the Memorandum of Understanding already signed earlier. The implementation of these work guidelines will also be followed-up later through the cooperation between Representative Offices of Bank Indonesia and the local Regional Police, poured into Pokok Pokok Kesepahaman-PKK (Understanding Principals). Ladies and Gentlemen,  Through the signing of this Work Guidelines, we believe that the efforts of Guidance and Supervision toward Security Business Service Agency that Conducting Money Conveyance Escorting Business Activities and Rupiah Processing in the future can be run more smoothly and effectively, so that our objective in providing protection to all people through the creation of Payment System industry that is safe and sound can be realized soon, and also can provide optimal contribution to the Indonesian economy. Page 3 of 4  These Work Guidelines are also expected to become a glue of excellent and intensive communication, synergic cooperation, coordination, and collaboration with POLRI, relevant ministries, law enforcement apparatus and other stakeholders.  Thus we conclude this speech with the belief that God the Almighty is always with us to bless and light our way toward the better future. Thank you. Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Ronald Waas Page 4 of 4

Title: Transforming Towards Strategic Talent Capacity in Central Bank (Keynote Speech Deputi Gubernur Ronald Waas pada36th Meeting of SEACEN Directors of Research and Training) Bali, 13 Agustus 2014
text: BANK INDONESIA Keynote Speech Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia At 36th Meeting of SEACEN Directors of Research and Training Transforming Towards Strategic Talent Capacity in Central Bank" Bali, August 13th 2014 Dear Colleges, Directors of Research and Training, Honorable Speakers and Heads of Department in South East Asia Central Banks, Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, Good Morning and May God bless us All, Introduction  It is such a great pleasure to be here today in the 36th Meeting of SEACEN Directors of Research and Training (DORT). It is also my honor to welcome you to one of Indonesia most beautiful and exotic island, Bali. I would also like to thank you SEACEN for excellent arrangements made for this event. All of you from the central bank representatives are our important partners in achieving economic and financial stability in Asia Pacific Region.  It was just over a year ago that SEACEN meet together in the Board of Governors (BOG) meeting in Nepal. On that event, Bank Indonesia gladly took a full commitment to be the host of three important agendas: (i) the High Level Seminar on Global Liquidity and Impact of Capital Flows on Exchange Rates in Emerging Asia, already held in Bandung last June, (ii) the 28th SEACEN-FSI Regional Seminar on Macro and Micro Stress Testing, that will be held in Bali next August, and (iii) is this 36th SEACEN DORT Meeting.  Thus here we are today, trying to make considerable progress in meeting its objective to provide a more focused and coordinated approach towards the development of talent capacity strategy in central banks.  These meeting will provide all participants the opportunity to listen and learn from top thinkers central bank practitioners and experts. It is one of the key strengths of SEACEN DORT programs that we have unique opportunity to establish strong social and professional networking and build lasting fraternity relationship with common understanding on how central bank works.  I am glad that this year's SEACEN DORT Meeting theme captures the spirit of the moment, "Transforming towards Strategic Talent Capacity in Central Banks". Building strategic capacity in central banks is not merely an objective. 36th Meeting of SEACEN Directors of Research and Training, Bali August 13th, 2014 Page 1 of 5 Indeed, it's a never ending journey. It is in this spirit I would like to share some thought about the importance of human capital development in this context. Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlement, Lesson Learned from The Crises  Indonesia is a land of enormous opportunities. Often referred to as the world's largest archipelago, with more than 17,000 islands that span more than 5000 km (around 3,200 miles). We have a huge potential market with massive population of 240 million people, abundant natural resources, and one of the largest and fastest growing middle class.  After the 1997 crises, many people feared that Indonesia is going to suffer and the economy will fade away and took a while before it can begin to stimulate back to normal. Instead, we bounced back a lot more rapidly than people could imagine. We started to grow swiftly by mending the economy that once contracted by 13.5% to make it one of the largest and fastest growing emerging economies. For the last decade, Indonesia has been able to make a difference because of our high growth and economic size.  Learned from 1997 crises, we also witnessed the changes in the constellation of the global economy in 2008 financial crisis that left a profound and widespread global anxiety. It is not a coincidence that our economy withstood up well against 2008 turbulence. Our resilience is inseparable from strong support of stable macroeconomic conditions and favorable financial system. But more importantly we were better prepared for this shock.  After the crises of 1997/98, Bank Indonesia and our government has implemented a wide ranging policy reforms to improve the macroeconomic management. A prudent monetary and fiscal policy, sound banking system, and other underlying project has strengthened our response in mitigating the adverse impact of the global economic crises.  From those crises, we learn that to be a successful management of central bank, we should deliver a clear, aspirational, and demanding vision through a combination of well management of its core function and its right culture. The history should be our great asset to learn from the crises. But how we response to the current crises is what matter the most. Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlement, The Importance of Human Capital Development  It is a high time for all of us to enhance the exchange information and cooperation on all issues relating to human capital development. The 36th Meeting ofSEACEN Directors of Research and Training, Bali August 13th, 2014 Page 2 of 5 collaborative and intensive communication among us, such as what we have today is needed, as rapid changes in the global condition and greater integration in the regional and the world economy is going ahead of us.  The adagio of "New Normal" is not a clear cut, as the period in which economic landscape converge to a more stable new equilibrium continue to reshape tremendously. Changes in global economic order have a substantially impact on the movement and vision of various entities, both financial and non-financial institutions. The intensification of globalization process, the path of economic integration, and the advancement of technology have contributed to these changes.  The future has therefore become more complex, uncertain, unclear, and more ambiguous. Effective response and performance is required to face this multifaceted economic landscape. Therefore, far bigger attention should be address to the necessary changes of human capital development.  We are here today for one good reason, to ensure that together, we agree on the actions we must continue to develop as a global community to encounter whatever the challenges might come ahead. For that reason, we need the most current policies and most importantly current capacity in handling the 21st century issues. This means we need a more creative, more cohesive, and more collaborative response than in the past. Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlement, The Transformational Principles: Some Priorities  I believe, in order to enhance the ability to cope with unprecedented global economic condition, the talent management need to focus on several key areas: (1) Investing on the people, (2) Getting the foundations right, and (3) building a collaborative partnership as part of competitive global system.  The first, investing the people. Investing in human capital has and always been an important part of any transformational journey to success. Human capital is the most critical internal capabilities that we should be aware of, as an intensified focus on human resources capacity building will bolster the knowledge depth and needed skilled in any circumstances.  Encouraging, sustaining, and enhancing economic stability require decisive action by leaders. Effective organization that is able to produce a born-skilled leader need continued productive and constructive talent transformation. Developing a talent management requires consistent focus and commitment from all levels of organization. The effort need to be sustained over many years, through good times and delicate moment. 36th Meeting ofSEACEN Directors of Research and Training, Bali August 13th, 2014 Page 3 of 5  People skills are also one and important thing to enhance our organizational capacity such as SEACEN to bring about institutional development. It will also bring an enhancement for our respective organizational effectiveness.  Secondly, getting the foundations right. As Mendzela said in "Managing the 21st century central bank", central banks have unique freedom to plan and manage change more successfully than most organizations. We can then use that freedom to become leading and exemplary institutions.  Talent strategies must be based on a great humanity that reinforced a strong and enduring ethical foundation of the organization. It should develop an individual and organizational ability to deal with specific challenging issues, embrace continued improvement changes, including changes induced by random external forces.  Talent development needs to be allocated with greater focus and priority on account of significant structural shift in economic and financial landscape. Central bank should rebalance their attention in developing external capabilities and internal capabilities. External capabilities related our ability to envision the economy run more effective and efficient. Internal capabilities have something to do with the run of management practices that include the fulfillment of talent requirement.  Third, building partnership and be a part of global competitive system. It is always not enough to be a king in our own territory, especially when the definition of territory has been blurred by borderless financial approach. In order to be competitive, we need to ensure that not only our system but also regional area that are robust and competitive to facilitate the common understanding and cooperation to build a better environment. Thus enhancing communication among our peer countries in the region will be very vital as we are facing complex nature of global challenges.  What SEACEN can contribute on this regard is to be a constant source and reference of excellent central bank capabilities. We also need to play a more pro-active role in the design and delivery of leadership agility and acuteness, and become the regional center of excellence in talent management development program. A comprehensive thematic training development program and a thorough joint research on central bank issues are very much welcomes and need to develop further. Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlement, Conclusion 36th Meeting of SEACEN Directors of Research and Training, Bali August 13th, 2014 Page 4 of 5  The very existence of government at all, infers inequality. As the new equilibrium is always on the rise, I believe that the great humanity must come first in the dynamic change of global economy.  The ultimate target of transforming toward strategic talent capacity is not only developing a system, but flourishing a matured leader who can navigate us into a right direction. It's not simple, and it perhaps took an extensive time investment to accomplish. A wise Chinese quotation saying that It takes ten years to grow a tree, and a hundred years to develop an individual.  However, we must not forget that it's not the quality of skill that makes a man worth it, but his value of great humanity that bring the reaped of prosperity worth it. Manhood is defined and decided by the ability to nurture and to protect, by the capability to provide and to sustain (C. JoyBell C.)  As closing remarks, I am delighted that we are here today. I have nothing but high hopes that the lucrative collaborations and thoughts about how strategic talent capacity in central bank should develop would become common wisdom and priority in creating a more credible central bank.  It is now my privilege and pleasure to officially open these series of 36th SEACEN DORT Meeting. Thank you and have an engaging and productive discussion. Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Ronald Waas 36th Meeting of SEACEN Directors of Research and Training, Bali August 13th, 2014 Page 5 of 5

Title: Speech of Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia, Ronald Waas in Dissemination of Use of Non-cash Transactions in The Process of Placement and Protection of Indonesian Workers Jakarta, 24 February 2015
text: POINTERS DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF BANK INDONESIA IN DISSEMINATION OF USE OF NON-CASH TRANSACTIONS IN THE PROCESS OF PLACEMENT AND PROTECTION OF INDONESIAN WORKERS Jakarta, 24 February 2015 Distinguished:  Resource Persons, Participants, and ladies and gentlemen, Good Morning and May God Bless Us All 1. To begin our event this morning, I would like to invite all of us to praise God the Almighty for giving us the opportunity to meet in this favorable occasion titled Dissemination of Use of Non-Cash Transactions in the Process of Placement and Protection of Indonesian Workers. 2. This event embodies our efforts to support Non-Cash National Movement (GNNT) launched by Bank Indonesia in August 2014. GNNT is a program of Bank Indonesia seeking to increase community awareness in using non-cash instruments to make transactions in their economic activities. Ladies and gentlemen, 3. On 16 February 2015, Bank Indonesia and the Ministry of Manpower, Financial Services Authority (OJK), and Agency for Placement and Protection of Indonesian Migrant Workers (BNP2TKI) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding on Increasing Use of Non-Cash Transactions and Expanded Financial Access for Placement and Protection of Indonesian Migrant Workers. Page 1 of 4 4. Todays activity is the initial actual step out of a series of dissemination and education activities to increase the understanding of the relevant institutions in the process of placement and protection of Indonesian Migrant Workers on the purposes and benefits of non-cash transactions. 5. In this event, we invite the management of Private Indonesian Migrant Workers Recruitment Agencies (PPTKIS), insurance companies providing protection for Indonesian Migrant Workers, Overseas Workers Training Centers (BKLN), health services providers, and the competence certification agency for Indonesian Migrant Workers, all of which are the main actors in various relevant activities in the Placement and Protection of Indonesian Migrant Workers. 6. This dissemination activity is coordinated by Bank Indonesia with 3 other relevant institutions and conducted in phases from February to March 2015 in 7 cities, namely Jakarta, Medan, Bandung, Semarang, Pontianak, Surabaya, and Mataram. I hope all of the dissemination materials to be presented by the resource persons will be comprehensive, including: a) Material from the Ministry of Manpower, namely Regulation of Minister of Manpower No. 22 of 2014 on Implementation of Placement and Protection of Indonesian Migrant Workers Overseas, one of the articles of which obliges noncash payment for placement and protection of Indonesian Migrant Workers. b) Material from BNP2TKI on Computerized System of Migrant Workers as an incorporated and integrated system which is connected to the banking system to serve non-cash payment and database of Indonesian Migrant Worker candidates. c) Material from OJK on insurance services for Indonesian Migrant Workers, BKLN services, health facility services, and competence certification services for Indonesian Migrant Workers. Page 2 of 4 d) Material from Bank Indonesia on the purposes of increasing non-cash transactions in the placement and protection process of Indonesian Migrant Workers, non-cash transaction services, introduction to non-cash payment instruments, and the roles of Bank Indonesia as a payment system authority. e) Material from banks on non-cash services through banking products, namely mobile banking, internet banking, ATM and branches for payment of services in the placement process of Indonesian Migrant Workers. Ladies and Gentlemen, Distinguished Guests, 7. Bank Indonesia highly appreciates the support of the Ministry of Manpower, OJK, and BNP2TKI to migrate all payment processes starting from insurance premium, worker training cost, health service cost, and certification cost for Indonesian Migrant Workers. It supports the effort of Bank Indonesia to reduce shadow economy and improve governance in the process of placement and protection of Indonesian Migrant Workers through transparent payment transaction recording. 8. Bank Indonesia consistently supports efforts to improve services for Indonesian Migrant Workers by continuously creating cooperation with the Ministry of Manpower, OJK, and BNP2TKI to continue the phases of activities specified in a memorandum of understanding, including optimized mechanism of payment of Indonesian Migrant Workers salary and utilization of money transfer services by Indonesian Migrant Workers through banking services and Government to Government strategy approach involving cooperation between central banks, primarily those of countries where our migrant workers earn their living. Distinguished guests, We expect that the series of dissemination through education and development of remittance services we make to support the placement and protection of Indonesian Page 3 of 4 Migrant Workers will strengthen our commitment to increase the dignity and welfare of Indonesian Migrant Workers and their families. Through todays activity, we also expect that we can realize our commitment to boost the use of non-cash instruments by the wider community and to aim higher public acceptance and awareness on non-cash instruments in our beloved republic. To conclude, we extend our deepest gratitude and appreciation to all invitees and parties attending and supporting this event. Thank you. Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Ronald Waas Page 4 of 4

Title: Sambutan Deputi Gubernur Bank Indonesia, Sugeng pada Peluncuran Program Desmigratif 2017, Jakarta, 11 September 2017
text: Welcome Launch of The Desmigrative Program 2017 Jakarta, September 11, 2017 Dear Minister of Manpower of the Republic of Indonesia, Mr. Muhammad Hanif Dhakiri Dear Minister of Villages, Development of Highest Regions, and Transmigration, Mr. Eko Putro Sa nd jo jo Dear Kepaia Creative Economy Agency, Mr. Triawan Munaf Attendees whom we respect for representatives of relevant Ministries/Institutions Assaiamuaiaikum Warahmatuiiahi Wabarakatuh 1. First of all, we congratulate the Ministry of Manpower of the Republic of Indonesia, because today it has launched the Productive or Desmigrative Migrant Village Program. 2. Bank Indonesia welcomes the Productive Migrant Village Program (Desmigratif) as an effort to handle migrant worker enclaves in an integrated manner, including social aspects such as maintaining the integrity of families. Migrant workers. 3. Taking into account the contribution of migrant workers' income to the country's considerable foreign exchange and the large number of migrant workers working abroad, we support this Desmigratif Program as efforts to empower migrant workers and migrant workers' families, as well as the surrounding communities. 4. As we all know, the Desmigratif Program consists of 4 main activity pillars, namely Layanan Migration (Pillar 1), Productive Business (Pillar 2), Community Parenting (Pillar 3), and Desmigratif Cooperatives (Pillar 4), it is hoped that it will be able to be a solution to the complexity of the challenges faced so far in developing the capabilities of migrant workers and their families. Ladies and Gentlemen Attend the happy 5. For this excellent program initiative, we as the macroprudential and payment system authority are ready to support through program synergy. This is in line with our duties and roles in realizing economic stability through the less cash society or the National Non-Cash Movement and financial inclusion. Various programs that we develop in the field of payment systems and financial inclusion, as well as the development of MSMEs, we believe can help the implementation of Pillar 2 andPillar 4 of the Desmigratif Program. 6. Through the synergy between Bank Indonesia's programs related to less cash society and financial inclusion with the Desmigratif Program, we hope that the outcomes and benefits generated can be optimal in mem ba ng un village pocket T KI. 7. The various programs that we have developed are: a. The First: Remittances for Migrant Workers In order to improve access to finance, particularly to the bottom of the pyramid, Bank Indonesia has developed financial inclusion policies and programs. The development and implementation of financial inclusion policies is carried out to support the achievement of the National Financial Inclusion Strategy target of 75% banked people in 2019 (in 2014 banked people in Indonesia of 36%). As one of the target segments of financial inclusion policy, BI is currently developing pro-gram remittances for migrant workers. The mechanism for sending money from migrant workers to their families currently still faces a number of challenges, such as the practice of HawalaI, remittances to only one trusted person (not directly to the families of migrant workers), as well as a less efficient and effective remittance process. To that end, Bank Indonesia encourages the development of a remittance business model that is more efficient, effective, easy, and affordable. The business model in question consists of developing cooperation with partners to facilitate remittance ilitation, which is in the form of transfers via mobile phones to mobile phones (mobilephone to mobilephone), hosted to host, from agent to agent, transfer using cash deposit machine, as well as transfer from post office to post office. To support the implementation of this business model, regulations are needed so that migrant workers before leaving have opened an account, which in this case is encouraged in the form of electronic money and savings. In this regard, BI has coordinated with the OJK for the ease of account opening by banks. In developing the business model, BI not only encourages the industry but also seeks through discussions with payment system authorities in other countries and exploring bilateral corridors. remittances between Indonesia and the sending country. b. The second: Digital Financial Services (LKD) In addition to encouraging the development of the remittance business model, BI also encourages the development of a cashless ecosystem in the migrant worker family community. For this reason, not only migrant workers are expected to have accounts, but also migrant workers' families. The development of the ecosystem has now begun in line with the non-cash social assistance program that is currently running in 98 districts/cities for the Family Hope Program (PKH) and Non-Cash Food Assistance (BPNT). To encourage migrant workers' families to transact non-cash, since 2014 BI has introduced Digital Financial Services (DFS) that allows people to transact their electronic money at LKD agents using mobile technology , such as cards or mobile phones. Transactions that can be done, for example, to shop for basic necessities, pay water bills, buy credit, etc. With the distribution of LKD agents which currently has reached 216,415 in 495 districts/cities, it is expected to meet the financial service needs of communities in villages that run the Desmigratif program. In addition to LKD and remittances, to improve the village economy, promote efficiency and effectiveness as well as financial transparency in villages, we also encourage the electronification of Village Funds. In this case, electronification is applied to the utilization of village funds in order support the improvement of the quality of life of rural communities, both for village development and the empowerment of rural communities. To that end, Bi encourages efforts to electronify the use of Village Funds, namely payments related to village development and community empowerment carried out in a non-cash manner. We initiated the concept of a cash management system (CMS), which is an internet banking-based application with a transfer mechanism from account to account. Thus, the transfer/payment process can be done by the appointed officer himself, from the Village Account to the designated account, for example the account of the teacher, foreman,etc. . c. The Third: Empowering MSMEs In addition to payment system-related programs, in order to improve the capabilities of MSMEs, Bank Indonesia also participates in developing MSME policies and programs. The MSME development program , which we think is good for synergy with the Desmigratif program , is BI as a resource person related to MSME education and development, entrepreneurship training and assistance of food security clusters. Currently, entrepreneurship training has been carried out in the area of 21 BI Representative Offices and has produced 634 entrepreneurs, while food security cluster assistance has been held in 173 locations spread across 45 regions of BI Representative Offices. If there is a village slice of the BI program and desmigrative, maka synergy can be carried out immediately. d. The Fourth: Education In order for the financial inclusion program as we mentioned to run smoothly, education is needed to all relevant stakeholders, including the service user community and a village pa rat. Ladies and Gentlemen Attend, 8. We hope that the program that is well-aimed and we believe that together will bring broad benefits to the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia will attract support from all parties, especially payment system actors in Indonesia. 9. Once again we congratulate you on the launch of this program. Hopefully, with efforts and coordination with all parties, this program can run well and provide optimal manfaat for migrant workers, all social elements of the village community, and Government. Wassalamualaikum Warohmatullahi Wabarakatuh Dr . text_original: Sambutan Peluncuran Program Desmigratif 2017 Jakarta, 11 September 2017 Yth Menteri Ketenagakerjaan Republik Indonesia, Bapak Muhammad Hanif Dhakiri Yth Menteri Desa, Pembangunan Daerah Tertinggai, dan Transmigrasi, Bapak Eko Putro Sa nd jo jo Yth Kepaia Badan Ekonomi Kreatif, Bapak Triawan Munaf Hadirin yang kami hormati perwakiian dari Kementerian/Lembaga terkait Assaiamuaiaikum Warahmatuiiahi Wabarakatuh 1. Pertama-tama, kami ucapkan selamat kepada Kementerian Ketenagakerjaan Republik Indonesia, karena pada hari ini telah meluncurkan Program Desa Migran Produktif atau Desmigratif. 2. Bank Indonesia menyambut baik adanya Program Desa Migran Produktif (Desmigratif) sebagai upaya penanganan desa kantong TKI secara terpadu, termasuk aspek sosial seperti menjaga keutuhan keluarga TKI. 3. Dengan mempertimbangkan kontribusi penghasilan TKI terhadap devisa yang cukup besar kepada negeri ini dan banyaknya jumlah TKI yang bekerja di luar negeri, kami mendukung Program Desmigratif ini sebagai upaya pemberdayaan TKI dan keluarga TKI, serta komunitas di sekitarnya. 4. Sebagaimana kita ketahui bersama, Program Desmigratif yang terdiri dari 4 pilar kegiatan utama, yaitu Layanan Migrasi (Pilar 1), Usaha Produktif (Pilar 2), Community Parenting (Pilar 3), dan Koperasi Desmigratif (Pilar 4), diharapkan mampu menjadi solusi atas kompleksitas tantangan yang dihadapi selama ini dalam pengembangan kapabilitas TKI dan keluarganya. Bapak/Ibu Hadiri yang berbahagia 5. Atas inisiatif program yang sangat baik tersebut, kami selaku otoritas makroprudensial dan sistem pembayaran siap untuk mendukung melalui sinergi program. Hal ini sejalan dengan tugas dan peran kami dalam mewujudkan stabilitas ekonomi melalui less cash society atau Gerakan Nasional Non Tunai dan keuangan inklusif. Berbagai program yang kami kembangkan di bidang sistem pembayaran dan keuangan inklusif, serta pengembangan UMKM, kami yakini dapat membantu implementasi Pilar 2 dan Pilar 4 dari Program Desmigratif. 6. Melalui sinergi antara program Bank Indonesia terkait less cash society dan keuangan inklusif dengan Program Desmigratif, kami harapkan outcome dan manfaat yang dihasilkan dapat optimal dalam mem ba ng un desa kantong TKI. 7. Berbagai program yang kami kembangkan dimaksud, yaitu: a. Yang Pertama: Remitansi bagi TKI Dalam rangka meningkatkan akses keuangan, khususnya kepada masyarakat lapisan bawah (the bottom of the pyramid), Bank Indonesia mengembangkan kebijakan dan program keuangan inklusif. Pengembangan dan implementasi kebijakan keuangan inklusif dilakukan guna mendukung tercapainya target Strategi Nasional Keuangan Inklusif yaitu 75% banked people pada tabun 2019 (tahun 2014 banked people di Indonesia sebesar 36%). Sebagai salah satu segmen target kebijakan keuangan inklusif, BI saat ini tengah mengembangkan program remitansi bagi TKI. Mekanisme pengiriman uang dari TKI kepada keluarganya saat ini masih menghadapi sejumlah tantangan, seperti masih terdapatnya praktek HawalaI, remitansi hanya kepada satu orang yang dipercaya (tidak langsung kepada keluarga TKI), serta proses remitansi yang kurang efisien dan efektif. Untuk itu, BI mendorong dikembangkannya model bisnis remitansi yang lebih efisien, efektif, mudah, dan terjangkau. Model bisnis dimaksud terdiri dari pengembangan kerjasama dengan partner untuk memfasilitasi remitansi, yaitu berupa transfer melalui telepon genggam ke telepon genggam (mobilephone to mobilephone), secara host to host, dari agen ke agen, transfer menggunakan Cash Deposit Machine, serta transfer dari kantor pos ke kantor pos. Untuk mendukung implementasi model bisnis tersebut, diperlukan regulasi agar TKI sebelum berangkat telah membuka rekening, yang dalam ini didorong berupa uang elektronik dan tabungan. Terkait hal ini, BI telah berkoordinasi dengan OJK untuk kemudahan pembukaan rekening oleh perbankan. Dalam pengembangan model bisnis tersebut, BI tidak hanya mendorong industri namun juga mengupayakan melalui diskusi dengan otoritas sistem pembayaran di negara lain serta menjajagi koridor bilateral remitansi antara Indonesia dengan negara pengirim. b. Yang kedua: Layanan Keuangan Digital (LKD) Selain mendorong pengembangan model bisnis remitansi tersebut, BI juga mendorong dikembangkannya ekosistem non tunai di komunitas keluarga TKI. Untuk itu, tidak hanya TKI yang diharapkan telah memiliki rekening, namun juga keluarga TKI. Pengembangan ekosistem tersebut saat ini telah dimulai seiring dengan program bantuan sosial non tunai yang saat ini telah berjalan di 98 kabupaten/kota untuk Program Keluarga Harapan (PKH) dan Bantuan Pangan Non Tunai (BPNT). Untuk mendorong keluarga TKI bertransaksai secara non tunai, sejak 2014 BI telah memperkenalkan Layanan Keuangan Digital (LKD) yang memungkinkan masyarakat mentransaksikan uang elektroniknya di agen LKD dengan menggunakan teknologi yang bersifat mobile, misalnya kartu atau telepon genggam. Transaksi yang dapat dilakukan misalnya untuk berbelanja kebutuhan pokok, membayar tagihan air, membeli pulsa, dll. Dengan sebaran agen LKD yang saat ini telah mencapai 216.415 di 495 kabupaten/kota diharapkan dapat memenuhi kebutuhan layanan keuangan masyarakat di desa yang menjalankan program Desmigratif. Selain LKD dan remitansi, untuk meningkatkan perekonomian desa, mendorong efisiensi dan efektivitas serta transparansi keuangan di desa, kami juga mendorong elektronifikasi Dana Desa. Dalam hal ini, elektronifikasi diterapkan pada pemanfaatan Dana Desa guna mendukung peningkatan kualitas hidup masyarakat desa, baik untuk pembangunan desa maupun pemberdayaan masyarakat desa. Untuk itu, BI mendorong upaya elektronifikasi pemanfaatan Dana Desa, yaitu pembayaran terkait pembangunan desa dan pemberdayaan masyarakat dilakukan secara non tunai. Kami menginisiasikan konsep cash management system (CMS) yaitu aplikasi berbasis internet banking dengan mekanisme transfer dari rekening ke rekening. Dengan demikian, proses transfer/pembayaran dapat dilakukan sendiri oleh petugas yang ditunjuk, dari Rekening Desa kepada rekening tertuju, misal rekening guru, mandor, dan lain sebagainya. c. Yang Ketiga: Pemberdayaan UMKM Disamping program terkait sistem pembayaran, dalam rangka meningkatkan kapabilitas UMKM, Bank Indonesia juga turut mengembangkan kebijakan dan program UMKM. Program pengembangan UMKM yang menurut kami sangat baik untuk disinergikan dengan program Desmigratif yaitu BI sebagai narasumber terkait pendidikan dan pengembangan UMKM, pelatihan kewirausahaan dan pendampingan klaster ketahanan pangan. Saat ini pelatihan kewirausahaan telah dilakukan di wilayah 21 Kantor Perwakilan BI dan telah menghasilkan 634 Wirausaha, sedangkan pendampingan klaster ketahanan pangan telah diselenggarakan di 173 lokasi yang tersebar di 45 wilayah Kantor Perwakilan BI. Apabila terdapat irisan desa dari program BI dan desmigratif, maka sinergi dapat langsung dilakukan. d. Yang Keempat: Edukasi Agar program keuangan inklusif sebagaimana kami sebutkan berjalan lancar diperlukan edukasi kepada seluruh stakeholder terkait, termasuk masyarakat pengguna layanan dan a pa rat Desa. Bapak/Ibu Hadiri sekalian, 8. Kami berharap bahwa Program yang bertujuan baik dan kita yakini bersama akan mendatangkan manfaat yang luas bagi Negara Kesatuan Republik Indonesia ini akan mendapat dukungan dari semua pihak, khususnya pelaku sistem pembayaran di Indonesia. 9. Sekali lagi kami mengucapkan selamat atas peluncuran program ini. Semoga dengan upaya dan koordinasi dengan semua pihak, program ini dapat berjalan dengan baik dan memberikan manfaat yang optimal bagi TKI, seluruh unsur sosial masyarakat Desa, dan Pemerintah. Wassalamualaikum Warohmatullahi Wabarakatuh Dr Sugeng Deputi Gubernur BI I Kata Hawala berasal dari bahasa Somalia (xawala), yaitu istilah yang biasa digunakan untuk mendefinisikan sistem transfer dana secara informal melalui perantara (disebut "Hawaladars"). --------------- ------------------------------------------------------------ --------------- ------------------------------------------------------------

Title: Sambutan Gubernur Bank Indonesia, Agus D.W. Martowardojo pada Penandatanganan Kesepakatan Bersama Pengembangan Integrasi Sistem Pembayaran Elektronik Sektor Transportasi, Jakarta, 6 September 2017
text: -Remarks by the Governor of Bank Indonesia- The signing of the Mutual Agreement Between Bank Indonesia with the Ministry of Transportation of the Republic of Indonesia & Joint Agreement Between BPTJ, Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta, and All Moda Operators in Jabodetabek on Integration Development Electronic Payment System Transporta si Sector Jakarta, 6th September 2017 What We Respect: 95 Minister of Transportation of the Republic of Indonesia, Bpk Budi Karya Sumadi 95 Governor of DKI Jakarta, Bpk Djarot Syaifui Hidayat 95 Deputy for Financial Services, Survey Services, and Services Consulation of the Ministry of SOEs, Mr. Gatot Trihargo 95 To pa la Jabodetabek Transportation Development Agency, Bpk Bambang Prihantono 95 Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia, Bpk Sugeng 95 Eseion I Officials within ministries/institutions 95 Banking Leaders, a.i. President Directors of BRI, BNI, Bank Mandiri, BTN, BCA, and Bank DKI 95 Leaders of Business Entities Providing Public Transportation Services in Jabodetabek wiiayah, namely the Directors of Transjakarta, Jabodetabek Commuter Train, PPD, Damri, MRT, LRT, Railink 95 Switching Company Leaders 95 Ladies and Gentlemen, Happy Sekaiian Audience Assaiammuaiaikum Wr. Wb. Morning and Saiam Well For All of Us. 1. Praise and gratitude, let us pray to God Almighty, and thank you for the leadership of the Minister of Transportation and the Governor of DKI Jakarta so that today we can all attend signed a Joint Agreement to realize an integrated electronic payment system in the transportation sector. 2. We welcome the various advances in reforms and improvements in the real sector area that continue to be pursued by the Central government and local governments. This certainly needs to be supportedg with the improvement of payment system services. Because otherwise efficiency will not be formed. 3. We welcome that the electronification program and the National Non-Cash Movement do not only exist in Jakarta, but exist in all regions in Indonesia and various Ministries and Local Governments. We also welcome the government's commitment to distribute social assistance entirely on a non-cash basis. 4. We also welcome the efforts made where all toll roads in Indonesia have committed to electronify payments and integrate with each other to create efficiency. 5. And today, under the leadership of the Minister of Transportation and the Governor of DKI Jakarta, we are witnessing the integration of payment systems in the environment of transportation modes, both land - sea - air - railways, and also have the full support of the Regional Government, in this case the Regional Government of the Provincial Capital city of DKI Jakarta. 6. This signing is a form of synergy between the Central Government, namely the Ministry of Transportation as the Authority in the field of Transportation; Local Governments, namely the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta; and Bank Indonesia as the payment system authority. 7. We consider this synergy to be very necessary to realize the integration of electronic payment systems between different modes of transportation but is in one region, so as to be able to create more efficient services and increase convenience and comfort for the community. 8. On this occasion, we would also like to specifically express our gratitude to the Ministry of Home Affairs as the supervisor of all Local Governments in Indonesia, and to the Ministry of SOEs as the coach of SOEs in this case in the field of transportation for close support and coordination in efforts to advance the National Non-Cash Movement, including through electronification of payments in the public transportation sector. Ladies and Gentlemen Of Our Respected Audience, 9. In the midst of the increasing urban population, the need for a variety of quality modesof transportation services is inevitable. On the other hand, along with the rapid development of information technology, demands for payment services that are increasingly secure, smooth, and efficient are also inevitable. 10. Therefore, synergy in encouraging people to pay for public transportation in a non-cash manner while integrating payments for various modes of transportation that currently still stand alone is our joint concrete progress in responding to the needs of society and the development of teknology. 11. In that context, in order to ensure its effectiveness and alignment with Bank Indonesia's policy direction in the field of payment system, we underline 3 main aspects that need to be guidelines, yes it is : (1) The use of electronic money as an instrumen payment for public transportation in place of tickets. This is considering the characteristics of electronic money that are in accordance with the needs of transportation transactions, namely safe, accurate, practical, and fast in processing transactions, so as to be able to serve high passenger v olume at one time to avoid queues. (2) Standardization of electronic money instruments in line with the National Payment Gateway (NPG) policy. The standardization is realized through the use of SAM Multiapplet in accordance with the criteria set by Bank Indonesia for electronic money berbasis chip, as well as in the future for electronic money server-based. (3) Maintain the sustainability of the business model and reward existing investments by adopting a pricing scheme in accordance with best practices. In this case, the imposition of a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) and/or Terminal Usage Fee (TUF) in each transaction is expected to maintain the fairness of income from each party, preventing the emergence of rents economy, while providing incentives for cashless payment infrastructure. 12. If these three things can be realized, then electronic money-based public transportation payments from various issuers (multi-issuers) will be able to be used in various modes of transportation (multi-issuer) mode). Fatherk/Mother of Attendees We Respect, 13. However, observing the diversity of modes along with each operator and payment system as in the Jabodetabek area, the Bank Indonesia considers the need for an Electronic Fare Collection (EFC) entity that does not carry out 4 main functions in the integration of intermodal payment systems, namely: (1) Provide, monitor and manage a dashboard of public transport data, including traffic data pen um pa ng which will provide a portrait of public transport behavior, which will be an important part in formulation of transport policy. (2) Conducting reconciliation, clearing and settlement processes between operators (3) Managing public service obligations (PSO) from several operators, namely price subsidies that are borne by the STATE BUDGET or APBD. (4) Organizing Customer Relation Management, including providing top-up facilities such as vending machines and compiling Customer Loyalty Programs such as memberships and discounts. 14. Then, taking into account the different ownership of each mode operator, as well as the existence of a Public Service Obligation in the form of price subsidies that are also different in the Jabodetabek area, Bank Indonesia view the synergy that needs to be pursued is through the formation of 2 different EFC entities. 15. The first EFC entitas houses the modes of transportation managed by BUMN, namely the Jakarta Commuter Train, PPD, Damri and in the near future plus the Soekarno-Hatta airport train, namely Railink, and LRT Bodetabek. For this group, the role of PT. Railway Indonesia under the direction of the Ministry of SOEs can become the EFC entity. 16.While the second EFC entity is the one that houses the mode of transportation under the management of BUMD, namely Transjakarta, and in the future it will be added mrt, as well as LRT Jakarta. For this group is expected a consortium can be formed under the DKI Jakarta Provincial Government to become the second EFC entity. 17. With the target time for the formation of the two EFC entities, namely by the end of 2017, the use of electronic money from various issuers (multi-zssuer) will not only be can be used in various modes of transportation (multi-modal), but will also operate in an interconnected and interoperated environment. Furthermore, by the end of 2018 it is expected that the two EFCs will be interconnected and can provide fully integrated services. And later the two EFCs will also be connected to the integration carried out on toll roads through the Electronic Toll Collection (ETC). 18.So that we optimis jabodetabek community in the future will be given more choices of electronic money products, with access to wider inter-mode transportation utilization, and with the ease of instrument purchases and top-ups are constantly increasing. This is certainly in line with the direction of Smart City development in DKI Jakarta Province through one of its elements, namely Smart Mobility in the form of public transportation integration. Ladies and Gentlemen Of Our Respected Audience, 19. The signing of the Collective Agreement this morning we believe will further strengthen the momentum of improving the efficiency of public services through the implementation of cashless payments. We are also working on this in other sectors, as we have said. 20. We are optimistic that the strategis partnership that was built will bring huge benefits, both to the user community, operator business entities , and all relevant authorities. Some of the main benefits that Of course, we hope is an increase in accountability and security of transactions, an improvement in the quality of transportation data, and an improvement in the quality of services from all modes of transportation. 21. Therefore, before ending this speech, we would also like to express our gratitude for the commitment of all transportation mode operators operating in the Jabodetabek area. We believe that the success of the Jabodetabek area will one day be an example and role model that allows other cities in Indonesia to learn and follow it. 22.May God Almighty always ease our steps in an effort to provide the best service and benefits for the people of Indonesia. That's it and thank you. Wassalammualaikum Wr. Wb. Governor of Bank Indonesia Agus D.W. Martowardojo
text_original: -Sambutan Gubernur Bank Indonesia- Pena ndatanganan Kesepakatan Bersama Antara Bank Indonesia dengan Kementerian Perhubungan RI & Kesepakatan Bersama Antara BPTJ, Pemerintah Provinsi DKI Jakarta, dan Seluruh Operator Moda di Jabodetabek tentang Pengembangan Integrasi Sistem Pembayaran Elektronik Sektor Transporta si Jakarta, 6 September 2017 Yang Kami Hormati: <95> Menteri Perhubungan RI, Bpk Budi Karya Sumadi <95> Gubernur DKI Jakarta, Bpk Djarot Syaifui Hidayat <95> Deputi Bidang Usaha Jasa Keuangan, Jasa Survei, dan Jasa Konsuitasi Kementerian BUMN, Bpk Gatot Trihargo <95> Ke pa la Badan Pengeioia Transportasi Jabodetabek, Bpk Bambang Prihantono <95> Deputi Gubernur Bank Indonesia, Bpk Sugeng <95> Para Pejabat Eseion I di Lingkungan Kementerian/Lembaga <95> Para Pimpinan Perbankan, a.i. Direktur Utama BRI, BNI, Bank Mandiri, BTN, BCA, dan Bank DKI <95> Para Pimpinan Badan Usaha Penyedia Layanan Transportasi Pubiik di wiiayah Jabodetabek, yaitu Direksi Transjakarta, Kereta Commuter Jabodetabek, PPD, Damri, MRT, LRT, Railink <95> Para Pimpinan Perusahaan Switching <95> Bapak/Ibu, Hadirin Sekaiian Yang Berbahagia Assaiammuaiaikum Wr. Wb. Seiamat Pagi dan Saiam Sejahtera Bagi Kita Semua. 1. Puji dan syukur marilah kita panjatkan kepada Tuhan Yang Maha Kuasa, dan terimakasih atas kepemimpinan Bapak Menteri Perhubungan serta Bapak Gubernur DKI Jakarta sehingga pada hari ini kita semua dapat hadir menandatangani Kesepakatan Bersama untuk mewujudkan sistem pembayaran elektronik yang terintegrasi pada sektor transportasi. 2. Kita menyambut baik berbagai kemajuan reformasi dan perbaikan- perbaikan di area sektor riil yang terus diupayakan oleh Pemerintah Pusat maupun Pemerintah Daerah. Hal ini tentu perlu didukung dengan peningkatan layanan sistem pembayaran. Karena kalau tidak, efisiensi tidak akan terbentuk. 3. Kita menyambut baik bahwa program elektronifikasi dan Gerakan Nasional Non Tunai tidak hanya ada di Jakarta, tetapi ada di seluruh daerah di Indonesia dan di berbagai Kementerian dan Pemerintah Daerah. Kita juga menyambut baik komitmen pemerintah untuk menyalurkan bantuan sosial seluruhnya secara non tunai. 4. Kita juga menyambut baik upaya yang dilakukan dimana seluruh ruas tol yang ada di Indonesia telah berkomitmen untuk melakukan elektronifikasi pembayaran dan saling terintegrasi guna menciptakan efisiensi. 5. Dan pada hari ini, dibawah kepemimpinan Menteri Perhubungan dan Gubernur DKI Jakarta, kita menyaksikan integrasi sistem pembayaran di lingkungan moda-moda transportasi, baik darat - laut - udara - perkeretapian, dan juga mendapat dukungan penuh dari Pemerintah Daerah, dalam hal ini Pemerintah Daerah Ibu Kota Provinsi DKI Jakarta. 6. Penandatanganan ini merupakan wujud sinergi antara Pemerintah Pusat yaitu Kementerian Perhubungan selaku Otoritas di bidang Transportasi; Pemerintah Daerah yaitu Pemerintah Provinsi DKI Jakarta; dan Bank Indonesia selaku otoritas sistem pembayaran. 7. Sinergi ini kami pandang amat dibutuhkan guna mewujudkan integrasi sistem pembayaran elektronik antar moda transportasi yang berbeda namun berada dalam satu kewilayahan, sehingga mampu menciptakan layanan yang semakin efisien dan meningkatkan kemudahan serta kenyamanan bagi masyarakat. 8. Dalam kesempatan ini, kami juga ingin secara khusus menyampaikan terimakasih kepada Kementerian Dalam Negeri selaku pembina seluruh Pemerintah Daerah di Indonesia, dan kepada Kementerian BUMN selaku pembina BUMN dalam hal ini pada bidang transportasi atas dukungan dan koordinasi yang erat dalam upaya memajukan Gerakan Nasional Non Tunai, termasuk melalui elektronifikasi pembayaran pada sektor transportasi publik. Bapak/Ibu Hadirin Yang Kami Hormati, 9. Ditengah semakin meningkatnya populasi penduduk perkotaan, kebutuhan ragam moda layanan transportasi publik yang berkualitas tidaklah terhindarkan. Di sisi lain, seiring pesatnya perkembangan teknologi informasi, tuntutan akan layanan pembayaran yang semakin aman, lancar, dan efisien juga tidak terelakkan. 10. Oleh karena itu, sinergi dalam mendorong masyarakat untuk membayar transportasi publik secara non tunai sekaligus mengintegrasikan pembayaran berbagai moda transportasi yang saat ini masih berdiri sendiri-sendiri adalah progress konkrit kita bersama dalam merespons kebutuhan masyarakat serta perkembangan teknologi. 11. Dalam konteks tersebut, guna memastikan efektivitas dan keselarasannya dengan arah kebijakan Bank Indonesia di bidang sistem pembayaran, kami menggarisbawahi 3 aspek utama yang perlu menjadi pedoman, ya itu: (1) Penggunaan uang elektronik sebagai instrumen pembayaran transportasi publik menggantikan tiket. Hal ini mengingat karakteristik uang elektronik yang sesuai dengan kebutuhan transaksi transportasi, yaitu aman, akurat, praktis, serta cepat dalam pemrosesan transaksinya, sehingga mampu melayani volume penumpang yang tinggi dalam satu waktu guna menghindari antrian. (2) Standarisasi instrumen uang elektronik yang selaras dengan kebijakan National Payment Gateway (NPG). Standarisasi tersebut diwujudkan melalui penggunaan SAM Multiapplet yang sesuai dengan kriteria yang ditetapkan oleh Bank Indonesia untuk uang elektronik berbasis chip, serta kedepan untuk uang elektronik berbasis server. (3) Menjaga sustaina bi litas model bisnis dan menghargai investasi yang telah ada dengan mengadopsi skema harga {pricing} sesuai dengan best practices. Dalam hal ini pengenaan besaran Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) dan/atau Terminal Usage Fee (TUF) dalam tiap kali transaksi diharapkan dapat menjaga kewajaran pendapatan dari setiap pihak, mencegah timbulnya rente ekonomi, sekaligus memberikan insentif perluasan infrastruktur pembayaran non tunai. 12. Apabila ketiga hal tersebut dapat diwujudkan, maka pembayaran transportasi publik berbasis uang elektronik dari berbagai penerbit (multi- issuer) akan dapat digunakan di berbagai moda transportasi (multi-moda). Bapak/Ibu Hadirin Yang Kami Hormati, 13. Namun, mencermati keberagaman moda beserta masing-masing operator dan sistem pembayarannya sebagaimana di wilayah Jabodetabek, Bank Indonesia memandang diperlukan suatu entitas Electronic Fare Collection (EFC) yang paling tidak menjalankan 4 fungsi utama dalam integrasi sistem pembayaran antar-moda, yaitu: (1) Menyediakan, memantau dan mengelola dashboarddata transportasi publik, termasuk data lalu lintas pen um pa ng yang akan memberikan potret perilaku transportasi masyarakat, yang akan menjadi bagian penting dalam perumusan kebijakan transportasi. (2) Melakukan proses rekonsiliasi, kliring dan setelmen antar-operator (3) Mengelola Publik Service Obligation (PSO) dari beberapa operator, yaitu subsidi harga yang ditanggung oleh APBN atau APBD. (4) Menyelenggarakan Customer Relation Management, termasuk penyediaan fasilitas top-up seperti vending machine dan menyusun Customer Loyalty Program seperti membership dan diskon. 14. Kemudian, dengan mempertimbangkan kepemilikan yang berbeda dari masing-masing operator moda, serta adanya Public Service Obligation dalam bentuk subsidi harga yang juga berbeda di wilayah Jabodetabek, maka Bank Indonesia memandang sinergi yang perlu ditempuh adalah melalui pembentukan 2 entitas EFC yang berbeda. 15. Entitas EFC pertama menaungi moda transportasi yang dikelola BUMN, yaitu Kereta Commuter Jakarta, PPD, Damri dan dalam waktu dekat ditambah kereta bandara Soekarno-Hatta yaitu Railink, serta LRT Bodetabek. Untuk kelompok ini diharapkan peran PT. Kereta Api Indonesia dibawah arahan Kementerian BUMN dapat menjadi entitas EFC tersebut. 16.Sedangkan entitas EFC kedua adalah yang menaungi moda transportasi dibawah pengelolaan BUMD, yaitu Transjakarta, dan kedepan akan ditambah MRT, serta LRT Jakarta. Untuk kelompok ini diharapkan dapat dibentuk konsorsium dibawah Pemerintah Provinsi DKI Jakarta guna menjadi entitas EFC yang kedua. 17. Dengan target waktu pembentukan dua entitas EFC tersebut yaitu pada akhir tahun 2017, maka penggunaan uang elektronik dari berbagai penerbit (multi-zssuer) nantinya tidak hanya akan dapat digunakan pada berbagai moda transportasi (multi-moda), namun juga akan beroperasi dalam lingkungan yang saling interconnected dan interoperated. Lebih lanjut, pada akhir tahun 2018 diharapkan kedua EFC tersebut telah saling terhubung dan dapat menyediakan layanan yang terintegrasi penuh. Dan nantinya kedua EFC tersebut juga akan terhubung dengan integrasi yang dilakukan pada jalan tol melalui Electronic Toll Collection (ETC). 18.Sehingga kami optimis masyarakat Jabodetabek kedepan akan diberikan lebih banyak pilihan produk uang elektronik, dengan akses pemanfaatan antar-moda transportasi yang semakin luas, serta dengan kemudahan pembelian instrumen dan top-up yang terus meningkat. Hal ini tentunya sejalan dengan arah pengembangan Smart City di Provinsi DKI Jakarta melalui salah satu unsurnya yaitu Smart Mobility dalam bentuk integrasi transportasi publik. Bapak/Ibu Hadirin Yang Kami Hormati, 19. Penandatanganan Kesepakatan Bersama di pagi hari ini kami yakini akan semakin memperkuat momentum peningkatan efisiensi layanan publik melalui penerapan pembayaran secara non tunai. Hal ini juga sedang terus kami upayakan pada sektor lain, sebagaimana telah kami sampaikan. 20. Kami optimis bahwa kemitraan strategis yang dibangun akan membawa manfaat yang begitu besar, baik bagi masyarakat pengguna, badan usaha operator, maupun seluruh otoritas terkait. Beberapa manfaat utama yang tentunya kita harapkan adalah peningkatan akuntabilitas serta keamanan transaksi, peningkatan kualitas data transportasi, dan peningkatan kualitas layanan dari seluruh moda transportasi. 21. Oleh karena itu, sebelum mengakhiri sambutan ini, kami juga ingin menyampaikan terimakasih atas komitmen seluruh operator moda transportasi yang beroperasi di wilayah Jabodetabek. Kami meyakini keberhasilan wilayah Jabodetabek kelak akan menjadi contoh dan role model yang membuat kota-kota lain di Indonesia dapat mempelajari dan mengikutinya. 22.Semoga Tuhan Yang Maha Kuasa senantiasa meringankan langkah kita dalam upaya memberikan pelayanan dan manfaat terbaik bagi masyarakat Indonesia. Sekian dan terima kasih. Wassalammualaikum Wr. Wb. Gubernur Bank Indonesia Agus D.W. Martowardojo

Title: Sambutan Gubernur Bank Indonesia, Agus D.W. Martowardojo pada Penandatanganan MoU antara Bank-Bank Anggota HIMBARA dan PT Telkom Indonesia tentang Pembentukan Perusahaan Prinsipal, Jakarta, 09 September 2016
text: -Remarks by the Governor of Bank Indonesia- Signing of the MoU between HIM BARA Member Banks and PT Telkom Indonesia about Principal Company Formation Jakarta, 9th September 2016 What we respect: 95 Minister of SOEs, Mrs. Rini S. Soemarno 95 Deputy Commissioner of the Financial Services Authority, Mr. Budi Armanto 95 President Director of Telkom Indonesia, Bpk Alex J Sinaga 95 Chairman of the Association of State-Owned Banks (HIMBARA) as the President Director of BRI, Mr. Asmawi Syam 95 President Director of BNI, BpkAchmad Baiquni 95 President Director of Bank Mandiri, Bpk Kartika Wirjoatmodjo 95 President Director of BTN, Mr. Maryono 95 Eseion I Officials in the ministry of SOEs 95 Ladies and gentlemen of the happy invited audience Assaiammuaiaikum Wr. Wb. It's morning and Saiam's well-being for all of us. 1. First of all let us offer praise and gratitude to the presence of True Source, for only for His approval can we all gather this morning to follow along" MoU between HIMBARA Member Banks and Telkom Indonesiaa on the Establishment of Principle Company" 2. Starting our remarks, let us express our appreciation and condolences to the Ministry of SOEs, Banks HIM BARA, and Telkom for an initial step that we have made very critical for the efficiency of the upcoming national payment system. 3. Bank Indonesia as the National Payment System Authority in this case certainly supports the efforts made by the Government together with industry in the spirit of increasing competitiveness, increasing efficiency, and increase efforts to build the independence of the national payment system. Ladies and Gentlemen, Ladies and Gentlemen whom we respect, 4. As a developing country with economic growth that reached 5.5% (yoy) in the last five years and Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in 2015 of Rp 11,540 Trillion, Indonesia certainly has the need for the provision of a huge retail payment system. This is necessary to support the increase in economic activity of the entire community. 5. Based on data from Bank Indonesia, the nominal ATM/Debit Card transactions in 2015 have touched Rp 13 trillion/day, with transaction volume reaching 12.5 million transactions/day. This achievement was also followed by the continuation of transaction volume growth in the last five years, which on average grew above 20% (yoy). 6. Observing these developments, retail payment system service providers, in this context including principals, will face various challenges, including demands for capacity building, quality service readiness, system security and integrity, and fare affordability. Moreover, the processing of such transactions is carried out through the infrastructure and network of the principal company. 7. Therefore, we welcome the initial study and the inclusive follow-up of the Ministry of SOEs in realizing the idea of establishing a Principal through the synergy of SOEs as part of the Roadmap Financial Services and Banking Sector. 8. Armed with the reach of the HIM BARA retail banking payment system which represents at least 50% of the national Debit Card transaction volume, as well as telkom Indonesia's capabilities which have experience in supporting HIMBARA in providing ATM LINK network, Bank Indonesia responds positively to this idea and believes in the added value that can be provided. Ladies and Gentlemen, Ladies and Gentlemen whom we respect, 9. After reviewing the proposal submitted by the Minister of SOEs regarding the plan to establish this Principal. Bank Indonesia on 11th July 2016 has provided support and approval of principles, as well as conveyed 4 (four) main things that need to be followed up, namely: 1) In order to form a legal entity that will later act as a principal. 2) In order to be committed to providing a system that is able to connect (interconnection) and saling can serve (interoperability) with existing systems. 3) In order to be committed to meeting international standards and best practices for the implementation of payment systems, such as the use of central bank money in settlement activities. 4) In order tocomply with the terms and conditions that will be set by Bank Indonesia for aspects such as pricing, capital, ownership, and system security. 10. In response to the principle approval given, we have also received a statement of ability from the Ministry of State-Owned Enterprises on August 10, 2016.
