Bapak/Ibu, Hadirin yang kami hormati, 14. Bank Indonesia telah secara seksama mengikuti dan mendalami perkembangan inovasi teknologi pada layanan jasa keuangan yang ditawarkan oleh Fintech. Kami sampai kepada kesimpulan bahwa inovasi teknologi adalah suatu keniscayaan. Dengan pesatnya perubahan landskap yang terjadi, regulasi tidak seharusnya mencoba untuk mendahului inovasi. 15. Namun kami meyakini, bahwa regulasi perlu selalu berada di dekat inovasi. Sambil mencermati berbagai potensi risiko yang timbul, iklim berusaha yang kondusif perlu diwujudkan. Dalam hal ini, pendirian BI-FTO adalah upaya kami untuk menjaga level of playing field melalui rezim regulasi yang berimbang dan proporsional tanpa harus mematikan laju inovasi. 16. Sebagai gugus tugas baru yang diposisikan dekat dengan industri, terdapat 4 fungsi utama yang akan dilakukan oleh BI-FTO, yaitu: - Pertama, adalah sebagai katalisator/fasilitator bagi pertukaran ide inovatif pengembangan Fintech di Indonesia. - Kedua, adalah sebagai business intelligence, dimana BI-FTO akan secara rutin memberikan update melalui diseminasi hasil kajian dan pertemuan termasuk dengan kementerian dan otoritas terkait serta lembaga internasional. - Ketiga, adalah fungsi asesmen. Dalam hal ini, BI-FTO akan melakukan pemantauan dan pemetaan atas potensi manfaat sekaligus risiko dari inovasi model bisnis dan produk yang ditawarkan. Hasil asesmen tersebut akan menjadi dasar bagi perumusan kebijakan di Bank Indonesia. - Keempat, adalah fungsi koordinasi dan komunikasi, yang berperan memberikan pemahaman atas kerangka pengaturan yang ada, dan mendorong harmonisasi regulasi lintas otoritas. Bapak/Ibu, Hadirin yang kami hormati, 17. Sebagai bagian dari fungsi asesmen yang dilakukan BI-FTO, kami juga memperkenalkan didalamnya sebuah inisiatif yang dinamakan Regulatory Sandbox. Inisiatif ini dapat dianalogikan sebagai sebuah laboratorium yang digunakan bersama oleh pelaku Fintech dan regulator untuk menguji model bisnis dan produk/layanan sebelum masuk ke dalam rezim perizinan secara penuh. 18. Pengujian ini dilakukan dalam lingkungan terbatas untuk memastikan identifikasi dan mitigasi seluruh risiko yang mungkin timbul. Pembatasan tersebut diberikan dalam bentuk perizinan terbatas pada layanan, jangka waktu, dan/atau wilayah penyelenggaraan. 19. Melalui Regulatory Sandbox, regulator dapat memonitor secara intensif keberlangsungan Fintech dalam perimeter risiko yang terjaga. Selain digunakan untuk evaluasi, hal ini juga akan memberikan ruang bagi regulator untuk mengambil langkah antisipatif dan korektif di waktu yang tepat apabila diperlukan. 20. Lebih lanjut, data yang dihasilkan sepanjang proses monitoring dan pendampingan dapat dioptimalkan untuk meningkatkan kualitas respon kebijakan. Karena ditengah tren pertumbuhannya yang eksponensial, data telah menjadi aset utama bagi regulator maupun pelaku industri sebagai dasar pengambilan keputusan. 21. Seiring akan beroperasinya BI-FTO, kami mengharapkan ikatan jejaring pelaku Fintech dengan otoritas akan semakin erat. Dengan secara konsisten meningkatkan basis pengetahuan atas proses dan fungsi yang dilakukan oleh Fintech, kami meyakini BI-FTO akan dapat berkontribusi dalam menciptakan industri Fintech yang sehat. Bapak/Ibu, Hadirin yang kami hormati, 22. Selain dari perkembangan Fintech yang merupakan cermin dari inovasi teknologi di area keuangan, Bank Indonesia juga mencermati kuatnya inovasi teknologi dalam area perdagangan. Sebagaimana yang telah kami singgung sebelumnya, pertumbuhan dan adopsi e- commerce oleh masyarakat Indonesia begitu luar biasa. Terminologi "Pasar" sebagai tempat bertemunya penjual dan pembeli saat ini sepenuhnya telah dapat diwujudkan secara maya. 23. Meskipun tidak lagi harus dilakukan dengan tatap muka secara fisik, namun kebutuhan transaksi melalui sistem pembayaran tetap menjadi bagian yang tidak terpisahkan dari aktivitas jual-beli. Oleh karena itu, Bank Indonesia memandang perlu untuk melengkapi ketentuan pada area sistem pembayaran yang sudah ada, khususnya melengkapi ketentuan mengenai Alat Pembayaran Menggunakan Kartu (APMK), Uang Elektronik, dan Transfer Dana yang telah lebih dulu ada. 24. Peraturan Bank Indonesia mengenai Penyelenggaraan Pemrosesan Transaksi Pembayaran (PBI No. 18/40/PBI/2016) kami terbitkan sebagai wujud komitmen kami atas 4 hal utama, yaitu (1) Mengakomodir inovasi; (2) Meningkatkan keamanan, termasuk pemenuhan standar dan audit keamanan secara berkala; (3) Menjaga level of playing field, dan (4) Perlindungan konsumen, ditengah ancaman /randan cyber security yang berkejaran dengan inovasi. 25. Ketentuan ini mengatur dua subjek utama dalam suatu aktivitas pemrosesan transaksi pembayaran, yaitu: - Penyelenggara Jasa SP, sebagai pihak yang bertanggung jawab atas tahapan Otorisasi, Kliring, dan Setelmen. Pihak ini yaitu penyelenggara Switching, Payment Gateway, dan Dorn pet Elektronik (e-Wallet) diwajibkan untuk memiliki izin dari BI. - Penyelenggara Penunjang Transaksi Pembayaran, seperti perusahaan penyedia kartu, ATM, EDC, dan data center. Dalam hal ini, Penyelenggara Jasa SP perlu meminta persetujuan kerjasama dan bertanggungjawab untuk memastikan keamanan dan kelancaran pemrosesan transaksi yang difasilitasi mereka. 26. Selain itu, dalam rangka meningkatkan ketahanan dan daya saing industri sistem pembayaran nasional, ketentuan ini juga mengatur struktur kepemilikan dari penyelenggara jasa sistem pembayaran. 27. Pada akhirnya, seluruh pengaturan ini kami yakini selaras dengan berbagai inisiatif lintas Kementerian dan Otoritas terkait, terutama dengan Roadmap e-Commerce yang baru saja diterbitkan sebagai Paket Kebijakan Ekonomi Jilid XIV di tanggal 10 November 2016. Bapak/Ibu, Hadirin yang kami hormati, 28. Bank Indonesia menyambut baik dan mendukung penerbitan Roadmap e-Commerce ini. Langkah ini kami panda ng juga sejalan dengan Arahan Presiden RI pasca kunjungan kerja menghadiri Konferensi G20 di Tiongkok dalam Rapat Terbatas tanggal 27 September 2016 perihal Pengembangan Ekonomi Digital. 29. Presiden RI melihat kemajuan ekonomi digital di Tiongkok yang sangat menakjubkan, dan mengarahkan kepada seluruh instansi terkait, termasuk Bank Indonesia untuk dapat mendukung pengembangan ekonomi digital di Indonesia. Lebih lanjut, dukungan tersebut juga perlu diberikan agar Generasi Muda Indonesia yang mempersiapkan perusahaan Start-Up dan berbagai inisiatif di bidang ekonomi digital dapat senantiasa kita bantu penuh. 30. Oleh karena itu, kesempatan hari ini juga merupakan respons Bank Indonesia bersama dengan kementerian dan otoritas terkait, untuk kita dapat mendukung perkembangan ekonomi digital di Indonesia, termasuk dunia usaha khususnya yang berskala kecil dan menengah. 31. Kami mencermati bahwa Roadmap tersebut akan menjadi pedoman yang komprehensif baik bagi regulator maupun industri. Mulai dari aspek pendanaan, kualitas SDM, sampai dengan aspek perlindungan konsumen serta infrastruktur menjadi fokus bahasan. Hemat kami penerbitan nya a mat tepat waktu dan tepat sasaran guna mendukung pertumbuhan e-commerce dan juga Fintech di Indonesia. Bapak/Ibu, Hadirin yang kami hormati, 32. Berbekal kolaborasi dan dukungan regulasi yang tepat, kami optimis pelaku Fintech dapat berjalan beriringan dengan institusi keuangan tradisional yang lebih dulu ada. Adaptasi yang dilakukan oleh institusi keuangan konvensional, serta bergabungnya Fintech menjadi bagian sistem keuangan kami yakini akan mendorong kompetisi yang sehat dan memberikan nilai tambah serta alternatif bagi masyarakat. 33. Dalam konteks tersebut, kami juga perlu mengingatkan kepada institusi keuangan konvensional agar tidak terjebak dalam zona nyaman. Gelombang inovasi datang tidak terbendung dan menciptakan kompetisi yang semakin ketat. Hanya pelaku yang memiliki model bisnis yang solid dan adaptif yang dapat tumbuh secara berkesinambungan di masa yang akan datang. 34. Menutup sambutan kami, kami berharap kolaborasi antara pelaku dengan otoritas, dan antar otoritas dapat semakin erat dan produktif, sehingga tren positif perkembangan Fintech dan e-Commerce di Indonesia dapat terus dipertahankan. 35. Dalam prosesi peresmian BI-FTO pada hari ini, akan ditampilkan secara simbolis bagaimana ketujuh Regulator dengan didampingi oleh tujuh pelaku Fintech/Start-Up secara bersama-sama membangun koordinasi dan kolaborasi untuk mendukung perkembangan ekonomi digital di Indonesia. 36. Selain itu, pada acara ini juga difasilitasi pertemuan dan kesempatan berdialog antara para pelaku Start-Up dengan investor. Sehingga dapat diikuti dengan seksama bagaimana profil Start-Up yang diinginkan oleh investor, dan bagaimana pelaku Start-Up dapat mulai membangun komunikasi kepada investor dengan cara yang baik. 37. Bahkan Bapak Presiden dalam Rapat Terbatas sebagaimana kami singgung sebelumnya, meminta secara khusus untuk seluruh pihak dapat ikut membimbing para Pelaku Start-Up. Supaya mereka siap, dan tidak perlu melepas investasi mereka terlalu cepat. Kemudian, pada acara ini kami juga memfasilitasi para Pelaku Start-Up untuk dapat duduk bersama dengan Regulator guna membicarakan aspek pemenuhan regulasi dari berbagai Kementerian dan Otoritas terkait. 38. Semoga segenap upaya ini memberikan pesan, bahwa usaha-usaha yang baru berdiri tidak perlu terus menjadi usaha kecil. Dalam kurun waktu 10 sampai 15 tahun, usaha-usaha tersebut dapat menjadi usaha yang besar. Bank Indonesia bersama para regulator terkait berkomitmen dan ingin melihat Generasi Muda Indonesia bangkit, dan kita akan berikan dukungan dan pendampingan yang diperlukan. 39. Dengan sinergi bersama untuk meningkatkan efisiensi, mendorong inklusi, dan menumbuhkembangkan inovasi, maka revolusi digital niscaya akan dapat mengeluarkan seluruh potensi nyatanya bagi kehidupan masyarakat Indonesia yang lebih baik dan sejahtera. Sekian dan Terimakasih Wassalammu'alaikum Warrahmatullahi Wabarakatuh. Agus D.W. Title: Sambutan Deputi Gubernur Bank Indonesia, Sugeng Pada Seminar Nasional "Penyaluran Bansos Nontunai untuk Perluas Akses Keuangan Masyarakat", Jakarta, 18 Desember 2017
text: Remarks by the Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia national seminar " Non-Cash Distribution of Social Assistance as a Strategy to Expand Public Financial Access" , Jakarta, 18 December 2017 What we respect: 1. Deputy for Coordination of Poverty Reduction and Social Protection, Coordinating Ministry for Human Development and Culture, Mr. Tubagus Achmad Choesni 2. Director General of Postal and Informatics Organizers, Ministry of Communication and Informatics, Mr.AhmadM. Ramii 3. Director General of Handling the Poor, Ministry of Social Affairs, Mr.AndiZainai A. Dulung 4. Deputy for Financial Services Business, Survey and Consultant Services, Ministry of SOEs, Mr. Gatot Trihargo 5. Executive Secretary, TNP2K, Mr. Bambang Widianto (The list is optional, can be unnamed, just the institution) 6. Officials from the Financial Services Authority a. Head of the Financial Literacy and Inclusion Department, Mrs. Sondang Martha Samosir b. Senior Executive Analyst of Group Strategic Committee andResearch Center, Mrs. Ida Rumondang 7. Officials from the Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs: Assistant Deputy for Capital Markets and Financial Institutions, Mr. A. Heri Susanto 8. Official from the National Development Planning Agency: Director of Poverty Reduction and Social Welfare, Mrs. Vivi Yulaswati 9. Official from the Ministry of Agrarian affairs and Spatial Planning: Secretary of the Directorate General of Agricultural Legal Relations, Mr. Pioneer 10. Officials from the Ministry of Finance: Head of the Financial Sector Policy Center, Fiscal Policy Agency: Mrs. Ayu Sukorini 11. Officials from Bank Indonesia a. Head of the Payment System Policy Department, Mrs. Eni V. Panggabean b. Director of the Payment System Policy Department, Mr. Pungky P. Wibowo and ladies and gentlemen of the audience whom I respect Assalammualaikum Wr. Wb. Sela mat Pagi and Peace be upon us all, [Preamble] 1. First of all, let us together offer praise and gratitude to the presence of Allah Almighty, God Almighty, for for upon His gift and favor we can all gather in the morning it is in good health and full of happiness. 2. On this good occasion, we will jointly attend the National Seminar with the theme "Distribution of Non-Cash Social Assistance as a Strategy for Expanding Public Financial Access ". The selection of a theme that we think is very important, given that expanding people's access to finance is one of the biggest challenges facing this nation, including due to the large number of indonesian population, as well as the vast area and geographical conditions of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia which consists of 16 thousand islands. 3. On behalf of Bank Indonesia, which today collaborated with the National Financial Inclusion Council and the Non-Cash Social Assistance Control Team in organizing this national seminar, express our gratitude the greatest love to all resource persons and panelists from Ministries and Institutions, for being willing to attend for various information and safe information related to expanding financial access communities under the grand umbrella of the National Financial Inclusion Strategy, with social assistance as one of its main strategies. 4. Through this activity, it is hoped that all relevant stakeholders can have the same views and understandings, so that they can move in an integrated manner to succeed in achieving the level of inclusion finance in Indonesia, as stipulated in the National Financial Strategy Inclusive, that is, 75% of the population in Indonesia already has an account with a formal financial institution. [National Strategy for Financial Inclusion] Ladies and Gentlemen of the Audience We Respect, 5. As we all know, the condition of financial access in Indonesia is still not encouraging. This is reflected in the low level of keuangan inclusion in Indonesia, which based on the world bank's last survey in 2014 was only 36%. This means that only 36% of the adult population in Indonesia has an account with a formal financial institution. 6. The low level of financial inclusion can be negative in various aspects. a. From the community side, financial exclusivity has an impact on the absence of a savings culture so that people do not have funds just in case or needs in the future. In addition, financial exclusivity can also close the opportunity for the community to cultivate assets, so that it cannot improve welfare, and cause inefficiency in doing payment transactions. b. In terms of financial system stability, financial exclusivity can hinder the growth of n Third Party Funds , resulting in a suboptimal intermediation function of financial institutions. Not only that, financial exclusivity can also enlarge the shadow economy or unrecorded economic transactions so that they are prone to cause money laundering and terrorism financing, and reducing '/w/Ter' for the financial system in the event of a recession. c. Finally, for the national economy, financial exclusivity can widen social inequality, not support the reduction of poverty and economic growth, and increase national inefficiency . 7. Taking into account the negative impacts that can occur, the need for expanded access to finance is something that cannot be delayed anymore. Therefore , in 2016, the Government through the Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs has issued Presidential Regulation Number 82 of 2016 concerning the National Strategy for Financial Inclusion (SNKI). 8. The Presidential Regulation was issued to strengthen the commitment of the parties in realizing the expansion of financial access, especially for the unbanked community. As we mentioned earlier, the main target to be achieved through the Presidential Regulation is toreduce the level of financial inclusion to 75% in 2019. 9. In achieving this target, we can generally convey that the National Financial Inclusion Strategy has established 5 Pillars, namely (i) Financial Education in the First Pillar, (ii) Rights Properti Community on the Second Pillar, (iii) Intermediation Facilities and Financial Distribution Channels in the Third Pillar, (iv) Financial Services in the Government Sector on the Fourth Pillar, and (v) Protection Consumers on the Fifth Pillar. 10. The five pillars are supported by three basic foundations, namely (i) Conducive Policies and Regulations, (ii) Supporting Financial Information Technology and Infrastructure, and (iii) Organization and Effective Implementation Mechanisms. 11. In each of the pillars and foundations that we mentioned, there are various strategies and programs that will be carried out by various Ministries and Institutions. Those strategies and programs are what we need to know and understand together, so that each can contribute according to their respective tasks and responsibilities. 12. We will not explain each of the programs and strategies that exist on the pillars and foundations of the National Financial Inclusion Strategy, because of course it will be elaborated by speakers and panelists who are already present and ready sharehis knowledge with all of us this morning. [Cashless Social Assistance] Happy Ladies and Gentlemen, 13. Today's national seminar will also discuss more deeply the transformation of non-cash social assistance distribution as an effort to acceleratethe expansion of financial access. 14. Accelerating the expansion of financial access through non-cash social assistance is considered a major impact step, considering that the number of recipients of social assistance programs and subsidies is very large, that is, it almost reaches a 30 million families throughout Indonesia. 15. In addition, in order to encourage Indonesia's economic growth, which in the third quarter of 2017 recorded a figure of 5.06%, the role of social assistance is very important, especially in order to encourage consumption levels. Indonesians who are in the lower class atau bottom of the pyramid. 16. Of course, the transformation of social assistance distribution into non-cash must be carried out to realize the distribution of social assistance to be more efficient and effective, as well as support the achievement of the 6T principle, namely Right Target, Right Quantity, Right Time, Right Quality, Right Price, and Right Administration. 17. We can say on this occasion, the distribution of non-cash social assistance has been started since one year ago. Starting from the distribution of part of the Family Hope Program (PKH) non-cash in 2016 to 1.2 million Beneficiary Families (KPM) and then in 2017 the target was expanded to 6 million KPM and the Non-Cash Food Assistance (BPNT) program to 1.2 million KPM. In the future, the non-cash social aid program will be gradually expanded to reach 10 million recipients, each for PKH and BPNT. 18. As a legal umbrella for the distribution of social assistance on a non-cash basis, the government through the Coordinating Ministry for Human Development and Culture this year has issued Presidential Regulation No. 63 of 2017 concerning Non-Cash Social Aid Disbursements. 19. Theissuance of the Presidential Regulation is intended to provide clear guidelines and maintain the standardization of non-cash distribution mechanisms for various social aid programs. Thus, in the event that in future developments there are various social assistance that will be distributed non-cash, the standardization mechanism can refer to the Presidential Regulation referred to and seeing the implementation of non-cash social assistance that has been implemented first. [Role of Bank Indonesia] Your Father/Mother, 20. In implementing the National Financial Inclusion Strateg i, including the distribution of non-cash social assistance as one of the main initiatives, Bank Indonesia has committed to supporting the smoothness and success of the program in question. 21. Bank Indonesia's support is realized in the Payment System Blueprint, which consists of three main pillars, namely: (i) expansion of the use of non-cash instruments (electronification), (ii) infrastructure reliable and secure payments, and (iii) robust and sharp and rigorous oversight and oversight . 22. All programs and initiatives related to financial inclusion including non-cash social assistance are implemented under the first pillar, namely electronification. In the implementation of the first pillar initiative, infrastructure support between lain in the form of the implementation of the National Payment Gateway (NPG) in the second pillar will fully contribute to interoperability and interconnection of non-cash social assistance disbursements to ensure efficiency and effectiveness of disbursements. 23. Furthermore, in order that in its implementation there are no matters that are contrary to the provisions and policies of Bank Indonesia in the field of payment system, strong and comprehensive supervision, as pillars third The Payment System Blueprint will be carried out by Bank Indonesia in the sequence of stages and phases of non-cash social assistance disbursements. 24. Not only that, considering that the implementation of financial inclusion programs and the distribution of non-cash social assistance are implemented in various regions in Indonesia, Bank Indonesia is also fully committed to the UK monitoring process and monitoring the distribution of non-cash social assistance, through Bank Indonesia Representative Offices in various provinces, regencies, and cities, which on today's occasion was also present to participate and understand the financial program inklusif and the distribution of non-cash social assistance. Recoverer Ladies and Gentlemen of the Audience We Respect, 25. I don't think we'll use any longer to deliver today's opening remarks. The main things that we mentioned earlier will be conveyed in more detail at the material session that will be presented by officials from relevant Ministries and Institutions. 26. Finally, in order to succeed efforts to expand financial access, including through the distribution of non-cash social assistance as one of the main strategi, we hope that all parties present at today can provide contributive input and fully support programs to improve financial inclusivity in Indonesia. Through shared views, close cooperation and coordination, and joint commitment between relevant Ministries and Institutions, industry players, and communities, we believe in the program this will provide great benefits for the people and also the Indonesian economy nationally. 27. That's our welcome. We hereby declare that the National Seminar "Distribution of Non-Cash Social Assistance as a Strategy for Expanding Public Financial Access" was opened. Anchovies ma love Wassalamu'alaikum Warahmatullahi Wabarakatuh Jakarta, 18th December 2017 Dr. Sugeng , Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia
text_original: Sambutan Deputi Gubernur Bank Indonesia Seminar Nasional "Penyaluran Bantuan Sosial secara Non Tunai sebagai Strategi Perluasan Akses Keuangan Masyarakat" Jakarta, 18 Desember 2017 Yang kami hormati: 1. Deputi Bidang Koordinasi Penanggulangan Kemiskinan dan Perlindungan Sosial, Kementerian Koordinator Bidang Pembangunan Manusia dan Kebudayaan, Bapak Tubagus Achmad Choesni 2. Direktur Jenderal Penyelenggara Pos dan Informatika, Kementerian Komunikasi dan Informatika, BapakAhmadM. Ramii 3. Direktur Jenderal Penanganan Fakir Miskin, Kementerian Sosial, BapakAndiZainai A. Dulung 4. Deputi Bidang Usaha Jasa Keuangan, Jasa Survei dan Konsultan, Kementerian BUMN, Bapak Gatot Trihargo 5. Sekretaris Eksekutif, TNP2K, Bapak Bambang Widianto (Daftar seianjutnya optional, dapat tidak disebutkan nama, cukup institusinya) 6. Pejabat dari Otoritas Jasa Keuangan a. Kepala Departemen Literasi dan Inklusi Keuangan, Ibu Sondang Martha Samosir b. Analis Eksekutif Senior Group Strategic Committee dan Pusat Riset, Ibu Ida Rumondang 7. Pejabat dari Kementerian Koordinator Bidang Perekonomian: Asisten Deputi Pasar Modal dan Lembaga Keuangan, Bapak A. Heri Susanto 8. Pejabat dari Badan Perencanaan Pembangunan Nasional: Direktur Penanggulangan Kemiskinan dan Kesejahteraan Sosial, Ibu Vivi Yulaswati 9. Pejabat dari Kementerian Agraria dan Tata Ruang: Sekretaris Direktorat Jenderal Hubungan Hukum Keagrariaan, Bapak Pelopor 10. Pejabat dari Kementerian Keuangan: Kepala Pusat Kebijakan Sektor Keuangan, Badan Kebijakan Fiskal: Ibu Ayu Sukorini 11. Pejabat dari Bank Indonesia a. Kepala Departemen Kebijakan Sistem Pembayaran, Ibu Eni V. Panggabean b. Direktur Departemen Kebijakan Sistem Pembayaran, Bapak Pungky P. Wibowo dan Bapak/Ibu hadirin sekalian yang saya hormati Assalammualaikum Wr. Wb. Sela mat Pagi dan Salam Sejahtera bagi kita semua, [Pembukaan] 1. Pertama-tama, marilah kita bersama-sama memanjatkan puji dan syukur ke hadirat Allah SWT, Tuhan yang Maha Kuasa, karena atas karunia dan perkenan-Nya kita semua dapat berkumpul pada pagi hari ini dalam keadaan sehat wal afiat dan penuh kebahagiaan. 2. Pada kesempatan yang baik ini, kita akan bersama-sama mengikuti Seminar Nasional dengan tema "Penyaluran Bantuan Sosial secara Non Tunai sebagai Strategi Perluasan Akses Keuangan Masyarakat". Pemilihan tema yang menurut hemat kami sangatlah penting, mengingat perluasan akses keuangan masyarakat merupakan salah satu tantangan terbesar yang dihadapi bangsa ini, antara lain dikarenakan besarnya jumlah penduduk Indonesia, serta luasnya wilayah dan kondisi geografis Negara Kesatuan Republik Indonesia yang terdiri atas 16 ribu pulau. 3. Kami atas nama Bank Indonesia, yang pada hari ini bekerja sama dengan Dewan Nasional Keuangan Inklusif dan Tim Pengendali Bantuan Sosial Non Tunai dalam menyelenggarakan seminar nasional ini, menyampaikan ucapan terima kasih yang sebesar-besarnya kepada seluruh narasumber dan panelis dari Kementerian dan Lembaga, karena telah bersedia hadir untuk berbagai informasi dan pengalaman terkait perluasan akses keuangan masyarakat dalam payung besar Strategi Nasional Keuangan Inklusif, dengan bantuan sosial sebagai salah satu strategi utamanya. 4. Melalui kegiatan ini, diharapkan seluruh stakeholder terkait dapat memiliki pandangan dan pemahaman yang sama, sehingga dapat bergerak secara terpadu untuk menyukseskan tercapainya tingkat inklusi keuangan di Indonesia, sebagaimana telah ditetapkan dalam Strategi Nasional Keuangan Inklusif, yaitu 75% penduduk di Indonesia telah memiliki rekening di lembaga keuangan formal. [Strategi Nasional Keuangan Inklusif] Bapak/Ibu Hadirin yang Kami Hormati, 5. Sebagaimana kita ketahui bersama, kondisi akses keuangan di Indonesia masih kurang menggembirakan. Hal itu tercermin dari rendahnya tingkat inklusi keuangan di Indonesia, yang berdasarkan survey terakhir Bank Dunia pada tabun 2014 hanya sebesar 36%. Artinya, hanya 36% penduduk dewasa di Indonesia yang memiliki rekening pada lembaga keuangan formal. 6. Rendahnya tingkat inklusi keuangan tersebut dapat berakibat negatif pada berbagai aspek. a. Dari sisi masyarakat, eksklusivitas keuangan berdampak pada tidak adanya budaya menabung sehingga masyarakat tidak memiliki dana untuk berjaga-jaga ataupun keperluan di masa depan. Selain itu, eksklusivitas keuangan juga dapat menutup peluang masyarakat untuk memupuk asset, sehingga tidak dapat meningkatkan kesejahteraan, serta menyebabkan inefisiensi dalam melakukan transaksi pembayaran. b. Dari sisi stabilitas sistem keuangan, eksklusivitas keuangan dapat menghambat pertumbuhan Dana Pihak Ketiga sehingga berakibat pada kurang optimalnya fungsi intermediasi dari lembaga keuangan. Tidak hanya itu, eksklusivitas keuangan juga dapat memperbesar shadow economy atau transaksi ekonomi yang tidak tercatat sehingga rawan menimbulkan tindak pencucian uang dan pendanaan terorisme, serta mengurangi '/w/Ter'bagi sistem keuangan apabila terjadi kondisi resesi. c. Akhirnya, bagi perekenomian nasional, eksklusivitas keuangan dapat memperlebar kesenjangan sosial, tidak mendukung penurunan kemiskinan dan pertumbuhan ekonomi, serta meningkatkan inefisiensi secara nasional. 7. Memperhatikan dampak negatif yang dapat terjadi, kebutuhan akan perluasan akses keuangan menjadi hal yang tidak dapat ditunda lagi. Oleh karena itu, pada tahun 2016 yang lalu, Pemerintah melalui Kementerian Koordinator Bidang Perekonomian telah menerbitkan Perpres Nomor 82 tahun 2016 tentang Strategi Nasional Keuangan Inklusif (SNKI). 8. Perpres dimaksud diterbitkan untuk memperkuat komitmen para pihak dalam mewujudkan perluasan akses keuangan, khususnya bagi masyarakat unbanked. Sebagaimana telah kami sebutkan sebelumnya, target utama yang ingin dicapai melalui Perpres dimaksud adalah kenaikan tingkat inklusi keuangan menjadi 75% pada tahun 2019. 9. Dalam mencapai target tersebut, dapat kami sampaikan secara umum bahwa Strategi Nasional Keuangan Inklusif telah menetapkan 5 Pilar, yaitu (i) Edukasi Keuangan pada Pilar Pertama, (ii) Hak Properti Masyarakat pada Pilar Kedua, (iii) Fasilitas Intermediasi dan Saluran Distribusi Keuangan pada Pilar Ketiga, (iv) Layanan Keuangan pada Sektor Pemerintah pada Pilar Keempat, dan (v) Perlindungan Konsumen pada Pilar Kelima. 10. Kelima pilar tersebut ditopang oleh tiga pondasi dasar, yaitu (i) Kebijakan dan Regulasi yang Kondusif, (ii) Infrastruktur dan Teknologi Informasi Keuangan yang Mendukung, serta (iii) Organisasi dan Mekanisme Implementasi yang Efektif. 11. Di dalam masing-masing pilar dan pondasi yang kami sebutkan tersebut, terdapat berbagai strategi dan program yang akan dilakukan berbagai Kementerian dan Lembaga. Strategi dan program itulah yang perlu kita ketahui dan pahami bersama, sehingga masing-masing dapat berkontribusi sesuai dengan tugas dan tanggung jawabnya masing-masing. 12. Kami tidak akan mejelaskan masing-masing program dan strategi yang ada pada pilar dan pondasi Strategi Nasional Keuangan Inklusif, karena tentu nanti akan dielaborasi oleh narasumber dan panelis yang telah hadir dan siap membagikan ilmunya pada kita semua pagi hari ini. [Bantuan Sosial Non Tunai] Bapak/Ibu Hadirin yang Berbahagia, 13. Seminar nasional pada hari ini juga akan mendiskusikan lebih dalam mengenai transformasi penyaluran bantuan sosial secara non tunai sebagai upaya akselerasi perluasan akses keuangan. 14. Akselerasi perluasan akses keuangan melalui bantuan sosial secara non tunai dianggap sebagai langkah yang berdampak besar, mengingat jumlah penerima program bantuan sosial dan subsidi sangatlah besar, yaitu hampir mencapai angka 30 juta keluarga di seluruh Indonesia. 15. Selain itu, dalam rangka mendorong pertumbuhan ekonomi Indonesia yang pada Triwulan III 2017 lalu mencatat angka 5,06%, peran bantuan sosial sangat penting, khususnya dalam rangka mendorong tingkat konsumsi masyarakat Indonesia yang berada di kelas bawah atau bottom of the pyramid. 16. Tentu saja, transformasi penyaluran bantuan sosial menjadi non tunai harus dilakukan untuk mewujudkan penyaluran bantuan sosial menjadi lebih efisien dan efektif, serta mendukung pencapaian prinsip 6T, yaitu Tepat Sasaran, Tepat Jumlah, Tepat Waktu, Tepat Kualitas, Tepat Harga, dan Tepat Administrasi. 17. Dapat kami sampaikan pada kesempatan kali ini, penyaluran bantuan sosial secara non tunai telah dimulai sejak satu tahun yang lalu. Diawali dari penyaluran sebagian Program Keluarga Harapan (PKH) secara non tunai pada tahun 2016 kepada 1,2 juta Keluarga Penerima Manfaat (KPM) dan selanjutnya pada tahun 2017 diperluas targetnya kepada 6 juta KPM serta program Bantuan Pangan Non Tunai (BPNT) kepada 1,2 juta KPM. Ke depan program bansos non tunai akan semakin diperluas secara bertahap hingga mencapai 10 juta penerima, masing- masing untuk PKH dan BPNT. 18. Sebagai payung hukum penyaluran bantuan sosial secara non tunai, pemerintah melalui Kementerian Koordinator Bidang Pembangunan Manusia dan Kebudayaan pada tahun ini telah menerbitkan Perpres No. 63 Tahun 2017 tentang Penyaluran Bansos secara Non Tunai. 19. Penerbitan Perpres tersebut dimaksudkan untuk memberikan pedoman yang jelas dan menjaga standarisasi mekanisme penyaluran secara non tunai berbagai program bansos. Sehingga, dalam hal pada perkembangan ke depan terdapat berbagai bantuan sosial yang akan disalurkan secara non tunai, maka standarisasi mekanisme dapat mengacu pada Perpres dimaksud dan melihat implementasi bansos non tunai yan sudah lebih dahulu diimplementasikan. [Peran Bank Indonesia] Bapak/Ibu Hadirin sekalian, 20. Dalam mengimplementasikan Strategi Nasional Keuangan Inklusif, termasuk penyaluran bantuan sosial secara non tunai sebagai salah satu inisiatif utama, Bank Indonesia telah berkomitmen pen uh dalam mendukung kelancaran dan kesuksesan program dimaksud. 21. Dukungan Bank Indonesia diwujudkan dalam Blueprint Sistem Pembayaran yang terdiri dari tiga pilar utama, yaitu: (i) perluasan penggunaan instrumen non tunai (elektronifikasi), (ii) infrastruktur pembayaran yang andal dan aman, dan (iii) pengawasan serta oversight yang kuat dan tajam serta menyeluruh (rigorous). 22. Seluruh program dan inisiatif terkait keuangan inklusif termasuk bansos non tunai diimplementasikan di bawah pilar pertama, yaitu elektronifikasi. Dalam pelaksanaan inisiatif pilar pertama tersebut, dukungan infrastruktur yang antara lain berupa implementasi Gerbang Pembayaran Nasional (GPN) pada pilar kedua akan berkontribusi penuh bagi interoperabilitas dan interkoneksi penyaluran bantuan sosial non tunai guna memastikan efisiensi dan efektivitas penyaluran. 23. Selanjutnya, agar dalam pelaksanaannya tidak terdapat hal-hal yang bertentangan dengan ketentuan dan kebijakan Bank Indonesia di bidang sistem pembayaran, pengawasan yang kuat dan menyeluruh, sebagaimana pilar ketiga Blueprint Sistem Pembayaran, akan dilakukan Bank Indonesia pada seluruh tahapan dan fase penyaluran bantuan sosial non tunai. 24. Tidak hanya itu, mengingat pelaksanaan program inklusi keuangan dan penyaluran bantuan sosial non tunai diimplementasikan di berbagai wilayah di Indonesia, Bank Indonesia juga berkomitmen penuh untuk melakukan proses monitoring dan pemantauan penyaluran bantuan sosial non tunai, melalui Kantor Perwakilan Bank Indonesia di berbagai provinsi, kabupaten, dan kota, yang pada kesempatan hari ini turut hadir untuk mengikuti dan memahami program keuangan inklusif dan penyaluran bantuan sosial non tunai. <Penutup> Bapak/Ibu Hadirin yang Kami Hormati, 25. Kiranya kami tidak akan menggunakan waktu lebih lama lagi untuk menyampaikan sambutan pembuka pada hari ini. Hal-hal utama yang kami sebutkan tadi akan disampaikan secara lebih detail pada sesi materi yang akan dibawakan pejabat dari Kementerian dan Lembaga terkait. 26. Akhir kata, guna menyukseskan upaya perluasan akses keuangan, termasuk melalui penyaluran bantuan sosial non tunai sebagai salah satu strategi utama, kami berharap seluruh pihak yang hadir pada hari ini dapat memberikan masukan yang kontributif dan mendukung secara penuh program-program untuk meningkatkan inklusivitas keuangan di Indonesia. Melalui kesamaan pandangan, kerja sama dan koordinasi yang erat, serta komitmen bersama antara Kementerian dan Lembaga terkait, pelaku industri, dan masyarakat, kami meyakini program ini akan memberikan manfaat yang besar bagi masyarakat dan juga perekonomian Indonesia secara nasional. 27. Demikian sambutan kami. Dengan ini kami nyatakan Seminar Nasional "Penyaluran Bantuan Sosial secara Non Tunai sebagai Strategi Perluasan Akses Keuangan Masyarakat" dibuka. Teri ma kasih Wassalamu'alaikum Warahmatullahi Wabarakatuh Jakarta, 18 Desember 2017 Dr. Sugeng Deputi Gubernur Bank Indonesia

Title: Opening Remarks by Ronald Waas Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia on Dissemination of Book Titled "Activities of Bank Indonesia on Flagship Commodity Based Cluster Development" jakarta 19 June 2014
text: SPEECH OF THE DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF BANK INDONESIA ON DISSEMINATION OF BOOK TITLED ACTIVITIES OF BANK INDONESIA IN FLAGSHIP COMMODITY BASED CLUSTER DEVELOPMENT (REPLICATION MANUAL) Jakarta, 19 June 2014 The Honourable, - Vice Minister of Agriculture, - Heads of Ministries, - Heads of Agriculture and Food Security Offices of 26 Provinces in Indonesia, - Heads or officers of banks, - Academicians, - Representatives of Business Associations, - Heads of Working Units of Bank Indonesia Head Offices and Heads of Bank Indonesia Representative Offices, - Distinguished guests. Good morning and greetings to all of us. 1. To begin this meeting, allow me to invite all of you to praise God the Almighty for the blessings bestowed upon us so that we have the opportunity to gather today in a healthy and favourable condition in the Thamrin Office of Bank Indonesia. This morning, we will witness the launching of book titled Activities of Bank Indonesia in Flagship Commodity Based Cluster Development. 2. This book is a replication manual for implementation by Bank Indonesia in response to the policy and role of Bank Indonesia in maintaining price stability through regional flagship commodity based food security cluster development and at the same time promoting development of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises in regions. Ladies and gentlemen, and distinguished guests, 3. The role of Bank Indonesia in MSME development has been running since for more than 4 decades through financial institutions and MSME. For financial institutions, Bank Indonesia activities aim to encourage banks to increase MSME credit extension through regulations, which allow participation of banks in extending credit for MSME and development of supporting financial infrastructure. 4. For MSME, BI activities aim to increase their capability and access to various resources which support self-sufficiency and business sustainability of MSME. Capacity building and bridging information gap between banks and MSME are some of the possible activities. In addition, all of these activities are conducted through strategic alliance with Ministries, Regional Governments, banks, and other relevant stakeholders. 5. For MSME capacity building, the main program conducted by Bank Indonesia is cluster development and food security commodity based entrepreneurship. This is important since food becomes one of the commodities contributing to inflation and current transaction deficit. Therefore, going forward, MSME development by Bank Indonesia will emphasize on efforts to support such food security through commodity cluster development in various areas in cooperation with regional governments and relevant regional institutions. Today, there are 130 clusters throughout Indonesia, 59 of which are food commodity clusters. 6. Food security is a problem many countries are focusing in line with the increasing number of the worlds population. Needs for food become the main issue in various world meetings. Indonesia, as a country with the fourth largest population, average population growth of 1.49% per year and average economic growth from 2009 to 2013 of 5.9% per year, must be alert to the increasing food needs in line with the public consumption increase. 7. Such condition certainly becomes the main attention of the government by making food security development a national priority and specifying it in the National Mid Term Development Plan 2010-2014. 8. To support food security program, as the central bank of a developing country, Bank Indonesia has a role to develop MSME as one of the main actors in national economy. Food security program indirectly supports the task of Bank Indonesia to maintain price/inflation stability, especially to control volatile food. It is expected inflation to return to the target of 4.51% in 2014 and to reach 4.01% in 2015. 9. One of the efforts is through food security cluster development program based on rice, onions, red chillies, beef and garlic. 10. From 2012 to 2013, in implementation of food security cluster activities in regions, Representative Offices of Bank Indonesia has made some achievements in cluster program, such as production increase and agricultural system improvement. 11. Diverse activities and research results of the Central Banks Education Centre (PRES) related thereto are recorded in a book we will launch this morning, with the expectation that the program/model portrayed in this book can serve as an inspiration for replication and development by Representative Offices of Bank Indonesia and stakeholders, like regional Agriculture Offices, according to the respective regional condition and potential. Furthermore, we can use this book as a means of information exchange based on Bank Indonesias experience in cluster development and it is expected to enrich information in supporting the achievement of our food security target. Ladies and gentlemen, and distinguished guests, 12. I welcome all initiatives and efforts to promote food security as well as real sector and MSME development, primarily in promoting more stable and balanced economic activities. 13. Finally, upon the blessings of God the Almighty, I extend my highest appreciation to all staffs of Bank Indonesia and all parties for devoting their thoughts and energy for supporting and assisting to succeed this Bank Indonesias program. 14. Hopefully, all measures taken by Bank Indonesia and other policy makers can reach sustainable food security in Indonesia. Thank you. Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Ronald Waas

Title: Speech by Ronald Waas Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia in Media Briefing on "Green Banking" in Cooperation Between Bank Indonesia and Ministry of Environment. Jakarta, 21 August 2013
text: SPEECH OF THE DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF BANK INDONESIA IN MEDIA BRIEFING ON GREEN BANKING IN COOPERATION BETWEEN BANK INDONESIA (BI) AND MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT (MOE) Press Conference Room, Gedung Thamrin 1st Fl., Bank Indonesia Jakarta, 21 August 2013  Good morning and greetings to all of us. Welcome to Bank Indonesia. Since we are still in Idul Fitri season, we would like to extend our sincerest apology.  The Honourable: - Deputy for Environment, Ministry of Environment, Mr. Imam Hendargo, - Mrs. Felia Salim of BNI, - Mr. Raymond Bona of ICED-USAID, - Environmental and economic desk journalists, and - Distinguished guests.  First, allow me to invite all of you to praise God the Almighty for the blessings bestowed upon us so that we have the opportunity to attend this Media Briefing on Green Banking.  We must also be grateful that our good intention to promote the Role of Banks in Implementing Green Economic Development may be continued as a cooperation between Bank Indonesia and the Ministry of Environment. Ladies and gentlemen, and dear journalists,  As we all know, the World Economic Forum in its 2013 annual report puts economy and environment as the worlds main risks. The two aspects correlate and it is believed that environmental degradation due to unsustainable industrial management poses negative impacts on global economy. It results in stronger efforts to reconstruct development policy, where there is a balance between efforts to promote economic growth, social equality, and environmental maintenance (green economy).  There are two reasons why Bank Indonesia considers it important to develop this green banking. o First, in response to Law No. 32 of 2009 on Environmental Protection and Management, all economic activities must promote environmental conservation by imposing sanctions, either criminal punishment or environmental permit revocation. If this law is not observed by banks, there will be a potential increase in credit, legal and reputation risks. Therefore, banks need to understand and have a better knowledge on environmental risk management. o Second, an unsolved national issue is food and energy security. These two sectors significantly contribute to economy, primarily due to relatively high import value; commodity price fluctuation affects inflation and pressure to exchange rate and deficit in Indonesias Balance of Payment. For that reason, banks support to finance the two sectors becomes very important. By supporting green energy and agriculture financing, it is expected not only to result in energy and food self-sufficiency, but also to contribute to other green economy issues, such as decrease in glass house gas as Indonesias commitment to the international world. Dear journalists,  This green banking policy is based on the vision that national banks must play an active role according to evolutionary phases of sustainable development, where success indicators include banks capability to provide efficient development financing sources and direction to productive investment by observing environmental protection and management principles. Achievement of such vision is believed to increase bank competitiveness, especially in facing ASEAN Economic Community era from 2015 and financial sector from 2020. Basically, we wish to place bank as one of the solutions to the problems we are facing.  To achieve the vision and objective of green banking, an MOU has been entered into between BI and MOE focusing on harmonization of policy and management, increase of bank awareness and capacity and banks supervisor in environmental risk management and introduction to green finance, and joint research program.  We also consistently coordinate with the relevant ministries to promote harmonization of policy and its implementation which can promote green finance, primarily in the context of providing incentive for businesses and banks willing to finance green business sector, regulatory improvement, and implementation phases. Green banking will be effectively implemented if banks business orientation paradigm changes to sustainable banking, competent human resource availability, micro-prudential policy support, sufficient information availability, and legal certainty and enforcement against environmental violation by the competent authorities. Ladies and gentlemen,  As one of the efforts to promote and disseminate this green banking policy and program to our banks, BI and MOE has organized workshops and training of Environmental Analysts for 4 (four) classes in 2013.  Banks officials also participated in the training in order to increase the capacity building and technical assistance of human resources to improve analysis quality of risks related to environment in credit extension to green projects.  For further understanding on green banking measures and policies, we present some resource persons. The first is Mr. Irwan Lubis, Head of Bank Research and Regulation Department of Bank Indonesia. Thereafter, material presentations and information and experience sharing from panellists: Mr. Imam Hendargo of MOE, Mrs. Felia Salim of BNI, and Mr. Raymond Bona of ICED-USAID will complete our reference with the results of green banking benchmarking studies in various countries.  Last, I expect todays meeting will run better with the participation, sharing and discussion with the journalists here.  We expect that this Media Briefing as a cooperation between BI and MOE will add the knowledge of journalists on green banking. We conclude our speech. Have a fruitful discussion. Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Ronald Waas

Title: Speech of Bank Indonesia Deputy Governor Ronald Waas on The Signing of Work Guidline Between BI and The Indonesian National Police (Bali, 20 November 2014)
Subtitle: PROCEDURE ON IMPLEMENTATION OF HANDLING OF ALLEGED BREACH OF RUPIAH USE OBLIGATION WITHIN THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA AND ALLEGED CRIME AGAINST RUPIAH AND: SIGNING OF MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING: between BANK INDONESIA REPRESENTATIVE OFFICES OF REGION III (BALI AND NUSTRA) and POLICE COMMAND OF BALI PROVINCE on COORDINATION IN HANDLING OF CRIMES IN PAYMENT SYSTEM & FOREIGN EXCHANGE BUSINESS ACTIVITY
text: SPEECH OF BANK INDONESIA DEPUTY GOVERNOR SIGNING OF WORK GUIDELINE BETWEEN BI AND THE INDONESIAN NATIONAL POLICE: PROCEDURE ON IMPLEMENTATION OF HANDLING OF ALLEGED BREACH OF RUPIAH USE OBLIGATION WITHIN THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA AND ALLEGED CRIME AGAINST RUPIAH AND: SIGNING OF MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING: between BANK INDONESIA REPRESENTATIVE OFFICES OF REGION III (BALI AND NUSTRA) and POLICE COMMAND OF BALI PROVINCE on COORDINATION IN HANDLING OF CRIMES IN PAYMENT SYSTEM & FOREIGN EXCHANGE BUSINESS ACTIVITY Bali, 20 November 2014 The Honourable, Head of Criminal Investigation Bureau of Indonesian National Police, Drs. Suhardi Alius, M.H.; Governor of Bali Province, represented by ... Heads of Indonesian National Police Headquarter; o Director of Crime of Special Economy, Brig. Gen. Pol. A. Kamil Razak, SH., MH; o Head of Sub-directorate of Counterfeit Money, Senior Commissioner Agus Nugroho; o Head of Cooperation between Institutions Section  Legal Division of Indonesian National Police, Senior Commissioner Syahri Gunawan; o Head of Police Command of Bali Province, Inspector General Police A.J. Benny Mokalu, S.H.; Heads of Bank Indonesia Representative Offices and Heads of Bank Indonesia Departments: o Head of Bank Indonesia Representative Office of Region III, Mr. Benny Siswanto; Page 1 of 9 o Head of Representative Office of East Nusa Tenggara Province, Mr. Naek Tigor Sinaga; o Head of Representative Office of West Nusa Tenggara Province, Mr. Bambang Himawan; o Director of Money Management Department, Mr. Eko Yulianto Members of Regional Head Communication Forum of Bali Province Distinguished guests. Good Morning and Greetings to all of us 1. First of all let us to praise God the Almighty for the blessings bestowed upon us so that we have the opportunity to see the sunrise in Sanur Beach and meet in this nice room and condition to attend the Signing of Work Guideline and Memorandum of Understanding between Bank Indonesia and Indonesian National Police. 2. On this occasion, we just witnessed 2 signing activities consisting of: 1) Work Guideline between Bank Indonesia and Indonesian National Police on Procedure on Implementation of Handling of Alleged Breach of Rupiah Use Obligation within the Republic of Indonesia and Alleged Crime against Rupiah. 2) Memorandum of Understanding between Bank Indonesia Representative Office of Region III (Bali and Nusa Tenggara) and Police Command of Bali Province on Coordination in Handling of Crimes in Payment System and Foreign Exchange Business Activity also known as money changer. 3. The two activities are part of a series of institutional cooperation between Bank Indonesia and Indonesian National Police, which is officially marked by the signing of Memorandum of Understanding on Cooperation to Support Implementation of Institutional Tasks and Authorities by Bank Indonesia Governor and Indonesian Page 2 of 9 National Police on 1 September 2014. The same activity will also be carried on in all provinces between Bank Indonesia Representative Offices and regional Police Commands. 4. Cooperation in Crime Handling as set forth in the Work Guideline and Memorandum of Understanding is an institutional synergy effort between BI and Indonesian National Police, primarily in Law Enforcement. Broadly, the scope of cooperation will include:  Exchange of data and/or information;  Security and control;  Supervision;  Improvement of Human Resources; and  Dissemination. Distinguished Ladies and Gentlemen, 5. As one of the favourite tourist destinations in the world, every year Bali receives the visits of millions of foreign tourists. Based on the data of Statistics Indonesia, in 2013 the number of foreign tourists entering Ngurah Rai Airport gate reaches 3.24 million people or 36.83% of the total foreign tourists coming to Indonesia. This data confirms Bali as the most favourite tourist destination in Indonesia for foreign tourists like in the previous years. 6. Tourism industry advancement has been contributing significantly to the economy of Bali. Business sectors related to tourism industry, such as trade, hotel, and restaurants, are the biggest support for economic growth in Bali. According to the data of Gross Regional Domestic Product (GRDP) in 2013 published by Statistics Indonesia, the sectors contributed 29.88% to total GRDP of Bali Province of Rp 94.55 trillion (GRDP at current price). Page 3 of 9 7. Considering the significant role of tourism industry in the economy of Bali, we should pay a special attention to the continuity of different sectors related to the tourism world. The positive image established in the eyes of foreign tourists as the manifestation of prime services provided must be maintained and improved. 8. Foreign Exchange Business Activity is one of the parts of services contributing to tourism industry in Bali. Therefore, we must arrange this industry properly in terms of business and institution with a view to running this business smoothly and safely, providing satisfaction to the users, and avoiding any misuse by irresponsible parties. 9. To realize it, Bank Indonesia as the competent authority will consistently take necessary measures and policies, among others through issuance of regulations, supervision, guidance and law enforcement through cooperation with the Indonesian National Police as carried on today. Distinguished ladies and gentlemen, 10. In addition to tourism industry, law enforcement in foreign exchange is very important to prevent any misuse by irresponsible parties considering it is a business vulnerable to misuse. Many of such misuse may include money laundering and terrorist funding, drug trafficking, and disguised smuggling as if coming from foreign exchange business. 11. Denpasar is one the main centres of foreign exchange activity in Indonesia, which may be seen from the 122 licensed non-bank money changers or ranked second nationwide together with Batam. In terms of volume, as of September 2014 foreign exchange transactions in Denpasar rank second after Jakarta. The average total transaction value of foreign paper money and travellers check purchase reaches Rp985 billion per month. Meanwhile, the average total transaction value of paper money sales reach Rp966 billion per month. Page 4 of 9 12. In terms of violation, as of September 2014, it is recorded that 70 violations are committed by non-bank money changers in Bali, 21 of which are sanctioned by business license revocation. In general, the violation is in the form of delay in periodic report submission. 13. In order to prevent such crime, BI has issued Regulation of Bank Indonesia No. 16/15/PBI/2014 dated 11 September 2014 on Non-Bank Foreign Exchange Business Activity. This regulation will encourage the strengthening and recovery of all non-bank money changers, which must obtain a license from Bank Indonesia. It is also expected to mitigate potential risks of misuses and crimes related to foreign exchange. Distinguished Ladies and Gentlemen, 14. Particularly for Work Guideline on Handling of Alleged Breach of Rupiah Use Obligation within the Republic of Indonesia and Crimes against Rupiah, it is our joint effort to encourage Rupiah sovereignty. In my opinion, there are three major dimensions as the ground for enforcement of Rupiah use obligation. 15. First, Legal Dimension. Different regulations, starting from the Currency Law, the Foreign Exchange Traffic Law, Bank Indonesia Regulation on Requirements and Procedure on Carrying Rupiah from and to the Customs of the Republic of Indonesia, and Regulation of Ministry of Trade on the Inclusion of Goods Prices and Service Tariffs, also strengthen the legal ground for Rupiah Use in the country. Those regulations confirm Rupiah use obligation in each transaction of payment within the Republic of Indonesia, both cash and non-cash. 16. Second, National Dimension. Rupiah is the symbol of sovereignty of the Republic of Indonesia. Therefore, currency use in each transaction within the Republic of Indonesia Page 5 of 9 is a must for all citizens. Only with this condition can Rupiah become the host in its own country. 17. Third, Economic/Business Dimension. Foreign exchange transactions within the country have been one of the factors resulting in domestic foreign exchange demand increase. Such high foreign exchange demand for economic transactions will make our economy vulnerable to economic turbulence. The trust of domestic and international community to Rupiah will reinforce the national economic resilience in general, so that Rupiah has dignity within and outside the country. Distinguished Ladies and Gentlemen, 18. Enforcement of this WG pertaining to Rupiah certainly helps the implementation of the tasks of Bank Indonesia, primarily in Rupiah management. As a central bank, Bank Indonesia may implement Rupiah management in order to meet Rupiah demand in the community in sufficient amount and banknotes and fit for circulation and also to control Rupiah use obligation in each transaction, including cash and non-cash, within the Republic of Indonesia with a view to supporting Rupiah exchange rate stability and realize Rupiah sovereignty. 19. In accordance with the authority given by the state, Bank Indonesia has a significant role in facilitating the use of Rupiah as a legal tender in the national economy. Like blood circulation in human body, the role of Bank Indonesia in maintaining smooth payment system and money management is very vital to prevent any blockage of the national economy veins. 20. Realizing such huge mandate, in implementing its tasks, Bank Indonesia cooperates not only with the law enforcement and government institutions but also with private sector. As conducted on 14 November 2014, Bank Indonesia and the Indonesian Airline Page 6 of 9 Ticketing Association (ASTINDO) and the Indonesian Hotel and Restaurant Association (PHRI) signed a cooperation agreement on Rupiah use obligation within the Republic of Indonesia in each transaction related to the business fields of the two associations. 21. Through this cooperation, four points are jointly agreed: first, ASTINDO and PHRI are committed to encourage all of its members to apply Rupiah use obligation and include goods prices and/or service tariffs in Rupiah in each transaction related to airline ticketing, hotels, and restaurants within the Republic of Indonesia. 22. Second, ASTINDO and PHRI also agree to provide data and/or information to Bank Indonesia in terms of Rupiah use obligation. Third, in order to improve human resource quality, it is also agreed to administer education and training activities in connection with the implementation of Rupiah use obligation within the Republic of Indonesia, particularly for the management and members of ASTINDO and PHRI. Fourth, it is agreed to disseminate Rupiah use obligation not only to the management and members of ASTINDO and PHRI but also to other parties. Distinguished Ladies and Gentlemen, 23. In making cash and non-cash transactions, security is the main concern of the community. The survey result of Bank Indonesia confirms that security in non-cash transactions is the first and foremost factor for the community, followed by transaction convenience, and interoperability between financial transaction service providers. We believe the same also applies to cash transactions where security is expected by all parties, especially security from crimes, like money counterfeiting. 24. In relation to money counterfeiting, based on the record of BI and the Indonesian National Police, 3,531 banknotes of counterfeit money are found in Bali and Nusa Page 7 of 9 Tenggara as of 2014, significantly decreasing compared to 4,924 banknotes in 2013. Such finding contributed 4.23% nationwide. 25. To reduce crime potentials in payment system and foreign exchange business activity, handling of alleged crimes must be conducted intensively. Close coordination and strong consolidation between the authority and law enforcement is expected to prevent and minimize crimes in payment system and foreign exchange business activity. In addition, strict sanctions may give a deterrent effect for the perpetrators. 26. This close coordination and consolidation needs to be specified in a clear and transparent mechanism according to the tasks and authority of BI and the Indonesian National Police in the central and regional levels, referring to the applicable laws and regulations by considering the principles of justice, benefit, and legal certainty. 27. I welcome the signing of the Work Guideline and Memorandum of Understanding we do today as an integral part of our joint effort to mitigate crimes among the community. Distinguished Ladies and Gentlemen, 28. Through this MOU signing, we believe that in the future, handling of alleged crimes in payment system and foreign exchange business activity, breach of Rupiah use obligation within the Republic of Indonesia, and Crimes against Rupiah, will run more smoothly and effectively, and therefore, our cause to provide protection for the whole community through the establishment of payment system and foreign exchange business activity industry as well as sound and secure Rupiah management may be realized. 29. This Work Guideline is also expected to become a facilitator of good communication, intensive coordination, and synergic collaboration between Bank Indonesia, Police, and the Government in the central and regional levels as well as all parties concerned in Page 8 of 9 maintaining and improving law enforcement effectiveness in payment system and foreign exchange business activity, and Rupiah management. 30. I conclude my speech. On behalf of the Board of Governors of Bank Indonesia, I would like to extend my appreciation to all parties who have supported and attended todays event making all run properly and smoothly. May God bless all efforts we make for the improvement of this country, nation and community and give us the strength to implement it all. Thank you. Bank Indonesia Deputy Governor Ronald Waas Page 9 of 9

Title: Speech of the Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Ronald Waas at Handover Ceremony at the Bank Indonesia Representative Office in Aceh Province, Banda Aceh, 20th October 2015
Subtitle: Handover Ceremony at the Bank Indonesia Representative Office
text: Speech of the Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Handover Ceremony at the Bank Indonesia Representative Office in Aceh Province Banda Aceh, 20th October 2015 Distinguished Governor of Aceh Province, Mr Zaini Abdullah; The Communication Forum of Aceh Regional Leaders; Distinguished Chairman of the Peoples Representative Council of Aceh, TGK H Muharuddin; Regents and Mayors of Aceh province; Chairman of the Financial Services Authority (OJK) Representative Office in Aceh; Members of Regional Inflation Control Teams (TPID); Leaders of the banking community, academics, religious leaders, entrepreneurs and the media; Leaders and staff from Bank Indonesia; Ladies and Gentlemen Good morning, 1. Before commencing my speech here this morning, I would like to thank the Lord God Almighty for bestowing His blessings that we can all congregate here today to welcome Zulfan Nukman at the Bank Indonesia Representative Office in Aceh to replace Ahmad Farid. 2. Replacing the Chief Representative at Bank Indonesia is an ongoing dynamic that ensures the organisation of Bank Indonesia remains motivated and performs well, thereby supporting the function, tasks, role and responsibility of Bank Indonesia in terms of developing the economy nationally and regionally. Ladies and gentlemen; 3. According to our observations, the global economy will remain blighted by widespread uncertainty through to yearend 2015. Current global dynamics are driven by the two locomotives of economic growth, namely the United States and China. 4. US economic gains this year prompted concerns over a proposed Federal Funds Rate hike. Uncertainty regarding the magnitude and timing of the hike triggered shocks on global financial markets and saw the US dollar appreciate broadly. 5. The normalisation policy of the Federal Reserve could trigger a deluge of capital outflow and, thus, pressures on financial markets in the region, including Indonesia, after maintaining inflows of cheap funds thanks to the policy of the Federal Reserve to flood the market with billions of US dollars, otherwise known as quantitative easing, in order to recover from the crisis that befell the United States in 2008. 6. On the other hand, the economy of China, which has recorded double-digit growth for the past two decades, has begun to moderate over the last few years. Chinas economy expanded at just 7% during the first two quarters of 2015. The downturn has reduced demand for goods from China, which ultimately perpetuated the international commodity price slide. For a number of economies that rely on primary commodities, such as Indonesia, this implies the upcoming challenges of economic recovery will become increasingly burdensome. Ladies and Gentlemen: 7. Due to economic developments over the past several months, concerns have emerged in Indonesia that current conditions are heading towards another crisis similar to that experienced in 1998. In response, I would like to reassure that the economic foundation of Indonesia is currently much stronger than in 1998. 8. During the economic crisis of 1998, economic growth in Indonesia contracted to 13.7%, with inflation peaking at 77.6% and the BI rate jumping to 57%, while the position of reserve assets was just USD23.76 billion. 9. Furthermore, exchange rate volatility saw the US dollar hit Rp16,650, which brought down the banking sector and forced numerous banks to close. Conditions were further exacerbated by non-performing loans (NPL) that reached 483.6% and the Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) of banks at just -15.7%. 10. Looking at conditions today, however, economic fundamentals are much sounder than in 1998. The economy of Indonesia achieved positive growth of 4.67% (yoy) in Q2/2015 and is projected to accelerate to 4.85% (yoy) in Q3. 11. In line with positive economic growth, inflationary pressures were well controlled through to September 2015. Nationally, deflation of 0.05% (mtm) was recorded in September, or 2.24% (ytd) cumulatively for the year or 6.83% (yoy) on an annualised basis. Based on inflation through to September 2015, Bank Indonesia is satisfied that the inflation target of 41% in 2015 will be achieved. 12. The position of reserve assets is also much stronger now than back then. In September 2015, reserve assets stood at USD101.7 billion, equivalent to 6.8 months of imports and servicing public foreign debt, which is well above the international adequacy standard of around three months. Bank Indonesia perceives the current position of foreign exchange reserves as sufficient to maintain external sector resilience and preserve sustainable domestic economic growth moving forward. 13. Rupiah volatility is also not as severe as during the crisis in 1998. At that time, the rupiah depreciated 48% in a brief period of time. Conversely, from January until the first week of October 2015, the rupiah depreciated just 8.32%, which was still not as acute as that recorded in other countries, such as Brazil (41.70%), Turkey (24.71%), Malaysia (18.31%) and Chili (11.41%). 14. Bank Indonesia, as the monetary authority, constantly maintains rupiah stability and we are avowedly committed to market intervention in order to stabilise the rupiah in line with the currencys fundamental value, which bolsters macroeconomic and financial system stability. 15. In terms of the banking sector, the latest indicators show that the banking system is far more resilient now than in 1998. The Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) averaged 20.68% for the industry in August 2015. Credit and deposit growth, despite moderating slightly, still achieved 10.95% and 13.24% respectively. Meanwhile, nonperforming loans (NPL) remain relatively low and stable at 2.76% of total credit. Ladies and Gentlemen: 16. Monitoring current macroeconomic and banking conditions, we strongly urge against concerns of a repeat of the 1998 crisis. Nevertheless, as the monetary, macroprudential and banking system authority, Bank Indonesia vigilantly monitors global and domestic economic performance. 17. We are also keenly aware that the economy of Indonesia continues to confront a variety of onerous global and domestic challenges. Externally, Indonesia must remain cognisant of the uncertainty overshadowing the global economy. 18. On the home front, however, the economy is currently moderating, there is low absorption of infrastructure spending and sluggish credit growth. In addition, there remains the twin deficit (current account deficit and fiscal deficit), spiralling foreign debt as well as the weather phenomenon known as El Nino that could decimate food production. 19. Confronting the challenges, Bank Indonesia instituted a policy mix that prioritises stability to ensure sound economic growth. Furthermore, Bank Indonesia policy is consistently directed towards creating stable macroeconomic conditions, primarily in the form of on-target inflation, while reducing the current account deficit to a more sustainable level. 20. Exchange rate policy, however, aims to maintain rupiah stability in line with the currencys fundamental value, thereby avoiding excessive expectations of depreciation that could undermine economic stability. Complementing the policy mix, we continuously strive to strengthen coordination with the Government and other relevant authorities concerning macroeconomic policy management. 21. Several weeks ago, on 30th September 2015, Bank Indonesia released a policy package to stabilise the rupiah as a follow-up to the policies issued on 9th September 2015. The policy package focused on three pillars, namely: (1) maintaining rupiah exchange rate stability; (2) strengthening rupiah liquidity management; and (3) strengthening foreign exchange supply and demand management. 22. The policies instituted by Bank Indonesia are also in line with the policy packages released by the government in September and October 2015. Similarly, the Financial Services Authority (OJK) also issued a policy package containing a number of initiatives for the financial sector, which now falls under the jurisdiction of OJK. We warmly welcome and appreciate the policy measures introduced by the Government and Financial Services Authority (OJK). 23. Coordination between Bank Indonesia and the Government, specifically the fiscal authorities and other institutions such as the Financial Services Authority (OJK), has remained sound and synergic. Policy synergy is crucial to maintain stability and restore national economic conditions. Ladies and Gentlemen: 24. National economic growth is a reflection of regional economic growth. Therefore, as the central bank, we give full attention to regional economic development, inflation control and policy formulation. Bank Indonesia constantly fosters monetary, fiscal and real sector coordination in local areas, strengthens the role of regional inflation control teams (TPID) and advises local governments through regional financial and economic reviews as well as local competitiveness analyses. 25. In addition, pursuant to its authority, Bank Indonesia will continue to strengthen financial market deepening as a basis of development financing, including infrastructure financing, while promoting financial inclusion as well as micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). 26. We have seen fruitful coordination between the Bank Indonesia Representative Offices in Banda Aceh and Lhokseumawe and the Provincial Government of Aceh at the provincial as well as city/regency levels facilitated by regional inflation control teams (TPID) along with cooperation and coordination to develop local economies, dissemination of the Regional Financial and Economic Review (KEKR) as well as real/MSME sector development and the Bank Indonesia Social Program (PSBI). 27. Concrete evidence of successful collaboration and synergy between Bank Indonesia and the Government at the provincial level, as well as other related parties in the region, comes in the form of low inflation. In September 2015, aggregate inflation for the province of Aceh was recorded at 4.19% (yoy) on an annualised basis, which is below the national average of 6.83%. 28. Similarly, cumulative inflation from January to September 2015 was recorded at just 0.31% (ytd), which is well below the national average of 2.24%. Deflation of 0.15% was recorded at the provincial level in Aceh for the month of September 2015, compared to 0.05% nationally. Low inflation is one positive consequence of 17 regional inflation control teams operating at the city/regency level and one at the provincial level. 29. In light of the positive accomplishments and fruitful coordination enjoyed so far, allow me to express our heartfelt appreciation to the Governor and Deputy Governor of Aceh as well as all regents and mayors, along with their corresponding staff, who have backed and supported our efforts. 30. The successful accomplishments should not lead to complacency, however. Indonesias interminable journey remains beset by increasingly complex challenges that demand a more active contribution from us to the problems faced. 31. In terms of economic growth, we believe that the ongoing hard work and existing collaboration between Bank Indonesia, the Provincial Government and other related parties should be enhanced. Bank Indonesia recorded slower economic growth in Aceh during 2014 at just 0.59%, which is even lower than that posted in 2013 at 2.8%. Furthermore, Aceh contracted by -2.12% and -1.72% in the first two quarters of 2015. 32. Therefore, we sincerely hope that the clear communication, intensive coordination and synergic collaboration built up over time will continue and improve, thereby reinforcing the economy of Aceh towards greater prosperity and equality. Ladies and Gentlemen: 33. I would like to take this opportunity to graciously thank Mr Zulfan Nukman, who has served the mandate of Bank Indonesia emphatically. As Chief Representative of Bank Indonesia in Aceh, Mr Zulfan Nukman built a solid foundation through harmonious coordination and collaboration with all stakeholders, in particular the Provincial Government of Aceh. 34. Armed with vast experience and insight, Mr Zulfan Nukman will fill his new role as Deputy Chief Representative of Bank Indonesia in Bali with enthusiasm. 35. To Mr Ahmad Farid, the new Chief Representative of Bank Indonesia in Aceh, we extend great expectations to maintain existing performance, while optimising Bank Indonesias monetary and macroprudential role and that of the payment system amongst all stakeholders in Aceh. 36. We also hope that Mr Ahmad Farid, Chief Representative of Bank Indonesia in Aceh, will more actively accelerate structural reforms, while seeking solutions to the challenges faced by the economy of Aceh. Consequently, the presence of Bank Indonesia in the province will be felt by all social strata. 37. In closing, on behalf of the Governor of Bank Indonesia, we would like to thank everyone in attendance for sparing your valuable time this morning. May all our undertakings to advance the country, state and people be blessed by the Lord God Almighty and let Him give us the strength to carry on. Thank you. Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Ronald Waas

Title: Speech of the Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Ronald Waas at Handover Ceremony at the Bank Indonesia Representative Office in New York, New York, 24th August 2015
text: Speech of the Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Handover Ceremony at the Bank Indonesia Representative Office in New York New York, 24th August 2015 Honourable Consul General of the Republic of Indonesia in New York, Ghafur Akbar Dharmaputra; Distinguished guests from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York and our strategic partner institutions; Officials and staff of the Consulate General of the Republic of Indonesia in New York; Leaders of the banking community, Indonesia Investment Coordinating Board, academics, media, religious leaders and citizens of New York; Officials and staff of Bank Indonesia from head office and the Bank Indonesia Representative Office in New York; Ladies and gentlemen in attendance. Good morning and welcome: 1. Let me begin my expressing thanks to the Lord God Almighty for bestowing His blessings that we can all congregate here today to welcome Erwin Haryono at the Bank Indonesia Representative Office in New York, replacing Sugeng as Chief Representative. 2. Replacing the Chief Representative at Bank Indonesia is an ongoing dynamic that ensures the organisation of Bank Indonesia remains motivated and performs well, thereby supporting the function, task, role and responsibility of Bank Indonesia in terms of developing the economy nationally and regionally. Ladies and gentlemen: 3. Just days ago, we commemorated the Declaration of Independence on 17th August 1945, celebrating the struggle and victory of our predecessors, who sacrificed their lives and property. We are sincerely grateful because thanks to our fighters we can breathe deep the air of freedom as Indonesia was unshackled from colonial rule. 4. The long 70-year journey of independence has been replete with transformation efforts through development to realise the ideals of our predecessors, namely Indonesia as an independent, sovereign, unified, just and prosperous nation. 5. We are grateful and proud of the transformation achievements of Indonesia. We have enhanced the education system and extended it to the broader community. In terms of the economy, Indonesia has successfully become a middle income country, boasting the largest and fastest growing middle class population in Southeast Asia. Furthermore, in 2014 the Word Bank placed Indonesia as the eighth largest global economy based on Purchasing Power Parity. 6. From a political standpoint, the successful transformation of Indonesia is predicated upon Indonesias standing as the third largest democracy in the world, after the United States and India. Through transformation, Indonesia is currently more unified, peaceful, prosperous and democratic. Ladies and gentlemen: 7. Our successful accomplishments should not lead to complacency, however. Indonesias interminable journey remains beset by increasingly complex challenges that demand a more active contribution from us to the problems faced. 8. Concerning the economy, Bank Indonesia acknowledges a number of onerous external and domestic challenges to current and future conditions in Indonesia. 9. The global economy is currently reeling from sluggish growth with a bias towards the lower end of the projection, accompanied by ubiquitous risk blighting global financial markets. Projected global economic growth of 4% for 2015 has been revised down to 3.3%, which is lower than actual growth achieved last year at 3.4%. 10. Potential bias towards the lower end of the projection is the result of weaker-thanexpected US growth, with Q2 actuals of 2.3% (yoy) coming in below the projected 2.6% (yoy). 11. In addition, concerns over the proposed Federal Funds Rate hike, which prompted market uncertainty, is also affecting the global economy. The normalisation policy of the Federal Reserve could trigger a deluge of capital outflow and, thus, pressures on financial markets in the region, including Indonesia. Based on surveys and observations of the latest US economic indicators, the FFR hike is expected as early as September but possibly as late as December 2015 or January 2016 if indicators do not improve. 12. Against the inauspicious backdrop of a protracted US economic recovery, the global economy continues to suffer due to economic moderation in China as a key driver of growth. Several real sector indicators, such as retail sales and industrial production, continue to show signs of weakness in China.
