The stock market crashed, accompanied by lingering volatility that continues to undermine domestic investor confidence in stock market stabilisation and economic rebalancing measures. 13. Furthermore, the decision of the Peoples Bank of China to devalue the yuan by 1.9% against the US dollar on 11th August 2015 exacerbated pressures on the global economy. Market reaction was evident through a slump in exchange rate performance amongst trade partners of China, including the rupiah in Indonesia. Yuan devaluation policy wiped 8.3% (yoy) off exports from Indonesia in July 2015, the largest single decline in four months. Globally, yuan depreciation also adversely impacted trade partner countries that rely on exports of natural resources, including Indonesia. 14. On the other hand, the economic crisis that befell Greece demanded grater vigilance from countries in Europe concerning the negative spillover that could result. Crisis pressures eased modestly after the Hellenic Parliament approved preliminary reforms stipulated by the creditors of the bailout. Notwithstanding, the resignation of the Prime Minister, coupled with the bailout and restructuring of the Greek economy, continues to threaten economic stability in Europe and other regions. 15. The prolonged global recovery has also perpetuated the international commodity price slide. In Q2/2015, leading export commodities from Indonesia, including coal, palm oil, nickel and coffee, dropped in price. For a number of economies that rely on primary commodities, such as Indonesia, this implies the upcoming challenges of economic recovery will become increasingly burdensome. Ladies and gentlemen: 16. Global economic conditions demand our vigilance due to their impact on developing economies, including Indonesia. The challenges we face are becoming increasingly complex, especially as Indonesia continues to confront a variety of challenges at home. 17. Indonesia is currently marred by economic moderation, balance of payment and fiscal deficits, spiralling foreign debt, low absorption of infrastructure spending, sluggish credit growth as well as the weather phenomenon known as El Nino that could decimate food production. 18. Economic growth was recorded at 4.67% (yoy) in Q2/2015, slowing from 4.72% (yoy) in the previous period on weak investment, government consumption and household consumption. 19. Confronting the challenges, Bank Indonesia instituted a policy mix that prioritises stability to ensure high-quality economic growth. Furthermore, Bank Indonesia policy is consistently directed towards creating stable macroeconomic conditions, primarily in the form of on-target inflation, while reducing the current account deficit to a more sustainable level. 20. Exchange rate policy aims to maintain rupiah stability in line with the currencys fundamental value, thereby avoiding excessive expectations of depreciation that could undermine economic stability. 21. Bank Indonesia considers recent rupiah depreciation the result of overshooting, leaving the currency undervalued. Addressing the challenge, Bank Indonesia has and will continue market intervention efforts to stabilise rupiah exchange rates. 22. Facing the current domestic and global economic dynamics, Bank Indonesia will optimise its policy mix, supported by tighter coordination with the Government and relevant authorities concerning macroeconomic policy management. Ladies and Gentlemen: 23. It is important to note that inflationary pressures through to July 2015 were controlled. National inflation was recorded at 0.93% (mtm) in July 2015, or 1.90% (ytd) cumulatively for the year or 7.26% (yoy) on an annualised basis in line with anchored inflation expectations. Based on the current trend, Bank Indonesia is satisfied that the inflation target of 41% in 2015 will be achieved. 24. The BI Board of Governors decided on 18th August 2015 to hold the BI Rate at 7.50%, while maintaining the Deposit Facility rate at 5.50% and the Lending Facility rate at 8.00%. The decision was consonant with efforts to control inflation within the target corridor of 41% in 2015 and 2016. Furthermore, the policy mix instituted by Bank Indonesia is consistently directed towards preserving rupiah stability, despite persistently uncertain global financial markets, as well as optimising monetary operations on the rupiah money market and foreign exchange market. 25. A consistently tight monetary policy stance taken by Bank Indonesia is expected to restore investor confidence in the consistency and quality of macroeconomic policy management in Indonesia as the proposed FFR hike looms. We consider investor confidence crucial to maintain global liquidity flows to our stock and bond markets, in particular government bonds. This, in turn, will reduce the burden of development financing through tradeable government securities (SBN). Ladies and Gentlemen: 26. We view investment an important pro-growth sector in Indonesia, especially as other supporting sectors, such as exports and consumption, are decelerating. Consequently, ongoing efforts to attract more investment into Indonesia require greater optimisation. 27. Therefore, the international role of representatives of the Republic of Indonesia is vital. Indonesian Embassies and Consulate Generals, which are located in nearly every country in the world, are expected to extol the economic potential of Indonesia, thereby attracting investment to the country. 28. Such efforts would be greatly improved if, in their function, the Embassies and Consulate Generals were supported by the Indonesia Investment Coordinating Board (BKPM), Bank Indonesia, the banking industry and other state apparatus available in each country. 29. Hitherto, the mutually supportive roles played by RI representative offices, the Indonesia Investment Coordinating Board (BKPM), Bank Indonesia and other related parties in the United States to attract US investors to Indonesia has borne fruit. Consequently, the United States has ranked in the top ten largest investors in Indonesia for the past five years. In 2014, actual US investment topped USD1.3 billion, ranking the country sixth, while there remains clear room for further growth. Ladies and Gentlemen: 30. We consider the US position as an engine of the global economy vitally strategic for Indonesia, especially in line with the US status as one of the leading investors in Indonesia. Furthermore, as our exports attest, the United States is also an important trading partner of Indonesia as one of our leading export destinations. 31. In 2014, total exports from Indonesia to the United States amounted to USD16.5 billion, making the US the third largest export destination for Indonesian products after China and Japan. In the case of non-oil and gas shipments, the United States represents the second largest export destination after China, totalling USD15.8 billion, increasing 5.56% (yoy) on the position in 2013. 32. The prevailing facts and data confirm the close links enjoyed between the United States and Indonesia. Therefore, we sincerely hope that the clear communication, intensive coordination and synergic collaboration built between representatives of the Republic of Indonesia, the Bank Indonesia Representative Office, the Indonesia Investment Coordinating Board (BKPM), the banking industry and other relevant parties in the United States will continue and improve. The positive contribution of all parties will help to create a cordial relationship and mutually beneficial cooperation between Indonesia and the United States towards the betterment of society in both countries. 33. In light of the positive accomplishments and fruitful coordination enjoyed so far, allow me to express our heartfelt appreciation to the Honourable Ambassador and Consul General, along with their corresponding staff, as well as to all those here in the United States who have backed and supported our efforts. Ladies and Gentlemen: 34. I would like to take this opportunity to graciously thank Mr Sugeng, who has served the mandate of Bank Indonesia emphatically. As Chief Representative of Bank Indonesia in New York, Mr Sugneg has built a solid foundation through harmonious coordination and collaboration with all stakeholders, in particular the Honourable Consul General of the Republic of Indonesia in New York. 35. Armed with vast experience and insight, Mr Sugeng will fill his new role as Head of the Bank Indonesia Institute with gusto, tasked with creating a competent and highly motivated workforce at Bank Indonesia. 36. To Mr Erwin Haryono, the new Chief Representative of Bank Indonesia in New York, we extend great expectations to maintain existing performance, while optimising Bank Indonesias role and growing the relationships with all stakeholders and strategic partners in country. 37. In closing, on behalf of the Governor of Bank Indonesia, we would like to thank the Honourable Consul General of the Republic of Indonesia in New York and his staff for their assistance with the organisation of this event here today. I would also like to thank all of you in attendance for sparing your valuable time this morning. May all our undertakings to advance the country, state and people be blessed by the Lord God Almighty and let Him give us the strength to carry on. Thank you. Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Ronald Waas

Title: Message from the Deputy Governor Halim Alamsyah On Opening "Strategic Entrepreneurship Policy Forum" in Jakarta, 21 November 2014
Subtitle: At The Opening of Entrepreneurship Strategic Policy Forum
text: Keynote Speech Deputy Governor Halim Alamsyah At The Opening of Entrepreneurship Strategic Policy Forum Jakarta, 21 November 2014 The Honorable, Mr. Ciputra as the representative of Global Entrepreneurship Week in Indonesia, The respectful,  Mr. Dane Stangler, Vice President of Research Policy & Policy of Ewing Marion Kauffman Foundation;  Mr. Jeff Hoffman, International Advisory Boards of Global Entrepreneurship Week;  Mr. Herry Suhardiyanto, Rector of Institut Pertanian Bogor (IPB)  Mr. Harun Hajadi, Managing Director of Ciputra Group  Officials from the Ministries and their Staff;  Leaders and officials of Financial Services Authority (OJK), Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta, Banking, Universities, Business Associations and Distinguished Guests Assalamualaikum Wr. Wb, Good afternoon and Greetings to us all. 1. To start this afternoons agenda, I would like to ask us all to praise God the Almighty, Allah SWT, for His blessings we have been given the chance to meet in this excellent atmosphere, in the opening ceremony of Entrepreneurship Strategic Policy Forum 2014. I would like to extend my highest appreciation to Ladies and Gentlemen, attendances of this event. I hope your present may provide the maximum contribution in the efforts to build a national entrepreneurship ecosystem. 2. In the last few years, we all observed that entrepreneurship has become the hot topic of discussions in various societies, from academicians, policy makers to business actors. Based on the survey of Ernst and Young Consultant Agency to 1,500 entrepreneurs in the G20 country group1, this was due to the fact that entrepreneurship was an agent of vital changes in the creation of business models and new industries, the development new products and services or the implementation of efficient production methods. Aside from that, from macro perspective, entrepreneurship has an important role as the driver and controller of regional economy, nation, and country through the creation of jobs/employment and encouragement of economic growth. Ladies and Gentlemen, 3. Indonesias economic growth in the period of 2009-2013 has reached 5.9% per annum, which was the highest economic growth after we went through the economic crisis fifteen years ago2. This figure also indicates that among the G20 member countries in year 2012 and 2013, Indonesia has become the country with the third highest economic growth after China and India. Besides, Indonesia also has been uplifted to the middle-income country and included in the category of 10 top world economics if calculated from the Purchasing Power Parity, 1 The EY G20 Entrepreneurship Barometer 2013 2 BPS, 2014 having the biggest middle-class population in Southeast Asia and the fastest middle-class growth in Asia3. 4. Our success in the economic sector, in reality has not been offset by entrepreneurial growth. This is reflected by three things, namely: First, the population of new entrepreneurs only reached 1.65% from the total population. That figure is far behind if compared to the neighboring countries such as Malaysia, Thailand, and Singapore that have reached above 4%4. Whereas, as we often hear, Sociologist David McClelland said that to become a prosperous nation, a country must have a minimum of 2% entrepreneurs from its total population. Second, in regard to the entrepreneurial ecosystem health, Indonesia ranks as the 68th out of 121 countries in the world according to The Global Entrepreneurship & Development Index 20145. Third, based on EY G20 Entrepreneurship Barometer 2013, Indonesia among the G20 countries is included in the fourth quartile, the country group that has the lowest rank in the entrepreneurial ecosystem calculated from 4 (four) indicators weighted equally, i.e. financing access, entrepreneurial culture, tax and regulation, education and training, and also coordination support. Apart from Indonesia, included in the fourth quartile are Argentina, India, Italy and Turkey. Distinguished Guests, 5. Knowing the fact that entrepreneurship and the conductivity of entrepreneurial ecosystem in Indonesia are still at low level, the fundamental question would be how far the efforts that we have undertaken to support the development of 3 GBI Keynote Speech in the Anniversary of Indonesias 69th Independence Day, 17 August 2014 4 Kemenkop and UKM (SME), March 2013 5 Global Entrepreneurship and Development Index (GEDI) 2014 Report entrepreneurship all this time. To answer that question, let us be reminded of Gerakan Kewirausahaan Nasional-GKN (National Entrepreneurship Movement) that has been launched by the President with the 13 Ministries in year 2011. It cannot be denied that since the launching of GKN, various institutions have held programs on the creation of new entrepreneurs both in the form of business plan competition, training and coaching of entrepreneurs, internship, facilitating promotion up to seed capital provision. From the view of the ease in starting business, several agencies have implemented online licensing system and the application of One Door Integrated Services or the socalled One Stop Service. 6. Similar thing has been conducted by Bank Indonesia through the initiation of entrepreneurship program in the 8 Representative Offices of Bank Indonesia with the target of students, former TKI (Indonesian workers), and the community of various business fields. Such program then followed by mentoring program continuation in 2013 through a series of training, internship and promotion. In year 2014 the program shall be expanded by involving 24 Bank Indonesia Representative Offices throughout Indonesia with the target of entrepreneurs in the sector agribusiness and/or exportoriented business in order to support food resilience and improvement of balance of trade structure. 7. In reality, the efforts in the development of entrepreneurship in Indonesia are still in the form of partial programs by various institutions so that the impact caused still not optimal and sustainable. In order to make entrepreneurship movement more effective and growing as well as to enhance the coordination of new entrepreneurship growth in Indonesia, it requires a formulation of a more macro policy to encourage the development of entrepreneurial climate which is conducive as entrepreneurial ecosystem. Ladies and Gentlemen, 8. Entrepreneurial Ecosystem may be viewed as an effort to encourage the growth of entrepreneurship so it can create new economic centers in the region that eventually can have a role in the economic growth nationally. 9. Aspen Network of Development Entrepreneurs, a global organization which has a vision to motivate entrepreneurship in the developing countries, concludes that there are 8 (eight) important areas in developing entrepreneurial ecosystem. Those areas are finance, business support, policy, market, human capital, infrastructure, R&D and culture. 10. These areas of classification can help the policy makers to provide development areas of priority based on each mandate and capability6. Development areas of finance, support, policy, and markets are the responsibility of financial institutions and relevant government authorities directly handling the financial institutions both banks and non-banks, association of entrepreneurs and entrepreneurs mentoring institutions, regional and central governments, as well as domestic and international companies. Meanwhile, the development areas of human capital, infrastructure, research and development, and also culture are the responsibility of universities, relevant BUMN (state-owned enterprises), research institutes, as well as media and social organizations. 6 Entrepreneurial Ecosystem Diagnostic Toolkit, Aspen Network of Development Entrepreneurs, 2013 11. In this forum, present among us are 2 (two) prominent international entrepreneurs, Mr. Dane Stangler, researcher from Ewing Marion Kauffman Foundation that has conducted study/research on the best practices of entrepreneurial ecosystem in various countries, and Mr. Jeff Hoffman, a successful entrepreneur and motivator who has a passion to develop entrepreneurial ecosystem in the developing countries. It is expected that both can provide positive inputs and inspirations in striving for developing entrepreneurial ecosystem in Indonesia. Such insight will be more complete and meaningful with the presence of our two national speakers, Mr. Harun Hajadi, Managing Director of Ciputra Group, and the Rector of IPB, Mr. Herry Suhardiyanto. Ladies and Gentlemen, 12. Before I close my speech, I would like to express my gratitude to all members of the committee and all parties involving in the organization of this event. Furthermore, I also would like to invite all attendances, Ladies and Gentlemen, to actively participate and provide constructive inputs in order to support the development of national entrepreneurial ecosystem. Let us together learn from the experiences of the resources and take advantage of the best possible for the development of entrepreneurial ecosystem in Indonesia. 13. I sincerely hope that todays activity may become the start of communication in order to formulate a policy recommendation at national level related to the efforts in building entrepreneurial ecosystem in Indonesia. 14. Finally, by saying Bismillahirrahmanirrahim and by asking for the blessing of Allah SWT, the God Almighty, I officially declare that this Entrepreneurship Strategic Policy Forum 2014 is open. Thank you. Wassalamualaikum Wr. Wb. Jakarta, 21 November 2014 DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF BANK INDONESIA Halim Alamsyah

Title: Sambutan Gubernur Bank Indonesia, Agus D.W. Martowardojo pada "Peluncuran Bantuan Pangan Non Tunai" Jakarta, 23 Februari 2017
text: Launch of Non-Cash Food Assistance Jakarta, 23rd February 2017 What we respect: 95 President of the Republic of Indonesia 95 Coordinating Minister for Human Development and Culture 95 Minister of Social Affairs 95 Minister of SOEs 95 Chairman of the Board of Commissioners of the Financial Services Authority 95 In re kt your Main Logistics Affairs Agency (BULOG) 95 President Directors of Bank HIM BARA 95 Happy Father/Mother of Honor Assalammualaikum Wr. Wb. Morning Mats and Greetings For All of Us, 1. We are very grateful because today is a step of change and a very big progress in the distribution of social assistance to all Indonesian people. 2. If previously social assistance was provided in cash; currently, the assistance is directly provided non-cash through the banking system and is sufficiently accessed through a card. The card used is a combo card with savings and electronic money features, called the Prosperous Family Card (KKS). 3. If previously all the aid money received would be immediately spent until it ran out; nowadays people can accept it as a whole, use it in moderation, and start practicing to save money soas not to be consumptive. Moreover, assistance through a card is much safer, than carrying cash. 4. And if previously people needed to come and queue at a withdrawal location located far from their homes; nowadays people can save time and simply come to e- warong as a banking agent in their own environment to attract the benefits of assistance programs social with PSC. Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen Of Our Respectful Audience, 5. After the successful distribution of the Keluarga Harapan Program (PKH) in 68 regencies/cities throughout 2016 using PSC, today the distribution of Non-Cash Food Assistance nationwide will be carried out which is also using PSC, simultaneously in 44 Cities for more than 1.2 million Manfa At Recipient Families which will be inaugurated directly by Mr. President. 6. As directed by mr. President on April 26, 2016 that the distribution of social assistance and subsidies must be carried out non-cash and through the banking system, we are proud and big-hearted for being affected. osan that we are able to go together to realize an increasingly effective and efficient distribution. 7. We welcome and fully support the transformation of the Poor Rice Program (Raskin) into Non-Cash Food Assistance (BPNT) which will be launched today. Throughthe provision of staples by BULOG and non-cash distribution, it is hoped that the community will get more quality food, in appropriate quantities, and can be purchased more and more easily and affordably. 8. We from Bank Indonesia are also grateful to be able to take part in this transformation. Various process improvements and improved convenience for the community have been pursued together. This can be seen from the early stages of the distribution process, where the community prospective beneficiaries will be provided with the convenience of opening a bank account through simpler requirements and collective registration. 9. Then the community will also be given intensive education and socialization about the benefits of the assistance provided, including the procedure for transacting using cards and withdrawing assistance at agents . In addition, the public will also be informed of how to complain if they encounter difficulties or obstacles when they want to take the assistance provided. 10. When the community ingin take the assistance provided, the community is also increasingly facilitated, because it can directly come to e-warong as agents of HIMBARA banks who have been appointed as social assistance distributors. Together with the Financial Services Authority, we at Bank Indonesia continue to encourage the readiness of these banking agents to serve the receiving community. ll.In line with the target distribution area set by the Ministry of Social Affairs, there are currently 15,878 Digital Financial Services (LKD) and Laku Pandai yang agents spread throughout Indonesia and have ready to distribute Food Aid. 12. With the realization of the Family Hope and Food Assistance Program into one card, namely the PSC, we are optimistic that in the future the social assistance program and other subsidies will also be integrated with the more efficient. 13. Furthermore, by holding accounts in banks and PSC, it will open up opportunities for people to get access to formal finance, train them to save, and also train more baik financial management in society. 14. Therefore, let us express our gratitude for the direction of Mr. President and the close synergy of the Ministry of Coord. Human Development and Culture, Ministry of Social Affairs, Ministry of SOEs, Financial Services Authority, BULOG, and HIMBARA Banking, as well as all parties who have carried out joint efforts in da lam realizing the ideals of mem ba ng un Indonesian society that is increasingly inclusive and prosperous. That's it and Thank you. Wassaiammuaiaikum Wr. Wb. Agus D.W. Martowardojo Governor of Bank Indonesia
text_original: Sambutan Gubernur Bank Indonesia Peluncuran Bantuan Pangan Non Tunai Jakarta, 23 Februari 2017 Yang kami hormati: <95> Presiden Republik Indonesia <95> Menteri Koordinator Bidang Pembangunan Manusia dan Kebudayaan <95> Menteri Sosial <95> Menteri BUMN <95> Ketua Dewan Komisioner Otoritas Jasa Keuangan <95> Di re kt ur Utama Badan Urusan Logistik (BULOG) <95> Para Direktur Utama Bank HIM BARA <95> Bapak/Ibu Hadirin sekalian yang berbahagia Assalammualaikum Wr. Wb. Sela mat Pagi dan Salam Sejahtera Untuk Kita Semua, 1. Kami amat bersyukur karena hari ini adalah sebuah langkah perubahan dan kemajuan yang amat besar da lam penyaluran bantuan sosial kepada seluruh masyarakat Indonesia. 2. Jika sebelumnya bantuan sosial diberikan dalam bentuk tunai; saat ini bantuan tersebut langsung diberikan secara non tunai melalui sistem perbankan dan cukup diakses melalui kartu. Kartu yang digunakan adalah satu kartu kombo dengan fitur tabungan dan uang elektronik, yang dinamakan Kartu Keluarga Sejahtera (KKS). 3. Jika sebelumnya seluruh uang bantuan yang diterima akan langsung dibelanjakan sampai habis; saat ini masyarakat dapat menerima secara utuh, menggunakan secukupnya, dan mulai berlatih untuk menabung serta untuk tidak bersikap konsumtif. Apalagi, bantuan melalui kartu jauh lebih aman, dibandingkan membawa uang tunai. 4. Dan jika sebelumnya masyarakat perlu datang dan antri di lokasi penarikan yang terletak jauh dari rumah mereka; saat ini masyarakat dapat menghemat waktu dan cukup datang ke e- warong sebagai agen perbankan yang ada di lingkungan mereka sendiri untuk menarik manfaat program bantuan sosial dengan KKS. Bapak Presiden, Bapak/Ibu Hadirin Yang Kami Hormati, 5. Setelah keberhasilan penyaluran Program Keluarga Harapan (PKH) di 68 Kabupaten/Kota sepanjang tahun 2016 menggunakan KKS, pada hari ini akan dilakukan penyaluran Bantuan Pangan Non Tunai secara nasional yang juga menggunakan KKS, serentak di 44 Kota bagi lebih dari 1,2 juta Keluarga Penerima Manfaat yang akan diresmikan langsung oleh Bapak Presiden. 6. Sebagaimana arahan Bapak Presiden pada 26 April 2016 bahwa penyaluran bantuan sosial dan subsidi harus dilakukan secara non tunai dan melalui sistem perbankan, kami ikut bangga dan besar hati atas terobosan yang mampu kita tempuh bersama guna mewujudkan penyaluran yang semakin efektif dan efisien. 7. Kami menyambut baik dan mendukung penuh transformasi Program Beras Miskin (Raskin) menjadi Bantuan Pangan Non Tunai (BPNT) yang akan diluncurkan hari ini. Melalui penyediaan bahan pokok oleh BULOG dan penyaluran secara non tunai, diharapkan masyarakat akan mendapatkan bahan pangan yang semakin berkualitas, dalam jumlah yang sesuai, dan dapat dibeli dengan semakin mudah dan terjangkau. 8. Kami dari Bank Indonesia juga bersyukur dapat turut ambil bagian dalam transformasi ini. Berbagai perbaikan proses dan peningkatan kemudahan bagi masyarakat telah diupayakan bersama. Hal ini terlihat sejak tahap awal proses penyaluran, dimana masyarakat calon penerima bantuan akan diberikan kemudahan pembukaan rekening bank melalui persyaratan yang lebih sederhana dan registrasi secara kolektif. 9. Kemudian masyarakat juga akan diberikan edukasi dan sosialisasi intensif mengenai manfaat dari bantuan yang diberikan, termasuk tata cara bertransaksi menggunakan kartu dan penarikan bantuan di agen. Selain itu, masyarakat juga akan diinformasikan bagaimana tata cara pengaduan apabila menemui kesulitan atau hambatan pada saat ingin mengambil bantuan yang diberikan. 10. Pada saat masyarakat ingin mengambil bantuan yang diberikan, masyarakat juga semakin dimudahkan, karena dapat langsung datang ke e-warong sebagai agen bank-bank HIMBARA yang telah ditunjuk sebagai penyalur bantuan sosial. Bersama dengan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan, kami di Bank Indonesia terus mendorong kesiapan agen perbankan tersebut da lam melayani masyarakat penerima. ll.Sejalan dengan target wilayah penyaluran yang ditetapkan Kementerian Sosial, saat ini telah terdapat 15.878 agen Layanan Keuangan Digital (LKD) dan Laku Pandai yang tersebar di seluruh Indonesia dan telah siap menyalurkan Bantuan Pangan. 12. Dengan telah diwujudkannya Program Keluarga Harapan dan Bantuan Pangan kedalam satu kartu, yaitu KKS, kami optimis kedepan program bantuan sosial dan subsidi lainnya juga akan dapat diintegrasikan dengan semakin efisien. 13. Lebih lanjut, dengan kepemilikan rekening di bank dan KKS, maka akan membuka kesempatan masyarakat mendapatkan akses keuangan formal, melatih mereka menabung, dan juga melatih pengelolaan keuangan yang lebih baik di masyarakat. 14. Oleh karena itu, izinkan kami menyampaikan terimakasih atas arahan Bapak Presiden dan sinergi yang erat dari Kementrian Koord. Bidang Pembangunan Manusia dan Kebudayaan, Kementrian Sosial, Kementerian BUMN, Otoritas Jasa Keuangan, BULOG, dan Perbankan HIMBARA, serta seluruh pihak yang telah menjalankan ikhtiar bersama da lam mewujudkan cita-cita mem ba ng un masyarakat Indonesia yang semakin inklusif dan sejahtera. Sekian dan Terimakasih. Wassaiammuaiaikum Wr. Wb. Agus D.W. Martowardojo Gubernur Bank Indonesia

Title: Sambutan Gubernur Bank Indonesia, Agus D.W. Martowardojo Pada Peluncuran Gerbang Pembayaran Nasional, Jakarta, 4 Desember 2017
text: Launching of National Payment Gateways Jakarta, 4th December 2017 What We Respect: 95 Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs 95 Minister of SOEs 95 Minister Sosiai 95 Minister of Finance 95 Minister of Communication and Informatics 95 Wakii Chairman of the Board of Commissioners of the Financial Services Authority 95 De wan Members of the Governor of Bank Indonesia 95 Chairman of The Indonesian Payment System Association 95 The Directors of Uta ma Banking 95 The Directors of Uta ma Switching Organizers 95 Ladies and Gentlemen, Happy Sekaiian Invitation Attendees Assaiammuaiaikum Wr. Wb. Morning and Saiam Well For All of Us. 1. Praise and thanks let us pray to God Almighty, for only by His grace can we gather, in good health, be present together following the Launching of Gerbang National Payments. 2. All of us Indonesians certainly realize that every one of our daily economic activities, from buying groceries, subscribing to telecommunications services, to meeting needs Transportation is inseparable from the use of payment instruments, both cash and non-cash. 3. Especially in the current era of digitalization, we pay close attention to how electronic retail payment instruments and facilities are growing increasingly prevalent in Indonesia, in order to meet the public's need for payment tools that are getting faster, easier, and more practical. 4. For example, in 2017, in every minute there were more than 10,000 ATM, Debit, and Credit Card transactions in Indonesia. Therefore That, Indonesia as a country with such a large population and such a wide geographical reach, should have a national payment system that is safe, smooth, efficient, and reliable. 5. However , we note that amid the need for transactions, there are still fragmentations, inefficiencies, and security risks faced by consumers. Fragmentation arose due to the industry's tendency to build payment system platforms that are exclusive in nature, that is, they can only serve their own published instruments. 6. The existing platforms are also not interconnected or interconnected with each other, so they have not been able to provide an ecosystem of services that can serve each other (interoperable). The simplest illustration that we often encounter is the large number of ATM machines in the mall and the row of EDC machines at the supermarket cashier. 7. Kami also sees that the capability of implementing switching and processing domestic transactions in Indonesia, which has existed since more than 20 years ago, is still limited to ONLY ATM services. While other services, such as debit card transactions lintas issuer and acquirer (off-us) where the card is issued in Indonesia, held by Indonesians, and used to buy goods / services in Indonesia, until now still have to be processed transactions abroad. 8. Such fragmentation in turn gives birth to inefficiency, which can be seen from several main points, namely: 1) The investment cost of expanding infrastructure and technology has become high, as the industry is reluctant to share services, such as the investment of ATM machines and EDC which is so large only for one location. In fact, if these machines can be interoperable, there is such a great potential to relocate them to areas across the country that are still experiencing shortages. So that it will be able to encourage the expansion of akses and financial inclusion in Indonesia. 2) People become necessary to have many cards, because the acceptance of cards is still limited. This is because certain cards can only be used in certain payment terminal machines, as a result of each ATM or EDC cannot accept all types of cards. 3) Even if accepted, cards used at different ATM / EDC terminals will be charged a relatively high fee, where the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) can reach 2-3% per transaction. This cost is certainly ultimately insured by consumers. Ladies and Gentlemen Of Our Respected Audience, 9. Taking into account these conditions, Bank Indonesia believes that the presence of the National Payment Gateway (NPG) is very important and needed by all Indonesians. NpGgan carrying out is the implementation of the mandate given by the Law to Bank Indonesia as the National Payment System Authority to achieve a safe, smooth national payment system , and efficient. 10. We are so heartened, since it was initiated more than 20 years ago, namely in the Blueprint of the National Payment System of 1995/1996, this morning will be a moment historic because NPG will be launched and its implementation begins. 11. There are at least three main objectives of NPGimplementation: 1) Creating a payment ecosystem that is interconnected, interoperable, and able to carry out transaction processing that includes authority, clearing, and settlement domestically. 2) Improving consumer protection, among others, through the provisionof customer transaction data in every transaction. 3) Ensuring the availability and integrity of national payment system transaction data, in order to support the effectiveness of monetary policy transmission, intermediation efficiency, and financial system resilience. 12.Jamn that, NPG is also presented as a backbone to provide full support to government programs. These include the distribution of non-cash social assistance, electronification of toll roads and public transportation, financial inclusion, and the development ofa national trade system based on electronics that have been mandated in PRESIDENTIAL REGULATION 74 of 2017 concerning the E-Commerce Roadmap. Ladies and Gentlemen Of Our Respected Audience, 13. In order to achieve this target, Bank Indonesia has issued NPG provisions consisting of six policy points, namely: 1) Establish three NPG Operators, namely Standard Institutions, Switching Institutions, and Services Institutions. 95 Standards Institution, in charge of compiling and managing national payment technology standards set by Bank Indonesia and must be obeyed by all industries, namely for ATMs/Debits are NSICCS, and for Money Electronics is through the application of SAM Multi Applet. Currently the Standards Institute has been established and run by the Indonesian Government Systems Association (ASPI) as an industry representation. Henceforth, the Standards Institution will be directed in the form of a legal entity with professional, competent and independent management. 95 Switching Institution, in charge of organizing the processing of domestic payment transaction data in a secure and efficient manner. At the launch of NPG, we would like to convey that Bank Indonesia has established 4 domestic switching operators as NPG Switching Institutions, namely Jalin Pembayaran Nusantara, Artajasa Pembayaran Elektronik, Rintis Sejahtera, and Alto Network. 95 Lembaga Services, has four main tasks, namely (1) maintaining transaction security by ensuring end-to-end encryption of transaction data, (2) organizing reconciliation-clearing-settlement efficiently; (3) handling transaction disputes d.r. consumer protection; and (4) encourage the expansion of acceptance of non-cash instruments. Lembaga Services is formed and jointly owned by the NPG Switching Institution and subsidiaries of the main industry players, namely BRI, BNI, Bank Mandiri, and BCA, which account for a 75% share of national retail payment transactions through a consortium. The establishment of the consortium will begin with the signing of the agreement this morning, and it is expected that it will soon be incorporated to be fully operational in July 2018. 2) Infrastructure structuring, namely by requiring issuers , acquirers , agents, and pay/77e/7fpaten/ayterconnected to a minimum of two NPG Switching Institutions. As well as followed by the obligation of interconnection between NPG Switching Institutions, so that service reliability can be maintained. 3) Domestic transaction processing obligations {routing} , i.e. to instruments issued domestically and transacted through domestic payment channels, are mandatory to be processed through existing infrastructure and systems in the country. 4) Establish a reasonable pricing policy. For the initial stage, in the NPG PADG, the amount of debit card MDR has been set at 1% per off-us transaction, or lower than what has been valid so far in the range of 2-3%. This reduction in MDR is effective nationwide following the launch of NPG this morning. We believe that this pricing scheme will be able to drive efficiency, healthy competition, and service innovation. 5) Implementing the national logo, in order to expand the acceptance of non-cash retail payment instruments that can be used at all domestic merchants. Starting in 2018, all issuers are required to provide cards with the national logo and explain the benefits to customers. 6) Standardize service features, so as to be able to answer the development of community transaction needs. The features of the services that must be provided include payments, transfers, cash withdrawals, balance inquiry, and other services that will be further determined by Bank Indonesia. In the future, there will also be a standardized and interoperable routine bill payment feature, such as electricity, water, and health insurance bills through the Electronic Billing and Invoicing Presentment and Payment (EBIPP) feature. ). 14. With a series of policies inplace, the expected positive impact: 1) Encourage sharing infrastructure, so that the utilization of ATM/EDC terminals can increase and excess ones can be relocated to deprived areas. The cost of infrastructure investment can then be diverted back to financing/loan activities which will ultimately have a positive impact on economic growth. 2) Reducing the complexity of the connection from previously bilateral between parties, to being centralized to NPG. 3) People can transact from any bank, using any instrument and payment channel {any bank, any instrument, any channel). 4) National efficiency will be created from a more competitive pricing scheme. Ladies and Gentlemen Of Our Respected Audience, 15. The launch of NPG this morning is the fruit of the synergy that has been built with the industry for a long time. In order to ensure readiness and smooth implementation, starting in 2016 Bank Indonesia and the industry have intensively completed concept tests and conducted piloting at 122 large merchants on a national scale. We are grateful that, to date, the 4 NPG Switching Institutions have been connected to 60 issuers and 14 acquirers, with an interopera bi litas rate of debit transactions reaching 75%. 16. Taking into account the readiness and progress that has been achieved, in the series of events this morning, 4 documents will be carried out that mark the start of NPG operationalization, namely: 95 Consortium Agreement to inaugurate the establishment of the Services Institute 95 Cooperation Agreement on the Interconnection of the 4 NPG Switching Institutions 95 Cooperation Agreement interopera bi litas Debit Card 95 Cooperation Agreement interopera bi litas Electronic Money 17. In addition, the national logo of NPG will also be launched as a symbol of the identity of the national payment system which will be part of the transactions of the entire community that are increasingly safe, reliable, and trusted. Mr/Mrs. Hadi tin Whom We Respect, 18.Before concluding our remarks, we would like to express our high gratitude and appreciation to the Ministry, Authority Financial Services, industry, and associations for their synergy and support in the success of NPG development. We hope that the synergy and support can be stronger, in overseeing the implementation in order to realize the main ghgn targets that are aspired to. 19. On this occasion, we also invite the Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs, Mrs. Minister of SOEs, Mrs. Minister of Social Affairs, Mrs. Minister of Finance, and Mr. Minister of Communication and Information Technology to be pleased to provide support and welcome, which we believe is in line with fostering optimism for all of us to welcome An Indonesia that is ready to face the digital era, through a safe, reliable national payment system, efficient, and smooth. 20. Finally, along with the benefits, conveniences, and conveniences that will be felt, we hope that all these efforts will be able to encourage an increase in cashless transactions as a catalyst and lifeblood for Indonesia's current and future economic growth. Thank you. Wassaiammuaiaikum Wr. Wb. Governor of Bank Indonesia Agus D.W. Martowardojo
text_original: Sambutan Gubernur Bank Indonesia Launching Gerbang Pembayaran Nasional Jakarta, 4 Desember 2017 Yang Kami Hormati: <95> Menteri Koordinator Bidang Perekonomian <95> Menteri BUMN <95> Menteri Sosiai <95> Menteri Keuangan <95> Menteri Komunikasi dan Informatika <95> Wakii Ketua Dewan Komisioner Otoritas Jasa Keuangan <95> Para Anggota De wan Gubernur Bank Indonesia <95> Ketua Asosiasi Sistem Pembayaran Indonesia <95> Para Direktur Uta ma Perbankan <95> Para Direktur Uta ma Penyeienggara Switching <95> Bapak/Ibu, Hadirin Undangan Sekaiian Yang Berbahagia Assaiammuaiaikum Wr. Wb. Seiamat Pagi dan Saiam Sejahtera Bagi Kita Semua. 1. Puji dan syukur marilah kita panjatkan kepada Tuhan Yang Maha Kuasa, karena hanya atas rahmat-Nya kita dapat berkumpul, dalam keadaan sehat, hadir bersama mengikuti Launching Gerbang Pembayaran Nasional. 2. Kita semua masyarakat Indonesia tentu menyadari, bahwa setiap aktivitas ekonomi kita sehari-hari, mulai dari membeli bahan makanan, berlangganan jasa telekomunikasi, sampai dengan memenuhi kebutuhan transportasi tidak terlepas dari transaksi menggunakan alat pembayaran, baik tunai maupun non tunai. 3. Apalagi di era digitalisasi saat ini, kami mencermati bagaimana instrumen dan sarana pembayaran ritel elektronik tumbuh kian marak di Indonesia, guna memenuhi kebutuhan masyarakat akan alat pembayaran yang semakin cepat, mudah, dan praktis. 4. Sebagai contoh, di tahun 2017, dalam setiap menit terjadi lebih dari 10.000 transaksi ATM, Debit, dan Kartu Kredit di Indonesia. Oleh karena itu, Indonesia sebagai negara dengan populasi yang begitu besar dan jangkauan geografis yang begitu luas, sudah semestinya memiliki sistem pembayaran nasional yang aman, lancar, efisien, dan andal. 5. Namun kami mencermati, ditengah pesatnya kebutuhan bertransaksi, masih terdapat fragmentasi, inefisiensi, dan risiko keamanan yang dihadapi konsumen. Fragmentasi muncul karena kecenderungan industri untuk membangun platform sistem pembayaran yang sifatnya eksklusif, yaitu hanya dapat melayani instrumen yang diterbitkannya sendiri. 6. Platform-platform yang ada juga belum saling terhubung atau interconnected satu sama lain, sehingga belum mampu menyediakan ekosistem layanan yang dapat saling melayani (interoperabel). Ilustrasi paling sederhana yang sering kita jumpai adalah banyaknya deretan mesin ATM di mall dan berjejernya mesin EDC di kasir supermarket. 7. Kami juga melihat bahwa kapabilitas penyelenggaraan switching dan pemrosesan transaksi domestik di Indonesia, yang telah ada sejak lebih dari 20 tahun lalu, masih terbatas hanya pada layanan ATM. Sedangkan layanan lainnya, seperti transaksi kartu debit lintas penerbit dan acquirer (off-us) dimana kartunya diterbitkan di Indonesia, dipegang oleh orang Indonesia, dan digunakan untuk membeli barang/jasa di Indonesia, hingga saat ini masih harus diproses transaksinya ke luar negeri. 8. Fragmentasi tersebut pada gilirannya melahirkan inefisiensi, yang dapat dilihat dari beberapa hal utama, yaitu: 1) Biaya investasi perluasan infrastruktur dan teknologi menjadi tinggi, karena industri enggan berbagi layanan, seperti investasi mesin ATM dan EDC yang begitu besar hanya untuk di satu lokasi. Padahal, apabila mesin-mesin tersebut dapat saling interoperabel, terdapat potensi yang begitu besar untuk merelokasinya ke daerah-daerah di penjuru tanah air yang masih mengalami kekurangan. Sehingga akan mampu mendorong perluasan akses dan keuangan inklusif di Indonesia. 2) Masyarakat menjadi perlu untuk memiliki banyak kartu, karena akseptasi kartu yang masih terbatas. Hal ini dikarenakan kartu tertentu hanya dapat digunakan di mesin terminal pembayaran tertentu, akibat setiap ATM atau EDC tidak dapat menerima semua jenis kartu. 3) Kalaupun diterima, kartu yang digunakan pada terminal ATM / EDC yang berbeda akan dikenakan biaya yang relatif tinggi, dimana Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) dapat mencapai 2-3% per transaksi. Biaya ini tentu pada akhirnya ikutditanggung oleh konsumen. Bapak/Ibu Hadirin Yang Kami Hormati, 9. Memperhatikan kondisi tersebut, Bank Indonesia meyakini kehadiran Gerbang Pembayaran Nasional (GPN) menjadi amat penting dan dibutuhkan oleh seluruh masyarakat Indonesia. Pengembangan GPN merupakan pelaksanaan mandat yang diberikan Undang-Undang kepada Bank Indonesia selaku Otoritas Sistem Pembayaran Nasional untuk mencapai sistem pembayaran nasional yang aman, lancar, dan efisien. 10. Kami begitu berbesar hati, sejak digagas lebih dari 20 tahun yang lalu, yaitu dalam Cetak Biru Sistem Pembayaran Nasional Tahun 1995/1996, pada pagi hari ini akan menjadi suatu momen bersejarah karena GPN akan diluncurkan dan dimulai implementasinya. 11. Paling tidak terdapat tiga sasaran utama dari implementasi GPN: 1) Menciptakan ekosistem pembayaran yang saling interkoneksi, interoperabel, dan mampu melaksanakan pemrosesan transaksi yang mencakup otoritasi, kliring, dan setelmen secara domestik. 2) Meningkatkan perlindungan konsumen, antara lain melalui pengamanan data transaksi nasabah dalam setiap transaksi. 3) Meyakinkan ketersediaan dan integritas data transaksi sistem pembayaran nasional, guna mendukung efektivitas transmisi kebijakan moneter, efisiensi intermediasi, serta resiliensi sistem keuangan. 12.Selain itu, GPN juga dihadirkan sebagai backbone untuk memberikan dukungan penuh kepada program-program pemerintah. Termasuk diantaranya penyaluran bantuan sosial non tunai, elektronifikasi jalan tol dan transportasi publik, keuangan inklusif, serta pengembangan sistem perdagangan nasional berbasis elektronik yang telah dimandatkan dalam PERPRES 74 tahun 2017 tentang Roadmap E-Commerce. Bapak/Ibu Hadirin Yang Kami Hormati, 13. Dalam rangka mencapai sasaran tersebut, Bank Indonesia telah menerbitkan ketentuan GPN yang terdiri dari enam pokok kebijakan, yaitu: 1) Membentuk tiga Penyelenggara GPN, yaitu Lembaga Standar, Lembaga Switching, dan Lembaga Services. <95> Lembaga Standar, bertugas menyusun dan mengelola standar teknologi pembayaran nasional yang ditetapkan Bank Indonesia dan wajib dipatuhi oleh seluruh industri, yaitu untuk ATM/Debit adalah NSICCS, dan untuk Uang Elektronik adalah melalui penerapan SAM Multi Applet. Saat ini Lembaga Standar telah dibentuk dan dijalankan oleh Asosiasi Sistem Pembayaran Indonesia (ASPI) sebagai representasi industri. Untuk selanjutnya, Lembaga Standar akan diarahkan berbentuk badan hukum dengan pengelolaan yang bersifat profesional, kompeten dan mandiri. <95> Lembaga Switching, bertugas menyelenggarakan pemrosesan data transaksi pembayaran domestik secara aman dan efisien. Pada momen peluncuran GPN ini, kami ingin menyampaikan bahwa Bank Indonesia telah menetapkan 4 penyelenggara switching domestik sebagai Lembaga Switching GPN, yaitu Jalin Pembayaran Nusantara, Artajasa Pembayaran Elektronik, Rintis Sejahtera, dan Alto Network. <95> Lembaga Services, memiliki empat tugas utama, yaitu (1) menjaga keamanan transaksi dengan memastikan enkripsi data transaksi secara end-to-end, (2) menyelenggarakan rekonsilisasi- kliring-setelmen secara efisien; (3) menangani perselisihan transaksi d.r. perlindungan konsumen; dan (4) mendorong perluasan akseptasi instrumen non tunai. Lembaga Services dibentuk dan dimiliki bersama oleh Lembaga Switching GPN dan anak usaha dari pelaku industri utama yaitu BRI, BNI, Bank Mandiri, dan BCA yang mencakupi 75% pangsa transaksi pembayaran ritel nasional melalui konsorsium. Pendirian konsorsium akan diawali dengan penandatanganan perjanjian pada pagi hari ini, dan diharapkan akan segera berbadan hukum untuk dapat beroperasi penuh di Juli 2018. 2) Penataan infrastruktur, yaitu dengan mewajibkan penerbit, acquirer, agen, dan pay/77e/7fpaten/ayterkoneksi kepada minimal dua Lembaga Switching GPN. Serta diikuti kewajiban interkoneksi diantara Lembaga Switching GPN, sehingga keandalan layanan dapat terjaga. 3) Kewajiban pemrosesan transaksi {routing} domestik, yaitu terhadap instrumen yang diterbitkan di dalam negeri dan ditransaksikan melalui kanal pembayaran dalam negeri, wajib untuk diproses melalui infrastruktur dan sistem yang ada di dalam negeri. 4) Menetapkan skema harga {pricing policy) yang wajar. Untuk tahap awal, dalam PADG GPN telah ditetapkan besaran MDR kartu debit sebesar 1% per transaksi off-us, atau lebih rendah dari yang berlaku selama ini dikisaran 2-3%. Penurunan MDR ini berlaku efektif secara nasional pasca peluncuran GPN pagi hari ini. Penetapan skema harga ini kami yakini akan mampu mendorong efisiensi, kompetisi yang sehat, dan inovasi layanan. 5) Menerapkan logo nasional, guna memperluas akseptasi instrumen pembayaran ritel non tunai yang dapat digunakan di seluruh merchant dalam negeri. Mulai tahun 2018, seluruh penerbit wajib menyediakan kartu berlogo nasional dan menjelaskan manfaatnya kepada nasabah. 6) Menetapkan standarisasi fitur layanan, sehingga mampu menjawab perkembangan kebutuhan transaksi masyarakat. Fitur layanan yang wajib disediakan meliputi pembayaran, transfer, tarik tunai, cek saldo, dan layanan lainnya yang akan ditetapkan lebih lanjut oleh Bank Indonesia. Kedepan, akan dikembangkan juga fitur pembayaran tagihan rutin yang terstandarisasi dan interoperabel, seperti tagihan listrik, air, dan asuransi kesehatan melalui fitur Electronic Billing and Invoicing Presentment and Payment (EBIPP). 14. Dengan serangkaian kebijakan tersebut, dampak positif yang diharapkan: 1) Mendorong sharing infrastructure, sehingga utilisasi terminal ATM/EDC dapat meningkat dan yang berlebih dapat direlokasi ke daerah yang kekurangan. Biaya investasi infrastruktur kemudian dapat dialihkan kembali untuk kegiatan pembiayaan/pinjaman yang pada akhirnya akan memberi dampak positif pada pertumbuhan ekonomi. 2) Mengurangi kompleksitas koneksi dari sebelumnya bilateral antar pihak, menjadi ter-sentralisasi kepada GPN. 3) Masyarakat dapat bertransaksi dari bank manapun, dengan menggunakan instrumen dan kanal pembayaran apapun {any bank, any instrument, any channel). 4) Efisiensi nasional akan tercipta dari skema harga yang lebih kompetitif. Bapak/Ibu Hadirin Yang Kami Hormati, 15. Peluncuran GPN pada pagi hari ini adalah buah dari sinergi yang telah dibangun bersama industri sejak lama. Guna memastikan kesiapan dan kelancaran implementasinya, mulai tahun 2016 Bank Indonesia bersama industri secara intensif telah menyelesaikan uji konsep dan melakukan uji coba {piloting) di 122 merchant besar berskala nasional. Kami bersyukur, hingga saat ini, ke-4 Lembaga Switching GPN telah terkoneksi dengan 60 penerbit dan 14 acquirer, dengan tingkat interopera bi litas transaksi debit mencapai 75%. 16. Dengan mempertimbangkan kesiapan dan kemajuan yang telah dicapai, pada rangkaian acara pagi hari ini akan dilakukan 4 pendandatanganan dokumen yang menandai dimulainya operasionalisasi GPN, yaitu: <95> Perjanjian Konsorsium untuk meresmikan pendirian Lembaga Services <95> Perjanjian Kerjasama interkoneksi ke-4 Lembaga Switching GPN <95> Perjanjian Kerjasama interopera bi litas Kartu Debit <95> Perjanjian Kerjasama interopera bi litas Uang Elektronik 17. Disamping itu, juga akan diluncurkan logo nasional GPN sebagai simbol identitas sistem pembayaran nasional yang akan menjadi bagian dari transaksi seluruh masyarakat yang semakin aman, andal, dan terpercaya. Bapak/Ibu Hadi tin Yang Kami Hormati, 18.Sebelum mengakhiri sambutan kami, kami ingin menyampaikan terimakasih dan penghargaan yang tinggi kepada Kementerian, Otoritas Jasa Keuangan, industri, dan asosiasi atas sinergi dan dukungan dalam menyukseskan pengembangan GPN. Kami berharap, sinergi dan dukungan tersebut dapat semakin kuat terjalin, dalam mengawal implementasi guna mewujudkan sasaran utama GPN yang dicita-citakan. 19. Dalam kesempatan ini, kami juga mengundang Bapak Menteri Koordinator Bidang Perekonomian, Ibu Menteri BUMN, Ibu Menteri Sosial, Ibu Menteri Keuangan, dan Bapak Menteri Komunikasi dan Informatika untuk berkenan memberikan dukungan dan sambutan, yang kami yakini selaras dalam menumbuhkan optimisme kita semua untuk menyongsong Indonesia yang siap menghadapi era digital, melalui sistem pembayaran nasional yang aman, andal, efisien, dan lancar. 20. Akhirnya, seiring dengan manfaat, kemudahan, dan kenyamanan yang akan dirasakan, kami berharap keseluruhan upaya ini akan mampu mendorong peningkatan transaksi non tunai sebagai katalis dan urat nadi bagi pertumbuhan ekonomi Indonesia saat ini dan di masa mendatang. Sekian dan terima kasih. Wassaiammuaiaikum Wr. Wb. Gubernur Bank Indonesia Agus D.W. Martowardojo

Title: Rupiah as a Symbol of National Sovereignty and Obligation to Use Rupiah Within The Republic of Indonesia (Keynote Speech by Ronald Waas Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia in National Seminar on Rupiah Use in The Domestic Market) Jakarta 18 June 2014
text: KEYNOTE SPEECH OF THE DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF BANK INDONESIA IN NATIONAL SEMINAR ON RUPIAH USE IN THE DOMESTIC MARKET RUPIAH AS A SYMBOL OF NATIONAL SOVEREIGNTY AND OBLIGATION TO USE RUPIAH WITHIN THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA Jakarta, 18 June 2014 The Honourable,  Vice Chair of Commission XI of the House of Representatives, Mr. Dr. Harry Azhar Azis, MA;  Governor of Riau Islands Province, or the representative; Distinguished Resource Persons and Moderators,  Director for State Treasury Management, Ministry of Finance, Mr. Drs. Rudy Widodo, M.A.  Director for Economic and Special Crime, Criminal Investigation Agency of Indonesian National Police, Mr. Police Brigadier General Drs. A. Kamil Razak, S.H., M.H.  Secretary for Director General of Domestic Trade, Mr. Jimmy Bella, SE;  Heads of Departments of Bank Indonesia Head Offices; o Executive Director of Cash Management Dept., Mr. Lambok Anton Siahaan; o Director of Economic and Monetary Research and Policy Dept., Mr. Solikin M. Juhro; o Director of Communication Dept., Mr. Peter Jacobs;  Mr. Farial Anwar;  Head of Provincial Police Commands of Riau Islands or the representing Officer;  Heads of Provincial Attorneys or the representing Officers;  Heads of Appellate Courts or the representing Officers;  Heads of Bank Indonesia Working Units, from the Head Offices and Domestic Representative Offices;  Economic observer as the Moderator, Mr. Ryan Kiryanto;  Heads of Banks in Riau Islands Province;  Heads of Associations, Industrial Estate Administrators, International Seaports, Businesses, and other Economic Actors;  Academicians, Press  Ladies and Gentlemen and Distinguished Guests, Good morning and greetings to all of us.  To begin this meeting, allow me to invite all of you to praise God the Almighty for the blessings bestowed upon us so that we have the opportunity to meet in healthy and good condition in Batam, Riau Islands Province. In this beautiful morning, we attend a National Seminar themed Implementation of Law No. 7 of 2011: Rupiah as a Symbol of National Sovereignty and the Obligation to Use Rupiah within the Republic of Indonesia.  We welcome this National Seminar as a positive collaboration between policy holders including the authorities, regulatory bodies, law enforcement officers, and economic activity actors covering banks and non-bank institutions, businesses, and individuals. Your attendance here at the same time shows a real commitment to and awareness on the importance of Rupiah sovereignty as the currency of the Republic of Indonesia.  As one of the National Strategic Activity Centre (PKSN), Batam is selected for a reason to organize this National Seminar. The function of Batam as a city to cater activities at the international, national or provincial scale is very strategic, and therefore, nonRupiah currency is frequently needed for various transactions in the economic activities.  This National Seminar is expected to create shared public perception on the obligation to use Rupiah in making transactions in the domestic market. The same seminar to be organized in Denpasar and North Kalimantan is expected to serve as the initial momentum to raise the awareness of the public, businesses/private sector and government institutions in promoting the use of Rupiah. Ladies and gentlemen, and distinguished guests,  Despite its establishment in the law, we all realize that the use of non-Rupiah currency is frequently observed in many transactions within the Republic of Indonesia. Not only does the private sector make such transactions, but also government institutions. Price tags of goods and services in non-Rupiah currency become a common practice, thus it does not support the use of Rupiah within the Republic of Indonesia despite the possible settlement in Rupiah.  This is certainly of a serious concern. I think there are three dimensions to be observed related thereto. First, Legal Dimension. As previously mentioned, Law No. 7 of 2011 on Currency obliges the use of Rupiah in every transaction made within the Republic of Indonesia. In addition to Currency Law, several other regulations also strengthen the legal grounds and provisions of sanctions, among others are Law No. 24 of Foreign Exchange Traffic, Bank Indonesia Regulation of 2002 on Requirements and Procedure to Bring Rupiah Outside and Within Customs Areas of the Republic of Indonesia, and Trade Minister Regulation of 2013 on Price Tags of Traded Goods and Services.  One important thing in this National Seminar is the need to support understanding of the obligation to use Rupiah for transactions within the Republic of Indonesia. In line with Article 2 of the Currency Law, Rupiah means paper notes and coins, or the so-called Common Money. Meanwhile, Article 21 of the Currency Law implies that there are exemptions for non-cash transactions. It means that the Currency Law has comprehensively applicable to cash and non-cash payments.  The second is Nationality Dimension. Rupiah is a symbol of sovereignty of the Republic of Indonesia. Therefore, currency use in every transaction within the Republic of Indonesia is absolute to anyone therein. It is only in this condition that Rupiah can play host in the country.  The trust of Indonesian people in Rupiah will affect that of the international community in Rupiah and national economy in general, so that Rupiah holds dignity within and outside the country.  Third, Economic/Business Dimension. We witness that almost all global and domestic economic crisis are marked by a sharp weakening exchange rate. High foreign currency demand in economic transactions result in a fragile economy as the countrys economy is highly affected by turbulent global economic development.  Domestic foreign exchange transaction has been one of the factors increasing domestic foreign exchange demand. Such higher demand than supply will result in depreciation pressure against Rupiah, which potentially increases inflation. In addition to decreasing competition, such inflation pressure will also affect interest rate, posing a serious threat to economic growth at a wider scale. Ladies and gentlemen, and distinguished guests,  As the main component of economic transactions in the economic system, a countrys currency value relates to global and domestic economic dynamics.  We feel the turbulence of uncertain global economy within the last half decade, creating a new uncertain pendulum. Amidst weak domestic economic structure, any drastic change thereto adds a quite significant pressure against the domestic economy. Such weak competition and supporting value of the domestic economy is reflected from adjustment to the sharply weakening Rupiah exchange rate in 2013, i.e. up to 20.8%.  2013 is not an easy year for us. National economic activities slow down with lower growth than expected. However, amidst the worlds economic turbulence and sharp Rupiah depreciation, we must be grateful that in 2013, our economy survived at a quite high level with growth of 5.78%, far above the average growth of peer countries of 3.6%. Ladies and gentlemen, and distinguished guests,  While in 2013, macroeconomic policy is directed to stabilization efforts to support sound and balanced economic growth, in 2014 we are entering a different policy, namely structural policy and reform for sustainable economic growth. The basis for this is global economic uncertainty and domestic economic slowdown.  Unlike the previous prediction, the trend in economic recovery and growth rate between regions and countries moves in different acceleration. The economy of European countries is finally free from recession, while that of the United States indicates recovery momentum strength.  Meanwhile, the economy of emerging markets, particularly China, in entering the slowdown phase as a result of macroeconomic policy re-balancing. IMF predicts Chinese economic growth slowdown will continue to 7.5% from 7.7%. Furthermore, some emerging markets undergo an increasing indication of fragility, including risks of unsustainable current transaction and continuously increasing accumulated private external debts.  Such current conditions highly influence the financial market within ASEAN region with constantly increasing pressure. On the domestic side, economic growth at the Q1 of 2014 is lower than expected, i.e. 5.21% or lower than at the Q4 of 2013 of 5.72%. In line with the above, Rupiah depreciation pressure, which reduced at the beginning of 2014, increases, primarily affected by financial asset reposition of emerging markets related to possible monetary stimulus adjustment by the Fed as well as sentiments against fiscal and current transaction deficit within the country.  We are confident that on one hand there is a growing concern and anxiety on economic growth slowdown. However, Bank Indonesia, from a positive perspective, observes that the slowdown is like a detox process to cure economy in the long run.  Bank Indonesias Stability over Growth macroeconomic policy to maintain sustainable economic growth quality and the Governments audacity to apply concentrate ore export ban are proof of endorsement to domestic productivity and earnestness towards economic independence. I see that such policy mix of BI and the Government is a bitter pill to cure the economy in the long run, build economic resilience, and direct us towards value-added oriented growth.  We evaluate that economic adjustment process runs well despite some risks requiring more attention and alert. Therefore, an anticipatory policy must be focused to ensure achievement of inflation target and controlled performance of current transactions. Through such considerations, Bank Indonesia decides to maintain BI Rate at 7.5% at a lending facility rate and deposit facility rate of 7.5% and 5.75%, respectively. Ladies and gentlemen, and distinguished guests,  We realize that the challenges must be overcome as they slowly take their impacts on us. I think it is at this point that our capability of reading and anticipating future economic movements will be more proven. Quick answers to the challenges will affect our capability of maintaining growth.  Such challenges must be observed in line with the approaching commitment to ASEAN Economic Community (AEC) in 2015. On one hand, commitment to AEC will open market opportunities for goods, services, investment, manpower and capital. However, on the other hand, the consequence is stricter competition in the domestic market of each country.  With a massive market potential, I see that the most fundamental substance of AEC commitment is our ability to create competitiveness. Can we use AEC as the main actor of global production chain, or will we only become the market target and marginalized? Survivors are not always the strongest; they are the smartest.  Use of Rupiah in transactions within the Republic of Indonesia will not only increase the dignity of and trust in the currency of the Republic of Indonesia, but also boost more sound and balanced economic supporting capacity. Ladies and gentlemen, and distinguished guests,  The role as a circulation bank is a classic function of central banks throughout the world inherent and part of the long history of Bank Indonesia since 1828 (formerly, De Javasche Bank). In line with economic development, the function of Bank Indonesia expands and deepens to non-cash payment system, monetary system, financial system.  Like blood circulation in human body, the role of Bank Indonesia to maintain smooth payment system is very vital to prevent any clogging with economic veins. Accordingly, adequate cash availability in appropriate notes is a vital element to bridge Bank Indonesias duties in payment system and monetary sector in order to support national economy.  On payment system, cash management in Bank Indonesia is consistently directed to create quality and reliable rupiah availability, secure and optimum cash distribution and processing, and prime Cash Service.  On cash Payment System, BI also faces heavy challenges, not only in providing cash in good condition, but also in increasing cash service outreach throughout Indonesia, particularly to remote and forefront areas of the Republic of Indonesia. Therefore, Bank Indonesia consistently intensifies cooperation with some institutions, such as the Indonesian Navy, the National Police, and other parties.  Although cash management in Bank Indonesia requires very high cost related to production and distribution, Bank Indonesia understands that the duty mandated by the Law is a vital component for the life of this nation and wide community. For that reason, Bank Indonesia is committed to continuously make improvements in optimum cash processing. Ladies and gentlemen, and distinguished guests,  I welcome all initiatives and efforts to increase the use of Rupiah within the Republic of Indonesia, primarily to boost more stable and balanced economic activities.  Improved communication and coordination between BI and the Government, as well as close coordination and cooperation with all stakeholders, will determine the effectiveness of Rupiah use in domestic economic transactions to allow contribution to support national economic development.  It is expected that our good intention to build our nation and country through awareness on using Rupiah as the currency of the Republic of Indonesia, which can support national economic stability, will always be blessed by God. Thank you. Thank you. Jakarta, June 2014 Ronald Waas
