Title: Regional Inflation Control Report, by Agus D.W. Martowardojo, Governor of Bank Indonesia at National Coordination Meeting VI of TPID, Jakarta 27 May 2015
text: Governor of Bank Indonesia Regional Inflation Control Report National Coordination Meeting VI of TPID, Jakarta 27 May 2015 The honorable: His Excellency President of the Republic of Indonesia Ministers of the Working Cabinet Governors of Provinces Mayors/Heads of Districts Distinguished invitees and ladies and gentlemen Slide 1-2 Assalamualaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh, Good morning and may God bless us all, A. Opening 1. Praise God the Almighty for all blessings so that we are given the opportunity to gather in the Sixth National Coordination Meeting of Regional Inflation Control Team (TPID) in 2015. 2. It is an honor for all of us that His Excellency President of the Republic of Indonesia may attend this event together with us, not only to open but also to chair this National Coordination Meeting. Out of the five previously held TPID National Coordination Meetings, it is only in this sixth meeting that the President of the Republic of Indonesia is humbly willing to chair it directly. Therefore, we express our deepest appreciation to the President. 1 3. We would also like to express our appreciation to all Heads of Regions and invitees who have provided their time to attend this highest coordination forum on inflation control, a forum aiming to strengthen the synergy between the Central and Regional Governments to formulate solutions to various issues and challenges of price stabilization in regions. B. Development of Inflation and TPID Slide 3 His Excellency and distinguished ladies and gentlemen, Slide 4  5 4. We have passed 2014 with a relatively controlled inflation at a single digit of 8.36%. We consider this achievement as a success because amidst various challenges, one of which is increasing inflation pressure post-energy subsidy reform policy adopted at the end of 2014, we were able to maintain inflation rate at a rate slightly lower than 2013, which reached 8.38%. Decreasing inflation rate even continued in the first quarter of 2015 to 6.39%. Although inflation rate in April 2015 slightly increased to 6.79% (yoy), such increase resulted more from the continued impact of oil fuel price increase at the end of March 2015. 5. In an effort to promote coordination between Bank Indonesia and the Government, both on the central and regional levels, we are optimistic to successfully mitigate different risks, so that we can reach inflation target of 4%1% from 2015 to 2017 and 3.5%1% in 2018. Slide 6 6. On the central level, we highly appreciate the energy subsidy reform policy adopted by the Government. This policy will be effective to reduce inflation surge frequently occurring every time the government adjusts oil fuel price amidst fiscal pressure. 2 In addition, this policy provides an extra large fiscal room to be used to build various infrastructures to allow increasing competitiveness and reducing inflation pressure. We also highly appreciate the Governments policy response to minimize continued and social impacts of subsidized oil fuel price increase through tariff control of land transportation, management of major basic commodities distribution, and assistance for poor people. Slide 7 7. On the regional level, different policy innovations play a big role in inflation control. TPID National Working Group highlights that many policies and activities of TPID in various regions are aimed at an effort to preserve and implement the following program (called 4K in Indonesian): (i) Availability of goods and services; (ii) Price affordability; (iii) Smooth distribution; and (iv) Effective communication to manage public perception of prices. As well known, such program is one of mutual commitments produced in the Fifth National Coordination Meeting of TPID in 2014. Slide 8 8. We can report that the achievements strongly relate to the commitment, hard work, and support of 432 TPID established as of today. The increasing existence of TPID is expected to help solve different regional issues frequently hindering price stability. Slide 9 C. Future Challenges and Necessary Efforts His Excellency and distinguished ladies and gentlemen, Slide 10 9. Going forward, challenges to achieve inflation target determined by the Government at 41% from 2015 to 2017 and 3.5%1% in 2018 will remain huge. 3 Slide 11 10. There are many structural obstacles in the real sector, which frequently result in price instability. First, domestic production capacity is limited, primarily strategic food commodities, due to low productivity and decreasing land area. Second, rupiah exchange rate is susceptible to external turbulences owing to our high dependence on natural resources based exports and raw material imports. Third, food production is susceptible to supply disruption due to the increasingly difficult climate change anticipation. Fourth, national energy dependence on oil fuel and LPG imports remain high. Fifth, inefficient markets as reflected on long distribution chain dominated by a few big actors. Sixth, connectivity between regions is still weak. 11. Besides different structural challenges, inflation is highly affected by unique regional characteristics, which oftentimes require a separate management. However, the characteristics of a region may also relate to another region making a synergy necessary between regions, on the regional and central levels, and on the central level in their management. In connection therewith, an intensive and participatory coordination is necessary in various sectors, between ministries, involving the central and regional governments, including through TPI and TPID forums. Slide 12 12. In this connection, the Coordinating Ministry of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Home Affairs, and Bank Indonesia, under the TPID National Working Group, have a central role in strengthening policy coordination through implementation of various programs; among others are (i) development of the Centre of National Strategic Food Price 4 Information and (ii) efforts to expand market access to farmers by strengthening cooperation between regions. We expect the programs above may continue and expand to all regions. Slide 13 His Excellency and distinguished ladies and gentlemen, 13. We warmly welcome all of the Governments agenda in the future economic development, primarily to realize food sovereignty, through acceleration of supporting infrastructure development in agriculture. Efforts to reach food sovereignty closely relate to inflation control. In line therewith, the Fourth TPID National Coordination Meeting in 2015 took the theme Optimization of Regional Governments Roles in Supporting Price Stability through Infrastructure Development Acceleration and Business Administration in Regions. 14. In the context of regional role optimization, the TPID National Working Group highly appreciates TPID initiatives in almost all regions which have developed regional inflation control road maps. The road maps have a strategic role in ensuring sustainable improvement of various structural issues described above and may be used as a reference in building a synergy between the central and regional policies. Slide 14 15. Following the theme, we highly expect in todays forum to be able to formulate synergic and concrete steps and strengthen the national commitment to realize food sovereignty through infrastructure development acceleration and food business administration improvement in regions. D. Announcement of TPID Award Winners and Closing His Excellency and distinguished ladies and gentlemen, 5 Slide 15-16 16. In this forum, TPID National Working Group will give The Best TPID awards to regions having TPID with the best work performance in supporting price stability achievement. Similar to the previous four National Coordination Meetings, the evaluation criteria for The Best TPID awards are based on two aspects, namely process aspect measuring intensity and quality of TPID activities and output aspect measuring the level and volatility of inflation in the relevant region in 2014. 17. In line with the increasing number of TPID in districts/municipals, which are not the basis for national inflation calculation, as commenced in the last years National Coordination Meeting, in this year we will also give awards to the best TPID in the relevant districts/municipals. Such award is called Achiever TPID whose evaluation criteria are based only on the process aspect because the relevant districts/municipals do not have any inflation rate. 18. The evaluation and determination of The Best TPID and Achiever TPID are conducted by an Evaluation Team consisting of members of TPID National Working Group and experts coming from academicians. Winners are classified in three Regions, namely Sumatra, Java, and the Eastern Part of Indonesia, and winners on the province and district/municipal level are differed. 19. Winners will be announced through a short movie to be displayed after we complete this report. After such winner announcement, we would like to invite His Excellency to present the awards to the Best TPID and Achiever TPID in 2014, and at the same time open and chair the Sixth TPID National Working Meeting in 2015. 20. We conclude our report. We appreciate the attention of His Excellency and all attendees. 6 Wabillahi taufik wal hidayah. Wassalamu alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuh. 7

Title: Closing Remarks - OIC Expert Group Workshop, Dr Halim Alamsyah - Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia, Surabaya, 5 November 2014
text: 13 BANK INDONESIA CENTRAL BANK OF REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA Closing Remarks - OIC Expert Group Workshop Dr Halim Alamsyah - Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia Surabaya, 5 November 2014 Bismillahirahmaannirrahiim, Praise be to Allah SWT, May the peace and blessings of Allah be on the Last Prophet and Messenger, Muhammad SAW and on his household and companions a6 H.E. Dr. Abdul Aziz Alhinai, Vice President of Islamic Development Bank a6 H.E. Prof. Savas Alpay, Director General of SESRIC a6 H.E. Governors of Central Banks of the OIC member countries a6 Distinguished Representative of COMCEC a6 Distinguished Delegates from Prominent Institutions a6 Ladies and gentlemen Assalamu'alaikum Warahmahtullah Wabarakatuh, 1. Let me invite you to praise Allah SWT that with His mercy and guidance, we can conclude this international workshop very successfully. During this day, we have seen fruitful discussion and deliberation taking place on various issues regarding macro-prudential policy, potential financial deepening and broadening in Islamic financial industry. With prominent speakers, panelists and chairs with us, the discussion was enriched by multi-dimensional arguments like economics, fiqh, and the elements of regulation and supervision. I would like to thank all of you for your priceless participation. 2. The conference has raised the importance of the inclusion of Islamic finance in the national policy development, particularly when the industry is showing greater significance in the national economy. The adoption of international standards and the exercise on financial assessment are also important in pursuing higher confidence from the public. In addition to the commercial sector development, Islamic finance could provide significant contribution to the financial inclusion. 3. Concluding the program today, let me reiterate some important aspects that we can draw as follows: 4. Firstly, it is undeniable that the development of Islamic financial sector has to be incorporated into the national agenda of jurisdiction which operate Islamic finance. Multidimensional supports are needed so that the industry could secure its long-term growth without necessarily create substantial excess of risk or unintended consequences. The thoughts of Islamic finance should be present in all aspects of policy development including 113 BANK INDONESIA CENTRAL BANK OF REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA macro-prudential, fiscal and monetary policies along with industrial policies. The inclusion of Islamic financial industry in the Financial Sector Assessment Program, for example, would drive the commitment of the government to pay more attention and efforts in developing the industry in a more systematic way. Taking into consideration that the coverage of international standards of Islamic finance are currently not as comprehensive as the mainstream, then regulatory observance to some existing references is inevitable as long as the frameworks are not in conflict with the sharia principles. 5. Secondly, in the frontier of financial stability, the Islamic financial industry has to develop its own macro-prudential policy. Despite its sound business models, Islamic finance shares the same concerns towards the systemic robustness to withstand any uncertainty either coming from internal or external factors. In order to address this issue, the Islamic financial system should be equipped with instruments, infrastructure and policies at the same level as the conventional system has already had, even though we recognize some technical differences. Those include liquidity instruments, indicators for risk measurements, and policies to control the dynamics of the industry within the acceptable prudential corridor. 6. Thirdly, as I mentioned earlier, we should encourage international collaboration more intensely in terms of working group to come up with more comprehensive international standards. Those standards have to gain acknowledgment from the existing international standard setters in order to give substantial value added to the member countries which adopt those principles. The development of these standards is carried out by the Islamic standard setters such as IFSB, AAOIFI, and 1IFM with the support of the member countries and multi-lateral institutions. 7. Lastly, the development of Islamic financial industry need also touch the Islamic social finance that is currently less developed compared to the commercial sectors. The social finance covers the zakat and awqaf that would equip the government with additional formidable vehicle for poverty alleviation program and enhanced financial access. Besides, collaboration with other Islamic commercial sector may also provide significant leverage to the financial system to outreach low-income society and to provide them with low-cost financial services. The establishment of sound zakat and awqaf system, in fact, requires persistent efforts in terms of more systematic development program and international collaboration. The effort should be in-line with other international programs conducted by leading multilateral institutions such as the World Bank, Islamic Development Bank, Asian Development Bank and many others. At the national level, the development of zakat and awqaf as social finance should also be a part of national economic program that is smoothly integrated into more tangible and effective programs. Excellencies, distinguished ladies and gentlemen 8. 1 believe that all the conception contemplated during this workshop will highly contribute to the development of Islamic financial industry. May Allah SWT bless us with His knowledge and wisdom so that together we can lead the Islamic financial industry to advancement in order to accomplish our objectives of prosperity to our people and nation. 9. Finally, on behalf of all chairs, speakers, panelists and participants, I would like to thank all the parties who have prepared and supported this program for the excellence jobs which provide us a very comfortable air to discuss all day long. I would like to also apologize to all participants should there be any inconvenient occurred during the program. Once again thank you very much for your involvement and I'll welcome all of you to our dinner this evening. Wa billahi tawfiq Wai Hidayah. Wasalamu'alaikum Warahmatullahi wabarakatuh Surabaya, 5 November 2014 DR. Halim Alamsyah Deputy Governor

Title: Agus D.W. Martowardojo Speech MoU Between Bank Indonesia and IDB, Surabaya, November 3rd, 2014
text: C& BANK INDONESIA BANK SENTRAL REPUBLIK INDONESIA GOVERNOR SPEECH MOU BETWEEN BANK INDONESIA AND IDB AGUS D.W. MARTOWARDOJO SURABAYA, NOVEMBER 3rd, 2014 His Excellency: President of Islamic Development Bank, Dr. Ahmad Mohammad Ali Al Madani, His Excellency: Dr Muliaman D Hadad, Chairman of Indonesian Financial Services Authority (OJK); His Excellency: Governor of the Province of East Java, Mr. Soekarwo, Head of Badan Amil Zakat Nasional, Mr. KH Didin Hafidhuddin, Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia, Mr. Halim Alamsyah, Distinguished Guests, Ladies and gentlemen, Assalamu'alaykum Warrahmatullah Wabarakatuh, 1. In this blessing morning, I feel fortunate to witness that Bank Indonesia and the Islamic Development Bank could embark in a new episode of cooperation in the areas of Islamic economic and finance development and capacity building. Indonesia with the largest Muslim population has a potential to develop Islamic finance and economy. At the academic side, we have more than a hundred universities running Islamic economic program and we have also more than 27 thousand Islamic traditional schools with millions of students. i C& BANK INDONESIA BANK SENTRAL REPUBLIK INDONESIA 2. The Indonesian Islamic finance has also shown significant development in the last 15 years that takes shapes in terms of business volume, financial products and financial subsectors. We hope that strengthening the development of Islamic finance could bring prosperity to all segments including low-income society with inclusive financial services so that we could see that the development of Islamic economy and finance is coherent with equitable development and broader economic production base. 3. From the central bank point of view, the development of Islamic economy and finance offers new challenges and hopes. With the salient features that are pro real sector development, I believe that Islamic finance could provide stronger foundation to sustained economic development that is based on real production. But at the same time, the financial authorities should be able to accommodate some peculiarities in the financial transactions and contracts that might be different from the existing regulatory setting. We have to make sure that the elements of Islamic economics and finance always appears in all financial regulatory aspects. 4. The Islamic Development Bank has marked its long standing to promote Islamic finance since it was established almost 40 years ago. Besides, we also recognize the growing contribution of IDB in Indonesia in the areas of Islamic banking, higher education and health services. 5. The signing of the Memorandum of Understanding today is aiming at enhancing the collaboration and cooperation between BI and IDB particularly in the area of zakat system activities and capacity 2 C& BANK INDONESIA BANK SENTRAL REPUBLIK INDONESIA building program. As we may have acknowledged, BI and IDB has had an MOU before as a basis to undertake the international seminar on Inclusive Islamic Financial Sector and the first meeting of international working group on Core Principles of Zakat System in last August 2014. The first area to be covered in today's MOU is a continuation of the last MOU to support the continuation of the international working group activities in drafting the Core Principles toward an establishment of an efficient and Sound Zakat System. We believe that setting the international standard for good governance in the zakat system will enhance the public confidence on the zakat authorities to allocate and distribute the zakat optimally, including for micro financing. Meanwhile, on the second area of MOU, namely capacity building, we would lend support for the IDB experts to help us enhancing the quality of our people so that our efforts in developing Islamic economy and finance would become effective. Excellency, Ladies and Gentlemen, 6. With a new vision of IDB to support its member countries in delivering better quality of life, I believe that a closer cooperation between Indonesia and the IDB could bring many differences. 7. The signing of the Memorandum of Understanding could open up to more technical cooperation between the IDB and Bank Indonesia in particular and also other relevant institutions that stake to the Islamic economic and finance development. In this occasion, I would like to express my great appreciation to the President of IDB that has come a long way from Jeddah to Indonesia to be a part of our 3 C& BANK INDONESIA BANK SENTRAL REPUBLIK INDONESIA development process. I also wish that Allah Subhana Wa Ta'ala will always bless your effort through the IDB actions in promoting better quality of life of Muslim in the world. Thank you very much and Wassalamualaykum Warahmatullah Wabarakatuh. 4

Title: Sambutan Utama Deputi Gubernur Bank Indonesia, Ronald Waas, Membangun Kemitraan untuk Pelaksanaan dan Pengembangan Kebijakan Inklusif Menuju Sistem Pembayaran yang Aman, Efisien, dan Andal di acara 14th JCB World Conference, Bali, 19 Oktober 22, 2015
text: Keynote Speech by the Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia ," Building Partnerships for the Implementation and Development of Inclusive Policies Towards a Safe, Efficient and Reliable Payment System" 14th JCB World Conference Bali, 19 October 22nd, 2015 To the Honorable: 4-Bapak Ichiro Hamakawa; President & Chief Executive Officer, JCB Co., Ltd, -Bapak Yasuhiro Maeda; Board Member Senior Executive Officer, JCB Co., Ltd, 4- Bapak Koremitsu Sannomiya; President & Chief Operating Officer JCB International Co., Ltd, 4- Bapak Yuichiro Kadowaki, President Director of JCB International Indonesia, 4-Payment System Industrial Society, 4- Attendees I respect. Good morning and peace be upon you, Om Swastiastu. 95 To begin this welcome, let us offer thanksgiving to God Almighty th Esa for the grace of health and beautiful Bali weather at the 14l JCB World Conference. All representatives of JCB and other payment system communities are our important partners in realizing a safe, efficient and reliable payment system in Indonesia. 95 It is time for all of us to increase the exchange of information and cooperation in all matters related to the payment system. Collaborative and intensive communication as we do today is necessary because a vulnerable and bumpy road seems to be constantly facing us. 95 I welcome the theme of this year's conference which captures the spirit of the moment, "Connecting with Partners to Create New Values". In this spirit, I would like to share my views on the payment system, the role and steps of transformation for the implementation and development of more inclusive policies towards a secure, efficient and reliable payment system. Ladies and gentlemen I respect, 95 After the 1997 crisis, many people worried that Indonesia would feel the adverse effects and it would take a long time to start stimulation in order to return to normalcy. But, we're rising much more rapidly than many people think. We begin to grow rapidly by improving the previous economy contracted 13.5% and became one of the largest and fastest growing economies. 95 We also witnessed the financial crisis of 2008 that has left tremendous global anxiety around the world. It is no coincidence that our economy held up well in the face of the turmoil of 2008. Our resilience is inseparable from the strong support of stable macroeconomic conditions and a sound financial system, but it is more important that we are better prepared for shocks this was after the 1997 crisis. 95 Learning from the crisis, we observed at least 3 (three) important management challenges. First, the ability to be firm in the execution and execution of policies. Second, transparency in policymaking with adequate public consultation. Third, coordination is established between the Central Government, Local Governments, relevant authorities, and Stakeholders. 95 These attitudes will prevent us from signaling conflicting policymaking and involve the entire community so that we can make the best contribution in formulating appropriate and credible policies. This is what we call inclusivity of implementation and policy development. Ladies and gentlemen I respect, 95 The infrastructure of the payment system is the invisible piping system of the economy of each country. "The infrastructure of the payment system is a set of channels that are important, evaporate, and penetrate until a malfunction occurs" (Kahn and Roberds, 2008). Thanks to the advancement of information technology and the spread of social networks as its logical impact, we are now entering the era of an interesting world of payments. 95 Rapidly changing information technologies and ever-growing business and investment activities have added to the need for reliable and real-time payment settlement support. Recent developments in media, instruments, and payment mechanisms are utilizing advanced technology to provide more practical and efficient payment services. 95 With the addition of innovative payment solutions, Bank Indonesia has and will always involve the payment industry community to ensure optimal valueof payment services for customers. Ladies and gentlemen I respect. To improve payment system effectiveness, Bank Indonesia has implemented a number of policies in four main areas: (1) Investing in human resources, (2) Building infrastructure, (3) Establish supervision and regulation of thefinancing system, and (4) Encourage institutional synergy. First, invest in human resources. Investing in human capital has always been an important part of the transformation journey to success. The success of a system will be preceded by individual consciousness. An intensive focus on capacity building will support the depth of knowledge and skills required in the industry. Second, strengthen infrastructure that adds to intraconnection or interoperability in the payment system to improve industry efficiency. The quality of the payment system infrastructure determines the stability of the economy, the efficiency and reliability of intermediation, as well as the possibility for the private sector to innovate and provide new services for customers. Currently, Bank Indonesia is improving infrastructure for the Second Generation of Bank Indonesia Real Time Gross Settlement (BI-RTGS) and Bank Indonesia Scriptless Securities Settlement System (BI-SSSS). This development aims to guarantee the effect of high operational vitas in the payment and settlement system, which will add to the ability to overcome complexities in the financial system . Third, Bank Indonesia will strengthen the supervisory function and legal aspects of transactions to ensure customer protection in using the payment system. It is also needed to develop an early warning system to support financial stability. Learning from the great crises we experienced in the past decade, it is important to have a precautionary guide to crisis management protocols. Last but not least, initiating Institutional Synergy. Facing the challenges ahead, the payment system community must be able to play an active role to encourage intensive communication and coordination. The key success factors for developing a secure, efficient and reliable payment system will be determined by our ability to build collective leadership in handling change. In this case. Bank Indonesia has initiated the establishment of the Indonesian Payment System Forum (FSPI), which is a coordination forum between the government and business, as well as the payment system community to provide input for the sake of supporting the development of Indonesia's Payment System. FSPI is expected to strengthen the harmonization of policies, regulations, and the implementation of cooperation programs in the field of payment systems. Ladies and gentlemen I respect, 95 Bank Indonesia, both as an authority and facilitator of the payment industry, will always strive to realize an efficient and safe payment system by developing policies and regulations, increase competition, and encourage cooperation between players in the industry. 95 We will ensure that the development of payment system policies is built on the principleof fair competition, open access for the public, and based on national interests. 95 In closing, I'm happy we're here today. I just hope that the collaboration and favorable views in building partnerships for the implementation and development of inclusive policies of the Payment System will be a common wisdom in building a better place for all of us. 95 May God Almighty be meridhoi and illuminate our steps towards a better future. Thanks. DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF BANK INDONESIA Ronald Waas
text_original: Sambutan Utama Deputi Gubernur Bank Indonesia "Membangun Kemitraan untuk Pelaksanaan dan Pengembangan Kebijakan Inklusif Menuju Sistem Pembayaran yang Aman, Efisien, dan Andal" 14th JCB World Conference Bali, 19 Oktober 22, 2015 Kepada yang terhormat: 4-Bapak Ichiro Hamakawa; President & Chief Executive Officer, JCB Co., Ltd, ^-Bapak Yasuhiro Maeda; Board Member Senior Executive Officer, JCB Co., Ltd, 4- Bapak Koremitsu Sannomiya; President & Chief Operating Officer JCB International Co., Ltd, 4- Bapak Yuichiro Kadowaki, President Director of JCB International Indonesia, 4-Masyarakat Industri Sistem Pembayaran, 4- Hadirin yang saya hormati. Selamat pagi dan salam sejahtera, Om Swastiastu. <95> Untuk memulai sambutan ini, mari kita panjatkan puji syukur kepada Tuhan Yang Maha th Esa atas rahmat kesehatan dan cuaca Bali yang indah di 14l JCB World Conference. Semua perwakilan JCB dan masyarakat sistem pembayaran lain adalah mitra penting kami dalam mewujudkan sistem pembayaran yang aman, efisien, dan andal di Indonesia. <95> Inilah saatnya bagi kita semua untuk meningkatkan pertukaran informasi dan kerja sama dalam semua hal yang terkait dengan sistem pembayaran. Komunikasi kolaboratif dan intensif seperti yang kita lakukan hari ini diperlukan karena jalan yang rentan dan bergelombang tampaknya terus menerus menghadang di depan kita. <95> Saya menyambut baik tema konferensi tahun ini yang menangkap semangat momen tersebut, "Menjalin Hubungan dengan Mitra untuk Menciptakan Nilai-Nilai Baru". Dalam semangat inilah, saya ingin berbagi pandangan tentang sistem pembayaran, peran dan langkah transformasi untuk pelaksanaan dan pengembangan kebijakan yang lebih inklusif menuju sistem pembayaran yang aman, efisien, dan andal. Hadirin yang saya hormati, <95> Setelah krisis 1997, banyak orang khawatir bahwa Indonesia akan merasakan dampak buruk dan membutuhkan waktu lama untuk memulai stimulasi agar kembali ke keadaan normal. Tetapi, kita bangkit jauh lebih pesat daripada perkiraan banyak orang. Kita mulai tumbuh dengan cepat dengan memperbaiki ekonomi yang sebelumnya terkontraksi 13.5% dan menjadi salah satu ekonomi yang tumbuh paling besar dan paling cepat. <95> Kita juga menyaksikan krisis keuangan 2008 yang telah menyisakan kecemasan global yang luar biasa di seluruh dunia. Bukan kebetulan bahwa ekonomi kita bertahan dengan baik menghadapi gejolak 2008. Ketahanan kita tidak terpisahkan dari dukungan kuat kondisi makroekonomi yang stabil dan sistem keuangan yang baik, tetapi lebih penting lagi bahwa kita lebih siap menghadapi goncangan ini setelah krisis 1997. <95> Belajar dari krisis tersebut, kami mengamati setidaknya 3 (tiga) tantangan manajemen penting. Pertama, kemampuan tegas dalam eksekusi dan pelaksanaan kebijakan. Kedua, transparansi dalam pembuatan kebijakan dengan konsultasi publik yang memadai. Ketiga, koordinasi yang terbangun antara Pemerintah Pusat, Pemerintah Daerah, Otoritas terkait, serta Para Pemangku Kepentingan. <95> Sikap-sikap tersebut akan menghindarkan kita dari sinyal pembuatan kebijakan yang bertentangan dan melibatkan seluruh masyarakat sehingga dapat memberikan kontribusi terbaik dalam merumuskan kebijakan yang tepat dan kredibel. Inilah yang kami sebut inklusivitas pelaksanaan dan pengembangan kebijakan. Hadirin yang saya hormati, <95> Infrastruktur sistem pembayaran adalah sistem perpipaan tak kasatmata ekonomi setiap negara. "Infrastruktur sistem pembayaran adalah sekumpulan saluran yang penting, meresap, dan menembus sampai terjadi malfungsi" (Kahn and Roberds, 2008). Berkat kemajuan teknologi informasi dan penyebaran jaringan sosial sebagai dampak logisnya, kita sekarang memasuki era dunia pembayaran yang menarik. <95> Teknologi informasi yang berubah cepat serta kegiatan bisnis dan investasi yang terus tumbuh telah menambah kebutuhan akan dukungan penyelesaian pembayaran yang andal dan real-time. Perkembangan terkini dalam media, instrumen, dan mekanisme pembayaran telah memanfaatkan teknologi canggih untuk memberikan layanan pembayaran yang lebih praktis dan efisien. <95> Dengan bertambahnya solusi pembayaran inovatif, Bank Indonesia telah dan akan senantiasa melibatkan masyarakat industri pembayaran untuk memastikan nilai-nilai optimal layanan pembayaran bagi nasabah. Hadirin yang saya hormati. Untuk meningkatkan efektivitas sistem pembayaran, Bank Indonesia telah menerapkan sejumlah kebijakan dalam empat bidang utama: (1) Berinvestasi dalam sumber daya (manusia), (2) Membangun infrastruktur, (3) Menetapkan pengawasan dan peraturan sistem pembayaran, dan (4) Mendorong sinergi kelembagaan. Pertama, berinvestasi dalam sumber daya manusia. Berinvestasi dalam modal manusia (human capital) selalu menjadi bagian penting dari perjalanan transformasi menuju keberhasilan. Keberhasilan suatu sistem akan didahului dengan kesadaran individu. Fokus intensif pada pengembangan kapasitas akan mendukung kedalaman pengetahuan dan keterampilan yang dibutuhkan dalam industri ini. Kedua, memperkuat infrastruktur yang menambah intrakoneksi atau interoperabilitas dalam sistem pembayaran untuk meningkatkan efisiensi industri. Kualitas infrastruktur sistem pembayaran menentukan stabilitas ekonomi, efisiensi dan keandalan intermediasi, serta kemungkinan bagi sektor swasta untuk berinovasi dan memberikan layanan baru bagi nasabah. Saat ini, Bank Indonesia tengah meningkatkan infrastruktur untuk Generasi Kedua Bank Indonesia Real Time Gross Settlement (BI-RTGS) dan Bank Indonesia Scriptless Securities Settlement System (BI-SSSS). Pengembangan ini bertujuan untuk menjamin efektivitas operasional yang tinggi dalam sistem pembayaran dan penyelesaian, yang akan menambah kemampuan untuk mengatasi kompleksitas dalam sistem keuangan. Ketiga, Bank Indonesia akan memperkuat fungsi pengawasan dan aspek hukum transaksi untuk memastikan perlindungan nasabah dalam menggunakan sistem pembayaran. Ini juga dibutuhkan untuk mengembangkan sistem peringatan dini untuk mendukung stabilitas keuangan. Belajar dari krisis besar yang kita alami dalam dekade lalu, penting untuk memiliki panduan kehati-hatian untuk krisis manajemen protokol. Hal terakhir yang tak kalah pentingnya, memprakarsai Sinergi Kelembagaan. Menghadapi tantangan ke depan, masyarakat sistem pembayaran harus dapat memainkan peran aktif untuk mendorong komunikasi dan koordinasi intensif. Faktor keberhasilan utama untuk mengembangkan sistem pembayaran yang aman, efisien, dan andal akan ditentukan oleh kemampuan kita untuk membangun kepemimpinan kolektif dalam menangani perubahan. Dalam hal ini. Bank Indonesia telah memprakarsai pembentukan Forum Sistem Pembayaran Indonesia (FSPI), yang merupakan forum koordinasi antara pemerintah dan bisnis, serta masyarakat sistem pembayaran untuk memberikan masukan demi mendukung pengembangan Sistem Pembayaran Indonesia. FSPI diharapkan dapat memperkuat harmonisasi kebijakan, peraturan, dan pelaksanaan program kerja sama dalam bidang sistem pembayaran. Hadirin yang saya hormati, <95> Bank Indonesia, baik sebagai otoritas dan fasilitator industri pembayaran, akan selalu berupaya untuk mewujudkan sistem pembayaran yang efisien dan aman dengan mengembangkan kebijakan dan peraturan, meningkatkan kompetisi, dan mendorong kerja sama antar pemain dalam industri. <95> Kami akan memastikan bahwa pengembangan kebijakan sistem pembayaran dibangun dengan prinsip persaingan yang adil, keterbukaan akses untuk masyarakat, dan berdasarkan pada kepentingan nasional. <95> Sebagai penutup, saya bahagia kita berada di sini hari ini. Saya hanya berharap bahwa kolaborasi dan pandangan yang menguntungkan dalam membangun kemitraan untuk pelaksanaan dan pengembangan kebijakan inklusif Sistem Pembayaran akan menjadi kearifan bersama dalam membangun tempatyang lebih baik untuk kita semua. <95> Semoga Tuhan Yang Maha Esa meridhoi dan menerangi langkah kita menuju masa depan yang lebih baik. Terima kasih. DEPUTI GUBERNUR BANK INDONESIA Ronald Waas

Title: Keynote Speech, Hendar, Deputy Governor of Bank Indonesia in The Communication Forum of Regional Leaders and High Level Meeting of Regional Inflation Control Team (TPID) of East Priangan Tasikmalaya, 7 December 2015
text: KEYNOTE SPEECH DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF BANK INDONESIA IN THE COMMUNICATION FORUM OF REGIONAL LEADERS AND HIGH LEVEL MEETING OF REGIONAL INFLATION CONTROL TEAM (TPID) OF EAST PRIANGAN Tasikmalaya, 7 December 2015 Distinguished,  Mayor of Tasikmalaya, Drs. H. Budi Budiman;  Head of Tasikmalaya District, H. Uu Ruhanul Ulum, SE;  Mayor of Banjar, Hj. Ade Uu Sukaesih, S.Ip, M.Si.;  Head of Ciamis District, H. Iing Syam Arifin;  Acting Head of Pangandaran District, Drs. H. Daud Achmad;  Prof. Dr. Rina Indiastuti of Padjadjaran University; Heads of Representative Offices of Bank Indonesia  Department Head of Regional II (Java region), Dwi Pranoto;  Head of Bank Indonesia Representative of West Java Province, Rosmaya Hadi;  Head of Bank Indonesia Representative of Tasikmalaya, Wahyu Purnama;  Head of Bank Indonesia Representative of Cirebon, M. Abdul Majid Ikram;  Distinguished ladies and gentlemen. 1 Assalamualaikum Wr. Wb. Good morning and may God bless us all, 1.First of all, allow me to invite all of us to praise God the Almighty for the blessings given to us to come here and attend the Regional Leader Forum and High Level Meeting of Regional Inflation Control Team (TPID) of East Priangan under the title Strengthening of Cooperation between Regions to Boost Economic Development in East Priangan. 2.On this occasion, I warmly welcome and appreciate the implementation of this event, as a part of routine meetings held 2 (two) times in a year in the Communication and Coordination Forum of Regional Leaders (FKKPD). Possible implementation of this forum and your attendance indicate a strong commitment to jointly intensify communication, coordination and cooperation in order to build the economy of 2 East Priangan. This synergy becomes vital and highly relevant to face challenges encountered by the national and regional economy both now and in the future. Ladies and gentlemen, Global Economy Challenges 3.The end of 2015 is the right momentum to reflect on challenges encountered by Indonesia's economy throughout this year as well as some risks to be properly anticipated pertaining to the adoption of economic policies in the following year. On this occasion, allow me to share views on the theme of today's meeting: The Importance of Cooperation between Regions and Inflation Control to Boost Sustainable and 3 Quality Economic Development in Welcoming ASEAN Economic Community (AEC). 4.As an open economy, Indonesia's economic development in 2015 faces at least 3 challenges. First, uneven global economic recovery. On one hand, in advanced countries, the economy of the United States of America is consistently showing improvement, supported by the improving labor sector and stronger consumption demands. The US economic growth is estimated to increase as inflation is maintained at a low level. Meanwhile, the European economy, though gradually improving, has not recovered. The economic performance of Japan remains weak with 4 unstable unemployment level improvement and declining labor wage. In the meantime, in emerging markets, China's economy, which previously managed to grow by two digits, has been significantly slowing down below 7% in the last decade. Rebalancing of China's economy from investment driven to consumption driven is constantly occurring. Uneven economic recovery of advanced countries and weak China's economy result in declining global demands. 5.Second, global monetary policy divergence results in higher pressure on and volatility of exchange rates. Uneven global economic recovery results in divergence of monetary policies of major countries in the world. The European Central Bank (ECB) and Bank of Japan (BOJ) plan to 5 continue monetary easing by extending Quantitative Easing upon considering possible occurrence of deflation. The People's Bank of China (PBoC) is also adopting easing policy, Yuan devaluation and reform program of Chinese Government to boost their export growth. Meanwhile, optimism in US economic recovery increases the expectation of rising Fed Fund Rate, resulting in stronger USD exchange rate against all currencies, followed by their increasing volatility. This rate policy normalization dominates the dynamic global financial market and potentially results in capital reversal from emerging markets to advanced countries, including Indonesia. 6.Third, declining prices of world's commodities. Declining global demands result in 6 sharply decreasing prices of export commodities, primarily natural resources, such as coal, palm oil, rubber, nickel and copper in line with the increasing economic dependence on domestic consumption. It also closely relates to the weaker China's economy as the world's biggest natural resource customer, resulting in declining commodity prices in the global market. Relatively high pressure occurs to developing countries whose export commodities depend on natural resources, including Indonesia, where 56.3% of their total export products are natural resource commodities. Ladies and gentlemen, Domestic Economy Challenges 7.What are the impacts and development of the global economy on Indonesia's economy? On the domestic economy side, on this occasion, I will briefly highlight 3 aspects we should pay attention 7 to, which are relevant to the theme of our forum this morning. First, weak global economy results in declining national economic growth. Indonesia's economy at the third quarter of 2015 grew by 4.73%, higher than the previous quarter of 4.67%. Such growth rested on domestic demand (government's consumption and investment as well as household's consumption), while export is contracting in line with the low commodity prices and weak export demands from major trade partners, such as USA, China and Singapore. Weak global demand results in weak Rupiah exchange rate, which further makes it unable to significantly boost exports. 8.From spatial aspect, we see that economic recovery occurs only in Java. 8 The economy of Sumatera is also recovering, but the growth is relatively limited. On the other hand, the economy of East Regions of Indonesia slowly grows, and Kalimantan even records negative growth for the first time in the last 10 years. Insufficiently solid national economic recovery may also be observed from the increasing open unemployment level from 5.9% in August 2014 to 6.2% in August 2015. Such increasing unemployment level occurs resulting from declining elasticity of employment, primarily in agriculture, industry and services. In addition, weak economic recovery results in decreasing tax revenue, and therefore, the deficit of 2015 State Budget is estimated to increase by 2.7% from GDP, which further results in increasing expenditures. 9 9.Second, although inflation in 2015 is estimated to be in the lower limit of inflation target range of 41%, inflation control challenges in 2016 will not be easy and need early mitigation. The release of inflation in November 2015 shows inflation pressure in some regions increases despite its low pressure level. Nationwide, inflation is recorded 0.21% (mtm) after a deflation by 0.08% (mtm). Annually, inflation in November reaches 4.89% (yoy) or lower than the previous month of 6.25% (yoy). 10. Inflation control in regions still faces some structural challenges, primarily pertaining to connectivity, production and land use change. In Java, food commodities remain frequently affecting inflation although this region is one of the centers of 10 agricultural production, especially rice and red chili. It closely relates to food distribution connectivity, declining agricultural land, dismal weather and inefficient market structure. 11. Inflation in 2016 has the risk to pass the upper limit of inflation target, primarily resulting from disturbed food supply due to delayed planting season by the occurrence of El Nino in 2015 and tariff adjustment by the government in energy sector, such as price adjustment of 3 kg LPG by Rp1000,-/kg; change of electricity customer from 450VA and 900VA to 1300VA; and impact of household tariff adjustment of 1300VA and 2200VA for post-paid electricity customers. This potential price adjustment will rise higher if the State Budget fails to assume the increasing subsidy. 11 12. Third, low competitiveness of national industry and export compared to neighboring countries. In the last 10 years, industry sector in GDP tends to decline owing to the shifting export structure to natural resource commodities and limited incentive to boost industrial transformation. The national industrial product export against the total export decreases from 57% to 43.7%. For example, in Banten, as one of the industry-based regions in Java, the industrial export decreases by 10% against GDP. 13. Lacking competitiveness of national export and industry is in line with the unsupportive trade facilities and logistics system compared to neighboring countries, which have first applied economic reforms. Moreover, lacking preparedness of the national industry to face Free Trade Area 12 (FTA) results in declining access of domestic industrial market and more aggressive efforts of neighboring countries to utilize FTA. Labor productivity in Indonesia remains low. A survey by McKinsey Global Institute (MGI) and Global Competitiveness Report 2014- 2015 show that labor productivity and efficiency in Indonesia are lower than other countries in the ASEAN region. 14. Implementation of ASEAN Economic Community (AEC) is approaching, marked by the era of zero-tariff barrier at the end of December 2015. On one hand, AEC will open market opportunities with the freer flow of goods, services, investment, labor and capital. However, on the other hand, it also results in higher competition in the domestic market 13 of each country. Big and basic questions for us on the AEC commitment arise, namely how big is our capability of creating competitiveness and utilizing AEC as an opportunity to play a role as the major actor of global production chain, or will we only become a market target. Ladies and gentlemen, Policy Response 15. In facing the challenges, it becomes more vital to create synergy and cooperation of various parties to strengthen Indonesia's economic foundation to allow consistent growth and competitiveness. The government has issued economic policy packages, which generally aim to boost competitiveness through industrial estate development, investment facilitation under one-stop 14 services, tax incentive, infrastructure project acceleration and different deregulation and debureaucratization policy packages. An emerging issue is their implementation in regions. Oftentimes, short term interests sacrifice long term ones. 16. To support such different government policies, Bank Indonesia consistently prioritizes monetary policy stance, which may maintain economic stability following the target. In addition, high uncertainty remains in the global financial market, particularly owing to the increasing Fed Fund Rate and various monetary policies adopted by the central banks of Europe, Japan and China, and therefore, Bank Indonesia takes careful monetary policies. Pertaining thereto, monetary policy 15 by Bank Indonesia under RDG decision on 17 November 2015 is adopted by decreasing Primary GWM in Rupiah from 8.0% to 7.5%, which is expected to increase banking financing capacity to support the improving economic activities since the third quarter of 2015. Decreasing Primary GWM of 50 bps will add banking liquidity to around Rp18 trillion. 17. In relation to inflation control, because inflation pressure comes not only from the demand side but also from the supply side, especially owing to food price fluctuation and government's policy on prices, it is necessary to increase cooperation between relevant Ministries, Regional Governments and Bank Indonesia. Regional Inflation Control Team (TPID) is a form of strategic coordination to 16 identify unstable price issue in regions and to formulate and follow up steps to control inflation through short and long term programs internalized in the Regional Government's Work Plan (RKPD), among others through budget support and price stabilization program alternatives in regions. 18. The form of cooperation between Bank Indonesia and Tasikmalaya regional government on food resilience program needs continuous development and improvement. In the meantime, BI Representative Office of Tasikmalaya and stakeholders have taken efforts to develop Chili Cluster under a Pilot Project of Agricultural Financing Scheme for Chilis in Tasikmalaya City, Tasikmalaya District and Ciamis District. Organic Rice Cluster Development in cooperation with Gapoktan Simpatik in 2015 has managed to 17 export their products to the USA. Furthermore, Horticultural Cluster Development in Tasikmalaya is made through credit facility extension from banks. Such forms of cooperation are appropriate steps, which need expansion as a part of food production capacity increase, which will eventually support inflation control in regions. 19. Regional inflation control strategies also need cooperation and synergy between regions, provinces, cities and districts. In overcoming increasing food deficit between cities and provinces, Government to Government and Business to Business cooperation models between regions are possible. 20. The most important step ahead in increasing industry and export competitiveness 18 is reorganizing integrated industrialization strategies and priorities with relevant policies, directed at domestic industrial integration strengthening as a part of global value chain. In addition to increasing the roles of industries, the roles of MSMEs are also vital to fill the limited capability of the Government in economic development. MSMEs, as one of the pillars of the economy of Indonesia and East Priangan, need to consistently transform in order to strengthen the competitiveness of local flagship products amidst dynamic global economy and increasing competitiveness. 21. We just receive a report on an activity conducted by West Java Incorporated Forum where BI Representative Office of West Java Province is also involved therein. 19 Based on the result of WJI dissemination, business matching and market study in Belgium and Holland in September 2015, it is concluded that the European market is quite promising for West Java MSMEs, but it is necessary to make improvement and adjustment to the market taste, standard and segment of respective export destination countries. The result of business matching also shows positive information. One of Dutch importers, NIVO, is interested in the products of Bank Indonesia MSME (WUBI) in West Java, which is followed up by sending product request questionnaire. It proves that MSME products have export opportunities and can compete in the global market. Synergy between Bank Indonesia through representative offices in West Java, Regional Governments and MSMEs may be strengthened through training, support 20 and dissemination of export opportunuties for MSME products. 22. East Priangan with abundant cultural and natural richness and highly creative local industrial products may be developed to drive the economy. Events, like the recently held Tasikmalaya Creative Festival, are expected to increase collaboration between the government, business associations, art and cultural communities and financial institutions, like banks, to build the city branding of Tasikmalaya as a creative city. It is expected to be able to stimulate local economic activities through tourist visits and to attract investments, which may eventually increase regional income and job opportunities because the main contributor of Tasikmalaya's economy comes 21 30% from trade activities, hotels and restaurants. Ladies and gentlemen, Economic Prospect 23. We are still confident that Indonesia's economy will improve with the support of healthier, more balanced and resilient economic structure. Our optimism in economic resilience closely relates to our commitment to constantly boost sustainable economic growth, supported by consistent policies in one synergy. 24. Global economy in 2016 is estimated to recover as supported by economic recovery of America and Europe, Japan grows limitedly and China's economy continues to weaken. 1 2013 Data (BPS) 22 National economy in 2016 is also estimated to improve. In addition to the continuously increasing government's infrastructure projects, rising private investments and strong consumption, economic growth in 2016 is also supported by export recovery in line with global economic recovery. We estimate that economic growth in 2016 will increase to 5.25.6%. In line with economic recovery prospect, banking credit and financing growth in 2016 is estimated within the range of 12-14%, as supported by the growing third party fund within the range of 13-15%. In line with the commitment to maintain economic stability and through cooperation of various parties in TPI and TPID on inflation pressure risk mitigation, we estimate inflation will be within the target range of 41%. 23 Ladies and gentlemen, Closing 25. Before ending my speech, I would like to extend my appreciation to all Regional Leaders and their staffs for their close cooperation. I expect this activity may improve communication to formulate policy recommendations to build the quality and sustainable economy of East Priangan. I hereby end my speech to open our discussion today. Thank you. Wassalamualaikum Wr Wb. Tasikmalaya, 7 December 2015 Deputy Governor Hendar 24

Title: Welcoming Speech OIC Expert Group Workshop, Mirza Adityaswara - Senior Deputy Governor, Bank Indonesia, Jakarta, 5 November 2014
text: 13 BANK INDONESIA BANK SENTRAL REPUBLIK INDONESIA WELCOMING SPEECH OIC Expert Group Workshop Mirza Adityaswara Senior Deputy Governor, Bank Indonesia Jakarta, 5 November 2014 Bismillahi rahmani rahiim, Your honour Director General SESRIC, Prof. Savas Alpay, H.E. Governors of Central Banks of the OIC member countries. Distinguished Speakers, and Ladies and gentlemen Assalamu'alaikum Warahmahtullah Wabarakatuh, very good morning to all of us [Greeting] 1. I am pleased to be here to deliver an opening remark in this important workshop. This Expert Group Workshop serves as a preliminary session leading to the OIC Central Bank Governors' Meeting that has put macro-prudential issue as the central theme of program. Let me express our gratitude to the OIC that has given the opportunity to Indonesia to host this important event and to take part in this international initiative aiming at achieving greater stability and more significant contribution of Islamic financial sector to the real economy. [Recognizing the development of Islamic financial market] Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, 2. We have recognized the remarkable growth of Islamic financial industry in the last two decades. The development has taken shape in many fronts, such as asset size, variety of products offered by the industry, supporting infrastructure, and the financial subsectors like awqaf and zakat sectors. In terms of growth, the Islamic financial industry has exceeded the conventional despite the small base number. A higher number of Islamic financial products and services have also been available in the market to serve wider segments of customers. This growing presence in the economy can be seen as achievement and also challenges to the financial authorities. The relevant authorities have to allocate more effort to equip the system with better regulatory framework and tools to make sure effective monitoring activities can be carried out well and market discipline and governance are implemented well. [The relevance of Islamic finance in the macro-prudential policy development framework] Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, 5. We have witnessed slow economic recovery years after the financial and economic turmoil erupted. Despite a lot of resources allocated for regulatory reforms to strengthen the financial system, the global financial system is still struggling to regain its financial stability and economic growth to curb increasing unemployment as a result of economic downturn. We were shown that exponential expansion of the financial sector cannot be sustained without sufficient development of the economic production sector. 1  13 BANK INDONESIA BANK SENTRAL REPUBLIK INDONESIA The financial expansion was initiated by some reasons such as financial deregulation which allowed the financial institutions to widen their scope of activities, technological advancement that promoted innovation in financial product development, and long period of low-interest rate regime. An excessive debt to GDP has also contributed to the economic stability since it gave tremendous pressure on fiscal sustainability. The regulatory framework has also failed to curb excessive risk taking behaviour by the financial players in maximizing their financial return without sufficiently understand the increasingly complex products. This risk taking behaviour was in fact supported by incorrect incentive mechanism that facilitated the financial managers with high rewards for its speculative activities. Indonesia has learnt very important lesson from the 1997/1998 Asian financial crisis on how a crisis could destroy years of our achievement in the economic development and it took substantial recovering period before we can really regain the economic momentum to deliver prosperity to our society. 4. In order to address that importance, G20 financial summit to the Financial Stability Board (FSB), the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) and other standard- setting bodies to work closely together seeking for better institutional arrangement and tools so that the central bank supported by relevant institution can have sufficient capability to withstand any possible disturbance. The effort was formulized into a well- designed macro-prudential policy framework that links micro-prudential issues and the financial stability to ensure sustainability of the economic development. It has been evident that in most of cases monetary policy alone is not sufficient to curb excessive risk-taking behaviour committed by the economic agent, including the bankers. Whilst the success of the monetary authority in controlling the inflation would also be dependent upon its surrounding stability. Henceforth, a lot of attention and effort have been paid to develop macro-prudential policy in complementary to the existing monetary policy. [The need to develop indicators, tools, instruments, and other support to other sector that could potentially support macro-prudential framework] Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, 5. In order to address the importance of financial stability, the ability of financial authorities to equip themselves with financial system surveillance and policy research activities is very crucial. This includes the development of surveillance technique with many tools and indicators to prescribe the best measures to reduce the vulnerabilities and imbalances in the financial system through macro and micro prudential approach. This set up has helped Indonesia in withstanding the wave of 2007/2008 global financial crisis. The central bank continues to develop its tools and policy instruments within the macro-prudential framework which includes the development of indicators, methods or models to capture systemic risks early and timely so that the risks can be mitigated before they are too late or too overwhelming to handle. Besides developing technical aspects, coordination among relevant authorities such as the Ministry of Finance, the Financial Services Authority and the Deposit Insurance Corporation is very crucial. Good coordination allows us to synchronize the policy formulation process so that a way to establish credible financial system is easier to achieve. 2 13 BANK INDONESIA BANK SENTRAL REPUBLIK INDONESIA 6. As a part of the national financial system, Islamic financial system has the same concern over the financial stability. Technically, Islamic finance might have different sets of financial contract that might require different arrangement of risk management and skill sets. But at the same time, Islamic bank and financial institutions are also exposed to credit, market, liquidity, and operational risks. Therefore, financial reforms that are taken place under Basel III framework are relevant to Islamic banking since the reform is trying to address some issues regarding competitive distortion and regulatory arbitrage that are universal when it comes to implementation. To address the importance, the IFSB has been trying to accommodate those regulatory aspects into the IFSB standards that will finally be implemented by the Islamic banks internationally. 7. Systemically, the stability of Islamic financial system is very important for two reasons. Firstly, Islamic financial system could serve as the other pillar to sustain the national development program, particularly with the characteristics that are pro-growth, pro- employment, and pro-stability. Secondly, with the growing presence of the industry, potential adverse impact resulted from the failures in the Islamic financial system may become more severe if it is poorly managed. A number of steps have been initiated through the implementation of micro-prudential and macro-prudential regulations, policy instruments and supporting infrastructure. The presence of lender-of-the-last- resort facility that allows the central bank to provide solvent but illiquid Islamic banks is one of the examples to maintain the operational soundness high. [Islamic financial system stability and social sector development] Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, 8. Besides equipping the system with sophisticated and comprehensive measures for achieving financial stability, allocating resources to broaden economic production base is also crucial in assuring adequate level of resilience to withstand any possible shocks. It is commonly believed that small and micro entrepreneurs have contributed a great deal of support to the economic robustness particularly in the period of financial or economic downturn. The search of long-term and low cost funds combined with innovative business model has been one the focuses of economic development programs in many countries and also multilateral development banks like Islamic Development Bank, African Development Bank, Asian Development Bank and the World Bank. Henceforth, financial deepening in a broad sense can be manifested in terms of product enhancement in the financial market and product innovation to promote wider financial access to broader segments including low-income society. 9. Islamic social sector that cover Zakat and Awqaf systems, if managed properly, can play very important role in delivering equitable economic development in terms of narrowing income gap by providing low income segment greater financial access and eventually better chance for starting-up business activities. Supported by efficient zakat and awqaf system we could expect that financial inclusion program can be carried out more efficiently to support national poverty alleviation program. Different from other commercial sources of funds, the existence of zakat funds would never cause unnecessary burden to the economy since the type of the funds managed is not 3  13 BANK INDONESIA BANK SENTRAL REPUBLIK INDONESIA commercially claimable, and hence, no excessive social cost will occur. Moreover, with the presence of efficient zakat system, more people particularly to those who come from the low-income society would have a better chance to be served. The same also goes to the Awqaf sector where, as a matter of fact, more people are endowed with low cost assets. Unfortunately, the majority of the assets are poorly managed so that potential benefits are not optimally materialized. Referring to information from Indonesian Awqaf Board, we have not less than four billions of meter squares of Awqaf land. Imagine how much economic drive that can be derived from these lands in terms of low cost infrastructure. I personally believe that these ideas are in-line with those of the governments, including those of the Multilateral Development Banks. 10. There are many areas that can be improved to achieve better quality of deliverables. One of the areas is the regulatory aspects of zakat and awqaf that is very important to be developed. Technically, we can benefit from the current development in other Islamic financial sectors or even the conventional counterpart. The initiative to propose Zakat core principles is very much appreciated as it could serve as the main reference for the establishment of zakat system in the OIC member countries. In the long run, better understanding toward the potential benefits of Islamic social sector may promote recognition internationally. Improvement in the quality of disbursement may also signify the contribution of the social sector towards the economic development. [Closing] 11. Finally, please allow me to wish you all a fruitful discussion and deliberation in this important event. I am sure that supported by internationally reputable academics and players, we can achieve significant outcomes that are beneficial to promote development in this particular area. I wish this program a great success and I declare this conference open. Thank you very much, wassalamualaykum warahmatullah wabarakatuh. Jakarta, 5th November 2014 4

Title: Globalization, financial stability and regional cooperation
Subtitle: Keynote address by Mr Burhanuddin Abdullah, Governor of Bank Indonesia, at the 33rd Asean Banking Council Meeting, Bali, 10...
text: Burhanuddin Abdullah: Globalization, financial stability and regional cooperation Keynote address by Mr Burhanuddin Abdullah, Governor of Bank Indonesia, at the 33rd Asean Banking Council Meeting, Bali, 10 October 2003. * * * Mr. Secretary General, Mr. Chairman, distinguished officers and members of the ASEAN Banking Council, honored guests, ladies and gentlemen, Good morning and Assalamualaikum wr.wb It is indeed a great pleasure for me to welcome all of you to this beautiful island of Bali and to open this Meeting today. It is also a most gratifying experience to speak before a large gathering of distinguished representatives of Bankers Association from the 10 ASEAN nations. Your presence here is an opportunity to further enhance cooperation among bankers to promote regional growth in a new global environment. As we all may aware, globalization is a reality and no country in the world is immune to its impact. It has opened up tremendous opportunities, but it has also posed a wide range of challenges and risks. We must therefore strive to maximize the benefits of globalization while endeavouring to minimize the costs. Our experiences in the past crisis has shown that even the most dynamic economies are vulnerable. In spite of the judicious macroeconomic policies that we adopted and the structural adjustments that we carried out, the development gains that we earned over decades could crumble in the span of a few weeks. The severe crisis proved that our banking system had some structural weaknesses. Those weaknesses had led most of the ASEAN countries banking system into deep trouble, reflecting in the mounting amount of non performing loan, serious liquidity problems, huge amount of losses and eventually caused many banks to became insolvent. In the face of these realities, the ASEAN banking industry has rightly responded to restore the solvency and the stability of the banking system, through banking restructuring program, and improvement of banking supervisory and regulatory capability. Ladies and Gentlemen, This crisis may be abating, but greater challenges still lie ahead. The challenges that we are going to faced, first is the heightened competition among banks that requires bankers to make the basic strategic decision. As financial modernization going forward, bankers will be forced to decide what kind of institution they want to be. Bankers need to figure out where they want to be in terms of a whole spectrum of activities whether they want to be a local bank, regional, or global bank. The second is a challenge of effective risk mitigation and risk intermediation. We have to ask how do we keep our risk management skills honed enough to deal with the world of high tech and sophisticated finance. I believe that the nature of the risk is changing. Its changing because the products and services are also changing in a more sophisticated way; that means the ability to recognize risk, measure risk, manage risk, offset risk, is utmost important for financial institution. The third challenge, obviously, is the process of financial deepening which affected market structures, complicating the task of regulatory oversight in several ways. As financial instrument become more complex; the boundaries between different types of financial market activity (lending, trading, insuring) become blurred; more claims become securitized and were exchanged in markets as traded instruments; and much financial activity became international in nature, blurring boundaries of responsibility among authorities. Now, the question is, what are the implications for bankers and regulators such as central banks? Ladies and Gentlemen, The first implication is that we have to acquire, improved, and further enhance our skills and capabilities. We need to improve our risk management skill considering that the nature of risk is changing very fast with new technology and products. 44/2003 1 The other is the requirement for us to conduct good corporate governance in the business. The need for transparency and corporate governance in any business including banking is very critical. Banking supervision cannot function well if sound corporate governance is not in place. Supervisory experience underscores the necessity of having the appropriate levels of accountability and checks and balances within each bank. Put plainly, sound corporate governance makes the work of supervisors infinitely easier. Sound corporate governance can contribute to a collaborative working relationship between bank management and bank supervisors. Consequently, central banks or regulator showed, by necessities, to impose market discipline and strengthen risk-based supervision as implied in the Basle Core Principles. Ladies and Gentlemen, In the face of these challenges and implication, ASEAN countries should make every effort to take advantage of the globalization and liberalization of investment and trade, knowing that it is the order of our global economy today. We should therefore actively involved in the many multilateral cooperation and/or institution. To strengthen economic cooperation among ASEAN countries, the leaders of ASEAN has just launched a new series of economies policies and initiatives as mentioned in Bali Concord II during their ninth ASEAN Summit, three days ago. One of the concept in Bali Concord II is the establishment of ASEAN Economic Community. That community envision "a stable, prosperous and highly competitive ASEAN economic region in which there is a free flow of goods, services, investment, labour and a freer flow of capital." The goal is to create a single market and production base by 2020; emulating other regional trade arrangements, particularly of the European Economic Community in the 1960s-1970s. With a population of some 500 million people and a combined GDP of about equal to Chinas, ASEAN Economic Community is clearly not an economic lightweight. ASEAN Economic Community should continue to cooperate to make the region more integrated, dynamic, and ultimately prosperous. We should also continue to cooperate in the area of financial sector, among other; to develop the Asian Bond Market that could facilitates Asian savings to be smoothly reinvested in the region, encourage alternative longer term financing through capital market, and formulate the task for the regulatory oversight to deal with the complexities of financial instrument between banks and non banks financial institution. Our ultimate objective is, of course, to establish the financial stability in the region. The role of central banks has to be in conjunction with that of other guardians of financial stability. Complexity, globalisation, and institutional interdependence forcefully argue for close cooperation between central banks, monetary authorities and other standard setters. It is within this sphere that ASEAN swap arrangement could be further strengthened for the benefit of the region. In line with the objective to maintain financial stability, there is an even greater need to promote our common interest and exchange views on regional issues. A major concern to most ASEAN financial sector nowadays is to revive the intermediation function of banking system. Alternatives route toward the recovery of intermediary function should be explored, for example; Indonesia has been trying to improve intermediary function through among others by promoting credit channelling to the micro or small and medium enterprises. There has been quite some success in this area and we are very much willing to share with you the achievement so far. Another concern for ASEAN financial sector is the implementation of Basle Accord II which has raised question of the readiness of the banking system. We should therefore continue strengthening collaboration between central banks, monetary authorities, bankers, and private sector. In this regard, central banks have to provide the infrastructure where financial markets rely on, so that the best practices can be adapted. We also need to harmonized/standardized the financial institution structure, skill, and regulation in the region to face the Accord. Ladies and Gentlemen, On bilateral level, cooperation among bankers in the region is also essential in preparing the system for a more sophisticated and complex banking practice in the globalized era so that the region could still achieving financial stability. This is the challenge for us and also for ASEAN Bankers Association. The ASEAN Bankers Association has played an important role in facilitating the exchange of information and expertise on banking among the staff of the banks in Southeast Asia. There is room 2 44/2003 for greater cooperation among banks, such as exchange, attachment, and apprenticeship among the staff of the banks in the region, as well as cooperation with other regional groupings and international financial institutions. ASEAN Bankers Association should explore ways to create greater synergies through partnership and cooperation. I believe that the ASEAN Bankers Association will deliberate at length a strategic review of cooperation in Finance, Investment, and Trade; Education; and Inter Regional relation on this meeting. This is an opportunity for the Council to re-examine the relevance of ASEAN Bankers Association roles, and explore ways in which it can better serve its members. ASEAN Bankers Association has to reposition itself to meet the challenges of the new globalized economy. Finally, may I now take a great pleasure in declaring the Meeting open and wishing all of you success in your deliberations. Thank you. 44/2003 3

Title: Monetary and banking in Indonesia - developments and challenges ahead
Subtitle: Speech by Mr Burhanuddin Abdullah, Governor of Bank Indonesia, to the Financial Club, Jakarta, 21 August 2003.
text: Burhanuddin Abdullah: Monetary and banking in Indonesia - developments and challenges ahead Speech by Mr Burhanuddin Abdullah, Governor of Bank Indonesia, to the Financial Club, Jakarta, 21 August 2003. * * * Excellencies members of Indonesian Council of World Affairs Distinguished Guests, Colleagues and friends, Good afternoon, and Assalamuaalamualaikum wr wb. It is both a pleasure and an honor for me to be here today to speak before distinguished audience. Let me first thank you for inviting me, to share with you some of my thought regarding our current situation that could probably shape our future. If one ponders on our world today and tries to look back for a while to not too distant past, one may find himself in a bewildering circumstances. It seems that the past is to starkly different than that of today and that has no relevance with the present, let alone the future that we know nothing of. Our very existence at the present is in danger of detachment from our historical root of yesterday. And, yet, we know the passage of time is a continuous events that whatever the dynamic of transition in human endeavour, there is always element of continuity. What is the element of continuity of the economy in transition like the one in our country? Does this element of continuity need to be preserved as such that whatever the social dynamics, it has to be maintained at all cost? Time is the element of continuity for the evolutionary process of nature and macroeconomic stability, in my view, is the element of continuity for the Indonesian economy in transition. The stability is so important that whatever the cost to maintain it, we are ready to pay for it. It is so important simply because we can not imagine what the economy can do without. Macroeconomic stability is the word of the day and macroeconomic stability is a regular preaching of central bankers. As a person who has been in the central bank for years, and so get used to the phrase monetary stability and/or macroeconomic stability that some time questioning the real meaning of these very words. Especially if we look around and see many of our fellow countryman are out of job and many more becoming parasites of our social web. Should we forego some degree of stability in return for employment opening or should we stick to it, and let the other authorities take care of employment issue. The mandate that was given to Bank Indonesia by its constitution is precisely the maintenance of our monetary stability. BI is no longer engage in lending activities known as liquidity financing to be extended by our banking sector to a number of the so called development program. BI is no longer giving a bridging financing to government. The task of BI is so focused on maintaining stability, that it was granted independence from any policy interference from anybody. BI has no function in development, but take care and nurture of the foundation of development, i.e., stability, without which there will be no development at all. Ladies and Gentlemen, It is within this mandate that BI is now trying to perform. In the past several months, we have been quite successful in curbing inflationary pressures. As measured year-over-year, the inflation rate at the end of July fell to 5.79%.
